The Inquisitors served as vanguard to eliminate heretics and dark forces, and were also reserves for Heroes. The probability of a Hero emerging from this group was very high.

Jeanne, as one of the Inquisitors, was also pushing herself to the utmost this time, determined to successfully become the 234th Hero and finally end her lingering regret.

Her strength among the Inquisitors was not weak — she ranked in the upper tier. Coupled with her devout faith in the Goddess, her chances of becoming a Hero were very high.

There weren't many people who could compete with Jeanne — only a handful. She believed she was the best candidate for this Hero selection. No one was more suitable than her.

Moreover, a few days ago, when Pope George came here to observe the warriors' drills, he patted Jeanne on the shoulder and personally said he had high hopes for her. This greatly boosted Jeanne's confidence!

In the noisy training ground, Jeanne closed her eyes, took a deep breath, and gripped her holy spear, Scarlet Enchantress, tightly. Saint-tier battle aura surged powerfully within her, her strength significantly greater than before.

She swung her holy spear and twisted her body. A bloody afterimage flashed across her sight, and the massive boulder in front of her was instantly shattered to pieces. Countless neat cracks even appeared on the floor of the training ground!

Jeanne slowly opened her eyes and found that the warriors around her were startled, their eyes filled with awe. She let out a long breath, overflowing with confidence —

This time...

I will definitely become a Hero!

title: Chapter 10 — Not Worth Mentioning
content:
Chapter 10 — Not Worth Mentioning

Volume 35 · Chapter 10

Hey hey, you're really working hard, Joan, but you'd better pay attention to the impact, don't scare others, many of them are newcomers, hoping to kill enemies and achieve merit on the battlefield— A man about the same age as Joan walked over slowly, wearing a sleeveless shirt, his muscles tensed, his steps light, as if walking on tiptoe. This person is Ayana Mi, a member of the Inquisition squad, like Joan possessing considerable Saint-tier strength, and among the Hero reserves he stands out. If anyone could compete with Joan for the Hero position this time, then this Ayana Mi would be one of them. Apart from lacking Joan's devout heart, Ayana Mi has no weaknesses, and his chance to become the new Hero is equally great. "Is that you? Ayana Mi, sorry, I was too focused just now and didn't notice the people around me." Joan eased her fierce aura, not wanting to put pressure on the newcomers who had just joined the team. "Having someone as strong as you among the Hero candidates has dealt a heavy blow to many newcomers, who no longer dare to hope to become Heroes." Ayana Mi smiled. "If being scared by me makes them lose all fighting spirit, then they truly aren't fit to be Heroes; they'd be better off farming." Joan paused, speaking sternly: "The battlefield is no child's play; we must face ruthless demons who won't show mercy, only swing their slaughtering blades coldly. If they feel fear toward me they can still live, but if they fear the demons, they are surely doomed." "Don't put it so bluntly; damaging the newcomers' confidence isn't good." Ayana Mi spread his hands; although what Joan said is true, it will cause many new recruits to retreat. "Letting so many people with no combat experience join the crusade is not a good idea; they won't help at all and might even drag us down." Joan spoke without mercy, adding: "These temporarily conscripted soldiers don't realize the danger of fighting demons; they only think about exchanging demon heads for more money, unaware that demons are far stronger than they imagine. If they don't wet their pants on the battlefield, that's already not bad." "Joan, don't you know the Church's situation? In the battle against Lucifer III, we suffered heavy losses; being able to recruit so many people again for the crusade is no small feat." Ayana Mi shrugged helplessly, explaining: "Not long ago His Holiness the Pope wrote to the monarchs of various kingdoms seeking aid, showing how short-staffed we are." "Useless; no matter how many people form a crusade, if they lack sincere faith in the Goddess, they are just a rabble that will crumble before the demons." Joan fixed her eyes on Ayana Mi, emphasizing: "A team capable of defeating demons must each harbor steadfast faith; only then will they receive the Great Goddess's blessing. Unfortunately, there are too many opportunists joining the Church now, and our steadfast faith is hanging by a thread." Ayana Mi immediately became solemn, greatly admiring Joan's devout heart, which made him feel ashamed: "I feel deeply inferior; I also wanted to gain merit through this crusade and possibly serve as the Pope's personal guard, but my faith in the Goddess is nowhere near as pure as yours." "The Goddess is merciful; as long as you sincerely repent, she will grant you forgiveness." Joan's expression turned solemn. "I hope so; may the Goddess protect me and let me survive this war." Ayana Mi made a prayer gesture, then shifted the topic: "This crusade is completely different from before; its scale is enormous, demanding we seize the Seventh Demon Lord's Palace by any means in a very short time. Do you know any inside information?" "Um." Joan indeed heard some things, lowering her voice: "The cause of this crusade is internal chaos among the demons; their ancestors have awakened. This ancient demon god is far stronger than previous Demon Lords and also more dangerous. To prevent the war from spreading worldwide, His Holiness the Pope chose to strike first." "No wonder; no wonder the Vatican lately reeks of gunpowder, an enemy stronger than the Demon Lords." Ayana Mi muttered, then suddenly asked: "Joan? I heard you've actually faced a true Demon Lord? Could you share your impressions?" "Sorry, I don't want to recall those things." Joan's face turned grim; recalling the Demon Lords she has seen, she still trembles all over. "No way? Even the bravest of the Inquisition, Joan, fears something?" Ayana Mi said meaningfully. Joan furrowed her brows, took a deep breath, and replied helplessly: "They are immensely strong, so strong that I see no hope of victory; I cannot forget that terrifying pressure, and even a slight recollection brings about a death-like suffocation." A bead of cold sweat slid down Ayana Mi's forehead; from Joan's words he could feel how terrifying the demons are—creatures at the top of the food chain, even dragons must lower their proud heads. "Your ordeal sounds pitiable; this time we face an existence more terrifying than demons, and whoever becomes Hero will have to bear an unimaginable pressure for ordinary people." "I firmly believe the Great Goddess will protect us; she will provide help from the unseen, letting us safely pass this crisis." Joan prayed, saying, even though she knows this is extremely dangerous, her devout faith will overcome fear. "It seems I have no chance left; this time the Hero will most likely be you." Ayana Mi spread his hands helplessly, adopting a resigned pose. "That depends on the Pope's decision; whoever becomes Hero, as long as they are a faithful follower of the Goddess, I will show respect and support." Joan frowned, speaking bluntly: "The Hero is the soul of the Church's crusade army and the Goddess's martial symbol in the mortal world; we shouldn't let cunning opportunists or heretics take the role, for that would taint the spirit of the Hero lineage passed down through generations. Don't you want to become a Hero, Ayana Mi?" "If the Pope is willing to entrust me with this burden, I won't refuse, but there is someone else more suitable than us." Ayana Mi said meaningfully. "Who?" Joan asked curiously. "Alice Claudiyah; don't forget that the former Hero is still alive, merely cast out of the temple for losing the Hero's inheritance armor; otherwise the Hero position would never come to us. As for how to fight demons, I think her experience is richer than ours, right?" Ayana Mi's smile grew; the fact that the previous Hero is still alive is not good news for those vying for the Hero position. Joan recalled Alice, that "archenemy" who snatched her future from her hands, causing her to unconsciously clench her fists— "A hundred thousand Temple Knights perished in the Death Marshes; only she alone survived." "Those who come purely for fame and money are utterly unworthy to wield the Goddess's sword." "Without a doubt, she is the most failed Hero in history, not worth mentioning."

title: Chapter 11 — Hero of the Subjugation Battle (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 11 — Hero of the Subjugation Battle (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 35 · Chapter 11

"Even though the 233rd Hero was a complete failure, compared to us she still has a considerable advantage, after all she once ventured deep into the Death Marsh and fought
that terrifying Lucifer III." Ayanaomi looked around, lowered her voice, "Actually I heard that after leaving the Church, Alice became an adventurer and achieved quite a bit; His Majesty the Pope intends to recall her, I don't know if it's true?"

"No matter what conditions His Majesty the Pope offers, she will never come back, I am absolutely certain of that."
Jeanne recalled Alice's attitude, her thoughts already completely on that heretical man.

"Why are you so sure?" Ayanaomi asked.

"Because she never belonged here." Jeanne replied concisely.

"Since that's the case, let me congratulate you in advance, O glorious 234th Hero."
Ayanaomi thought no one could compete with Jeanne; without a doubt, she was the most suitable candidate.

"Don't be like that; before His Majesty the Pope announces the result, we all have a chance."
Jeanne said this with her mouth, but deep down she still firmly believed in her own abilities.

"Since there's no result yet, shall we spar a bit?"

Ayanaomi assumed a stance, Saint-tier battle aura coiled around her fists, a golden lion's phantom faintly appearing behind her.

Jeanne smiled, wielding the holy spear with her left hand, tracing a cross in front of her with her right, divine power bolstering her.

Their duel caused quite a commotion in the training field; people around scattered, fearing they'd be caught in the aftermath.

If the two individuals capable of contending for the Hero's position sparred, they might very well demolish this training ground—

Ayanaomi bared her teeth in a grin, launching the first attack; as her fists swung, waves of lion roars erupted, like sharp fangs capable of easily piercing an opponent's body.

Jeanne was no less impressive, her whole body bathed in holy light, her holy spear striking twice to form a huge scarlet cross, the sharp spear-light thrusting straight out.

Before they even touched each other, their Saint-tier auras had already collided, making it hard to tell who would win in the short term?

Suddenly, a red-clad figure descended from the sky, left hand blocking Ayanaomi's lion fist, right hand gripping the impact from Jeanne's holy spear, successfully withstanding the combined assault of two Saint-tier masters single-handedly, and emerged unscathed.

The newcomer had a grim expression, dressed in the garb of an ascetic, only a few strands of pale hair remained on his head, his emaciated, bony frame appearing utterly devoid of menace.

Ascetics are a sect of the Holy Church of Light; they harbor an almost fanatical devotion to the Goddess, believing that self-mortification is an act of loyalty to her, which can alleviate humanity's sins.

Their bodies are often bound with many straps, and those straps are studded with numerous sharp nails; whenever they move, the nails pierce the flesh, causing the ascetics to emit anguished wails.

Yet the ascetics consider this not pain, but a dedication of their bodies to all humanity, letting themselves bear suffering to lessen the sins of all people—this is a benevolence surpassing all believers.

Whenever they are in agony near fainting and see some inexplicable visions, they say they have seen the great Goddess.

What seems like foolish, anti-intellectual behavior actually greatly hones the ascetics' mental fortitude; this group easily produces astonishingly strong individuals, and among the ten legendary Heroes in history, half came from the ascetics among the faithful.

When the ascetic elder appeared, the onlooking crowd burst into cries of astonishment, their eyes filled with respect—clearly his status was not ordinary.

Ayanaomi startled, quickly put on a smile, and spoke humbly, "Lord Srain, why have you come? We, we were just sparring."

"Sparring?" the elderly Srain released them, saying sternly, "Your sparring will destroy the training field; why not devote your energy to fighting demons? The 234th Subjugation has begun—you need to give it your all."

"Terribly sorry, Lord Srain." Ayanaomi bowed deeply, not daring to offend this elder in the slightest.

Srain snorted coldly, gazing at the still‑shocked Jeanne, and said solemnly, "Jeanne, your strength is still lacking; you must intensify your training, break through to Saint‑tier as soon as possible—sparring with Ayanaomi is just a waste of time."

Ayanaomi's face flushed a bit, she embarrassedly scratched her heated cheeks with her fingers.

Jeanne came to her senses, quickly bowed respectfully, "Yes, I will strive."

"I hold Jeanne in high esteem; among the younger generation, your faith is the most devout, your ability is also quite good—no one is more suited than you to be the Hero of the 234th Subjugation. I've heard His Majesty the Pope also favors you; I expect that when the result is announced tomorrow, we will hear your name."

"Srain paused, then continued, 'If you encounter any difficulties or problems in your training, you can come to me anytime; I have instructed many Heroes, and O'Brian was once my student.'"

"Thank you for your kindness." Jeanne lowered her head even further; a cold sweat had broken out on her forehead at some point, her heart unable to calm for a long time—

Srain, not merely a red‑clad cardinal, often appears beside Pope Ji'ougen.

Moreover, he is the head of the entire Inquisition squad, overseeing many mysterious authorities.

His existence is little known; he is more like the Church's shadow, helping it handle all sorts of dirty business.

Rumor has it his strength is formidable; he has not only guided many Heroes, but he himself possesses the capability to become a legendary Hero.

However, due to his eccentric, reclusive personality, he dislikes showing his face, refused the chance to become a Hero, and has always remained secluded in the temple.

From the way he just easily subdued two Saint‑tier powerhouses, this old man's power is unfathomable!

The next day, inside the temple.

The Hero for the 234th Subjugation is about to be chosen here.

All eligible Hero candidates have gathered here, waiting for the Pope to personally announce the name.

Yet the outcome is already obvious; everyone occasionally glances at the composed Jeanne, she is the most suitable person to become the Hero—aside from her strength still being lacking, there is nothing else to fault.

"In order to safeguard peace in the mortal world and protect humanity's prosperity, we shall launch the 234th Subjugation against the demon race! The Hero is the indispensable soul of the Crusade Army! She must possess both virtue and talent, harbor devout faith! Without hesitation, wield the sword for the great Goddess!" Pope Ji'ougen, beneath the colossal statue of the Goddess, frenziedly fed the youth with chicken soup, "As for who will take up the mantle of Hero, I think you already have someone in mind—she is a pure‑hearted woman, young yet already possessed of great strength!"

Below, Jeanne suddenly lifted her head, her eyes igniting with hope.

"She possesses unparalleled devout faith; even if treated unfairly, she would willingly return to the Goddess's embrace."

Jeanne's lips gradually curled upward, an unwilling smile of pride spreading across her face.

"She has battled the perilous Demon Lord and, fortunately, survived; she has abundant experience in dealing with demons!"

Jeanne's smile beamed; she stood up proudly on the spot, her heart thrilled, thinking—

"This isn't about me, could it be someone else?"

title: Chapter 12 — Intimidation (Monthly Vote Request)
content:
Chapter 12 — Intimidation (Monthly Vote Request)

Volume 35 · Chapter 12

In the presence of the hero candidates, they all gazed at Joan of Arc standing up, some even raising their thumbs to congratulate her.

Joan of Arc had never experienced such a feeling of being the center of attention. Surveying the surroundings, this was the closest she had ever been to the position of Hero.

She believed her efforts had finally been rewarded, and she had finally escaped the shadow brought by Alice, fulfilling her long-cherished dream,

to become a Hero honored to defend the Goddess!

Joan of Arc had always kept in mind the matter of Alice "stealing" her position as Hero, believing that losing to a faithless opportunist was an unforgivable great shame in her life!

However, at this moment, the clouds covering Joan of Arc's heart dissipated, leaving only a smooth road ahead.

Pope Georig saw Joan of Arc suddenly stand up for no reason, and couldn't help but look somewhat puzzled, thinking that he clearly hadn't announced the result yet, so why did Joan stand up?

"The 234th extermination battle will be continued by Alice Clodya!"

With Pope Georig's announcement, the atmosphere in the temple instantly fell into dead silence, and unexpectedly, they heard an unexpected name?

The people below whispered in surprise, not understanding why the Pope didn't choose Joan—

"Who is this Alice? Why can she push Joan aside and become Hero?"

"I don't know, it just means you're a newcomer. The Hero of the last extermination team was Alice, didn't you know? Not expecting it's her again this time."

"Alice originally lost the important Hero relic armor, such a failure of a person, how can she still have face?"

Joan of Arc was petrified on the spot, her joyful smile instantly frozen, her eye corners constantly twitching, her brain falling into a blank—

What?!

Why did Alice suddenly come back?

Previously, she continuously extended olive branches, but she never paid any heed.

Why specifically this time?

Is it deliberate targeting me? Wanting to snatch the opportunity to become Hero from my hands again!

Joan of Arc's resentment surged in her heart, her lips bitten until they bled, her tightly clenched fists turned pale, and her hatred toward Alice was taking root and sprouting.

Drip, drip, in the corridor outside the temple, the sound of footsteps could be heard.

Accompanying the discussions and doubts of the crowd, Alice appeared before everyone, her expression calm and composed, every movement filled with confidence.

Once upon a time, Alice was disgraced and driven out of the church due to her poor performance. After several years, she returned, and she was no longer the novice Hero she used to be.

No matter from which aspect one looks at it, the current Alice is the best candidate for Hero, and she also has the opportunity to challenge the Legend, making her name permanently recorded in history, becoming the object of worship by future believers.

"Long time no see, everyone."

Alice swept her sharp gaze over the crowd and discovered many familiar faces.

Although Alice had not lived in the temple for a long time, she still recognized many friends she had trained with back then—

"I know everyone is surprised, why I suddenly came back to serve as Hero again?"

"I want to say, I am not coveting the prestige and honor brought by Hero, but the turmoil of the demon race has already begun to threaten the safety of the entire mundane world. If handled improperly, no one would be able to escape this disaster."

"To guard the prosperity and stability of humanity, I am duty-bound, so I agreed to Pope's request to serve as Hero again."

"The current situation is dire, I hope everyone can understand and support me. As long as we unite, we will definitely be able to get through this crisis!

After listening to Alice's impassioned speech, the people below remained completely silent, and no one was willing to respond to her.

In everyone's eyes, Alice was a failed Hero, unqualified to return, suddenly descending and snatching Joan's opportunity to become Hero, it seemed not in line with the rules?

Actually, Alice's words were half-true and half-false, she just hoped to become Hero again and have the qualification to use the Church's power.

Although Alice's desire to maintain the stability and prosperity of the mundane world was true, what was even more important was that she wanted to use the Church's power to rescue Merlin, who was sealed in a pot.

To deal with the ancient demon god Behemoth, Alice herself was absolutely impossible. She very much needed a capable helper, obviously the Church is the best choice, not only is it the arch-enemy of the demon race, but it also values her greatly.

"Cough cough!" Pope Georig awkwardly coughed twice, seeing everyone refusing to buy it, and then stood out to say, "The former Alice as Hero was indeed somewhat immature, but it's different now, she has grown up."

"She has no genuine devotion to the Goddess, she's just a despicable opportunist, mixing with heretics every day, how can such a person become the soul of an extermination team?" Joan of Arc loudly put forward her objection, her heart very dissatisfied.

"Right, she's not even a believer. Becoming Hero would only become a joke. Back then there was no choice, but it's different now!" Ayanami sitting in the crowd chimed in, equally very resentful of Alice becoming Hero.

Pope Georig frowned and immediately put on a stern face, scolding—

"Be quiet! This is a decided matter!"

"Hero is the soul of the extermination team. Having genuine faith is far from enough; one also needs the strength to defeat demons!"

"Compared with empty faith, the power to kill demons is more important. Obviously, Alice possesses this power."

"Empty faith?" Joan of Arc's whole body trembled, unexpectedly not expecting such words to come from the Pope's mouth, which made her originally firm heart begin to waver a bit.

"Pope His Holiness, Alice is the shame of the Church. All 100,000 Holy Knights were buried in the marsh, only she survived, and she even lost the precious Inherited Hero armor. I even suspect she actively offered the precious treasure to the demon, so she had the chance to survive. " Ayanami paused, her eyes full of hostility, saying, "If she becomes the Hero of this extermination, the tragedy will be repeated! This time, what precious thing do you plan to offer? I can imagine how humble you would beg the demons."

"Shut your stinky mouth!"

Alice was so angry that the veins on her forehead jumped, her gaze fixed, the pressure of a pseudo-god directly surged forward like a mountain.

Ayanami stared wide-eyed in astonishment, her face pale, unable to move in Alice's pressure, her throat as if being tightly pinched by an invisible big hand!

Just moments ago, Ayanami was chattering non-stop, but now she immediately fell silent, cold sweat wetting her back, shivering and thinking, this huge pressure is a bit similar to Senior Sreian!

Even Joan of Arc was startled, gaping in surprise, the pressure released by Alice now made her recall the pressure when facing the Demon Lord, very close!

Joan of Arc couldn't understand what Alice had experienced? Her strength improvement speed was comparable to riding a rocket, unknowingly already invisible behind her back.

The hero candidates were dead silent, everyone lowered their heads and fell into self-closure, where was the courage to question Alice?

Just based on this power close to Demon Lords, the believers' so-called noble faith? Would also become fragile and inadequate.

"If you think yourselves more suitable to serve as the Hero of this extermination? Welcome everyone to challenge me." Alice quickly restrained her aura, her gaze sweeping over everyone—

"I will make everyone recognize the gap between ideal and reality."

I worked all day on a plane, I just arrived at my residence two hours ago, the update is late.

It's the beginning of the month, and you readers probably have monthly tickets in your hands?

Don't be stingy, give them to me, I'll update more!

title: Chapter 13 — Preparation for the Crusade
content:
Chapter 13 — Preparation for the Crusade

Volume 35 · Chapter 13

Alice's sharp refusal to suppress dissenting voices left the Hero candidates speechless.

Though Alice did not want things this way, she needed the Holy Church's power now more than ever, and could not let this chance to serve as Hero slip away.

Merlin was sealed inside the teapot with his fate unknown, and she refused to sit idle. She had to rescue him as quickly as possible.

With overwhelming strength advantage, Alice swept aside all opposition. She looked toward Jeanne among the crowd, a wave of guilt rising in her heart—

I'm sorry, Jeanne. Just this once, I cannot give up.

Jeanne's face was extremely grim. She unconsciously clenched her fists, her eyes flashing with unwillingness as resentment and jealousy grew like weeds, spreading wildly in the depths of her heart.

If only I had the power to defeat Alice, I would absolutely never let her run rampant!

That a despicable opportunist with no faith whatsoever should become Hero was a disgrace to every single believer!

Pope Geogen scanned everyone, and when he saw that no one dared object further, he finally felt somewhat relieved.

Truthfully, he had originally wanted to nominate Jeanne as Hero, but Alice had suddenly returned.

Aside from her insufficient loyalty to the Church, Alice was superior to Jeanne in every other aspect.

This crusade was different from previous ones—it would be far more dangerous—and the expedition team urgently needed a powerhouse like Alice on board.

"I hereby announce that the 234th crusade expedition shall be commanded by Alice Cloodya. Her return will surely bring the Church long-awaited victory!"

"Also, welcome back, Alice. As I have said before, the Church's doors are always open for you."

Late at night, Alice politely declined the Pope's enthusiastic invitation and did not stay within the cathedral, instead settling at a small inn somewhere in the Holy City of Vatican.

The reason was that demons were too conspicuous in their identities. In a holy city overflowing with Temple Knights, they risked exposure at every turn.

Furthermore, they felt a deep fear of sacred power, and entering the cathedral caused them extreme discomfort. The oppressive aura radiating from the giant statue of the Goddess made it difficult for them to breathe.

To ease the demons' suspicions, Alice had no choice but to abandon the plan of housing Chris within the cathedral.

"So that's your so-called plan? Rejoin the Church and become a lapdog for a bunch of creepy holy men?"

Lilith crossed her arms, staring at Alice with an eerie expression, her tone resembling an interrogation of a prisoner.

"Is there a problem with that?"

Alice covered her sleeping baby daughter with the blanket, then shot back with a stern face.

Little Chris knew nothing of her father's situation; everyone had kept it from her. Even in her dreams, she believed her father would be back soon.

"Of course there's a problem."

It wasn't just Lilith—every demon present shared similarly suspicious gazes, deeply perplexed by Alice's decision.

"I've seen it from the beginning; you're a church spy planted beside my brother!" Lilith's tone was aggressive. She believed Alice had always maintained ties with the Church and that this return was part of a long-term plan.

"Why would you think that?"

Alice frowned, irritated. She couldn't understand why Lilith harbored such enormous hostility toward her.

She was bewildered—if she were truly a Church spy, what on earth would she be gaining by staying with Merlin?

Besides, what kind of spy would be so foolish as to have a child with the enemy? That would be losing both the wife and the army!

Alice grew angrier the more she thought about it, until she actually laughed at herself. It seemed these demons still refused to trust her.

"You're a female spy cultivated by the Church, deliberately attaching yourself to my brother to extract inside information about the demon race from him, even attempting to turn him against his own kind, which caused other demons to suspect him during the Expectation Conference. Now that the demon race has fallen into crisis, you simply retreat back to the Church." Lilith narrowed her eyes, conjuring an atmosphere of conspiracy theories. "Even Chris is merely a tool you use to keep my brother in check. Everything was planned by you all along, right!"

"???" Alice froze for a moment, thinking to herself—I hated Merlin so much back then, why didn't I come up with such an ingenious plan? What a waste!

"No way!" Lilith glanced around nervously, her voice tense. "There are Church knights埋伏ed all around this room, ready to capture us all in one net!"

"Princess Lilith, don't be ridiculous. Xiu has already scouted the area. This isn't the cathedral—it's just a small inn in Vatican City. Aside from occasional Church guards on patrol, the rest are all civilians. Where would there be any ambush?" Blackman said exasperatedly.

"Shut up! It's better to be careful than sorry! Do you all want to trust this despicable human woman?" Lilith glared at the other demons.

"Miss Alice isn't a spy. If she had any ill intentions toward His Majesty Merlin, she would have acted long ago." Helena thought back to when Merlin had reverted to his juvenile form. If not for Alice's careful care, he might have already met with danger.

"What makes you so certain?" Lilith furrowed her brow.

"Isn't it obvious? Miss Alice likes His Majesty Merlin very much. Who would harm someone they like?" Helena said with a completely serious expression.

"Pfft!" Alice nearly choked on her own saliva, her cheeks flushing red as she fumbled defensively. "I never said I liked him! It's all just misunderstandings."

"Never mind, Miss Alice. Everyone in Lexem knows that fact. Only you two still believe it's all just misunderstandings." Helena looked at her with sympathetic eyes.

Alice opened her mouth as if to speak, but her flickering gaze betrayed her inability to form words. She wondered inwardly—was I really that obvious?

"Pfft!" Lilith had only intended to make things difficult for Alice, never expecting to end up force-fed dog food herself.

"I think it's understandable that Miss Alice rejoining the Church to serve as Hero." Xiu spoke up suddenly.

"What did you just say, Xiu?" Lilith's face twisted with anger.

"The Church has profound resources and influence. By borrowing their power, we might actually be able to rescue our sealed monarch." Xiu answered after careful consideration.

"That's right. With our current strength, we can't even enter Demon Castle, but if the Church is willing to lend its strength, it should be able to hold off the ancient Demon God." Duke nodded gloomily.

"To rescue His Majesty Merlin, borrowing the Church's power is also the only option. As the saying goes, the enemy of my enemy is my friend. The Church and Behemoth could never coexist peacefully." Ophelia believed Alice's plan was viable.

"Hey! You lot! She's human! Don't let your guard down!" Lilith noticed several of the other demons beginning to gradually accept Alice's presence.

"Right now, apart from trusting Miss Alice, do we have any other options?" Xiu asked solemnly.

"Princess Lilith, rescuing His Majesty Merlin should be our top priority. Even if you can't stand this human woman, that can wait until later." Ophelia said in an older-sister tone.

"Hmph!" Lilith glared hatefully at Alice. "I will absolutely never trust her."

"Excuse me, but when exactly does the expedition begin? We need to prepare in advance." Duke asked earnestly.

"Normally, after the Hero candidate is decided, the expedition will set out within two weeks." Alice paused, then added meaningfully, "If the Church takes this crusade seriously—"

"Then they will surely dispatch powerful Cardinals to accompany us."

title: Chapter 14 — The Eroded Lucifer (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 14 — The Eroded Lucifer (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 35 · Chapter 14

The Holy Church's secret stronghold was incredibly spacious, vast enough that one could not see the end of it with a single glance.

Numerous white whales, each crowned with a golden halo, drifted lazily above, emitting eerie low growls.

These were identical to the monsters Merlin had killed before leaving the Demon Lord Palace, except that here there were countless such whales.

These whale-like creatures were all artificial demons, a secret research project of the Church, requiring countless efforts to complete.

They not only possessed the strength of demons but also obeyed the commands of their human handlers, making up for the lack of intelligence in wild demons.

Among the countless white whales, one stood out—a completely black whale with numerous small wings along its back and a peculiar purple halo atop its head.

Its temper was extremely volatile, and its furious roars made even its companions dare not approach.

Several thick chains were embedded in its body, forcibly restraining it and hanging it in the broadest area above.

This black whale was a mutated artificial demon, possessing overwhelming strength that could crush white whales, but unfortunately, it lacked obedience and was too volatile to control, making it more akin to a true wild demon.

Ordinary white whales had Saint-tier power, and after mutation, their strength would surge to unimaginable levels!

Through the towering transparent glass, a middle-aged man in a prison uniform knelt, desperately tearing at his hair, emitting a heart-wrenching cry from the depths of his throat.

His eyes were bloodshot, tears streaming uncontrollably, and his veins bulged and grew, even piercing through his skin and dancing wildly.

Red Robe Archbishop Slein stood outside the transparent glass, watching the middle-aged man in agony with a mix of anticipation and admiration in his eyes.

The poor middle-aged man had been tormented to the point of losing his mind, using his nails to slash his own flesh, spraying blood that congealed into flesh tumors, which devoured him and expanded at a visible rate.

Within just a few breaths, a white whale calf was born from the flesh tumor, its tender wings flapping as it floated in the air.

If devout believers witnessed this, their faith would surely collapse. All these artificial demons were born from human sacrifices.

Red Robe Archbishop Slein sighed disappointedly, pulled out a black notebook, and crossed out a name, "43,254th experimental subject, failed again..."

Behind the seemingly cold numbers lay countless living lives. The Church had gone to such extremes to create more black whales to bolster their forces.

Compared to the demon's one-hit kills that slaughtered humans, the Church's methods seemed more merciful.

Slein was the creator of the artificial demon technology, despite sacrificing countless human experimental subjects, but still couldn't create another mutated demon.

"Slein, how are the experiments going?" Pope Eugene walked out from the darkness.

"Still failing. Creating a mutated demon requires luck. To get more black whales, it's probably not possible." Slein answered truthfully.

"Is that really the case?" Pope Eugene's voice was laden with disappointment. "Time is running out. Prepare to send all the white whales into this crusade."

"All of them?" Slein nodded and continued, "Yes, this group of artificial demons will turn any Demon Lord Palace into ruins."

"Even the mutated black whale should be sent to the battlefield. We need its strength." Pope Eugene gazed through the glass at the most powerful monster being restrained.

"That's not safe. The black whale is too volatile and cannot be controlled." Slein frowned, feeling the risk was too great.

"We have no other choice. All forces that can be utilized must be sent into this crusade. Our enemy is not just a Demon Lord but a powerful ancient god." Pope Eugene paused and continued, "Even you must participate in this crusade."

"I don't have the ability to defeat an ancient god. You know that." Slein shook his head.

"The Blood Pool Seal is a miracle left by the demon race's seers, capable of even imprisoning time. With seven important nodes, the ancient god's awakening in the Demon Lord Palace must be due to the seventh Demon Lord Palace's seal being damaged." Pope Eugene thought deeply and said slowly, "I know you can't defeat the ancient god, but with your knowledge and insight, you might be able to repair the damaged seal of the seventh Demon Lord Palace. If successful, we will win this war."

"Don't worry, Alice will help you gain precious time. Even if she dies, it will cause us no loss."

The turmoil caused by the Seven Kings' Council had already passed a long time.

Other Demon Lord Palaces had gradually learned the truth, and the remaining demons were in an uproar, even wanting to join forces with Behemoth to rescue the imprisoned rulers.

Even the usually weak Milanda, upon hearing about her brother's predicament, gathered the courage to take up her sword and lead Belsebuub's subordinates to attack the Demon City.

The flames of war first ignited within the demon race, and each Demon Lord Palace began organizing forces, preparing to sound the war horn for the seventh Demon Lord Palace.

However, Behemoth had anticipated this crisis and had already made preparations.

In the Demon City, before the ruined altar.

Samiel, Asmodeus, Belsebuub, and Leviathan, the four rulers, knelt before the sky's clouds, expressing respect.

Their gazes were hollow, like empty shells with no soul, only to be manipulated.

But compared to before, the rulers' aura was much stronger, having advanced to a higher level due to the enhancement of the demon god's blood!

The sky's clouds rolled on, and Behemoth's wicked face appeared, with flames burning endlessly in his eyes.

"Go, crush all the rebels from other Demon Lord Palaces. Show no mercy to those who once served me. Only those who obey me will have a chance to live."

"As you command, our great master!"

The once proud Demon Lords spoke in unison, having completely become tools, like mindless puppets at someone's whim.

Eulogia closed her eyes and reported calmly, "The officials of the First Demon Lord Palace seem to have known the news in advance and have all secretly fled, their whereabouts unknown. Additionally, the Vatican's stock has been very active lately, and it seems they will soon come to attack you."

"Some rats ran away early, and it doesn't affect me. As for the threat from the Church?" Behemoth grinned, his fiery light illuminating the Demon City, "It's not worth worrying about. A bunch of ants don't need me to handle them personally."

As soon as his words fell, a metallic scraping sound echoed from the shadows!

Merlin, clad in the heavy demon armor once belonging to Mammon, slowly walked to the ruins of the altar.

His appearance had changed significantly. His golden hair was mixed with many white strands, his eyes were lifeless, resembling a creature without emotion.

After absorbing a large amount of demon god's blood, he had not only been enhanced to an unimaginable level but also been corrupted by the blood, with half his body turning black.

Upon closer inspection, Merlin's half-black face was grotesque, with blood vessels spreading to his temples, and his right eye, corrupted by the demon blood, emitted flames similar to Behemoth's!

Eulogia saw Merlin's current appearance, seemingly still calm, but his heart unconsciously felt a chill.

Even he had been successfully corrupted and controlled by the demon god's blood?

It seemed Behemoth had no weak points left.

The world would once again be shrouded in the shadow of the ancient god!

title: Chapter 14 — As If It Were Yesterday
content:
Chapter 14 — As If It Were Yesterday

Volume 35 · Chapter 14

The Behemoth in the sky cracked its mouth, revealing a strange evil smile, and scorching flames spewed forth. Obviously it was very satisfied with its 'masterpiece', even thinking that after Merlin was completely corroded by demon blood, it would be the substitute it had long dreamed of. 'A group of ants is coming to subjugate me; the task of guarding Demon City is entrusted to you, no problem?' The corrupted Merlin has lost his own consciousness and can only obediently follow Behemoth's commands. Merlin slowly put on his heavy helmet, completely covering his hideous appearance at this moment, his right hand lightly stroking the hilt of Banri Garan at his waist. Stimulated by the demon god's blood, it awakened its long-dormant true form—. The scorching demonic fire burned Banri Garan, instantly turning its originally bright red color to pitch black, with patterns resembling red blood vessels spreading across the scabbard. The hilt twisted under the flames, the top gradually forging a pattern like a demon. Terrifying demonic fire coiled around the blade, even gushing out from the gaps in the scabbard, filling the air and refusing to dissipate. Demonic fire is a power inherent in Behemoth's body, but after absorbing a large amount of demon god's blood, Merlin also gained the ability to control flames. Along with the forging of demonic fire, Banri Garan revealed its original form, a flame blade emitting a terrifying evil aura, its oppressive force no less than that of the demon sword Tyr's Edge, and the artifact's quality is only higher, never lower. Until this moment, the Banri Garan that had lain dormant for several epochs truly awakened. As the blade of a great prophet of the demon race, it inherently possesses power beyond ordinary imagination; legend says that when swung, the sky will be set ablaze, enemies will be completely vaporized in the high heat rather than burned to death, and even ancient gods cannot escape the demonic fire. After Merlin donned his heavy helmet and slowly lifted his head to gaze at the Behemoth in the sky, he answered—. 'Rest assured, my master, as long as I am here, no enemy can enter Demon City.' 'No matter how many enemies come, they are useless before me.' 'I don't mind turning this place into a graveyard burying countless beings...' 'Very good, this is exactly the answer I wanted to hear.' Behemoth let out a series of proud laughs, its gaze turning to the blood pool deep in the altar, where a large number of monsters crafted from demon god's blood were about to be completed. 'I still need a little time; when my servants hatch, the world will have no need for humans, elves, or dragons—demons will be the sole species.' Europa lowered his head, feeling a chill in his heart. Behemoth only needs obedient slaves; demons unwilling to be enslaved will likewise be eliminated. My father ordered me to serve this monster wholeheartedly—what for? Is it truly for the future of the demon race? 'Europa, your task is only one: guard the Demon-Sealing Vase well, understood?' 'Yes.' Europa bowed slightly, lowered his head, but the doubt in his brows grew deeper—. Besides becoming Behemoth's slave, enduring endless oppression. I cannot imagine what we will ultimately gain.

Two weeks are about to pass, in the royal capital of Britain. The first knight of the Thorns, Mersfield, pushed open the door to the queen's study. Under the guidance of the lake fairy, her strength grew ever stronger; the king's sword at her waist symbolized that she had inherited Egbert's legacy. Mersfield had already learned what had happened among the demons, as Britain had recently been invaded by demons, and she worried that the flames of war would reignite on this land. No one knows what the demons in chaos will do; if the war spreads to the kingdom, preparations must be made in advance. 'Your Majesty, the Holy City Vatican held a departure ceremony today; besides support from the southern nations, most of the northern kingdoms are merely watching and waiting.' Mersfield softly reported the recent situation. 'Are we departing today? That's fast.' Elizabeth put down her quill, pausing her work, 'How many people are going out?' 'News from the Holy City says the Templar Knights number 150,000, other southern kingdoms spontaneously formed a 120,000-strong allied army, also incorporated into the expeditionary force, plus countless unnamed giant monsters, numbers temporarily impossible to tally, not to mention magic cannons, catapults, and heavy ballistae.' Mersfield obtained a rough estimate. 'Such a massive scale, already surpassing past investments in demon subjugation; the church seems to be afraid of something? This hastily assembled force is too quick.' Elizabeth the queen pondered. 'Perhaps they want to take advantage of the demons' internal strife to wipe them out in one fell swoop.' Mersfield speculated. 'That's possible, but not long ago an eerie fire‑cloud rose in the east; I always have an ominous feeling. The demons' chaos is not simple, perhaps related to their previous sudden foreign war.' Elizabeth the queen felt helpless, unable to obtain intelligence beyond human realms, only able to guess. 'This is the demons' due retribution; they deserve the harshest punishment, perhaps as the church preaches—demons will always be humanity's greatest threat.' Mersfield said angrily, never forgetting that his father died at the hands of demons, and he has tacitly become a supporter of the church. Elizabeth slightly furrowed her brow, quickly changed the subject, not wanting to dwell on demons any longer, 'By the way, who is the hero this time?' 'Mersfield felt a bit embarrassed replying, an overseas Thorns knight, Alice Claudia.' 'Huh? She has returned to the church?' Elizabeth was momentarily speechless, not wanting to see this; Alice being merely a neutral adventurer would be fine, but now she is both a hero and an overseas Thorns knight, clearly standing at the center of the struggle between divine and royal authority.' 'Is her husband, Mr. Merlin, also by her side?' 'Ah?' Mersfield started, not understanding why Her Majesty always cares about other people's husbands—could she be interested in married women? Thus she gave a strange look and answered, 'I don't know; that sort of minor role goes unnoticed.' 'Ha, Elizabeth gave a dry laugh, feeling she had been imprudent, shouldn't have asked Mersfield, after all, Elgar the Sword Master remains a mystery to the outside world. 'Your Majesty, are we really not going to aid the church? After all we suffered demon attacks; if the church loses, aren't we in danger too?' Mersfield asked doubtfully. 'It's not that we don't support the church; only this expedition does not require it, and the number of church believers within the kingdom keeps growing, which remains a hidden danger.' Elizabeth paused, then added meaningfully—. 'I would rather see the church suffer a crushing defeat in this expedition, to pour a bucket of cold water on those radical zealots, letting them calm down.' 'You need to know, we need a lion on its last breath—we cannot let it die, nor let it grow strong.'

In the quiet depths of the temple, light dim, priests hummed the blessing chant beside, nuns clasped their hands silently praying for the hero. Pope Gaiogen sprinkled holy water with an olive branch, splashed wine on the hero; here the final pre‑departure rite was being performed. 'O righteous hero, I sincerely bless you! May you not forget the glorious mission bestowed by Goddess Mary, to dispel darkness and sow the seeds of light across the world, may you return victorious and safe! The God of Light shall forever protect you!' Alice had already bathed in the holy spring and once again donned the hero's armor inherited with the goddess's blessing. Everything before her eyes she had experienced before; recalling her naive beginnings as a hero, it still feels like yesterday. Alice lifted her head, gazing up at the towering goddess statue in the open air, though its surface bears the marks of time, the oppressive presence inevitably inspires awe—. Merlin, wait for me, I will come to rescue you right away! Although you this guy have a host of bad habits, . I will absolutely never give up on you! I have already commissioned an artist for a full‑body depiction of Merlin's demonic form, fire‑themed. I also want a half‑face picture showing the corroded visage; I don’t even have enough for the monthly ticket, you guys can check out the LO L Lucian Shadow of the West promo video to fill in the gaps, it’s fairly close. title: Chapter 15 — Vigilance (Monthly Ticket Extra)
content:
Chapter 15 — Vigilance (Monthly Ticket Extra)

Volume 35 · Chapter 15

The temple resounded with a bright hymn, and all the clergy fixed their gazes on Alice's back; the light pouring through the stained glass made her seem as if she stood amidst a sea of flowers.
In the ceiling mural, the countless eyes of the saints seemed to be watching the Hero, offering her their most sincere blessings.
Many believers thought Alice was standing devoutly before the solemn statue of the Goddess of Light, praying, unaware that her mind was filled only with rescuing her demon lover.
Pope Jiogen personally placed the cloak embroidered with the church's insignia on Alice's shoulders and gave her a heavy pat. "Now it's up to you, Alice." "Rest assured, I will do my utmost." Alice nodded, donned her helmet, took a deep breath to ease the pressure, then turned to her companions and said, "Time's up; let's set out."
Numerous Hero candidates nodded and fell in behind Alice one after another; before leaving the Holy City, there was still a grand parade, and the crusade troops needed to be neatly attired as they slowly departed along the central avenue of the Holy City.
Cardinal Sorein lowered his head, having prepared himself as a follower of this expedition; as he passed the Pope, he whispered, "I cannot guarantee I can repair the damaged blood pool, but I can try." "That will be enough," Pope Jiogen said, furtively producing a precious teleport scroll and whispering, "If you discover you cannot restore the seal, then flee quickly—don't worry about anyone else." Sorein revealed a mysterious smile, tucked away the scroll, and said, "Understood."
Ayana mi waved at Jeanne behind her, saying, "Goodbye—I never imagined you'd be ordered to guard the Holy City; what a pity, I thought we could fight side by side, await our victorious news. Though I don't think highly of Alice serving as Hero, her strength is indeed formidable."
Jeanne's face was expressionless, her spirits sunk to the depths; she had no mood to speak.
Not being chosen as Hero was bad enough, but she wasn't even given a chance to fight; just as before, she was ordered to stay and guard the Holy City.
Jeanne felt utterly despondent; in her rivalry with Alice she had never won, each time ending in utter defeat—this situation was no different from before.
Gazing at Alice's retreating back, Jeanne felt intensely unwilling; her faith wavered once more—"I am so devout, yet I receive no fair treatment, while a lowly opportunist snatches away my future—is this what I deserve?" The exalted Goddess above—does she even see my plight?
Seeing Jeanne ignore her, Ayana mi shrugged helplessly, quickened her pace to catch up with the troop, her mind filled with thoughts of how to earn merit in the crusade.
The temple's massive bronze doors were slowly pushed open, and instantly— a tremendous cheer, like a mountain‑shaking tsunami, burst in from outside, ringing in people's ears. The Holy City's populace greeted the Hero with an enthusiasm beyond imagination, tossing handfuls of flower petals into the air to pave the road for the departing crusade. Alice stared for a moment; the sight of the crowds seeing her off, far more fervent than before, made her—who had been placed under great expectations—feel a faint pressure.
Suddenly, an ethereal low roar echoed across the Holy City's sky, and numerous artificial magic‑created white whales, haloed, glided through the air. People assumed they were messengers sent by the Goddess of Light to the mortal realm, unaware of how many human lives had been sacrificed to bring them into being. The white whales were bound in chains that interwove into a gigantic iron net, with the mutated black whale at its center. To prevent this mutated beast from suddenly running amok, several spikes had been driven through its jaws beforehand, silencing its angry roar so as not to disrupt the crucial departure ceremony. The black whale's power was astonishing; it took the white whales pulling together on their chains to restrain it, otherwise it would have already rampaged above the Holy City. Countless magic cannons and siege engines were pushed onto the streets by the temple knights, slowly moving outward from the Holy City.
This unprecedented, largest crusade force officially began its march, yet many knights and soldiers remained unaware of what dangers lay ahead.
Among the crowd, the four demons—Helena, Pluton, Dulux, and Blackman—were waving to Alice. They had decided to accompany her on this crusade, while Lilith, Ophelia, and Xiu chose to remain in the Holy City to look after Chris for a while.
In fact, Alice did not want them to follow, because many in the crusade were church members and the demons' identities were too perilous; a slip would expose them. If any demons were discovered in the ranks, not only would Helena and her companions surely die, but Alice would also find it hard to explain herself, likely being charged with colluding with the demon race and burned at the stake.
This was all Lilith's decision; she simply did not trust Alice, fearing that this human woman would not spare no effort to rescue her brother, and therefore she had arranged for a few demons to trail Alice, at least to serve as watchers.
The demons hidden among the crowd had already concealed

title: Chapter 16 — Approaching the Demon Castle
content:
Chapter 16 — Approaching the Demon Castle

Volume 35 · Chapter 16

Cardinal Srein's gaze was sharp, sensing something unusual about the people around Alice. Compared to the surrounding residents who were enthusiastically cheering, they seemed cold—clearly not the attitude expected of Holy City citizens.

Alice was so scared her whole body trembled, stiffly turning her head around, her heart pounding. Had they been discovered? Bringing demons into the Holy City was indeed too dangerous! What should she do? What excuse could she use to muddle through? This cardinal probably wouldn't be easy to fool!

The demons raised their heads, staring at Srein with hostile eyes. If he could see through their disguises, he was clearly no ordinary person.

Alice was so nervous she started stammering. "We are Miss Alice's friends, and also adventurers from Britain," Pudom stepped forward pretending to be calm, lying without even blinking. "I heard the demon race has been in turmoil, threatening the safety of human realms. We recently experienced a demon attack and deeply understand the harm demons pose to all humanity. Therefore, to protect our shared home, we followed Miss Alice to the Holy City hoping to join the extermination team. Slaying brutal demons is our shared mission!"

"? ? ?" Alice looked at Pudom in shock, thinking: This demon who looked like a bookworm was so quick-witted at a critical moment, able to spout such nonsense!

"Hmm?" Srein frowned, somewhat moved by these words, but still asked suspiciously, "Alice, are all the things he said true?"

"Ah..." Alice barely recovered, finding herself in a difficult spot, she could only nod heavily. "Yes, yes, they are all my adventurer friends."

"Adventurers?" Srein narrowed his eyes, scanning the several demons in disguise, his mind wavering, unable to confirm if the evil aura he had just sensed was wrong.

"Impossible? You won't give us a chance to revenge against the demons? That's too cruel! My sister was killed by demons in the Britain defense battle! She was only seven!" Pudom looked grief-stricken, frequently pounding his own chest, pointing at the other demons and saying— "This guy! Don't look how strong he is, he's an idiot! Only son in nine generations! In the war the demons played tricks on him, his manhood was cut off! His family is doomed to extinction!"

"Me?" Blackman was completely baffled, his eye twitching from anger. Under pressure, he had no choice but to cross his eyes, grabbing his arm and trembling all over, calling out foolishly, "Aba ababa baba!"

"He! Although he's cold like a killer now, before he was different—an open and warm person! Raised by his single mother from young, but demons took away his only relative. Losing his mother and becoming an orphan made him grief-stricken and his mind started becoming abnormal!"

"I'm an orphan? Ah right, I'm mom-less..." Duru lowered his head gloomily, veins bulging on his forehead, picking up the poison-coated chain beneath his black cloak, wanting to stab Pudom right there and then!

"This beauty! She..." Helena's heart skipped a beat, suspecting she'd also be assigned some ridiculous soap opera backstory by Pudom, so she secretly kicked him hard.

"Ah!" Pudom cried out in pain, his foot burning, face turning red instantly. "She... she is a devout believer. Participating in the sacred extermination battle was always her dream!"

Helena breathed a slight sigh of relief, glad she hadn't been assigned some dead relative, born with a congenital deficiency backstory—that would have been an insult to her.

"We all have reasons to revenge against demons! Can't you give us a chance to personally slay demons? We absolutely won't be a burden! Please consider!" Pudom lowered his head, lowering his posture, appearing extremely humble, but thinking: What? So many people who believe in the Goddess of Light here, the Church's con artists are always hypocritical, they definitely won't openly do something that damages their image, leading humans to complete the revenge against demons script, impossible to refuse!

"What is Pudom doing? Alice couldn't figure it out. What's the use of making up these lies?" After hearing this, the Holy City residents couldn't help but start whispering among themselves, their eyes showing sympathy— "Such pitiful people, the great Goddess should give them salvation." "Yeah, I heard demons invaded the Kingdom of Britain a few months ago, many died." "Demons are too cruel. If we don't exterminate them all, who knows who will suffer next?" The surrounding gazes put pressure on Srein. If he refused this group, it might negatively impact the Church? Plus they were Alice's adventurer friends, they should be useful.

"Clearing his throat! I sympathize with your plight. The Church's gates are not only open to devout believers but forever open to every human. We welcome all like-minded friends to join the demon extermination team. This is a mission for humanity's continued prosperity. I gladly accept your goodwill. May the Goddess's light be with you all!"

As soon as he finished, enthusiastic applause erupted from the crowd. The Holy City residents were immersed in the harmonious dream woven by the Church—this was the religion they loved. The demons showed slight smiles on their faces, having successfully blended in. As Pudom had predicted, the hypocritical clergymen cared greatly about their image of greatness and righteousness in the people's eyes.

"Alice, since they are your friends, then it's up to you to arrange things," Srein said seriously. "Okay." Alice nodded, her heart still pounding.

Cardinal Srein rode his black warhorse, continuing onward, leading the team out of the Holy City, but his mind was filled with doubts— Are these guys really adventurers? They aren't even wearing adventurer credentials. Is it because they're afraid participating in the extermination battle would break the adventurers' neutrality rules? But since Alice acknowledged them as friends, there doesn't seem to be much to suspect about their identities. What about that evil aura just now? Could they be practicing dark magic or martial arts? Though it might be my illusion, I can't be careless. I need to pay more attention to these people of unknown origin.

Alice let out a breath, saying displeasedly, "You almost got me killed." "Didn't I not cause you any trouble either?" Pudom said triumphantly. "Who's the idiot?" "Who's the orphan?" Blackman and Duru came over, their faces very ugly. If not for more important matters, Pudom would have been bedridden for months.

"Who's taking care of Chris?" Alice asked worriedly. "It's Princess Lilith. She, along with Shu and Ophelia, will take good care of her," Helena answered. "Can they handle it? I'm a bit worried," Alice said with an ugly expression, recalling Lilith's petty face. "Don't worry, Ophelia has rich experience taking care of children. With her here, there won't be any problems," Pudom answered seriously, after all, Ophelia took care of Merlin and Lilith since childhood.

"Alright, don't let your guard down. After joining the extermination team, your risk of exposure is equally high." Alice warned with a stern face, not wanting to completely break with the Church before rescuing Merlin.

After nearly two months, the dusty extermination team crossed multiple southern kingdoms and grandly arrived at the perilous Eastern Sand Sea. This was demon territory, belonging to the Seventh Demon Lord Palace's master, Berial's domain. It was filled with poison insects and illusions; the hanging sun could burn the knights' armor scorching hot. The extermination team rested overnight on the outskirts, and at dawn the next day, they resolutely entered the Sand Sea to search for the hidden Demon City. Originally the Sand Sea was a dead end with no exit, but with the Church's full preparation, the largest extermination team in history advanced like breaking bamboo! The elite Church army of nearly 300,000 people continuously approached the core area where the Demon City was located.

title: Chapter 17 — Assault (Bonus)
content:
Chapter 17 — Assault (Bonus)

Volume 35 · Chapter 17

The Sea of Sand is a natural barrier of Demon City, itself an extremely dangerous area; the Seventh Demon Lord Palace located in the city is the safest place for the demons and also the most well‑preserved. The poisonous insects hiding in the sand are extraordinarily ferocious; their danger is no less than that of demons, and they are even harder to guard against, easily causing the death of any humans who enter here. Although the mighty crusade army had made many preparations, after entering the Sea of Sand for seventeen days, the death toll among knights and soldiers rose to thirty thousand! Most of them died from bites of poisonous insects such as scorpions and snakes; they did not die at the hands of demons but in the mouths of insects, their flesh and bones buried under layers of yellow sand. Besides frequent ambushes by poisonous insects, an even more dangerous situation followed—The temperature difference between day and night in the Sea of Sand is extreme; at night it is like Greenland's eternal permafrost that never melts, so cold that one can die in their sleep. When daytime arrives, the Sea of Sand instantly transforms into a furnace capable of evaporating one's soul, roasting the knights and soldiers into a daze, and even touching their armor can cause burns. Moreover, the supplies the crusade army brought into the Sea of Sand have run out, causing extreme shortages of food and water; recently, the knights have frequently engaged in bloody fights over these precious resources. Accompanying the despair, panic, and death, a plague silently spread through the ranks, invisibly threatening and depriving the soldiers of their lives. Compared to dying from insect poison, the devastation brought by the harsh environment over the next few days will only grow worse. This place is practically a natural graveyard prepared for the invading enemies; countless Holy Temple Knights will be buried here.

At a certain location in the Sea of Sand, the crusade army had temporarily set up camp to rest; the warriors had eaten the last of their food and water, and if they could not find more supplies, hunger alone would be enough to annihilate this massive force—no need for the demons to lift a finger. “This is my food! You've already finished yours!” “Bullshit! It's clearly mine! You're forcing me to kill you!” Two Holy Temple Knights fought over a loaf of bread in front of everyone, even drawing their waist swords. Even worse, some lay on the ground licking the droplets of water that had fallen into the sand, their exhausted appearance as if they could die of thirst at any moment. “Tsk tsk, these guys are hopeless; they seem utterly useless. Most will die in this desert, those of mid‑rank and above might barely survive thanks to their physical abilities, while the low‑rank will be tortured to death in the coming days. How many will remain?” Du Lu said gloomily, watching the Holy Temple Knights in this state, feeling quite pleased. “If we can still have a force of 150,000 to fight the demons, that would already be quite good.” Budum paused, speaking in a teasing tone, “The Church has greatly underestimated the danger of the Sea of Sand; now they are reaping what they sowed.” “Our First Demon Lord Palace lacks such geographical advantages; otherwise, we would be far safer than now.” Buchakeman sighed.

Inside the temporary tent, Cardinal Sclein looked at the map of the Sea of Sand, his face ashen with anger, and he tore it into pieces in his fury. The crusade army had actually gotten lost in the Sea of Sand; they had tried every method, but still could not find the correct direction. Now Sclein finds himself in a dilemma: if he wants to flee, there is no exit; if he wants to attack, he cannot locate Demon City. Whether advancing or retreating, they face the danger of the crusade army being wiped out by the Church; moreover, the situation is fraught with difficulties—the torment of poisonous insects and harsh conditions, but the most deadly is the lack of food and water. Strong individuals can hold out for a while, but the low‑ranking warriors cannot; they likely cannot endure even seven days. “We haven't even formally engaged the demons yet, and already over thirty thousand have died; now our supplies are completely exhausted, we're at a dead end.” Alice frowned, feeling a great headache. “We are trapped here; we must find a way to save ourselves.” Perhaps Sclein lowered his head and said solemnly, “We should turn back, gather more supplies, and then try again. I am worried that before we find Demon City, the warriors will already be unable to hold on.” “Thinking about this, Alice considered that to save Merlin she needed the Church's help; with casualties so massive, she could not accept it.” Helena lifted her head, worried; she knew very well the army's position, already quite close to Demon City—if they marched for three more days, they would surely catch sight of Demon City; she had once followed Asmodeus here, leaving some impression in her mind. “Well, wanting to go back the way we came—isn't that a bit of a pity? Besides, we've lost our sense of direction; whether we can leave smoothly is still unknown.” Sclein lifted his head, fixing his gaze on Helena's eyes, and said, “We cannot be certain we will find Demon City, but we can be certain that within a few days many will starve to death; the loss is enormous. That the Holy Temple Knights did not die on the battlefield fighting demons is an unparalleled humiliation.” *Demon City will definitely have abundant food and water; otherwise, how would the demons of the Seventh Demon Lord Palace survive? If we find and capture Demon City, all problems will be resolved.* Helena did not want to give up now. Alice glanced at Helena, faintly sensing that Demon City was already near; otherwise, she would not have felt alarmed just because the Cardinal showed reluctance to retreat. “I also think we should continue searching; we have no retreat, the wind and sand have covered our tracks when we came in, and even returning the same way might not let us escape this barren desert. Rather than waste away, why not stake everything on finding Demon City?” “But where exactly is Demon City? We have been wandering aimlessly in the Sea of Sand for over half a month; continuing to search deeper is too risky.” Sclein did not want to see the crusade army lose many warriors; now he hasn't even seen a shadow of the ancient demon god, and he is about to break down under the harsh environment. “Don't give up!” Helena sprang to her feet, blurting out in desperation, “We will find Demon City; as long as we keep exploring in our current direction, we will surely have results within three days!” The atmosphere inside the tent instantly turned eerie, silent to the point of being frightening—— Alice stared wide-eyed in shock, panic rising in her mind; “Idiot! You said too much! The Cardinal will realize something is wrong!” “Uh!” Helena's whole body shuddered; she instinctively covered her mouth, thinking it was all her fault for wanting so badly to save the master in the pot; seeing the crusade army suddenly want to give up made her flustered, and in speaking too much she made mistakes and exposed a flaw! Cardinal Sclein narrowed his eyes and questioned, “Miss Helena, why are you so certain? You're not an adventurer, are you?” “Ah, that's right, I am an adventurer; I once came here on a mission and even saw Demon City, though I did not approach it.” Helena explained nervously. “Oh?” Sclein's brows knit tightly, the suspicion in his eyes growing stronger, and he began to think. She is lying; she truly does not know what an adventurer is. A genuine normal adventurer would refuse risk and would not willingly step into such dangerous demon territory. Why is she lying? And why is she so certain that Demon City is nearby? Humans could not possibly have come here; therefore, the answer can only be one. Demon! Sclein's expression turned playful; even his gaze toward Alice changed considerably, his tone full of killing intent as he probed, “Miss Helena, .”

Boom—— A sudden loud roar shattered the tense atmosphere inside the tent, and chaotic cries erupted outside one after another. “Demons! They're demons! They've come!” “Alert! Full alert!”

title: Chapter 18 — Lion's Roar
content:
Chapter 18 — Lion's Roar

Volume 35 · Chapter 18

"Alert! Everyone, alert!"

At the shout, the Temple Knights on site immediately sprang to attention, stopping their scuffles over food and grabbing the weapons at hand, preparing for combat.

Far off, massive clouds of yellow sand were whipped up, churning through the air as the billowing dust drifted in every direction. Judging from the size of them, something colossal was clearly lurking deep within the desert.

The panicked humans were nearly driven mad by the harsh desert environment; their nerves had been stretched taut as a single thread, ready to snap at the slightest disturbance, and they'd mistaken this for a sudden demon incursion!

Though exhausted, hungry, and fatigued to the bone, the well-trained Temple Knights hoisted their heavy shields imbued with sacred power and bravely held the front line, forming an immovable human wall.

"It's the aura of demons, but it feels somewhat unusual," Duluo said, his brow furrowed as he kept watch in all directions.

"The feeling of that aura..." Blackman shivered, sensing the pressure pressing down upon his very bloodline.

"It strongly resembles the scent of the First Generation demons, doesn't it? I have a similar feeling," Pudom said, forcefully suppressing his inner restlessness. The invading demons were closer to the Creator in terms of their bloodline than they were!

The Temple Knights holding their large shields faced the surging sandstorm. Though their faces showed no fear, cold sweat had already soaked through their backs. They lowered their bodies and let out a unified roar—

"Haaah!"

The shields enhanced by sacred power blazed with brilliant radiance, and in an instant they merged into one, forming a magnificent wall of light to block all evil forces!

BOOM—

Thunderous noise erupted as yellow sand flew wildly across the sky!

The sacred light wall violently trembled, visibly cracking with dense spiderweb fractures!

The Temple Knights were thoroughly shocked. Their defensive formation of giant shields should have been capable of withstanding a fierce swarm of ordinary magical beasts, yet after just one strike it was on the verge of collapsing. The attacking enemy must have been at least Saint-tier!

Outside the light wall, the rolling dust settled, and from deep within the yellow sand, a pitch-black monster suddenly burst forth—a monstrous visage so horrifying that even the Temple Knights sucked in their breath!

A demon resembling a scorpion erupted from the ground, wildly swinging its two iron pincers!

Its upper body was demonic, with horns entirely composed of flames on its head, completely unlike any normal demon.

Its lower body was that of a massive black scorpion, its eight legs clicking loudly against the ground with a "click-clack-click" sound that sent chills down the spine!

The scorpion's stinger at the end of its tail glowed with a terrifying cold gleam, and crimson venom dripped from its tip, corroding the sand beneath it into pitch-black pits.

"Who is that? A demon executive from the Seventh Demon Lord Palace?" Blackman muttered in confusion.

"Impossible. I've never heard of an executive with scorpion traits in the Seventh Demon Lord Palace," Duluo replied with certainty.

Pudom frowned deeply, thinking to himself: this is wrong! A demon with flame horns was unheard of! Where did it come from?

The demon with a scorpion's body was indeed the product created by the Scorpion Behemoth in the blood pool, having inherited part of an ancient Fiend God's power and bloodline. It wasn't strange that it emitted an aura similar to the First Generation demons.

The scorpion demon turned toward the humans hiding behind the light wall and let out a ferocious roar, breathing out fierce demonic fire from its eyes and nostrils—as if there was no blood within its body at all.

The Temple Knights holding their shields paled and instinctively stepped back.

But the enemy would not give them a chance to flee. The scorpion demon swayed its tail, and its stinger plunged viciously into the indestructible light wall!

Craaaack—the massive light wall was further damaged, and under the stinger's assault, it shattered into countless points of light in the blink of an eye.

The scorpion demon swept through as though no one were there, beginning its killing spree. With a single swing of its steel-like pincers, it crushed the internal organs of armored Temple Knights and could effortlessly bisect them at the waist.

"Splat!"

One unfortunate soul was struck by the scorpion demon's stinger, and his body immediately ignited from the inside out, consumed alive by flames until he was reduced to a pile of ash.

Against a Saint-tier demon, these ordinary Temple Knights were no match at all—they were like lambs waiting to be slaughtered.

"Stand aside!" Ayunami arrived, his expression grave. "Leave this to me!"

Seeing Ayunami step forward, the Temple Knights scattered and surrounded the demon, clearly placing their trust in this Inquisitor.

"Hmph, foolish humans. At a time like this, you should use an army surge to overwhelm the enemy rather than choosing one-on-one combat," Duluo sneered.

"Isn't that just what humans love to do? I think they call it... noble knightly spirit or something," Blackman grinned.

Ayunami strode toward the scorpion demon, assuming a fighting stance, and beckoned at the enemy with his finger—

"Come on, filthy demon!"

"Gogogogo—"

The scorpion demon let out a grotesque sound from its throat, enraged by the feeble humans, and charged at them with all eight legs spiraling forward.

Its enormous iron pincers swung wildly, smashing toward Ayunami with murderous intent!

Ayunami's gaze hardened, his golden Saint-tier battle aura surging through his body, unleashing the Roar of the Lion!

His legs drove hard into the ground, his body becoming a blur as he charged courageously at the scorpion demon.

Using his agile body, he dodged the demon's iron pincers and unleashed a barrage of rapid-fire blows in return!

Fierce fist winds exploded through the air, shaking the scorpion demon's entire body until it trembled uncontrollably, unable to counterattack, as the Lion's Roar rang out again and again!

Enraged beyond measure, the scorpion demon raised both pincers and smashed down hard, but Ayunami had anticipated this. He leapt from the ground, then lightly stepped onto the demon's twin pincers as deftly as a dragonfly skimming water!

"It's over!"

Twisting his body in a spinning motion, Ayunami attacked like a lion king pouncing on its prey, delivering a devastating kick that sent the scorpion demon's head flying clean off!

Blood dyed the yellow sand red, and the decapitated demon swayed unsteadily before its headless corpse collapsed to the ground with a thunderous crash.

Seeing the demon defeated, cheers and applause erupted around them, praising Ayunami's extraordinary strength for defeating a high-ranking demon executive single-handedly.

Ayunami turned around, spread his arms wide to graciously accept all the praise, even bowing in thanks as though slaying the demon were merely a performance.

Just as everyone was immersed in the joy of victory, the decapitated scorpion demon silently rose again, its stinger pointed directly at Ayunami, who was still enjoying the acclaim.

At such close range, even if Ayunami reacted in time, there was no escape—it was a death sentence!

"Heh heh heh." Duluo let out a gloomy laugh, a mocking expression crossing his face as he spoke to himself.

"Foolish humans, why do you insist on showing off like that?"

"You put on a dazzling display, but your track record says otherwise—"

"Hehe~"

I'm dealing with a typhoon here, and my residence and surrounding area are flooded. The power's out, and the 4G base station seems to be having issues too—I need to walk over two hundred meters just to get a signal on my phone. I'm not at home; I'm updating from another location using my phone. No signal is killing me.

My power bank is still half charged, so I should be able to write a chapter and do an extra update. If the power's still not back tomorrow, things could get pretty serious.

Food delivery and restaurants are all closed, and there's standing water everywhere around my place. I've already finished the bread I got from the front desk, and my drinking water isn't enough either. This is really uncomfortable.

The key thing is, I'm a northerner and I'm not used to wearing slippers. If I had slippers, I'd just wade through it.

If the power's still out tomorrow, I'll be ditching these loafers I'm wearing—hilarious~
