title: Chapter 19 — The Wall of Sighs (Monthly Ticket Bonus Update)
content:
Chapter 19 — The Wall of Sighs (Monthly Ticket Bonus Update)

Volume 35 · Chapter 19

Ayanami was fully immersed in the taste of victory, not noticing the danger approaching from behind at all.

This was his first time participating in a war to hunt demons; he didn't truly understand demons at all, and had only ever heard about the demon race from his seniors—

They were usually fierce and brutal, fond of slaughter and conquest, possessing extremely formidable power, as well as racial talents no worse than dragons.

Against such evil creatures, one should avoid fighting alone at the same tier; it was best to have two people fight together to reliably kill them.

This was Ayanami's impression of demons, entirely from the oral accounts of seniors who had survived demon-hunting battles. Though somewhat exaggerated, it was the best advice for the young—at least it would prevent them from sacrificing themselves so easily in battle against demons.

Yet Ayanami had forgotten this point; his desire to make a name for himself in this demon-hunting battle drove him to act recklessly.

Ayanami had single-handedly defeated a demon whose power rivaled that of an executive, and the easy victory had gone to his head, inflating his confidence. He believed demons weren't as powerful as imagined, or perhaps he himself was simply too strong—his years of arduous training had paid off. What terrifying demons? Their power wasn't that great, right? Maybe the Demon Lord wasn't that strong either, just a hollow shell.

Was Jeanne deliberately exaggerating to scare me, so I'd voluntarily give up my chance to become the Hero?

Ayanami was still basking in his self-satisfaction, but others had already noticed the headless scorpion demon standing back up and launching a sneak attack from behind, so they shouted warnings.

"Ayanami! Watch your back!"

"Hm? ?"

When Ayanami turned around, he saw the scorpion demon's venomous stinger already thrust at his face. With his abilities, there was almost no way to dodge this fatal strike!

His pupils constricted sharply, staring at the incoming stinger as tendrils of crimson venom surged. His mind went blank—This is impossible! How could it still move without a head?

No one had ever told him that demons possessed such tenacious vitality!

As death loomed, Ayanami closed his eyes and finally recalled his seniors' advice, but it was too late. The poison would burn through his body, and with just three breaths, he would become a pile of ash.

In the blink of an eye!

A figure suddenly rushed over, faster than the stinger descending by countless times? The distance to Ayanami's death was merely two fingers' width, yet this person still managed to arrive in time!

When Ayanami opened his eyes, he saw the red-robed Cardinal Srein blocking in front of him, pinching the scorpion demon's venomous stinger with two fingers. The crimson venom couldn't even damage his skin.

"Cardinal Srein?!"

"Disappear, lowly evil creature."

Srein didn't even turn his head. His seemingly frail, elderly body seemed to possess power surpassing all else. Every movement radiated the aura of an experienced demon hunter—confidence so powerful that young Ayanami could never compare.

The headless scorpion demon's body rapidly swelled and exploded into a stinking mass of flesh and blood. Without any fight, the moment their eyes met, the powerful Saint-tier demon dropped dead!

The Holy Knights present fell completely silent, unable to utter a word. The demons they had fought tooth and nail against were, before Srein, no different from babies casually pinched to death. This made them wonder if their existence was even necessary.

"Did you see clearly?" Podom asked in a low voice, sweat pouring down his face.

"No, I saw nothing. Not even the pressure of battle aura. He hid too well, not a single flaw exposed. I can't even figure out how that Saint-tier demon died just now."

Blackman swallowed nervously, adding, "You can't tell his power level at all. The way he killed the demon was quite skillful. To be honest, I'm a bit scared."

"That old fellow is unfathomable. At the very least, he possesses power to rival the Demon Lord. If we faced him, could he give me a chance to surrender?" Tyrul, who normally bowed to no one but Merlin, was even frightened by him. The terror of Srein had deeply shaken him.

"We'd better be careful. The red-robed cardinals who participated in hunts before were all useless chatterboxes, but this one is different!" Podom felt his legs trembling, his eyes full of caution.

Cardinal Srein turned around, his face grim, and questioned, "Haven't I taught you? Ayanami, never let your guard down until a demon is truly dead. You nearly paid with your life for your foolishness. I hope you'll reflect on yourself."

"I'm terribly sorry, Cardinal Srein! This is all my fault!" Ayanami quickly lowered his head, his face burning, feeling his dignity utterly shattered before everyone.

When Alice and Helena arrived, they found the commotion had ended. The demon's blood had already begun to solidify in the desert sand.

Srein had no patience to fuss with Ayanami. His piercing gaze swept over everyone as he announced loudly—

"Depart at first light tomorrow. Continue deeper into the desert sea. Rest well tonight—this may be our last respite."

Helena secretly sighed with relief. Good thing the hunting party hadn't given up halfway, or who knew when the plan to rescue the sealed Demon Lord would succeed?

Srein's meaningful gaze swept over Alice and the others, especially those mysterious newcomers—

I never expected demons to have the audacity to infiltrate the Holy City, even mixing into the hunting party?

What scheme could they be plotting? Trying to lure us into a trap for massacre? Very likely.

But they probably don't know I've already identified them. Better to play along, pretend to be ignorant for now, and use them to find the Demon City.

My goal is singular: find the Demon City, repair the damaged seal, and prevent the ancient demonic god from threatening the Church's safety.

If the Demon City isn't found within three days, none of these scoundrels will escape—including Alice.

Daring to betray the Church and consort with demons—she must pay in blood!

Time passed quickly. At noon on the third day, after a long march, the grand hunting party finally discovered the Demon City hidden in the desert sea—a vast ancient city built upon an oasis.

The white whales in the sky let out long cries. Clearly, they had sensed the aura of powerful demons emanating from the distant black city!

"Cardinal Srein, look! We found it!" Ayanami shouted excitedly. These past few days he'd been worried about not finding it; without food and water, escaping the desert would be incredibly difficult.

"Is this the Demon City?" Alice gazed into the distance, glancing at Helena beside her.

Helena secretly nodded, confirming the news. The hunting party had arrived at the city where the Seventh Demon Lord Palace was located.

"It doesn't seem like a mirage illusion. Should be correct." Srein put down his telescope, his mood somewhat agitated. He could finally complete the task the Pope had assigned.

Yet the Demon City, lonely in the desert sea, was eerily quiet—not a single trace of demons. This unusual situation made everyone uneasy.

Looking out, the Demon City and the hunting party seemed like tiny black ants, drawing the warriors' attention.

I bet all the Holy Knights couldn't imagine that the tiny ant standing in the distance—

Was none other than Lucifer III, who made them tremble with fear!

And also the Wall of Sighs, which they could never pass through.

Brother, are you there? Any...

title: Chapter 20 — Standoff
content:
Chapter 20 — Standoff

Volume 35 · Chapter 20

Alice gazed at the Demon City, her heart restless with desire. Was the Demon Sealing Flask inside that city? As long as she shattered it, Merlin would be saved—but—
The place was unnaturally quiet. Why, with the Crusade Army at their doorstep, were the enemies in the Demon City showing no reaction? Had they set a trap to "welcome" them?

The situation before them made the Crusade Army hesitate, unwilling to launch a rash assault on the Demon City.

Ordinary commanders, driven to the brink of madness by the desert, would find it hard to resist the temptation of a Demon City built upon an oasis and refrain from attacking.

Even many Crusade soldiers found themselves swallowing saliva unconsciously—the Demon City in the distance surely held the food and water they dreamed of; if they could occupy it, everyone could survive the desert.

But this time the commander was Red Cardinal Sreyn, a harsh ascetic who was cruel enough to himself—no matter what torment he faced, his inhuman will was hard to shake.

Sreyn was notorious in the Church for his caution; he considered things more deeply than others, possessing not only abundant knowledge but also an uncommon calmness.

The calmer the situation appeared, the more Sreyn suspected it; until the circumstances were clear, even if all the Templars starved to death here, he would not order a full-scale assault on the Demon City—

He had not expected that those fellows pretending to be adventurers would honestly lead them to the Demon City?

So that was it—they were the group of demons the Pope had mentioned, unwilling to be enslaved by the ancient demon god and wanting to fight to the death.

In a sense, these demons were not the enemies of this crusade, but allies instead.

But wanting to use our strength to defeat the ancient demon god—such scheming was too cunning.

Forget it. These demons' power was negligible, their impact on the situation almost zero, and they had a bit of use value. They must know more about the Blood Pool Seal than I did; repairing the Blood Pool required their assistance.

After everything was settled, it wouldn't be too late to settle accounts with them. And of course, there was Alice—perhaps in his lifetime, he would see the first Hero in history burned at the stake.

"What's that? It looks like someone's there!" Ayanamo made a new discovery, pointing in a direction.

Yellow sand filled the air; between the Crusade Army and the Demon City, a tiny figure flickered in and out of sight.

Sreyn immediately picked up his telescope. As the layers of sand were blown away by the wind, a bizarre man wearing demon armor and carrying a black long sword at his waist was vaguely revealed, standing there like a statue without moving.

"That demon?"

"Hmm?"

Alice followed Ayanamo's pointing direction and saw that man too, but she couldn't recognize him as Merlin.

Because Merlin was completely hidden beneath the demon armor, his face not revealed at all, and the Banri Garan at his waist had changed its appearance entirely.

But Alice could still recall the armor's original owner—the Demon Lord who had nearly destroyed Britain, Mamen.

"Uh! That—"

"Strange," Podom lowered his head and muttered quietly, "Mamen isn't dead, is he? Who put on his armor?"

"Couldn't be Mamen's subordinate?" Blackman speculated.

"Impossible. Unless the demons of the Third Demon Lord Palace have submitted to Behemoth, I can't imagine the seven Demon Lord Palaces of the demon race being completely suppressed in such a short time." Dulu was convinced the guy in the demon armor couldn't be Mamen's old subordinate.

"That sword—" Podom stared at the weapon at the enemy's waist, feeling like he had seen it in some ancient book, but couldn't recall it for the moment. Plus, the distance was too great to see clearly.

Alice looked at Helena beside her, hoping for an answer.

But Helena shook her head slightly, indicating she didn't know either.

Alice frowned, suspecting whether the dead Mamen had revived? If they wanted to attack the Demon City, they would definitely be unable to get past this opponent.

"The surroundings are very quiet, it seems there are no traps or ambushes, really only this one demon," Sreyn confirmed the surroundings and couldn't help laughing, "The other party wants to single-handedly block our nearly three-hundred-thousand-strong Crusade Army and protect the Demon City behind him. Too crazy. This is almost impossible. Who could have such confidence?"

As Sreyn said, only Merlin himself was defending the Demon City; he didn't need any support at all.

Facing the largest crusade army in history, for Merlin, it was merely a matter of swinging his slaughter knife a few more times.

"Maybe he's bluffing, using this bizarre strategy to try to scare us," Ayanamo thought, completely failing to learn from the previous days' lessons, believing it was only his own momentary carelessness that caused the embarrassment; demons weren't as powerful as imagined.

"No, the ones capable of such crazy actions are only two types: one is a thoroughgoing madman, the other is a confident strongman. Either way, the other party had the courage to block us alone; one had to admire that courage." Sreyn spoke in a low voice, his heart swaying left and right, unable to make up his mind.

"What should we do?"

"Hold position."

Five hours passed. Without Sreyn's order, no one dared to move rashly.

But the scorching sun hung high in the sky, about to sink below the horizon, yet Sreyn still refused to launch an attack, even though there was only one enemy in front of the Demon City.

The Templars were already dying of thirst and hunger, mentally exhausted, nearly three days without a drop of water, feeling that even spitting would be the strongest bitter coffee.

After the unbearable heat came the bone-chilling cold of night; the crusade soldiers probably couldn't hold on any longer.

Sreyn didn't blink, observing the enemy's every move, hoping for a perfect opportunity, but Merlin, eroded by demonic blood, had no flaws, making him extremely annoyed—

Madman or strongman?

If madman, we would charge into the Demon City with overwhelming advantage.

But if strongman, we might be annihilated entirely, losing all chance to defeat the ancient demon god.

Why did that guy have no flaws at all, like a straw man without a soul?

"Lord Sreyn! Order the attack! We can't hold out any longer! Without food and water, everyone might not live past the day after tomorrow! This must be a demonic plot—we hope to be buried in this cursed place without having to fight!" Ayanamo couldn't bear it anymore, stood up and shouted, "If you're worried the enemy poses a huge threat, why not send a knight to probe them?"

"Hmm?" Sreyn's heart stirred; his gaze fell on Alice and the demons mixed in the army, a cunning smile appearing on his face, "Well then, how about—"

"Let me go and probe them! Please believe in my ability!" Ayanamo volunteered, thinking full of confidence—

This was a good chance to wash away the shame of the past few days; I could finally regain a little dignity.

Standing still for so long, he must be a bluff.

Let me rip off his disguise and let everyone see their own stupidity. I bet even Lord Sreyn would look at me with new eyes!

title: Chapter 21 — Ignorant
content:
Chapter 21 — Ignorant

Volume 35 · Chapter 21

"???"

Cardinal Serein was dumbfounded on the spot, caught off guard by Ayanami's self-volunteering. This was completely different from what he had expected.

He had originally planned to have Alice and those demons who had infiltrated the party go probe the situation first, to reduce his side's losses. But this rash Ayanami had jumped out excitedly, eager to take on this important responsibility.

If the figure in demon armor was truly powerful, then Ayanami's actions were equivalent to courting death.

However, the current situation was very unfavorable to the expeditionary force. They couldn't just sit around waiting here—someone had to go scout out the enemy's true strength.

The temple knights around them, ignorant of the full situation, not only failed to stop him but actually praised Ayanami, giving a thumbs-up for his courage.

"As expected of a Hero候补, so reliable!"

"Ayanami should be able to handle this without any problems."

"Maybe it's really just the demons bluffing to scare us!"

Ayanami couldn't help but feel pleased and wanted to seize this opportunity to make a good impression, to win back all the face he had lost yesterday. If he could expose the demons' tricks, that would also be a major contribution.

In fact, Serein was already beginning to view Ayanami with new eyes, startled by his abnormal level of stupidity.

Serein's face was grim, his dark gaze carrying a hint of anger. He desperately wanted to slap some sense into this ambitious yet foolish subordinate.

What a hopeless fool—why is he so eager to step on a landmine and court death?

This expedition should have brought Joanne instead of this kid!

He had taught her so much, yet she hadn't learned a single thing!

Serein closed his eyes, feeling profoundly disappointed. He had lost all patience with Ayanami. He wasn't a babysitter responsible for looking after little kids.

"Since you're so eager to go, then go."

"Thank you, Lord Serein! Rest assured, I have already completed my mission!"

Ayanami answered with full confidence, his gaze turning toward the mysterious demon in armor standing motionless in the distance. He thought to himself—

Here comes my chance to earn merit. No matter what bluffing strategy the other side is using, I'll expose it!

The expeditionary force continued to wait in place while Ayanami walked alone toward the Merlin clad in demon armor, a hint of unease in his heart.

Ayanami secretly infused his aura throughout his body. To the outside world he looked the same as usual, but inwardly he was like a lion with its fur bristling—ready to react a step faster if danger arose.

After arriving in front of Merlin, Ayanami took a long look before steeling himself to speak.

"Hey! Are you still alive?"

The heavy helmet tilted slightly upward, clearly indicating Merlin had noticed the young man before him. But he remained silent and offered no response.

"Why aren't you talking? You damn demon isn't mute, is it?" Ayanami frowned, wanting to probe out some useful information.

Merlin shook his head slightly. To him, the human before him was far too weak—not even worth the slightest interest. He could simply ignore him like a fly.

"Just you alone?" Ayanami was worried about an ambush. No one from the kingdom had come to help him this time.

Merlin paused, then gave a slight nod. He didn't mind revealing the truth, because with himself present, no matter how many came, none would be able to approach the Demon Castle.

"Heh!" Ayanami let out a laugh, speaking in a sarcastic tone. "You don't really think you can stop our elite knights all by yourself, do you? No way—such a stupid demon actually exists? I don't believe it."

Merlin tilted his head. Perhaps finding the insignificant human before him amusing, he didn't strike immediately but instead studied him carefully.

"What does tilting your head mean? Am I wrong?" Ayanami frowned, feeling as though the other party were looking down on him. "We're about to break into the Demon Castle. You can't stop us. Standing here is no different from a mantis trying to halt a chariot—completely pointless. Run away now—the farther, the better. Our bishop isn't as kind-hearted as I am."

"Make me flee?" Merlin's voice became very raspy, unlike the friendly tone he normally used.

"Eh! You're not mute!" Ayanami was startled, his eye twitching. "Ah, that's right. If you don't want to die, scram far away. Actually, we've already seen through it—all of this is your strategy, right? Sending out only one demon to bluff, trying to make us retreat without a fight. But what a pity, I've already seen through your trick!"

"And then?" Merlin asked, genuinely puzzled.

"Tch, stop pretending! Just scram! You're probably just some poor bastard who was forced to step up. So don't stand there acting like some mighty warrior. Running away now would still save your life. Can you see the force behind me?" Ayanami pointed behind himself, speaking with great assurance. "As long as our bishop gives the order, someone like you would be hacked to death with a hundred blades."

"I see. You want me to leave so I don't obstruct you, correct?" Although Merlin's voice was raspy, his tone remained relatively calm.

"You're not the stupid kind, then? Right, that's exactly what I mean." Ayanami continued his coaxing. He dared not strike recklessly but very much hoped Merlin would expose a weakness himself. If Merlin dared to flee, he could be classified as a weak demon, and Ayanami could deliver a fatal blow from behind.

"What a pity, I won't move aside, nor will I let you threaten the safety of the Demon Castle. However…" Merlin paused, taking a step forward and planting his feet firmly. "If you can wound me, I'll let you pass. Want to try?"

"Tch! Don't look down on me! Filthy stinking demon!" Ayanami felt himself being humiliated by his enemy, anger surging within him. He thought, *The guy shows not a single fluctuation of power. Without a doubt, he's just a glory-hound fool!*

Suddenly, Ayanami launched his attack. His body was bathed in golden aura like a lion锁定 its prey, letting out a beast king's roar.

With feral agility, Ayanami vanished into thin air in an instant. His ultra-high-speed movement made the air rumble, charging straight toward Merlin.

Whoosh! Ayanami's figure disappeared again. The next second he appeared at Merlin's left side. Watching the defenseless enemy, he grinned smugly—

Idiot! That was just a feint. I'll deal the fatal blow from the left! As expected, you're nothing but a bluffing piece of trash! Completely lacking any combat experience!

"Lion Fang!"

Ayanami roared, unleashing his trump card secret technique. With all his might, he hurled a lion's fist directly at Merlin.

An unprecedented lion's roar, the majestic might of the Sage King—knights far away were chilled to the bone as it pounced on the enemy with unstoppable momentum!

Vmmmm—

At the critical moment, Merlin's figure also vanished from his original position, causing Ayanami to lose his target entirely.

"Huh!?" Ayanami stared in shock, cold sweat dripping down from the tip of his nose. *How come I can't sense a single trace of his aura? I can't even catch a shadow of him! Is this some super-high-level instant movement? No—this seems like mere movement relying purely on physical strength!*

Merlin's figure flashed and appeared directly in front of Ayanami. Deep within the helmet, his eyes ignited with the flames of death!

"Impossible! How can some madman temper his body to this level?!" Ayanami's face went ashen, screaming in terror.

Merlin raised his arm and casually swung his fist, instantly exploding Ayanami's skull like a watermelon smashed by a club.

The sight was gruesome beyond bearing, utterly disgusting. Ayanami's headless corpse fell to his knees, convulsing—then lost all signs of life after a few seconds.

"You know nothing about true power, pitiful creature."

"This—" Cardinal Serein, who was usually calm, was still shaken by what he had witnessed. Shock played across his face.

*As I expected—the other side isn't a madman but a confident powerhouse!*

To kill someone with the strength of a Hero候补 so easily—

Without a doubt, this opponent's power is on par with my own!

That's it for today. I had some issues the other day.

And this one is even earlier, filling in yesterday's monthly ticket bonus chapter.

I'll give everyone two more chapters tonight, so I won't owe you anything.

If you have tickets, cast them—hoarding them till the end of the month is no fun.

title: Chapter 22 — The Hardest Opponent
content:
Chapter 22 — The Hardest Opponent

Volume 35 · Chapter 22

The demon armor greedily devours the blood and flesh splattered on it, the armor shines anew, becoming ever brighter.

Merlin coldly glanced at the corpse of Ayunami at his feet, then slowly lifted his head and gazed toward the vast crusade army in the distance.

“How cautious. This enemy is a bit hard to deal with. Could it be that they have already realized I cannot stray too far from Behemoth, that there is a secret limiting my range of activity?”

Seeing Ayunami's head smashed by an enemy's punch, all the temple knights felt a faint fear rise in their hearts.

An enemy that even Ayunami cannot defeat—if they go up, it would be nothing but a death sentence; perhaps by uniting there is a sliver of hope.

The atmosphere among the crusade army was dead and heavy, a massive pressure coiling around everyone's hearts.

Ayunami's death dealt a severe blow to the warriors' morale, like a dark cloud covering the sun above, suppressing their spirits to the extreme.

“We can confirm it now—who is the Demon Lord hidden within that armor?” Duru said with certainty, having already discerned some of the situation.

“Are you talking nonsense? How could the Lords betray us and willingly become Behemoth's lapdogs?” the Blacks refused to believe this fact, deeming it unlikely.

“No, Duru is right. To cleanly eliminate a Saint-tier strongman, only the Lords could possibly do it,” Produm said gravely. The duel ended too quickly, with almost no combat; the demon cadres could not have done it, only Demon Lords strong enough to crush a Saint-tier could.

“Miss Alice, we may be in trouble; the opponent might not be an ordinary demon,” Helena lowered her head, her expression turning severe.

Alice furrowed her brows; for some reason, the opponent's killing method just now resembled Merlin's in several ways, preferring a casual way to crush enemies, as if playing.

“If we want to enter the Demon Castle to rescue His Majesty Merlin, we must find a way to defeat that guy. There will be a chance; please do not hold back,” Helena paused, then added, “I feel the opponent's strength is close to the Lords', and there are few in our party who can stand against it.”

“Understood, I will give it my all,” Alice nodded, a hint of seriousness flashing across her brows.

Gulu——

Cardinal Sreyn, dressed in red, swallowed nervously, his nerves taut; Ayunami had already successfully probed the result.

Indeed, they lack skill; who would dare stand in front of the massive crusade army?

Sreyn, barely regaining composure from shock, began to consider how to handle the current situation—“To be safe, I should order the troops to leave the sand sea quickly and have the temple dispatch a few strong reinforcements.”

But the present circumstances do not allow it; supplies have been exhausted, and leaving the sand sea would likely cause half the knights to die en route, and I cannot enter the Demon Castle to repair the blood pool seal.

Is there now only the most dangerous path left to choose?

At any cost, crush this demon and seize the Demon Castle built upon the oasis.

But why doesn't the opponent come forward to attack us? It always operates within a certain range—could it be…

Its range is limited to the area around the Demon Castle; the position we are in now is the edge of its operational zone?

Sreyn seems to have found a key point, but cannot fully confirm yet; he must find a way to verify his thought, which is crucial to defeating the enemy.

“Release the holy whales.

“How many should we release?” a temple knight asked.

“All of them.” Sreyn stared fixedly at the distant Merlin, gritting his teeth, “I will wipe out the land beneath that demon!”

With Sreyn's command, countless white whales formed a chained battle formation soaring in the sky; at the center, a bound, mutated black holy whale, many times larger than its peers, grew increasingly violent, emitting hungry low growls.

The spectacular holy whale formation elicited awe from the temple knights below, who could hardly imagine how the Church created so many terrifying monsters.

The fleet of holy whales resembled a massive white cloud, their halos emitting a faint aura of holy spirit.

A huge shadow loomed over Merlin's head, encircling him at the center of the firestorm!

Sreyn's face showed a grim smile as he murmured, “Come on, let me see how you survive under the holy whales' bombardment. As long as we stand still here, you shouldn't have any way out, right?”

Countless white whales spiraled in the sky, each gaping its massive maw at the sole target below—Merlin!

Blazing white light brewed rapidly within their mouths, a raging divine power enough to make most dark creatures' legs go weak and lose all will to fight!

Yet Merlin, standing at the heart of the barrage, remained motionless, even crossing his arms, appearing to have given up all resistance, as if he hadn't noticed the danger descending from above.

“Heh heh heh,” Sreyn laughed smugly, thinking perhaps he had been scared stiff—his legs so weak he couldn't even run away?

Boom—

Accompanied by a thunderous roar, the holy whales in the formation fired at Merlin simultaneously.

Countless blazing lights intertwined, instantly lighting the sand sea like daylight, a sea of white everywhere.

Merlin endured an all‑directional assault from the sky, leaving virtually no blind spot for escape; Sreyn clearly intended to use the fiercest bombardment to deal with this inscrutable enemy.

At that moment, the sand sea seemed to turn into an actual sea, the yellow sand rolling like endless waves!

The massive shock hurled the ground around Merlin's feet high into the sky—mushroom‑like clouds of dust rose slowly, accompanied by white lightning!

The storm generated by the fierce fire forced every member of the crusade to gasp and crouch behind their shields.

“This is insane, what the Church has researched! Such power!” Blakeman gritted his teeth, feeling even the after‑shock of the explosion was intense; the destructive force of the holy whales' bombardment at the center was unimaginable!

“This destruction could rival the full‑force strike of the Demon Lords,” Produm speculated in his mind.

“If the demon armor truly contains a Lord, then this group of artificial demons will definitely give it a good drink!” Duru said with certainty.

The holy whales' cannon fire continued unabated, the relentless holy light cannons all focused on a single point at the center!

Sreyn's smile remained, but suddenly froze; his eyes widened in astonishment, *That... that is? I must have misread!*

At the core of the blazing bombardment, Merlin still stood with his arms crossed, completely unharmed.

Those seemingly ferocious blasts, when they reached within a meter of Merlin, were entirely dispelled by a strange force, vanishing without a trace.

“Magic immunity?” Sreyn trembled, his face turning an alarming shade, a faint suspicion forming in his mind—E

I've only ever heard of one demon possessing such ability!

The one hidden within that heavy armor—

Could it be the youngest Demon Lord among the demon race?

Damn! We've run into the most troublesome opponent!

title: Chapter 23 — Demon Fire
content:
Chapter 23 — Demon Fire

Volume 35 · Chapter 23

Merlin stood at the center of the Holy Whale cannon fire, relying on his own magic immunity to disperse all attacks. The cannon fire looked extremely fierce, but in reality it could not inflict even the slightest harm on Merlin. Alice's face changed instantly; she could hardly believe her eyes, and a horrified thought flashed through her mind— That magic immunity— Could it be that the one blocking my enemy right now is Merlin? Alice's brows were locked tight, she was uncertain and doubtful, secretly feeling it was Merlin, yet she refused to believe it no matter what. "Hey! Did you see that? That ." Du Lu's tone was somewhat trembling. "No way? Could it be...?" Pudom's heart wavered; if it really was Merlin blocking them, it would be better to surrender early. "What are you all daydreaming about? His Majesty's soul is sealed; how could he possibly stand before us." Blackman said firmly, afraid his companions would waver. Ah, that's right—it must be the magic-dispelling item taking effect." Pudom forced a smile, sweating coldly as he thought; although he said that, it's clearly magic immunity, right? Besides His Majesty Merlin, could there be a second person with such a rare ability? Cardinal Slein's face was filled with anger, his teeth clenched and grinding, the veins on his forehead throbbing. We originally thought the ancient evil god had no allies, relying on numbers we might have a chance to reseal it. But now, even the youngest Demon Lord of the demon race has submitted, making the hope of eliminating the ancient evil god grow ever slimmer. "Don't be so arrogant!" As the words fell, the sound of chains continuously breaking "crack crack" came from the center of the Holy Whale battle formation. The pitch-black mutated Holy Whale split its jaws wide, letting out a furious roar at Merlin on the ground, its halo suddenly turning a striking crimson, like a warning of impending danger! Merlin slowly lifted his head, gazing at the sky where the artificial beast raged violently; his hollow eyes flickered with waves of killing intent. The mutated Holy Whale began frantically inhaling air, causing its already massive body to swell—times, forcing nearby kin to keep their distance, then it suddenly plummeted downward with a thunderous crash! This colossal monster's size rivals a mountain, its weight incalculable; even an ordinary fall is like Mount Tai pressing down, making it nearly impossible for an ordinary person to survive beneath it. The sand sea churned violently, the wind sweeping yellow sand high into the sky, forming a scene like ocean waves! The Holy Temple knights had to lie down to avoid being swept away by the sand and wind; from afar, this desert seemed no different from a true sea to the mutated Holy Whale. Merlin's figure leapt out from the swirling sand dust, using his agility to dodge the mutated Holy Whale's Mount Tai–like crush early on. "Have you become skilled, not continuing to use magic attacks?" Whoosh— The wind roared, the whale's thick tail swept over and slammed straight into Merlin! The demon armor emitted mournful wails, as if it might shatter at any moment under the fierce impact! Merlin was like a tennis ball, brutally smacked by the mutated Holy Whale's tail and tumbled ignominiously into the sand. Seeing this, the crusade troops couldn't help but burst into cheers, feeling that this demonic war should pose no problem— "Scared the hell out of me; I thought this demon was something fierce, but this? This!" "The Holy Whale is the crystallization of our church's years of wisdom; its power is truly extraordinary!" "Now we finally have hope; we can directly assault the Demon City!" Alice's heart welled with worry; her stance wavered, she just wanted to pull off the opponent's helmet to verify her suspicion—if the other truly was Merlin, how would she face him? Cardinal Slein was far from pleased; without dealing with Merlin, he couldn't even crack a smile—this old rival prevented the church from gaining any advantage. "Don't hesitate, take him out!" The mutated Holy Whale lying in the sand sea received the keeper's order, instantly flew into a rage, sprang into action, gaping its spiked maw, writhing madly toward Merlin, intending to swallow him whole. Merlin had just risen from the ground, shaken his head, and looked up to see the ferocious creature lunging, its blood‑filled maw gulping down the sand along the way. At such close range, the naked eye could no longer make out the monster's full form; though not as colossal as Leviathan, it was still quite close. Merlin stood there blankly, listening to the whooshing wind in his ears, fine sand grains pelting his armor; to anyone watching, it looked like a hopeless situation. Yet deep within his heavy helmet, that eye flared again with demonic fire, seeping out from the cracks in his armor. Merlin gripped the pitch‑black Banri Garan at his waist, facing the mutated Holy Whale's devouring, he drew his weapon unhurriedly. The jet‑black blade bore a vein‑like red pattern, exuding a scorching aura that even the frenzied Holy Whale felt a violent suffocation! Merlin lifted Banri Garan high above his head; with a soft 'hiss', a faint flame sparked on the blade, at this moment when the sun had already set, like a torch burning fiercely. "Huh? Slein felt something off, craning his neck to look, "What wicked scheme is he cooking up now?" Whoosh— A torrent of demonic fire, like mountains and seas overturned, erupted from the tiny blade of Banri Garan and shot straight up! The roaring flames dyed the sky and sand sea a crimson red; the extreme heat made the place seem like a fiery hell, even the sand beneath showing signs of melting. This once‑worn blade of the great sage, sealed away for ages, finally revealed its true form before everyone's eyes, displaying its unparalleled divine artifact power! "That's... a divine artifact?!" Slein was somewhat at a loss for words, faintly smelling a burnt scent coming from his eyebrows and clothes. Even from this distance, the crusade forces found the heat radiating from Banri Garan hard to bear; sweat poured like an unshut tap, splashing incessantly. The armor faintly glowing red on their bodies was no longer protection but a torture device; if not for fear of danger, the warriors would gladly strip naked. Many frail knights had already collapsed unconscious on the spot; the temperature exceeded that of the daytime sand sea by more than tenfold! Even strong fighters like Alice and Slein were drenched in sweat; one can imagine the torment the others were enduring. Pudom lowered his head, his face grim to the extreme, his eyes hinting at a hint of despair— . - I know nobody wants to accept this fact, but that is His Majesty Merlin—there's no mistake about it. I recalled— that long blade capable of emitting demonic fire, isn't that the true form of Banri Garan?!

title: Chapter 24 — Exterminate All (Monthly Ticket Extra)
content:
Chapter 24 — Exterminate All (Monthly Ticket Extra)

Volume 35 · Chapter 24

We can't win. If His Majesty Merlin is blocking us, there is no chance of even approaching the Demon Castle!

Why? Why would His Majesty Merlin appear here?

His soul has already been sealed inside a pot. It is impossible for him to be released.

What on earth has happened?

Proup's heart remained unsettled for a long time, filled with confusion, and he didn't even dare to share his thoughts with his companions, fearing they would find it hard to accept.

The ferocious mutated holy whale, under tremendous pressure, roared as it charged at the tiny Merlin, showing no fear of the death threat from demon fire.

The foul stench from its massive mouth hit them squarely in the face.

Merlin coldly remained unresponsive. He slowly rotated the Banri Garan in his hands, and instantly unleashed a terrifying wave of heat!

The temperature in the desert sea rose to an unthinkable level in an instant, even creating the illusion of approaching the sun! The mutated holy whale hadn't even had time to react before it was reduced to ashes at the extreme heat!

The ordinary white holy whales filling the sky also couldn't withstand such temperatures, turning to flying ash and vanishing one after another.

There was no burning process in the holy whales' deaths; instead, they vanished into gray smoke in the blink of an eye. This was the most extreme flame power, achieving nothingness through complete combustion!

What a terrifying temperature! Serein's eye twitched nervously. He wanted to take back his previous words—the opponent's strength wasn't equal to his; it was beyond him!

The knights couldn't bear the intense heat, groaning on the ground. They were already dying of thirst, and now their sweat was almost all dried up.

Magma began to flow at Merlin's feet, the yellow sand dyed pitch black. Towering demon flames scorched the sky as his gaze locked onto the distant crusade army, and he swung the Banri Garan in his hand violently—

Demonic flames instantly surged toward the church's crusade army, rolling forward with waves of heat, intent on burning all life in their path to ash!

Merlin wielding the Banri Garan truly carried a touch of the great prophet's aura, bringing destruction to Asgard, the home of the gods, with demon fire!

In the distance, a towering wall of fire ignited on the horizon, like a massive flame tsunami surging straight toward the crusade army!

"Alert! Alert!"

Serein lost his composure entirely, shouting orders to organize defenses. The scorching demon fire could wipe out their entire army.

However, the flame tsunami arrived too quickly—they couldn't possibly organize a defense in time!

At this moment, Alice was forced to step forward, standing in front of everyone. She drew the slender sword Bright Aria from her waist and plunged it into the yellow sand.

Thump thump thump—

Countless ice pillars emerged from the sand, forming a dim golden ice wall of immense scale, protecting the crusade soldiers behind it.

Alice hoped to use this method to withstand the tide of demon fire. A cool breath spread through the air, making the knights feel much more comfortable.

Boom! The demon fire, like a tsunami, crashed against the ice wall. The fused ice crystals possessed extraordinary strength and actually managed to hold out against the demon fire's assault.

But the flames of the Banri Garan had, after all, destroyed the homeland of the ancient gods. With temperatures rumored to approach that of the sun, how could mere fused ice hope to resist?

The ice wall Alice had created couldn't hold long under the scorching demon fire. Massive cracks continuously spread, melting at a speed visible to the naked eye.

"Hah!"

Alice was reluctant to give up. Gritting her teeth, she continuously poured power into the ice wall, repairing the cracks.

But these countermeasures were useless. The demon fire's assault was unstoppable, and in an instant it shattered and melted the massive ice wall. The scorching storm knocked Alice's helmet from her head, and her waterfall-like silver hair was nearly set ablaze, faint black smoke rising from it.

Towering demon flames swept in with a howl, breaking through the ice wall's defense. Though weakened considerably, the super-high-temperature heatwave was still enough to claim massive numbers of lives.

The demon fire rolled above the crusade army's heads, then rose and drifted into the high sky before disappearing.

The warriors let out hysterical screams, making the place seem like hell on earth for a moment.

Serein had underestimated the power of the demon fire. After the flames dissipated, nearly half of the nearly 300,000-strong crusade army was killed or wounded. The Templar knights at the front suffered even heavier losses—only the Saint-tier warriors could barely survive.

As for the ants below Saint-tier, they had long since turned to ash and evaporated on the spot before the heatwave even arrived.

This was still the result of Alice standing at the front and using an ice wall to block most of the demon fire's power. If she hadn't courageously stepped forward, the crusade force would truly have been wiped out entirely. Not even a few Saint-tier demons would have survived. Only she and Serein had any chance of living.

Serein's heart bled. He had never suffered such humiliation. Every time he had led an expedition, he'd achieved at least modest success. This was the first time things had gone so catastrophically wrong.

The losses—over half killed and wounded—were somewhat unbearable for the Church. Even Serein's reputation would be tarnished. It was possible that, following the historically most failed Hero, a historically most failed bishop would emerge.

Serein's face went pale. He kept reminding himself to stay calm, not to act impulsively. To clash head-on with this demon—he feared he wouldn't have a single advantage.

Alice knelt on the ground, breathing heavily. In order to block the demon fire, she had expended a massive amount of magic power and battle aura, leaving her feeling somewhat weak. They hadn't even encountered the ancient demon god yet. If they truly attacked the Demon Castle—she feared they wouldn't be able to win.

"Are you alright, Miss Alice?"

Helena showed concern in her eyes. Although she also harbored feelings for Merlin, and Alice was somewhat her rival, she couldn't think about such matters at a time like this.

Alice was the only hope of rescuing the Demon Lords. Under any circumstances, her safety needed to be prioritized.

"I'm fine." Alice answered, putting on a calm exterior, though inwardly she was afraid of the demon fire she'd just witnessed. But in terms of destructive power, her Bright Aria couldn't compare—it only had advantages in functionality.

"What should we do?" Helena grew worried, anxious in her heart.

"Let's flee," Duru suddenly said.

"Huh? What did you say?" Blake Man looked thoroughly astonished.

"I said let's flee. This place is too dangerous. That guy is far too terrifying. We'll think of another way to rescue His Majesty Merlin," Duru said solemnly.

"Are you mistaken? We worked so hard to get here. If we give up, we might not get another chance," Blake Man was unwilling to agree.

"Duru is right. The current situation is a bit unexpected," Proup said meaningfully.

Serein looked around at the heavily damaged force, and a desire to retreat also sprouted in his heart—

This guy was standing in place again. That meant his range of movement was limited to the area around the Demon Castle.

As long as they chose to leave, he wouldn't pursue them.

In the harsh environment of the sand sea, although many would die on the way out, it was still better than everyone perishing here. He couldn't accept the disgrace of total annihilation!

This crusade had failed. They would need to have the Church send more reinforcements.

Serein took a deep breath, suppressed his nervousness, and spoke loudly.

"Everyone, stay calm! Don't be afraid. The enemy's range of movement is limited—he can't possibly pursue us."

No sooner had he finished speaking when Serein noticed wisps of yellow sand slipping past his feet, being drawn toward the direction of the Demon Castle.

Serein's eyelids fluttered wildly, his heart racing in shock. He turned to look and saw a vortex of incomparably powerful attraction, dragging everyone toward the depths!

Merlin raised both hands, casting Gravity Space, intending to pull all the remaining crusaders toward him for a merciless slaughter. He had no intention of sparing anyone. This was Behemoth's order!

Under the enhancement of demon god blood, the Earth Spirit within Merlin was similarly affected, amplified to an unthinkable degree—enough to lift and drag the very sand beneath the knights' feet.

Gravity Space formed a gray vortex, with layers of yellow sand being pulled toward the center, like an unstoppable tornado storm!

"!!?" Serein's entire body trembled. His aged face was completely devoid of color. His feet were slightly lifted off the ground as he was pulled, his voice carrying a tone of despair—

"Damn bastard!"

"You won't even give us a single path to live!?"

Correction Notice

There was indeed a bug with the demon fire in the previous Episode 23. My mistake.

I reread it and there was indeed a problem. When sealed, there shouldn't be thoughts of suspicion or betrayal. This was my typo, my fault.

I was in a hurry to update and my hands were too fast, I forgot. After I finished updating, people started threatening me with votes. I was pretty embarrassed too.

Also, Merlin being able to speak isn't a bug. Just understand it as sleepwalking, or like a robot. It can speak and move, but without its own conscious awareness—it needs to act according to commands. I've seen people who can talk and walk while sleepwalking. It really exists. They don't even know what they did the night before when they wake up.

Then for the bug, I asked the editor to fix it. It should be replaced by morning. Just refresh and it'll be fine.

(v)

title: Chapter 25 — Clash of Ice and Fire
content:
Chapter 25 — Clash of Ice and Fire

Volume 35 · Chapter 25

Merlin unleashed a fierce gravitational space, covering the distant, heavily casualties-laden crusade forces, continuously pulling them toward himself. The yellow sand beneath his feet began to flow, constantly drawn to Merlin's vicinity, forming a huge tornado mixed with sand! The ground under the soldiers' feet became extremely unstable, violently turbulent, as if they were in the ocean amidst a storm. Before many soldiers could recover from the fear of the demonic fire, they were yanked by the immense gravity into the sky, unable to resist, flying toward Merlin. Behemoth's order to Merlin was to kill all invading enemies; even if the crusade forces showed signs of retreat, he could not let them leave easily. Caught in chaos, the crusade army probably would not let anyone escape Merlin's slaughter today; all would be buried in the sea of sand. The cardinal furtively took out a random teleport scroll, his heart itching, wanting to abandon everyone and flee himself. But the immense pressure made him hesitate; in the Church, his status was extremely lofty, second only to the Pope, and countless people respected him greatly. If he abandoned everyone and fled back in disgrace, his reputation would surely plummet to the bottom, becoming a laughingstock in others' eyes. Not a few other cardinals hated him so much they wanted to replace Srain and become the Pope's closest confidant. Srain gritted his teeth, put away the random teleport scroll, thinking now was not the time to flee. Since the enemy did not want them to leave, why not engage in a outright slaughter? Who knows, maybe a miracle would appear? Srain decided to stake half his life, gave up resisting the pull of the gravitational space, and actively jumped into Merlin's range of movement. "Ugh!" Blackman lost his balance, tumbling in the air as he was sucked over. "Blackman!" Pudom exclaimed, failing to grab Blackman's foot. Duru raised his eyebrows, shooting chains from his black robe, binding Blackman, trying to pull him back. But then misfortune struck: Duru could not resist the gravitational space's suction and was himself pulled upward along with it. "Shout!" Alice plunged her slender sword into the yellow sand, straining to hold herself, yet the sand beneath her feet kept being drawn away, and she too was pulled by the tremendous force. The gravitational space ended; not a single soldier of the crusade forces escaped, all were dragged into Merlin's area of activity. Now the knights could only passively choose to fight Merlin, with no way to retreat. "Miss Alice! Miss Alice? Wake up!" Helena lifted Alice from the yellow sand, carefully checking her condition; aside from some fatigue, she seemed fine. Alice felt her head heavy—clearly she had expended much in just resisting the demonic fire's attack. "I—" In order to survive, the Holy Temple knights quickly organized an assault. They had lost all retreat; only by defeating the demon before them could they earn the right to live. The knights overcame their fear of death, deceiving themselves with the lie that after death they could live flexibly in heaven, firmly believing death was not frightening. The suppressed horn sounded, wave after wave charging at the enemy, attempting to use numerical superiority to wear down the foe. Although the demonic fire had caused over half the casualties, the remaining soldiers were still numerous enough to completely surround Merlin and carry out a encirclement. However, the soulless Merlin was merely a living slaughter machine, having lost all mercy and precious humanity; killing came as easily as picking up something, and without completing Behemoth's assigned task, he could not possibly stop. "Die! Demon!" A young Holy Temple knight brandished a spear, bravely thrusting at Merlin, his eyes filled with zeal for his faith. Merlin did not even lift his head; with a casual swing he stirred up scorching turbulence, tearing apart the charging knight together with his weapon. The aftershock spread behind, leaving several marks on the ground; the cavalry trying to rush forward were also torn apart into countless flesh chunks. Merlin merely flicked a finger casually; the turbulence, sharp as a blade, could inflict terrifying slaughter on the surrounding knights. Using a human sea tactic against such a perfect killing machine as Merlin was utterly futile; no matter how many rabble, it was merely a matter of moving a finger. Facing the Holy Temple knights' assault, Merlin stood still, responding with composure, waving his fingers to recklessly reap the enemies' lives, like a bloody music conductor standing on a stage built from countless corpses. "Stop!" A clear shout rang out; the blade's cold gleam accompanied by a biting wind came, breaking Merlin's rhythm of reaping lives. The sword's power was mature and its suction differed greatly from that of the Holy Temple knights; Merlin could not casually block it, only able to slightly turn his body to avoid the edge. In that instant, Merlin could only see the cold silver hair flash before his eyes, the biting cold wind making him feel ill all over. Alice landed lightly, quickly turned and assumed a defensive stance, finally about to strike, a few guesses forming in her mind— This guy possesses magic immunity, can control high-level strength of the scholar system, and has a nasty habit of toying with enemies. I don't believe so many coincidences could gather in one person; he must indeed be Merlin! His soul isn't sealed, is it? Why does he appear here to block the crusade army? Let me see exactly what happened. Alice's pseudo-divine power stood out uniquely among the many foes, naturally arousing Merlin's instinctive interest in strong opponents. With many Holy Temple knights present around her, Alice dared not casually call Merlin's name, thinking she had sneaked demonic influence into the crusade forces without anyone noticing. Merlin stared blankly at Alice; beneath his heavy helmet, no one could see his expression or face. Alice felt somewhat uncomfortable; observing his minute movements, she saw that this "Merlin" showed no reaction toward her, as if he didn't recognize her at all. Facing Alice, Merlin's head twitched slightly, using his ancestral skill—tilting his head to mock, provoking the enemy's anger to rise steadily. "Ugh! Unrepentant!" Alice's fury rose; her fighting spirit and magical power intertwined, the pseudo-divine pressure erupted explosively, making the black night sea of sand even more biting cold; instantly a layer of shimmering icy crystals condensed on the sand. Alice stomped the ground fiercely, her delicate body radiating a ferocious aura; holding her slender sword, she chanted the bright lament and suddenly lunged at Merlin. With a flick of her wrist, the sharp blade traced countless sword flowers, the piercing, bone-chilling cold light pouring forth and stabbing toward the enemy! Pudom's face turned ugly to the extreme; he clenched his fists tightly— According to records, once the Demon-Sealing Vase is used it cannot be opened; His Majesty Merlin could never appear here. Mo Is this the worst-case scenario? Weekend editors are off duty; the author lacks permission to modify VIP chapters, so we must wait until Monday to replace and notify everyone. The changes are minor—just altering the few sentences that suspected Merlin of betrayal; everything else is fine. Also I saw some friends claim Helena knows Merlin's body is controlled, which is wrong: Merlin was first sealed, then Behemoth planned to take the demon lords' bodies; Merlin himself doesn't know his own condition, so Helena would know even less; later chapters will clarify this doubt. Also, please vote for the monthly ticket—more updates will reduce everyone's doubts.

title: Chapter 26 — Danger!
content:
Chapter 26 — Danger!

Volume 35 · Chapter 26

“Alice's swordplay is fierce, the sharp blade cutting through layers of ice, relentlessly stabbing at Merlin, forcing him to retreat.

The biting cold wind rages, and none of the surrounding Paladins dare to approach, only occasionally providing support with arrows and magic to slightly distract the enemy.

Alice's goal is clear; she hasn't unleashed any dangerous killing moves. Every strike is aimed at Merlin's helmet, hoping to knock it off and dispel her doubts.

'Miss Alice,' Helena says with concern, 'I don't recommend you put yourself in danger. There are more important things to attend to.'

Blackman watches from afar, unable to suppress his admiration. 'Is Miss Alice already this strong? I didn't expect her to have the ability to fight a Demon Lord in such a short time. We should go help her; we can't let Miss Alice fight alone.'

'Don't be silly. The power gap is too large; we can't help, and we might even get in the way,' Dru dismisses Blackman's unrealistic idea, lowering his voice. 'Besides, we're still in disguise. If we act rashly, we'll expose our demon identities. Look around — it's all Paladins. Do you want to die?'

'What's the point of us being here if we can't do anything?' Blackman says in frustration.

Podom looks grim, keeping his head down and not speaking, his mind racing with thoughts of what sinister method Behemoth used.

The battle on the other side intensifies. Alice's offense is relentless, and she pursues Merlin relentlessly, growing more confident with each passing moment.

In contrast, Merlin is constantly dodging, occasionally letting out a hoarse laugh, mocking the foolish humans before him.

Alice jumps into the air, shaking her thin sword, scattering massive golden icicles like a rainstorm toward the fleeing Merlin!

Boom boom boom —

Numerous ice spikes plunge into the sand, kicking up a cold blizzard and quickly forming a solid cage, trapping Merlin and restricting his agile, erratic movements.

Seeing this, the other Paladins seize the opportunity and spring into action. A row of spear-wielding warriors bravely charge toward Merlin, thrusting through the gaps in the ice cage, their sharp spears aiming for the enemy's vulnerable spots!

'Hmph!'

A contemptuous cold snort comes from the heavy demon armor, and demonic fire erupts, surging toward the sky, dyeing the sea of sand a sinister crimson.

The brave Paladins who rushed forward are instantly vaporized, turning to ash that drifts in the air.

The hard-won ice cage is also destroyed, unable to withstand the terrifying temperature of the demonic fire.

As the flames dissipate, Alice has already blocked Merlin's retreat, holding her thin sword and stabbing straight at him, accompanied by a freezing blizzard, the tip of the sword shining with a cold, intimidating edge!

Facing the fierce cold wind, Merlin stands like a pine tree in the snow, unmoving. Confronting Alice's powerful attack, he does not dodge this time.

Clearly, Merlin has had enough fun and decides to get serious with the enemy.

Merlin calmly reaches out and grabs the blade Alice thrusts at him. To his surprise —

Under the burning of the holy power of the Lament of Light, he cannot hold this mysterious sword. His hand is scalded on the spot, emitting wisps of white smoke.

Alice seizes this rare opportunity, her spirit soaring, and plunges her sword into Merlin's left shoulder!

Even though Merlin is wearing demon battle armor, it cannot resist the Lament of Light's suppression of evil forces. In its presence, the armor is as fragile as paper, offering no protection.

Any creature or object containing evil, dark power is restrained by this divine artifact, the Lament of Light, and may even lose its abilities — it is truly a bane to darkness.

Because Alice believes the enemy is Merlin, she hesitates when attacking, not aiming to kill but rather to suppress him.

Otherwise, with her current mastery of swordsmanship, she could have struck Merlin's heart directly with the sword that just entered his shoulder, delivering a fatal blow!

Merlin quickly retreats, assessing his physical condition. His gloves and left shoulder plate are burning, constantly emitting white mist, and the demon armor itself is crying out in pain, clearly damaged by the Lament of Light.

If he hadn't retreated quickly enough, the Lament of Light would have pierced his shoulder, and under the destruction of the holy power, his entire left arm would have lost function!

Though Merlin's expression is hidden, one can imagine he is enraged by the human before him!

Alice steadies herself, looking at him with complex eyes, her confusion growing. 'Strange, if this were really Merlin, he wouldn't grab my sword with his hand. How could he not know about the Lament of Light?'

Merlin suddenly clenches his fist, raises his head, and glares at Alice, instantly unleashing an invisible magical shock. The air's earth elements become agitated —

Gravity Space!

Alice hasn't even noticed what's happening when she feels several mountains pressing down on her, making it hard to breathe.

Thud! Unable to resist the massive gravitational field, she drops to one knee, the frozen sand beneath her cracking!

Alice is pinned to the ground, unable to move, her bones creaking. She is unwilling to give up and tries to stand against the overwhelming gravity?

But Merlin's eyes shift, and the gravity space intensifies, pinning Alice firmly to the ground.

The affected Paladins are crushed into a bloody pulp within the gravitational field, not even having time to scream.

'Not good! Alice is in danger!' Blackman shouts in horror, wanting to rush over to help.

Dru stops the fool, scolding him sternly, 'Are you suicidal? Don't you see the Paladins aren't daring to charge? You'll be crushed into mush too!'

'Damn it, what can we do?' Blackman clenches his fists, sweating nervously. If Alice is harmed, the demons will never recover!

Helena lowers her head, her heart in her throat. She desperately wants to tear off her disguise and help, but there are many Paladins around. If they discover she's a demon, she'll likely be eliminated first, and there's also the unfathomable red-robed bishop, Slayne.

The air vibrates, and Merlin appears before Alice in an instant, his red cape fluttering in the wind and snow.

Merlin grips the hilt of the Banri Garan at his waist with his right hand, bending over in mid-air, resembling a tightly drawn bow!

Dru: 'That pose!?'

Blackman: 'No way! This bastard is actually —'

Podom: 'Miss Alice! Run!'

Indeed, the demon followers recognize this pose — it is the starting stance for a draw-cut, identical to Merlin's, a movement ingrained in his bones!

In the cold wind, Merlin assumes the draw-cut position, preparing to unleash the ultimate draw-cut technique that almost no one can evade!

He intends to perform a beheading in front of all the Paladins, cutting off the hero's head and destroying the hope of the crusade —

Alice's life is in peril!

title: Chapter 27 — Fate (Monthly Vote Extra)
content:
Chapter 27 — Fate (Monthly Vote Extra)

Volume 35 · Chapter 27

Under the powerful gravitational space, Alice was pressed firmly to the ground, unable to move, not even having the strength to lift her hand and swing her sword, she could only watch helplessly as the enemy approached. Merlin hovered in mid-air, assuming a sword-drawing stance, his cold gaze fixed on the kneeling Alice, hiding none of his surging killing intent. Alice's eyes widened, all color drained from her face as she stared at the familiar yet unfamiliar figure, her mind going blank, she instinctively shut her eyes— "Stop!" Accompanied by Alice's shout, Divine Power was triggered, bursting forth from her body. Almost instantly, everything was dragged into an eternally frozen world, and time ceased to flow. The sand sea seemed to turn into a bitter cold land, everyone frozen like statues, motionless. Even Merlin was not spared, frozen in mid-air, his dangerous sword-drawing technique halted, the immense gravitational space also disappearing. This was Alice's domain; only she could move, the frozen time reversed the situation, control returned to her. Alice staggered to her feet, gazing at the enemy before her, breathing heavily, under the gravitational pressure causing her whole body to ache terribly. She gritted her teeth, almost dragging her body, she approached Merlin, summoning courage to raise her slender sword. If Alice were to thrust the Light's Chant into Merlin's heart at this moment, once time flowed again he would still suffer a fatal wound, just like Mammon's death. But Alice, not yet knowing the truth, was unwilling to be ruthless. Crack crack— A series of cracking sounds came; the ice sculpture that Merlin had turned into began to show fissures, clearly about to break free from the bonds of frozen time. Alice's face showed astonishment, her heart leapt in shock—why could he break free so quickly? Even Nidhogg couldn't do it! Barely two seconds of frozen time! Seeing the frozen time about to end, Alice dared not hesitate; she thrust her slender sword toward the enemy's head. But at this very moment, beneath the dark, deep helmet of the demon armor, a— a beam of demonic fire light flared. The violent repulsive force space acted upon Alice, hurling her like a cannonball, directly blasting her away. "Ugh!" Alice felt as if a tremendous hammer had smashed into her chest; in panic she wildly slashed upward with her slender sword. The frozen time ice world instantly collapsed, vanished without a trace, everything returned to its original state. The Templar Knights had no idea what had happened; seeing Alice about to be beheaded, she was suddenly flung away, no one knew the process in between. "Huh?" Helena's face full of doubt, she had just been ready to risk intervening, but the enemy seemed to have deliberately let Alice go; the use of this repulsive force space left her bewildered. Alice crashed heavily onto the sand, rolling several times before barely shaking off the push of the repulsive force. Helena rushed over to help Alice up, asking, "Are you alright, Miss Alice? That was too dangerous just now; you shouldn't have done that." Alice had just risen when she couldn't help but suck in a breath of cold air; pain shot through her whole body, she couldn't speak, forced to grit her teeth and endure. Having just taken a direct hit from the repulsive force space, her body could barely withstand it, her bones felt as if they'd be shaken apart. Alice lifted her head, looking toward the distant enemy, who seemed to have disconnected again, standing motionless in place. Merlin stood silently in the cold wind, the heavy helmet on his head suddenly flashing a white line. In the instant she was blasted away, Alice's wildly swinging blade still managed to touch Merlin's helmet. Crack— With a crisp sound, the demon armor's helmet split in two, revealing Merlin's true face to all eyes. He was still that blond man, but strands of white hair made him look extremely eerie; half his face had been corroded by demonic blood, presenting a bark-like scorched black color. Dense blood vessels spread across the corroded right face; looking closely, one couldn't tell whether what flowed inside was blood or flame, faintly glowing red in the darkness. #Merlin. "Alice softly called, forgetting the pain shooting through her body; she couldn't understand why the one blocking the crusade army was Merlin—if it were another demon lord there might still be a chance, but facing Merlin she truly had no confidence." Merlin suddenly lifted his head, opening his empty, lifeless eyes; the right eye corroded by demonic blood surged with scorching demonic fire, lighting the dark night, a frenzied killing intent surged toward Alice! "Helena! Get out of the way! His target is me!" Alice shoved Helena aside, forcing her exhausted, fatigued body to rally, gripping her slender sword tightly, staring directly at the man she loved— "This scene was very similar to when they first met. The destined showdown between Hero and Demon Lord, replayed once again!"

title: Chapter 28 — Beheading
content:
Chapter 28 — Beheading

Volume 35 · Chapter 28

Merlin focused all his attention on Alice; failing to defeat this human, he felt very annoyed—
"Huff!"
The scorching demon fire surged, recalling the terrifying scenes of countless people evaporating in high heat; the Paladins instinctively retreated, and none dared to confront Merlin.
Merlin's gaze fixed on Alice, revealing no hint of the fierce murderous intent he exuded.
The demon subordinates present had never seen such a mad Merlin; they had reached a point of no recognition!
"Does Your Majesty not recognize us?" Blake Man asked with naive doubt.
"Yes, is there a possibility to awaken Your Majesty Merlin?" Duru also harbored a sliver of hope in his heart.
"Give up; Your Majesty is now a toy under Behemoth's control, his soul forever sealed in the demon sealing flask, impossible to recognize us, let alone be awakened, unless Your Majesty's soul can escape from the flask." Pudom answered seriously, fearing his companions might do something foolish.
"Sigh! It's really a headache; if we are to confront Your Majesty, we might as well surrender peacefully," Du Zeng said with a bad mood, very pessimistic.
"Exactly, Your Majesty's body is being used by an ancient demon god; do we still have a chance?" Blake Man sighed, continuing, "Perhaps we are not only fighting Your Majesty, but also other Demon Lords."
Pudom frowned, truly fearing something; indeed, his companions began to lose morale when facing Merlin, which was why he had just refused to state the facts.
But it cannot be denied that the situation before them was indeed terrible; to approach the Demon Castle and find the sealing flask, they must defeat the controlled Merlin, not to mention facing other Demon Lords.
The success rate of the rescue plan had already approached zero; Behemoth had already eliminated all possibilities.
"There is still a way to defeat Merlin Your Majesty,"
"Hmm!" Blake Man stared at Pudom in astonishment, "Are you serious?"
"Your Majesty still has some weaknesses, such as not knowing how to swim, and his resistance to poison is at ordinary human level," Pudom paused and whispered, "If there are a few mages surpassing the Saint-tier, turning this into a ... we might win."
"That is equivalent to saying nothing; where do we go to find a powerful water mage? Helena is indeed proficient in water magic, but to change the environment of the desert sea, her power is probably far insufficient," Duru said in a disappointed tone.
Pudom said nothing; he could not foresee any breakthrough, and could not find any exceptionally powerful water mage or alchemist.
On the other side, Merlin and Alice fought again, with ice and fire colliding in an unprecedented clash.
The temperature of the desert sea constantly fluctuated between heat and cold, making the Paladins somewhat intolerable.
The battle between the Hero and the Demon Lord entered a feverish stage; bystanders could not intervene, and the pressure from the two was enough to make countless onlookers tremble.
Compared to before, Alice had indeed become much stronger; she now had some means of counterattack before Merlin, rather than being defeated at first sight and becoming a pitiful captive.
However, the situation was very unfavorable for Alice; having already used Divine Power, she could not freeze time again, losing a decisive trump card.
To casually wield Divine Power, it would probably require a demigod or divine realm; Alice was still far from reaching that level.
Alice's breathing became much heavier, her movements slower than before; pain from her injuries pierced her body, adding to her already terrible condition.
Merlin's assault was swift, pressing closer to Alice; as a qualified killing machine, he would not give the enemy any breathing room.
Alice swung her slender sword, condensing countless golden ice blades in the shivering wind; the scale was vast, enveloping Merlin's head.
With the swing of the Bright Chant, countless golden ice blades began to pour from the sky like a river, surging to strike the enemy!
Merlin crossed his arms; the demon armor on his body roared, forming a black vortex that isolated the incoming ice blades.
The clashing sound continued; the sharp ice swords were shredded by the demon armor's vortex, unable to harm Merlin's body.
"Shout!"
Alice clenched her silver teeth, believing she had to deliver a heavy blow to make Merlin stop; the scraping damage was useless!
Only Alice's Bright Chant emitted destructive holy light, continuously expelling the evil forces in the desert sea.
Even Behemoth hidden in the Demon Castle could feel this extremely dangerous bright aura!
Merlin sensed a hint of threat, immediately adopting a sword-drawing stance; the Banri Garan at his waist began to vibrate slightly.
Alice leapt into the air, deciding to gamble everything against Merlin; all her strength drained, she directly unleashed the third form of the Great Snow Mountain Sword technique, Opening Heaven—
I have seen Merlin's sword-drawing technique countless times, and I have also heard him explain it; even the slightest movements, I know better than anyone else. If I seize the opportunity, even without freezing time, I can definitely avoid Merlin's sword-drawing!
Alice tightly gripped her slender sword, descending from the sky with a world-opening momentum, directly striking Merlin; behind her followed an extraordinarily magnificent Holy Spirit army, their phantasms glittering with light, their wings behind them whipping fierce wind!
Merlin's eyelids flickered; the demon armor on his body emitted a trembling fear, already frightened; if not for the pressure, he might have fled from the user.
Suddenly, two massive Holy Spirit phantasms, strong in form, rushed from both sides, swinging their great hammers to strike the distracted enemy!
Merlin was forced to abandon his sword-drawing stance, opening his arms, and unarmed he blocked the great hammer attacks from both sides of the Holy Spirits.
"Boom," a great sound; the ground beneath Merlin shattered instantly, scattering flying sand and stones!
Merlin's gaze turned cold; he used demon fire to burn the huge Holy Spirits on both sides alive, turning them into specks of light.
At this moment, Alice's strongest sword had already reached the front; betting all her strength, the attack's immense pressure made Merlin furrow his brows.
Merlin calmly took a half-step back, unhesitatingly using his sword-drawing slash to confront the enemy!
The lethal sword aura rolled up strands of demon fire, erupting loudly; its power was stronger than ever!
The ultimate sword-drawing technique was unstoppable; it was hard to imagine anyone surviving such a terrifying move.
Alice seemed prepared; a moment before Merlin drew his sword, she leapt like lightning into the air, passing over Merlin's head, arriving behind him.
spine
As long as my sword pierced Merlin's spine, it wouldn't kill him; it would only render his body unable to move!
Only this method can make him stop!
"Here!" Alice shouted, thrusting her sword, infused with all her strength, straight into Merlin's nape!
Mouth—
A great metallic collision sound, sparks flying!
Merlin, at some point, had the Banri Garan's blade behind his back, successfully cutting off all of Alice's hope, blocking the long-brewed decisive sword!
"Ah?" Alice looked bewildered, her face lacking any color; after planning for so long, she was simply undone by Merlin's simple counter.
Her mind stopped thinking.
Merlin slightly turned his head,
his right eye, eroded, pulsed with deathly fire,
with a hoarse noise, cold and icy, he said—
"You seem to understand my sword-drawing technique? But it's useless…"
"Your weak self can only give me a little more fun; vanish."
Alice had actually been cut by the sword-drawing slash long ago,
a faint red line lit up on her neck,
on the spot, before?
blood continuously sprayed
History did not change; the Hero failed again
The Demon Fire in episode 23 has already changed; everyone can refresh.
Also asking everyone for the moon ticket; have you all lost them?
Finally, a friendly illustration from book friend Asada Shino; feels love, I'm flattered.
