title: Chapter 29 — Encirclement of Demons
content:
Chapter 29 — Encirclement of Demons

Volume 35 · Chapter 29

Alice's head was severed by Merlin's own hand, blood spurted out, condensing into a layer of frost on the land, and the virtual shadows of the Holy Spirit Army vanished instantly, accompanied by a mournful song.

Seeing Alice fall, the warriors in the crusade team fell into fear, losing the trustworthy hero they relied on. Their hearts began to constantly waver. If not for the support of powerful faith, they would have long since dropped their weapons and fled in disarray.

"Alice Miss!" Blackman cried out, a chill rising from the bottom of his heart.

Duru closed his eyes and said softly, "Perhaps seeking help from humans was itself an error."

Dou Pom's brows furrowed high, thinking that the current Merlin was indiscriminately killing, and even this old subordinate of his probably couldn't escape the butcher's knife.

Merlin turned around, the Banri Garan in his hand pointing at Alice's body lying in a pool of blood. The blade was already burning with extremely high-temperature flames. He actually wanted to destroy the body and erase all traces? This was very much in line with the ruthless style of a demon, giving enemies no chance to survive!

Helen couldn't hold back any longer. Even if she had to face the encirclement of the Holy Knights, she had to tear off her disguise and act.

Her demon horns emerged, and the black fallen angel wings behind her unfolded in full view of the crowd.

Helen condensed a flow of water with both hands, then rotated at extreme speed, injecting Saint-tier magic power into it. However, as the wine was poured out, the water flow rotating at extreme speed swelled in the wind, and in the blink of an eye formed a torrent, surging and rising.

Monster-like creatures resembling fairies surged in the torrent, sometimes leaping out of the water and making piercing calls!

Merlin turned his head blankly, completely unconcerned about such an attack. The demonic fire emanating from Banri Garan grew even hotter.

Due to the magic immunity, the torrent automatically split apart when it rushed near Merlin, and the flexible water demons dispersed upon approaching.

However, Helen was not attacking Merlin; she wanted to change the terrain and imprison Merlin in a water prison.

" "

Merlin let out a cold snort, rotated the handle of the sword in his hand, and the demonic fire rose, scorching hot waves coming over, instantly evaporating the torrent Helen had cast!

Merlin, who now possessed the power of a demon god, actually had no weakness of not knowing how to swim. The demonic fire brought temperatures close to the sun, enough to evaporate any liquid.

"Still not working, though?" Helen bit her lip, but internally she felt a sigh of relief, because her plan had succeeded; she just wanted to save Alice.

Merlin suddenly turned his head and discovered that Alice's body was missing.

Duru used two chains to lower Alice's corpse back from the destroyed edge.

The demons had already torn off their disguises and were fully exposed in the sight of the Holy Knights, making the situation increasingly dangerous.

Helen quickly went to Alice's side, checking her injuries, discovering that her head had been completely severed, and the body was rapidly turning cold. If the soul had also fallen into hell, she probably couldn't be saved.

"Dead, Alice Miss is dead, do any of you know healing magic? If the fatal wound on the neck can be quickly repaired, maybe there's still hope!"

"Who would know healing magic? And with such severe injuries, simple healing magic is useless; one needs to arouse massive life force."

Duru said seriously from the side.

Dou Pom had seen a few vampires before; their life force was incredibly tenacious. Even after having their heads cut off, they could survive. If Alice also had such power, it wouldn't be hopeless, right?" Blackman's face was as pale as death. Alice died like this, and it might be that no one could use the Light Lamentation, and then the demon race would completely destroy everything.

"You guys think of a quick way already! Don't just stand there!" Helen, who had always been a quiet and elegant demon, was now full of anger, scolding her companions.

Blackman and Duru were both scared stiff, not knowing what to say. If there was really a way to revive Alice, they wouldn't be foolishly standing in place.

"You shouldn't be so anxious, Helen. At a time like this, never be hasty; you must communicate well." Dou Pom said with a hard head, afraid that the companions would fall into chaos, which wouldn't solve the problem.

"How could I not be anxious? Alice Miss has already encountered misfortune. We aren't the entire demon race going to be doomed! Not just Merlin's Majesty, even our Lord and the other Demon Lords will never be able to leave the sealing pot!" Helen looked at Alice's body, trembling and saying, "What exactly should we do? Will Alice Miss's soul disappear?"

"Let me try. I've recorded high-tier healing magic in my magic book, but with such injuries, the effect of healing magic is not great; whether Alice Miss can be saved depends on luck." Dou Pom squatted down, took out his "Merlin Records," and found the page on healing magic. It died—

Warm light began to shine, and the magic book floated above Alice's body, attempting to repair the fatal wound on Alice's nose.

But this healing magic had very limited effect on fatal wounds. Although the blurred flesh began to writhe, there was no sign of healing at all.

While the demons were busy healing Alice, the Holy Knights also became restless. The warriors discovered that a few demons had mixed into their team, which shocked them greatly—

"Demons! It's demons!"

"Those few demons mixed in as adventurers!"

"Is that true? Hero Alice is a traitor colluding with the demon race! We were deceived!"

"What huge audacity! This must be a trap they set intentionally to kill us all!"

"Kill them! Don't let them get away with it!"

For a moment, the warriors of the crusade team were enraged, their eyes all turning red. They attributed the sacrifices of countless companions to the demons mixed into their ranks.

Uninformed Holy Knights gradually approached the demons with the sharp weapons in their hands, thinking that compared to that troublesome Demon Lord, these few demons here were clearly easier to deal with. Their strength might not compare, but they could be killed by sheer numbers.

The situation had become extremely dangerous. The few demons not only had to worry about Merlin's slaughter but also had to guard against the Holy Knights' threats. The pressure in their hearts multiplied!

"I and Helen will take care of Alice Miss, Blackman, Duru, you go deal with the Holy Knights." Dou Pom's expression was serious, fully催动 the healing magic.

"Don't worry, I've long wanted to kill Holy Knights." Duru squirmed under his feet, several snake-like poisoned chains emerging, ready for battle.

Blackman also completed a gender transformation, holding a heavy雷 magic warhammer, thunder surging all over his body, and shouting, "Come on! Stupid Holy Knights, come and fight this grandpa!"

Angered Holy Knights rushed toward the few demons.

Both sides lost their rationality, fighting together. The Holy Knights, relying on their numbers advantage, had a large edge, but who knew how long they could resist?

Red Cleric Slein hid in the distance, carefully observing the situation, thinking, So that's how it is. Those few demons were actually subordinates of Lucifer the Third.

Suddenly! A wave of heat came over, and Merlin instantly arrived beside Slein. He had known for a long time that there was a powerful enemy hiding here. After dealing with Alice, he had actively come looking.

Uh! Don't kill me! I surrender! I surrender!

Slein moved quickly and didn't hesitate, turning and running, his mind thinking—

Complete disaster! If this monster locks onto me, I'm surely dead!

I can't beat it, only by running can I survive!

Why is he still chasing me? Does that mean I'm surely dead?

It's a joke! I'm the one who wins!

The fleeing Slein suddenly stopped abruptly and turned around, executing a counterattack. From his waist, he took out eight pure white daggers, almost at the same moment, all deeply stabbed into Merlin's body—

Hehehe, I've won.

Let me give you a good lesson, young Demon Lord!

title: Chapter 30 — Marionette
content:
Chapter 30 — Marionette

Volume 35 · Chapter 30

"!!?"

Merlin was struck by eight daggers simultaneously — four in his arms and legs, and two in his chest and abdomen — with every critical area pierced by Slayne.

These daggers were all forged from the bones of a saint, possessing terrifying lethality against dark creatures, especially demons.

With Slayne’s forceful throw, the armor’s defense was rendered useless, and the daggers penetrated directly through the demon plate.

Merlin quickly retreated, not expecting the enemy to act so deceitfully — turning back without fear and stabbing all eight daggers at once.

Waves of pain washed over him. Looking down, Merlin saw the daggers embedded in his flesh writhing like living things, burrowing deeper into his body until they disappeared.

He raised his head, his corrupted right eye blazing with fury, wishing to tear the old Slayne apart.

“Heh heh, what’s that look? Unconvinced? Young Demon Lord, Lucifer III,” Slayne said proudly, his eyes gleaming with satisfaction. “Though this is our first meeting, your name is known throughout the temple. You inherited Vivian’s legacy at a young age and became the third master of the First Demon Lord Palace. Your courage and vision surpass any previous demon lord, and your strength has repeatedly sent our crusaders to their deaths in the Death Swamp. You alone have kept the Pope awake at night — you’re truly different from past demon lords.”

Merlin remained expressionless, his mind focused solely on killing this troublesome opponent.

As he took a step forward, his legs failed him, and he tripped over his own feet, falling face-first into the sand.

Merlin was shocked — he couldn’t control his body, and suspected Slayne was manipulating him.

“Allow me to introduce myself: I am Slayne Manhartem Abdullah, one of the cardinal bishops, the Pope’s most trusted advisor, and head of saint research. The whale you saw earlier is my creation,” Slayne continued, dropping his smile. “I now declare you guilty in the name of the divine, and you must be punished. Are you ready, young demon lord?”

Merlin stood up angrily, ready to strike, but his hands betrayed him — they clenched into fists and began pounding his own head, echoing loudly.

The onlookers were stunned: the mighty demon lord was self-harming before the bishop, punching himself repeatedly.

It appeared he had succumbed to the authority of the divine messenger, using self-mutilation to seek forgiveness.

Only Merlin knew his body was being forced — the eight saint-bone daggers inside him were twisting his limbs, making him beat himself.

“Too light! More force! Mild pain won’t earn you absolution — only pain near death can redeem you. Your sins are deep; don’t think you can cheat your way out!” Slayne waved his finger, controlling the daggers within Merlin.

Merlin became a true puppet, with Slayne as the hidden puppeteer.

He increased the force of his self-punishment, each punch shaking the air.

Blow after blow drove him backward, his head reeling, face bruised, and blood trickling from his mouth.

“Not enough! Still not enough! You need more pain!” Slayne felt unsatisfied and intensified the control.

Merlin regained partial awareness but found his left hand raised, index finger trembling.

Crack —

His finger was snapped by an invisible force, bending far beyond 90 degrees, sending searing pain through his body.

“!!!”

“Why aren’t you screaming? Scream! The great goddess loves the wails of demons!” Slayne roared, proceeding to break more fingers —

Second finger!

Third finger!

Fourth finger!

To prevent Alice’s healing from being disrupted, Blackman and Dru engaged the templar knights in fierce combat.

The feminized Blackman wielded the Thunder Demon Hammer, unleashing storms that tore knights apart.

Dru was even more vicious, his poisoned chains snaking through the sand, impaling dozens of knights at once and hoisting them aloft like kebabs.

Though the demons fought bravely, driving the knights back, their strength was finite — mana and stamina were draining rapidly.

The knights began to conserve energy, waiting for the demons to exhaust themselves before counterattacking.

Helena looked at the lifeless Alice and asked, “How is she?”

“Not good. Prepare for the worst,” Pdom said grimly.

Suddenly, Alice’s hand — wearing the “Angel” ring — trembled, and a warm green light enveloped her, slowly closing the fatal wound on her neck.

“What is this?”

Pdom and Helena gasped as grass and flowers sprouted around Alice, despite the barren desert.

Pdom stared at the ring: “Angel? Why does Alice have this?”

“Angel, also called the Resurrection Ring, was created by Uriel, one of the seven archangels, using the goddess’s power. Every saint warrior wears one — it forces the body to heal even after death.”

“Can it revive the dead?” Helena marveled.

“No, strictly speaking, it’s not resurrection — that requires the soul to return from hell. This is just advanced healing. It repairs both body and soul, but if the soul has left, the ring is useless.”

“So if Alice’s soul is gone, the ring won’t help?”

“Not quite — it’ll still fix the body, so she’ll look better in death,” Pdom replied awkwardly.

Helena fell silent, watching Alice. If the soul is trapped in hell, no healing can bring her back. But since Alice died recently, there’s still a chance.

“Will Alice wake up?”

“She should — the ring’s power is strong enough to repair even a decapitated head. We just need to guard her until the healing finishes,” Pdom said, scanning the battlefield.

Then he saw Merlin in danger —

“That’s — !”

“I’m done playing. Time for the final redemption ritual. To show your sincerity to the great goddess, young demon lord, kill yourself with your own sword — cut your throat!” Slayne exclaimed, trembling with excitement at the prospect of a demon lord committing suicide before him.

Merlin’s eyes glazed over, his body shaking as he drew the Banri Garan and placed it against his neck.

Slayne spread his arms, eyes bloodshot with fanaticism —

“Yes! That’s it!”

title: Chapter 31 — Sacred Heart
content:
Chapter 31 — Sacred Heart

Volume 35 · Chapter 31

"Come on, slit your own throat!"

Cardinal Slayn, his expression fanatical, was already impatient to watch the youngest demon monarch in the demon race commit suicide right before him.

Merlin held the blade of the demon sword Banri Garan against his own neck, his arm trembling constantly as he fought against the Holy Spirit bone daggers eroding him from within.

The blade's edge drew closer and closer to the skin of his neck. Merlin could already feel the scorching breath searing his throat!

Merlin immediately clenched his teeth. The right side of his face, eroded by demon blood, was spreading, slowly creeping toward the other half of his body as crimson blood vessels lit up one after another.

"Hmm? What's going on? Hurry up and do it!" Slayn cursed angrily, constantly manipulating the daggers embedded in Merlin's body, but there was no response.

Enduring the erosion of the sacred aura within him, Merlin forcibly threw Banri Garan away from him, and it landed point-first in the sandy ground between him and Slayn.

Then Merlin clenched both fists, the demon god's blood surging through his body, and forcibly forced the eight bone daggers out of his flesh.

"Damn it! Don't even think about it!" Slayn was greatly startled. After successfully ambushing him, how could he tolerate Merlin escaping so easily?

With Slayn exerting all his strength, the eight bone daggers slowly sank back into Merlin's flesh.

Suddenly, Banri Garan, stuck point-first in the ground, erupted with blazing demonic flames, their light dyeing the night sky red.

Slayn discovered that he had lost connection with the Holy Spirit bone daggers — they seemed to have been destroyed?

Deep within the demonic flames, the eight daggers radiating sacred aura were burned to ashes.

Merlin was someone who bathed in magma, so he naturally didn't mind using demonic flames to sear himself. Instead, it eased his wounds and made the fusion between demon blood and his body even tighter.

As the flames dissipated, Merlin shot toward Slayn at extreme speed, snatching up Banri Garan from the ground mid-charge, and slashed at his enemy like lightning!

"No!"

Schhh —

Slayn was cut in half from waist to waist by Merlin's single stroke, blood gushing everywhere.

Merlin had just sheathed his blade when white feathers began slowly drifting down from the sky. He looked up.

Slayn, who had already died, reappeared. He tore off his black robe and shredded the bandages studded with nails, revealing his true form —

His entire body was deathly pale, and vivid human faces grew prominently on his upper body!

His pure white wings flapped behind him. Except for the lack of a halo symbolizing the Holy Spirit above his head, he looked like a living Holy Spirit!

Slayn specialized in Holy Spirit research. Not only had he successfully created creatures like the Holy Whale, but he had also mastered the technique of transplanting Holy Spirit bodies.

The three Holy Spirit faces on his body meant Slayn possessed three Holy Spirit hearts. Including his original body, that made four — four lives!

One of the three Holy Spirit faces slowly closed its eyes and rapidly withered. Clearly, Slayn had indeed been killed by Merlin, losing one precious life.

Slayn shook his sacred wings. Each Holy Spirit heart was his life's work, and suddenly losing one sent waves of extreme anger through him.

"As expected of our Holy Church's most feared enemy, truly extraordinary. But this is where it ends! Come, taste Holy Judgment!"

Slayn spread his wings, and the light of Divine Power shot upward like a sharp sword piercing the sky.

The oppressive pressure of a false god raged, creating rolling dark clouds. Light flashed, and a massive cross-shaped holy sword appeared, suspended above Merlin's head. The dense sacred aura clearly indicated a skill used by a Holy Spirit!

The Temple Knights watching from afar thought it was a divine miracle sent by the Goddess, and a urge to kneel and worship surged within their hearts.

Slayn flew to the top of the luminous cross sword and lightly stepped on it with his foot. The enormous holy sword crashed down!

"Vanish! Child of Vivian!"

Rumble — rumble —

The luminous cross sword descended with tremendous momentum, stirring up waves of pure white flames, as if it were heavenly punishment sent by a deity!

Merlin remained calm and composed. He drew his blade and slashed at the sky. A killing aura wrapped in demonic flames let out a furious roar, destroying both the cross sword above and Slayn himself!

A thunderous explosion rocked the sky, filled with sparks!

White feathers appeared once more. Slayn was reborn for the second time. The Holy Spirit face on his chest withered, leaving only his final Holy Spirit heart.

"No! What kind of bizarre iaijutsu is that?"

"Why is its power so enormous?"

"This is completely abnormal!"

The life force radiating from Angie was gradually dissipating. Alice's neck wound had also healed. The once-bright ring had grown dim and lost its healing power, now only usable as a spatial ring for storing items.

Helena placed her hand on Alice's chest. Though faint, she could still sense a heartbeat. "Miss Alice has a heartbeat now. We succeeded!"

"That's good. But it'll probably take time for her to wake up. Right now we should —" Puddum was just about to suggest a quick retreat when he noticed commotion on the other side.

"You despicable goddess lackey! Let her go! Otherwise I won't let you off!" Dru's chains floated up, surrounding the enemy.

Slayn was holding Blackman hostage, his emaciated hand gripping its throat as he loudly warned, "Don't you dare make any moves! Its life is in my hands. If you want it to survive, you filthy demons will behave yourselves! Don't think I don't know you snuck into the group. If I hadn't needed your help finding the Demon Castle, you'd have been dead long ago. And Alice — colluding with the demon race, she won't end well. The first thing I'll do when I return is burn her daughter alive!"

"You shameless charlatan, just a mere lackey!" Blackman was drenched in cold sweat. The opponent was far too powerful, and it had been completely suppressed.

"Hehehe, so what? As a lackey, I get to live, while you all will die here." Slayn's smile was brazen. In order to defeat Merlin, he had already abandoned all dignity and was resorting to any means necessary.

Helena picked up the unconscious Alice from the ground and anxiously asked, "What should we do now, Puddum?!"

"Tch!" Puddum gritted his teeth, thinking that they had been targeted by this old bastard after all. Using him to pin down Lord Merlin, when there had been a chance to lead his companions to safety!

Slayn was beginning to grow somewhat overconfident, seemingly not realizing at all —

At this moment, Merlin was a killing machine with no regard for anyone. Trying to stop his slaughter with Blackman was pure wishful thinking!

Slayn was choking Blackman by the throat, his nails already piercing into flesh. With a slight movement, its throat would be torn apart.

"Young Demon Lord, look who this is. It's your loyal subordinate, who genuinely respects you, who would go through fire and water for you, who has devoted themselves completely. Can you really bear to watch it die? Why not just meekly surrender to —"

Before the words were finished, an incredibly intense wave of demonic flames surged from a distance, engulfing Slayn and Blackman in an explosion of fire.

Under the scorching heat of the ultra-high-temperature flames, Slayn and Blackman were almost instantly reduced to ash, without even a chance to let out a pained scream.

Dru stared in shock, his eyes wide. He had never imagined his companion would die not at the hands of the Temple Knights, but at the blade of its own master.

"Blackman!!!"

There's more bonus content coming.

I hope everyone will wait until I finish explaining before saying anything. I haven't even finished explaining yet, and the power scaling is broken again, and again, and again?

I'm so anxious. I just wish I had eight hands so I could write the rest right now.

Gentlemen, I'm begging you for monthly tickets. Don't tell me you've all run out?

title: Chapter 32 — Fleeing
content:
Chapter 32 — Fleeing

Volume 35 · Chapter 32

"Heavenly Helena covered her mouth in horror, unable to believe her own eyes.

'Blake Drum.' Blaeptom closed his eyes, his entire body trembling uncontrollably, his heart burning with anger. Damn goddess dogs! Blackman didn't have to be sacrificed — that old bastard got him killed!

Demons had long anticipated this kind of situation; they just never expected it to actually happen.

At this moment, Merlin looked more like a ruthless Demon Lord than ever before. He hadn't hesitated to raise his sword against Alice, so dealing with old subordinates was equally no challenge for him.

The demonic flames dispersed, and both Sleighn and Blakeman had turned to ashes, with dark scorch marks left on the ground.

Suddenly, a pure white toad leaped out of the ashes, avoiding everyone's sight, and quickly fled into the distance.

'Doesn't he even spare loyal subordinates? Truly worthy of being the Demon Lord who slaughtered a hundred thousand palace knights without batting an eyelash. Though young, he's far more difficult to deal with than any Demon Lord before.'

This white toad was actually Cardinal Bishop Sleighn in disguise. He had already lost three Holy Spirit hearts, with no ability to regenerate left, only his final life remaining.

Sleighn's battle with Merlin had cost him heavily — even his body had been destroyed by the demonic flames. He could barely escape in toad form.

Sleighn had abandoned all thoughts of resisting Merlin. He only wanted to slip away as fast as possible. As for the palace knights... he couldn't care less anymore.

Merlin held Banri Garan in hand, flames blazing along the blade. His expression was cold, his gaze empty. He showed no reaction at all to having killed Blakeman!

Seeing Merlin advance again, the remaining fighting spirit of the palace knights was shattered. Fear dominated their souls, and their faith collapsed along with it.

Even the noble bishop had been burned to death. How could the knights possibly muster the courage to face Merlin? They abandoned their helmets and armor, fleeing in disarray, terrified of becoming the next unlucky soul to be incinerated.

'Run! Leave the Sand Sea quickly!' Drum was still relatively composed. Blakeman's death hadn't thrown him into chaos; his mind remained clear.

He was still reeling from the sight of his companions evaporating in flames.

'He's dead! We must stay calm! If we flee now, we still have a chance to leave alive!' Drum bowed his head and said in a low voice, 'Miss Alice is our hope. No matter what, we must ensure she leaves here alive. Only then do we have a chance to win!'

Drum took a deep breath and calmed down considerably. 'You're right.'

The white toad transformed from Sleighn arrived at an empty sand pit. After confirming the surroundings were safe, it opened its mouth and spat out a random teleportation scroll from its tiny body.

'Hehehe, luckily His Holiness the Pope favored me and gave me such a precious item. That guy's range of activity is limited. As long as I teleport to a place far from Demon City, I'll be completely safe~'

The white toad stretched out its long tongue, wanting to open the scroll and immediately escape this dangerous zone. But then —

Hummm —

A black shadow covered Sleighn. A wave of heat descended from above, making his entire body smoke.

Sleighn's toad body trembled violently. He subconsciously raised his head and saw Banri Garan's blade悬hanging directly overhead. He was nearly scared to death on the spot.

'Urgh! How could he notice me?! I've concealed all my aura!'

Merlin looked down at the toad Sleighn. His corrupted right eye reflected Sleighn's grotesque form.

'P-please don't kill me! I'm willing to do anything for you! I can even tell you the secrets of the Holy Spirits! Please, give me a chance to live!'

Sleighn was genuinely begging for his life this time, but it was already useless.

Merlin remained silent, impaling the toad Sleighn through the body with Banri Garan, personally sending the cardinal bishop to his death.

Above, in the sky, Helena cradled the unconscious Alice in her arms, while Pudo and Dulu escorted them.

Demons possessed flight ability, so their escape speed was far quicker than the palace knights.

Below, the palace knights were densely packed, chaotic like headless ants. But they weren't fools either — they realized the demons' escape direction was also the safe route, so they continuously crawled and stumbled, chasing after the demons.

'Can we escape?' Helena asked anxiously.

'I don't know. If there are humans in the Crusade Army stronger than us, then we're temporarily safe. Because His Majesty Merlin always loves challenging strong opponents, the weaker we appear, the safer we are right now.' Pudo thought for a moment before answering.

'Then wouldn't that mean it's our turn now?'

As soon as Dulu finished speaking, a gravity space slammed into the three flying demons, knocking them to the ground.

After Pudo got up, he saw the monstrous half of Merlin's face. 'Your Majesty...'

Helena's face turned pale, so terrified that her breathing became heavy. She could barely hold Alice in her arms.

'What do we do now?'

'I don't know... we can't beat him! Run? Running won't help either!' Pudo thought frantically but couldn't find any way to escape from Merlin.

Merlin's gaze locked onto the three demons. His left hand stroked the hilt of Banri Garan, while the demonic flame in his right eye flickered slightly.

Dulu suppressed the fear in his heart, exhaled deeply, as if making some kind of resolution. 'You two go first. Let me handle His Majesty Merlin.'

'Are you crazy?! You can't beat him!' Pudo shouted excitedly.

'I know I can't beat him.' Dulu, the deserter's son covered in stains, stepped forward resolutely at this moment. 'If I can buy you precious time, then my death will have been worthwhile. My father was a disgracefully cowardly man during the Holy War. This humiliation... I'll be the one to put an end to it.'

'But—'

Helena was about to say something, but Pudo stopped her. His expression grew solemn.

'I understand. Then I leave this to you, friend.'

Pudo grabbed Helena and quickly fled without looking back, appearing like a heartless bastard.

But for a baron like Pudo to call Dulu, this son of a deserter, his 'friend' — that was clearly regarding him as an equal, an enormous recognition.

In this race against time, there was no room for farewells. A single simple sentence was enough.

Pudo knew Dulu was serious. Persuasion would be useless. It was better to do everything possible to survive. Only in that way would their comrade's death have value. Cruel as it was, it was the most correct choice.

Merlin's gaze casually followed Pudo and Helena as they fled, but suddenly chains wrapped around him, forcibly turning his head back.

'What are you looking at? Your opponent should be me. Please show me the respect I deserve.' Dulu knelt on both knees, took out a perfectly clean white handkerchief from his chest, and placed it reverently before him. 'This is something you originally gave me. I never had the heart to use it. Thank you for your favor — for not minding my stains and ugliness, and for being willing to give me a chance to prove myself. You saved my sinful life. I am sincerely grateful—'

Merlin's face was expressionless. He tilted his head slightly toward Dulu, his head swaying.

'Heh. Saying all this, you can't hear me anyway, can you? Because you're not His Majesty Merlin — you're just an empty shell. Offending me—'

As soon as he finished speaking, countless chains flew from behind Dulu. The poisoned spikes gleamed with silver light, densely covering the sky, rushing toward Merlin like a mad swarm!

Merlin stood still, using his thumb to push forward a portion of Banri Garan's blade. A murderous sword intent surged outward in a devastating wave!

Dulu, kneeling on the ground, was instantly sliced to pieces. Blurry flesh and blood flew through the air —

One-shot kill!

Disgusting, Merlin. So disgusting.

How could anyone on the opposing side play with someone like this?

Right now 'Merlin-dog' is right beside me, everyone. Cast one monthly ticket, and I'll stab him in the back.

title: Chapter 33 — Crushing Defeat
content:
Chapter 33 — Crushing Defeat

Volume 35 · Chapter 33

Helena, clutching the unconscious Alice in her arms, had already fled far enough to be well outside Merlin's range of activity.

She glanced at Pudum beside her, whose expression was grim, and dared not ask anything further.

In times like these, when comrades fell in battle, no one could bring themselves to smile, and the atmosphere grew unbearably oppressive.

Pudum felt deep regret for Tullu. After finally breaking free from his father's shadow and rising to become a cadre of the Demon Lord Palace, he had ended up meeting such a fate.

The surviving Crusade Army soldiers scrambled to flee in every direction, their knightly dignity long forgotten, terrified that any moment of hesitation would see them slaughtered by the pursuing demons.

Their狼狈 retreat resembled nothing so much as a flock of sheep hunted by beasts, with not an ounce of courage to turn and fight back.

But if this group were allowed to escape so easily, it wouldn't be Merlin.

Suddenly, a terrifying gravitational pull surged from behind, tugging relentlessly at the fleeing formation.

A mighty gravitational space unfolded, and Merlin had no intention of sparing a single life as he dragged everyone who had escaped back into his domain.

The power of the gravitational field whipped up yellow sands, drawing them in toward Merlin. The Chaotic Crusade formation could not resist; many knights were swept into the sky.

Even Helena and Pudum, flying through the air, were severely affected and found themselves unable to escape the gravitational field's reach, instead being dragged backward toward Merlin.

Helena held the unconscious Alice tighter, gritting her teeth. "We can't escape like this. If we keep going, we'll just be pulled to His Majesty Merlin!"

Pudum tried pushing Helena forward from behind, but it was completely ineffective. Under the gravitational field, anyone lacking sufficient strength would be forcibly dragged toward Merlin.

"Damn it! Is there truly no way out?"

Pudum looked at Alice's dazed expression and once again recalled Tullu's decisive choice, then clenched his jaw and said solemnly—

"Helena, I'm leaving Miss Alice in your care. You must bring her back to the Holy City. As long as she lives, the demon race has hope of defeating Behemoth!"

"Huh?" Helena looked at Pudum in shock, faintly sensing his willingness to die, "Surely not? Could you also be wanting to—"

"There's no other choice. Although I deeply detest conflict, someone has to do this. I think I should step forward." Pudum lowered his head, his expression complex, unconsciously clenching his fists. He was still somewhat afraid of death and lacked Tullu's calm acceptance.

"Stay calm. Maybe, maybe there's still another way?" Helena found it hard to accept, not knowing how she would tell Lilith about everything that had happened here.

"There isn't. With no reinforcements arriving, the only way I can let you and Miss Alice escape is by sacrificing myself. This is far better than everyone dying here. Someone must convey what happened here and make preparations for the worst outcome—this is far more important than my life." Pudum had already seen through the calculus of survival and made his resolve.

"I think... this is too cruel." Helena's brows knit tightly; she could not bear to see another demon sacrifice themselves.

"But this is His Majesty Merlin. Almost no one escapes from his hands unscathed. If my death can secure victory for the demon race, then without a doubt, it is the most correct choice." Pudum pushed Helena with all his strength and shouted, "Don't look back! Just escape with everything you have. Take good care of Miss Alice—she is crucial to us!"

Helena bit her lip, desperately flapping her black wings to break free from the gravitational field. She could not waste this path to escape, bought with her companion's life.

Pudum abandoned all resistance and flew directly toward Merlin behind him. The magical tome known as *Merlin语录*, which was bound to his life, began to burn fiercely.

This magical weapon was linked to Pudum's life force. The destruction of the tome meant that his own life was reaching its end.

Sacrificing the entire magical tome, Pudum summoned forth Merlin's signature technique—the 999-tier Sword Drawing Art recorded within its pages.

"Let's go!"

As the magical tome burned to ashes, Pudum too lost all vitality. From within the layers of ash, violent killing intent surged, unleashing a devastating slash toward Merlin below.

The aura radiating from the sword art was extremely terrifying, with phantom blade edges flashing past the heads of the Holy Knights, causing massive explosions that sent them pressing themselves to the ground, trembling.

Merlin's eyelid twitched. Sensing the grave threat, he immediately stopped the gravitational field and launched a sword-drawing counterattack. Pillars of demonic fire erupted into the sky, scorching the entire sand sea and dyeing it with a crimson hue.

The two blade-drawing techniques collided head-on, triggering an enormous explosion that engulfed the fleeing Holy Knights. Everyone was swallowed by the raging flames.

Merlin's sword-drawing technique was clearly more powerful. The demonic fire wrapping around it scattered Pudum's summon, like a colossal wave crashing into an endless desert.

Watching Helena's retreating figure grow distant, Merlin could do nothing but sheathe his sword, the flames in his eyes slowly fading.

Alice lay cradled in Helena's arms, her eyelashes trembling faintly. In her blurry consciousness, she saw towering infernos, with countless Holy Knights evaporating within the flames—

*Merlin.*

*The 234th Crusade has failed.*

*Only two members survived.*

The Church had poured tremendous effort into this crusade, yet still proved unable to defeat the young Demon Lord.

Half a month later, word of the Church's crushing defeat spread. The losses were so severe that there was likely no strength left to organize a second expedition.

Somewhere in a little-known wasteland, Vivian emerged from the burrow where she had hidden for years. The blinding sunlight made her entire body uncomfortable.

"How long has it been since I last saw the sun?"

Abaddon stood respectfully beside her and replied, "Even this old servant has lost count. Since you took residence in this underground lair, this is the first time you have come to the surface."

"So long in ascetic seclusion that I've forgotten even the passage of time... I suppose I truly am growing old," Vivian said, her tone wistful.

"No, my lady. You will forever remain youthful. At your current realm, unless you encounter a formidable foe, your life will be eternal, and time will leave no trace upon you." Abaddon spoke softly.

"What is the situation?" Vivian's tone turned serious.

"The Church suffered a devastating defeat with massive losses. They no longer have the strength to stop a second offensive." Abaddon relayed the intelligence he had just gathered.

"As expected. The Church wanted to deal a heavy blow while the ancient demon god was still unsteady on its feet, but they moved far too slowly. If they had quickly assembled a small team to infiltrate the Demon Castle, there might have been a chance. Unfortunately, gathering a large-scale force wasted too much time. Behemoth should have long been prepared." Vivian paused, then a smile appeared on her face. "Still, the Church's heavy losses aren't entirely a bad thing. After all, they are our enemies as well. Perhaps this will keep this generation's Pope somewhat in line."

"Then, Your Majesty Vivian, what should we do next?" Abaddon asked tentatively.

"I trust the prophet's prophecy. Only my son can defeat Behemoth. We must find a way to shatter the demon-sealing pot." Vivian looked down at her own hands and spoke slowly. "However, I don't have full confidence in destroying a divine artifact. But I can certainly give it a try. We lack manpower now. How is Lilith doing?"

"Her Highness Lilith fled alongside the main cadres of the Demon Lord Palace when the demon race turmoil began. She is currently living with a human woman." Abaddon answered.

"Living with a human?" Vivian furrowed her brows. This was somewhat unexpected.

"That woman is His Majesty Merlin's human wife, and she was once a Hero as well." Abaddon spoke hesitantly, watching Vivian's expression closely.

A cold frost seemed to settle over Vivian's face, making it impossible to read her inner thoughts. Her tone turned icy. "Take me to see her."

■To Be Continued

Afterword

This volume may not be very friendly to friends who favor supporting characters, but it ends here. The next volume begins with a counteroffensive, with Vivian starring as the centerpiece in a story of maternal love and filial piety.

I'll sort out the next volume's counteroffensive content tonight. Everyone, rest early.

The next volume is the final chapter of the Demon Race arc, bringing a close to all the demon race plot threads.

I won't spoil specifics here. If you have spare monthly tickets, please cast them!

title: Chapter 1 — Integration
content:
Chapter 1 — Integration

Volume 36 · Chapter 1

The news of the 234th crusade's disastrous defeat spread across the human kingdoms, and many believers began to worry whether the demons would launch a counterattack against humanity, suffering a disaster like that of Britain. Due to this defeat, the Church suffered massive losses and hardly had any ability to form a new crusade; they also feared that the ancient demon god would leave the demon city and begin an assault on the human realms. Religious fervor within Britain cooled, the defeat of the crusade made many believers realize that mere faith could not defeat demons—they also needed sharp swords. The human alliance, which had been plotted for years, failed to achieve ideal results in its first operation, infuriating Pope Jiogeon; ultimately, it was still those short‑sighted rulers who liked to keep small accounts, unwilling to devote everything to the Church. At the same time, the chaotic demon realm endured a brutal slaughter, suppressing all opponents of Behemoth and unifying the demons. The Fifth Demon Lord's Palace, which originally belonged to Beelzebub, suffered an unprecedented devastation. Countless demon corpses lay scattered across the ground, their bodies riddled with bites from flesh‑eating flies, a gruesome sight. Several of Beelzebub's subordinates trembled in the distance, terror frozen on their faces, afraid to step forward. Beelzebub, controlled by demonic blood, tightly gripped his sister Miranda's neck and lifted her off the ground. “Your Majesty! What are you doing?” “Do you not recognize us?” “Stop! That’s your sister!” The demon subordinates shouted desperately, hoping Beelzebub would return to normal, but at this moment he could not hear them. Miranda felt her breathing grow difficult, her consciousness fading as she beheld Beelzebub's hideous demonic form, “Brother—” *crack*— Beelzebub snapped Miranda's throat with his own hands and coldly tossed her corpse aside. The demon subordinates behind were stunned by the scene; they knew how deeply Beelzebub cherished his sister Miranda, yet he had just killed her—who knows what has become of the Gluttony Demon Lord? Since Beelzebub returned here, he has launched a indiscriminate massacre against his former subordinates, leaving no survivors; any demon who tried to stop him was devoured clean by the flesh‑eating flies. This group of veterans who had followed Beelzebub for years could not comprehend how the demon lord, who had finally returned, had turned into a cold‑blooded killing machine. Beelzebub slowly turned, his eyes flickering with flames similar to Behemoth's, his hoarse voice saying: “Either sink or float with the great Behemoth.” “Or die.” The other demon lord palaces faced the same situation—opponents were suppressed, and the demons, wishing to survive, had to pledge allegiance to the ancient demon god. The power of all demon lord palaces was forced to merge together, becoming the vanguard for the assault on the Holy City.

Lilith, Ophelia, and Xiu have been carefully looking after Chris during this period, rarely going out and living cautiously in the Holy City.

Although Chris feels down whenever she thinks of her parents, Ophelia indeed has a way with children, constantly diverting Chris's attention so she can temporarily forget that her parents are not beside her.

"Heave-ho~ heave-ho~" Little Chris doodled on the drawing board with crayons, occasionally glancing up at Xiu opposite her. "What are you drawing?" Ophelia asked in a friendly tone, already quite familiar with the little one. "I'm drawing Uncle Xiu's portrait," little Chris exclaimed, holding up the drawing board eagerly to show off her "masterpiece." "Huh?" Xiu, hearing the little one drawing him, immediately straightened his posture, wondering why Chris kept looking at him—turns out she was using him as a model. "Let sister have a look." Ophelia looked at the drawing board with anticipation, her smile instantly freezing on her face, a look of wanting to speak but holding back. "How is it? Isn't it great? Chris's drawing skills are improving by leaps and bounds~" Little Chris jumped up and down, beaming with pride, displaying her just‑completed "Goat Eating Grass" picture. "This is overall not bad, right?" Ophelia forced a smile, thinking helplessly— "What the hell is this supposed to be? A total mess." "Surely this kid has no artistic talent at all; it must be the fault of that human woman—her virtues

title: Chapter 2 — Suppression
content:
Chapter 2 — Suppression

Volume 36 · Chapter 2

With a heart full of trepidation, Lilith opened the door and was shocked to find Helena standing outside!

Helena had clearly just returned to the Holy City, and the exhaustion on her face was severe.

This was not unexpected. Helena had managed to lead Alice out of the Sand Sea alive, but both her body and mind were pushed to their absolute limit.

"Helena!" Lilith exclaimed in surprise, thinking it was a Temple Knight on inspection duty.

Xiu immediately jumped down from the roof, no longer hiding himself. "How did the expedition go? Did you find the Sealed Demon Jar?"

"It was a failure. The expedition army was completely wiped out after entering the Sand Sea. Only Miss Alice and I survived," Helena said, her mood deeply dejected.

"What did you say?" Ophelia gasped, taken aback. "Where is Alice? Where is she?"

"She must go to the temple first to report what happened to the Pope," Helena explained.

"In that case..." Lilith said, her expression bewildered and disbelieving. "In that case... Pudom and the others..."

"That's right. They perished in the Sand Sea," Helena confirmed.

"What?!" Xiu showed utter disbelief. He felt that with so many Temple Knights present, Pudom and the others should have been able to protect themselves. "What on earth happened to you in the Sand Sea?"

Helena lowered her head, the pressure immense, momentarily unable to find the words to describe the event.

"We encountered an unexpected enemy."

Suddenly, a pained cry came from the temple. Pope Giovan collapsed to the ground, his face contorted in a grimace that was more painful than any smile.

"Failed again?"

"Yes. The Crusade Army was entirely buried in the Sand Sea. We couldn't defeat the enemy blocking our path, and we couldn't even get close to the Demon City," Alice replied, her head bowed, her tone helpless.

Blackford quickly helped Pope Giovan to his feet, comforting him, "Your Majesty, please pull yourself together. Since this has happened, we must accept this reality and not lose our composure."

"You're right," Pope Giovan nodded blankly, doing his best to suppress the urge to scream in rage, asking patiently, "What did you encounter in the Sand Sea? The scale of this Crusade Army was greater than ever, and you were leading it alongside Bishop Srein. How could it have been completely wiped out?"

"We..." Alice hesitated, her mind flashing back to Merlin's emotionless eyes and the countless people struggling in the demon fire.

Blackford saw the hesitation on Alice's face and assumed she was traumatized by her experience in the Sand Sea. He spoke in a gentle tone, "Alice, don't be nervous. This is the Holy City; you've left the dangerous Sand Sea. If you're feeling tired, why don't you go back and rest first?"

"No need," Alice shook her head, replying slowly. "We encountered Asmodeus III of the First Demon Lord Palace. He blocked our plan to attack the Demon City."

"Asmodeus III..." Pope Giogan gritted his teeth, his eye twitching with hatred. "That bastard again! I regret it so much. I should have forced O'Brien to kill it with the Knight's spirit back then! If I had, it wouldn't have become such a threat to us now! This is all my fault!"

Seeing the Pope about to have a heart attack from anger, Blackford soothed him, "Please take care of your health. This is not your fault. It was all because O'Brien was too stubborn back then."

Pope Giogan sat down, utterly disheartened. With each passing year, he found it harder to accept the setbacks of defeat.

He looked at Alice, a suspicion crossing his mind—did she bring bad luck to those around her? Both expeditions had ended in miserable failure, yet she was the only one who had returned alive and kicking.

But the Alice of today was no longer the clueless novice she once was. Her power was indeed strong enough to contend with the Demon Lords, yet she had unfortunately crossed paths with her nemesis?

The Church was now in dire straits, short of soldiers and generals. Giogan truly couldn't bear to banish Alice from the Holy City as he had before.

"I've understood the situation. Alice, you must be tired. Go back and get some rest. Greater difficulties may lie ahead for us."

"I am sorry for what happened," Alice said hesitantly.

"It's alright. I don't blame you at all. Everyone needs to experience failure to grow. Perhaps this isn't a bad thing. I hope you can become more mature in the future." Pope Giogan paused, then continued, "Go back. Your daughter must miss you. I sent knights a few days ago to bring your daughter to the temple for care, but it seems your friends don't like the Church very much?"

Alice's heart skipped a beat. She explained awkwardly, "They just don't like strangers. I hope you can understand."

Fortunately, the expedition army had been almost entirely wiped out. Otherwise, the fact that Alice had been with demons would have been exposed immediately. In that case, it wouldn't just be Alice and the other demons in danger; even the little one would be at risk.

After Alice left, the great hall fell into a suffocating silence. Giogan sighed, covering his face, and said sorrowfully, "Srein is dead too. Even though I gave him a teleportation scroll, he still didn't manage to survive."

"I've lost my most trusted confidant. Srein held the core secrets of studying the Holy Spirit; his value was far greater than anyone could imagine."

"If I hadn't hoped that he could repair the demon race's Blood Pool Seal, I would never have sent him to the battlefield."

Blackford frowned and asked in a low voice, "We have suffered an unprecedented blow. We must find a way to rally."

"This is too difficult. I don't believe that ancient demon god will forever hide in the Sand Sea. Its ambition is vaster than any opponent we've ever faced. We should prepare now for a fight to the death against the enemy that is coming."

Night had fallen. Because of the defeat, the residents of the Holy City had locked themselves indoors in panic, fearing that this ancient city, like Britain, might be attacked by the demons.

Alice walked along the central avenue at night. When she had left the Holy City, it had been with flowers and cheers; but now, her return was cold and desolate.

She looked at the "Angel" ring in her hand, its glow now dim. The ring had lost its powerful healing ability and had become an ordinary spatial ring.

Without this treasure Merlin had given her, she might well have died in this expedition.

She felt a pang of guilt regarding Pudom and the others, believing she bore an unshakable responsibility.

But before entering the Sand Sea, no one had known that the enemy they faced would be Merlin. For any opponent Merlin wanted to kill, even Alice would not escape—

The Church likely had no strength left to launch another expedition?

To get into the Demon City and find the Sealed Demon Jar...

Perhaps I should seek help from the Violet Knight Order?

Or Mr. Dawson at the Adventurers Guild headquarters?

Alice was contemplating her next steps when she suddenly felt a gaze watching her from the left alley. She looked up but saw nothing.

"Strange? Was it just my imagination?"

Just as she let her guard down, a black shadow darted over her head. She immediately gripped her slender sword and heightened her vigilance, scanning her surroundings.

"Who is there?"

The shadow lunged at her from the front, slamming her against the wall with brute force. Cold fingers choked her throat.

"W-who are you?!" Alice stammered, feeling a demonic aura.

The figure in black slowly pulled back her hood, revealing Merlin's mother, Vivien.

She tilted her head, her ruby-red eyes burning with intense killing intent!

title: Chapter 3 — Indirect Recognition (Monthly Ticket Extra)
content:
Chapter 3 — Indirect Recognition (Monthly Ticket Extra)

Volume 36 · Chapter 3

Vivian suppressed Alice with lightning speed, seizing her vital point.
Who would have thought Vivian's killing intent would be so heavy, her forceful nature exaggerated even beyond Merlin's memories?
The first meeting between Vivian and Alice turned out to be this way—Merlin would never have imagined it even in his dreams.

"Demon?!"
Alice saw Vivian's demon horns hovering above her forehead, and the aura she emitted was terrifying, far sharper than that of an ordinary demon.
Recalling the other demon lords she had seen, Alice thought the demon before her was even more overbearing, her demeanor locked down tightly—even Merlin couldn't compare.

"Shh." Vivian put her finger to her lips, making a silencing gesture, her smile turning grotesque. "This is the Holy City; I advise you not to shout loudly, otherwise it won't be just you who dies—all the residents here will be buried with you. Although I think humans taste sour and unpleasant, I've been starving for a long time and don't mind using you to fill my stomach. Do you understand?"

"Ugh!" Alice was startled; seeing the terrifying pressure emanating from this female demon, she didn't doubt the other would really carry out such a crazy act.
"It seems you've understood what I said." Vivian, hungry, stuck out her tongue and licked her red lips. "Actually, I don't want to kill in the Holy City, after all this is your territory."

A bead of cold sweat rolled down Alice's forehead, the icy claws on her neck nearly piercing her flesh.
"Is it her? Abaddon." Vivian turned to ask, glancing at Alice with the corner of her eye, tapping the flat plate armor on her chest, producing a dull thud. "Speaking of which, did we get the wrong person? This human looks utterly charm-less; I don't think she could seduce my son unless that kid has something wrong with his eyes."

Alice felt something stuck in her throat, unable to tell whether they were mocking her, wondering if they were commenting on how tightly her hero's inheritance armor was wrapped.
A black mist flashed, and Abaddon appeared beside Vivian, stepping forward to examine Alice closely, comparing her with the intelligence he had gathered.

"Another demon?" Alice looked at the elderly demon before her, her panic growing, "*Hey! You—"
Before they could finish speaking, Vivian suddenly lashed out, increasing her force; the stone wall behind Alice cracked with dense fissures. She stared icily into their eyes, saying, "Who gave you permission to speak? I warned you not to shout; are you rushing to seek death? Don't try to challenge my dignity—there will be no good outcome."

"Tch!" Alice felt her throat being choked, her breathing a little difficult.
Abaddon withdrew his gaze and replied respectfully, "No mistake, it's her; the traits match perfectly."

"Indeed it's her." Vivian withdrew her pressure, speaking meaningfully, "It's unbelievable that he would live with her—he's a hero, unafraid of danger, though his strength is merely passable; he probably poses no threat."

"Your Majesty, that's about enough." Abaddon reminded, "Coming to the Holy City on an adventure isn't about killing people."

Vivian snorted coldly and released Alice, clearly unable to accept Merlin being with humans, feeling strong aversion, and naturally gave Alice no pleasant expression.
If it weren't to see Lilith, Alice would likely have been ignored by Vivian, forgetting Merlin's dalliances in the human realms.

"Cough cough!" Alice coughed violently, her neck aching from being choked, but she temporarily relaxed, sensing the two demons harbored no malice—they had returned for some reason concerning her.
"Are you alright? Miss Alice, right?" Abaddon was much more courteous, even knowing her name, clearly having paid attention to her for a long time.

"Who are you? Are you also Merlin's subordinates?" Alice demanded angrily, her first impression of them poor, unlike Merlin's other subordinates who knew etiquette.
"Merlin's subordinates? Hah." Vivian let out a dry laugh, thinking her son had hardly mentioned her at all.

"No no, you've misunderstood. Upon first meeting, I am Abaddon-Alicek Otsuhaimer, steward of the First Demon Lord Palace. Although I haven't formally sworn allegiance to Lord Merlin, you may treat me as his servant—it's fine, but the one beside me cannot be allowed to speak."
Abaddon hinted to Alice not to speak recklessly.

"Ah? Who is she?" Alice glared at Vivian with hostility, still resentful about what just happened.
"This is Vivian Lucifer, the second master of the Pride Demon Lord's Hall, namely Merlin's mother." Abaddon introduced solemnly.

"Ah? ? ?" Alice stood frozen, her mind blank, unable to look away from Vivian—
Is this really Merlin's mother?
What's going on, suddenly appearing here?
But indeed she resembles Merlin somewhat, even sharing that arrogant, smug demeanor.

Vivian, seeing Alice silent and just staring at her, remarked, "This guy seems not very bright."
"Perhaps it's because you're too nervous to see me?" Abaddon said awkwardly.

"Uh! Hello, Alice came to her senses, flustered, the sudden event leaving her unsure how to face it—she even felt a bit timid—"I'm Merlin's roommate!"

Vivian and Abaddon exchanged a glance, obviously startled by Alice's reply, contrary to their expectations.
"What are you hiding? We all know you're my son's human wife, not to mention you already have a child—what's her name?" Vivian—when trying to recall.

"Your Majesty, her name is Chris, a very lovely girl." Abaddon's intelligence work was decent; he had even learned the names of their two daughters.

"Yes, her name is Chris; this child surprises me—I thought you two wouldn't have any love-child, but things have developed this way. Although I dislike human-demon hybrids, the deed is done, and I need to see her." Vivian's expression was grim; as a +point traditional demon, her feelings were very complex, unable to accept Alice, yet she could not deny that the mixed-blood granddaughter is a family member—unfortunately she cannot be accepted by all demons, leaving her in a very awkward position.

Alice didn't absorb a word; her mind was filled with Vivian's earlier remarks—
"You are my son's human wife!"
That sounded like an acknowledgment to her!
Originally Alice felt uneasy seeing Vivian, never expecting her to be so "agreeable," easily gaining that "approval." Alice's face flushed slightly, and she politely reintroduced herself.

"That's right! I am Merlin's wife, thank you for your recognition and acceptance!"
Vivian: "???"
Abaddon: "!!!"
The two demons exchanged glances again, finding Alice's behavior out of the norm, leaving them speechless.

"Um..." Abaddon said with a strange expression, lowering his voice, "Perhaps Miss Alice isn't foolish after all; maybe she's quite clever?"

"Tsk!" Vivian rubbed her forehead, face dark with irritation, saying—
"No, I didn't mean that just now..."

Are you there? Brother? Any more?

title: Chapter 4 — Long Separation
content:
Chapter 4 — Long Separation

Volume 36 · Chapter 4

"Never mind, I don't want to talk about this now." Vivian looked at the armor Alice was wearing and easily recognized it as precious equipment specifically provided for Heroes, so she asked, "Are you the Hero for this crusade?"

"That's right." Alice answered shyly.

"I heard your crusade army was annihilated. Did you encounter the ancient Demon God Behemoth in the desert?" Vivian pretended to be casual, hoping to get detailed intelligence on Behemoth.

"No, we didn't encounter the ancient Demon God. We only found the Demon City hidden deep in the desert, and couldn't even get close," Alice answered honestly.

"Strange, you didn't even see Behemoth, so how were you completely wiped out? I heard the Church's crusade this time was much larger than before, and they couldn't even break into the Demon City," Vivian suspected Alice wasn't telling the truth and countered, "Were the crusade soldiers all old, weak, and sickly?"

"You're mistaken. We encountered unexpected enemies, which is why we returned in defeat." Alice's face grew gloomy as she recalled the merciless Merlin.

"Unexpected enemies? As far as we know, Behemoth doesn't have any powerful allies." Abaddon asked doubtfully; it had investigated for a long time and was certain the enemy was isolated among the demon race.

"It's Merlin. We encountered Merlin. The crusade army couldn't defeat it and was reduced to ashes in the flames. Only Helena and I barely escaped." Alice answered truthfully.

Vivian's face instantly turned extremely ugly. She asked in disbelief, "That's impossible, right? My son, how could he help the enemy? Are you teasing me?"

"I'm not clear on the specifics either, but according to Helena, Merlin's soul was extracted and his body was modified by the Demon God into a puppet that can be manipulated at will. So now he only follows the Demon God's orders and can't recognize us." Alice only knew this much for now. At this moment, Merlin had completely become a killing tool used by Behemoth.

Abaddon was astonished and lost his words. Clearly the situation was unexpected and had become very troublesome. "Although we knew Behemoth could easily manipulate first-generation demons, we didn't expect it could also modify other demons' bodies, turning them into mindless tools."

"Damn! Why did things turn out like this?" Vivian felt a headache. After hearing this news, she could no longer act rashly.

"Your Majesty, since Prince Merlin has already been controlled by the enemy, I fear the other Demon Lords have also fallen into their clutches. The enemy we face may not be just Behemoth." Abaddon immediately saw the key point, and gravity settled between his brows.

Before leaving the cave, Vivian had already made a plan to deal with Behemoth, but after hearing this news, the plan was useless.

Because the enemies Vivian might face included not only the terrifying Behemoth but also the lineup of Demon Lords, including her own son Merlin.

Although Vivian had trained hard for a long time and her strength could now rival the former first-generation Demon Lords, facing so many powerful enemies gave her no confidence at all. If someone could share the pressure, she might try.

"I didn't expect the situation had developed to such a complicated state. To pull the demon race back from the brink of danger isn't as easy as I thought." Vivian took a deep breath and felt she must now grasp all the circumstances, then find a breakthrough anew.

"Your Majesty, are you confident you can defeat your son?" Abaddon asked tentatively.

"What do you mean? You don't think I can't even discipline my own son now, do you?" Vivian's face darkened, feeling her authority as a mother was challenged.

"But based on his usual behavior, I think he's no longer that incompetent prince he used to be." Abaddon said in a tactful tone.

"Yes, fighting against Merlin is dangerous. He doesn't recognize anyone now, not even his own loyal subordinates." Alice warned.

"Hah, do I really have to fight my own son? Can't I avoid—"

The moment she finished speaking, footsteps suddenly rang out from outside the alley.

Temple Knights held torches and patrolled the Holy City as usual.

A keen-eyed knight spotted them, immediately became alert, drew his sword from his waist, and shouted—

"Who's inside!? It's a special time. Nighttime outings are not allowed. Come out!"

Vivian immediately put on a hat to hide her horns, her eyes burning with murderous intent.

Abaddon also grew serious, silently gripping the poison dagger in his sleeve, ready to kill the Temple Knights at any moment.

"……Please calm down. I'll go talk." Alice stopped the two demons, not wanting to cause a big scene in the Holy City.

"You'd better be mentally prepared. If things go badly, they'll all be killed. I won't allow our traces to be discovered by the Temple." Vivian said coldly.

"Leave it to me."

Alice took a deep breath, walked out of the alley, and smiled while asking the Temple Knights.

"What's wrong? It's me. I was talking with a few friends. Is there a problem?"

"The Hero?" The leading Temple Knight was startled. "I'm very sorry. We're on patrol. The Holy City is under curfew now. You should reduce your activities at night."

"I just returned to the Holy City today, so I'm not clear about it." Alice answered awkwardly.

"As for you, it's no problem, but what about your friends?" The leading knight squinted into the alley, but the light was too dark to see clearly.

"If you have doubts, I'll call them out so you can inspect them." Alice said tentatively.

"No no no. If they're your friends, there must be no problem. We still have other places to patrol." The leading knight slightly bowed. "Pardon me."

Alice watched the Temple Knight patrol leave, secretly sighing with relief inside. She, the Hero, had acted like a thief in front of Temple Knights?

"It seems Alice-san can be relied on. Both of you trust her quite a bit. Maybe you were overthinking?" Abaddon said softly.

"Never let your guard down around any human. That's a lesson from history, Abaddon."

The demons' residence in the Holy City, after Helena's narration, already knew what had happened in the desert.

"Merlin has been controlled by the Demon God? Then we're all doomed?" Ophelia said in panic.

"We originally planned to rescue His Majesty from the Demon Sealing Vase, then defeat Behemoth with His Majesty's power. But now His Majesty has become the enemy. We have almost no chance of winning." She sighed long and couldn't think of any way to save the situation.

"Blackman, Pudom, and Duru all perished. What a heavy blow to us." Ophelia didn't doubt for a second that if she faced the current Merlin, she would be killed cruelly too.

"You all..." Helena wanted to speak but stopped, feeling the demons had lost their fighting spirit just because Merlin stood on the opposite side.

Lilith kept her face cold and said nothing, her teeth grinding "咯咯" (clacking), her anger reaching its peak.

Knock knock knock—

The knocking sound came. Lilith thought Alice was back, so she "sprang" up from her chair, rushed to open the door, and started cursing without even looking who it was.

"How dare you come back? It's all because of you that we're in this terrible state. You're a—"

"Cough!" Vivian's face gave no expression as she looked at her grown daughter.

"Huh?" Lilith sensed something was wrong, looked closely, and was immediately scared stiff—

"Pfft!!!"
