title: Chapter 5 — Monthly Ticket Extra Chapter
content:
Chapter 5 — Monthly Ticket Extra Chapter

Volume 36 · Chapter 5

Vivian originally wanted to take a good look at her cute daughter, but she didn't expect to be sprayed with saliva as soon as she came up. She suddenly realized her daughter was no longer as cute as when she was little; her temper had become unusually irritable. Vivian's face showed a few more signs of displeasure; this wasn't quite like the mother-daughter reunion she had imagined? Alice hid behind Vivian, seeing Lilith suffer, she inexplicably felt a bit pleased~. "Good heavens! I must be dreaming! This is impossible!" Lilith timidly stepped back, turned and asked, "Hey! Can you all see? My mother has risen from the dead! She's standing outside the door—surely I'm not the only one who can see her? No way! Give me some reaction!" "What are you talking about? Isn't it just me standing outside the door?" Alice said with a completely serious expression, taking the opportunity to add fuel to the fire. "Yah!!" Lilith let out a terrified scream, her face turned pale, she was frightened badly, covering her head and saying, "Ghost! It's my mother's ghost! It must have come to take me away—who are you guys? Come save me!!" Vivian was speechless, the veins on her forehead throbbing, she was angry enough at her stupid daughter. Other demons seeing Vivian's silhouette appear outside the door were all shocked and froze in place. In their understanding, Vivian had died long ago and could not possibly reappear! Several demons looked at Vivian; although they were much calmer than Lilith, they still looked as if they had seen a ghost—. "Your Majesty Vivian!" Ophelia widened her eyes, not blinking. "This is not an illusion." Xiu's expression turned serious, thinking maybe Her Majesty Vivian hadn't died? No wonder the battle with the Hero of the Spear was so strange! Indeed, there's something fishy! "Helena isn't a demon of the First Demon Lord Palace, but she still knows something about Vivian—she knows Vivian is a deceased monarch, yet now she's standing alive before her!" "What did I do wrong to be entangled by my mother's ghost? Could it be that my perfunctory yearly visits to the tombstone have been discovered?" Lilith couldn't help muttering to herself. "Oh?" Vivian sensed something interesting, placing her hand on Lilith's head, seeming to caress but actually gripping tightly, "My cute daughter, you seem to have grown quite a bit taller~" "Ow ow ow ow!" Lilith felt her skull about to split open. "Your Majesty, please calm down." Abaddon reminded her from behind, sweating. "Father? Why are you here?" Ophelia came to her senses, her gaze fixed in shock on Abaddon. "Long time no see, Ophelia. You've done well with the tasks I entrusted you, except for not being satisfied with letting His Highness Merlin inherit the throne, you've done your best in everything else, and I'm relieved." Abaddon nodded satisfactorily. "Where have you been all these years you disappeared?" I still—Ophelia glared angrily at her father, words stuck in her throat. "I have always been by Her Majesty Vivian's side; many matters need to be kept secret, so I couldn't casually contact you, sorry." Abaddon felt some guilt for having disappeared for so long. Xiu took a deep breath, continually calming his current shock—. "What is all this?" "Not only has Her Majesty Vivian returned from the dead—" "Has Senior Abaddon also come back?" "That's how it is. Left with no choice, I could only give up on extracting the puppet controlled by Behemoth, temporarily leave the demon race by feigning death, then accumulate strength to prepare for a future counterattack." Vivian recounted all the past events; the demons, hearing so much at once, were dumbstruck, and only after a long time did they barely digest it. Before Vivian, all the demons became very solemn and restrained, not as relaxed as when they were with Merlin; even the hot-tempered Lilith turned into a meek lamb. Compared to Merlin, perhaps the seasoned traditional Demon Lord Vivian is the true master of the Demon Lord Palace whom they submit to in body and spirit. "I see. In that situation, you made the right choice. At that time you had no evidence, so you couldn't topple Belial, whose foundations run deep in the demon race; doing so would have alerted the enemy, and you couldn't casually announce that Behemoth's soul had escaped the seal, as that would only worsen the demon race's internal and external troubles." Xiu understood everything, nodded, and said, "You're right. If it weren't for your return today, we would now be like headless flies in chaos; now you are our sole spiritual pillar." "Being able to understand this quickly shows I didn't misjudge you, Xiu—your talents are very suited to staying by my side." Vivian felt that this old subordinate of hers hadn't changed at all, still sharp. "You flatter me; I'm only suited for doing things that shouldn't see the light, and I'm hardly worth mentioning." Xiu replied modestly. "So..." Ophelia's expression was complex, she looked resentfully at her father Abaddon, "Because of Her Majesty Vivian's decision, you've been playing hide-and-seek with me, not contacting me for so long?" "I did occasionally look at you from afar, but you just didn't notice." Abaddon answered expressionlessly. "Isn't that going too far?" Ophelia, somewhat incoherent, her resentment heavy, "Even if you told me these things, it wouldn't matter—I would never leak them." "No, to deceive the enemy you must first deceive those close to you; isn't that the most basic awareness?" Abaddon explained. "" Ophelia was at a loss for words, angered by her stubborn father to the point of liver pain. Helena dared not speak casually, yet she felt astonished—originally the blood pool seal had already been problematic, only now erupting; her lord is addicted to cross-dressing sorcery and cannot extricate herself, basically paying no attention to the blood pool seal. "Dear Mother, how is this pressure?" Lilith leaned on Vivian's shoulder, putting on a fawning expression. "Press a little harder; I'm not here, you're used to being pampered, your massage skills aren't as good as before?" Vivian's anger hadn't subsided, "I've been gone so long, you haven't made any progress at all; you're an adult yet your strength is still wobbling around the Saint-tier—are you really my daughter? Merlin, as your older brother, has been too indulgent toward you." "Mm." Lilith pouted aggrievedly; the stern mother had just returned, and she instantly lost all status, being treated by her own mother as a maid to be ordered around and scolded at will. "I basically understand your situation; I regret things with Pluton and the others." Vivian paused, then spoke solemnly, "However, we must get Merlin back to normal, because the prophecy of the seer is undeniable—only my son can defeat Behemoth, and destroying the Demon-Sealing Vase is the crucial key." Alice lowered her head, curious about the seer's prophecy content—why does the demon race everywhere bear the shadow of that demon? "Miss Alice, could you take out your treasure and let me have a look?" Vivian suddenly looked over. Alice startled, drew out the Hymn of Light, and carefully held it square in her hand. The holy aura emanating from the slender sword made the demons present feel very uncomfortable; even Vivian frowned. "Ha, so that's it?" Vivian revealed an understanding smile, as if recalling something—. "The Goddess Maria forged a wicked divine artifact from the darkest part of her heart." "Born to kill the great prophet, it is the sinful—" "So the legends are really true?"

title: Chapter 6 — Sorry for the late update
content:
Chapter 6 — Sorry for the late update

Volume 36 · Chapter 6

Alice raised her head in surprise and asked, “Do you know this sword?”

“A treasure with such pure holy aura—aside from the lofty goddess, who could forge it?” Vivian paused, then added, “Actually, after the Age of Gods, it’s become very hard to forge new divine artifacts; most of those once‑famous treasures have vanished along with the ancient gods.”

“You mean…?” Alice looked at the Light Chant in her hand, “It comes from heaven?”

“Of course. When I was little, I once heard my father tell a story.” Vivian recalled slowly, “The goddess, in order to kill our great prophet, used her own heart as material and personally forged a sinister blade, lodging the power of the main god inside it. It has overwhelming restraint against dark‑natured things, and was created specifically to deal with the prophet.”

Alice frowned; Vivian’s words indeed matched the essence of the Light Chant—holy exterior hiding a sinister core.

“I can’t imagine such a precious thing falling from heaven to the mortal world… that’s not normal.” Vivian turned to Alice, her expression serious as she questioned, “Where did you get it?”

“I don’t know either; it’s my teacher’s hidden sword, and I stole it.” Alice answered somewhat embarrassedly.

“Your teacher? Who is she?” Vivian pressed on.

“My teacher used to be a knight of the Spanish Kingdom, but she’s already passed away.” Alice recalled Claudya, her expression dimming.

“A knight?” Vivian furrowed her brows, wondering how a knight could obtain such a treasure—could the goddess have lost it and someone picked it up?

“To kill our prophet, that goddess actually didn’t hesitate to cut out part of her own heart as material just to forge a weapon capable of slaying the prophet.” Xiu found this horrifying—what hatred would drive someone to such a mad act?

“Yeah, what exactly did the great prophet do? After ages, this hatred still hasn’t faded.” Helena sighed.

“I’m not entirely clear on that either, but the heavens’ hostility toward us has always existed; even before the Holy War, our struggle with the spirits never ceased.” Vivian obviously didn’t know much, and she didn’t trust the stories compiled by the church clergy.

“It’s normal for the goddess to be hostile toward demons; after all, in the Age of Gods she was humanity’s leader, personally destroying our era and bringing prosperity to humans—it’s only natural.” Abaddon lowered his head, offering his view, “The prophet is our leader, and also the obstacle to human prosperity.”

After Abaddon’s explanation, a few demons felt it made some sense; to lead their people toward prosperity, they could understand doing some crazy things.

“Mother, my brother was sealed and after that he had brief contact with Helena, saying this sword should be able to destroy the Demon‑Sealing Vessel.” Lilith behind* Vivian's shoulder, gently reminding her.

“Exactly, that’s what I said. Your Majesty Vivian, what do you think the chances are of destroying the Demon‑Sealing Vessel?” Helena asked eagerly, now Vivian had become the backbone of the remaining demons.

Vivian fell silent for a moment, considered many points, then replied—

“That line of thinking isn’t wrong; light‑attribute divine items have strong restraint against dark‑attribute objects, and besides, the Demon‑Sealing Vessel is merely a functional divine artifact—it may not be as sturdy as we imagine.”

“If I were the owner of this divine item, I’d have ninety percent confidence in destroying the Demon‑Sealing Vessel.”

“Unfortunately, its owner—” Uh!” Alice grew much more nervous, wondering what she had done wrong—did Vivian still not approve of her?

“Haha~” Lilith finally seized the chance, sneering, “Indeed, you can’t rely on this human woman at all; I knew asking her for help was a mistake!”

Alice clenched her silver teeth, unable to lash out in front of Vivian.

“You’re not even more hopeless than that?” Vivian gave her daughter a disdainful glance.

“Respected, beautiful, unmatched Mother, I’ll do my best.” Lilith put on a mournful face and earnestly massaged Vivian’s shoulders and legs.

*Even if Miss Alice’s ability is still lacking, she is the owner of this sword and still has a good chance of destroying the Demon‑Sealing Vessel.” Vivian gave up trying to destroy the vessel with her own power; using the Light Chant is clearly more reliable.

“But we now face a huge difficulty—with His Majesty Merlin and the other demon lords present, we have no chance to get near the demon city, let alone find the Demon‑Sealing Vessel.” Xiu’s tone was helpless; the forced assault on the demon city had already been tried, with heavy losses.

“If His Majesty Merlin truly is the demon prophesied to defeat Behemoth, then the situation has become dire beyond measure—he stands on the opposing side, this… no solution.” Helena clenched her fists, already lacking the courage to set foot in the Sand Sea again.

“Why do you think we must first defeat several monarchs before we can destroy the Demon‑Sealing Vessel? Can’t we avoid them and go straight to face Behemoth?” Vivian looked at the demons, speaking meaningfully, “Those demon lords controlled by Behemoth are merely pieces he can discard at any time; the death of their bodies means the souls inside the Demon‑Sealing Vessel will also perish. Studying how to deal with those demon lords? That’s falling into the enemy’s trap.”

Ophelia suddenly understood, astonished, “Ah, so if we think about defeating the demon lords, that’s a losing situation.”

“Wanting to bypass the controlled demon lords and go straight to face Behemoth? Almost no way, as long as the enemy stays entrenched in the demon city, we have no opportunity.” Xiu frowned slightly, unable to help but feel a headache.

“Behemoth has been sealed in the blood pool for ages, enduring humiliation and torment—do you really think he only wants to enslave our demons?” Vivian said meaningfully, “Be patient; he won’t stay hidden in the Sand Sea forever.”

The next day, little Chris woke up to a sweet scent, and only when the sunlight outside the window stung her eyes did she reluctantly lift her little bottom, stretching like a cat.

“You’re awake, little cutie?”

Vivian just lay quietly beside her, silently watching the whole night through, unwilling to wake the little one.

After Alice’s introduction, she learned a lot about her granddaughter and gained a preliminary understanding.

“Huh?” Little Chris turned her head to see Vivian, this stranger, looking at her with a dark, sinister smile; she thought she’d just woken up only to be kidnapped again, her mind going blank.

“Are you hungry right after waking, lacking energy? Actually I’m hungry too.”

Vivian stuck out her tongue, licked around her red lips, a wicked gleam flashing in her eyes—like an old witch who eats children.

She thought her smile was kind and gentle, but in Chris’s eyes it was nothing of the sort.

“Mmm!!!”

Little Chris’s face turned pale, she bit her lip, and from her throat came a series of sharp screams, her soul almost frightened out of her body.

Only see the little one stiffly lying in the baby crib, scared by Vivian to the point of breaking the connection.

Vivian couldn’t understand, turned back and asked, “Do I look scary?”

Lilith didn’t dare speak casually, just kept nodding like a chick pecking rice, thinking—

Please have some self‑awareness!

Your brother and you share the same demeanor; when you smile you look like an ill‑intentioned ruffian!

Spare Chris, she’s still a

title: Chapter 7 — Gathering of the Demon City
content:
Chapter 7 — Gathering of the Demon City

Volume 36 · Chapter 7

Little Chris hid in Alice's arms, still unable to recover from the morning's fright, feeling that Vivian was not kind and gentle at all, but rather like an evil old witch lurking deep in the forest. Especially just after waking up and seeing Vivian's "ill-intentioned" smile, it cast a sizable shadow over the youngster's tender heart. Chris sneakily glanced at Vivian, then shoved herself deeper into the crook of Alice's arm. "Don't be afraid, she's your father's mother, that is, your grandmother. Say hello properly." Alice whispered encouragingly to Chris, hoping she could be brave, since she could get along fine with a bunch of ordinary demons, so why was she timid and hesitant with her grandmother? Chris's little hand gripped Alice's clothes tightly, burying her head even deeper, still feeling scared. Alice showed a helpless expression and explained, "Sorry, this child has always been shy around strangers." "Really?" Vivian looked at the little one with a complex expression, thinking perhaps she herself was too frightening? After finally getting to see her granddaughter, the girl refused to get close to her. "Pfft" Lilith laughed on the side, a bit schadenfreude. "What are you laughing at?" Vivian gave Lilith a stern glare. "Hehehe." Lilith's eyes darted about nervously, thinking that's exactly why the kid doesn't want to get near you! After leaving the Demon Lord Palace for so long, can't you still put on airs? "Strange, where exactly is the problem?" Vivian furrowed her brow, puzzling to Lilith, "Just like your brother, you've been rejecting me since childhood, as if there's a huge barrier between us? Or are you just more clingy to me?" "Well... I had no choice; when I was little I preferred playing with gentle Ophelia sister." Lilith responded awkwardly. "What did you say?" Vivian's face darkened, her mood not good. "This is also unavoidable; you were so busy when we were young, you had no time to accompany us; it was all Ophelia sister taking care of me and my brother." Lilith defended herself, sweating. "So..." Vivian looked despondent, muttering lowly, "Do my children not like me? As a mother, what a failure—I'm surely doomed, destined to end up alone and miserable, how tragic." "???" Lilith was a bit taken aback, cautiously saying, "Do you really care about these things?" "How could I not? Do you think my heart is made of stone?" Vivian showed a pitiful look, sadly saying, "I've been quietly caring for you all, but because I spent little time with you, you've started to drift away. Being a mother is really hard." "We haven't drifted away from you; when we heard of your death, both I and my brother were heartbroken." Lilith said in a comforting tone, unable to bear seeing her mother unhappy. "Don't say that; I know I'm a failed mother with many flaws, but I can't see them myself. You'd better have a good talk with me, give me a chance to correct myself." Vivian's eyes glistened with crocodile tears. "Huh? You're serious?" Lilith stared wide-eyed, astonished—such a good thing had never happened before! The overbearing mother was actually willing to listen to her children's opinions? "Of course, I also want to become the kind of person you like; this is my dream." Vivian said sincerely. "Cough cough!" Lilith felt the opportunity was rare, gradually getting cheeky, "Your biggest problem is being too strict; in front of your domineering self I feel I have no status, I have to obey everything you say. I need the most basic respect; a normal mother should devote everything to me, pave the way, smooth out all difficulties, let me live a life of having clothes handed to me and food placed in my mouth, then you can just disappear, stop showing up in front of me and ruining my good mood. If you can do all that, you're a qualified mother—keep it up~" Vivian kept a stony face, silent, feeling the urge to start over. "What's that expression? Is it because you made me say that?" Lilith shrank her neck, feeling a chill down her back. Vivian clapped her palm onto Lilith's forehead, ruthlessly pinching her head, "Ah, is that all? I didn't expect your demands to be so many; I might as well just get a new daughter—it'd be easier. Your opinion is just for me to hear; whether I adopt it or not depends on my mood." "Ow ow ow ow!" Lilith's head felt like it was splitting, thinking Mom will always be Mom—how could that domineering her possibly listen to anyone else's opinion? "Really, compared to when you were little, you're worlds apart, not cute at all. Hurry up and turn back into a child, turn!" Vivian thought, if she knew there was an elixir to turn back time, she'd definitely pour two buckets down Lilith's throat right now. "Don't... don't force me!" Alice had spent a long time comforting Chris, telling her some things about Vivian, making her realize that that fierce old woman was actually a close relative. She set the little one on the ground, patted Chris's butt, and encouraged, "Go on, don't be scared, call her grandma." Chris looked at Vivian, then whispered softly, "Scary, Chris will get eaten." "What's there to be afraid of? She won't hurt you; do you think your dad is scary?" Alice patiently countered. "Not scary." Chris shook her head in a babyish voice. "Then what's there to worry about? She's the one who raised your dad." Alice rubbed Chris's head. The little tuft on Chris's head wiggled, she pouted her lips, "I'll work hard for Mom." "Huh?" Alice was taken aback, thinking don't make it sound like you're going to the battlefield for me! Chris stiffly moved her short carrot-like legs toward Vivian, looking full of momentum but her voice was like a mosquito's, "Grandma." Vivian picked up the little one and planted a hard kiss on her forehead, leaving a red lip print. Chris's face flushed red, she covered her little face, not daring to resist, and in front of her grandmother she behaved dozens of times more obedient than usual. "So you get shy this easily? Just like your dad when he was little—maybe he never got a chance to go out and play, today Grandma will take you out to play." "Wait! This is the Holy City, it's dangerous!" Lilith thought, a million objections in her mind. "Those Holy Temple Knights can't do anything to me; there's no danger, I'm just taking my little granddaughter out for a walk, I'll conceal my identity, you all don't need to follow me—too many eyes, too much fuss." Vivian said in an unquestionable command tone. Alice had some reservations but couldn't stop Vivian; after all, as a Hero she could evade the Holy Temple Knights' inspections, and having her along would be a bit safer. "Respected Mother, we still have more important things to do, not the time to take your granddaughter out to play." Lilith said with a fake smile. "The more important matters have already been entrusted to Xiu; we'll just wait for news tonight." Vivian said, then took the little one and left the room. Lilith's head was full of question marks, "Xiu?" In the demon city of the sand sea, demons subservient to Behemoth kept pouring in. An ominous crow flew over the demon city's sky, letting out a disgusting call.

title: Chapter 8 — Arsenal
content:
Chapter 8 — Arsenal

Volume 36 · Chapter 8

Looking like an ordinary crow, it is actually Xiu's familiar, able to see everything through the crow's eyes. Xiu needs to investigate two things: the movements of Behemoth, and where the Sealing Demon Vessel is hidden in Demon Castle. The crow circles in the sky, looking down at the scene below, the chaotic Demon Castle fully in view. The demons of the other Demon Lord Palaces, who originally intended to rise up in resistance, are all suppressed by the Demon Lords. All opponents are executed, while those demons willing to submit are gathered in Demon Castle, forming a massive army, preparing to launch a fierce attack on the Holy City of Vatican. Maemon's subordinate Ose is also among the demon horde, terrifiedly looking around, seeking the terrifying figure of Behemoth. After the turmoil at the Seven Kings Conference, it slipped back to its lair, always hiding in the Demon Lord Palace, not daring to leave easily. The situation within the demon race is extremely chaotic; Ose also does not dare to stir up trouble, merely observing silently. Although Ose's accusation against Merlin at the conference had no basis and did not affect Behemoth's plan, in a sense it still contributed a share of force to the demon race falling into danger's brink. Upon learning that the other Demon Lord Palaces are organizing troops, preparing to perish together with Behemoth, it also gathered some remnants of Maemon, preparing to join this resistance. However, the blood-controlled Samael suddenly appears, suppressing all opponents; Ose has no choice but to surrender and comes here. The originally damaged blood pool has been remodeled by Behemoth into an 'arsenal'; countless human-faced scorpion demons are continuously produced, emitting terrifying hisses from the depths of the blood pool, wishing to break free from their bonds and gain freedom. The scorpion demons encountered by the Crusade Army in the desert sea were personally created by Behemoth, possessing an aura similar to that of the original demons. Ose watches each powerful scorpion demon being born, his heart filled with shock and fear— In such a short time, Behemoth has actually created a troop loyal to himself!? It seems their strength is not bad; at the very least they possess power close to that of demon officers. What exactly does he intend to do? It seems we don't even need to— Ose's gaze falls upon the damaged altar; several Demon Lords corroded by demon blood stand like sculptures, their icy eyes sweeping over the demons below, guarding against anyone with ill intentions suddenly jumping out to rebel. Merlin notices Ose's gaze, immediately fixing him with his hollow eyes, wondering if he is recalling the events of the Seven Kings Conference? Ose, guilty and furtive, hastily lowers his head, lacking the courage to meet Merlin's eyes, praying in his heart that Merlin does not remember his scheme against him, otherwise he will surely die! Panicked Ose does not know that the demon lords corrupted and controlled are merely shells, possessing no memories at all. "Your Majesty Samael! It's me! Don't you recognize me?" a demon officer cannot help but jump out, stepping forward with gritted teeth, "I am your loyal servant attending at your side! Why do you side with the ancient demon god and strike down your loyal servants? Please give me an answer!" Ose startles, lifting his head to see the brave demon who stepped forward, "Are you seeking death?" Samael slowly approaches his subordinate, the demon god's blood surging on his body, causing the dense blood vessels to emit an eerie red glow. "Your Majesty?" the demon officer looks up at Samael, his expression becoming bewildered. Samael shows no mercy, extending his huge palm, crushing his loyal subordinate, squeezing his head into pulp! Blood and flesh splatter onto the demons below; they emit bursts of startled cries, lowering their heads, daring not to make any extra movement. Samael: "Hope you all behave, offering your loyalty to the great Behemoth." "Too horrible," Ose grits his teeth, muttering, already afraid to raise his head, fearing that a careless mistake will make the next poor soul whose head is crushed be himself. Even the Demon Lords have already taken opposing sides; Ose cannot help but sink into deep despair, resisting Behemoth's servitude is utterly worthless, merely a successive march to death. Ose silently clenches his fists, helpless before the current situation, somewhat regretting having framed Merlin at the Seven Kings Conference; if the Demon Lords had not turned on each other, Behemoth would never have had the chance to stir up trouble—it's all because he was addled by the death of Maemon's Majesty, failing to investigate the cause and effect thoroughly. Olo... stands on high ground, looking down at the demons with sympathetic eyes. To occupy the Holy City at the world's center, Behemoth does not need the help of other demons; just like these corrupted Demon Lords, this group of gathered demons are merely cannon fodder used to force the Church to reveal its trump cards when attacking the Holy City. Olo... needs no foresight to know that most demons' fate will be miserable, becoming corpses under the Holy Knights' gunfire—just a matter of time. Boom—rumble— Dark clouds roll across the sky; Behemoth's grotesque, enormous face appears again above, the ancient god's pressure making the demons tremble incessantly. "Those demons who gather here are willing to be loyal to me, right?" Under Behemoth's immense pressure, even if the demons are unwilling, they have no choice. Survival instinct triumphs over dignity; they all drop to one knee, forced to express their loyalty to Behemoth. In a sense, Behemoth is the 'father' of all demons; kneeling is not shameful, and many demons psychologically comfort themselves. "Hahaha, excellent, you are all sensible, clever demons, unlike those stubborn fools who have only a dead end!" Behemoth is pleased with this situation; after slaughtering many opponents, he still has a great number of demons submitting to him— "The masters you now serve are merely puppets I can manipulate at will; these failures are not worthy of your death‑bound allegiance—I am the only great demon worthy of your loyalty." "Rest assured, obediently follow my commands, and you will receive far greater benefits than before; I will lead you back to that longed‑for glorious demon era!" "Our first goal is to eliminate the obstructive Church; they are Mary's lackeys in the mortal world, unworthy of coexisting with us." Although these words are Behemoth's grand promises, some demons still feel moved, for the former demon era was indeed what they longed for. Ose remains silent, head bowed, trembling, unwillingly thinking that although reviving the demon era is his dream, it seems not the same! "The Holy City is the sacred place in the hearts of countless believers, and also the Church's headquarters; with these demons, they probably cannot even take it down." Olo... says expressionlessly. "There's nothing to worry about; I have already cultivated a large number of demon servants in the blood pool; as long as the blood pool exists, slain demons can be reborn there continuously." Behemoth pauses, his face grotesque, saying— "So our true strength—" "Is limitless!"

title: Chapter 9 — Bragging Capital (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 9 — Bragging Capital (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 36 · Chapter 9

. Limit

Orobus was somewhat stunned. This meant that during the war against the Holy Church, Behemoth's servants could continuously be reborn in the blood pool and throw themselves back into the battle.

"They are restricted by the blood pool. It's too far from here and the Holy City to be of any use."

"If the enemy can come after us, can't we go after them first?"

The moment Behemoth finished speaking, a deafening roar echoed across the ground, shaking everything constantly.

The demons were in panic, thinking some danger had appeared. If they weren't afraid of being killed, they would have already scattered.

The earth surrounding the Demon City cracked apart, terrifying fissures encircling the ancient city—

And the next moment, under Behemoth's command, the entire Demon City slowly rose into the sky, gradually separating from its original location.

This well-preserved demon city instantly became a flying castle capable of flight!

Behemoth had long since completed the改造 of the Demon City, turning it into a mobile fortress—

"This Demon City is an outstanding fortress born for war. It will replace the Holy City and sit at the center of the world!"

In the Demon Lord Palace, Orobus withdrew its gaze from the ever-changing scenery outside the window. The war was drawing near.

It looked at the demon-sealing flask in its hand, lost in thought, beginning to doubt itself once again. Was wholeheartedly serving Behemoth exactly as his father had commanded truly the right thing to do?

Orobus considered itself a member of the demon race, yet now the demon race had become a plaything in Behemoth's palm, which didn't seem like a good thing. So many demons perishing in tragedy during the turmoil—it had more than a little to do with him.

Orobus, who longed for art and freedom, naturally disliked slaughter. The deeds he'd been committing went against his inner self.

His father Belial's words pressed upon Orobus's heart like a heavy mountain, forcing it to abandon those extraneous thoughts.

Orobus prepared to hide the demon-sealing flask, believing carrying it on his person was unsafe, better placed somewhere only he could find.

Suddenly—

Orobus hugged the flask tightly, turned to face behind it, its expression grave and vigilant to all sides.

It faintly sensed someone secretly watching it, making it feel somewhat uneasy.

But after searching for quite a while, Orobus found nothing. There was no one spying on it from behind.

Finally, Orobus locked its gaze onto a crow standing by the window.

Its feathers were glossy black, and in the darkness its eyes flickered with faint red light, closely observing every move Orobus made. This was exactly the familiar sent by Xiao!

Orobus narrowed its single eye, picked up a stone from the ground, and stared down at the crow for a long time.

Then its gaze hardened, and the stone shot forward like a bullet, shattering the glass and piercing straight through the crow's skull.

"Caw! Caw caw!"

The crow familiar let out a few cries of agony and its lifeless body fell heavily to the ground.

Orobus exhaled in relief, then frowned and thought suspiciously—

Whose familiar was that?

Was it the Holy Church's spy on the Demon City?

Whichever it was, the death of that familiar would deal a severe blow to its owner!

"Cough!"

Inside the room, Xiao suddenly spat up a large mouthful of blood. His familiar being killed had caused him to suffer the same severe injury—

Damn it!

Who was that one-eyed demon? How did he see through my disguise?

Someone with such ability was absolutely not just some nameless ordinary demon!

"Xiao!" Ophelia quickly bent down to check Xiao's injuries.

"What happened?" Helena asked in astonishment. He had been fine just a moment ago, and in the blink of an eye he had been severely wounded.

"M-my familiar was killed," Xiao said, enduring the grievous wound, his head splitting with pain as if the crow that had just been shot through the head by a stone were him himself!

"Who did this? Your familiar may not have any offensive power, but it was extremely well-hidden. Even the Lords should find it difficult to detect so easily," Ophelia asked in surprise.

"I don't know it. It was a one-eyed demon I've never seen before," Xiao gritted his teeth and said.

"A one-eyed demon?"

Helena and Ophelia exchanged glances. Neither had ever heard of a demon born with a single eye.

Belial had kept his son well-hidden. Not only did these two not know about it, but even the other Demon Lords had never heard of it.

"How are you feeling?" Helena asked worryingly.

"For now I can barely hold out, but recovering will probably take a year or more," Xiao said bitterly. The death of his familiar had directly stripped him of all combat power, and he would be of little help afterward.

"If you're not up to it, then give up. Don't force yourself," Ophelia suggested.

"No! This was Empress Vivian's order, and there's only this one opportunity. Under no circumstances can I give up." Xiao clenched his teeth, his hands gripping tightly as he continuously suppressed the dead crow within the Demon City. "Please, hang in there a little longer!"

The once-dead crow trembled on the ground a few times, its blood spreading outward and gradually forming a small magic array. After the blood solidified, it became extremely concealed, blending seamlessly with the color of the earth.

"Done!"

Meanwhile, Vivian had come out with her adorable granddaughter and was wandering around the streets.

To build a closer relationship with the little girl, Vivian had to lower her own posture, speaking in an unusually gentle tone, and had even bought her some delicious treats.

Since arriving at the Holy City, young Chris had hardly left her room. She'd been cooped up with the demons for a long time, and every time she wanted to go out and play, she was stopped by various excuses. She'd nearly been suffocated from boredom.

Coming out with her grandmother Vivian this time gave her a chance to see the prosperous Holy City. She couldn't help but感叹 that it was so much larger than Rexham, with novel things everywhere.

Chris had originally thought her grandmother Vivian was someone a hundred times stricter than her mother, but privately she turned out to be so kind and amiable—just like Grandma Cloodia, treating her incredibly well, which naturally stirred some fondness in her heart.

The silly and straightforward Chris had always been an honest person; whoever fed her food was unquestionably a wonderful person, as blunt and forthright as ever.

The grandmother and granddaughter came across traveling bards on the street. They were skilled at plucking their lute strings and telling moving stories, immersing their audience in tale and music alike.

This was Chris's first time seeing such bards, and driven by curiosity, she couldn't resist tugging at Vivian's hand and pulling her over.

Vivian herself wasn't particularly interested in such traveling bards, but seeing how absorbed Chris was, those big bright eyes looking so cute, she decided to patiently keep her company.

Seeing the crowd growing larger, the bard displayed a polite smile, gently stroking the strings of his small harp. A soft and gentle melody continuously wove the atmosphere for storytelling, and he slowly began his recitation—

"Thank you all for coming. Next, we will recount the final legendary Hero, the love story of O'Brien. Surely everyone knows—he was a rare genius in human history, an incomparable hero who single-handedly slew the tyrannical Lucifer II..."

"????" Vivian stood in the crowd, her face filled with questions.

"Grandma? What's wrong?" Little Chris held a half-licked candy stick in one hand while tugging at her grandmother's other hand.

"N-nothing, just keep listening." Vivian's smile turned somewhat sinister as she cursed bitterly inside.

*So my fake death plan became the Holy Church's boasting capital?*

*Heh, interesting.*

title: Chapter 10 — The Only Man Living in Hell
content:
Chapter 10 — The Only Man Living in Hell

Volume 36 · Chapter 10

"It is widely known that the fate of a Hero is often a tragedy, and O'Brien was no exception.

The bard plucked the small lyre in his hands. After a simple introduction of the protagonist, this love story officially began—

'O'Brien returned in triumph after defeating Lucifer II, becoming the twelfth legendary Hero in history. In
the streets and alleys of the Holy City, his story was told everywhere. His handsome face even became the prince of many girls' dreams, leaving them unable to stop thinking of him.'

'Among them was a girl hailed as the Flower of the Holy City, named Gwendolyn Christian. She was a devout believer who possessed a beauty that stunned the heavens and extraordinary artistic talent. Her suitors stretched from the temple of the Holy City all the way to Greenland in the north.'

'By arrangement of fate, the two met in the temple and quickly fell in love. Pope Geoghen personally blessed them, and a wedding was held under the solemn statue of the Goddess, bearing witness to their mutual love.

'O'Brien vowed at the wedding that as long as he lived, he would protect his beloved forever.'

The bard's singing was steady, and the music became joyful and cheerful, depicting the happy love of the young man and woman, making the audience feel as if they were there.

Little Chris listened with great interest, the stray hair on her head twitching actively; she clearly liked happy stories.

Vivian curled the corner of her mouth, revealing a hint of a cold smile, thinking it was just another old story, cliché to the extreme, only able to trick children.

Suddenly, the rhythm of the strings in the bard's hand changed. The style shifted from joy to sorrow, and the story began to take a downward turn—

'Happy lives are always short. Two years after their marriage, the beautiful Gwendolyn died a pitiful death after being bitten by a venomous snake, leaving her husband behind.'

'O'Brien was overcome with grief, unable to accept the cruel reality that his wife was dead. He resolved to rescue his wife's soul from hell and give her a new life.'

'The mad O'Brien was like a lunatic, searching everywhere for a way to enter the realm of the dead. He even feared not the terrifying Kraken of the North Sea, seeking the secrets of the ancient gods.

'Finally, he succeeded. In the body of a living man, he entered the hell filled with despair and met the high and mighty King of the Dead, the master of hell, Satan, who controls all souls in the mortal world!'

The music became eerie, portraying Satan, the master of hell, to the extreme. Through music alone, one could feel the terror of hell.

The bard told the story to this point where a heart-wrenching twist appeared, and he began to manipulate the audience's emotions—

'O'Brien abandoned all his dignity as a Hero. He knelt on the ground and begged the master of hell, hoping for the return of his wife Gwendolyn's soul.'

'The heartless Satan was moved by O'Brien's obsession. He was willing to break the rules of hell once for him, giving him a chance to save his wife.'

'Satan said to O'Brien:
Take your wife and go. But before leaving hell, remember not to look back, otherwise, your wife Gwendolyn will be imprisoned in hell forever.'

'O'Brien agreed to Satan's condition. He took his wife Gwendolyn and walked for seven days and seven nights through cruel hell, killing countless spirits that blocked their path.

'He succeeded. He successfully crossed the gates of hell and saw the sunlight of the mortal world.'

The audience could not help but burst into waves of applause, marveling at O'Brien's courage in successfully saving his beloved.

If the story had ended here, it would certainly be a result everyone liked, but this was not a tragedy.

The bard intentionally waited until the audience was dancing with joy, and just as they were about to leave, he suddenly turned again. The music became mournful—

'O'Brien thought he could continue living a happy life with his wife. However, this was merely an unattainable wish.'

'He... he looked back, excited to share the joy of this moment with Gwendolyn, only to find that his wife was already gone, falling once again into the deepest part of hell, imprisoned there forever.'

'The dazed O'Brien realized then that he had not left hell. Everything he had just seen was an extremely realistic hallucination. He was only three steps away from crossing the true gates of hell.'

'What seemed like a short distance actually represented O'Brien's failure. He had failed to rescue his beloved wife and had caused her to suffer torment in hell.'

The audience let out sigh after sigh. Many sensitive people even cried out in sympathy.

They felt great regret for O'Brien; he had been just three steps away from success, but in the end, he still lost to the evil and cunning Satan, deceived by illusions.

A gamble with a god held no hope of victory and could not be retracted. Satan seemed to kindly grant O'Brien a chance, but it only made him fall into deeper despair.'

'Chris's little mouth wrinkled, and she pulled her grandmother's hand pitifulably; she clearly did not like this sad story. Tears flickered in her eyes.

Vivian saw her cute little granddaughter about to cry from anger, thought this was unacceptable. So she shouted loudly, "Hey! You bastard bard, can't you change the story? Let the two live happily together at the end, that's how it should be! Giving out knives in stories every day, aren't you mean? Do you think everyone's lives aren't tired enough, so you're intentionally causing trouble?"

These words clearly hit the hearts of the audience. They were only there to hear happy stories to relieve the pressure of life, not to intentionally seek suffering.

The bard showed a kind smile and answered politely, "Beautiful lady, every epic story needs to respect the facts. Randomly altering them has no benefit and only destroys authenticity."

"What is the use of talking so much nonsense? Seeing us in a bad mood, does it feel good, you twisted bastard? I really want to give you two knives right now so you feel the pain too." Vivian furrowed her brows and threatened.

"Please stay calm. It is just a story. Let me finish telling it." The bard ignored Vivian and plucked the strings once more.

title: Chapter 11 — Statue Intimidation
content:
Chapter 11 — Statue Intimidation

Volume 36 · Chapter 11

"The story is over. The bard lowers his lute and takes off his hat to ask for money from the audience.

But the audience isn't buying it. They shake their heads and leave, saying they won't be happy for the rest of the day after hearing that story — so why would they give the bard any money?

Little Chris pulls her grandmother's hand, feeling that the story of O'Brien isn't very pleasant; it's oppressive. She thought it would have a happy ending, but instead, it stabbed her heart.

"Don't cry, don't cry — it's just a fictional story."

Vivian picks up her almost-crying granddaughter and pats her back to comfort her, while glaring at the bard. She thinks: Why are humans so weak? Always moved by such trivial stories?

Compared to demons, this child's personality is more human-like. Demons are taught from a young age not to be weak.

I wonder how true that story is — did the hero really go to hell to save his wife?

The most prominent landmark in Vatican is the giant goddess statue in the temple, tall enough to overlook the entire holy city.

"Grandma, I want to go see it." Chris points at the majestic statue with curious eyes.

"This..." Vivian hesitates. Although she dares to roam freely in the holy city, she doesn't want to approach the temple — fearing something might happen. So she shakes her head: "No, as long as we don't get near the temple, we can go anywhere."

"Chris has never seen something so big — if we don't look, it'll be a shame!" Chris says in a pleading tone, shaking Vivian's arm.

Vivian is troubled, sweating slightly: "No means no. Don't think you can solve everything with cuteness."

"Can we just get a little closer? Please, Grandma!" Little Chris begs pitifully, full of curiosity.

Vivian can't resist the persistent pleading — and since it's her granddaughter, she loves her dearly — so she nods reluctantly: "We can only get a little closer, but definitely not into the temple's range."

"Grandma is like Mom, hehe!" Chris smiles happily.

"How am I like her? I'm a demon, your mom is human." Vivian emphasizes sternly — she doesn't like being compared to humans.

"Both are outwardly strict but actually very gentle. Even though Mom is strict with me, she's always the first to comfort me when I'm sad — and Grandma is the same." Chris's antenna wiggles as she slowly accepts her cold-on-the-outside, warm-on-the-inside grandmother.

"Is that so?" Vivian blushes slightly, feeling a bit embarrassed, and pinches Chris's cheek: "You little smarty."

The two hold hands and walk toward the distant goddess statue, intending only to get close enough to see — not to enter the temple's domain.

Chris still can't forget the bard's story and asks softly: "Grandma, was that story fake? Can that man named O'Brien only see his wife in hell?"

"Why haven't you forgotten such a boring story? Of course it's fake — it's just to make the audience cry." Vivian pauses, then asks: "Why do you care so much?"

"Because they're so pitiful — they love each other but are separated, like Dad and Mom." Chris lowers her head, feeling empathy for O'Brien's situation.

"Huh? Like your parents? That's not right." Vivian is surprised — what does the young girl mean?

"Dad and Mom are always apart lately. We haven't been together for a long time — either Mom is busy, or Dad suddenly has other things to do. They're always separated for various reasons." Chris becomes sad, muttering to herself — she doesn't dare express this to Alice.

Vivian freezes, realizing the sensitive heart hidden beneath the small body: "That's unavoidable. If they could, they'd be with you."

"No, Chris knows she's useless. If I could take care of myself, they wouldn't have to stay — they could be together. Because of me, one of them always has to stay to look after me." Chris blames herself, feeling guilty.

"No, no, no — it's not your fault. You're just a kid, don't think about these things." Vivian is startled, thinking Chris might have psychological issues. "You want your parents to spend more time with you? That's not hard."

"No, Chris wants a complete family — without Dad or Mom, it's incomplete." Little Chris states her wish — which isn't too high. "Actually, I know the demon uncles and aunts are good to me, but only because of Dad. They always talk about Dad, and I feel like an outsider."

"Uh!"

Vivian stiffens — how can such a young child perceive so much?

But Chris is right: in the First Demon Lord Palace, except for Lilith and Vivian (who are related), the other demons are only friendly because of Merlin. Otherwise, they wouldn't accept her ideologically.

The demons don't see Chris as one of their own — she's always Merlin's daughter.

Vivian doesn't know how to respond. She underestimated her granddaughter's sensitivity and doesn't want Chris to experience the malice Merlin faced as a child.

"Grandma, will Dad come back? You won't take Dad away, will you?" Chris grabs her grandmother's hand, worried.

Vivian hesitates. She does have thoughts of separating Merlin from Alice — at least making him return to the demon race for a long time, cutting ties with the human kingdom.

Suddenly, a terrifying divine pressure hits, making Vivian's hair stand on end and her consciousness blur momentarily!

The eyes of the distant goddess statue light up eerily, as if awakened by the approaching demon, staring directly at her —

What is that? Is it my imagination?

The statue's eyes just moved!

This pressure is extremely dangerous, even for me!

Is it the goddess?

"I miss Dad." The little girl keeps walking, then feels her hand empty and turns — Vivian is standing still, face pale. "Grandma?"

Vivian snaps back, thinking: We can't go any closer — there's danger beyond my control. That statue is suspicious, likely a hidden power of the church.

So she squats down, forcing a smile, and waves to Chris: "Chris, come back — we must return."

Little Chris doesn't think twice and runs back — but before she takes a step, a stranger grabs her from behind.

"What a lovely child." Pope Georg looks kindly at Chris, then smiles meaningfully at Vivian: "Right?"

I've had diarrhea since the day before yesterday, stuck on the toilet today — even musk pills didn't help. I'll go to the hospital tomorrow.

Sorry for the delay."

title: Chapter 12 — Water and Fire Cannot Coexist
content:
Chapter 12 — Water and Fire Cannot Coexist

Volume 36 · Chapter 12

The Pope Georig was waiting here as if he had prepared long ago, and took advantage of Vivian being stunned by the power of the statue to hold Chris, who was on the ground, in his arms.

Saint Knight Captain Blackfort stood behind the Pope, his sharp gaze fixed on Vivian, preventing her from suddenly making a move to threaten Georig's safety.

"Damn it!"

A cold sweat slid down Vivian's forehead, her heart tightening in her throat. If she weren't somewhat apprehensive of the solemn statue in the distance, she would probably find it hard to suppress her urge to kill.

If anything happened to her cute granddaughter, Vivian would definitely go mad. To ensure Chris's safety, she had to force herself to calm down.

Dense footsteps suddenly came from behind. Vivian turned her head vigilantly and saw that, for some reason, a large number of Saint Knights had appeared, blocking all her escape routes—

Damn it! When exactly were they ambushed nearby?

This is a trap. The Church must have realized my existence long ago.

So they set up a trap here, waiting for me to take the bait!

Because Chris was in the opponent's hands, Vivian dared not move lightly for the time being.

"Last night's patrol knights reported that Alice was with suspicious persons. As it turned out, it was all true. This child is Alice's daughter," Blackfort looked at the little one and said lowly, "Being able to take her out for a stroll, the relationship between this person and Alice is extraordinary. We should investigate carefully, Your Majesty Pope."

Alice had thought last night's encounter with the patrol knights was just a minor incident, and no one would delve deeper into it. But the patrol knights reported this matter up the line, and it caught the attention of Pope Georig.

Although there was no evidence that could prove Alice had colluded with the demon race, having survived twice from the hands of Lucifer the 3rd in consecutive extermination battles was somewhat unusual. Georig thought there was something fishy.

Since Alice returned, a large number of Saint Knights have been lying in ambush around her residence, monitoring the movements of the people inside.

Today, seeing Vivian taking Chris out shopping, separating from the crowd, the Saint Knights followed the Pope's orders and carried out covert actions, wanting to investigate everyone around her without attracting Alice's attention. Thus the current situation arose.

"You're right." Pope Georig nodded, looking down at Chris, "Little one, what's your name?"

"Um..." Little Chris was naturally timid, and even though the grandfather in front of her had a friendly smile, she dared not speak randomly, especially seeing her grandmother's ugly expression.

"Hahaha, it seems we scared her." Pope Georig showed a wry smile.

"!"

Vivian's whole body shuddered, and her pupils instinctively contracted. Although Georig was already old beyond recognition, she could still vaguely see some of his appearance from years ago—

Is he? The red-clothed cardinal who hid behind the hero back then!

Unexpectedly, he actually became the current Pope.

Truly narrow paths for enemies!

Vivian felt a bit irritated. Instinctively, she pulled the heavy hood on her head, not wanting to be recognized.

Anxious Vivian considered whether to kill all these Church people, but the goddess statue behind her made her feel a bit afraid. She always felt that a head-on collision would be a lose-lose situation. She still needed to preserve her strength to deal with Behemoth, and the situation was very unfavorable for her!

Pope Georig discovered Vivian's small movement and said loudly, "You don't need to be so cautious. We aren't meeting for the first time. In a sense, we can also be considered old friends."

"Hmm?" Vivian raised her head in surprise, her eyes vigilantly fixed on Georig, thinking, Old friends? Who is old friends with him?

What is this old fox really planning?

"Blackfort, temporarily help take care of this child. Without my order, don't act recklessly. I want to talk to that distant guest." *Pope Georig put Chris down and handed her to the knight captain to look after, then personally walked toward the not-so-distant bench, distancing himself from the protection.

"Understood." Blackfort nodded, holding Chris's small hand to prevent her from suddenly running away. "I know you are Alice's daughter. What is that woman to you? Can you tell us?"

"Little Chris lowered her head, sucking on her finger, pretending not to understand anything."

"Pah!" Blackfort frowned, sensing a hint of strangeness. Strange thought, this child was instructed not to speak randomly? A bit overly cautious. If Alice had no problem, why couldn't she say it openly and frankly?

Pope Georig came to the bench and made a "please" gesture. "Don't you want to talk to me? What a rare opportunity."

Vivian was full of anger, unable to figure out what Georig was up to? She dared not walk over easily, but she very much wanted to take her granddaughter and leave quickly.

"Don't be so guarded against me. Does my sincerity not suffice?" Georig spread his hands, showing he had no defenses, and voluntarily gave up all protection. "Clearly, after so many years without seeing you, your courage seems not as good as back then by a tenth—ah, becoming timid and fearful."

"Hmph!"

Vivian's eye twitched, feeling that Georig was looking for death. Without the knights' protection, she could easily kill him with a finger move. Yet he still had the cheek to mock him after two hundred years?

However, the other party took a negotiation posture. To safely take away the granddaughter, this invitation was obviously impossible to refuse.

Vivian looked at the frightened Chris, then glanced at the distant and awe-inspiring goddess statue. Carefully, she walked over.

Both sat on one end of the bench at the same time, leaving a very long distance in the middle. Obviously, they were very cautious and did not trust each other, which did not look like what "old friends" would be like.

Silence, silence lasting for several dozen minutes. No one spoke first, both secretly scrutinizing each other.

The leader of the Church and the leader of the demon race are deadly enemies who are water and fire incompatible. Meeting on the same bench one day, the style is truly bizarre.

No one would have thought that there was any possibility of negotiation between believers and demons. Today is also considered a day worthy of being recorded in history books, although it is only a secret contact.

Pope Georig scratched his itchy neck, took out a brown-old pipe from his pocket, lit it and took two heavy puffs, showing an enjoyment expression, but soon started coughing—

Cough core change

Vivian frowned, increasingly unable to figure out what the current Pope was playing at?

Pope Georig warned Vivian the same way, handing the pipe in his hand over. "You also come some?"

"Go far away." Vivian coldly replied three words.

"That's truly a regret." Pope Georig shook his head and asked lowly, "You haven't forgotten me, right? Isn't it that you didn't expect me to become Pope? This is all thanks to you."

"What about that?" Vivian narrowed her eyes.

"You really haven't changed, still the same as back then. Look at me? As an ordinary person, I'm already old and about to die. Now I can only rely on various medicines to keep going." Pope Georig paused, and sincerely sighed—

"Demons...

"Truly enviable, not needing to cultivate to have a long life."

title: Chapter 13 — Corrupted Faith (Monthly Ticket Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 13 — Corrupted Faith (Monthly Ticket Extra Chapter)

Volume 36 · Chapter 13

ViViian suddenly frowned, astonished in her thoughts, what did this mean? If the church leader said such a thing, it would definitely cause a huge commotion.

"I never had the qualification to talk to you face to face, but now I do." Pope Georig coughed out a smoke ring, speaking with deep meaning.

"I never dreamed I would have the opportunity to sit here and talk with you so calmly.

"Actually, I always thought you really died, defeated by us. Now looking at it, how ridiculous a thing that is.

"You really didn't die, and yet you appear in the Holy City so arrogantly?

"You wouldn't think that those kinds of Brave Warriors with spears could really defeat me? Even if my body was in a poisoned state at the time, dealing with you is as easy as pie." ViViian responded haughtily.

"O'Brien can defeat you, I am certain of it. He is a true genius among humans. Don't be deceived by his surface strength; he has the qualification to challenge a god." Pope Georig paused and added, "The Legendary Brave selection system is special. It requires the new Legendary Brave to be stronger than the previous one to be qualified, ensuring that every new Legendary Brave has power beyond the past. O'Brien is the last Legendary Brave. Do you know what this means? No one can replace him anymore."

"Hmph, alarmist talk." ViViian showed a disdainful smile.

"Whether you are willing to believe it or not, this is a fact." Georig said calmly.

"If he is so strong, why not let him come save you? Seems like you've forgotten your situation?" ViViian's eyes gradually turned ferocious. Magic was brewing in her palm, and her tone revealed killing intent. "Sitting together alone with you is a stupid decision you made. I can kill you without any effort. As the Pope of the church, you are an enemy of my race. If you die, the church will definitely suffer heavy damage. I am already suppressing my impulse."

"I died, that child cannot grow up either." Pope Georig faced the death threat calmly, "My Knight Captain's swordsmanship is very fast."

ViViian looked at Chris and found Blakefort beside her. His hand was always on the sword hilt, his gaze vigilant, observing her every move.

As long as ViViian had any move harmful to Georig, he would without hesitation swing his butcher's knife at the nearby Chris.

"I don't doubt you have the strength to wipe us all out, but you may not be able to protect that child from being unharmed." Pope Georig held his pipe, calm and said, "Even if you kill me at all costs, you won't have it easy either. I swear, I will not let you leave the Holy City unscathed."

ViViian lifted her head, looking at the huge Goddess statue in the distance. She was also staring at her. All of these were Georig's capital for coming down to negotiate.

"At the end of the day, we are enemies, but at least now is not the time, because there is a common enemy, and its threat is greater." The Pope looked at ViViian, his voice cold and solemn, "The situation of the demon race is very dangerous. You should know better than me. I have the determination to die together with the demons. Do you have that too?"

The atmosphere fell into dead silence. A cold chill permeated between the two.

ViViian narrowed her eyes. She indeed cannot here fight to the death with a group of superstitious fellows. Saving her son from the Demon Sealing Pot is more important.

Under pressure, ViViian withdrew all her killing intent and restored calm.

"You seem to care a lot about that child? Obviously Alice's daughter, what is your relationship with her?" Pope Georig asked.

"And you have nothing to do with me." ViViian answered coldly.

"Your son gives me a huge headache. He killed many of my subordinates. Compared to other Demon Lords, he is more difficult to deal with, cruel to the point of almost not letting go of any enemy." Georig's eyes added some anger.

"Unexpectedly, my son has some places that make me feel proud." ViViian said happily.

"Let me guess, Alice escaped from her son's hands twice without a scratch. This itself is very abnormal. If Alice colluded with demons? Then everything makes sense." Georig's smile on his face deepened, analyzing, "You care so much about Alice's child, her identity is already obvious."

"! ! ?" ViViian's face was calm on the surface, but her heart was already frightened, and she definitely does not want this matter known to outsiders, as it would only make mother and daughter more dangerous!

"It seems I inadvertently learned another secret that will make you suffer greatly." Georig laughed coldly, speaking with deep meaning, "As far as I know, the demon race cannot accept intermarriage with humans, not to mention accepting the offspring of demons and humans. As long as the fact is hidden, they can live in human kingdoms. But if the secret is revealed, they will definitely be burned at the stake, with no place to accommodate them."

ViViian's face turned black "brush" from being hit on her soft heart, and intense killing intent surged again.

"That child is very pitiful. Besides her parents, she has no other destination. I feel extremely sympathy for this. Perhaps I shouldn't have known this secret." Georig feigned a look of great pain.

"What do you want to do?" ViViian questioned.

"It's simple. That ancient Magic God has already seriously threatened your and my interests, so I need your power. Let's join forces to get rid of the terrible enemy." Pope Georig's expression was serious, and he said seriously, "This is my request. I hope you can consider it carefully."

"Hah, how ridiculous, to make me cooperate with you? You won't take me for a stupid fool, will you?" ViViian laughed coldly, mocking, "Don't think I don't know your calculations in your heart. You want to take advantage of me and the ancient Magic God being mutually wounded, and eliminate the threats of the demon race and the ancient gods together. I won't let you succeed. Your request has no sincerity at all."

"No sincerity? Your judgment is not unreasonable. So, to express my sincerity, let me tell you a secret. After you hear it, you will definitely believe me." Georig stared into ViViian's eyes and said lowly, "Please allow me to reiterate one more time. I am not your enemy, whether now or in the future. We have a common enemy, because my faith has already changed."

"Huh? ViViian did not understand the meaning in the other's words, only feeling that Georig's whole person's temperament had changed.

"Actually, I have already died long ago, my heart has stopped beating, I..." Pope Georig quietly said, slowly lifting his hat that he never takes off even when sleeping or bathing. On his bald area at the top of his head, mysterious black characters were clearly printed—

VII

The meaning of this ancient text represents the Eighth Apostle from Hell!

title: Chapter 14 — Betrayal
content:
Chapter 14 — Betrayal

Volume 36 · Chapter 14

Decades ago, Ji'ougen slowly opened his eyes, thinking he would as usual bask in the morning sunlight, sitting beneath the solemn statue of the goddess, performing a boring prayer. 'Why is it still so dark? Has dawn not yet come?' Ji'ougen wearily sat up; before him was pitch‑black darkness where he could not see his own hand, his mouth dry and throat parched, hoping someone would bring him a cup of water. 'Is anyone there? Fuot? Could you bring me a cup of water?' His voice echoed, but no one answered for a long while, and Ji'ougen wondered—surely Black Fuot, as his guard, should be standing outside no matter how late it was. So Ji'ougen sighed, reluctantly slipped on his slippers, and groped in the dark, hoping to find the kettle in the room. A hiss—pale blue ghost‑fire floated in mid‑air, drifting before Ji'ougen. 'Fuot! Where are you? This place feels strange!' Ji'ougen panicked, sensing something wrong, repeatedly calling out his own name. The appearance of ghost‑fire meant undead were nearby, yet this was the temple that worshipped the Light Goddess Maria—how could evil creatures approach here? A whoosh—more ghost‑fire suddenly ignited, forming a huge wall of fire that illuminated everything around! Undead! Countless undead! Wherever his gaze fell, all were hideous undead! They drifted aimlessly around, jeering at Ji'ougen with mocking laughter, as if ridiculing this newcomer to Hell. 'Ah…? ? ?' Ji'ougen felt a chill run down his spine, stunned on the spot, his old body collapsing to the ground and trembling. 'Another of Maria’s agents in the mortal world has come before me—what good is your loyal service to her? After death you’ll still end up here with me.' The undead slowly parted, and a colossal black shadow appeared before Ji'ougen, its gaze like looking at an ant; no one could see its true form. Ji'ougen panicked, shouting repeatedly, 'Someone! Someone!' 'Give up,' the shadow said, 'no one can come to save you; you haven’t realized it yet? Your life ended in your sleep, and now you are merely a wandering spirit in Hell.' 'Impossible! How could I have died so absurdly? I am Maria’s agent in the mortal world; she will protect me!' Ji'ougen’s face twisted in disbelief as he muttered, 'I will never come to this damned Hell! I should ascend to Heaven and become a noble holy spirit!' 'Hahaha, every believer of Maria has bought this lie—puny humans, how dare you share glory with the exalted god? You are nothing but pitiful pawns used by others.' 'I don’t believe it! Something must be wrong!' Ji'ougen lowered his head in confusion, angrily demanding, 'Who are you? How do you know this is a lie?' 'You are the pope of the mortal world and still don’t know my name? I am the supreme ruler here, the eternal master of the undead.' Ji'ougen’s eyes widened in horror, his whole body trembling uncontrollably, a name echoing in his mind—Satan! A deity equal in stature to the goddess Maria, who participated in the creation of the new world and governs the souls of all things. Ji'ougen’s face turned ashen, his heart sank like falling into an ice cellar, feeling no warmth at all, unable to accept that he was already dead. 'What will happen to me? Can you tell me?' 'You are a follower of Maria, you have interfered with the plan to break the barrier between Hell and the mortal world; without a doubt you now stand opposed to me, and you will suffer eternal torment.' Ji'ougen lowered his head, gritting his teeth and whispering, 'I don’t want to die.' 'Oh?' Satan’s tone shifted, his voice low, 'You differ from the previous popes; your desire to live far exceeds theirs.' 'I don’t want to die!' Ji'ougen tore up, tears streaming down his face as he lifted his head, kneeling without dignity, 'If you won’t torture me, I am willing to betray my faith in Maria and become your most fervent, most loyal follower!' 'Hah.' Satan let out a low chuckle, 'Indeed, you are unlike those former popes—they would rather be tortured than swear allegiance to me, but you have made a wise choice. Very well, I grant you an opportunity.' 'Command me as you wish; I will surely spare no effort to fulfill your orders.' Ji'ougen fawned like a lapdog, immediately wagging his tail for Satan. 'I have taken a liking to a certain person; you must lure him here.' Satan stated his condition. Ji'ougen asked cautiously, 'Who?' 'Your beloved hero, Oblien, who possesses the potential to challenge the gods; if he cannot be used by me, it would be a great waste.' Satan stretched his hand, covering the sky and blotting out the sun, placing it over Ji'ougen's head. 'Accomplish this, and I will bestow upon you eternal life.' 'Aaaaaah!' Ji'ougen jerked awake from his dream, finding himself back in the temple, everything around him familiar. A crowd had gathered, staring at him with bewildered eyes. Black Fuot hurried over, asking, 'Are you all right? The entire church has been frightened; you have been unconscious for three days, even your heart stopped—we thought you…' Ji'ougen shuddered, feeling his chest—still no heartbeat, meaning he was now a living corpse! It was not a dream; he had indeed died three days prior, his soul fallen into Hell, and Satan had sent him back. Ji'ougen’s expression was blank, his demeanor lost, yet deep inside he felt a flicker of gladness—he had not been tortured, but could continue living. 'I’m fine; everyone leave, I want to be alone.' Black Fuot’s eyes showed concern. 'Get out!' Ji'ougen said sternly. 'Yes.' Everyone left the room; Ji'ougen exhaled deeply, slipped on his slippers, and wearily walked to the mirror. He saw that the bald spot on his scalp slowly revealed the symbol 'ilI', officially making him an emissary from Hell. He had once devoutly worshipped Maria, strictly administered the church according to doctrine, gaining nothing but an overworked body. Yet from Satan he obtained what he had longed for—eternal life. One night, Oblien was dispatched from the Holy City on a mission. Under the cover of darkness, Pope Ji'ougen, carrying a sack, sneaked furtively to Oblien’s residence. Through the window he saw Oblien’s wife, Gwendolin. The weather had turned cold; the virtuous Gwendolin was knitting a scarf for Oblien, hoping to surprise him upon his return. Ji'ougen hesitated, then drew from the sack the poisonous snake he had prepared. Black Fuot held Chris’s hand, his gaze fixed on a distant bench. 'What are those two people talking about?' he wondered, unable to hear, oddly thinking they were very familiar, that the pope had grown so close as to show the other his bald spot. 'It was me, I did it all.' Pope Ji'ougen readjusted his hat, a chilling smile spreading across his face. 'Uh…' Vivian looked astonished, sensing the wicked aura from the symbol just now. 'I am no longer human, Lady Vivian.' Pope Ji'ougen paused, narrowed his eyes, and said softly, 'Now I am a wandering spirit.' 'In order to keep living, I have already sold my soul.'

title: Chapter 15 — Secret Agreement
content:
Chapter 15 — Secret Agreement

Volume 36 · Chapter 15

"To express my sincerity about this cooperation, I will tell you this secret," Pope Ji'ougen paused, speaking with a deep tone, "Now do you understand? I am absolutely not your enemy." Vivian's gaze was doubtful, her emotions unable to calm for a long time, indeed frightened by Ji'ougen's secret. The highest leader of the Holy Church of Light had actually betrayed the Goddess and become an apostle of Hell? If this were made public, it would surely cause an uproar throughout the entire human world! No matter how exalted Ji'ougen's position, the faithful would never allow the Goddess's agent in the mortal world to be a lackey of Hell; they would drag him from the papal throne and burn him alive. Ji'ougen could not withstand the wrath of the angry faithful; his fate would be miserable. Vivian, strong and composed, couldn't help but want to test Ji'ougen with a probing question. "You wouldn't... make this matter public?" "No fear, if you leak it, that child's fate won't be much better than mine," Ji'ougen said calmly, "Now that we each hold the other's secret, isn't that much fairer?" "As the Pope, why would you serve Hell?" Vivian questioned, puzzled. "Humans have long been abandoned by that lofty Goddess; I know this well. Just because of the doctrine she left behind, must we throw ourselves into a life‑or‑death struggle with the enemy? That's foolish. We are humans, not anyone's slaves—why should we obey a being holed up in Heaven?" Pope Ji'ougen showed a hint of weariness, continuing, "Besides, serving the Goddess brings no benefit at all. What I seek, she cannot give me, but Satan can. Humans are fragile; we don't want you demons and elves, whose innate vitality is extraordinarily tenacious." Vivian said nothing, thinking it no wonder Ji'ougen began speaking those strange words—he had already tasted the horror of death. "Some truths are only known after dying once; what fame and wealth? What people pursue are merely useless things. Being alive is the true precious treasure; I have realized that death is the eternal truth." Ji'ougen sighed, raising his head with a weathered look, "Perhaps humans and demons have an irreconcilable hatred, but what does that have to do with me? Most humans choose to believe in the Goddess, using them as cannon fodder against dark forces, and precisely because the Goddess exists, hatred cannot fade, right?" "I can hardly imagine such words coming from a Pope's mouth," Vivian said, greatly surprised. "It's nothing; the Church is merely the Goddess's shadow in the mortal world. If we don't fight you demons, what purpose do we have?" Ji'ougen suddenly laughed, "That's what the previous Pope told me on his deathbed; I didn't understand then, but gradually I realized many things are beyond our control." "What is Satan's aim? You're serving him now—what do you know?" Vivian still couldn't fully trust Ji'ougen. "That's not for you to know; I can only say that the mortal world is their secret chessboard, their thoughts are not unified and full of contradictions. Satan actually favors demons hostile to Heaven and always wants to bring you under his sway." Ji'ougen looked at Vivian, adding, "In a sense, we share a common enemy; though we're all in the same boat, our ideas differ, and Heaven's power is like a wave that can overturn the boat at any moment—a greater threat." Vivian felt Ji'ougen wasn't lying and indeed had some sincerity in revealing his hidden identity. Moreover, to resist Behemoth, if the Church were willing to help, that would naturally be good. After long consideration, Vivian deemed the plan feasible and continued asking. "Working with you isn't impossible, but we demons don't habitually make losing deals—what would we gain?" "As long as I remain in the papal throne, I will not send troops against the demon race; you will enjoy a long peace. I know your situation is dire; even if you succeed in disposing of the ancient demon god, you will be gravely wounded and desperately need time to recover." Pope Ji'ougen glanced at Chris, lowering his voice, "Also, I'll pretend that Alice's close ties with the demon race never happened and won't reveal it; let this matter pass. Are these terms satisfactory to you?" After exchanging terms, the previously tense atmosphere eased considerably. The Holy Knights didn't know what the Pope and this mysterious "woman" had discussed, nor even her identity. Until Pope Ji'ougen rose from the bench, returned safely, looked at Chris, and ordered, "Let this child go." "Yes." Blackford released Chris, who eagerly ran back to her grandmother. Little Chris hid in Vivian's arms, glancing occasionally at the knights, a little frightened. Vivian kept soothing her granddaughter, thinking it was good nothing had happened and that she had reached a secret agreement with the Pope. "Your Holiness, are you alright?" Blackford asked. "I'm fine, really nothing happened," Ji'ougen said, trying to sound relaxed, thinking Vivian was a bit better than her son—at least she could sit down and talk. "Who is that person? The knights reported last night she was suspicious," Blackford said, believing further investigation needed. "He's an old friend of mine, someone who loves to travel," Ji'ougen dispelled Blackford's doubts. "You certainly know her; just now I saw your actions—it didn't look like a first meeting," Blackford said, sighing slightly, if it weren't for some suspicious person sneaking into the Holy City, that would be good. "It was merely a brief encounter," Ji'ougen said with a meaningful tone. "Should we have the knights keep watching Alice?" Blackford asked. "Never mind; we must muster all the forces of the Holy City to face the crisis, and I can clearly feel the distant threat drawing ever closer." Late at night, Vivian gazed with affection at the little granddaughter sleeping on her lap. She gently stroked Chris's back, watching the child's peaceful sleeping face, and couldn't help recalling Merlin and Lilith when they were small. Vivian knew deep down that holding Chris like this now is only temporary; whether she will ever get another chance to see her remains uncertain. Dong dong dong— The white‑haired Abaton knocked on the door and entered, respectfully coming to Vivian's side. "Your Majesty, Shu has already taken care of everything." "We have left hidden traces in the demon city." "When the war breaks out, it will become our trump card for victory."

title: Chapter 16 — Besieged City
content:
Chapter 16 — Besieged City

Volume 36 · Chapter 16

"How is Xiu doing?" Vivian asked.
"For now there's no immediate danger to its life, but the death of its familiar has caused it considerable harm; it needs proper rest." Abaddon replied respectfully.
"It's been through a lot, managing to sneak into the demon city under Behemoth's control; I imagine the pressure on it has been huge." Vivian knew the task she gave Xiu was heavy, and aside from Xiu, no other demon had that capability.
"Xiu, thanks to his familiar, has learned many important things: Behemoth has gathered a large number of surrendered demons, forming a huge force, and has also produced vast numbers of demon servants that can be reborn endlessly in the blood pools, almost possessing immortal power." Abaddon reported the information he knew in detail.
