"This is entirely as expected; Behemoth is the creator of the demon race, able to create new servants, which is no difficulty for it." Vivian's expression remained calm; she had obviously guessed these things.
"The original demon city has been remodeled into a flying mobile fortress; Behemoth is leading the demons straight toward the Holy City, and the controlled demon lords have become the vanguard." Abaddon lifted his head, his voice low, saying, "That bastard is plotting to have us kill each other with his wishful scheme."
"I see." Vivian's expression shifted slightly; she nodded and said, "So Behemoth's target is here? No wonder the Pope is so eager to cooperate with us—it seems he's been driven to desperation."
"We could use Behemoth's power to get rid of that eyesore, the Church." Abaddon suggested.
"Now is not the time, and besides, the Church's high ranks have already betrayed their faith; they may not be our enemies. Our primary goal is still to pull the demon race back from the brink of danger." Vivian furrowed her brows, speculating, "*The Church might even help us restrain Behemoth's forces, buying us a chance to break the sealing pot."
Abaddon thought it over; feeling that since they had already reached a secret agreement with the current Pope, there was no need to tear it up, and given the dire situation, cooperation with the Church was indeed necessary.
"Has Xiu figured out the exact whereabouts of the sealing pot?" Vivian asked, very concerned about this matter.
"It does know something; the sealing pot is now in the Demon Lord Palace, guarded by a mysterious one-eyed demon." Abaddon answered truthfully.
"A one-eyed demon?" Vivian exclaimed, having never heard of such a thing among demons, "What is that demon's identity?" "I don't know; Xiu has never seen one, nor have I heard of demons being born with a single eye." Abaddon shook his head, then after thinking said, "However, since it lives in the Seventh Demon Lord Palace, it likely has some connection to Belial."
Vivian fell silent, pondering for a long time, then asked, "How strong is the other side?"
"Not an ordinary opponent; it saw through Xiu's familiar at a glance." Abaddon replied, frowning.
Vivian's face darkened considerably; she felt an unknown factor had emerged, and this mysterious one-eyed demon would become the biggest uncertainty.
Little Chris, asleep, lazily turned over on Vivian's lap, letting out an adorable, cooing sound.
Watching her granddaughter, Vivian's mood improved somewhat; she thought things had not yet completely slipped out of control.
"Your Highness is so clever and quick-witted; later we could take her back to the Demon Lord Palace to train, and perhaps she could become your successor in the future." Abaddon suddenly said.
"You're wrong, Abaddon," Vivian said, wanting to speak but hesitating, helplessly, "I don't intend to take this child back to the demon race."
"Why? After all, she is your descendant." Abaddon showed a look of incomprehension.
"She does not belong to the demon race; deep down, I still cannot fully accept her. The traditional demon notions are deeply rooted in my heart, and I believe other demons feel the same." Vivian said meaningfully.
"No, we can fully accept Lady Chris." Abaddon emphasized.
"If Chris weren't Merlin's child, would you still accept her?" Vivian suddenly asked back.
"This..." Abaddon fell into hesitation, thinking that Merlin's descendants are naturally different from ordinary demons.
"That's the crux of the problem: you may accept her in principle, but deep down you still have your own ideas; if Chris returned to the demon race, she would have no foothold at all. Think of the discrimination Merlin faced as a child—Chris would only be pushed out further. I don't want her to repeat that, to suffer setbacks mismatched with her age and experience." Vivian said with a worried expression.
"Having the little princess live in a human country seems improper." Abaddon had some objections.
"So what? We want to unite all the demon race's forces; Chris's presence is awkward and would also put us in a passive position. My son fell in love with a human and had a child—this would become fodder for other demons to mock us." Vivian had already thought that Chris would struggle to fit into the demon race; it would be better for her to continue living as a human.
"Do you really have the heart to let her go?" Abaddon asked suspiciously.
"This is also unavoidable; Chris has nothing but her parents, she knows her situation well, and so she always deals with us cautiously." Vivian's gaze toward Chris softened, her tone becoming gentle—
"As her grandmother, I cannot tear apart her family, nor can I destroy the dream she guards with her tiny body..."

The demon city, transformed into a sky fortress, began its departure.
Behemoth led the demon army, invincible wherever it went, utterly destroying all the small nations on the route to the Holy City.
Compared to Mammon, Behemoth's strategy is even more brutal; it leaves no chance for humans to flee, and several small nations, utterly unable to resist, see their populations nearly wiped out in a short time, as if they had become dead lands where no human has ever lived.
Although the demon city has not yet invaded the south, many human alliances formed with the Church have already fallen into disarray.
Large numbers of people began migrating toward the Holy City, hoping this ancient holy capital could protect their safety.
The lands trampled by the demons, without exception, meet the fate of national extinction and ethnic annihilation.
Those once high-and-mighty rulers, under the demons' blades, finally awoke to how feeble they were.
The demons made countless humans experience what 'equality of all beings' means—all are souls beneath the blade, noble or common alike.
The vanguard of demon lords formed by Merlin, Samael, Asmodeus, Beelzebub, and Leviathan can be called the most splendid lineup in demon history, capable of sweeping aside any single human superpower with ease, seemingly without needing Behemoth to lift a finger.
They lead numerous powerful demons, like a blood‑stained dagger—
Its target points straight at the Holy City where the Church resides!
The overwhelming advantage of the demon lord vanguard left Pope Geoffrey unable to sleep through the night, often startling awake from his dreams.
The Holy City, a sacred place where the Virgin Goddess once manifested great miracles, is now faintly shrouded by the demons' artillery fire.

title: Chapter 17 — Annihilate Civilization
content:
Chapter 17 — Annihilate Civilization

Volume 36 · Chapter 17

Sanderia was a small nation to the southeast. Though its area was less than one-twentieth of Britannia's before its fall, its population was remarkably substantial. Its people revered childbirth and worshipped the Light religion.

Due to its location in a region prone to frequent warfare, its people had a strong martial culture. Many who left Sanderia became mercenaries or adventurers.

They were brave and capable warriors, boasting a good reputation and prestige, which earned Sanderia the title of the homeland of warriors.

Even the women here underwent military training, and those who couldn't even lift a sword had no chance of survival. Children began learning martial arts with wooden swords at the age of four, and only upon reaching adulthood after successfully killing ten or more magical beasts on their own were they qualified to receive the title of warrior.

The cruel competitive法则 of survival of the fittest bore some resemblance to the customs of the demon race, and this was how the people of Sanderia carved out their place.

However, this small nation happened to lie directly on the route that demons took to attack the Holy City, making it the last country still standing. Under the leadership of the current king, Sanderia XVI, brave warriors formed a defensive line at Sirius Valley to resist the demon onslaught.

Sirius Valley was a naturally defensible position. The dense forest provided cover for the warriors, allowing arrows to easily pierce through the throats of demons!

Ground attacks were equally difficult to break through, with only a narrow path able to pass through here. As long as Sirius Valley was held, the demons' wish to attack the Holy City would never be realized.

Under the fierce resistance of the Sanderia warriors, they repelled seventeen demon waves, preventing the demon army from breaching the Sirius Valley defenses for three days and nights.

But ahead there were many kingdoms far more powerful than Sanderia, all falling under the demons' iron hooves, unable to protect their own civilizations.

With the Holy City occupied reinforcing its defenses and unable to spare support, how much longer could the tiny Sanderia hold out?

Many had already abandoned their hometown and fled to the Holy City. Those who stayed likely had already resolved themselves to sacrifice.

"Aaaaaah!!!"

The Sanderia warriors roared, holding their shields and bravely standing at the front, forming an indestructible wall of steel.

The demons charged like madmen, fearless of death, using their strong bodies and weapons to repeatedly batter against the enemy shields, hoping to break through the Sirius Valley defenses and clear a path for the main force behind them.

When the demons' charging momentum faded, the shields parted, and countless spear soldiers emerged from within, impaling and killing the demons like skewers on a tanghulu stick.

Then warriors wielding short blades rushed out for the final cleanup, slaughtering any escaping demons without leaving a single survivor, fully utilizing the terrain advantage of Sirius Valley.

King Sanderia XVI led by example, leading warriors charging at the very forefront. His heavy sword pierced the heart of a giant scorpion demon, and foul blood dyed his furious face red.

Another victory. This was the eighteenth wave of the demons' charge, and they still hadn't broken through the enemy's defenses, but were slaughtered without a fight.

The bravery of the Sanderia warriors could be seen at a glance; they didn't lag behind even the crazed demons.

Sanderia XVI stood atop the corpse of the scorpion demon, wiped the blood from his face with his hand, and let out a great laugh, shouting—

"Sanderia!!!"

The warriors raised their voices together. They had already forgotten how many times they had cheered for victory; it had become routine. From initially trembling before the demons to now remaining calm and composed, it had taken only three days.

They didn't know that the demons attacking these past few days were merely the tip of the iceberg from the Demon Castle's forces, a small-scale reconnaissance unit dispatched specifically to scout the path.

The truly terrifying enemy was still behind.

After winning the battle, the warriors began cleaning up the battlefield, preparing for the next wave of charges.

Sanderia XVI looked at the demonic corpses covering the ground and muttered to himself, "This was the eighteenth wave of the demons' assault. How many more are there behind?"

"Please rest assured, Your Majesty. No matter how many charges come, they cannot defeat us. Every warrior will defend our homeland alongside you until the last moment." A young warrior beside him said.

A faint smile appeared on Sanderia XVI's face as he said calmly, "The demons' attacks are growing more ferocious. We cannot let our guard down. I heard that several neighboring kingdoms were wiped out in a single night, and only five demons were involved."

"Is that so? I wonder if it's true?" The young warrior looked astonished. "From what we've seen in the past few days, the demons aren't particularly strong—they seem weaker even than fierce magical beasts. Is it really possible that five demons destroyed a kingdom with deep roots?"

"Perhaps," Sanderia XVI frowned, speaking with concern. "What we've taken down are only vanguard units. The enemy's main force is still on the way."

The young warrior's expression darkened. They had fought for three days and were already exhausted, yet it was only a small-scale vanguard. "Your Majesty, please don't frighten yourself."

"I must consider such things. The Church cannot offer us any help right now, and our other allies are barely surviving themselves. We are completely isolated." Sanderia XVI's face showed worry as he sighed. "If only my younger brother were here. He would be my most solid backing. I shouldn't have agreed to let him leave Sanderia to be some damned adventurer."

"Please don't say that, Your Majesty. Lord Moraby, though a noble purple-gold ranked adventurer, is also our pride as Sanderians. You should be happy instead." The young warrior paused, then continued, "Besides, given the current turmoil, Lord Moraby should already be on his way back."

"You're right. We need to wait patiently." Sanderia XVI raised his head, gazing at the blood-red horizon as the sun began to set. "Did we make it through another day safely?"

Suddenly—

"Look! What's that?!"

With a startled cry, a magnificent black castle broke through the clouds and hovered in the distant sky.

Surrounded by countless demons, it looked like an endless mass of dark clouds!

The eerie Demon Castle finally appeared before the eyes of the Sanderia warriors!

Such a massive fortress city, and it was flying in the sky. All the warriors were stunned, witnessing this bizarre sight for the first time.

The easily defensible Sirius Valley seemed like nothing more than a natural barrier before the Demon Castle. The enemy could easily cross Sanderia and attack the Holy City directly!

"Form ranks!" Sanderia XVI came to his senses and shouted an order.

The well-trained warriors quickly shook off their shock and rapidly formed defensive arrays. Everyone could vaguely sense that this might be the enemy's true main force—

A violent black wind struck, making it difficult for the warriors to keep their eyes open.

Sanderia XVI's heart pounded, a sheen of cold sweat forming on his forehead as he vaguely sensed several terrifying presences!

As the storm cleared, what stood before them—

Was the top demon lineup composed of five sovereigns: Merlin, Samael, Asmodeus, Beelzebub, and Levi—

title: Chapter 18 — Reinforcements (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 18 — Reinforcements (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 36 · Chapter 18

Sander XVI's gaze became wary. Although there were only five enemies, the aura and pressure on their bodies were not something ordinary demons could compare to.

Sending only five demons just to get rid of us?

Wait!

I had heard recently that several neighboring countries had been destroyed by five demons in a single night. Could it be—

Sander XVI had already realized the gravity of the situation. These few demons looked less aggressive than before, but their level of threat was entirely different; they could erase the civilization of a nation with absolute ease.

The other young warriors had not yet sensed the approaching death and even somewhat looked down on the opponents.

"No way? They only sent five demons to deal with us? It seems we are being looked down upon."

"Everyone be serious, do not underestimate the enemy!" Sander XVI scolded, not wanting his subordinates to be negligent. "Though the number of enemies is not great, their pressure is extremely terrifying. What is scary on the battlefield is not having many enemies, but when there are fewer, one must be vigilant."

After hearing this, the warriors immediately tucked away their smiles and became and serious. If even the King was this panicked, the enemies invading this time would likely be very difficult to deal with!

When there are fewer enemies, unless it is a defeat, it proves the matter is very serious. The strength of the opponents is often terrifying, giving them the confidence to face a siege by thousands of enemies.

The warriors of Sandandia were now facing exactly this situation. Every Demon Lord had the ability to destroy such a small country countless times, let alone acting in unison. The support from other demons was insignificant and far from a threat.

Perhaps this siege of the Holy City would not even require Behemoth to take action personally; the monarchs led by Merlin would be enough to serve as the main force.

The number of warriors guarding the Sirius Valley was not large, barely making up ten thousand people, but every warrior was an elite carefully selected. However, they now did not dare to make a hasty move.

Beelzebub began the attack first, opening his mouth to spit out countless man-eating flies, which immediately swarmed into the warriors' defensive formation, biting and tearing their bodies at a speed visible to the naked eye.

The seemingly sturdy armor and shields could not protect the warriors' safety at all; the man-eating flies could easily bite holes through the gear. The small Leviathan appeared harmless to humans and animals, but his methods were equally cruel. With a wave of his hand, high-pressure water sharp as blades instantly pierced through the warriors' defensive formation. Blood dyed the Sirius Valley red, and the casualties were unimaginably heavy.

"Stay calm! Everyone, stay calm!"

The proud Sandandia warriors fell into panic and chaos. Facing the casual attacks of the Demon Lords, they had no power to resist, and fear was instinctively born in their hearts.

What kind of noble warrior spirit? In the face of death, it seemed not worth mentioning at all?

Seeing his warriors flee in such disgrace, Sander XVI was very angry. He was, after all, a middle-aged man who had entered the Saint-tier, and was naturally not easily intimidated. However, the subsequent attack made his majesty as a king vanish instantly—

Smael was seen descending from the sky, his incredibly strong body like a meteor, hitting right in the center of the warriors!

With a loud boom, the explosion kicked up scorching flames. Countless warriors turned to ash in an instant, and the violent shockwave destroyed the entire Sirius Valley, erasing this natural defensive fortification from the map.

Losing the advantage of the terrain that was easy to defend and hard to attack, the warriors' final psychological defense also collapsed. The disappearance of the Sirius Valley meant that Sandandia would also face its destruction.

When Sander XVI crawled up from the ground again, what entered his eyes was a field of ruins and the corpses of soldiers. His heart was filled with despair; he had ultimately failed to protect his homeland.

"How pitiful." A strange light flickered in Asmodeus's eyes as he cast an illusion on Sander XVI.

Sander XVI turned pale, looking at his own body with terror. Countless rats were gnawing at his flesh, quickly eating him from feet to head until even his consciousness vanished.

To outsiders, he had not received any attack; his eyes simply became vacant as he died within the illusion.

Sander XVI knelt weakly on the ground, his head hanging lifeless to one side, becoming a corpse.

Merlin, dressed in demon armor, slowly walked to the side of this king, took the crown from his head, and melted it with scorching demon fire.

A small kingdom like Sandandia found it difficult to resist the attacks of demons, and their methods were not as numerous as the Kingdom of Britain.

Especially when facing a team composed of Demon Lords, it was impossible to stop the destruction of the kingdom.

These carefully selected warriors held no deterrence for the Demon Lords; no matter how many came, they could not change the fate of defeat.

Sandandia burned fiercely in the flames. This country hailed as the homeland of warriors completely disappeared from the map, and even the once brilliant civilization was erased.

Like those nations that vanished into the long river of history, they were brutally eliminated by the law of survival of the fittest—

With Sandandia destroyed, there were no more obstacles on the path of the demon team. The next step was entering the Holy Roman Empire, heading straight for the Holy City.

The airship was originally a product of the ancient goblin race, but unfortunately, the technology failed to pass down, becoming a magical tool in stories.

But with Merlin's return from the ruins of the gods, this mysterious transportation tool was able to see the light of day again. The ancient goblins' technology was mastered by humans.

Beelzebub, though a cynical guy, was deeply interested in the airships. With the wealth and help of the family, the "Beelzebub Aviation" plan finally made progress, using the original airship as a model to replicate a few models; although there was a power gap, they could now fly for long distances.

title: Chapter 19 — All Strong Reinforcements:
content:
Chapter 19 — All Strong Reinforcements:

Volume 36 · Chapter 19

"Oh?" Mesfield turned back in surprise, looking at Blaze. Being called by name by someone she didn't know well made her a bit unhappy.

Who was it again?

"Me?" Blaze felt hurt. He had already harbored fond feelings for this heroic female knight, but she didn't remember him at all.

"Haven't we met somewhere? You look familiar." Mesfield frowned.

Blaze was delighted and quickly explained, "I'm a knight by Princess Margaret's side. When our kingdom was attacked by vampires, didn't you help us? How could you forget so quickly?"

Mesfield recalled carefully and finally remembered that a knight had always followed the French princess. "Oh~ So it's you. Sorry for the rudeness, I have a bad memory, especially for plain-looking people."

"Plain-looking?" Blaze felt like his heart had been stabbed. He realized he had no distinguishing features at all. He felt his love growing wings and flying away.

"Why are you here? Aren't you supposed to guard Princess Margaret?" Mesfield asked with confusion.

"I've been dispatched to reinforce the Holy City. The demons' attacks are getting more fierce. His Majesty the King believes the Holy City holds special significance for all humanity and absolutely cannot fall." Blaze said solemnly.

Mesfield remained composed. Almost everyone rushing to reinforce shared the same view as the Queen, otherwise they could have participated in the 234th Crusade.

Blaze looked around, curious. "I've never seen a ship that flies in the sky before. It's amazing. It's faster than any previous means of transportation and can go anywhere."

"I feel the same. I heard this is called a sky ship. It was developed at great expense by the Rothschild family as an experimental product. Because the situation is urgent, we got the chance to experience it." Mesfield explained, knowing a bit about the sky ship's origins.

"This is just an experimental product? I thought it was already a mature product. Look at how sturdy this ship is." Blaze touched the railing and exclaimed, "To be honest, it could withstand several bombardments from demon cannons."

"This ship was made by Jacob, the heir of the Rothschild family. He looks a bit flamboyant." Mesfield commented, thinking of Jacob's reputation—apparently, if he wasn't flamboyant, he wouldn't be the son of a richest man.

"What? Jacob? That good-for-nothing second-generation rich kid?" Blaze stared in shock, unable to imagine that the famous spendthrift could achieve anything. "Incredible. Such a miraculous thing was made by him?"

"It seems this wastrel isn't completely useless after all; he has some merits."

"You seem to know him?" Mesfield asked curiously.

"Because Jacob once publicly confessed his love to Princess Margaret, sending twelve golden roses directly. It caused a huge stir, but unfortunately, he wasn't Margaret's type and failed. I still have a deep impression of it." Blaze recalled.

Mesfield was somewhat shocked. Twelve golden roses—that was a considerable fortune. Such generosity was indeed enough to move many women. No wonder he was a Rothschild heir.

"By the way, for this reinforcement of the Church, did Britain only send you alone?" Blaze asked curiously.

"That's right, only me. What about you?" Mesfield countered.

"I brought a few capable attendant knights. Hehe~" Blaze revealed a simple smile and continued, "After all, I'm not as strong as Miss Windsor. We might need several helpers to deal with powerful demons. I heard about your outstanding performance in the defense of Britain—you slaughtered the demons completely, leaving not a single scale behind. It's admirable."

"No, it's nothing." Mesfield shook her head, looking at the King's Sword at her waist. Defeating the army of Demon Lord Asmodeus mainly relied on divine artifacts and the lake fairy's power.

"You're too modest. Among the female knights I've seen, you're the bravest. I admire you from the bottom of my heart. Not everyone has the courage to stand before the Demon Lord." Blaze paused and earnestly asked, "Dealing with demons, you already have rich experience, while I'm just a rookie. I hope you can share some tips on fighting demons. I don't want to make a fool of myself in front of a few attendant knights."

"What tips?" Mesfield's face darkened. She said meaningfully, "It's not those ordinary demons that are scary, but the Demon Lords whose power towers above countless people. Their deterrent force far exceeds our imagination. In the defense of Britain, I never even saw the true Demon Lord—only the enemies' substitutes. This time reinforcing the Holy City, my pressure isn't small either."

"Miss Windsor, don't worry. The people on this ship are companions who will fight alongside you in the Holy City. Though they come from different kingdoms, they are all renowned strong ones. There are even several royal guard knights like me." Blaze, though nervous about reinforcing the Holy City, felt more confident after learning about some of the people on board.

"Oh?" Mesfield hadn't communicated with anyone on the sky ship yet and didn't know there were such big shots?

"The reinforcements dispatched are all kingdoms that have signed human alliance agreements with the Church, so there are many royal guards on the ship." Blaze looked around and lowered his voice—

"For example, Westcott from Prussia, the Human War Machine. He's the knight who guards the capital and has fought the Giant King of foreign races without falling behind."

"There's also the Bull Warrior from Northern Rus. He never says his real name or removes his mask, but his strength is extremely formidable. When I was still an apprentice knight, I had already heard of his legend. He's someone who grew up with beasts since childhood and can communicate with them."

"Even Greenland from the far north sent their court mage, Logan. You should have heard of him. He's a guest professor at many magic academies, with students all over the world."

Mesfield lowered her head, her heart unsettled for a long time. How many familiar names were on this ship? Almost all renowned strong ones from northern kingdoms.

"Besides those related to royal families, there's a special existence—a purple-gold adventurer. I think he's the most inscrutable person on this ship. I don't know why he's on board either—adventurers should refuse to participate in conflicts."

Blaze muttered in confusion.

"Who?"

"Morabi. He comes from Sandibia, the homeland of warriors."

At this moment, in a room on the sky ship, a middle-aged man gazed out the window, his eyes filled with grief and anger, silently clenching his fists. The adventurer's badge around his neck shimmered with a purple-gold luster—

"Brother, I will personally twist the necks of the demons and avenge the people of Sandibia!"

title: Chapter 20 — Bottle Opener
content:
Chapter 20 — Bottle Opener

Volume 36 · Chapter 20

Morabi, from the "warrior's homeland" Sandbia, is the younger brother of King Sand Sixteen.

He was supposed to enjoy the luxuries of his position, but he grew tired of the monotonous life and left his homeland to become an adventurer.

Morabi never reveals his past, and only a few people know he is the brother of King Sand Sixteen.

He hopes people admire his abilities, not because he is the brother of Sandbia's king.

With his martial arts honed from a young age, Morabi quickly stood out among adventurers, achieving near-perfect performance in countless missions. After passing various trials, he became a prestigious Purple Gold adventurer.

Unlike Alice, who has a bit of a watered-down reputation, Morabi rose to Purple Gold through his own hard-earned strength. In every aspect, he embodies the image of a powerful adventurer.

Morabi intended to take this fast spaceship to the Holy City, then immediately go to Sandbia to support his homeland. However, just before he could, he heard that Sandbia had fallen. All the towns and villages were destroyed by demons, and his brother led the warriors in a fierce battle in the Valley of the Sky Wolves for three days and nights, but ultimately couldn't stop the demon's advance, and fell under the demon's blade.

Morabi's heart ached, and he regretted not being able to return to his homeland sooner, perhaps saving Sandbia from destruction.

Initially, he wanted to be like other adventurers, living freely and leaving everything to his brother, but he ended up leaving an irreparable regret.

Although Sandbia's destruction had nothing to do with Morabi, he still felt deeply guilty.

If he had only listened to his brother, he wouldn't have been so selfish.

In the evening, the spaceship was speeding through the vast starry sea.

The ship's interior had a dining room, serving a generous dinner for all passengers.

The Holy City was getting closer, and they would likely arrive in the morning.

"Wow," Blaze pretended to be elegant, his voice excited, "I never thought I'd have the chance to have dinner with the Miss Windsor?"

"Ah? It's just a regular dinner," Mestfield bluntly broke the formal atmosphere. "Besides, there are more people on this ship than I imagined."

Looking around, the dining room was very noisy, all wearing strange clothes, and their origins could be guessed from their traditional costumes, all dispatched to the Holy City for reinforcement.

Many faces were familiar to Mestfield, mostly people from the royal court, and she had seen some of them when she accompanied Queen Elizabeth on her visit.

"It can't be helped, it's a bit noisy here, but after we arrive in the Holy City, we'll be partners in fighting the demons together. Getting to know each other a bit in advance isn't a bad thing," Blaze said with a silly smile.

"That's true," Mestfield nodded, carefully observing the people in the dining room, and suddenly noticed a middle-aged man who looked out of place, sitting alone in the corner, drinking in silence, with his Purple Gold adventurer badge hidden under his clothes, barely visible. That's the only Purple Gold adventurer on the ship, Morabi?

He seemed to be in a bad mood, did something happen?

"Mestfield?"

Suddenly, an old man in a gray robe and a large magic hat approached.

This man was the royal court magician of the Greenland kingdom, Logan, who was highly skilled in magic, and even little Johnson's father had to treat him with respect.

"Didn't forget me, old man? I remember when I was teaching Princess Michelle, you were always standing by, a very responsible knight," Mestfield said, helping Logan arrange the chair.

After Logan sat down, he smiled and said, "Elizabeth Queen is willing to send you out to support the Holy City, which shows how much she values the safety of the church. Isn't that right?"

"Well, it's something like that."

Mestfield's face showed an awkward smile, unwilling to say the queen's thoughts outright.

Because she had heard that this Logan not only was the royal court magician of Greenland, but also a follower of the Light Church.

Greenland Kingdom was one of the earliest northern kingdoms to actively join the human alliance, and it was clear that this Logan had played a significant role in it.

"Queen Elizabeth has a far-sighted vision, becoming a member of the human alliance, I feel deeply happy. Under the condition of having a common belief, humanity will be invincible," Logan looked very enthusiastic, seemingly a human supremacist.

Mestfield and Blaze looked a bit complicated, although Logan was a simple believer, their masters all had their own plans, and what was called the human alliance was more of a form.

"The Holy City has a long history and has special significance for all humanity. It is said that it was where Goddess Maria opened the heavens, in any case, it cannot fall into the hands of the filthy demons," Logan paused and slowly said, "Actually, we don't have to worry, even if we don't go to support, the demons will be very difficult to break into the Holy City. The church has inherited the legacy of the great goddess, and they have many ways to resist the invasion of the demons."

"Goddess's legacy?" Mestfield was surprised.

"That's right, Goddess left many precious things before leaving the mortal world, most of which were inherited by the church, and there may be treasures used to fight the demons inside," Logan only heard rumors, seemingly not very clear either.

Mestfield fell silent, thinking that this time was just to share some pressure, and the church should have already prepared for "welcoming" the demons.

"Hmm?" Logan turned around and looked back.

Not far away, the dining room was very noisy, and almost everyone had gathered there.

It was the Cow Warrior and West Zeckosel playing a drinking game, with the bet being the Cow Warrior taking off his mask.

Both were very strong men, and their huge bodies were intimidating, and their boisterous personalities were also similar.

To show off their strength, the two men even performed a stylish bottle-opening act, seeing who was tougher.

West Zeckosel pulled up his sweaty shirt and squeezed the bottle cap open with his belly, drinking the strong liquor in one go, "How about that? Are you convinced now? Still not taking off your ridiculous mask!"

"I won't!" The Cow Warrior pushed two bottles of liquor into his eyes and popped the caps with his eyelids, then drank them down, much harder than West Zeckosel.

The onlookers couldn't help but start cheering and mocking this human tank.

"Zeckosel, you're not as good as you think."

"Yes, you should play harder."

"Are you really a human tank? Your eyelids can even be used as corkscrews?"

West Zeckosel grinned, slightly provoked by these words, but didn't want to lose to the other.

So, in full view of everyone, he took off his pants and slowly extended the bottle towards his buttocks, ready to perform a bold move.

Human Buttocks Bottle Opener!

title: Chapter 21 — Dangerous City (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 21 — Dangerous City (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 36 · Chapter 21

Mesfield covered his eyes, unable to bear such an eyesore, thinking to himself how these bandit-like fellows had become knights?

"Indeed worthy of being a human tank, he's even trained his buttocks to be so tough." Blaze sighed with emotion.

The atmosphere in the restaurant reached a climax, everyone egging it on.

They had seen all sorts of bottle-opening techniques, but using one's buttocks as a bottle opener was a first.

Suddenly, a discordant voice sounded, interrupting the noisy atmosphere—

"Two stupid fellows, can't you be quiet? This isn't a tavern, you're really asking for a beating."

Ox Warrior and Westze Kessel both frowned, their bodies stiff as they turned around, staring coldly at Morabi who was drinking alone in the corner.

Both were famous strongmen; even if they weren't exactly refined, no one dared to point fingers at them.

When they were having fun and got scolded, Ox Warrior and Westze Kessel both felt their faces burning, their dignity severely challenged.

The people around immediately went quiet, automatically clearing a path; they dared not provoke these two madmen, whispering secretly:

"Who is that guy? Daring to scold Kessel and Ox Warrior in public."

"Looks a bit unfamiliar, don't recognize him."

"Could be some greenhorn, doesn't know how fierce these two madmen are, right?"

Ox Warrior and Westze Kessel stopped their contest, storming over to Morabi's side, looking down at him with murderous intent.

Their strong bodies cast shadows, looming over Morabi; everyone held their breath, terrified this unfamiliar man would be killed on the spot by the two madmen.

"Oh? There'll be a good show." Old Logan laughed, quite pleased to see a good show.

Ox Warrior and Kessel were clearly simple-minded fellows who didn't recognize Morabi at all; besides, he had hidden his Purple Gold Adventurer certificate in his clothes, so his identity was naturally hard to discern.

Both thought Morabi before them was just some nobody from a small northern kingdom; if they had known he was a noble Purple Gold Adventurer, they would never have dared to provoke him so easily.

"Tscheh!" Mesfield frowned, thinking they wouldn't really start fighting, would they? This isn't some dueling arena!

"Hey, who are you? Daring to meddle, have you never heard of my name?" Westze Kessel demanded coldly.

"Maybe this guy's brain is broken, needs us to fix it." Ox Warrior's voice rolled like thunder, full of confidence.

Morabi stood up; his mood was already terrible, and then these two guys provoked him, making his face even uglier.

"What? Want to fight?"

"Ha ha, you seem pretty confident in yourself?" Westze Kessel sneered.

"Give you a chance, do you want your left arm broken, or your right?" Ox Warrior started rubbing his fists, eager to try.

Both began emitting powerful Saint-tier pressure, thick aura rolling like tides, shaking the restaurant slightly.

"Stop! We're here to reinforce the Holy City! Not here to fight! Everyone comes from different places, it's normal to have conflicts, but we need restraint!" Mesfield stood up to stop them, not wanting internal strife before fighting the demons.

"Give up." Blaze stopped Mesfield, whispering, "Those two are lunatics, impossible to reason with."

Mesfield felt somewhat annoyed, thinking the people on this ship were completely scattered sand; even if they went to reinforce the Holy City, they probably wouldn't accomplish much.

Over there, Ox Warrior and Kessel couldn't hold back any longer, ignoring Mesfield's劝阻 as wind; they couldn't tolerate others' provocation, and directly struck first—

Both punched almost simultaneously, the piercing wind of their fists whistling, faintly emitting thunder-like explosions, crashing toward Morabi's face!

Everyone's hearts leapt to their throats, even closing their eyes in terror, certain the next second would bring a bloody scene.

Attacked from both sides by these two madmen, could he survive?

Only Morabi's brows slightly furrowed, yet he remained calm, advancing instead of retreating!

Buzz—

A slight booming sound rang out, Ox Warrior and Westze Kessel were knocked down spitting blood foam, unable to rise!

Both lost in an instant without suspense, barely any exchange of blows.

The whole venue fell silent, everyone holding their breath; it ended too fast, many didn't even see what happened?

Two Saint-tier powerhouses had already fallen.

With this overwhelming strength, Morabi could crush all knights present; he was already far beyond the Saint-tier level.

Ox Warrior and Kessel though looked very strong, but before Morabi they were clearly not worth mentioning; this was the power and confidence of a Purple Gold Adventurer.

"Just two sycophants, once you leave the so-called royal family, will anyone know you? Maybe you should reflect on yourselves." Morabi snorted coldly, leaving the restaurant without looking back, finding the dinner very dull.

The moment he turned, someone with sharp eyes saw Morabi's Purple Gold Adventurer certificate hidden in his clothes, couldn't help but exclaim—

"Good heavens! He's a Purple Gold Adventurer?"

"Purple Gold Adventurer?! These two madmen hit an iron plate."

"Fists too fast to see, supersonic boxing, Morabi, it must be him!

The people in the restaurant discussed animatedly; though Morabi was always low-key, not as famous as Gregory, he was still well-known in the strongmen's circle.

"Such fast fists, impossible to see with the naked eye; if not for Morabi holding back, these two youngsters would surely die." Old Logan asserted.

"Why does this person have such a violent temper? Hard to get along with." Mesfield frowned slightly.

"Maybe because his mood is bad?" Blaze said softly.

"Hmm? What's wrong?" Mesfield asked curiously.

"Not long ago, Morabi's homeland Sandibia was destroyed, and even his brother sacrificed in the war." Blaze sighed helplessly.

Mesfield lowered her head; she understood this feeling all too well.

Three days after the reinforcement team arrived at the Holy City, they hadn't even had time to rest before starting full alert.

The flying Demon City appeared two miles out, its huge blurry castle shadow visible to all residents of the Holy City from afar.

The demons had successfully invaded here; the historic Holy City Vatican was suddenly in a critical moment of life and death.

The Temple Knights assembled, led by Knight Captain Blackford, preparing to fight the demons to the death!

The reinforcement knights were also incorporated into the defense force; they rubbed their fists, ready to go.

Dark clouds covered the Holy City, blocking warm sunlight; almost everyone prayed devoutly in their hearts for the Holy City, hoping to see tomorrow's sun.

Large amounts of siege equipment were pushed onto the walls, magic cannons lined up one after another; even the interior of the sturdy walls had many cannon ports made.

Obviously, to "welcome this group of demons," the Church had also made full preparations.

Fear permeated everyone's hearts; this was an unavoidable fight to the death!

In the cathedral, Pope Giojen watched the external projection from the crystal ball, discovered the vanguard composed of Merlin and four other Demon Lords, sweat beading on his forehead—

"Want to rely on Demon Lords to break the Holy City?"

"That ancient demon god, he's underestimating people too much."

title: Chapter 22 — Holy City in Crisis
content:
Chapter 22 — Holy City in Crisis

Volume 36 · Chapter 22

A cold wind swept through, but unlike Pope Julius' expectations, there were no hordes of demons gathered outside the Holy City.

Instead, only five demons appeared, looking more like visitors than attackers.

However, Pope Julius knew the significance of these five demons. They represented the most powerful forces in the demon race, while ordinary demons were more like supporting actors, playing a limited role in the siege of the Holy City.

Pope Julius had no doubt that the Demon Lords, led by Merlin, had the capability to breach the gates of the Holy City and possibly even reach the temple itself.

Behemoth did not intend to engage in direct combat with the enemies. Instead, it entrusted all matters to the Demon Lords, led by Merlin. Even if the Holy Church had powerful hidden cards, they would be used by the Demon Lords, not Behemoth itself.

This was Behemoth's strategy: using the Demon Lords to force the Holy Church to reveal all its hidden cards. When the time was right, Behemoth would step in to reap the rewards, enjoying the fruits of their labor. This was the most cautious approach, ensuring that Behemoth would never face any threats.

On the towering and sturdy city walls, the Holy Knights were in a state of high alert, ready to engage in bloody combat with the demons. However, seeing only five demons below, their hearts began to waver, wondering about the demons' strategy.

"Only five demons are sent to face us? They must be very confident in their abilities."

"Don't be reckless," Blackford's stern reprimand echoed, his gaze fixed on Samir. "Although the enemy numbers are few, each one is a master of the Demon Lord Palace, capable of withstanding the onslaught of countless soldiers. Attack them with full force, leaving no room for hesitation. Even a slight delay will lead to our defeat."

Demon Lord Palace masters? They are Demon Lords?

The knights were shocked, their expressions turning grave. They had never seen true Demon Lords before, and this was the first time.

Below the towering city walls, the Demon Lords stood motionless, their icy gazes scanning the knights on the walls, assessing their capabilities.

Blackford suppressed his fear, maintaining his composure. With so many knights watching him, he couldn't afford to show any signs of cowardice.

Are these the true Demon Lords? They don't seem any different from ordinary demons.

Let me test their strength.

Blackford's gaze sharpened, and he issued a command.

"Archers, prepare!"

Due to the Holy Church's defeat in the 234th Crusade and the heavy losses incurred, the Holy Knights had not been able to replenish their forces in such a short time. The number of Holy Knights guarding the Holy City was less than fifty thousand, and even with support from some northern kingdoms, it was still insufficient.

With such a small defensive force, guarding the Holy City and repelling all demon attacks, Blackford's heart was filled with anxiety. The situation was highly unfavorable for the Holy Church.

With the Knight Commander's order, tens of thousands of archers drew their bows and prepared to fire. The cold silver arrows had a significant deterrent effect on the dark creatures.

"Fire!"

Swoosh, swoosh, swoosh, accompanied by the sound of arrows breaking the air, a dense rain of arrows like locusts descended from the sky, targeting the Demon Lords.

The Demon Lords watched the arrow shower with calm, not even raising an eyebrow. Such attacks were too weak for them.

The Demon Lords remained motionless, standing in their place. The dense arrow shower, which would have been impossible for even a sparrow to evade, failed to hit them. Instead, all the arrows pierced the surrounding land.

"Uh! What's happening?" Blackford's eyes widened in surprise, wondering how the elite archers could miss every single arrow. What technique were they using?

Asmodeus let out a mocking laugh, having already cast his illusionary domain. The so-called elite archers saw a false position for the Demon Lords and were unable to hit them. All the archers were blinded by the illusion.

"Damn it! Open fire! Increase the power of the magic cannons to the maximum! I won't believe we can't hit these demons!" Blackford shouted angrily, feeling humiliated by the demons' unchallenged stance.

Two hundred magic cannons stacked on the city walls were pushed forward, with magic crystals inside spinning wildly, releasing all their power. The output had been increased to its maximum.

A terrifying aura of non-attributed magic filled the air, causing the surrounding space to distort slightly.

Boom!

Almost simultaneously, the two hundred magic cannons fired.

The flames shooting from the barrels shook the city walls slightly.

The magic cannon fire intertwined, forming a dense fire cover, making it impossible for the Demon Lords to escape.

Facing the full-force cannon barrage, the Demon Lords remained unphased, even finding the Holy Church's carefully planned defensive structures to be of little consequence.

Baal suddenly opened his mouth, and the massive cannon fire was all drawn into his mouth, gradually converging into a single point before being swallowed whole.

The powerful cannon fire, which was intended to strike the Demon Lords, was instead consumed by Baal, not only failing to harm them but even strengthening the enemy.

After consuming all the cannon fire, Baal licked his lips and scratched his stomach, still feeling unsatisfied.

"What? ? ?" Blackford was speechless, as all their attacks had no effect on the Demon Lords. What should they do now?

Roar!

The roar of a beast echoed, and Leviathan, whose massive form was hidden in the clouds, emerged, coiling around the sky like a terrifying serpent. It surveyed the tiny humans below, its enormous body encircling the entire Holy City with ease.

Leviathan's head emerged from the clouds, and it opened its mouth, spewing a red demonic light cannon that swept across the northern city walls.

Where the light cannon passed, everything was reduced to dust. All the magic cannons were destroyed, and some weaker Holy Knights were unable to escape and perished in the flames. Blackford's fate remained uncertain in the chaos.

Leviathan's attack destroyed the sturdy city walls, leaving no defensive structures to stop the demons' advance.

At this moment,

a large number of demons appeared behind the Demon Lords, waiting for the Holy City gates to be breached.

Among them were not only ordinary demons but also countless scorpion demons, all created by Behemoth himself as loyal servants. If any demon intended to betray and flee during the siege, they would likely be killed on the spot by the scorpion servants.

Under the leadership of the Demon Lords, the demons surged into the Holy City with great momentum, as if entering an unguarded space.

This ancient holy land was being invaded by demons for the first time in history, awaiting the cruel slaughter and trampling of the human race.

title: Chapter 23 — Time Race
content:
Chapter 23 — Time Race

Volume 36 · Chapter 23

The knights guarding the Holy City charged at the demons, clashing with the invading demons in brutal combat.

The ruthless demons kept pouring in, overwhelming the Holy Temple Knights in sheer numbers and scale. Especially the scorpion demons—barely killed by the knights, they would immediately regenerate in the blood pool and reappear on the battlefield, earning the nickname of an "eternal" armory.

The knights, wielding their blades, charged fearlessly toward the Demon Lords, only to be blocked by countless demons, unable to even get close. The demon forces advanced step by step toward the heart of the Holy City, approaching the Temple of Maria, slaughtering every human in their path.

Enemies of this caliber didn’t even need the Demon Lords to lift a finger—other demons alone were enough to crush the knights defending the city.

Ose, brandishing his curved sword, slaughtered through the crowd with reckless abandon, slicing open the knights’ throats effortlessly, blood spraying everywhere.

These knights defending the city were at best mid-tier in strength—how could they possibly stand against a Saint-tier demon like Ose?

*"Is this the Holy City?"* Ose’s nose twitched as he caught the scent of a strong enemy, then abruptly lifted his head—

A gleaming golden great sword descended toward him.

*"Accept the judgment of light! Demon!"*

Blackford plunged his blade from the sky, cleaving Ose in two before the demon even had a chance to scream.

Ose’s corpse lay in the blood, never imagining that the joy of breaking into the Holy City would end so abruptly—with the "justice" of the Goddess of Light.

Blackford wiped the demon blood from his blade, then stood tall and shouted:

*"Stay calm! Don’t run! The demons aren’t truly terrifying! The Goddess of Light will guide us to victory!"*

At this moment, rallying morale was useless—the city gates were shattered, and the knights had lost all will to fight. Their instinct to survive overrode everything.

The Holy Temple Knights fell into chaos, fighting and retreating in disarray, hoping to reach the temple for refuge.

Blackford grew irritated, preparing to lead the charge himself to restore morale, even if it meant using his body to block the demons from reaching the temple.

*"Brave knights! For the Goddess! Charge with me!"*

Blackford, true to his title as the Holy Temple Knight Commander, proved unexpectedly dependable in this crisis. He gripped his sword and charged alone toward the demons.

But then, he saw the hulking, headless Samiel before him, and his heart skipped a beat. His eyes, once blinded by Samiel, began to ache again, and the old fear resurfaced—

He wasn’t the first to face Samiel. Once, he had nearly died at the Demon Lord’s hands, only surviving by sheer luck. If he hadn’t, he wouldn’t have reached this day.

Everyone thought Blackford was a fearless knight commander, a hero to be emulated and worshipped from the heart. But in truth—

He was a coward, through and through.

Blackford happily accepted everyone’s praise, constantly boasting about his bravery against Samiel, loving to show the younger knights his strength.

Yet he knew the truth—he was neither brave nor strong.

After Samiel pierced his eyes, Blackford had chosen to lie motionless on the ground, pretending to be dead, barely daring to breathe. He had watched as other knights were slaughtered before him, only escaping by sheer luck.

The young Holy Temple Knights, seeing Blackford’s "bravery," were all inspired.

*"The commander has set the example! What are we afraid of? Death? The great Goddess will welcome us in the heavens!"*

*"Charge with the commander! Slaughter these filthy demons!"*

*"Long live Maria!"*

With shouts ringing out, the knights no longer fled in panic but turned to face the overwhelming demons, throwing death behind them.

Yet at that moment, Blackford’s face paled, his breathing ragged, his courage completely consumed by the old fear. He had no will to face the Demon Lords head-on.

Blackford froze, then turned and fled faster than a newborn baby could be reborn, abandoning the knights who had just regained their spirit.

*"Retreat! Everyone retreat!"*

The young Holy Temple Knights stared in stunned silence at their commander, who was running faster than anyone else.

Inside the temple, a sharp *crack* echoed.

Pope Eugen didn’t spare Blackford’s face, slapping him in front of everyone. The blow made him tremble violently.

*"You—you coward! How dare you call yourself a Holy Temple Knight? I’ve gone blind! How could I have appointed you as commander? Even Bares is a thousand times better than you!"*

*"I—I’m sorry, Your Holiness, I’ve sinned!"* Blackford bowed his head in apology. He had always been a defeated general of Samiel’s—no matter how many lives he had, he couldn’t stop the Demon Lords. If he hadn’t fled, he would have died at the city gates anyway.

*"Apologies won’t do anything! You should have killed yourself before the Goddess’s statue in repentance!"* Pope Eugen snarled, *"Disobeying orders and fleeing mid-battle—you didn’t even hold the city gates. The temple is now fully exposed to the enemy’s attack, and the demons will have an unobstructed path to the temple. This is all your fault!"*

*"Your Holiness, I only made the right decision,"* Blackford argued boldly, *"Those weren’t just ordinary demons—there were Demon Lords among them. We couldn’t have held them off. We needed reinforcements."*

*"Do you want reinforcements?"* Pope Eugen roared, *"That’s just cowardice! You abandoned the other knights and ran back alone! You’ve disgraced the Holy Temple Knights!"*

Blackford lowered his head, seeing the disdainful and even mocking glances from the surrounding knights and bishops. It left him utterly humiliated.

From now on, Blackford’s legend of bravery would likely be erased, his cowardice ridiculed by everyone.

*"We must use the power the Goddess left behind—this is our most urgent task,"* Pope Eugen’s face returned to calm, though he clearly hadn’t expected Blackford to flee outright, *"From today on, you are no longer the Holy Temple Knight Commander. You’ll stay in the temple as a common knight. Reflect on your mistakes before we discuss your future."*

Blackford dared not lift his head, his disappointment overwhelming. Maybe pretending to be dead would have been a better outcome after all.

Outside the temple, the colossal head of Leviathan emerged from the thick clouds, its eyes glowing crimson. It opened its blood-red maw and fired a devastating Demon Lord cannon, the scorching fire barreling straight toward the temple, aiming to obliterate the Church’s stronghold.

The impact sent shockwaves through the temple. The bishops and knights could barely stay on their feet, stumbling and collapsing to the ground. The more timid ones even crouched under the tables, trembling in fear.

*"Stay calm! The demons can’t harm us yet!"*

*"Once the power of faith is gathered, the Goddess’s strength will annihilate all demons—even the Demon Lords. Today, they will all perish here!"*

title: Chapter 24 — Frenzied Gaze (Monthly Ticket Extra)
content:
Chapter 24 — Frenzied Gaze (Monthly Ticket Extra)

Volume 36 · Chapter 24

"Good thing I was prepared in advance. The temple's defensive barrier can still buy us some time." Pope Giougen said calmly.

The panicked people recovered their wits and reluctantly regained their composure, then began to praise the Pope's caution.

Blackfort felt the temple still shaking. How long can the defensive barrier hold? It's hard to say; it might be broken by Leviathan soon.

"Aside from these, I also prepared some gifts for the Demon Lords." Pope Giougen said meaningfully.

Blackfort shuddered, thinking about what the Pope had secretly prepared. He had actually kept it all from himself.

Outside, seeing that he couldn't blast the temple away with one shot, Leviathan secretly increased his firepower, continuously firing Demon Lord light cannons at the temple barrier that had appeared out of thin air.

The barrier composed of sacred light completely enveloped the vast temple, repelling all of Leviathan's attacks.

How could the Church stand for so long and be easily broken by the Demon Lords? This was under the condition that all the Demon Lords had had their strength raised a level by the demon blood.

Under Leviathan's nearly crazy firepower output, the sacred barrier gradually developed tiny cracks, obviously unable to hold much longer.

The towering goddess statue's staff slightly glowed with golden light, frantically absorbing the power of faith, preparing to kill the Demon Lords.

The power of faith is the power generated by countless believers' prayers, similar to a kind of thought. When gathered together, it produces terrifying destructive power.

Underground, beneath the goddess statue, numerous devout believers knelt on the cold, damp ground, hands clasped together, constantly praying for the goddess to provide help. The power of faith gathered and was eventually absorbed by the statue.

This stone statue capable of absorbing the power of faith was a legacy left by the goddess. It was a Saint-tier structure serving both offense and defense. Not only could it provide a defensive barrier, but it could also unleash attacks with tremendous destructive power, containing the supreme power of the Lord of the Heavenly Realm.

In the center, surrounded by numerous believers, Joan wore white priestly robes and held a small bottle the size of a palm in her hand. Inside was a strange creature—

A viscous creature with bizarre large eyes, its pure white body covered in tentacles, with a structure similar to cells?

This thing had an extraordinary origin. It was the starting point of Bishop Slerin's research on the Holy Spirit. The powerful Holy Whales that had been transplanted were all related to this small thing, like maternal cells.

Joan hesitated, silently looking at the creature in the bottle, recalling what the Pope had said a few days ago. Pope Giougen had brought Joan to a secret place. The two slowly advanced through the black corridor.

Joan kept her head down in silence. For not being able to become a Hero, she had never been able to forget it, and it had dealt a heavy blow to her faith, to the point that her whole person had become much thinner.

"Joan, are you blaming me? I'm sorry I couldn't make you a Hero. Actually, in my heart, you have always been the best candidate for a Hero." Pope Giougen said, not turning his head.

"No, I have no complaints. Perhaps my cultivation is not enough yet. Compared to Alice, I indeed have many shortcomings." Joan answered calmly, having heard too many comforting words that were just polite phrases; she was already immune to the Pope's words.

"Don't despair, my child. I think your abilities would be too much of a waste if you became a Hero. There are more important things that need you to do," Pope Giougen suddenly said.

"More important things?" Joan was astonished in her heart, feeling that only by becoming a Hero could she realize the value of her life.

"Exactly, you are not suited to become a Hero. With your boundless piety, you are more suited to become a true warrior loyal to the Goddess. He is more noble than a Hero and also rarer. Only you are worthy of forever serving by the side of the great Goddess. I am deeply convinced of this," Pope Giougen said meaningfully.

"What are you referring to?" Joan became more and more confused as she listened.

"Wait a bit and you will know, my child."

They came directly to Bishop Slerin's secret laboratory. Many miraculous things here caught Joan's attention.

From the huge glass, he could see many bodies with pure white wings, and also the skeletons of Holy Whales.

Joan felt she was coming into contact with an extremely mysterious field. "Here

"This is Bishop Slerin's laboratory. At my request, he has been researching the Holy Spirit. The powerful Holy Whales were born here," Pope Giougen said softly.

"Saint Joan murmured to herself, recalling the powerful beings in the Church's stories. They had been created by the goddess by hand and were forever loyal to the goddess, messengers of the great divine.

"Under Bishop Slerin's research, we have learned many secrets about the Holy Spirit. They have a direct connection with the Goddess Maria. They are a species that can only survive in the heavenly realm for a long time. The mortal realm imposes all kinds of constraints on them. The longer the time, the closer they get to humans, losing all the power and characteristics of the Holy Spirit. In fact, they are not as mysterious as we imagine," Pope Giougen said leisurely.

Joan felt some shock in her heart. She had no idea that the Church had been secretly researching the Holy Spirit all along. She thought such beings could only appear in stories.

"Joan, do you want to become a Holy Spirit, to become a loyal direct guard of the Goddess? This responsibility is heavier than that of a Hero, and it will also depart from human identity," Pope Giougen kept hinting.

"Eh! Is this even possible?" Joan was horrified and stared wide-eyed, thinking how could humans possibly become Holy Spirits?

"Of course it is possible. The Holy Spirit and humans have many similarities. To be precise, the Holy Spirit is the perfect new human species created by the Goddess.

Just as the words fell, Pope Giougen recited a mysterious incantation. The stone platform slowly rose, and a mysterious small bottle appeared.

Pope Giougen took the small bottle and handed it to Joan. His tone suddenly became serious.

"In the late Demon Era, humans and demons engaged in a tragic Holy War. The heavenly realm helped us establish a prosperous era for humanity. Countless Holy Spirits fell in the war, among which were several powerful Holy Spirit leaders who served by the Goddess's side."

"The Church spent a lot of effort, successfully finding the remains of one Holy Spirit leader on the ancient battlefield. Its name was Gabriel, one of the Seven Virtues."

"Bishop Slerin, with his special techniques, successfully extracted the cell tissue from Gabriel's remains and successfully activated it. That is what is in this bottle. It is the mother body of all Holy Whales."

Joan stared wide-eyed, looking at the bizarre creature in the bottle, its ugly and disgusting appearance, difficult to associate with the noble Holy Spirit.

"If you eat it, the Holy Spirit will transform your body, integrate your bloodline, and let you also become a true Holy Spirit. No, perhaps you will become the successor of the Seven Virtues, Gabriel's successor," Pope Giougen paused, then lowly added a sentence—

"Of course, this has great risks.

"It is possible to lose oneself, letting your consciousness completely disappear..."

In the dimly lit underground room, under the encirclement and prayer of countless believers.

Joan held the bottle containing the cells of the Holy Spirit leader Gabriel, feeling very hesitant—

Might lose oneself, becoming a soulless shell?

If I could become a Holy Spirit, could I really accompany the great Goddess? Becoming a messenger of light that shines brightly!

More noble than a Hero, more powerful than Alice.

Devout faith exchanged for the Goddess's attention

Isn't this the thing I have been pursuing all along?

Joan's eyes became fanatical. Her body had already begun to act unconsciously. She slowly twisted the bottle cap.

title: Chapter 25 — Friends, It's the End of the Month — Cast Those Expiring Monthly Votes Already!
content:
Chapter 25 — Friends, It's the End of the Month — Cast Those Expiring Monthly Votes Already!

Volume 36 · Chapter 25

The demon forces surging into the Holy City were relentlessly advancing toward the cathedral.

They set fire to buildings along the way, destroying everything in their path.

This ancient city was about to be replaced by the Demon City.

The barriers protecting the cathedral were on the verge of collapse under the assault of Leviathan.

It seemed the Holy Church had little chance of turning the tide, completely dominated by the demons.

BOOM—

Suddenly, accompanied by a series of explosions, the Holy City began to rotate around the cathedral, its layout shifting as if it were a giant maze compass, separating the demon forces into several groups, preventing them from gathering together.

Then, high walls were erected to block the demons' path to the cathedral and successfully dispersed their forces.

The Demon Lords found themselves scattered across different locations, some closer to the cathedral and others farther away. Breaking through this complex maze would undoubtedly take some time.

Since the establishment of the Holy City, the Holy Church had made preparations for the possibility of demon invasions. The entire city was built on a massive mechanism.

If the cathedral was attacked from the outside, the city's mechanism would activate, raising a rotating maze that would continuously repel enemies away from the city, making it difficult for them to approach the cathedral easily.

With this mechanism, the Holy Church could gain valuable time, and as time passed, the scales of victory began to tip slightly in favor of the Light.

Knights from various parts of the world supporting the Holy City joined the war, tasked with delaying the demons' advance—

Beelzebub surveyed the surrounding high walls, his face expressing a few moments of confusion.

Blaise, hiding in the shadows, saw that he had been randomly paired with Beelzebub and sighed in his heart. What bad luck.

He recalled their last encounter, where he had been defeated badly, and Margaret's throne had been seized. Now, they had run into each other again.

"That's the Demon Lord? Looks like a simpleton." West Zechser commented.

"I don't know which Demon Lord, but I'd like to see that mighty Samiel." The Bull Warrior clenched his fists, eager to try his strength.

"You two should stay calm. That demon is Beelzebub, the Gluttony Demon Lord, with extremely formidable power." Blaise knew these two simple-minded individuals had no experience facing a Demon Lord. "We should come up with a plan before attacking."

"Plan? Are you crazy? We should charge in and catch them off guard!" West Zechser scoffed, not wanting to be compared to Blaise. "Any enemy in front of me will be crushed into pieces."

"That's right, true warriors never retreat." The Bull Warrior admired West Zechser and was not impressed by Blaise, who seemed like a coward.

"Wait! I'm serious. Charging in recklessly is suicide." Blaise urged seriously.

"Shut up, you cowardly Frenchman. If you're afraid, just pretend to be dead. That's very French." West Zechser sneered.

"As you all know, your cowardly Frenchmen surrender quickly, and we understand." The Bull Warrior said, his nose twitching, his spirit high.

"You?" Blaise felt bitter, wanting to cooperate with them but finding that they not only didn't appreciate it but also discriminated against him.

"Zechser brother, how about we team up and chop off that demon's head?" The Bull Warrior suggested.

"Of course, my brother." West Zechser had become familiar with this warrior from the cold lands and shared a similar temperament. "But if I take out the enemy first, you'll have to remove your mask."

"Impossible. I will definitely take out the enemy first." The Bull Warrior insisted.

Blaise rolled his eyes, having nothing left to say to these two idiots. He thought to himself how unlucky he was to have such dim-witted companions.

Beelzebub stroked the high walls, planning to find the direction of the cathedral and then advance toward it.

Suddenly, a deafening roar echoed, and someone launched an ambush.

The Bull Warrior moved like a human giant, trampling the ground with incredible speed, pouring all his strength into his fists and striking Beelzebub's face with a force that distorted his features.

"Demon, how's my punch?" The Bull Warrior boasted.

Beelzebub's eyes flickered, then locked onto the Bull Warrior, his gaze burning with the flames of demon blood.

"Huh?" The Bull Warrior felt a chill, as if he had been frightened. Normally, an enemy hit by his punch should have been knocked unconscious, but Beelzebub seemed unharmed.

"That's all you've got? Haven't you eaten?" Beelzebub asked, his expression wooden.

"Watch this!"

West Zechser arrived to support, his strong physique causing the ground to shake, his massive arms sweeping forward, resembling a crushing war machine.

The Bull Warrior charged forward, pouring all his strength into a punch aimed at Beelzebub's stomach.

BOOM—

A loud explosion echoed, and Beelzebub was knocked to his knees, with the impact of the punch causing a dent in the wall behind him.

Beelzebub stiffly lifted his head, asking, "Can you hit harder?"

"Uh!"

Both men were startled, as Beelzebub had taken two full-force punches and yet remained unharmed.

This level of resistance was far beyond the imagination of Zechser and the Bull Warrior, and they even felt a sense of humiliation.

The enemy did not dodge, allowing them to attack freely, as if they had complete confidence in handling them, treating them like kindergarten children.

West Zechser and the Bull Warrior realized the severity of the situation, as the enemy's strength was beyond estimation, and they regretted not following Blaise's advice to plan carefully before acting.

However, the current situation left no room for regret. They had no choice but to press forward, as only defeating the enemy in front of them could open a path for them to escape.

Thus, West Zechser and the Bull Warrior joined forces, burning their energy to the limit, pouring all their power into Beelzebub in a relentless onslaught of punches, showing no signs of stopping.

BOOM BOOM BOOM—

The sound of punches echoed continuously, and the surroundings were filled with blood and destruction.

"Hey, give it back to you!"

Beelzebub grinned, continuously absorbing their power. When the time was right, he reflected their attacks back at them.

A terrifying shockwave erupted, instantly destroying the walls behind him. West Zechser and the Bull Warrior's chests were blown open, and they collapsed into the blood.

Beelzebub gradually revealed his true form, his body now completely black, with the King of Flies' appearance slightly altered. With the infusion of demon blood, his body bore new patterns of fire.

Blaise had known this was the outcome, so he had not joined the two idiots in charging in to die, instead staying hidden and praying silently—

Don't see me, don't see me.

title: Chapter 26 — Month's Start: Request Wave Tickets, Extra Chapter Granted
content:
Chapter 26 — Month's Start: Request Wave Tickets, Extra Chapter Granted

Volume 36 · Chapter 26

Samer grabbed the head of the old wizard, lifted his corpse from the ground, confirmed that he was already dead, and then threw him away like trash.

This famous court wizard from Greenland had no means of resistance in front of Samer, and could only delay the inevitable by a few moments.

Samer's strength was already above that of the other Demon Lords, and after being enhanced by the blood of the demon god, his power increased even further, putting him just one step away from breaking through to the divine realm.

Although the old wizard was not bad among humans and was often invited to teach at various magic academies, in front of a true powerhouse, he was clearly not enough, especially when facing the former genius of the demon race.

All of the old wizard's magic failed to inflict any damage on Samer. The other party could simply crush him with brute force.

The result was obvious—the old wizard was instantly killed by Samer, with no suspense whatsoever. Standing behind them, Asmodeus didn't even lift a finger, just watching as a bystander.

The old wizard was probably the unluckiest person in this battle for the Holy City. He encountered two Demon Lords at once, but as a devout believer, dying for the protection of the Holy City was probably a death without regrets.

Samer and Asmodeus exchanged glances and prepared to move quickly toward the temple. The task that Baphomet had given the Demon Lords was—capture the Holy City and quickly occupy the temple.

So killing people was secondary; taking down the temple was the most important thing.

"Wait, are you really going to leave now? Didn't you ask me?"

A proud voice suddenly rang out. Samer and Asmodeus were surprised and turned around, only to find that there were still survivors nearby.

Morabi slowly walked over, tore off the purple and gold adventurer's badge on his neck, making it clear that he was sending an obvious signal—Morabi had temporarily set aside the adventurer's aspirations. He came to the Holy City not for himself, and even less for protecting the birthplace of human religion.

He was here as the younger brother of King Sanders the 16th, to take revenge on the demons!

"I heard you destroyed many places on your way here. Just five demons were enough to make an entire civilization disappear. It must have been you guys, right?"

Samer and Asmodeus said nothing, silently eyeing this fearless man. There was someone bold enough to step forward—his guts were not ordinary.

"My older brother, the King of Sanders, died at your hands. Who did it? Can you step forward so I can see you?" Morabi asked calmly, his face showing no trace of emotion.

Samer took a step forward, intending to deal with Morabi, but was stopped by Asmodeus's fan.

This left Samer puzzled, but seeing that Asmodeus was very interested in this prey, he fell silent and stopped interfering.

Asmodeus took a step forward and leisurely approached Morabi, a smile gradually spreading across his face.

King Sanders the 16th and Morabi were indeed brothers, and their facial features bore some resemblance.

Although the Demon Lords had all contributed to killing King Sanders, Asmodeus had indeed delivered the fatal blow—the very person Morabi wanted revenge against.

"Is it you?" Morabi demanded.

Asmodeus evaded the question and said casually, "Was he your older brother? You look so much alike. I remember, on his deathbed, he was looking forward to something. Could it have been you?"

"Tch."

Morabi's fist shot out before anyone could react, his face dark as the sky, his desire for revenge burning fiercely in his mind.

"What are you so proud of? Are you looking for death? I don't care if you're a Demon Lord or not."

Samer was shocked as he turned around. On the sturdy wall behind them, a fist mark had suddenly appeared, accompanied by a series of "crackling" sounds. The front wall was covered in cracks, as if it might collapse at any moment.

Morabi's fist, moving faster than sound, was incredibly powerful and hard to defend against. Just one punch was enough to nearly destroy the high wall—his speed and destructive power were truly astonishing!

"Hiss."

Asmodeus's flawless face was slashed by the recent gust of wind, and blood seeped out, staining it red.

Samer doubted whether Asmodeus could handle the current enemy, and thought it would be safer for him to step in.

"Asmodeus."

"Let me handle it."

Asmodeus's expression turned ugly. The thing he hated most in the world was someone hurting his perfectly beautiful face.

He spent half his day every day maintaining his appearance, showing just how much he treasured his looks. Suddenly being slashed, how could he possibly tolerate it?

Asmodeus wiped the blood seeping from his face, his eyes like winter, radiating a piercing coldness.

"The first person to hurt my face—you're the first."

"What does that matter? I want you dead!"

As the words fell, Morabi's martial spirit erupted violently, his fists flying in all directions, launching a full-scale assault on Asmodeus.

The supersonic punches created violent sonic booms that kept exploding in the air. The speed was so fast that no one could see the shadows of his fists, only feeling the sharp wind blades raging like knives.

Asmodeus was not skilled in close combat, but Morabi's speed and destructive power had reached an incredible level. He couldn't dodge at all and was beaten to a pulp right there!

"So weak! Something's wrong!"

Morabi became alert. The enemy could single-handedly destroy a nation—how could they be this weak, with no means of resistance at all? He couldn't believe his own eyes.

His older brother would have died at the hands of such an enemy? He must be hiding his strength, setting a trap for him to fall into!

Morabi was surrounded by flames of martial spirit, every pore on his body tensed, ready to guard against hidden attacks.

"Come on, let me see what tricks you're playing!"

Asmodeus's body turned into a pool of mud, quickly spreading out and wrapping everything around, plunging the area into complete darkness.

"Hehhehe, you'll never escape from here."

Under Asmodeus's mocking laughter, Morabi's martial spirit flames became the only light in this world.

"This is an illusion!"

In the darkness, sharp daggers appeared out of thin air, "swooshing" continuously, rushing toward Morabi.

"Ha!"

Morabi let out a roar, his oppressive pressure reaching its peak. His steel-like fists swung in all directions, forming a dense wall of fists that left no gaps.

Due to the lack of light, Morabi could only rely on sound to locate the incoming daggers and swat them all away.

But the number of daggers was too great, their whistling as they pierced the air rising and falling, becoming increasingly difficult to withstand.

After only a brief moment of defense, Morabi was finally pierced by countless daggers, his body resembling a wretched hedgehog, his condition deteriorating rapidly.

"Don't panic! This is all an illusion! The method to break the illusion..."

In reality, Morabi's consciousness was completely trapped in the illusion, his body standing motionless in place.

Asmodeus had great confidence in his illusion technique and didn't think Morabi could escape easily. He smiled and approached Morabi.

The fan in Asmodeus's hand ejected a sharp blade, slicing toward Morabi's throat, preparing to chop off his head.

Suddenly, Morabi's body moved, as if he had been prepared all along, waiting for Asmodeus to take the bait. With one powerful punch, he struck Asmodeus's face.

"You think you've won? Dream on!"

Asmodeus: "!!!"

title: Chapter 27 — Familiar (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 27 — Familiar (Bonus Chapter)
