Volume 36 · Chapter 27

"!!!"

Asmodeus's face contorted as Moraby punched him with a single blow, sending him crashing into the cold wall.

The aura on Moraby's body surged again, allowing him to successfully break free from Asmodeus's illusion.

Asmodeus held his cheek, brows furrowed, asking in disbelief,

"You broke free of my illusion? How is that possible?"

"Your illusions are indeed powerful, but breaking free isn't difficult either." Moraby said coldly. "Simply cut off your own consciousness and enter a pseudo-death state."

As an outstanding warrior of Sandabia, Moraby had mastered control of his body to the extreme. Entering a pseudo-death state by cutting off consciousness was something he could do at any time.

If the body was compared to a computer, then the pseudo-death state was like shutting down and restarting—it could eliminate the effects of illusions. Though illusions were tricky, they couldn't possibly still affect a dead man.

"I see. I was wrong to underestimate you." Asmodeus stumbled to his feet.

"Asmodeus, how about—" Sammel was about to say something.

"I can handle it myself, no need for assistance." Asmodeus replied stubbornly.

"Although you are merely a demon, I do admire your fondness for fair duels. But my brother's death must be paid for with your life!"

Moraby assumed a fighting stance, already resolved to take the Demon Lord down with him.

Asmodeus snorted coldly, swinging the fan in his hand and summoning a whirlwind that shot straight into the sky, churning the dark clouds overhead.

A gray, world-destroying tornado streaked toward Moraby, crushing everything in its path.

Moraby's eyes flickered, and he unleashed over a hundred punches in an instant. The howling force of his fists scattered Asmodeus's magic entirely.

The seemingly powerful world-destroying whirlwind was nothing before Moraby's supersonic fist technique!

Seizing the opportunity, Moraby closed in and launched a ferocious flurry of blows at Asmodeus!

Asmodeus couldn't keep up with the lightning-fast strikes and could only constantly evade, completely suppressed by Moraby to the point of being unable to catch his breath.

After several exchanges, Asmodeus was entirely at a disadvantage, pinned down by Moraby's fists, quickly covered in wounds.

"You're supposed to have killed my brother? This isn't even worth watching!"

"Don't get too cocky, human!"

Asmodeus's gaze hardened, and an invisible attack struck Moraby right between the eyes, like a needle piercing into his mind, causing excruciating pain.

Asmodeus cast his illusion on Moraby once again, halting the other's pursuit.

Moraby fell to the ground like a corpse, his eyes hollow and lifeless.

Asmodeus gritted his teeth and swung his fan, unleashing wind blades aimed at Moraby, wanting to take advantage of this moment to end the enemy's life.

Rumble—

The wind blade carved a gruesome trench into the ground, kicking up dust high into the air!

Asmodeus exhaled, believing Moraby must be dead, but when the dust cleared, he couldn't find the enemy's body.

"Hm!?"

"Are you looking for me?"

Moraby suddenly teleported in front of Asmodeus, his expression radiating endless killing intent.

He had used the same method to break free from Asmodeus's illusion, narrowly avoiding the deadly wind blade at the last moment.

"Argh!" Asmodeus panicked, continuously retreating. A mage forced into close combat with a warrior was fatal!

"This punch is on behalf of my beloved brother!"

Moraby roared, his fist like the sharpest blade, piercing straight through Asmodeus's chest!

Asmodeus stared in horror, coughing up a pool of blood, then slowly raised his head to reveal a strange smile—

"What a pity…"

"What!?!"

Moraby froze in shock. His chest had been pierced through, blood gushing all over the floor. He stared dumbfounded at what was happening, then suddenly realized something.

"I… I'm still inside the illusion!"

"The method you mentioned did work to break my illusion, but it could only remove one layer." Asmodeus's face curled into a smug grin.

"My illusions consist of thousands of stacked dream layers."

"Only the dead can break free of my illusions."

In the real world, from Samael's perspective, both Asmodeus and Moraby stood motionless, never having moved. Everything around them was exactly as it had been moments before.

Even time had barely passed more than three breaths.

But bizarrely, Moraby had driven his own hand through his chest, looking like suicide?

However, Samael knew this was all Asmodeus's doing—killing the enemy within an illusion.

From the moment Moraby had charged out and locked eyes with Asmodeus, that esteemed Purple Gold-class adventurer was already doomed.

While other Demon Lords killed their enemies directly and clearly, Asmodeus was dangerous precisely because his victims never even knew how they died.

Moraby's blood pooled on the ground as his gaze gradually scattered.

Asmodeus turned to look at Samael and said calmly,

"It's handled. Quite simple."

Meanwhile, on the other side, two old rivals had coincidentally been paired against each other once again.

Merlin:

Melsfield:

The two had been standing in standoff for a long time, neither daring to make the first move.

Unlike the fierce battles raging elsewhere between other Demon Lords and humans, this spot was unnaturally quiet, the atmosphere somewhat eerie.

Merlin hid beneath his Demon Battle Armor, the heavy helm tilted low, casting his face in shadow.

Melsfield couldn't read her opponent's strength, nor was she certain if the figure before her truly was the master of the Demon Lord Palace. But the enemy was a powerful Demon Lord, so she dared not let her guard down for even a moment—being extremely cautious.

*He must be waiting for me to show an opening.*

*I won't let him succeed. Let's see who runs out of patience first!*

Ten thousand years later (allegedly)

The two were still standing there facing off. By now, the other Demon Lords should have finished their opponents and be approaching the palace, yet they were just glaring at each other.

Melsfield's nerves had been tight this entire time, her patience nearly worn away. She thought, *Could this guy be an idiot? What's the point of me just standing here?! Show me your true demon nature already!*

"Surely His Excellency has nothing to say?"

Merlin paused, then removed his gauntlets and stuck his pinky finger into the shadows beneath his helm.

"Urgh!" Melsfield stared in shock, a strange sense of anticipation rising in her chest—

He moved! He finally moved! Reconnected!

What was he going to do next?

Was he going to remove his helm and reveal a terrifying face to frighten her?

That had to be it!

Merlin pulled his pinky finger out, gave a sharp flick, and sent whatever he'd picked from his nostril flying onto the ground, then hummed contentedly, feeling greatly relieved.

"????" Melsfield stood dumbfounded, black lines sliding down her forehead. *What was that?! After all that anticipation, he just picked his nose? And he's this relaxed right in front of me? Is he looking down on me!?*

Merlin reattached his gauntlets, tilted his head quizzically at Melsfield, and activated his ancestral skill.

"Damn you!" Melsfield lost her temper completely, drawing the Divine Weapon King's Sword from her waist, her forehead veins pulsing wildly—

*He doesn't respect me at all!*

*First picking his nose in front of me, then tilting his head to mock me?*

Wait!

His behavior… why does this feel familiar? It's like

That bastard Elgin the great swordmaster.

(7.7)?

PS: It's the start of the month again, my friends. Don't hold back now.

The Merlin demon illustration should come out this month. I've seen the artist's draft, and I'll share it with everyone as soon as it's finished.

title: Chapter 28 — **Focus on the Essentials**
content:
Chapter 28 — **Focus on the Essentials**

Volume 36 · Chapter 28

Although it was only a slight movement, it still brought back bad memories for Mesfield, the man she hated with her whole heart.

However, Mesfield didn't think much of it, assuming she was just too sensitive and overthinking things.

Mesfield's eyebrows twitched, and her anger rose, as she gripped the King's Sword in her hand.

"I, Mesfield, come here by the command of Queen Elizabeth to defeat you, whatever Demon Lord you are."

Since Mesfield had experience fighting demons and had some understanding of the Demon Lord's power, she didn't dare to underestimate her opponent. She attacked with all her might from the start.

Mesfield fully activated the power of her artifact, raising the King's Sword above her head. Her control over this divine weapon had clearly improved.

The sword's blade opened, with electric currents dancing in the middle, eventually converging into a single point. The overwhelming pressure rose, shaking the sky and the earth.

Although Mesfield's strength was at the Zong level due to the help of the Lake Fairy, the artifact in her hand allowed her to unleash extraordinary power.

Merlin seemed calm, but his hands had been subtly moving towards his waist, where the Banri Garan was. He must have felt a slight pressure.

The enemy was the ruler of the demon race, and Mesfield didn't hold back, attacking with all her might.

The King's Sword was swung down, and a fiery light beam erupted, roaring towards the lone Merlin.

The powerful shockwave shattered the earth, and even the distant temple could feel the pressure from the artifact.

Merlin's face remained unchanged, as he watched the fiery light beam from the King's Sword about to engulf him. He used his thumb to push aside the Banri Garan.

Suddenly, a killing aura accompanied by demonic flames shot out, tearing apart the fiery light beam and attacking Mesfield.

Mesfield's eyes widened in terror, her pupils contracting rapidly, feeling the near-terrible killing intent.

In a desperate moment, Mesfield stumbled and rolled on the ground, barely avoiding the deadly killing aura.

Casually, the sword-drawing technique cut through half of the Holy City, destroying all the buildings along the way, leaving a devastated wasteland.

Mesfield's heart was pounding, and cold sweat was sliding down her face. She thought that if she hadn't dodged fast enough, she would have been torn into pieces just now.

This power beyond imagination?

This familiar yet disdainful fighting style!

It was too much like the same person!

Mesfield hadn't fully recovered from the shock when Merlin suddenly appeared in front of her, giving her no chance to react.

"!!?"

Merlin grabbed Mesfield's throat and the arm holding the sword, lifting her up, unable to hide the killing intent on his body.

"Uh." Mesfield felt some difficulty breathing, unable to move as Merlin had her under control, her arm holding the sword feeling like it was being held by iron tongs.

Merlin increased his grip, planning to break Mesfield's neck, and after dealing with this enemy, he would immediately head to the temple.

At the last moment, the Lake Fairy emerged from Mesfield's mouth, and without hesitation, she hit Merlin with a slap, knocking him back.

Mesfield fell to the ground, rubbing her neck and taking deep breaths, feeling that she had almost died just now.

After stabilizing himself, Merlin looked at the Lake Fairy guarding Mesfield, not expecting the enemy to bring reinforcements.

The Lake Fairy waved her arms, summoning a surge of currents from all around, instantly imprisoning Merlin in a giant water prison.

Being imprisoned in the water prison, Merlin didn't panic but instead drew half of the Banri Garan, with the scorching demonic flames beginning to dance and stir in the water, evaporating the prison in an instant.

A large amount of steam began to spread, obscuring Merlin's vision, making it difficult to see the surroundings.

Suddenly, Mesfield launched another attack, emerging from the thick mist, holding the King's Sword and angrily slashing towards Merlin's neck.

But who knew, Merlin turned his head and without hesitation, used a technique that was unexpected.

"he——tui!"

"???"——

A mouthful of sputum suddenly blocked Mesfield's eyes, making her see nothing and her brain go blank.

Merlin took the opportunity to assume a sword-drawing stance, his eyes becoming sharp, wanting to kill the enemy under his blade.

Mesfield couldn't open her eyes, not realizing the danger was approaching, and she had no chance of survival under Merlin's sword-drawing technique.

Time passed quickly.

The Lake Fairy suddenly appeared behind Mesfield, pulling her out of danger, and then turned into a stream, entering the underground drainage system of the Holy City and quickly escaping the dangerous enemy.

Merlin suddenly stopped, putting away the sword-drawing stance, looking at the ground where they disappeared, and then looking at the distant temple being attacked by Leviathan.

This time, Behemoth's command was not to kill, although Merlin could continue to pursue Mesfield, it seemed unnecessary. Conquering the temple was obviously more important.

After confirming that the enemy was not pursuing, the Lake Fairy pulled Mesfield out of the drainage system, sighing in relief.

Mesfield was coughing, looking disheveled, "What are you doing? Why are you running?"

The Lake Fairy said without expression, "You only came to support the Holy City's army, not as a believer, so there's no need to die for the Church. It's too stupid, and besides, we only need to delay the demon's attack on the temple. The mission has been completed."

Mesfield had nothing to say, feeling that she had been a bit reckless.

"And besides, you can't beat that guy, so it's better to give up early. That's the wise choice." The Lake Fairy added.

Who said that? If I try hard, I can also do it. Mesfield was very indignant.

"Forget it, have you ever seen someone who can cut through the light of the King's Sword?" The Lake Fairy asked back.

Mesfield was speechless, recalling the strange moment just now, which was indeed too surprising.

"Don't say you haven't seen it, not even I have seen someone do this before. The person seems to be very skilled in sword-drawing, and the power is extraordinary. This feeling, I have fought Merlin before, and I have some impression." The Lake Fairy said with a confident tone.

"Indeed, it's very similar, isn't it? I also thought so!"

Mesfield's heart was excited, as if she had discovered a great secret.

She just wanted to say something more, but her body felt strange, with a strange vibration, just like every time she was spit on by the great swordmaster Elkin.

Recalling the thick sputum that blocked her eyes just now, wasn't it the same as being hit by his sputum?

Mesfield's whole body turned red and trembled, tightly hugging her legs, her expression becoming meaningful.

"What's wrong?"

Nothing.

Mesfield's face turned red, and she couldn't say what she was feeling now.

At this moment, she thought about many things. Why did the great swordmaster Elkin's sputum have a seductive effect, and she thought it was because he was chewing some secret medicine in his mouth.

Now it seems not to be the case. Maybe he was not a human, but a demonic creature that was good at controlling desires. It was the first time she had heard of a male succubus.

Damn Elkin, he must be one!

He's not human, he's a demon!

He's probably not an ordinary demon, but one of the Seven Lords!

No, I must bring this news back to Britain.

title: Chapter 29 — Power of the Main God (Monthly Vote Extra)
content:
Chapter 29 — Power of the Main God (Monthly Vote Extra)

Volume 36 · Chapter 29

Giant light barrier continuously guarding the God's Temple, it still appears somewhat precarious under Leviathan's fierce cannon fire.

Cracks have been continuously spreading; it looks like it might collapse at any moment.

However, the faith power collected by the majestic goddess statue is becoming increasingly surging. I see the sacred glow on the tall staff becoming increasingly brilliant, and a terrifying aura begins to continuously diffuse.

The situation has evolved into a race against time. If the demons rush into the temple first, then all the Church's efforts will be in vain.

At this moment, Beelzebub arrived first, surveyed the scene, and immediately chose to support Leviathan, working together to accelerate the destruction of the temple's defensive barrier.

Beelzebub vibrated the thin wings behind him, floating in the sky, and spat out a large amount of man-eating flies. With a buzzing sound, they assailed the defensive barrier. The intense impact caused the light barrier to start trembling, and the man-eating flies drilled into large and small gaps, constantly biting with their fangs at the energy wall, causing the light barrier to be further broken.

Leviathan and Beelzebub joined forces. The seemingly impregnable barrier now appears somewhat fragile.

In the temple, countless knights and bishops were anxious, their faces showing fear and unease, worried that the demons would rush in and tear them all to pieces.

But as the Pope, Giugen remained calm, his eyes fixed intently on the goddess statue, observing the collection of faith power. He was very close to achieving great success.

Blakefort was anxious. Outside, two Demon Lords were about to break through the defensive barrier and invade the temple to slaughter. He had no ability to stop the Demon Lords; he couldn't beat them even alone, let alone two Demon Lords working together? He couldn't even delay the enemy's attack rhythm.

The temple was shrouded in an atmosphere of fear and pessimism. It had been completely sealed off; even if one wanted to escape, it was impossible. Everyone was bound to share the fate of the temple; no one dared to casually ask about the Pope's condition. They could only continuously pray, hoping a miracle would happen.

Blakefort could no longer hold back. Gathering his courage, he stepped forward and asked in a low voice, "Your Majesty, the Demon Lords have gradually been asking for the maze. Soon they will gather outside the temple. The barrier probably won't be able to hold much longer."

"What is there to panic about? The faith power is about to be completed, and victory belongs to us," Pope Giugen said confidently, with a confident smile. According to the secretly formulated plan, he estimated that there should have been some movement on Vivian's side by now.

Blakefort felt very worried.

"Do you have any other opinions?" Pope Giugen impatiently glanced at Blakefort.

"No." Blakefort dared not say more, lowering his head silently. At a time like this, he could only believe that the Pope could turn the tide.

"Don't worry. You will just watch from the side. The so-called powerful Demon Lords are nothing in the face of the Goddess's power. The Holy City will bury all daring demons who dare to attack," Pope Giugen said confidently.

Blakefort was uneasy inside. Now two Demon Lords had already attacked the temple. Soon, other Demon Lords would probably feel it, and there was also a massive demon army.

Resolving the crisis of the temple? It was simpler than ascending to heaven. Unless an unparalleled powerhouse appeared immediately, capable of resisting all demons.

Blakefort had started thinking about his last will and testament in his heart. If the temple were destroyed, the Light Church would also collapse, and the believers would become a heap of sand.

Boom—

Accompanied by a huge sound, the light barrier protecting the temple, crushed together by Leviathan and Beelzebub, disappeared without a trace.

Everyone in the temple turned deathly pale, realizing that great disaster had arrived. The demons would not spare a single person.

Buzzing, a large number of man-eating flies swarmed into the temple, beginning to frantically tear and gnaw at the knights and bishops. Almost in no time at all, an adult could be eaten down to bare white bones.

People fell into chaos, constantly fleeing here and there in the temple. Where was there any look of noble bishops? They were just a group of ants on a hot pan.

"Your Majesty Pope, let me take you out through the secret passage, and if we are late, it will be too late," Blakefort urgently said. If they escaped now, maybe there was a chance to survive. There was a secret passage in the temple that could lead directly out of the Holy City.

"I said, Fort, don't be hasty."

As the voice fell, the majestic goddess statue suddenly emitted rings of light, gradually spreading throughout the temple.

Those fiercely man-eating flies, after contacting the halo, fell to the ground and died one after another.

Everyone stared blankly at the scene before them, astonished in their hearts, completely unaware of what had happened? They thought their prayers had worked, that the goddess had manifested.

Pope Giugen slowly lifted his head. The gloom on his face dispersed, replaced by an excited smile.

"Done! The faith power has been fully collected. The great power left by the goddess has been activated. The scale of victory has completely tilted towards our side!"

Outside the temple, Beelzebub frowned, discovering that he had lost all contact with the man-eating flies. This made him suspect there was a trap in the temple.

Under the escort of countless believers, Pope Giugen openly appeared before the Demon Lords, his face bearing an immensely confident smile.

"Dirty demons, daring to invade the Holy City? You will pay the price for your actions!"

"This sacred land absolutely does not allow you to easily desecrate it!~

"Today is the day you demons are sent to the grave! I, as the agent of the goddess, will give you a just judgment!"

In the sky, Beelzebub and Leviathan remained silent. In their eyes, this old man probably went crazy.

Neither of the two Demon Lords was one to swallow their anger. Without hesitation, they launched devastating attacks on the temple—

Leviathan hovered in the sky, opening its mouth to spit out a fierce Demon Lord light cannon. The destructive aura instantly enveloped the entire temple.

Beelzebub was not to be outdone. He inserted his hands into the ground, summoning a stomach comparable to a small world. The tender flesh walls continuously eroded the ground, spreading towards the clergy, intending to drag everyone, including the Pope, into his stomach.

"Let these two ants see a corner of the power of the Supreme Deity of the heavens!"

Pope Giugen roared, and behind him, the massive goddess statue roared. From his staff, brilliant light shot out like lightning, sweeping across the sky and the earth!

This is the power of the Supreme God, coming from the high and only ruler of the heavens. It is also a great legacy left for the Church!

The so-called Supreme God is the true controller of the world. Since ancient times, there have only been three. One is the God King of the Age of Gods, Odin. The other two are the key figures who constructed the new world order, Maria and Satan!

Under the power of the Supreme God, everything is an ant. Even Beelzebub and Leviathan, having been reinforced by demon god's blood, are not worth a hit under the power of the world's controller!

The attacks of the two Demon Lords were instantly shattered in the blink of an eye. Their bodies were blown apart, leaving only pale skeletons.

Leviathan's huge skeleton fell from the sky with a loud bang, stirring up a violent storm.

Instant kill! The two great Demon Lords were defeated and killed!

This was an undeniable confrontation. The goddess's power was overwhelming. - No wonder Pope Giugen had once said that even if an ancient Demon God came to the Holy City, he still had a certain chance of victory.

Now it seems, his words were not false!

title: Chapter 30 — Sweeping the Net
content:
Chapter 30 — Sweeping the Net

Volume 36 · Chapter 30

Inside the Demon Sealing Bottle, the souls of several Demon Lords had nothing to do, all worrying about the outside situation.

Suddenly, the souls of Leviathan and Beelzebub vanished into thin air in plain sight.

The sudden situation shocked all demons in the bottle, not knowing what had happened.

"Hey! Did you see that?" Merlin widened his eyes in astonishment, looking at the other demons. "Beelzebub and Leviathan's souls are gone!"

"What's going on? Did they both get freed?" Samael said in a low voice, thinking everyone's soul was imprisoned here, how could only Leviathan and Beelzebub be missing.

"No!" Asmodeus had a solemn expression, his face ugly, vaguely realizing something. "They're dead, their souls didn't fall into hell, but completely dispersed!"

"What did you say?" Merlin looked up, his face gaining some gravity. "Asmodeus, are you joking?"

"I'm not joking, it's all true. The Demon Sealing Bottle is a completely closed world. Souls disappearing here means being completely annihilated, not even qualifying to enter hell." Asmodeus explained seriously, hoping the other companions would realize the severity.

"Damn it!" Merlin subconsciously clenched his fists, unable to believe this fact. "Their souls were sealed here, how could this happen?"

"Body! My body!" Samael sensed the key point.

"Right, only this possibility. Our bodies left outside were used by Behemoth. The death of the flesh means the destruction of the soul." Asmodeus paused, guessing, "The flesh left outside by Beelzebub and Leviathan must have suffered fatal blows!"

"Oh my god, what's going on outside?"

Merlin frowned, his heart heavy with worry. If even Leviathan and Beelzebub suffered fatal blows, wasn't he in danger too?

Possibly never seeing Alice and his cute daughter again.

Merlin couldn't accept this, secretly hating himself for not being able to escape the Demon Sealing Bottle, only to wait to die here!

"It's possible Behemoth controlled our bodies to fulfill its ambitions and encountered unknown dangers." Asmodeus didn't dare be sure, but had some guesses in his heart. Beelzebub and Leviathan became Behemoth's sacrificial lambs.

"Can we only wait here and obey fate's arrangement? Isn't there another way?" Merlin found it hard to suppress his anger, dying so stiflingly, he couldn't bear it.

"We have no way to leave now, nor can we contact the outside. Besides praying for the Goddess of Luck's favor, what else can we do?" Asmodeus's tone was also helpless, having to accept reality.

"Damn it!" Merlin gritted his teeth, subconsciously clenching his fists. "I will definitely kill Behemoth."

"Merlin, calm down a bit. Although Beelzebub and Leviathan's deaths were sudden, in a sense, maybe it's not a bad thing." Asmodeus suddenly said meaningfully.

"What do you mean?" Merlin asked in surprise.

"Their deaths prove Behemoth's enemies aren't weak. The probability of us leaving the Demon Sealing Bottle is high. Conversely, we might be trapped here forever." Asmodeus said this, but the pressure in his heart was still huge.

Merlin didn't speak, thinking whether people outside could really defeat Behemoth? This was almost impossible.

Hahaha...

Before the temple, Pope Georgio laughed madly with triumph. Things were smoother than he imagined. The power left by the Goddess was incredibly strong, far beyond imagination, taking down two difficult Demon Lords in one strike.

Everyone's mood shifted from sorrow to joy. They also didn't expect the Goddess's power to be so terrifying, showing incomparable deterrence on first use.

Too bad this statue couldn't move, couldn't be used for offense, only for defending the Holy City. Otherwise, they would have crushed all Demon Lord Palaces long ago.

This was the first time the Church used the Goddess's power. The conditions for collecting faith power were extremely harsh, requiring numerous devout believers to pray together for seven days and seven nights to collect the faith power. If not used in time, or if believers stopped praying, the faith power would dissipate immediately.

After taking down two Demon Lords, the pressure of the Holy City falling weakened a lot. Those bishops who were scared silly earlier started to feel smug again, constantly praising Pope Georgio—

"No wonder you are His Holiness the Pope! You are simply the hero of the Holy City! No! The hero of the entire Church!"

"I knew His Holiness the Pope was far-sighted. How could he allow a group of dirty demons to pollute the Holy City?"

"The brilliant Pope will lead us out of the demons' shadow!"

Pope Georgio enjoyed countless praises, his heart becoming somewhat intoxicated. As long as the Goddess's power was there, demons were just a group of fools specifically coming to die.

"Hmph! Demon Lords? Just so-so!"

"Before the great Goddess, they are just tiny ants, can be easily crushed at any time!"

"We have the Goddess's protection, demons have no resistance at all. Are they so scary?"

Blackford saw the Pope looking at him, quickly nodded, "You're right. I'm really incompetent."

"In the end, the demons were too naive. They actually had the courage to invade the Holy City, so they should be mentally prepared to die here." Pope Georgio calculated silently in his heart. Things were going smoothly on his side. As long as Vivian took action somewhere, the siege crisis could be resolved.

Bang—

It was as if a meteor fell from the sky, hitting in front of the temple, stirring up thick sand and dust.

Samael in demon form appeared slowly, his terrifying shadow once again shrouded over everyone's heads. Six steel-like arms with prominent veins, abdomen furnace burning with angry flames.

A red-skinned demon fell from Samael's shoulder, with four horns on its head, its membranous wings behind looked very strange, like a light veil draped over the body. This was Asmodeus's demon form, his true hideous appearance.

Not far away, a figure appeared and disappeared. Merlin finally reached the temple, seeing Leviathan's huge skeleton. Behind the helmet, his face showed more confusion.

The temple was surrounded by Demon Lords again, this time three, seemingly falling into crisis. Everyone should have been scared shitless, but because of the Goddess's power, everyone had more confidence facing Demon Lords.

Pope Georgio was even more ecstatic. He was just worrying other Demon Lords wouldn't approach the temple, but unexpectedly the remaining ones all came to his door themselves.

"Good! Very good!"

"Today is the moment to round up all you Demon Lords!"

The majestic giant Goddess statue emitted rumbling sounds, the staff glowing with brilliant sacred light again.

title: Chapter 31 — Confronting Fear
content:
Chapter 31 — Confronting Fear

Volume 36 · Chapter 31

The majestic goddess statue radiated terrifying divine pressure, her scepter gleaming with brilliant light as power of faith gathered together, letting one faintly feel the tremendous strength of the sovereign of Heaven!

"Accept the judgment of justice! Demons!"

With Pope George's thunderous shout, the goddess's power shot forth from the top of the scepter, transforming into an irresistible wave that swept across the three Demon Lords who had gathered.

Even Leviathan and Beelzebub were shattered before the power of the Sovereign Deity; the other Demon Lords would likely find it difficult to withstand such danger as well!

The surge of the Sovereign Deity's power came straight for Samael and Asmodeus, its oppressive aura so intense that they were thoroughly startled, never having expected the Church to hide such a terrifying trump card!

Samael, relying on being stronger than Asmodeus and possessing body strength second to none among the demon race, surged forward, determined to withstand the Sovereign Deity's wave.

Samael's six steel-like arms formed a barrier, shielding himself and Asmodeus.

The Sovereign Deity's power swept across, churning up the earth before smashing into Samael's muscular frame. Several of his arms were visibly disintegrating, breaking down into white bones!

Even though Samael was stronger than the other Demon Lords, he could hardly withstand the power of the goddess, and at any moment he would end up like Beelzebub — reduced to bare bones, his soul inside the flask dissipating along with him.

Just at this critical moment —

Merlin suddenly stepped forward, positioning himself in front of Samael and Asmodeus, raised both hands, and strained to unfold spatial energy, erecting an invisible barrier to resist the Sovereign Deity's power!

The pressure on Samael and Asmodeus decreased significantly, giving them a sliver of room to breathe. They looked up and saw Merlin's figure standing directly in the front line of the goddess's assault!

"Hah! Naive! The power of the Great Goddess — how could it be so easily thwarted?"

Pope George laughed triumphantly, thinking Lucifer III was simply courting death.

He had originally planned to let Merlin off after reaching a secret cooperation agreement with Vivian, but since the other party was actively seeking death, there was no reason for him to hold back his ruthlessness.

The brilliant light of the Sovereign Deity's power relentlessly pounded the repulsion barrier, accompanied by the sound of cracking fractures. This layer of defense clearly could not hold out much longer —

"RUMBLE!"

A deafening explosion rang out, and a massive mushroom cloud slowly rose above the Holy City, flames dancing wildly around the temple!

The three Demon Lords lay powerless on the ground, severely wounded in their confrontation with the Sovereign Deity's power, with almost no chance of standing up again.

Pope George stared in shock, his eyes wide. This was beyond his expectations —

They had actually blocked it?

Impossible!

Could Lucifer III possess the power to resist the Sovereign Deity?

Tch! — It must be an illusion. Perhaps because the power of faith was nearly depleted, they had gotten lucky and survived!

Pope George, unwilling to give up, decided to use the goddess's power one more time to deliver the final blow to the Demon Lords —

"You got lucky blocking it once.

"But can you block it a second time?"

"You pesky, filthy demons, disappear!"

The goddess's scepter lit up with brilliance again, and this time the oppressive pressure was even more terrifying than before — clearly all the remaining power of faith had been poured into this single attack.

At the same time, on another front, a scorpion demon had burst into Alice's temporary residence, only to have its heart ripped out and killed by Ophelia.

The scorpion demon wailed in agony and collapsed, dying right at the doorway.

Lilith covered Chris's eyes with her hand so she wouldn't have to witness such a gruesome scene.

The little girl was somewhat frightened. This was the first time she had seen such a vicious demon, and she had thought all demons would be as friendly as these few around her. Unfortunately, all her illusions were shattered.

Chris shrank deeper into her aunt's embrace, too scared to raise her head, dreading the possibility of seeing a demon's grotesque face.

"There are more and more demons in the Holy City. It's probably dangerous at the temple as well," Ophelia said gravely.

"These scorpion demons are completely uncommunicable. They are BeheMos's servants and nothing like us," Abaddon explained.

The gates of the Holy City had fallen, and countless demons poured in to begin massacring. The situation here was merely a small缩影 of what was happening everywhere.

In such a short span of time, the Holy City had already turned into a sea of fire. The human residents here were suffering unprecedented persecution — demons were forcibly breaking into homes and slaughtering humans by the countless.

Fortunately, the demons under Lilith still had some ability to fight back; otherwise, they would have been cleaned up by BeheMos's servants as well.

"Don't be afraid, don't be afraid. Auntie is here," Lilith gently patted Chris's back, comforting her. "We need to find a way to leave. It's too dangerous here. Before long, there will only be more and more enemies surrounding us."

"No, Princess Lilith. BeheMos has not been eliminated yet. If we leave recklessly, we'll be surrounded and attacked by both demons and humans," Helena argued against leaving now.

"Tch! What a bother." Lilith gritted her teeth, glancing toward the adjacent room and thinking —

What on earth is Mother thinking?

At this rate, we're going to be buried alongside the Church!

Inside the room, Shu was reporting the current situation to Vivian.

"The Demon Lords have all gathered at the temple. It is confirmed that besides that one-eyed demon, BeheMos has no other helpers nearby. The opportunity has come, Your Majesty."

"Very well. It is about time. We can begin our operation and utterly eliminate BeheMos," Vivian nodded, feeling everything was still within her calculations.

"Your prediction was correct. The Church has drawn the vast majority of firepower, creating an opening for us to face BeheMos head-on," Shu said deeply.

Vivian smiled without speaking. This was merely one part of her secret cooperation plan with George — the Church would handle drawing fire, while she would deliver the fatal strike to the enemy.

"Miss Alice, come over. It is time to depart. What's wrong with you?"

Alice's expression was not good. She felt what was about to happen was far too dangerous. If something happened to her, would Chris be left an orphan?

"I'm very worried about Chris…"

"Lilith will take good care of her. Don't worry," Vivian said sternly.

Alice opened her mouth, hesitated, then said, "That's not what I mean. If this plan fails… Chris she…"

"We have no choice. This is a desperate, all-or-nothing battle. Even if we die, the other demons will raise Chris. She will be safer than anyone," Vivian had already given her orders. If the plan failed, Lilith and the other demons would continue living in the human kingdom and raise Chris to adulthood. She had already prepared herself to sacrifice for the sake of saving the demon race.

"That's right, Miss Alice. Do not worry. We will take good care of the young miss and will not let her suffer any wrongs," Shu promised beside her… but… Alice kept her head down. She did not want her lovely daughter to become an orphan without parents. No matter how well Lilith and the other demons treated Chris, they could never replace Merlin and Alice.

"Do you like Merlin?" Vivian suddenly asked.

"T-this…" Alice's face flushed red. She awkwardly lowered her head and answered in a voice barely louder than a mosquito, "Of… of course I like him."

"Then there's no problem."

Vivian sighed. Even though she deeply resented that Alice was human, she could not deny a fact at this moment.

Alice was the only hope for the demon race, and simultaneously Merlin's only beloved, and young miss's only mother.

"Do not carry too much pressure. The survival or destruction of the demon race has nothing to do with you. This is my matter."

"But you are Merlin's beloved and Chris's mother, so you cannot run away."

"To draw your sword to save your loved one is an admirable thing."

"Happiness is always wrestled from the jaws of fate. You should understand this principle."

Alice subconsciously clenched her fists and resolutely stepped into the magic array. She felt she should not shrink back in fear. Merlin and Chris were equally important to her. Why not fight for a complete family for her daughter? Why not bring her beloved back?

"Begin, Shu."

"At once!"

Shu's hands moved rapidly through a series of intricate mudras, pouring all his strength into activating the magic array pre-set with raven's blood. Eerie purple light slowly flickered on, swallowing the figures of Vivian and Alice —

In the blink of an eye, the two were teleported to the Demon City!

What they were about to face was an even more dangerous enemy —

The ancient Demon God, BeheMos!

title: Chapter 32 — Eighth Demon Lord
content:
Chapter 32 — Eighth Demon Lord

Volume 36 · Chapter 32

In the depths of the Demon Lord Palace, Shou had already used his familiar’s blood to successfully set up the teleportation array, allowing Vivien to enter safely.

Alice scanned the surroundings, taking in the ancient, shadow-filled city that seemed steeped in malevolent energy. She sighed, her voice tinged with awe, *"This... is the Demon Lord Palace?"*

*"Yes,"* Vivien confirmed, *"a city that has existed since the Age of Gods, the ancestral home of countless demons—long before the Seven Demon Lord Palaces were built."*

Alice froze mid-step, her gaze fixed on the sky where a monstrous, cloud-like visage emerged, its edges ablaze with demonic fire. *"What... is that?"*

*"Behemoth,"* Vivien said, her tone sharp with urgency, *"the creator of the demon race, the root of all chaos. We must destroy it."*

Alice’s eyes narrowed as she felt the crushing weight of Behemoth’s presence pressing down upon her. *"Same as an ancient god, but this pressure... it’s not even in the same league as the Black Dragon Nidhogg. How is that possible?"*

*"It’s not strange,"* Vivien interrupted her thoughts, her voice stern. *"You’ve only faced a fragment of Nidhogg, but Behemoth is a whole ancient god. Don’t waste time. Your mission is to find the Sealing Cauldron in the Seventh Demon Lord Palace and destroy it. According to Shou’s intel, it’s guarded by a one-eyed demon. Deal with him."*

*"I’ll do my best,"* Alice nodded, her expression growing grave, her shoulders heavy with the weight of the task. *"Though my power is already on par with a god, facing an ancient god that once ruled this world... I’m still not strong enough to defeat Behemoth. But I’ll buy you time. Before I fall, you must destroy the Sealing Cauldron. If the Demon Lords’ souls are freed, we win."*

*"Leave it to me."*

Alice’s body was enveloped in a radiant dragon warrior’s armor, and she soared upward, racing toward the Seventh Demon Lord Palace. Every second counted—time was of the essence.

Behemoth’s attention remained fixed on the Blood Pool, where the faces of scorpion demons kept emerging from the churning crimson. A smug grin spread across its features. *"Human, do you still not realize who you’re up against? Endless demons will trample the Holy City into ruin. I will stand at the world’s center, plunging all races into an unparalleled age of darkness."*

Suddenly, Behemoth sensed two unfamiliar pressures. Its gaze snapped toward the sky, scanning like twin searchlights, locking onto Alice as she rapidly approached the Seventh Demon Lord Palace.

*"A rat? To sneak past me? How dare you!"*

Behemoth’s eyes narrowed, his mood souring. With a roar, it spat a torrent of demonic fire toward Alice, attempting to halt her advance.

*"Ugh!"* Alice felt the scorching wave hit her, her head tilting back as if gazing into a sea of flames—only for a sudden gust of freezing wind to strike alongside it.

At the critical moment, a small black orb appeared, pulsing with eerie darkness and emitting waves that made listeners feel their souls being stripped away. The sound and waves corroded the oncoming demonic fire, shielding Alice from any real harm under Vivien’s protection.

Alice gritted her teeth, seizing the opportunity. She flexed her steel dragon wings, whipping up a biting cold wind that shattered the window of the Demon Lord Palace’s upper floor, allowing her to crash inside.

The demonic fire that had dispersed Vivien’s dark resonance was too late—Alice had already breached the palace.

Behemoth snarled in frustration, its pride wounded by the rat’s intrusion. *"I’ll burn you to ash for daring to enter my domain!"*

Its burning eyes flickered as it spotted Vivien below. Its expression darkened with meaning. *"Vivien?"*

*"It’s me,"* Vivien lifted her head, a mocking smile playing on her lips. *"We’ve met before, haven’t we? You’ve been hiding inside Belial’s body. We’ve crossed paths countless times."*

*"So you’re still alive,"* Behemoth said, not surprised. *"I always suspected. How could cautious you let a snake bite you so easily?"*

*"I never expected to fool you completely,"* Vivien replied calmly. *"All I needed was for you to lower your guard."*

*"Pathetic,"* Behemoth scoffed, his voice smooth but edged with irritation. *"Now that I’m free, what good is your long-term deception? Trying to stop me? Don’t be naive, Vivien. My power has grown—you’re not my match. Surrender, and become my servant. That’s the wise choice."*

*"I know I can’t defeat you,"* Vivien tilted her head. *"But I will free my son. He’ll end you. The shadow over our world has lingered too long—it’s time for it to dissipate."*

*"Relying on that human rat to save your son?"* Behemoth sneered. *"You must be joking, Vivien."*

*"She possesses something you never expected—a divine weapon of light,"* Vivien said, her voice heavy with implication. *"As the creator of the Sealing Cauldron, you should know what that means."*

*"You think I’m unprepared?"* Behemoth’s voice sharpened with anger. *"Eulobos, Belial’s son, the perfect tool—it will tear that human rat to pieces!"*

Vivien frowned, wondering aloud if Behemoth had ever heard of Belial having offspring. Had Shou seen the one-eyed demon?

*"You’ll fail,"* Behemoth roared, his voice dripping with venom. *"All your plans will crumble! I’ll burn you to ashes and use your remains to cultivate new demons!"*

With that, Behemoth’s eyes blazed with fire, summoning a relentless downpour of flames toward Vivien, determined to eliminate this pesky obstacle—even if it meant destroying the entire Demon Lord Palace.

Vivien raised her hands, and an invisible surge of divine power erupted from her body, forming 120 dark resonance barriers. Each barrier was infused with overwhelming divine energy, meant to withstand Behemoth’s fiery assault.

The 120 barriers stretched out in an inverted pyramid formation, their defensive power increasing from top to bottom.

Vivien was clearly stalling—to buy Alice time by holding off Behemoth, the greatest threat.

But even at the Saint-tier, Vivien was no match for the ancient god. The relentless fire rain shattered 40 of the barriers in quick succession, reducing her defenses by a third.

Vivien bit her lip, a bead of cold sweat slipping down her temple. The pressure was mounting—

*Damn it!*

Behemoth was stronger than I thought.

Maybe I can’t hold out for long. Alice has to hurry.

title: Chapter 33 — The Demon Bathed in Flame
content:
Chapter 33 — The Demon Bathed in Flame

Volume 36 · Chapter 33

Alice struggled to guess the opponent's identity but dared not underestimate them, so she braced herself and angrily scolded—

"Are you the demon guarding the Seal of Demons?"

"Hand over the Seal of Demons!"

"Otherwise, don't blame me if I don't hold back!"

The figure on the throne of laziness slowly stood up and walked down the high steps.

It wore a massive goat skull mask on its head, looking quite eerie, completely different from other Demon Lords, with its aura almost completely concealed, making it difficult to discern its true form.

Alice frowned, feeling that the mysterious demon before her was somehow familiar. Suddenly, she remembered the fortune-teller she had met with Merlin in Rhexum.

"Is it you?!" she exclaimed, recognizing the fortune-teller.

"We meet again, Miss Alice."

Orobas removed his mask, no longer playing mysterious, revealing his naturally single-eyed appearance, which looked quite eerie.

"..." Alice was stunned, seeing Orobas' single eye, and immediately realized that he was the guardian of the Seal of Demons mentioned earlier.

"It seems you have a deep impression of me, not forgetting me at all. I still remember that the fortune-telling result you received was quite interesting," Orobas said calmly.

"Who are you?!" Alice asked seriously.

"I am not a traveling fortune-teller, but the son of the Lazy Demon Lord Belial, and the legitimate heir to this Demon Lord Palace." Orobas did not hide his identity but stated it plainly.

"Belial's son?" Alice was stunned, thinking that this fellow was like most demons, a second-generation demon!

"Wasn't it just that a crow familiar was peeking around here? As I suspected, it was a staff member who had escaped the First Demon Lord Palace." Orobas paused, knowing that someone would come to seize the Seal of Demons. "But it's a pity, the Seal of Demons will not be given to you. Guarding it is my duty, as ordered by Behemoth."

"You are a member of the demon race, why do you serve Behemoth? That doesn't make sense!" Alice asked in confusion.

"My life is to live as a tool, no need to think, just follow my father's words and it is correct." Orobas looked at Alice and said indifferently—

"Obedience to Behemoth is my father's last will, I must act according to Behemoth's will.

"So I advise you to give up, leave here peacefully, and abandon all illusions."

"I don't like fighting, don't force me."

"Don't be so stupid! You've been deceived!" Alice learned some insider information from the demons and clarified,

"You father was already controlled by Behemoth, don't continue to be stupid, wake up!"

Orobas remained expressionless, unable to tell what was in his mind.

"You should think carefully, wasn't your father Belial, who suddenly changed his nature, making you feel completely unfamiliar? Parenthood cannot be faked! No matter how Behemoth hides it, it will definitely reveal itself!" Alice tried to make Orobas realize the truth; otherwise, a fierce battle for the Seal of Demons was inevitable. "Since you are Belial's son, no one knows him better than you!"

Orobas remained silent for a moment, saying meaningfully, "Oh, so you're quite cunning, Miss Alice."

"Ah?" Alice was surprised, wondering if she had said something wrong?

"Want to confuse me and steal the Seal of Demons? You underestimate me." Orobas looked at Alice and questioned, "Even the lie that my father was controlled by Behemoth can be made up, you've worked hard."

"Go!" Alice realized that Orobas was stubborn, almost a mindless tool, and even if she revealed the truth, he wouldn't believe it. It seemed that only force would work. "Hand over the Seal of Demons! Don't make me repeat it again!"

"I refuse." Orobas answered firmly.

Alice gritted her teeth and did not hesitate, the dragon warrior armor on her body roared, accompanied by a gust of wind, and she directly attacked Orobas.

The holy sword Light Clarion shone with divine light, the blade cutting through the air, creating countless golden ice blades, and launched a relentless assault without mercy!

"Although I am not a Demon Lord, my strength is not much different from a true Demon Lord, don't underestimate me."

Orobas pulled out a fortune-telling crystal ball from his pocket and bravely faced Alice's fierce sword techniques.

There was no fierce collision as imagined. The crystal ball emitted a terrifying suction force, instantly pulling Alice into the mysterious crystal ball.

In the palace, peace was restored again, leaving only Orobas, the demon, who stared at his crystal ball and said coldly—

"Welcome to my fantasy world, Miss Alice."

In the cathedral of the Holy City, the three Demon Lords were severely injured by the Goddess' power and lay unconscious.

Seeing that the Church possessed such powerful forces, many people could not help but cheer, the danger of the Holy City was saved.

Blackford also let out a sigh of relief, thinking that these demons were no match for the Goddess' power, and their invasion of the Holy City was completely suicidal.

"What good is surviving? In the face of the great Goddess, it's just a matter of time, isn't it? If you have the courage, continue to resist, let me see!" The Pope, Eugene, looked menacingly, preparing to give the three barely conscious demons a final blow, sending them straight to hell.

The scepter of the Goddess' statue was filled with divine power, ready to unleash a strike infused with all its power, far surpassing the previous two.

The Pope, Eugene, was determined to kill all three demons, making the Holy City an area that demons would never dare to approach again!

The sky over the cathedral resounded with divine chants, brilliant light soaring into the heavens, pushing away layer after layer of dark clouds!

The divine power transformed into an unstoppable radiant blade, sweeping towards the three demons!

Suddenly—

Merlin crawled up from the ground, his body surging with demonic blood, his body swelling, and the demon armor was forcibly torn open and ripped apart!

The demonic blood continued to erode Merlin's body, transforming him from within, rapidly entering the fully corrupted true demon form!

Merlin transformed into a demon bathed in flames, his face twisted into a grotesque expression, the red horns on his head wrapped in flames, and his sharp teeth like saw blades, looking like a human beast!

"What is that form?" Blackford was startled, his face pale, his heart trembling under the demon's overwhelming pressure!

The divine power blade struck, and the demonic form of Merlin unfurled his black wings, roaring into the sky—

"Rooooar!!"

The massive sound waves caused a space shockwave, like a compressed cannonball, instantly exploded outward!

The unstoppable divine power blade was shattered and dissipated by the demon bathed in flames, the light blade broken and scattered.

title: Chapter 34 — Chief of the Holy Spirits
content:
Chapter 34 — Chief of the Holy Spirits

Volume 36 · Chapter 34

"The Goddess's power... has been scattered!?

The sight before everyone left them utterly astonished, some struggling to believe their own eyes.

Merlin in his demon form had completely countered the main deity's power with merely a roar, far exceeding everyone's expectations.

In the same demonic state, Merlin was clearly several tiers above the other Demon Lords — it wouldn't be an exaggeration to say he existed in a completely different dimension.

Merlin himself had absorbed a vast amount of Demigod blood, far surpassing the other Demon Lords, and the短板 of his thin demonic bloodline had vanished without a trace, leaving him as an ultimate and perfect demon!

Bhehemoth had spared no effort in raising Merlin as his substitute, providing abundant resources along the way.

Rather than calling Merlin a Demon Lord, it would be more accurate to title him a new Demigod. This was not a confrontation between a Demon Lord and the main deity's power — it was a standoff between a new Demigod and the Goddess.

The demonized Merlin appeared monstrous and terrifying. A slight parting of his lips revealed sharp teeth, and viscous saliva connected in gossamer strands. A scorching pressure radiated from his entire body, causing the surrounding space to constantly quake and distort.

Merlin didn't need to make any moves. The sheer狂暴ness of his oppressive presence was enough to crush his enemies' will to fight!

Blackfoot trembled all over, his back already drenched in cold sweat. He could feel that every part of the terrible demon before him harbored destruction that crossed dimensions. "To resist the Goddess's power head-on... this isn't something a normal demon could do. What in the name of everything... what monster are we facing?"

"Are you kidding me? Someone is actually able to confront the great Goddess directly?" Pope Geoegen's face drained of color, nearly fainting on the spot. "This can't be real! Something must be wrong. Has the collected faith power run insufficient?!"

At that moment, Samael and Asmodeus also rose to their feet, gradually recovering from their severe injuries, their gazes fixed angrily upon the Holy Church's enemies. Fierce killing intent poured from them without restraint.

Everyone fell into panic once again as they realized the Church's trump card might not work. The oppressive pressure from three Demon Lords attacking simultaneously drove them into frantic screams —

"No! Are we going to die here? Murdered by filthy demons—"

"We beg you, oh great Goddess, save us! Your believers — don't abandon us!"

"Flee quickly! The sanctuary... the sanctuary is no longer safe. We'll be eaten as snacks by these demons!"

Panic spread continuously throughout the ranks. The once-united Holy Church descended into chaos, and many began contemplating abandoning their faith and fleeing the Holy City.

Watching the situation deteriorate further, Pope Geoegen could no longer remain silent. He loudly reprimanded the other bishops —

"What is there to fear? All of you, stay calm!"

"That was just a coincidence! I refuse to believe that filthy demons can withstand the great Goddess's power one after another!"

"Disappear! Obey the Goddess's judgment and accept your fate!"

Pope Geoegen behaved like a madman, unwilling to accept defeat so easily. He insistently launched another attack — this was the fourth time he had mobilized the main deity's power!

The scepter of the Goddess statue once again blazed with brilliant light, but the oppressive force had significantly weakened. Clearly, the faith power was nearing exhaustion, and this fourth strike was somewhat forced.

But Geoegen could not care less. His mind was consumed only with eliminating the demons threatening the sanctuary's safety. Even if the believers in the basement perished from exhaustion, he would not spare a single thought for them.

The fourth main deity's power swept forth, bearing down upon the three Demon Lords. Fierce winds surged like countless blades, relentless and unending.

Demonized Merlin assumed a sword-drawing stance. Just as the main deity's power was about to crash into him, he drew his blade in one explosive motion and slashed toward the sky!

Killing intent accompanied by scorching demon flames instantly scattered the Goddess's power. The towering and majestic Goddess statue was bisected and crashed down in a thunderous collapse of rubble!

This single strike had nearly destroyed half the Holy City. The area behind the Goddess statue was entirely engulfed in a sea of flames, scorched relentlessly by demon fire — a post-apocalyptic scene resembling the aftermath of a celestial catastrophe.

The bishops were so terrified they lost all composure. Abandoning all thoughts of noble faith, they scattered in every direction in sheer panic, afraid they would be devoured if they lingered even a moment longer. What they didn't realize was that demons were already everywhere throughout the Holy City — areas several times more dangerous than this one.

Pope Geoegen collapsed onto the ground, his face ashen. The precious Goddess statue had been directly destroyed, shaking the very foundation of the Holy City.

"We're finished. The Goddess's legacy has been destroyed — this is the very cornerstone of our existence!"

"Why can a third-generation demon like that counter the divine power that even the original Demon Lords struggled to withstand?"

"Lucifer the Third... he's not right! This completely violates all sense of reason!"

Blackfoot hurried forward anxiously. "Your Holiness, we must flee the Holy City quickly!"

"Flee the Holy City? Impossible!" Geogen's eyes flashed with unwillingness. "If the Holy City falls, the Church will cease to exist as well. Besides, do you truly believe we can escape?"

The Demon Lords were already steadily advancing, making it clear they had no intention of sparing any of the Church's high-ranking officials guarding the sanctuary.

Blackfoot panicked, drew the broadsword at his waist, and stood before Pope Geoegen. Steeling himself, he roared, "D-don't come any closer!"

As Samael and Asmodeus drew near, Blackfoot's breathing grew rapid and his legs trembled violently. A warm stream began flowing from between his legs.

*Be brave! I should be braver! Charge forward and clash with the Demon Lords. Even if I die, I can wash away the stain of cowardice!*

Blackfoot's eyes widened, his breathing heavy, as he continuously urged himself on within his mind. Yet he still couldn't bring himself to bravely swing his sword.

Samael and Asmodeus didn't even acknowledge Blackfoot. They brushed past him as though he were nothing more than air, heading straight for the aged Geoegen.

A weakling with no fighting spirit was hardly worth calling an enemy in the eyes of Demon Lords — he was merely a tiny ant.

As if all strength had been drained from him, Blackfoot collapsed to his knees, his body going limp. Cold sweat poured down his face in streams as his mind fell into complete blankness.

This knight still possessed no courage to face a Demon Lord. His瞎掉 left eye had become a psychological shadow that would haunt him for life.

The shadows of Samael and Asmodeus loomed over Pope Geoegen's head. Killing the weak man would require nothing more than a flick of a finger.

"You filthy demons, you want me to submit? Never!" Pope Geoegen spoke with unshakable confidence, believing that with Satan's protection, he could never truly be killed. No matter how many times he died, he could always return from the underworld.

Samael showed no mercy, raising his fist and launching a full-power blow straight at Geoegen.

Asmodeus also revealed the blade hidden within his fan, its sharp cold gleam pointing directly at Geoegen's throat.

BOOM——

With an earth-shattering explosion, a dazzling holy light erupted from beneath the sanctuary, shooting straight into the dark, cloud-laden sky. The radiance spread outward in concentric ripples!

Suddenly, a rain of feathers began to fall from the heavens. Countless shimmering pure white feathers drifted slowly downward.

Faintly, one could hear the echoing bells of the heavenly realm, playing a movement celebrating virtue and righteousness.

Pope Geoegen's expression shifted from despair to elation. Hope burned once more within his heart as he said with fanatical intensity —

"It worked!"

"Let me show you the power of the Goddess's exclusive guardian — the Chief of the Holy Spirits!"

title: Chapter 35 — Natural Enemy
content:
Chapter 35 — Natural Enemy

Volume 36 · Chapter 35

Pope Eugenius was on the brink of death when suddenly, fully ascended to a Saint-tier being, Joan of Arc appeared. With her own strength alone, she deflected the full might of the two Demon Lords.

Joan’s body had been completely consumed by Saint-tier cells, her flesh transformed into a true Saint-tier entity. Her skin was pure white with a faint translucent quality, revealing the blood flowing through her veins. Two pairs of pristine white wings stretched behind her, their powerful flutters stirring a biting gale.

Joan raised her head slowly, her eyes hollow and lifeless, the golden halo of a Saint-tier being forming above her head. Sacred power surged endlessly from her.

She was no longer the devout Inquisitor of her former self, but had inherited the strength of the Seven Virtues and Gabriel, embodying the new Saint-tier Guardian, wielding all the power reserved for the Goddess’s personal protectors.

Despite knowing the risks were immense, Joan chose to sacrifice herself for her faith, consuming the corpse of the fallen Gabriel to complete her transformation from human to Saint-tier being.

The living tissue of the deceased Gabriel was the Church’s core research subject for studying Saint-tier beings. If the Holy City hadn’t been on the brink of annihilation, Pope Eugenius would never have risked creating an uncontrollable new Saint-tier Guardian in such a dangerous manner.

Joan’s original consciousness had vanished, replaced by the newborn Seven Virtues’ awareness. Still fresh from birth, she didn’t obey Pope Eugenius’ commands and lacked full intelligence—like an infant—but she instinctively harbored an innate hatred for evil creatures.

The Saint-tier Joan muttered to herself, as if her dim mind were struggling to think.

Her gaze suddenly filled with murderous intent, radiating a terrifying holy shockwave from her body.

Blackthorn was hurled backward, crashing through several buildings before finally stopping, buried in the rubble. Clearly, both he and Asmodeus had taken severe damage.

Joan was no longer human—she was a Saint-tier Guardian who had once battled the original Demon Lords in the Holy War. Even as a newborn, her power rivaled that of Gabriel.

Though Blackthorn and Asmodeus had been enhanced by Demon God blood, they still paled in comparison to the original Demon Lords. They were no match for the Saint-tier Joan.

*"This is Joan? Why does she look like this?"*

Blackthorn’s eyes twitched wildly as he stared at Joan, feeling utterly unfamiliar with her—she no longer seemed human, more like a mindless machine.

Yet Blackthorn was puzzled. Joan’s power had skyrocketed in a short time, her aura as terrifying as Lucifer’s demonic transformation. He couldn’t tell who was stronger—his level simply couldn’t penetrate the truth.

*"Amazing! This is the power of a Saint-tier Guardian? No wonder they could drive demons to the brink of extinction in the Holy War!"* Pope Eugenius’ face twisted into a grotesque grin. *"This is a divine miracle! Humans have once again made contact with the heavens!"*

Saint-tier Joan suddenly locked eyes with Eugenius, her hollow gaze revealing a flicker of hostility. She advanced relentlessly.

A blade of holy light appeared in Joan’s hand, her murderous intent toward Eugenius unmistakable. She wasn’t resentful of the Pope altering her fate—she instinctively sought to purge the dark creature before her, even if it was the Pope himself.

The Heavenly Messenger’s attempt to kill the Goddess’s earthly proxy was unimaginable to ordinary people. It looked like Joan had gone mad.

But Pope Eugenius knew exactly what was happening—he even felt a pang of guilt, retreating further.

*"What are you doing? I’m the Pope! The Goddess’s proxy on earth! You owe everything to me! You should obey my orders!"*

*"Joan, what are you doing? That’s Pope Eugenius!"*

Blackthorn, terrified, lunged forward to stop Saint-tier Joan, only to be struck by her white wings and sent flying.

*Thud—*

Blackthorn crashed into a wall, sprawling on the ground with blood trickling from his mouth. His bones felt shattered, the power difference too vast for him to comprehend—Joan had changed in an instant.

*"Damn it!"* Pope Eugenius was cornered against the wall, realizing Slein had been right. Even if they artificially created a powerful Saint-tier Guardian, it wouldn’t be controllable—and it seemed to have instantly recognized his identity as a Hellbound Messenger.

Suddenly, a massive boulder crashed toward them, drawing Saint-tier Joan’s attention. She sliced it apart with her blade of light.

Unlike Asmodeus, Blackthorn managed to stagger to his feet, his demonic limbs twisted and monstrous, the flames in his abdominal furnace roaring higher.

Blackthorn growled, plunging his four arms into his belly to compress the flames before unleashing them straight at Saint-tier Joan.

The ground before the temple melted under the flames, forming a river of molten rock. The fire illuminated Joan’s enemy in crimson.

Saint-tier Joan remained composed, ignoring the insignificant Eugenius. The demons’ threat was far greater.

She raised her blade of light and hurled it at Blackthorn, splitting his flames in two and piercing his shoulder.

Holy power invaded from within, destroying Blackthorn’s formidable body. The two forces clashed violently inside him, forcing even this flesh-bound Demon Lord to let out a wail of agony.

Saint-tier Joan seized the moment, firing two more blades of light into Blackthorn’s thighs and abdomen, aiming to kill him outright.

Blackthorn knelt, his abdominal flames flickering weakly—his life was hanging by a thread.

Joan toyed with her blade, her gaze hardening as she fired the fatal strike.

At that moment, Merlin—who had remained motionless—suddenly darted in front of Blackthorn, grabbing the blade of light hurtling toward him before crushing it in his hand.

*Boom—*

An explosion rocked the air, flames rising into the sky.

Merlin, in his demonic form, stood amidst the fire and smoke, his sharp teeth grinding in fury as the Saint-tier being enraged him.

Saint-tier Joan froze, sensing she had finally found a worthy opponent. She flapped her wings and took to the air, summoning a holy blade array in the process. The sky filled with countless blades, suspended like a storm of deadly meteors.

The pressure of divine power raged above the temple, each suspended blade a sword of Damocles, terrifying to the demons.

The blades shimmered like countless stars, their light blinding.

Saint-tier Joan looked down at demonic Merlin, as if she had returned to the brutal war between Saints and demons at the end of the Demon Era.

With a flick of her fingers, the blade array descended like a vast storm of light.

Pope Eugenius, hiding in the corner, couldn’t help but smirk darkly, muttering to himself.

*"That’s right. Even if you don’t listen to me, as long as you obediently attack the demons, that’s success."*

*"Joan, though you can’t become a Hero, you’ve become a Saint-tier being who can eternally accompany the Goddess. You should truly thank me."*

Demon-form Merlin harbored the greatest murderous intent toward this Saint-tier enemy. As the holy light rained down upon him, his Demon God blood surged wildly.

title: Chapter 36 — Massacre (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 36 — Massacre (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 36 · Chapter 36

The demonic-form Merlin roared as he charged into the sky, where a storm of divine blades raged down upon him. The deafening shockwave scattered countless blades, shattering the formation into chaos.

Saint Chastity was hurled by the blast, slamming violently into the cold, high wall. Cracks spread like spiderwebs across the surface before the entire structure collapsed beneath her.

Chastity stumbled out of the rubble, rubbing her neck with a grating sound—she hadn’t suffered any real damage. Floating in the air, she looked down at Merlin below, her wings casting a radiant glow behind her.

Merlin lunged forward, his massive black wings beating as he soared toward the sky-bound Chastity. Her eyes flickered with alarm as she crossed her arms, and a golden light erupted above her head, forming a protective barrier that deflected Merlin midair.

Seizing the moment, Chastity pressed her advantage, relentlessly pursuing him as he plummeted. She struck three devastating blows to his chest, each punch shaking him like a meteorite crashing to earth. The ground trembled, fissures spreading as debris flew in every direction.

The force of those punches rattled Merlin’s bones. Chastity descended from the sky, her blade of light piercing toward his skull, aiming to end him in one strike.

*"Did it work?"* Pope Eugenius gasped, his eyes wide. From his angle, Chastity’s blade had indeed pierced Merlin’s head—but it was an illusion. The demon twisted his head, dodging the fatal strike, and the blade instead buried itself in the earth beside him.

Merlin exhaled a scorching breath from his nostrils, seized Chastity’s neck, and snapped it like a twig before hurling her toward the temple like a javelin. She crashed through dozens of stone pillars, embedding herself in the wall like a crushed insect.

Chastity struggled to adjust her broken neck, but the injury wasn’t fatal. Before she could react, Merlin suddenly appeared before her, his sword *Banri Garan* already drawn and swinging in a lazy arc—

Chastity was bisected, her upper body severing from her lower. Blood spurted violently.

Though Saint Chastity was no angel, her resilience was legendary—even the fallen archangel Gabriel had survived for so long. Chastity was no exception.

Merlin pressed forward, his sword igniting a blaze of demonic fire as he aimed to finish her. Desperate, Chastity flapped her wings, fleeing upward—but her lower half was already consumed in flames.

Merlin looked up in disbelief as Chastity, half her body gone, still struggled to move. The wound at her waist, though sealing shut, hadn’t regrown her legs—her regenerative ability paled compared to the bloodline’s.

*"You’re strong,"* Chastity rasped in a mechanical tone, *"but I must erase you."*

She spread her arms wide, and a blinding light descended from the sky, unbearable to behold. Within the radiance, a weapon’s silhouette emerged—its aura reminiscent of a divine relic, pressing down upon them.

Chastity plunged her hands into the light and withdrew a pure-white spear, its surface wrapped in countless threads of blood.

*The spear of Longinus*—a semi-divine artifact once wielded by the archangel Gabriel in the Holy Wars, said to have been forged with the blood of a goddess, containing fragments of the Primordial God’s power. Even as a semi-divine weapon, its might rivaled true divine relics.

*"Longinus... Chastity has fully inherited Gabriel’s power,"* Pope Eugenius realized, a cold sweat trickling down his brow. He’d heard the legends—this spear had made the original Demon Lords tremble, their blades unable to stand against its edge.

*"Time to decide the victor,"* Chastity muttered without expression, gripping the spear tightly. She poured all her divine power into it, then hurled it downward at Merlin.

A searing light erupted as the spear streaked toward him, its blood-threads glowing with divine energy. No wonder the first Demon Lords had dared not face it—its power could slay all dark beings.

The spear moved so fast that Merlin barely registered it before it pierced his lower lip, embedding itself in the earth behind him.

Merlin froze, staring at the spear jutting from the ground. He touched his bleeding mouth, the wound refusing to heal—it had struck a nerve.

Chastity recalled the spear, recharged it with divine power, and her gaze turned colder.

*"This time, I won’t miss. I’ll pierce through your body."*

Merlin’s eyes burned with fury as Chastity locked onto him. His lip wound was already knitting shut.

Chastity aimed the spear once more and hurled it with all her strength.

Then—

An impossible shift. Merlin vanished in an instant, reappearing before Chastity and slashing upward with *Banri Garan*.

*"Clang!"*

Chastity was split open like a ripe fruit, her semi-divine spear *Longinus* shattered in two.

*"!!?"* Pope Eugenius’s eyes widened in horror. He hadn’t expected Lucifer III to be this terrifying—even the archangel Gabriel would have been killed instantly. Chastity had been winning, but in the blink of an eye, she was defeated.

Eugenius watched in stunned silence as Chastity plummeted from the sky, her blood spraying across the air. Her body lay half-severed on the ground, clutching *Longinus* tightly as the earth beneath her turned crimson.

Merlin descended, his boot crushing Chastity’s back. He reversed his grip on *Banri Garan*, the blade’s heat radiating as he aimed for her heart.

His jagged teeth rattled in a mocking growl—

The sword pierced Chastity’s torso, and the demonic fire within her erupted.

title: Chapter 37 — Sorry for the Late Update
content:
Chapter 37 — Sorry for the Late Update

Volume 36 · Chapter 37

The blazing fire of the demon lord rose high into the air, and Saint Theresa was reduced to ashes in the flames. The Church had given up all its secrets, but it still couldn't resolve the crisis facing the holy city. Demon lord Merlin emerged from the flames, step by step approaching Jörgen, making him feel an unprecedented threat of death. "Even the power of the seven virtues can't do anything to Lucifer the Third?" Jörgen trembled with fear and retreated backward, being pushed into a narrow corner, thinking to himself, "What's Vivian doing? I'm already at my limit here!" Merlin held the Banri Garan, pointing it at Jörgen, with demon flames blazing in his eyes, and the pressure was so intense that the high-ranking pope could hardly breathe! Jörgen had once issued a bounty to hunt down Merlin, but now Merlin was standing right in front of him, not even daring to let out a fart. Suddenly, the thought of Behemoth came from afar, and Merlin turned his head towards the direction of the demon castle. There, it seemed that something was wrong, and Behemoth was constantly calling out to him, Demon Castle. The fire rain continued to pour down, covering the entire city in flames, with high temperatures constantly attacking, making it seem like being in a furnace. Vivian summoned out 120 dark defensive restrictions, but under the constant attack of the fire rain, only the last three layers were left to struggle. She had a cold sweat on her forehead, feeling an enormous pressure facing Behemoth's attack! Vivian gritted her teeth, constantly pouring divine power into the defensive restrictions, hoping to hold on a bit longer, but the increasingly intense fire rain was shaking her confidence - - What about Alice? It seemed that things were not developing as smoothly as she had imagined. It was really terrible, her power would probably not be able to withstand for much longer, and if Alice didn't succeed, they would be doomed. What other way was there? "Surrender, Vivian, you can't hold on for much longer, becoming a slave is not so bad? I created the demons, and your existence is to be unconditional obedience to me, this is your purpose." Behemoth was tempting Vivian, and it had already seen that Vivian was at her limit, unable to hold on for much longer. Although god-tier beings could be on par with gods, they were still a few steps behind in terms of opposing ancient gods. "Don't dream, Behemoth, the demon race will never become anyone's slave, not even our creator, since the ancient prophet freed the demons and gave them freedom, the demons have never been your vassals!" Vivian responded seriously, not wanting to turn back the clock of history, to return to the era when Behemoth ruled the demons. "We ancient gods are the great existences that existed since the beginning of creation, all things were created by us, this is a fact that cannot be changed, you demons are just my toys, and now you want to rebel against me? How ridiculous!" Behemoth emphasized, "Except for me, no one can give you freedom, the prophet you idolize is just a despicable and shameless thief, using him as a savior is how pitiful!" "As long as we can free the demon race from your brutal rule, what does it matter if he's a thief?" Vivian lifted her head, staring straight at Behemoth, "Your ambition will not succeed." "I have already summoned the other demon lords, and when they arrive, you will face a desperate situation, and you will see how you can still be stubborn!" Behemoth angrily scolded, and the fire rain in the sky suddenly became ten times more intense, bombarding Vivian with all its might! The dark defensive restrictions were immediately destroyed, leaving only the last layer to struggle. Vivian was already at her limit, with a worried expression, if Behemoth's words were true, then soon the other demon lords would arrive to support him, and she would be doomed! It was probably impossible for anyone to resist the attack of Behemoth and Merlin and the other demon lords, and Vivian had no confidence at all. "Since you refuse to submit to me, then you should disappear! The fire rain concentrated in the sky, forming a giant fire skeleton, like a small sun burning fiercely, and it was about to fall on Vivian. Boom, boom, boom - - The explosion shook the heavens, and the flames continued to bombard the last layer of the dark defensive restrictions! Vivian gritted her teeth, trying to separate the support, but it was still impossible to resist the terrifying power of the ancient god, accompanied by the faint "crack, crack" sound, the defensive restrictions began to crack, and finally shattered! The demon-like flames were like a rainbow, and Vivian was instantly engulfed in them. "Ha ha ha, this is the fate of those who dare to oppose me!
