The sky was filled with Behemoth's laughter, and his burning eyes stared at the Seventh Demon Lord Palace in the demon castle, thinking it was time to get rid of the human mouse that had intruded on his territory. But suddenly, the raging demon fire disappeared completely, as if it had been corroded by some power. In the center of the demon castle, a huge black whirlpool appeared, with corroding gas flowing out, constantly corroding the scorching flames. When the dark attribute power reached its peak, it could corrode all matter, including flames and air, and corrode everything down to nothingness. This was Vivian's dark power, and the pressure of the god-tier being spread rapidly, soon corroding a huge pit in the ground, passing through the demon castle. A black demon with twelve wings fluttering behind her floated in the air, with a fiery and seductive figure, red gemstone-like eyes flashing with icy light, and a red-colored horn on her head stood out prominently, like a shining crown! Vivian revealed her demon form, and her original appearance was more feminine and beautiful than the other demons, who were grotesque and ugly. "It's true, I couldn't easily get rid of you, but you're not even half as good as your father, Mephistopheles!" The sky darkened, and Behemoth opened his massive mouth, large enough to swallow the entire demon castle! A tsunami of flames was released, mixed with thunder, and it was about to collide with the tiny Vivian! The expanding black whirlpool continued to corrode Behemoth's lightning, and Vivian, in her demon form, furrowed her brow, using all her strength to maintain the stability of the whirlpool - - The two entered a fierce stalemate. When Alice opened her eyes again, the surroundings were pitch black, and a thick white mist filled the air. Alice vaguely remembered that she had been sucked into the crystal ball of Eulobius, and this was the enemy's domain. In this situation, Alice had to be even more cautious, thinking of how to escape from here. She was very anxious, wanting to find the seal bottle as soon as possible, to give herself time outside, and to help the struggling Vivian, the pressure was equally huge. Suddenly, the white mist began to move rapidly, gathering in front of Alice, and gradually taking shape, becoming a real entity, a silver-haired, blue-eyed young girl. Alice was shocked, instinctively gripping the slender sword in her hand, with a look of incredulity - - This girl was not anyone else, but herself!

title: Chapter 38 — Perfect Match
content:
Chapter 38 — Perfect Match

Volume 36 · Chapter 38

In the crystal ball mystery of Europa, another Alice appeared!
She looked exactly like Alice herself, even the light lament in her slender sword was identical.
The only difference was the expression on her face; unlike the righteous and stern Alice, her smile carried a hint of malicious evil.
“What is this?”
Alice stared at her exact double, stunned, not knowing what was happening.
The replica Alice gradually emerged from the mist, wearing a sinister smile, assuming the exact same defensive stance.
Alice furrowed her brows, wondering if this was an illusion created by Europa to deliberately confuse her.
She waved her hand toward the opposite replica, wanting to test her idea.
The opposite replica Alice almost perfectly mimicked and captured her movements; both waved their hands simultaneously, face to face.
“Huh?” Alice felt something was off, feeling as if the other was her projection in a mirror.
In the invisible space between Alice and the replica, it was as if a mirror existed, creating a perfect replica entity; without looking at their expressions, it was impossible to tell who was the real Alice.
In this mist-filled crystal ball world, the atmosphere instantly turned eerie.
Under normal circumstances, Alice would never dare act rashly, but now the situation was urgent—every second was bought with Vivian's life, extremely precious, leaving no room for much hesitation.
“Never mind all that; if I just take down this fake, I can get out of this damned place, right? Then it’s simple.”
Alice immediately assumed a stance; the iron wings on her back roared as she launched the first attack, the Light Lament flashing with cold light, wrapped in piercing wind and snow, thrusting straight at the replica's throat!
At almost the same moment, the replica mimicked all her actions, her blade likewise thrusting toward Alice's throat!
Their movements were completely identical, even the pressure they exuded and the sharpness of their swordsmanship were the same, making it look as if they were exactly the same person!
Alice and the replica quickly closed in, on the verge of fierce close-quarters combat; she sensed the opponent's blade seemed faster than her own, possibly able to slit her throat with a single strike!
So Alice instantly withdrew all her attacks, placed her slender sword horizontally across her chest, adopting a defensive posture—but then a bizarre scene unfolded.
“Eh!”
The replica also withdrew all attacks, holding her slender sword horizontally across her chest, mimicking the exact same defensive posture!
The two were very close; any sword strike could wound the other, yet both defended cautiously, neither daring to strike first.
The replica's evil, charming smile grew thicker, as if mocking the timid Alice like a mouse?
“Shout!”
Alice felt she was being toyed with, as if she were truly fighting her own reflection in a mirror.
She immediately launched a fierce assault without hesitation, shaking her slender sword, silver light bursting forth, countless sword rays stabbing toward the replica.
The replica responded in kind, facing Alice's fierce sword technique, not falling behind in the slightest!
The clash of blades sent sparks flying; it was impossible to tell who would win, the replica's strength was not inferior to Alice's, and even seemed to have a slight edge.
Impatient, Alice abandoned all defenses, wanting to quickly defeat the troublesome opponent, she thrust her sword straight through the replica's left shoulder with full force.
However, at the exact same moment, the replica used the same sword technique, piercing Alice's shoulder!
The two quickly retreated, creating a certain safe distance—
Drip, drip, blood trickled down from Alice's shoulder; she gritted her teeth, glaring at her replica, noticing the smile on the other's face had lingered, and the pierced shoulder was emitting thin white smoke.
Obviously, the damage from the fight affected only Alice herself; the replica was a lifeless puppet.
If she could not defeat her own replica, the result could only be mutual destruction—Alice would be killed by her “self2”.
“What on earth is going on?”
“Don’t waste your effort, Miss Alice.”
Alice raised her head, hearing Europa's echoing voice, she demanded, “What did you do?”
“This is my fantasy secret realm; I can replicate an opponent completely identical to you in appearance, power, behavior patterns, and so on—everything can be copied. In a sense, the one standing before you is yourself.” Europa replied calmly.
“Nonsense, this must be your blindfold trick, right?” Alice said through gritted teeth.
“No, you misunderstand; a true blindfold wouldn’t harm you, but here, it will take your life.” Europa emphasized.
“Don’t bluff! I will get out of this damned place!” Alice stared at her replica.
“Give up; you cannot leave my secret realm. To leave, you must defeat the replica—no, you must defeat yourself. Almost no one can do this. I have seen many enemies trapped in my secret realm; without exception, they all ended in mutual destruction with themselves.” Europa paused, then continued, “So just stay here obediently; as long as you behave, your replica won’t pose a threat. When the Holy City falls completely, I will hand you over to Behemoth for him to personally judge you.”
“You’re dreaming! You demon race traitor will surely be despised by other demons! Your father was already a puppet manipulated by Behemoth; as his son, you haven’t even noticed the abnormality?” Alice said persuasively, hoping Europa would turn traitor at the last moment.
“Sorry, I cannot determine whether your words are lies or truth; therefore, I will go by my own understanding.” Europa answered blandly.
“You are a sentient being with self-awareness, not a block of wood! Please think for yourself—why would you willingly become a tool of the demon god? Do you truly have no independent thought at all?” Alice shouted angrily, puzzled in her heart.
“My father taught me that I need not overthink; just obey his words. Loyalty to Behemoth is his dying wish, so I will naturally follow it.” Europa paused, then said seriously, “To me, my father’s words are absolutely correct, beyond doubt.”
“That isn’t your father’s last words; it’s Behemoth’s excuse to deceive you!” Alice frowned, speaking low, “Your father is the leader of the demon race; now the demon race is on the brink of annihilation, all demons will become slaves of Behemoth—is that what your father wants to see?”
Silence, a long silence—
Alice could not discern Europa’s thoughts at this moment, nor could she understand how difficult it is for someone who has been brainwashed since childhood, told to obey, to now question and doubt their own father.
Alice must defeat herself in the secret realm to gain freedom; Europa’s situation is actually the same.
After a long silence, Europa finally responded—
“It’s regrettable, but perhaps what you say is true.”
“But before the truth is clarified, I will not let you out, nor will I hand over the Demon Sealing Vase.”
“You can try to escape my secret realm; good luck.”

title: Chapter 39 — Live Toward Death
content:
Chapter 39 — Live Toward Death

Volume 36 · Chapter 39

Alice studied her duplicate, realizing it could perfectly mimic every one of her movements and her razor-sharp swordplay.

Though Alice could strike it, the duplicate would retaliate in the same way, leaving only her to suffer the consequences.

No wonder those dragged into this forbidden realm chose to perish together—this might be the only way to escape alive.

If she wanted to survive, she couldn’t afford to move at all, wasting time here would be fatal.

The situation was dire, and Alice had to find the seal potion and destroy it immediately. She couldn’t just wait here to die.

Alice crossed her sword in front of her chest, deciding to try using Divine Power. If even freezing time couldn’t stop the duplicate’s movements, she’d truly be trapped here.

She believed the duplicate created by Orphalea lacked the strength to perfectly replicate her, especially extreme techniques like freezing to the absolute limit.

*"Stop!"*

Alice gathered her power, then suddenly opened her eyes wide. The pitch-black forbidden realm instantly transformed into a frozen tundra covered in ice, even the swirling mist was frozen solid.

The duplicate Alice became an ice statue, unaffected by the frozen time effect.

*"It worked!"*

Alice’s heart leapt with joy, seizing this rare opportunity without hesitation, she swung her sword at her duplicate.

But the frozen time effect hadn’t ended yet, and the duplicate suddenly broke free, radiating the same Divine Power.

Despite the surrounding mist still being frozen, in this icy world, both Alice and her duplicate could move freely.

Clearly, the two who controlled extreme cold power could cancel each other out, allowing movement even in the frozen time domain.

Alice was stunned—she hadn’t expected the duplicate to also have frozen time! This far exceeded her expectations.

It seemed Orphalea’s forbidden realm was far more troublesome. Without overwhelming strength, escaping here was nothing but a fool’s dream.

Alice gritted her teeth and swung her sword at her duplicate again.

But the duplicate’s wicked smile deepened, mimicking her, and struck back immediately.

*Clang!*

Their blades clashed violently, sparks flying everywhere.

The force of the impact shattered the layers of mist.

Alice was knocked back, barely steadying herself. She glared at the duplicate, thinking, *This thing is just another version of me—everything I know, it knows too. What do I do? Time is running out.*

---

Outside the forbidden realm, Orphalea’s single eye narrowed as it carefully watched Alice’s every move, though its focus seemed scattered.

Its mind kept replaying Alice’s words, making it increasingly doubtful.

*What she said—was it true?*

*My father was controlled by Behemoth all along, and the oath of loyalty wasn’t his will, but Behemoth’s lie.*

This possibility wasn’t impossible, but the probability was too low. Even if it were true, when exactly did my father get controlled?

Was it when I was a child? Then who raised me—my father, or Behemoth?

Orphalea’s head throbbed, its thoughts tangled in confusion. Who was its father really?

*"My father never acted strangely."*

Orphalea forced itself to calm down, carefully recalling every detail from the past, searching for evidence that its father was manipulated by Behemoth.

In Orphalea’s memory, its father, Belial, had always been unusually strict, disapproving of its love for poetry and music, calling it shameful.

But Belial never overpunished Orphalea—he had even given it a hand organ on its birthday.

Belial’s attitude was clearly unsupportive, not outright forbidding.

That hand organ was one of the few precious items holding warm memories, something Orphalea could never forget. But from when did my father start suppressing me? Every slight deviation from his expectations was met with harsh punishment.

*That’s right—it was when I saw that human girl in the Demon Lord Palace’s dungeon.*

Though she was a slave, in a way, she was my friend. From her, I learned about the vast world outside the Demon Lord Palace, and about others who shared my love for poetry and music.

But she’s dead now, killed by my father himself, and he warned me not to seek out meaningless things.

That was the most terrifying moment for me—the first time I realized how truly cruel my father was.

Orphalea’s eyes widened, cold sweat trickling down its forehead as it thought harder. Something felt terribly wrong.

If it wasn’t mistaken, its father, Belial, as the sole surviving Primordial Demon Lord, was always extremely busy. For months at a time, he wouldn’t even see it once.

Orphalea refused to believe that such a father would allow it to swear loyalty to Behemoth, dragging the entire demon race toward destruction.

*"This situation must not be what my father intended. What went wrong?"*

Orphalea gripped its own hair, teetering on the edge of madness. Self-doubt made it suffer unbearably.

When Orphalea’s gaze returned to the crystal ball, it was stunned by what it saw—Alice had made a desperate move, shocking it beyond measure.

*"Are you crazy?!"*

*"I advise you not to do this—it’s too reckless!"*

*"Didn’t I say before that if you behave, the mirror duplicate won’t harm you?"*

*"Why do such foolish things? Are you afraid of death?"*

---

In the forbidden realm, at some point, Alice invoked the divine relic *Lumen Cantus*, summoning the Holy Legion. Endless golden spectral archers, bows drawn, aimed their arrows at the Alice and her duplicate below.

The situation grew tense—it looked like Alice was about to perish with her duplicate.

Alice waved her hand, dissolving all her defenses. The Dragon Knight Armor vanished instantly, and the duplicate did the same at the same moment.

Alice raised her head, looking up at the countless spectral archers in the sky aiming at her and her duplicate. She took a deep breath—she was about to gamble her life.

*"You said ‘good luck,’ right?"*

*"Then I’ll take your blessing."*

No sooner had the words left her lips than *twang-twang-twang*, the sky filled with the sound of countless bowstrings vibrating.

A storm of golden arrows rained down, covering Alice and her duplicate.

Alice lowered her head, clenched her fists, and instinctively closed her eyes.

title: Chapter 39 — Deadly Situation (Monthly Ticket Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 39 — Deadly Situation (Monthly Ticket Extra Chapter)

Volume 36 · Chapter 39

Alice closed her eyes, listening to the swirling wind and feeling countless arrows whizzing past her ears.

Swoosh, swoosh, swoosh—dense arrows rained down, with almost no one able to evade them completely.

Alice was using this near-suicidal method to gamble with her own copy.

If she was lucky, she might survive, but if she was even slightly unlucky, she would be killed by the arrows without a doubt!

Alice firmly believed that while her copy could mimic her appearance, skills, and strength, luck—something intangible—could not be copied. Perhaps this was the key to escaping the secret realm.

Two arrows of light struck Alice's back. She gritted her teeth, enduring the pain without summoning the Dragon Warrior armor for protection, clearly determined to fight her copy to the end.

The arrows of light kept coming, soon engulfing Alice and her copy in a sea of arrows. The secret realm was filled with arrows flying haphazardly.

Outside the secret realm, the Demon Lord Eulogas was stunned. To escape the secret realm, Alice had used such a decisive method—something he had never expected.

Did she really not fear death? It was so reckless! She would be shot into a hedgehog! Such dense arrows could not be completely avoided!

After a while, the arrow shower stopped, and the holy spirits disappeared, leaving behind the devastation caused by the arrows.

Alice slowly opened her eyes, and what she saw was the unlucky copy, covered in arrows of light, having been filtered by the dense arrows!

In contrast, Alice was only struck by five arrows of light, though she was also seriously injured, it was not fatal.

The comparison of their luck was overwhelmingly in Alice's favor. It was difficult to find someone who could survive in such dense arrows and only be struck by five arrows!

Alice gritted her teeth, enduring the pain, and pulled out all the arrows of light from her body. She said calmly—

"Although your secret realm seems flawless, making it almost impossible to escape, and creating a copy of me, but every person has their own unique destiny, and luck is one of them that cannot be copied!"

The copy of Alice let out a loud cry, and several arrows of light struck fatal points, causing white mist to erupt from its body before finally disappearing in an explosion.

Outside the secret realm, Eulogas was shocked, unable to speak, as if he had been thoroughly taught a lesson by Alice.

Is this possible?

Why, when facing the same arrows, did the copy and Alice have such a big difference in results?

My secret realm has such a big flaw, and luck cannot be copied!

Eulogas was in a state of numb shock. Alice was the only one who could successfully escape the secret realm and defeat himself. In the past, enemies imprisoned in the secret realm had all met the same fate.

Undoubtedly, Eulogas had lost. Despite having the strength of a Demon Lord, he had been thoroughly defeated by a human!

Crack, crack—

The crystal ball shattered, causing a huge impact!

It sent Eulogas flying, crashing heavily onto the steps.

The destruction of the secret realm had caused significant damage to Eulogas' body, leaving him almost without the ability to resist.

Eulogas' lips bled, trying to stand up but feeling a cold sensation in his neck. When he opened his eyes, he saw Alice standing in front of him, with a sword already placed on his neck.

"I won. Hand over the Seal of the Demon Lord, or I won't be merciful." Alice warned sternly, having no patience left.

"Hmph!" Eulogas scoffed, bitterly smiling, "I never thought I would be defeated by a human. If my father were still alive, he would be ashamed."

"Stop talking nonsense. Your father may already be dead. The father you speak of may very well be a puppet controlled by Behemoth."

Alice said coldly.

"Are your words true?" Eulogas leaned against the cold steps.

"I have no reason to deceive you." Alice answered, frowning.

"Maybe you're right. I must have gone crazy to act against my own will." Eulogas sighed, then snapped his fingers.

The floor of the Demon Lord Palace began to rotate, and a stone platform slowly rose from the center, displaying the black Seal of the Demon Lord.

"That is the Seal of the Demon Lord, but destroying it is difficult. Sacred artifacts are not easily destroyed." Eulogas said calmly, unsure if Alice could destroy the Seal of the Demon Lord.

Alice didn't say anything more, letting Eulogas go and directly approaching the Seal of the Demon Lord.

She looked at the Light Song in her hand, unsure, but the urgent situation did not allow her to hesitate. If she failed, she and Vivienne might not be able to leave the Demon City alive.

Alice gripped the Light Song tightly, focusing all her strength, and struck the Seal of the Demon Lord on the stone platform with all her might!

Outside, Vivienne, transformed into a demon, was defending with the purest dark power, with a swirling purple-black vortex corrupting the flames from Behemoth.

"How long can you last, Vivienne?"

Behemoth roared, unleashing a tidal wave of flames that overwhelmed Vivienne's dark vortex.

The demonic flames poured out, shrinking Vivienne's defensive range. The purple-black dark vortex could not withstand the large amount of flames and had to retreat.

Vivienne's face darkened, feeling a slight fatigue. This way, she would definitely be severely burned by Behemoth's flames. She was anxious—

Has Alice succeeded yet?

I'm almost holding on.

Should I give up?

"Turn to ashes!" Vivienne!

Behemoth roared from the sky, unleashing a massive wave of flames that shattered Vivienne's dark vortex!

Vivienne's figure was engulfed by the flames, burning her body. Even as a God-tier warrior, she could not endure flames comparable to the temperature of the sun!

Vivienne was covered in black smoke, falling from the sky, with burns covering her entire body. Even her black wings, which were burned to mere stumps, could not fly for a short time.

"What are your last words?" Behemoth said smugly.

"Uh." Vivienne endured the burning pain, gritted her teeth, and stared at Behemoth. "Don't be too happy. No one can escape the prophecy of fate. Your ambition will fail!"

"Only the weak believe in such nonsense as fate. Look behind you, Vivienne. I've already seen your expression before you die~" Behemoth said meaningfully.

Vivienne's heart skipped a beat, looking back—

Merlin, Samiel, and Asmodeus, the three Demon Lords, had returned, forming a front and rear encirclement.

For Vivienne, this was a death sentence!

Merlin, in his demonic form, stared at Vivienne, with his sharp teeth dripping with sticky saliva, not hiding the overwhelming killing intent he radiated!

Vivienne frowned, slowly standing up, looking at her beloved son—

Merlin

title: Chapter 41 — Collision Turmoil
content:
Chapter 41 — Collision Turmoil

Volume 36 · Chapter 41

"Have you finally realized your situation, Vivian?"

"Though it's a real shame, I won't give you any chance to beg for mercy."

"I'm quite curious about how you feel right now, about to be killed by your own son's hands."

Behemoth spoke with triumphant sarcasm. The scales of victory had tilted entirely in its favor, with almost no possibility of turning the tide.

Vivian was in dire straits, completely surrounded by Demon Lords such as Behemoth and Merlin. There was absolutely no way she could escape from these enemies.

It seemed that Vivian's long-planned scheme had failed. Alice's actions had been too slow; she hadn't been able to find and destroy the Demon-Sealing Vessel before the other Demon Lords returned.

Behemoth held an absolute advantage. Vivian before it was already a dead woman walking, posing absolutely no threat.

"Why aren't you saying anything? Have you given up completely? I gave you a chance to live, but you didn't know how to cherish it."

"No matter how many chances you give me, my answer will always be the same." Vivian staggered to her feet, horrific burns covering her body and sending up black smoke. "I will never submit to you, even if you kill me."

"At a time like this, you're still being stubborn. You don't still have some false hope that this situation can be turned around, do you?" Behemoth found this somewhat incomprehensible. Under normal circumstances, a desperate enemy should be on their knees begging for mercy.

"That's right, I still harbor hope." Vivian paused, then said softly, "Because I firmly believe in the prophecy of fate!"

"Oh? How pitiful, Vivian." Behemoth narrowed its eyes and said calmly, "Then die clinging to your obsessions."

No sooner had the words left its mouth than several Demon Lords behind it began advancing toward the heavily wounded Vivian, ready to carry out Behemoth's command and kill her.

But suddenly, a earth-shattering explosion echoed from the Demon Lord Palace in the Demon Castle—

The floating land shook wildly, cracking open with thunderous roars!

A brilliant light shot into the sky, punching a hole through the dark clouds above!

The Hymn of Light and the Demon-Sealing Vessel — two artifacts with completely opposite attributes — collided, creating tremendous turbulence!

Alice hesitated not at all, going all-out from the very beginning. Even though the collision of the artifacts would cause her severe harm, she didn't back down, her conviction unshaken.

As expected, the suppressive effect of the light-aligned artifact on dark items was quite obvious. Under Alice's full-force assault, faint traces of cracks began to appear.

The turbulence generated by the artifact collision flattened the Seventh Demon Lord Palace in an instant and continued to spread outward, reducing the entire Demon Castle to nearly ruins!

The Blood Pool in the altar also collapsed in the turmoil. Countless servants of Behemoth who were about to be reborn perished before they could complete their gestation.

Vivian and several demons including Merlin were immediately scattered by the powerful turbulence. Even Behemoth in the sky was affected, its face becoming twisted—

The Demon Castle was shrouded in thick dust and smoke, plunged into chaos.

In the Holy City, after the Demon Lords had left, the defensive pressure had eased considerably, but the other demons continued their wanton attacks.

Especially the scorpion-like demons — they were all Behemoth's servants. Unless they wiped out all the humans in the Holy City, they probably wouldn't stop.

Mesfield and Blaise fought valiantly, continuously killing demons in the Holy City and rescuing distressed civilians.

Without the threat of the Demon Lords, the two seemed to have regained their former prowess. Facing the demons, they showed not a shred of fear, their sharp swords repeatedly claiming enemies' heads.

However, the number of demons was somewhat unexpected — so many that no matter how many they killed, the count never decreased. They were unaware that Behemoth's servants could be endlessly reborn in the Blood Pool, making it impossible to kill them all.

The two stood back-to-back, covering for each other. Facing the large numbers of scorpion demons closing in on them, they couldn't help but feel a trace of pressure.

But as the turbulence from the artifact collision destroyed the Blood Pool, this group of scorpion demons also instantly melted into pools of blood, disappearing without a trace.

Blaise asked in complete bafflement, "What's going on? Where did the demons go?"

Mesfield frowned and gazed toward the distant floating Demon Castle, saying suspiciously—

"It seems something happened on the Demon Castle side."

The surviving civilians, with nowhere left to flee, poured into the temple for refuge, praying they would still see tomorrow's sun.

The Temple Knights, having received orders, had all gathered at the temple, prepared to guard the "Pure Land" with their lives.

Countless knights used their bodies to block the entrance to the main hall, forming a human wall that continuously withstood wave after wave of demon charges.

Pope George's expression was grim. He had yet to recover from the fear he'd felt moments ago when Lucifer III appeared. His face was pale and his spirits were low.

If Behemoth hadn't suddenly recalled the Demon Lords, George might have encountered Satan once again, and would have been punished for his incompetence—

Has Vivian actually taken action or not?

Why is it that even though all the Demon Lords have left, the other demons still haven't stopped their attacks?

Could I have been deceived? It wasn't impossible, apparently.

From the crowd of civilians taking refuge behind him, bursts of children's crying erupted, interrupting George's thoughts and making his already irritable mood even more furious—

"Be quiet! Isn't it annoying enough to be whining and crying at a time like this?"

"If you can't control these crying and fussing brats, you're better off just choking them to death!"

"Be quiet, all of you, or I'll throw you outside to feed the demons!"

A woman holding an infant stood up and hurriedly bowed, apologizing. She was so frightened that her face had lost all color, and she had to cover the infant's mouth.

The others were also startled, not daring to even breathe heavily. It was the first time they had ever seen such an irascible pope, quite different from the one they usually saw.

In the eyes of countless people, Pope George was a kind and amiable old man. Little did they know, this was his true nature.

Pope George's face was full of fury as he looked at the group of helpless civilians. He thought to himself: Why should I protect these useless things? Protecting the weak is inherently a foolish notion.

"Your Holiness! Good news!" Blackfoot hurried over from outside, speaking in a low voice. "Most of the demons in the Holy City have already vanished. The reason is unknown, but we are temporarily safe here."

"Oh?"

Pope George raised an eyebrow, and his previously unpleasant expression improved somewhat. This was indeed good news—

It seemed that Vivian's side had made some progress, greatly reducing the pressure on his end.

George felt that things were gradually improving. He immediately put on a different face, assuming his usual amiable demeanor, and turned to address the people:

"Under my wise leadership, the knights have already eliminated the majority of demons, and the Holy City is gradually emerging from danger.

"Let us jointly give thanks for the protection of the great Goddess. The merciful Maria will not abandon any believer—

"Even a child who won't stop crying and fussing—"

"Cough, cough!"

Orobos kept coughing and climbed up from the ruins, in a very weakened state.

The collision between the artifacts had also produced a significant impact on it. Its internal organs seemed to have shifted positions, sending waves of sharp pain through its body.

Orobos looked around, wanting to understand the current situation, and was stunned to discover—

The Demon-Sealing Vessel placed on the stone platform had been poked with a small hole!

This meant that the sealed Demon Lords had gained their freedom. The true counterattack had begun.

title: Chapter 42 — Lone Wolf
content:
Chapter 42 — Lone Wolf

Volume 36 · Chapter 42

"She actually did it?"

Orbus felt somewhat incredulous. By his expectation, even if the sealing vase was handed over to Alice, it would have been difficult to destroy.

This made him begin to doubt what origin the weapon in Alice's hands actually was.

Orbus looked around but couldn't find Alice anywhere, and in confusion thought—

Where did she go?

Could she have perished in the clash of divine artifacts?

It seemed quite possible. She was so close to the collision's center and must have sustained unimaginable damage.

<. Hisss>

The excruciating pain coursing through her body forced Alice back to consciousness. Before her eyes appeared the floating Demon City, and she had already crashed to the ground, smashing a massive impact crater beneath her.

In the explosion triggered by the clash of divine artifacts moments ago, the Demon Lord Palace had been almost entirely destroyed. Alice had also been caught in the blast and sent flying out of the Demon City, plummeting from the high altitude to this very spot.

The Dragon Knight armor that had appeared on Alice's body had saved her life through the explosion and the fall.

Watching the Demon City floating in the air, she had no idea what the current situation was. But at the moment before losing consciousness, she was certain she had successfully destroyed the integrity of the sealing vase. The mission was complete.

Alice gritted her teeth and tried to stand up, wanting to return to the Demon City to provide assistance, but the bone-shattering agony running through her body forced her to gasp repeatedly. She could only lie helplessly on the ground.

Just now, Alice had been the person closest to the collision's center. That she had suffered heavy damage was only natural—

"No choice,"

"I'll just lie here and recover for a bit first."

The Merlin in his full Demon form had already deteriorated into a semi-eroded state, forcibly suppressing the restless demonic god blood surging within his body.

Merlin could feel that his body had changed drastically, faintly showing signs of slipping beyond his control, hungrier for slaughter and blood than ever before.

Although Merlin didn't understand what Béhémoth had done to his body, he could figure it out with a little thought. Béhémoth had cultivated him as a vessel, intending to claim this very body for itself.

Unfortunately, Alice had successfully destroyed the sealing vase, causing Merlin's soul to return to its place earlier than expected. This had been a variable Béhémoth hadn't anticipated.

If Merlin hadn't broken out in time, the consciousness of this body might have already become Béhémoth, while Merlin's own soul would have been sealed within the vase forever.

Merlin had already noticed that the demonic blood within him was becoming hard to control, frantically striving to seize dominance over his body. He could suppress the bloodline transformation, keeping the demonization held at a half-demon state, but that was about his limit.

Still, fortunately, Béhémoth had only modified his body for a relatively short time, and Merlin could still barely maintain control over it.

Merlin carried the severely burned Vivian to a safe corner, gently setting his mother down. Clearly, she had exhausted herself to buy Alice time, and she could no longer provide meaningful help against Béhémoth.

Vivian frowned, leaning against the wall, gazing at the tall figure of her son before her and thought many things at once.

Merlin was no longer the cold, aloof brat of childhood. His broad shoulders had grown into those of an adult demon capable of bearing heavy responsibilities and standing on his own.

Vivian had always been watching Merlin's every move from the shadows, fully aware of all the difficulties he had faced.

She felt somewhat guilty as a mother for not being by Merlin's side when he needed her most. She had a hundred things she wanted to say, yet upon seeing him face to face, she didn't know where to begin.

"You still managed to recognize me. Good, you haven't forgotten who I am."

"How could I?" Merlin let out a long breath and spoke slowly. "I never fully accepted the news of your death. I always held onto a sliver of doubt. I never expected to see you standing before me again."

"The matters of that year were complicated, and the story is long. I had no choice but to make a decision for the future of the demon race." Vivian's expression was weary as she looked at her son. "And it seems my choice was the right one."

"I thought only Alice and I were involved. Didn't know you'd gotten caught up in this too. Where is Alice?" Merlin asked worriedly.

Vivian suddenly paused, her expression complicated as she said, "You care about her that much? We've barely reconnected, mother and son, and you can't help but bring up that human woman again? Why do I suddenly have the taste of sour lemons in my mouth? It's like the pig you raised doesn't want the pig slop anymore and has started dreaming of cabbage instead."

"???" Merlin's expression turned awkward, somewhat at a loss for words.

"Oh~, I see. So this is what people mean by 'once you take a wife, you forget your mother.' Right?" Vivian felt inexplicably irritated. Lilith had already been giving her plenty of headaches, and now her own Merlin was starting to disobey too. Both her children were showing signs of defying their mother's authority. Perhaps this was the drawback of not personally raising them. "Normally, shouldn't you be asking about your mother's health first?"

Merlin: "How are you feeling?"

"That's too perfunctory now. You're just trying to brush me off, aren't you?" Vivian puffed out her cheeks, rolling her eyes in frustration. She kept getting undercut in front of her two children.

"This…" Merlin hesitated, genuinely unable to understand his mother's mood, and said helplessly, "I'm just trying to confirm Alice's condition."

"Her task was to destroy the sealing vase. Although the clash of divine artifacts was powerful, she couldn't have died from it. As for Chris, she's fine. I've already met with her." Vivian answered irritably.

"So you already know everything?" Merlin hadn't expected his mother to have had such deep contact with both Alice and Chris.

"How could I not know? I'm perfectly aware of everything." Vivian gazed at the churning dark clouds in the sky, where Béhémoth's enormous face was slowly regenerating. "Now isn't the time for this kind of conversation. We're not completely safe yet."

"Rest easy, Mom. Take care of yourself, and leave the rest to me." Merlin looked up at the sky and added, "After all, you're getting old. You should leave matters to younger people."

"Cough! You really dare to say that!" Vivian suddenly felt chest tightness and shortness of breath, and the pain from her wounds intensified. Had she really become an old woman everyone wanted to discard?

Merlin turned and looked at Samael and Asmodeus, speaking seriously, "Watch over her for me. I'm going to deal with Béhémoth."

"Are you okay going alone?" Samael felt uneasy. Whether Merlin could defeat a demon god was uncertain. After all, an ancient deity like this was far too overpowered for the current era.

"Yeah, do you want our help? If we join forces, our chances of taking it down might be greater." Asmodeus suggested.

"No, I'm enough on my own." Merlin declined the offer to fight together.

"Merlin, it's not the time to think about taking on Béhémoth single-handedly. Cooperation is the wise choice." Asmodeus frowned, feeling Merlin was being a bit reckless.

"You've misunderstood, I don't mean that." Merlin paused and emphasized—

"I'm afraid you'd slow me down. After all, once the fighting gets intense, I won't be able to protect you."

Samael:

Asmodeus:

o((O_._ 0))o.

title: Chapter 43 — The Battle That Determines the Future
content:
Chapter 43 — The Battle That Determines the Future

Volume 36 · Chapter 43

The sky roiled with layer upon layer of storm clouds, and once again, Behemoth’s face emerged, its gaze fixed on the ruins of the Demon Lord Palace—already sensing the loss of connection to the Sealing Cauldron.

*"The Sealing Cauldron was destroyed?"*

*"How is that possible? In this era, who could possibly destroy a divine artifact?"*

*"No—that must be something wrong with Europa! If it didn’t voluntarily bring out the Sealing Cauldron, how could the enemy have found it?"*

*"You’re right, that bastard Europa!"*

*"Could it dare betray me?"*

Behemoth was plunged into confusion, unable to fathom how a mindless puppet it had brainwashed could betray it. According to Behemoth’s logic, Europa would unconditionally obey Belial—it had been its own handcrafted tool.

Yet the reality defied all expectations. Europa had become too useful, earning Behemoth’s complete trust.

*"Your servant betraying you isn’t normal at all—it’s not even the first time. You’ll never get true loyalty."*

*"Ugh!"*

Behemoth’s eyes widened in shock, its breath cutting off as its face twitched uncontrollably.

Below it, Merlin was walking slowly toward the ruins, half his body consumed by corruption, though the raging demon blood had been temporarily suppressed.

Behemoth’s gaze burned with fury—Merlin’s face was the one that had kept it from ever sleeping peacefully, and the killing intent in its heart surged relentlessly.

*"After all, you’ve finally gained your freedom."*

*"I and this bastard are bound to clash again!"*

*"I refuse to endure the humiliation of being sealed for another eon!"*

Their eyes locked, the simmering battle intent between them palpable. Everything seemed to fulfill the prophecy of the great seer: Merlin and Behemoth would face a war that would decide the fate of the demon race.

The unseen hand of fate had brought Merlin directly before Behemoth, making him the fulfillment of the prophecy for the demon race’s future.

*"You shouldn’t have appeared before me. You should have vanished forever—I won’t allow you to be the nightmare I can’t forget."*

Behemoth’s massive face in the sky began to distort, unable to bear the disruption of its plans—especially after it had worked so hard to eliminate Merlin, only for him to stand before it once more.

*"Vanish! Get out of my sight, you worthless thief—don’t dare humiliate me any longer!"*

The sky crackled with lightning and thunder, and bolts of red fire darted between the clouds, unleashing a torrent of divine power that made all living things tremble and kneel in fear.

Merlin stood unmoved, watching Behemoth’s wrath unfold, curious to see just how powerful the creator of the demon race truly was.

A torrent of crimson lightning crashed from the heavens, piercing the storm clouds like a wall of fire, both magnificent and terrifying.

*"Boring."*

Merlin’s expression remained unreadable, undeterred. Without hesitation, he drew his sword and slashed downward, splitting the sea of lightning in two. The scorching waves of heat were dispersed by the merciless blade energy.

The overwhelming confidence radiating from Merlin made Behemoth feel an extreme sense of dread—it couldn’t gauge where Merlin’s true limits lay.

Behemoth’s expression flickered with unease, unsure if its attacks would even land.

*"Completely ineffective?"*

Merlin leapt from the ground, closing in on Behemoth in the sky. His eyes flashed with crimson lightning, his killing intent razor-sharp.

*"Move away! Don’t come near me!"*

Behemoth seemed utterly panicked, its voice trembling as it roared and summoned endless bolts of red lightning, striking at Merlin as he drew closer.

The lightning, infused with Behemoth’s ancient divine power, was capable of reducing a mountain range to dust in an instant. It moved with terrifying speed, resembling a serpent of red light coiled in the sky.

*"Useless. You must die. You’re the first enemy to ever ignite this kind of fury in me. Let me see—what is the true strength of an ancient god?"*

Merlin took a deep breath, channeling all his spiritual energy into an impossible speed. With a blur, he slashed through seventeen bolts of lightning in rapid succession—his sword-drawing technique had long since reached a transcendent level, faster than the lightning itself.

*"Ah!"*

Behemoth’s face twitched as it realized none of its attacks were landing. Merlin moved like an unstoppable blade, unstoppable.

Desperate, Behemoth split its mouth open and vomited a torrent of fire, forming a dense net that even flies couldn’t escape, attempting to block Merlin’s advance. It hoped to buy itself some time to prepare for a counterattack.

But Merlin’s killing intent was stronger than ever before—how could he give the enemy even a moment to breathe?

Merlin’s gaze hardened. The fire rain that rained down was swallowed whole by the flames, heading straight for Behemoth’s vital spot.

*Sizzle-sizzle-sizzle!* The fire rain ignited Merlin’s clothing, scorching his face, but he didn’t even flinch. The conviction to kill Behemoth outweighed any physical pain.

Merlin forced his way through the fire barrier, crouching midair as he drew his sword, his eyes glowing with lethal intent, fixed on Behemoth.

*"Slash!"*

The blade unsheathed with a spark.

Demon blood fueled the Banri Garan, turning the sword’s edge crimson with infernal fire, instantly granting it a flaming enhancement.

*Slash—*

The blade’s killing energy and infernal fire merged into a single, devastating force, roaring toward Behemoth in the sky.

*Crack!* The storm clouds were split apart, revealing a straight line of crimson light cutting through Behemoth’s massive face.

*"Damn it!"*

Behemoth let out a hysterical scream, exploding in a burst of flames. The shockwave rippled through the upper atmosphere, shaking not only the demon city but even the holy city, where the tremors were felt strongly.

The storm clouds parted, revealing a clear, endless blue sky.

Merlin landed on the ground, sheathed the Banri Garan, and looked up—only to freeze. Below the clear sky stood a figure.

Not quite human, but closer to a centaur from the half-demon race—human torso paired with a goat-like lower half. Its black fur bristled, and the runes on its chest glowed with eerie red light. Its horns were twisted like ancient, withered branches.

*"Who—?"* Merlin furrowed his brow, sensing an overwhelming pressure from the figure—one eerily similar to Behemoth’s, yet far stronger.

The centaur-demon let out a low, sinister chuckle, covering its face with its hand and peering through the gaps at Merlin.

*"Besides the former god-king Odin, you’re the second person to force me to reveal my true form."*

*"No wonder—you’re indeed as troublesome as I expected. You’re harder to deal with than any other opponent."*

*"It seems I’ll need to take this seriously."*

*"Disguise is a heavy burden for me. You’ve helped me shed some of it—I should thank you."*

*"But you’ll face someone who is far stronger than just Behemoth—ten times stronger!"*

*"Are you ready to accept your death?"* The demon’s voice dripped with contempt. *"You despicable, thieving bastard."*

title: Chapter 44 — Pretending
content:
Chapter 44 — Pretending

Volume 36 · Chapter 44

Merlin frowned, carefully observing the appearance of the Behemoth's true form. The centaur-like demon, which was almost nonexistent in the demon race, was indeed much more powerful, radiating a much stronger aura.

Ancient gods were born from the primordial giant Ymir and inherited some of the power of the primordial gods, possessing the unique ability to create life. Over time, they could also lead everything toward destruction.

Therefore, ancient gods with bloodlines tracing back to the primordial ancestors were far more powerful than those who had cultivated to the level of gods. In a certain sense, ancient gods were the original builders and controllers of the world's rules, holding the source of power.

Merlin's tightly furrowed brow gradually relaxed, and he was not intimidated by the Behemoth. Instead, his sense of battle grew even more intense.

"You think you can defeat me? Dream on. The era of the gods has passed, and ancient gods should not appear again. The world now has no place for you."

"It doesn't matter. You are my biggest obstacle. Once you are gone, any place will be a paradise for me." Behemoth said, clutching his face and gnashing his teeth.

"You can try." Merlin narrowed his eyes and gripped the hilt of the Banri Garan.

Behemoth's gaze became sharp, and he extended his hands, creating two long swords made of dark elements, which had no physical form but were entirely composed of dark elements.

Creating weapons directly from elemental forces is a super-high level ability, which even the elven race, with their special talent in magic, would find difficult to achieve.

Without hesitation, Behemoth's elemental weapons, created with a wave of his hand, were already close to the power of true artifacts. This gave an idea of the extent of his control over power.

Behemoth crossed the dark elemental swords in front of his chest, his eyes filled with malice, and struck out with an invisible slash!

Merlin saw nothing, but he could feel the sharp wind approaching, causing him to stare in shock.

There was nothing, yet the sharp wind struck Merlin's face, cutting deep grooves into it!

Merlin's face paled, and he quickly drew his sword to resist. When he realized the invisible attack was coming, it was already too late to defend, and the black cross slash tore through the space in front of him.

"Boom!"

The invisible cross slash struck Merlin's sword, knocking him down and sinking him deeper into the ground.

Accompanied by a thunderous roar, a horrifyingly large cross-shaped trench appeared on the ground, intersecting with each other!

Behemoth was not lying. Without his disguise, he was even more powerful than before, and his every movement radiated incomparable divine power.

No wonder, during the era of the gods, all races were enslaved by the ancient gods. From Behemoth, one could glimpse the power of the ancient gods.

If not for the appearance of the demonic prophet, the world might have remained unchanged, forever under the control of the ancient gods.

Merlin shook his dizzy head and glared at the Behemoth in the sky, his right hand, holding the sword, ached.

He had to admit that Behemoth was much stronger than any opponent he had faced before, at least causing him some pressure.

Merlin was curious about the demonic prophet. How did he destroy the ancient gods? The enemies he faced were not only numerous but also as powerful as Behemoth.

"Hmph, you're tougher than I thought. Let's see how long you can last in front of me?"

Behemoth began to wildly swing his elemental dual swords, sending out dense invisible black cross slashes that intersected to form a net of destruction, sure to tear the entire demon city into countless pieces!

The ground began to crack with numerous cross fissures, and soon, stones flew in all directions, a storm raged, and the chaotic flows seemed like sharp blades, colliding violently.

Merlin, in a ghostly manner, dodged the deadly cross slashes, wandering in the chaotic flows, but since he couldn't see Behemoth's attacks, evading them was difficult, and he could only rely on instinct.

"Like a rat running around, you want to defeat me? Be brave and face me directly!"

Behemoth taunted, swinging his dual swords faster and faster, sending out even more invisible black cross slashes.

"Yell!"

Merlin's pressure increased, and he couldn't find a chance to approach Behemoth. Everywhere was filled with hidden dangers!

In a critical moment, Merlin had no choice but to sit tight and wait, and he had to take back his initiative. Continuing like this might lead to him being suppressed by Behemoth.

Merlin sank his body and suddenly drew his sword, using the killing aura to push away all the invisible cross slashes around him.

After catching his breath, Merlin dared not relax at all and immediately took to the skies, approaching the enemy with a speed that defied gods and demons!

"Swoosh!"

A disturbance in the air, Merlin instantly appeared behind Behemoth. He was confident in his speed, and the enemy could not sense Merlin staring at Behemoth's back, his gaze filled with killing intent, and the next second, he would strike at the enemy's head!

However, just as Merlin was about to draw his sword, he discovered that Behemoth had rotated his head 180 degrees, his face twisted in a sinister smile.

"You think I wouldn't know? The"

Behemoth opened his mouth, creating dark elemental blades from his mouth, which pierced Merlin's abdomen!

"Uh?!" Merlin was a bit surprised, and the burning sensation in his abdomen made him sweat, realizing that Behemoth had been waiting for him to fall for it!

Behemoth turned his body and raised his hooves, kicking Merlin from the sky and swinging his dual swords to throw him down!

The black elemental dual swords, filled with corrosive power, shot out and pierced Merlin's body, and even in mid-air, Behemoth added two more slashes!

"Boom!"

Before Merlin hit the ground, the three elemental weapons stuck in his body exploded, sending black flames skyward, continuously corroding everything around him!

"Hahaha!" Behemoth laughed in the sky, mocking, "You're not so great. I already know you well. Even your feet can tell you what you're thinking~"

"Swoosh!"

A black object shot out from the thick black smoke, straight at Behemoth's throat!

Behemoth was startled and quickly grabbed it, almost getting hurt, and upon closer inspection, it was Merlin's Banri Garan.

"What are you doing? Giving up?"

Merlin suddenly appeared again at Behemoth's head, with large patches of his body corroded by dark elements, and his white bones could be seen.

"Uh?!"

Behemoth's eyes widened, just as he turned his head, he was kicked in the face by a foot, his features distorted and pressed together.

"What are you proud of?"

Merlin asked coldly, kicking Behemoth from the sky and that kick almost broke his neck, with the air even transmitting a shockwave!

Behemoth groaned, "Bang!" and fell to the ground, his neck stiff and unable to move.

Merlin landed and picked up the Banri Garan from the ground, swung it in his hand, and leaped into the air, stabbing towards Behemoth on the ground!

"Swoosh!" The air shook, and Behemoth disappeared, Merlin stabbed empty air—

Damn it! This guy's speed isn't slower than mine. It's obvious that he's good at close-quarters combat, and all those attacks were just feints!

Behemoth had suddenly appeared behind Merlin, holding the dark elemental dual swords, and slashed towards his nape!

"Die!"

title: Chapter 45 — Newly Appointed Demon Deity
content:
Chapter 45 — Newly Appointed Demon Deity

Volume 36 · Chapter 45

Behemoth held twin dark-element blades, his eyes brimming with surging murderous intent, swinging at Merlin's nape!

Merlin's gaze hardened, his figure vanishing instantly in place; Behemoth only hacked through afterimages.

"Hmm? Fast enough to deceive my eyes?"

A cold sweat bead slid down Behemoth's head; he whirled around, discovering Merlin had already struck from behind, swinging the blade toward the enemy's neck without hesitation!

In panic, Behemoth quickly crossed his twin blades before his chest, desperately backing away.

The blade of Banri Garan shattered the dark-element twin blades; the explosive shock tore up the ground, sending thick smoke billowing!

The sounds of explosions and clashes echoed through the smoke; flames swelled, constantly devouring surrounding things—ordinary people had no courage to approach.

The intensity of their slaughter had reached white heat; their speed duel was no longer something the naked eye could track—within mere breaths, they'd exchanged over a hundred blows!

Obviously, this fierce battle might never end unless someone fell.

Behemoth charged out of the thick smoke first, his left arm already severed by Merlin, demonic blood flowing like a spring.

Against Merlin, Behemoth was at a disadvantage—not only failing to suppress him, but stumbling instead!

Behemoth's face turned pale; his wounds were severe, and losing his left arm affected him greatly.

Hum—

The air trembled; Merlin's blade-wielding figure appeared to Behemoth's right, imposing and murderous, his eyes revealing cold killing intent!

"Tch!" Behemoth gritted his teeth, having no choice but to fight back, resisting with his remaining right hand.

Puchi—

Yet Merlin's speed was beyond mortal comprehension—blink, and he teleported to Behemoth's left side, the sharp blade already descending, slashing from shoulder to abdomen!

Though Behemoth was no weak close-combatant, his speed and strength formidable, he still lagged behind Merlin.

With Behemoth's perceptual abilities, he couldn't even accurately judge Merlin's position, frequently deceived by the afterimages of Merlin's high-speed movements.

Phew! Behemoth's blood surged like a fountain, splashing over Merlin, nearly suffering a waist-severing blow—only the force fell a bit short.

"Hmm?" Merlin froze in surprise, probably not expecting Behemoth's flesh to be so tough, taking a blow head-on.

"You despicable dog! I'll make you pay!"

Behemoth gnashed his teeth in curse, weakened after suffering heavy injuries.

Yet it grabbed Merlin fiercely, as if afraid he'd escape.

The demonic blood on the ground and inside Behemoth surged, seeming to gain life of its own, quickly wrapping around Merlin.

Masses of viscous, soft demonic blood, like a puddle of mud, sealed and wrapped Merlin's entire body.

"What's this?!" Merlin was stunned, discovering the demonic blood spread fast, his body unable to move, and even Banri Garan couldn't be withdrawn from Behemoth's corpse.

The demonic blood soon submerged Merlin's eyes, forming a pitch-black coffin like one entombing a mummy, imprisoning him completely inside.

Behemoth quickly retreated, waving his hand to summon twelve dark-element spears hovering in the sky, infusing all his power, aiming for a fatal strike on Merlin—even if he couldn't kill him, he'd deal heavy damage.

"Feel the pain of your body being torn apart!"

Twelve elemental spears burst with brilliant light, shooting out simultaneously, turning heaven and earth pale!

The power of an ancient god could utterly erase any creature, especially Behemoth's dark corrosion, far stronger than Vivian's!

Where the spears passed, space tore apart, dimensional rifts flickered in and out, the mortal world struggling to bear this apocalyptic dark power!

Duh duh duh—twelve dark spears, almost at the same moment piercing through the pitch-black coffin imprisoning Merlin!

Rumble—

Then the explosion of the spears came, deafening, audible even from the distant Holy City.

The shockwave spread, countless buildings like tofu dregs, collapsing instantly—the Demon City leveled to the ground!

"It's all your own doing, hehe..."

A heat wave comparable to the sun's temperature surged forth, dispersing the corrosive smoke surrounding them.

Behemoth's smile froze on his face, his eye corners twitching, shocked in his heart—how was he still alive?!

To survive, Merlin had no choice but to passively enter full demonization, revealing his monstrous form again, yielding partial control of his body, letting bloodlust devour his consciousness.

Twelve holes pierced his body, blood gushing forth, clearly suffering heavy injuries.

In demon form, Merlin picked up the scorching-hot Banri Garan in hand, using high heat and flames to cauterize the holes in his body, stopping the blood quickly—the whole process without blinking, without even a whimper.

Behemoth watched with heart in mouth, taking flight toward the sky to create distance from Merlin—he knew well that blood-corroded Merlin was a madman, every move brimming with destructive power.

This was the new body Behemoth prepared for himself, naturally crafted with all his might—only it failed.

Behemoth looked back, discovering Merlin had vanished—his heart trembled uncontrollably—

Puchi!

The monstrous demon Merlin was more vicious than usual, his power in every aspect surging several-fold—literally a machine tailor-made for slaughter.

Unknowingly, the demon Merlin, beating his black wings, had already caught up; in the instant Behemoth turned his head, Banri Garan pierced through his heart!

"Ugh! You!" Behemoth howled in agony, experiencing pain unimaginable to ordinary people, feeling his heart as if frying in a pan!

The monstrous demon Merlin parted his mouth full of sharp fangs, stretched out his thin tongue, licked Behemoth's nose tip, his vicious eyes revealing mocking intent.

"Don't get too cocky!" Behemoth opened his mouth, brewing a dark-element spike, planning to repeat his old trick, trying to shake off Merlin's entanglement!

But Merlin had learned his lesson, stretching his neck, using his fang-lined mouth to bite hard on Behemoth's throat!

Simultaneously flapping his black wings with all his might, dragging Behemoth toward the sky!

Banri Garan ignited with fire, exploding above the clouds, demon-fire radiating sun-like temperatures, raging madly, expanding flames like demons baring fangs, burning the Vatican sky crimson!

Behemoth turned to ash in the flames, probably never expecting even in death to die by the hand of the killing machine he created—the very thing that pushed Merlin to an unfathomable realm!

Demon-form Merlin floated in the sky, like a new demon lord born from flames, personally burying the "old predecessor" and taking his place—

In his palm lay a faintly glowing soul.

It was the soul of the ancient god Behemoth, and the final material needed to forge Mistilteinn.

title: Chapter 46 — **The One Who Never Returned**
content:
Chapter 46 — **The One Who Never Returned**

Volume 36 · Chapter 46

The dark clouds hovering over the Demon Lord Palace dissipated, and the oppressive aura of the ancient god Behemoth vanished.

The demons in the Holy City immediately abandoned their attack and fled towards the Demon Lord Palace.

Even the demons hiding in the Holy City, including Lilith, left the city to reunite with Vivienne and confront the human kingdom.

Lilith did not forget to bring Chris along, intending to take the little one back to the demon race.

The demons unfurled their membrane wings and flew through the sky with Chris, steadily approaching the Demon Lord Palace, which had already become a wasteland.

"Grandma? Where are we going? Are we going to find Mommy?" Little Chris asked curiously.

"Don't ask too many questions; you'll find out later," Lilith whispered, hesitating to reveal the truth to Chris, fearing she might cry on the way.

Chris lowered her head and stopped asking, assuming Lilith was either taking her to find her father or her mother, so she became much more obedient.

Miu approached quietly and whispered, "Princess, this isn't right. Taking Chris away without permission is unfair to Alice."

"Hmph! How ridiculous," Lilith rolled her eyes and answered in a very small voice, trying not to let Chris hear, "What does it matter? Chris belongs to us anyway. If she doesn't live among the demons, why not leave her in the human kingdom? Besides, Alice is a lowly human; what right does she have to talk about fairness?"

"Miu, you have no right to interfere in this matter; it's up to Lilith's decision."

Abaddon, who had some seniority and was a close confidant of Vivienne, stepped forward to offer some advice, but even if Lilith was the princess, she should be given some consideration.

"Lilith Princess, we cannot take this child back. Vivienne has already made it clear that this child is better suited to live as a human. The demon race does not have a place for her, and she will face endless discrimination due to her mother's bloodline. Think about your brother; would you want this child to experience the same fate?"

"There's nothing to worry about; I'll protect her from any discrimination," Lilith refused to let go, determined to take Chris with her, "As for my mother, I'll take care of that. Besides, this child is a member of the Lucifiel family; she cannot be left to fend for herself."

"Your actions are too hasty," Abaddon frowned, believing Lilith was not considering the practical situation and was acting on emotion.

"Abaddon, I agree with Lilith," Ophelia immediately stood by Lilith's side, wanting to take Chris away and let that human woman suffer, which she found exciting, "Father, you're getting old; you should consider our opinions more."

Abaddon was speechless, already imagining the scene of Lilith being severely scolded by Vivienne.

Helena remained silent throughout, as it was an internal matter of the First Demon Lord Palace, and she was not comfortable interfering.

However, thinking about young Chris, who might never see her mother Alice again, she felt some sympathy.

After careful consideration, Helena believed that Chris would be happier living in the human kingdom, at least without constant discrimination.

"We need to hurry up! The Demon Lord Palace seems to be moving again!"

The dormant Demon Lord Palace rumbled and began to move, steadily moving away from the Holy City.

After Behemoth was defeated, Vivienne took control of the Demon Lord Palace, using it as a mobile fortress to return to the desert and restore the demon race to stability.

The situation was going smoothly, but suddenly, an unexpected situation arose.

In front of Lilith and the other demons, the temperature suddenly dropped, and countless pale gold ice swords appeared out of nowhere, surrounding them and blocking their path back to the Demon Lord Palace.

Alice's "Miu" immediately frowned, sensing something was wrong.

Lilith looked down and saw Alice standing below, pointing a thin sword at them, having noticed their intention to take Chris away.

Alice's injuries had not fully healed, but she could still move, noticing Lilith and the other demons flying towards the Demon Lord Palace with Chris.

"You what do you mean?" Lilith shouted, furious.

"What do you mean? What are you trying to do with my daughter?" Alice glared at them, having never heard of the demons wanting to take Chris back to the demon race, and she would never allow it.

"Mommy!" Little Chris saw her mother and grabbed her hand, wanting to return to Alice's side.

Lilith hugged Chris tightly, saying without any hesitation, "This child does not belong to humans or you; she belongs to the demon race. Taking her back is only right!"

"Nonsense! She is my daughter; she is not a member of the demon race! Give Chris back, or I won't hesitate to fight!"

Alice unleashed the power of the pseudo-dragon, continuously intimidating the demons. If they dared to take Chris away, they would be in for a fierce battle.

All the demons were surprised, instinctively adopting a defensive stance, bracing themselves against the sharp ice swords, ready to face Alice, who had reached the pseudo-dragon level.

What had once been allies, working together to defeat the ancient demon god, had now turned into enemies, with irreconcilable conflicts.

"Grandma?" Little Chris looked at Lilith, confused about why she wouldn't let go.

Lilith's face darkened, furious at Alice, her whole body trembling with anger, and she couldn't bear to see young Chris.

"Let's fight! There's nothing to be afraid of!" Ophelia clenched her fists.

"Be reasonable, none of us can match her. If she is determined to fight, we all won't get away," Abaddon sighed, speaking seriously, "Lilith Princess, please consider this carefully. This child's future does not belong to the demon race. When the time comes to let go, do it decisively, and don't regret it when it's too late."

"Princess, follow Vivienne's wishes," Miu agreed.

"The Demon Lord Palace is almost gone; we don't have much time left," Helena looked at the Demon Lord Palace that was gradually disappearing, still hoping to return the child to Alice.

"Hmph!" Lilith was forced to make a choice, gently placing Chris on the ground and saying, "We'll see!"

The demons followed Lilith, flying quickly towards the Demon Lord Palace and leaving Vatican City.

"Mommy~" Little Chris couldn't help but throw herself into her mother's arms, pressing her face against her.

Alice helped tidy up the little one's messy hair, feeling a great sense of relief, and she was already thinking about what she would do without Chris.

She looked up at the Demon Lord Palace that was gradually fading away.

Her heart was filled with expectations, but gradually turned to disappointment and sadness.

She had never seen Merlin return.

Regarding Merlin's battle with Behemoth, I originally wanted to write it as a one-hit kill, as it was simple and didn't require much brainpower. However, I was afraid you would think I was deceiving you.

But if you don't like it, we can just do a one-hit kill, which would also be a relief for me, and it's fine.

Because I don't read books for the battles; the excitement comes from the good buildup, and I don't find the punches and kicks meaningful, so I don't want to write them, as they would slow down my progress towards completion.

This chapter is finished, and it's the second-to-last stage, with completion soon.

Finishing here is also acceptable, but it would be better to have a stage completion with some lingering thoughts and suspense, although it might leave a slight sadness, which I don't want to do.

title: Chapter 47 — Safety: Safe Categories: None
content:
Chapter 47 — Safety: Safe Categories: None

Volume 36 · Chapter 47

"What?" Asmodeus looked incredulous, frowning. "You want to leave the Demon City now to go find that human woman?"

"That's right. I have to see her, and besides, my daughter hasn't seen me in a long time." After dealing with Behemoth and pulling the demon race back from the brink of disaster, Merlin felt the urge to leave.

"Don't be silly. You're a demon—why are you so obsessed with a human female?" Asmodeus couldn't understand, his tone shifting. "You proposed to me, didn't you? Fine, I accept. Let's get married. Right now."

"Asmodeus, I'm not in the mood to joke." Black lines slid down Merlin's forehead.

"Merlin, don't be stubborn. You can't leave. The turmoil has just passed, and the demon race is in shambles. We need you here more." Samael said in a low voice, disagreeing with Merlin leaving the demon race, at least not now.

"That's right. Leviathan and Beelzebub have both left. We should unite to resist risks. The situation is unstable now; the interests of our race matter more than personal affection." Asmodeus nodded in agreement.

"But..." Merlin hesitated, feeling she had to see Alice and her daughter once. Leaving directly felt terrible.

"Drop that thought, Merlin. I can allow you to hang around in the human realm, but you can't leave now. It's for the best of everyone."

Vivian, who had been silent all along, suddenly spoke, also disapproving of Merlin leaving, her repulsive emotions already written on her face.

"Why?" Merlin asked in surprise, vaguely feeling that her domineering mother was back, always making decisions on her own.

"Look at yourself. Do you really think you can go back? With this appearance, the human realm has no place for you." Vivian said in a stern tone.

"Uh..." Merlin's whole body trembled. Her body was still in a demonified state, the demonic blood in her body harder to suppress than before, even returning to her original form was difficult.

Going back like this would scare Chris to tears in a minute, and would be seen as a threat by humans. Returning to a peaceful life was impossible.

Merlin looked at her demonic arm with claws, falling into deep self-doubt, feeling very alienated from her own body.

"Your body is being eroded by Behemoth's blood, and your consciousness will slowly disappear, turning you into a madman who kills indiscriminately." Vivian paused, her tone softening. "So don't leave the demon race until you learn to control the demonic blood in your body. This is not just for you, but also for Alice and her daughter."

Merlin instinctively clenched her hands, took a deep breath, and had to accept this reality. With her current appearance, she really couldn't go anywhere except the demon race—

"Alice..." Several days after the war besieging the Holy City subsided, the believers barely emerged from the shadow of the demons, sincerely thanking the Goddess of Light's protection for helping humanity survive the disaster.

On the surface the Church won, but the huge losses were only clear to Pope Ji Ougen. It couldn't be called a victory at all.

Alice didn't wait for Merlin to return, feeling disappointed. She decided to return to Rekisiman and continue being an adventurer, so early in the morning she submitted her resignation.

"This is the Hero's Legacy Armor. Return it to you. The Holy City is no longer in danger, and I should go back."

"What do you mean?" Pope Ji Ougen looked at the Hero's Legacy Armor, not wanting Alice to leave from the bottom of his heart.

Now the Church had no trump cards left, lacking the support of the strong.

A powerful swordswoman like Alice at the Pseudo-God realm was naturally someone who had to be courted.

"You're leaving? Where to?"

"Rekisiman, that's my home. The rent seems to be due again. I haven't been there for these days. Thinking about it, I've lost so much." Alice said reminiscing.

"What nonsense are you talking about, my child? The Church is your home forever. You don't need to leave. Going back to a countryside like Rekisiman, isn't life in the temple better?" Pope Ji Ougen persuaded gently.

"Sorry, I can't fit in here. The Church isn't my destination. Maybe Rekisiman is a small village in your eyes, but not in mine." Alice shook her head, declining the Pope's kindness.

"Alice, calm down. Don't be like this. You can't leave casually. It's too irresponsible. The demons haven't been completely eliminated. We need you." Pope Ji Ougen looked pleading, pitifully saying, "You are the Hero, a righteous warrior who fights evil to the end. Everyone has high hopes for you."

"I have no attachment to being the Hero anymore. Whoever wants to inherit this cause can let someone else do it. My departure is already decided." Alice bowed slightly, speaking softly, "Goodbye."

"You'll regret it, Alice. You'll come back sooner or later. Only the Church is your true home." Pope Ji Ougen said angrily, his mood at its worst.

"I will never come back."

At the Church cemetery, before leaving, Alice came here alone deliberately.

All fallen Temple Knights were buried here. After the Holy City defense battle, the cemetery had grown larger.

Alice stood before Joan of Arc's tombstone, placing a bunch of white wildflowers on the steps.

Learning of Joan of Arc's death, Alice was quite surprised. She thought if she hadn't encountered a Demon Lord-class opponent, she wouldn't have died. The result was unexpected.

Alice's mood was complex. She stared at Joan of Arc's tombstone in silence for a long time.

Although Alice considered Joan of Arc a friend, Joan of Arc didn't see it that way, feeling Alice had stolen her life.

If Alice weren't here, Joan of Arc could have fulfilled her dream and become a Hero admired by all. Sadly, she had no chance. She died burned alive by demonic flames.

"So you're here too? Alice." Blackford walked over, seemingly also here to mourn the fallen knights.

"Knight Commander?" Alice turned back in surprise.

"Heard you gave up being the Hero and are leaving soon?" Blackford asked curiously.

"Yes, leaving early tomorrow." Alice had already set her itinerary.

"Your leaving is a huge loss to the Church. The Pope was shouting in his bedroom, couldn't eat. Haha." Blackford laughed.

"I feel out of place in the Church. Leaving is understandable, especially since the war is over." Alice said softly.

"Maybe you're right. Leaving is better." Blackford looked at Joan of Arc's tombstone, saying meaningfully—

"A church full of corruption doesn't deserve your noble spirit:"

title: Chapter 48 — Fairy Bell
content:
Chapter 48 — Fairy Bell

Volume 36 · Chapter 48

Blackford was glad that Alice was able to leave, otherwise she might have encountered a fate similar to Joan of Arc's. Although he didn't know exactly what had happened, he could still guess that in the end, Joan had transformed into a saintly form, with no distinction between friend and foe, and that the Pope, Gergius, was somehow involved. As the Pope's personal guard, Blackford knew many secrets that the Church didn't want to reveal, but there were also many things he didn't understand, such as how to turn people into saints. Blackford felt a deep sense of sympathy for Joan's fate, and he knew that countless devout believers like her were being exploited by the Church. So, Alice's decision to take a stand against the Church was a good thing. If Joan had been as brave as Alice, she would never have ended up like that. Alice looked at Blackford and thought that his words didn't sound like something a Grand Master of the Order of the Temple would say, "What did you mean?" "Nothing," Blackford said, trying to change the subject. He wanted to tell her about Joan's fate, but he quickly reconsidered, knowing that revealing secrets could have serious consequences. "I was just wishing you good luck," he said. "The Church isn't suitable for someone like you, a lone and adventurous woman. Wouldn't it be better for you to be a free spirit?" "I didn't expect you to encourage me," Alice said, surprised. "I thought you were just like the Pope." "How could that be?" Blackford scratched his head, speaking in a low tone. "The Pope is a rather dark person, and I've never been able to understand him." "I think he's a dark old man too," Alice said, shaking her head. "I didn't notice it before, but it's become more and more obvious lately." "Good luck on your journey," Blackford said. "Just don't get involved with the Church anymore. After all, beneath its glamorous exterior, it's full of filth." Alice looked at Blackford again, feeling that he was trying to tell her something, but his eyes were fixed on Joan's tombstone, and he remained silent. Hobbes' house was located in a remote area of Rexton, far from the hustle and bustle of the city. The lighting inside was dim, and the facilities were simple and rough, giving the impression that it was not a home for a family of three, but rather a messy bachelor's pad. In fact, it was just that. The room was cluttered, with only children's and men's belongings visible, with no signs of any adult women. Although Hobbes claimed to have a wife, his temper was not good, but in reality, he was a single father, raising his daughter, Minnie, on his own. Hobbes sat beside Minnie, waiting for her to fall asleep, but the little girl was still chattering away, sharing stories of her day. "Today, the nose bug went to steal someone's apple, but it got caught, and it was so stupid. And the four-eyed kid, he didn't even help, he just ran away faster than anyone else when things got tough." "Why did you go steal something? I gave you money, didn't I?" Hobbes asked, surprised. "Buying things is boring, but stealing is exciting. It's the first step in our Guwa Warriors' rebellion against the adults." Minnie said seriously. "Too bad Chris wasn't here, she might have been able to help. She's better than the nose bug and the four-eyed kid any day." "She'll be back soon," Hobbes said, stroking Minnie's head. "I haven't seen Chris in a long time, and I don't know where she's gone. I miss her a bit." Minnie's eyes sparkled as she imagined Chris returning. "Maybe tomorrow we'll see her again." Hobbes used his hand, which reeked of alcohol, to gently brush away Minnie's eyelids, and she quickly fell asleep. Hobbes helped Minnie tidy up her bed, then got up and went to the desk, lit an oil lamp, and began to sort through the envelopes on the desk. Hobbes was not only the most useless black iron adventurer in Rexton, but also a well-known information broker in the underworld. If he weren't an information broker, he wouldn't be known as "Old Hob." In this mysterious world, information brokers were divided into different levels, and their abilities varied greatly. Although they claimed to know many secrets, as long as the price was right, they could even reveal the color of the queen's underwear, but the accuracy was not guaranteed.
