However, the information provided by Old Hob was extremely accurate, and the price was also very high, making him a highly sought-after figure in the underworld. It was said that not only did the nobility and royal family pay a high price to learn about things, but even the Dark Council was one of his clients. Black and white, he was a master of both, and his information was always accurate and timely, making him a rare talent in the world of information brokers. Today, Old Hob was also working on his daily tasks and received a very interesting secret letter. Hobbes opened the envelope, read the letter, and burst out laughing, unable to help but drink a few more glasses of liquor. "Who is the legendary great sword master, Elgin?" "Ha, with your abilities, you'll never find out who it is." "Even if you knew, what would you do?" Hobbes looked at the letter, fell silent for a moment, and his eyes became deep and profound, like a wise chess player thinking about his next move. "The world is getting more and more chaotic, and it's a good thing. Why not take advantage of the situation and eliminate a few obstacles?" Hobbes picked up his feather pen and decided to take on this task, answering the customer's question truthfully. He slowly wrote, "Elgin's legendary great sword master, Merlin: Lucifer, the three-generation Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace." Hobbes looked at his handwriting and smiled, feeling satisfied, and stroked his chin, muttering to himself. "I know the answer, and it's someone I'll never be able to defeat." "So, how do you plan to avenge your father?" "The determined pirate's son, I'm looking forward to seeing your next move." The Devil's Castle successfully returned to the desert, using the natural barrier to begin rebuilding their home. All the demons were summoned to the Devil's Castle, although the internal situation was still unclear, they had begun to revive this ancient city. Due to the short time, Merlin still couldn't control the demon blood, but he could barely maintain his consciousness, preventing himself from becoming a killing machine. Merlin sat alone on the ruined city wall, staring out at the endless desert, wondering what had happened to Alice and the others. He suddenly remembered something, a golden bell that the fairy, Phry, had given him before leaving. It was said that after collecting the materials to forge Mistral, he could use it to ask for Phry's help to deliver the materials to Master Balin. Merlin rummaged through his clothes, found the small, unobtrusive golden bell, and thought that maybe it could help him. He didn't know if Phry was still around, or if Balin was still being harassed by the dwarf king.

title: Chapter 49 — Revelation
content:
Chapter 49 — Revelation

Volume 36 · Chapter 49

As the tinkling bells rang, a faint halo spread outward, and the tiny figure of the fairy Firi slowly emerged, a beige crossbody bag still slung over her shoulder.

Firi rubbed her sleepy eyes, stretched languidly, and looked around in surprise, curious about the unfamiliar surroundings.

"Where is this? It's so barren, what a shitty place."
Firi had always lived in the fertile Southern United Kingdom; she had never seen a place as barren as the Sand Sea.

Merlin looked at Fairy Firi, a faint smile on his face, thinking that this foul-mouthed fairy hadn't changed at all. "This is the Sand Sea, territory of the demon race."

Hearing the familiar voice, Firi turned back in surprise, but seeing Merlin's demonic form made her suck in a breath, thinking she had been teleported to the mouth of some monster. "Who the hell are you?!"

"Did you forget me that quickly? Think harder." Merlin felt a bit helpless, thinking his current appearance had changed too much—if he couldn't freely control his demonic form, it was normal not to recognize him.

"Only after confirming there was no danger did Firi dare to approach cautiously. After examining him closely, she widened her eyes in shock. 'Merlin! How did you turn into this?'"

"Long story short, I'm originally a demon. Turning into this isn't a big deal." Merlin didn't want to explain too much.

"Oh~" Firi crossed her arms, staring at Merlin with interest. "But you look so scary. I thought I'd been summoned to a monster's lair. I was about to be eaten at any moment."

"With a mouth that foul, you probably don't taste good either. Don't worry, no one would want to make a snack out of you." Merlin commented casually.

"So that means I don't even qualify to be a snack? A bit upset." Firi frowned, unsure whether to be happy or not.

"How is Master Balin doing? After I left, the Dwarf King didn't give you trouble, did he?" Merlin asked curiously.

"Master Balin is fine, the forge is doing great business. As for the Dwarf King? Seems he hasn't caused trouble either. If you haven't caused trouble for him, consider it a blessing." Firi paused, then added, "Bari is also following his father to learn forging skills properly. He's stopped dreaming about becoming a warrior."

"I see." Merlin nodded, thinking he hadn't caused any trouble for the dwarf father and son. The forge had been peaceful all along.

"Did you summon me for something? Not just to chat, I'm busy." Firi said in an impatient tone.

"I need you to help carry back the materials for forging Mistilteinn." Merlin answered simply.

Fairy Firi's eyes lit up, excitedly saying, "You've found the remaining two materials? That's amazing! Master Balin often sighs, saying finding the remaining materials is almost impossible! Because times have changed, it's not the age of the ancient gods anymore; many materials have completely disappeared."

"Although the forging materials were hard to find, I managed to gather them. I can have Master Balin help and start forging." Merlin took out the soul of Behemoth and handed it to Firi. "This is the soul of an ancient god, one of the forging materials. Give it to Master Balin."

"This is the soul of an ancient god? It feels like a damp fog." Firi played with it in her hand for a moment, quickly losing interest, and put the ancient god's soul into her dimensional bag. Then she held up her fingers to count. "Gold essence, ancient god's soul... only two materials. Still missing one."

"The other material, the Sealing Stone, is with my companion. You need to go get it from her. She should have returned to the Britannia Kingdom by now."

Merlin had placed the Sealing Stone in Angel's ring and didn't carry it with him. After all, the Sealing Stone was half of Odin's throne, very heavy.

"Your companion?" Firi couldn't quite remember.

"Her name is Alice. You should remember her, right? We went to the United Kingdom together." Merlin reminded her.

"Oh~ That silver-haired washboard? At first you were just a little kid, I thought she was your mom." Firi grinned with embarrassment, showing her teeth.

Merlin had no response, unwilling to recall those days of little Merlin.

"Then I'll head to Britannia now. We fairies are small, but we're fast." Firi gripped her crossbody bag, full of confidence. "Fairy courier, mission accomplished!"

"Wait—"
Fairy Firi stopped mid-air, embarrassed. "What else? Can't you say it all at once?"

"I have a few words I want you to pass along."

In the Britannia Palace, Elizabeth was busy with work. The conflict between demons and humans had recently ended completely, but the shadow of fear brought by the demon race had not yet dissipated.

Sightings of wandering demons occurred frequently throughout the kingdom. Although most were misunderstandings, they still caused panic, with people believing the demons hadn't left.

Although the Church suffered defeat in the 234th Crusade and suppressed religious fanaticism within the kingdom, the demons' consecutive wars caused the number of believers to grow daily.

The Church couldn't protect the safety of believers, yet believers were willing to believe that as long as they had faith in the Church of Light, they could luckily escape demonic harm—a kind of spiritual comfort.

Elizabeth realized that suppressing the Church's power was not something that could be accomplished overnight. She must strengthen the kingdom's defensive forces and regain the people's trust.

This time, Mesfield's support of the Church had achieved victory. Elizabeth planned to publicize the heroic deeds of the Purple Gold Flower Knights, constantly diminishing the Church's influence.

"Your Majesty!"

Mesfield had just returned to the capital and couldn't wait to come to the palace to see the queen. He didn't even knock when entering, his face very agitated.

Elizabeth was startled, looked up to see Mesfield, and asked in surprise, "Windsor, when did you get back?"

"I just got back. No, now isn't the time for that." Mesfield shook his head anxiously. "Your Majesty! I have something urgent and important to report!"

"Hmm? What is it? Don't rush, take your time." Elizabeth rarely saw Mesfield so anxious and out of character.

"Your Majesty, what I'm about to say, I can guarantee with my honor, and it's of great importance. Please prepare yourself mentally!"

Mesfield's expression was extremely serious.

"Okay." Elizabeth instinctively sat up straight, becoming somewhat tense.

"This time when I went to support the Church, in the fight against demons, I discovered a major secret!" Mesfield paused, taking a deep breath—

"Elgin, the legendary great swordsman—"

"His true identity is actually a demon!"
("°o"n)

title: Chapter 50 — Arrest
content:
Chapter 50 — Arrest

Volume 36 · Chapter 50

When Mesfield finished speaking, the atmosphere in the room suddenly fell into a complete silence, almost to the point where a needle could be heard falling.

Elizabeth Queen put down her quill and leaned back in her chair, giving an awkward smile, "Windsor, are you joking, right? How could this possibly be?"

"No! Your Majesty, I'm not joking, I'm serious!" Mesfield stepped forward, placing both hands on the queen's desk, speaking in a very serious tone, "Elkin the Swordmaster is indeed a demon, and it's very likely not an ordinary demon, but one of the seven princes of the demon race!"

Elizabeth Queen was somewhat difficult to believe this fact. The Demon Lord had lived on his own territory for so long, and now it was only discovered, which was both astonishing and terrifying.

"Your Majesty, please believe me, I'm very clear-headed, all of this is true. We have always considered demons to be heroes, how ridiculous is that?" Mesfield hesitated, then speculated, "Perhaps Elkin the Swordmaster is a spy from the demon race infiltrating the kingdom, collecting information here, preparing for the demon's invasion of the kingdom. The disaster we suffered this time may also be related to him!"

Elizabeth Queen fell silent, looking at Mesfield's expression, it didn't seem like he was casually slandering Elkin the Swordmaster, but that he knew something?

"Why are you so sure? Do you have evidence?"

Mesfield was speechless at this point. Her evidence was truly embarrassing to admit, as she felt a similar seductive effect from Elkin's saliva, and such a shameful basis didn't match her usual image at all.

Elizabeth Queen saw her knight hesitate and ask in surprise, "What's the matter? If there's no evidence, just say Elkin the Swordmaster is a demon, that's not acceptable."

"No, I do have evidence, just..." Mesfield's face turned red, and she didn't feel very comfortable.

"What is it?" Elizabeth Queen asked in confusion.

Mesfield bit her lip and decided to abandon all her dignity, revealing everything, as it was only being told to the queen, not made public.

Thus, Mesfield approached Elizabeth and whispered in her ear, telling her everything she had experienced.

Elizabeth's facial expression changed continuously, feeling as if she had heard many unknown secrets, her two willow brows were tightly knitted together, "Do you mean all of these are true?"

"It's absolutely true, Your Majesty, I won't lie to you." Mesfield nodded firmly.

"Elkin the Swordmaster's saliva has such an effect?" Elizabeth had never heard of such a thing.

"Yes, initially, I thought he might have some lewd medication in his mouth, but it seems I was wrong." Mesfield replied.

"Did you encounter Lucifer III in the Holy City, and did you feel the same? Could it be a mistake?" Elizabeth also felt a bit embarrassed, speaking in a very gentle tone.

"It's not a mistake, the feeling is the same, and their temperament and habits are completely consistent." Mesfield hesitated and answered, blushing.

Originally, I had never heard of male succubi, perhaps your guess was correct." Elizabeth Queen thought deeply, feeling that Mesfield's suspicion was not without reason.

"It's not a guess, I'm certain Elkin the Swordmaster is a demon, and a terrifying Demon Lord." Mesfield emphasized with a resolute tone, as soon as she was salivated in the Holy City, she could be certain.

"How long have we lived with the Demon Lord on the same land?" Elizabeth Queen's face turned pale, speaking with a sense of dread, "It's too terrifying, no one would believe such a bizarre thing."

"I believe that the kingdom's previous encounters with demon invasions are related to Elkin the Swordmaster, we must be vigilant towards him and no longer consider him a hero. Only then will the kingdom be safe." Mesfield spoke firmly, wanting to get rid of Elkin the Swordmaster for a long time.

"What you say also makes sense, but..." Elizabeth Queen hesitated, she had contact with Merlin, who was not as ruthless as the Demon Lord, if it weren't for Mesfield's revelation, she would have always considered Merlin to be just an overly powerful human.

"Your Majesty, this matter cannot be delayed, the threat to the kingdom's security must be eliminated, otherwise the consequences are unimaginable." Mesfield spoke emotionally.

"Elkin the Swordmaster and the kingdom's encounters with demon invasions, there may or may not be a connection, now it's all speculation." Elizabeth Queen hesitated, then continued, "If Elkin the Swordmaster is the third ruler of the First Demon Lord Palace, why didn't he join forces with the demons to attack us when we retreated to Wales? Perhaps the only answer is that the demon race is not united, and the positions and ideologies of each Demon Lord Palace are different."

"Your Majesty! Please don't have any illusions about Elkin the Swordmaster, he is a demon and cannot be trusted!" Mesfield spoke stubbornly.

"I have had contact with Elkin the Swordmaster and have some understanding, my views are different from yours, I believe he is not on the same side as demons like Mammon." Elizabeth Queen carefully recalled, remembering that Merlin only asked not to disturb him, which was different from the ambitious Demon Lord like Mammon, otherwise, she should have already died at the hands of the sword, and the kingdom would have fallen to the demon race.

"Your Majesty!" Mesfield was very unhappy.

"Windsor, calm down a bit, I now understand why you so hate Elkin the Swordmaster, but we still have to respect the facts, don't we?" Elizabeth Queen spoke seriously, feeling that Mesfield, as her personal guard, even if she hated him, she couldn't slander him.

"Mesfield lowered her head, frowning, "I understand, but what should we do next? Can't we just let this guy run wild in the kingdom?"

"I won't allow that to happen." Elizabeth Queen leaned back in her chair, looking out the window for a long time—

"We should take him down from the people closest to him."

Several days later, Alice resigned from her Hero position, returning from the Vatican to Britain, preparing to return to Lichfield to live a peaceful life with her daughter.

Because Merlin had not returned, the little girl had been in a low mood for this period, and when she asked her mother Alice, she also didn't get an answer, not even the usual evasion.

Because Alice couldn't be sure whether Merlin could return or not, she couldn't make any promises to her daughter, and could only keep changing the topic, hoping that Chris could temporarily forget Merlin.

Just as the mother and child had just disembarked and reached the port of the British kingdom, they were suddenly surrounded by a group of wisteria knights, and the atmosphere immediately became tense, with a strong smell of gunpowder.

Alice hugged her daughter, who was scared, and asked angrily, "What do you mean?"

Mesfield slowly walked out from among the knights, speaking in a stern tone—

"Please come with us, Miss Alice."

"You have a serious suspicion of threatening the safety of the kingdom."

title: Chapter 51 — Emergence
content:
Chapter 51 — Emergence

Volume 36 · Chapter 51

Alice was forced to temporarily leave her daughter behind and was directly taken to the palace by Meisterfeld to undergo an investigation. She had thought she would be taken to a dimly lit interrogation room, but instead, she was directly brought to the queen's private office.

Alice believed there must be some misunderstanding, and she had never threatened the kingdom's safety. She needed to clarify this matter. A group of knights brought Alice to the palace, and she was sitting on edge, feeling inexplicably nervous, unsure of what had caused such a big misunderstanding.

After a while, Elizabeth walked in with Meisterfeld by her side. Alice stood up, looking puzzled, and was about to ask a question when Elizabeth spoke up first.

"I'm sorry to have brought you here by force, did I scare you?" "Alice's expression froze," "No, it's fine."

"I have some things I need to clarify with you, so I had to use a bit of force, please don't mind it." Elizabeth spoke in a gentle tone, not wanting Alice to feel hostile, but rather to clarify Merlin's background.

Seeing Elizabeth's attitude was not hostile, Alice slightly relaxed, "What is it?"

"This." Elizabeth hesitated, thinking it was better to keep this information to herself, so she whispered to Meisterfeld, "Windsor, you stay outside for now, I want to talk to Alice alone."

"But Your Majesty, Meisterfeld doesn't want to leave, wanting to know more about the Elgin Great Sword Hero." "Alice is not a bad person, it's fine." Elizabeth gave Meisterfeld a reassuring look.

Meisterfeld had no choice but to leave, deciding to eavesdrop on the conversation from outside. After Meisterfeld left, the room was left with only Elizabeth and Alice, creating an awkward atmosphere.

"Please sit down, Alice." Elizabeth sat down across from Alice, speaking softly, "I know you, as a hero, participated in the Saint City defense war, and just returned, I'm also quite sorry."

"It's fine, I was planning to rest in the capital for a night." Alice replied.

"I've recently heard about your heroic performance against demons, although you're an external Thorn Knight, the knights often talk about you in private, regarding you as a role model." Elizabeth smiled.

"A role model?" Alice felt a bit embarrassed.

"We can all see your excellence, and there's no need to be modest about it. And if you're willing, you can become a formal Thorn Knight at any time." Elizabeth said meaningfully.

"No, I'll pass, I don't like living in the capital, thank you for your kindness." Alice declined Elizabeth's proposal, asking instead, "By the way, you didn't just want me to join the Violet Thorn Knights, did you?"

"Alice, you're so clever, actually, I wanted to ask you about your husband, Merlin." Elizabeth replied straightforwardly.

"Merlin?" Alice furrowed her brow, wondering why the queen was so interested in Merlin. She had heard whispers about them before, but they were just rumors.

"No, I'm not mistaken, you're standing on the human side, or are you on the demon side? I hope you can answer honestly." Elizabeth looked at Alice intently, wanting to know her relationship with demons, a former hero, why she became the wife of a demon king.

"Huh?" Alice thought she would be asked something scandalous, but Elizabeth's question caught her off guard, making her tense up, unsure of how to respond.

Of course, she was standing on the human side, but she lived with a demon king every day, she could accept Merlin, but not the entire demon race, that was a completely different matter.

"My stance is definitely on the human side, why are you asking this?" "Because your husband, Merlin, is a demon, isn't he?" Elizabeth asked nonchalantly.

"? Alice unconsciously gripped the armrest of her chair, being startled, thinking this was a secret only a few people knew, why did the queen know?

"And he's one of the seven demon lords, isn't he?" Elizabeth added.

"!!!!" Alice suddenly looked up at Elizabeth, her expression shocked, her mind reeling in confusion, seeing the queen's smile, she was taken aback.

How did she know so clearly? Did she know that Merlin was a demon king? Who told her? It couldn't be Merlin himself, no way, Merlin would never voluntarily reveal his true identity!

All of Alice's reactions fell on Elizabeth's eyes, and her doubts were dispelled, she was certain that Meisterfeld's report was correct, Merlin was indeed a demon king!

Even Alice herself didn't realize it, she was not good at lying, many things were written on her face, and people could see through her thoughts.

"Your Majesty, what are you talking about? Could you possibly know more about my husband than I do? He's human, how could he be a demon?" Alice tried to deny it.

"Alice, don't hide it, I already know, Merlin is a demon, and a rare male succubus." Elizabeth revealed another fact, further attacking Alice's psychological defenses.

Seeing the queen's confidence, Alice felt that hiding it wouldn't make a difference, the other party already knew everything, "If you already know, then I don't need to explain it, but Merlin is different from ordinary demons, I can guarantee that he has no malice towards humans, and no ambition like other demon kings, please believe me, we've lived together for a long time, and I know his character well."

"Are you certain? Without ambition?" Elizabeth asked tentatively.

"Of course! If he had any ambition, how could he be content with living in a small town like Rekzem, always working as a low-ranking black iron adventurer? He's pursuing something far more simple." Alice replied confidently, hoping to dispel the queen's doubts, understanding that the ruling class was afraid of someone threatening their status.

Elizabeth fell silent, seeing Alice's gaze so sincere, her heart was moved, and after a while, she said, "I believe what you said, and I believe that Merlin is different from other demons, after all, the Elgin Great Sword Hero is a hero who saved Britain, willing to help humans, I've only seen one like him, so I believe he's not on the same side as the demons invading the kingdom."

"Wait a minute! You just said Merlin was what?" Alice's face was filled with surprise, as if she had caught something important.

"Originally willing to help humans?" "The previous sentence. "Because Merlin is the Elgin Great Sword Hero?" Alice's body shook, her expression shocked, knowing the secret that had been lingering in her heart.

"???"

title: Chapter 52 — Farewell
content:
Chapter 52 — Farewell

Volume 36 · Chapter 52

Alice's expression fell into stunned surprise, her mind going blank at the secret Queen Elizabeth had suddenly let slip.

Her idol and role model, the great sword hero Elgin, was actually Merlin? ? ?

Though Merlin had once openly admitted that he was the great sword hero Elgin, Alice had found it hard to believe such a thing, unable to reconcile his image with the legendary sword hero.

Just thinking about Merlin's usual behavior, he looked nothing like someone who would act heroically; it was far more likely he'd immediately run away from any trouble.

A guy who kept his nose out of other people's business and stayed far removed from it had almost nothing in common with a hero who rescued the weak.

Alice seemed to have not realized that the so-called image of justice surrounding the great sword hero Elgin was entirely embellished and exaggerated by others, combined with her own imagination, pushing Elgin's heroic image toward perfection.

In reality, no one had ever truly come into contact with the great sword hero Elgin or attempted to understand what kind of person he was; even Queen Elizabeth had only met him once.

If Alice had the chance to spend some time up close with the great sword hero Elgin, all her fantasies would shatter, and she would realize this guy was none other than Merlin, full of flaws.

"Uh, Merlin is the great sword hero Elgin? You, you're sure?"

"Of course I'm sure. We've met privately, so— could it be that you?" Elizabeth paused, then asked curiously, "Miss Alice has lived with Mr. Merlin for so long and didn't even know that?"

"I, I did know. I thought I was the only one who knew this secret."

Alice forced a stiff smile; the secret spoken by the queen needed no verification.

After all, she was Merlin's wife in name. If she didn't even know the secret of Merlin being the great sword hero Elgin, wouldn't that make a laughingstock of herself before Queen Elizabeth?

So Alice could only bluff and say she knew perfectly well, putting on a calm exterior while her heart churned within—

It was confirmed then. Merlin was the great sword hero Elgin.

Oh my god! How could things have turned out like this?

Does this guy Merlin also have a side willing to stand up for justice on behalf of the weak? I've been underestimating him too much. No wonder I always felt a shadow of Merlin on the great sword hero.

The idol and role model I had always pursued was actually right by my side this whole time? What an incredible coincidence!

I finally understand why Merlin always wore such a strange expression whenever the great sword hero Elgin was mentioned.

And I naively expressed that I had a fondness for the great sword hero Elgin. Wasn't that a veiled confession to Merlin? This guy must have been treating me like an idiot all along!

I'm done for. I have no face to see—

Alice's mind was in complete turmoil. She lowered her head and covered her face, wishing she could simply crawl into a crack in the ground. Her mind was filled with Merlin's triumphant smile.

"Miss Alice? Are you alright? Your complexion looks rather poor." Queen Elizabeth asked with concern.

"I, I'm fine." Alice took a deep breath, temporarily setting the matter aside. With Merlin not by her side, there was nothing she could do to learn more anyway.

"I can大概 guess Mr. Merlin's position, but whether the kingdom's invasion by demons is connected to him, I cannot yet confirm." Queen Elizabeth said meaningfully.

"Merlin has nothing to do with this matter. He was expelled from the demon race and is the only deposed ruler. The recent expansion by the demons externally is related to turmoil within their own ranks," Alice responded quietly.

"Turmoil within the demon race?" Elizabeth, though lacking precise intelligence, had guessed as much.

"Yes. Speaking of which, Alice feels the matter is in the past and can be discussed without restraint—"

Until late at night, Alice went on recounting the story of the demons rebelling against the bondage imposed by their creator.

At the temporary post house in the royal capital, Alice was escorted to the palace, leaving little Chris behind in the room, with instructions not to wander off.

The little one lay gloomily on the desk, occasionally lifting her head to glance at the clock, hoping her mother would return soon.

"Hmph, foolish human cub~"

The fairy Feiry suddenly appeared in the room. Having failed to find Alice, she unexpectedly discovered Merlin's daughter.

Chris's ahoge instantly sprang up like an antenna. Upon seeing Feiry with translucent insect-like wings, her eyes sparkled with stars. "Wow! A talking firefly!"

"Who's a firefly? I'm a fairy! Haven't you heard of fairies?" Fairy Feiry crossed her arms, displeased. Kids were so troublesome—so ignorant they'd equate me with an insect.

"A fairy?" Little Chris hopped down from her chair, came to Feiry's side, and tilted her head to ask in a baby voice, "Is it you who takes the baby teeth from under my pillow and grants my wishes?"

"What the—?" Fairy Feiry frowned. "You're Chris, and Merlin is your father, right?"

"So impressive! You even know both my name and my dad's! I never told you!" Chris's eyes widened innocently, convinced the fairy before her could predict the future.

"What's with that?"

Feiry wouldn't tell Chris it was Merlin who had said it. Being praised by a child made her somewhat giddy.

Fairies, by instinct, are drawn to pure beings—especially innocent children.

"What's your name?" Chris asked curiously.

"Feiry. You can call me Uncle Feiry."

"But you look smaller than me..."

"Pfft! Size isn't the point; wisdom is." Fairy Feiry said in an aged manner, flapping her cicada-like wings behind her, hands on hips, standing proudly on Chris's palm. "You really do resemble young Merlin in your posture, especially your eyes. But your aura is much more likable."

The little one grew somewhat excited. Having encountered a fairy for the first time, she found it far more exquisite than any doll she had ever seen.

Chris cupped Feiry in both hands, her little face rosy as she studied it.

"You've seen my dad?"

"Of course. Otherwise how would I let you call me Uncle Feiry? I once played Merlin like a fiddle. Pretty impressive, huh?" Fairy Feiry raised her eyebrows proudly. Savoring the bragging rights felt thrilling.

Hearing her father's name, little Chris's mood dropped considerably. She murmured sadly, "Dad hasn't come back in such a long time. Do you think something happened to him?"

"Nnnn no, don't cry! Your dad's fine, I just—"

Just as Feiry was at a loss for what to do with the about-to-cry child, the door to the room opened.

Alice had already cleared up all misunderstandings with Elizabeth. Upon returning and seeing the fairy in Chris's hands, she paused briefly, slightly recognizing it. "You're that fairy from the Allied Kingdom?"

Fairy Feiry rose into the air and approached Alice. "That's right, it's me. Merlin sent me to fetch the Deification Stone to forge Misteln."

"The Deification Stone?"

Alice looked down at the now-dull ring "Angela" on her hand. The object had always been stored inside it.

But Alice felt somewhat unwilling. Merlin had finally managed to send word, and it was only to retrieve something, without a single caring word for her or their daughter.

This left Alice quite displeased, even a touch angry. Since the end of the Siege of the Holy City, she had worried about Merlin's situation every day.

"Uh, how is he?"

"He's fine, I'd say. No danger, just looks rather lonely. Every day he sits alone on the city walls watching the sunrise and sunset." Fairy Feiry replied.

"I see." Alice felt somewhat relieved. At least Merlin had recovered and was not in life-threatening danger. "Has he said anything else?"

"Oh! I almost forgot. Merlin asked me to pass on a message to you." Fairy Feiry slapped her forehead, speaking in a serious and resolute tone—

"He said he will definitely come back for you. He hopes you can wait for him."

To Be Continued

Author's Note

Hey everyone, I need to take a day off today.

I know the updates have been slow this month. The reason is I'm currently out of town and won't be back until the end of the month. I didn't bring my laptop, and typing on my phone is painfully slow.

But once I'm back at the end of the month, I'll definitely make up for it with extra updates. Don't worry.

The real reason I'm taking a break today is that I've hit a writer's block. The opening jumps straight into events three years later, and the world situation and character portrayals undergo significant changes—that's too large a leap.

So finding the right entry point is proving difficult for me.

When the book was first published, this was supposed to be the emergency完结 point. If the performance wasn't good here, the story would end quickly, wrapping up with regret and anticipation.

The awkward part is that Merlin and Alice never get together, so ending it here doesn't sit well with me. Plus, there's not much left; the ending is visible in plain sight.

I should properly think it over. Normally, I'd start a new volume tomorrow. Actually, I want to start a new book. If I can't get the new volume started, ending it here might actually work—

The truth is, while the outcome at the end is positive, the process will be extremely turbulent.

Anyway, I'll think it over tonight and see where would be a suitable entry point for the story set three years later.

Volume 37 · Chapter 1

In the dimly lit room, labored breaths came in fits and fits, and a corpse lay in a pool of blood, growing colder by the moment.

Loyal servant Makhmud had been killed by Cain himself.

Even Lamia was badly wounded, barely able to resist in Cain’s presence, completely subdued throughout.

*"Huff... huff..."*

Lamia knelt on the ground, cold sweat trickling down her face, her spirit shattered, her body oozing crimson blood.

She and her servant had always hidden in a remote valley where few humans ever ventured. But Lamia didn’t realize Cain could scent their presence, making it easy to track them down.

Lamia slowly closed her eyes, her heart filled with despair. From the moment Cain found them, she knew her fate—death was finally upon her, paying the price for deceiving him long ago.

*"What are you thinking? Regretting anything? You should know that anyone who deceives me will not escape death. Today is your reckoning."*

Lamia let out a bitter, detached laugh. *"I knew I would die someday, but I never expected it to be at your hands. In my memories, you were just the pitiful creature forever trapped in a bottle."*

*"What a pity, I’m free now."* Cain’s smile grew increasingly sinister as he murmured, *"I should thank you for teaching me a lesson: never trust anyone but yourself."*

*"You shouldn’t act like a victim. Even if we freed you from the bottle, you would have killed us anyway, wouldn’t you?"* Lamia shot back.

*"You’re right. But you’ve already gained what you wanted—far beyond human lifespan. How does it feel? Eternal life?"* Cain loomed over her in his girlish form.

*"This isn’t a blessing. Eternal life is torture. It’s given me nothing but suffering. I’ve been treated like a monster, forever barred from humanity. I only feel endless loneliness."* Lamia closed her eyes again, as if accepting her impending doom.

*"Recognizing that is already a good thing."* Cain stared into her eyes, speaking slowly. *"This is the punishment and curse my mother gave me. I’ve endured loneliness for far too long, growing accustomed to it."* *"Not bad."* Lamia sighed weakly.

*"Time to go. I think you’ve lived long enough—it’s time to return the undying power to me."* Cain’s voice dripped with authority.

*"If I die here, won’t all my efforts be in vain?"*

Lamia’s eyes snapped open, and with her last ounce of strength, she lunged at Cain.

She pulled a gleaming silver dagger from her waist—the final countermeasure forged from the Divine Stone, meant to strike him down.

She had waited for this moment, when Cain, confident in his victory, would lower his guard.

But Cain’s expression remained unreadable as he watched Lamia’s frantic attack. *"Still not learning, I see?"*

Lamia’s body froze mid-motion, as if struck by a paralyzing spell, rigid in place.

The sharp silver blade in her hand was just inches from Cain’s chest—yet the distance felt like an impossible chasm.

Her face twisted in despair, her body no longer obeying her, completely under Cain’s control.

*"Everything you have is mine to give. So you can’t defy my command—this is the suppression of blood. Killing you would take but a word from me, easier than crushing an ant."* Cain stepped closer, tilting his head as he traced the dagger’s edge with his fingertip. *"Did you really prepare this just to kill me?"*

Lamia’s sweat poured down her face, her body trembling violently as she gasped for words.

*"Pity. It might have some effect on me, but you’ll never have the chance to strike. You’re too weak."* Cain leaned in, baring his sharp fangs as he bit into Lamia’s slender neck.

Lamia’s eyes rolled back, her flesh shrinking and withering at an alarming rate, her face visibly aging before her eyes. Soon, Cain drained her dry, leaving only a hollowed-out corpse.

Cain wiped his lips with satisfaction, his strength surging as he absorbed Lamia’s power. Even his appearance shifted subtly, maturing from his girlish form.

With one more victim—Bathory—Cain would reclaim all his undying divine power, returning to his prime state, his strength peaking once more.

Dickter, the gambler standing obediently behind Cain, had witnessed everything in silence, not daring to breathe.

He had planned to strike the fatal blow the moment Cain returned to Heaven, then claim all the rewards as the new godling and seize the undying power.

But now the situation was spiraling out of control. Cain’s power was growing stronger by the moment, soon reaching an unstoppable level.

Dickter’s doubts gnawed at him. Even if he fired a Divine Stone bullet straight through Cain’s heart, he wasn’t sure he could kill this monster.

He stared at Lamia’s drained corpse for a long time, unable to speak. Should he slip away? Staying near Cain seemed even more dangerous.

*"Dickter, watch closely—this is what happens to those who betray me. You took my things, and you’ll have to return them eventually."*

*"Uh—!"*

Dickter’s body froze, cold sweat breaking out on his forehead as he wondered if Cain suspected his loyalty.

He quickly bowed his head, avoiding Lamia’s corpse, fearing he might meet the same grotesque end.

*"My loyalty to you is beyond question! I will never betray you! I’ve realized how foolish betrayal is!"* His voice trembled. *"Their fate was just. They don’t deserve pity!"*

*"Nice words, but I won’t fully trust you. You understand, don’t you?"* Cain spoke with deliberate meaning.

*"I understand! I only believe that serving the great True Ancestor is my honor. I don’t dare hope for your trust."*

Dickter slouched like a sycophant, not daring to lift his head, his heart pounding from fear. *"Then... should we continue hunting the last deceiver?"*

*"Not yet. I need time to absorb Lamia’s power."* Cain stroked the hilt of his demon sword, Tilfyn. *"Every time I reclaim divine power, I need time to digest it—so I can always stay at my peak."* *"What’s going on?"* Dickter asked in shock.

*"If I’m not mistaken, the last target has sensed me hunting them and used some special method to conceal their presence entirely."* Cain paused, his gaze growing distant. *"What a clever little thing..."*

title: Chapter 2 — Collapse
content:
Chapter 2 — Collapse

Volume 37 · Chapter 2

"What should we do now? If you can't sense his aura, wouldn't it be hard to find him?" Dickterpin asked softly, unable to figure out what method had been used to sever the connection with Cain.

"Do you think that by concealing all aura, one can evade my pursuit?" Cain said with a knowing smile. "Foolish. Unless one leaves the mortal world, there is absolutely no escaping my grasp."

Seeing Cain's confident demeanor, Dickterpin couldn't help but feel sympathy for the final prey, Bártory. Clearly, she wouldn't be able to escape the hunt either. Cain would reclaim all the undying divine powers, and his strength would reach unbelievable levels.

Dickterpin knew very well that escaping the mortal world was nearly impossible. Neither the Underworld nor the Heavenly Realm were places that mortals could enter casually. Bártory was still hiding somewhere in the mortal world.

Cain's gaze turned westward, his eyes narrowing. "That's the direction where her aura disappeared. Follow that direction to investigate and search. We'll eventually find some traces."

Dickterpin opened his mouth as if to say something but hesitated, sensing that things were not straightforward. "This lead is too vague. It won't be easy to find the final prey. Our resources are limited, and we're short-handed."

"There can be as many hands as you need. Have you forgotten that you are not human, but a member of the Vampire Clan?" Cain's tone carried a hint.

"Your servant is foolish. Your meaning is—" Dickterpin furrowed his brow slightly.

"Dickterpin, do you want to become someone like Dracula, create your own domain, and become the new master of the Vampire Clan?" Cain paused, then added persuasively, "Serve me, and I won't treat you unfairly. This is your reward."

"Huh!"

Dickterpin shuddered. He hadn't never thought about it. Dracula's dream was to establish an eternal night empire belonging to vampires, and that was something Dickterpin had dreamed of for years—transforming from a mere bandit into the master of a new empire.

However, Dickterpin was quite suspicious and wondered if Cain was testing his ambition, so he dared not show it too obviously.

Dickterpin knelt on one knee, bowed his head, and answered respectfully.

"The Vampire Clan will always have only one master, and that is you. Letting me become your loyal hound is the greatest kindness bestowed upon me."

"You're indeed a shrewd fellow, making not a single mistake. I can see your ambition—it won't escape me. But even a dog needs to eat its fill before it has the strength to work, doesn't it?" Cain looked down at Dickterpin, having seen through this man who chased profit and abandoned his soul long ago.

"Dickterpin broke into a cold sweat, thinking that no matter how obsequiously he groveled, he could never win Cain's trust. Even if he couldn't replace Cain, becoming the master of the Vampire Clan's domain wouldn't be a bad deal."

"Stop being so timid. Use my blood to create servants. No matter what methods you use, you must find the final prey. Otherwise, you will lose something—including your life." Cain rolled up his sleeve, revealing a fair wrist, and held it out before Dickterpin.

Dickterpin raised his head and stared at Cain's pale, rosy arm. Subconsciously, he swallowed hard. The impulse craving blood continuously stimulated him, and he couldn't help but reveal his sharp fangs.

***

In the capital of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, deep within a mysterious and pitch-black underground prison, Countess Bártory was imprisoned in an eerie bone cage.

Pure white bones shimmered with a metallic luster, interlocking to form a sturdy cage that radiated a sacred aura belonging to the Holy Spirit.

Bártory, being a vampire and a creature of darkness, was highly resistant to the dark aura emanating from the cage. The torment kept her from sleeping, leaving her weak and exhausted as she lay listlessly inside.

Cough.

Dais, the Chief Grand Knight of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, was ordered to keep close watch on Countess Bártory at all times, except for bathroom breaks.

However, Dais was naturally frail and sickly. Focusing his energy on watching Bártory only made his condition worse, and he couldn't stop coughing.

Dais had interrogated Bártory for a long time and had basically learned everything, including many secrets of the Vampire Clan and some information about that terrifying demigod, Cain.

Though the young and beautiful-looking Countess Bártory had mingled within the upper noble circles of the Austro-Hungarian Kingdom, she was actually an old hag whose age could rival the kingdom's history.

When the Emperor of the Austro-Hungarian Empire heard this truth, he nearly fainted on the spot. He had often exchanged flirtatious glances with Countess Bártory and privately exchanged love letters, only to discover he had fallen for a woman older than his grandmother—had he really had a跨-century romance?

If such a ridiculously melodramatic story got out, the ruler's dignity would be completely ruined, becoming the talk and joke of the nation.

To cover up the truth, the Emperor ordered Dais to seal off all information, place Countess Bártory under indefinite imprisonment, and secretly dig up the secrets and utilitarian value of the Vampire Clan.

Dais's face was pale as he stared at the dying Bártory in the bone cage. He felt somewhat sympathetic toward this "woman." Being turned into a monster by Cain was one thing, but now that her vampire identity had been exposed, she was being drained of all her value. This wasn't how one treated a human—it was how one treated livestock to be slaughtered at will.

However, Dais was an experienced knight and wouldn't soften toward Bártory out of pity. He knew very well that the once-glamourous socialite of the noble circles before him was nothing more than a monster wrapped in a beautiful skin.

No matter how much one harmed this woman, her wounds would heal rapidly, leaving not even a scar.

He wondered how many people within the empire had been deceived by Countess Bártory's human skin, becoming unfortunate victims who fell to her charms.

Just thinking about it made Dais feel somewhat disgusted. No matter how pitiful Countess Bártory appeared, it couldn't conceal her ruthless side.

TheListlessly sitting in the bone cage, Bártory suddenly sat up, her eyes filled with terror as she stared toward a certain direction in the prison. Her lips trembled.

"Dead again… another one has died! She couldn't escape either!"

"Who died?" Dais frowned, perking up a bit.

"My former companions, those who deceived Cain together to gain undying power. Her aura has completely disappeared. Now I'm the only one left!"

Countess Bártory shouted excitedly, her emotions on the verge of collapse. She was the last one alive.

This meant that Cain would soon find Bártory and inflict the cruelest punishment. She would pay the price for her earlier deception.

Bártory's expression was blank, as if she had already seen her own death countdown.

Dais, knowing about vampire matters, asked, "Do you mean that one called Lamia? She's dead?"

"That's right! Just now, her aura completely vanished!" Countess Bártory ruffled her hair, looking like a lunatic.

"Who did it?" Dais pressed seriously.

"Cain! It must be Cain! I can feel her threat closing in!" Countess Bártory curled up in the cage, muttering in disbelief—

"Lamia has been killed, so next it'll be my turn."

"What should I do?"

"What exactly should I do to escape Cain's punishment…"

title: Chapter 3 — Three Years Later
content:
Chapter 3 — Three Years Later

Volume 37 · Chapter 3

“I don’t want to die, especially not at the hands of Cain! She must hate us for deceiving her, and now she wants to cruelly avenge us!”

Bartoli Lady curled up in the bone cage, shouting excitedly, “Come on, think of a way! Soon Cain will arrive here, and we’ll all die at her hands!”

“Hmm,” Dais spoke without any expression, showing no concern.

“Why are you so calm? Won’t you think of sacrificing me to save yourself?”

“I don’t rule out that possibility,” Dais replied coldly. If this divine child is as powerful as legend says, she poses a serious threat to the empire. Sacrificing Bartoli Lady might defuse the crisis, though it’s a terrible choice that doesn’t align with the empire’s current interests.

“Ha, ridiculous! You won’t think Cain is someone you can negotiate with, right? Even if you hand me over, you won’t survive. Humans are mere worms in her eyes.” Bartoli Lady scoffed, continuing, “After I die, Cain will reclaim all her immortal power, transforming into a divine child. Then not only the Austro-Hungarian Empire, but the entire world will be devastated. Expecting such an extremely dangerous person is too foolish.”

“Sacrificing you to Cain is a last resort, and it’s not time yet. You can be at ease,” Dais paused, speaking calmly. “Moreover, Cain may not even find you. You’re temporarily safe.”

“Find me? With this broken cage?” Bartoli Lady looked at the cage holding her, her fingers barely touching it caused intense pain, as if she had touched a high-voltage wire.

“Yes, don’t underestimate this specially made cage. It’s built entirely of holy bones. The emperor spent great effort to obtain the materials, which the church retrieved from ancient battlefields. The value of each bone far exceeds your fortune,” Dais explained slowly. To restrain and protect Bartoli Lady, the imperial side also made a significant investment, aiming to obtain the secrets of her immortal power and the bloodline’s secrets.

“Oh?” Bartoli Lady looked up, dissatisfied, “Besides restraining and tormenting me, it has no other use.”

“No, you misunderstood. The cage made of holy bones can isolate your aura and prevent external detection, especially from the perception of dark creatures,” Dais looked at Bartoli Lady seriously, “If everything goes well, all your auras have been completely masked. Cain cannot find your exact location and cannot easily come here.”

Bartoli Lady looked around, impressed by the cage’s supposed safety, but she still felt uncertain. To find her, Cain would undoubtedly resort to ruthless means.

“Who knows if this cage works? Staying here all the time, I’ll eventually go crazy!”

“Even without this cage, you’ll still be imprisoned, just in a more spacious place. Don’t forget, you’re a criminal of the empire, not a noble lady anymore,” Dais emphasized sternly, already annoyed by Bartoli’s complaints.

“Pfft!” Bartoli Lady scoffed, resentful. If not for the black guild’s thugs, she could have continued her luxurious widow life.

“We won’t harass you or sacrifice you to Cain. The emperor has said that as long as we can research the secrets of immortality, we’ll set you free. Hope you cooperate,” Dais stated the royal family’s attitude towards Bartoli, valuing her body that never ages or gets hurt.

“Heh, pursuing immortality is something many people dream of. You’re just trying to squeeze out my last value, aren’t you?” Bartoli Lady said meaningfully.

“We won’t pursue your crimes of colluding with the black guild and harming humans, and even protect you from Cain’s hunting. That’s the price you should pay,” Dais looked directly into Bartoli’s eyes, adding frankly, “This is a win-win deal. Doesn’t it sound good?”

“If you really want immortality, I can give it to you anytime. Just let me bite you, and you’ll become my bloodline,” Bartoli Lady said seductively.

“That’s too dangerous. Although we can achieve immortality, we won’t be human anymore, but vampires who fear sunlight, and also your servants,” Dais’s gaze sharpened, refusing this suggestion.

“What’s wrong with that? I remember you have a severe lung disease, right? You’ve been coughing all the time, must be suffering every day. Why not try becoming a vampire? You can immediately cure all your ailments, and have a body that will never be tormented by pain. Isn’t that tempting?” Bartoli Lady opened her lips slightly, her fangs glinting.

“I admit it’s tempting, but at the cost of becoming an unsightly monster, I choose to refuse,” Dais replied coldly.

“You’ll regret it. You’ll eventually collapse from the strain and come to me,” Bartoli Lady said confidently.

“Perhaps by then, we’ll have found a way to achieve immortality without becoming monsters.”

As the words fell, a group of doctors wearing bird-masked helmets and black robes entered the prison, carrying large and small toolboxes and even heavy saws.

Seeing these eerie figures, Bartoli Lady’s face turned pale, fear filled her eyes, and she almost every day endured the torment of her body being dismembered.

“Sir Dais, today, besides taking blood, we’ll also saw off the limbs and take the heart for research. Vampires have extremely strong life force, but their hearts are weak points. Maybe we can discover new secrets.”

Dais nodded, approving of the action, his gaze coldly staring at Bartoli in the cage, whispering, “Good luck, go ahead.”

“Don’t worry, she won’t die.”

“Monsters are monsters. No matter how much we torment her, she’ll recover.”

“Removing the heart? Sawing off the head? That’s just child’s play.”

Three years later, great calamities began spreading relentlessly towards the west.

Dikter obtained Cain’s permission and began creating vampires with her blood. Shadows of the night emerged one after another.

The newly appeared vampire group, led by Dikter, regarded her as the master of the new bloodline.

Dikter experienced feelings she had never had before, a desire to turn all humans into vampires. She now understood why Dracula was so obsessed with the Eternal Night Empire. It was an irresistible temptation.

Vampires began spreading like a virus or plague towards the west, expanding secretly at an astonishing speed. The groups in the dark also became increasingly large.

It seemed like it had been a long time ago, an era when vampires ruled the world, more ferocious than demons, and more hidden. They often hid among humans, difficult to discover.

They were wolves in sheep’s clothing, mingling among the sheep, threatening their safety.

The profession of vampire hunters was born in such a background, but unfortunately, most have already been eliminated.

In a dark cellar of a certain village, Alice stepped on the chest of a vampire with her foot, her dagger flashing—

“Answer me, where are your allies?”

title: Chapter 4 — Dominion in the Shadows
content:
Chapter 4 — Dominion in the Shadows

Volume 37 · Chapter 4

To find the hiding Bartori, Dictor Plains ordered the vampires to constantly infiltrate each of the kingdoms, searching for clues. This led to the vampires' threat growing larger and more frequent, with vampire attacks on humans occurring all over the world, even in remote villages. Vampires can create new members through initial possession, without the need for reproduction, allowing them to expand their population. With their incredibly powerful life force, the vampires' numbers may have already surpassed those of the disaster that occurred in France, a period in history known for being the most prosperous. The existence of vampires is like a constantly spreading virus, and by the time danger is detected, it may be too late. To counter the vampires, people have been seeking help from the Church, hoping to receive protection and blessings. However, the Church has been weakened since the Saint City Defense War and has not fully recovered in the past three years, providing mostly superficial help, such as leading prayers or selling expensive scriptures. Even more ridiculous is the claim that daily bathing with holy water can repel nearby vampires using sacred power. The public has begun to criticize the Church's inaction, and under pressure, they have sent the Order of the Knights to handle the situation. Although the Knights know that piercing a vampire's heart with silver can kill them, these creatures are not easily defeated, with formidable strength and strange behavior, making it difficult to completely eliminate them. Moreover, vampires are extremely intelligent and will not easily reveal themselves, unless thoroughly investigated, which is a time-consuming and exhausting process. This situation has provided a fertile ground for the vampires' rampage. Experts who used to deal with vampires and vampire hunters have long since disappeared, and it is now difficult to find a successor, as this profession has disappeared from history. People have no choice but to seek help from adventurers, who are more approachable and down-to-earth than the high-ranking Church and kingdom knights. In recent times, the number of commissions from major guilds has increased to unprecedented levels, with most being related to vampires. Adventurers have been forced to work overtime, investigating all over the world, and their manpower is stretched thin, as they have had to learn a lot of knowledge to deal with the ruthless bloodline, with silver daggers becoming a standard equipment that they never leave behind. Alice appeared in the nearby village of Reksem due to a recent mission to eliminate a vampire hiding in a cellar. Three years later, Alice's appearance has not changed much, but her demeanor has matured significantly, and she is also known as the renowned purple adventurer in the British region, with a reputation and status that rivals that of the former London Guildmaster, Gregory. She accepted the small village's designated task without considering the reward, as it is close to Reksem and can be done in a day, allowing her to spend more time with her daughter. To be able to spend more time with Chris, Alice has rarely left Britain in the past three years, spending most of her time within the kingdom. In the dark cellar, the vampire was cornered by Alice, its chest crushed, and a thin sword hung around its neck, radiating a cold, bone-chilling chill. "Alice Clodia, the renowned strong purple adventurer, I never thought that the noble you would come for me, a mere small bloodline." "Don't waste my time, didn't you understand what I said?" Alice stood tall, her hand holding the Light Chant, slowly cutting through the vampire's throat. "Reksem is definitely not just you, there must be other vampires. Where are they?" The sacred aura of the Light Chant continuously invaded the vampire's body through the neck wound, causing it immense pain, as if it was being burned by flames. The vampire gritted its teeth, laughing miserably, giving up all hope of escape, with no confidence in escaping from a purple adventurer. "You won't think I'll tell you the truth, will you? Kill me, and I won't resist anymore. I just hope you'll have mercy and give me a quick death, this is my last plea." "Hiding the truth won't benefit you, I'll kill you, but whether I'll let you die without pain depends on your behavior." Alice coldly threatened, if not for wanting to know more secrets, she would have killed the vampire long ago. "You can't threaten me, give up." The vampire paused, its tone unwilling, "If it weren't for a villager escaping and reporting to the Adventurer's Guild, you would never have discovered me." "You've been hiding in this village for a long time, haven't you? You've drained the blood of four villagers and even created three more of your kind to do your bidding." Alice's gaze was stern, questioning the vampire, "Your crimes, death cannot compensate for." "Survival of the fittest is an unchanging law, I was once a human, thinking that dark creatures were all dirty and disgusting, but after becoming a vampire, I realized the power and immortality that came with it, no one can easily reject these benefits." The vampire paused, its gaze mesmerized, "The monster that humans fear, is so excellent? The great bloodline has not dominated this world, it is clearly against the natural law." "Talk nonsense." Alice coldly evaluated, the person in front of her had been blinded by power and immortality, and was unable to communicate. "As for the strong you, you are already very powerful, and you have a long life, you must look down on these things, but for ordinary people who are long sick, these are the things they dream of, giant dragons can never understand the feelings of weak ants." The vampire, facing death threats, still wore a mocking smile on its face, "I won't reveal any information to you, nor will I give you the opportunity to torture me." "What do you mean?" Alice's gaze condensed, suspecting that the other party might have some hidden cards, so she immediately became vigilant, ready to strike down the vampire's head with her sword at the slightest sign of resistance. The Light Chant, as the enemy of dark creatures, did not need to pierce the vampire's heart, as long as it caused sufficient damage, it could take their lives! Alice was not unfamiliar with vampires, having fought a Saint-tier vampire in France in the past, and she was well aware of their bloodthirsty nature. "About the truth of the great bloodline... " The vampire's words suddenly stopped, as if triggering a curse? Its body burned from the inside out, with a smile on its face, turning into ashes in front of Alice. Alice was unable to kill the vampire herself, but it chose to end its own life? This left Alice puzzled, even if it was dead, it refused to reveal the mastermind behind the scenes, what was it hiding? Alice furrowed her brow, sheathing her sword, muttering softly, "If I want to reveal the secrets of the bloodline, will it trigger the mechanism of death?" "It seems that things are more serious than I thought."

title: Chapter 5 — **Missing in Action**
content:
Chapter 5 — **Missing in Action**

Volume 37 · Chapter 5

After dealing with the bloodsucking vampires in the cellar, Alice stepped out with a grave expression on her face.

She was deeply puzzled by the recent bloodline’s relentless threats to human safety—

In past encounters with vampires, Alice had learned many things about the bloodline.

The current situation mirrored the time when Count Dracula sought to establish his eternal night empire in France!

As far as she knew, besides Dracula, the bloodline had two other primordial ancestors. Was it possible they were secretly stirring trouble? Or perhaps the fallen son of God, Cain, was expanding his influence?

Alice couldn’t obtain concrete intelligence, and no matter how long she thought about it, she couldn’t find an answer. It seemed all vampires were gagged—anyone who dared to reveal the truth would be burned alive.

Outside the cellar, a large crowd of villagers had gathered, each holding out their finest wine and food to properly reward the renowned Purple Gold Adventurer.

Alice’s name was well-known among the villagers, and at first, they couldn’t believe that such a powerful adventurer would come to this remote village to help them.

But when they finally decided to ask for help, they were stunned to find Alice had actually come. Their impression and evaluation of her instantly improved—they thought she was approachable and had no airs.

The villagers were very clear that hiring an adventurer meant paying a fee, especially for a Purple Gold Adventurer, which was exorbitantly expensive—even rich people couldn’t always afford one. So they were deeply grateful to Alice.

Alice looked at the villagers, all brimming with anticipation, and announced loudly, “The vampires in the cellar have been eliminated, and you’re all safe now. But you must still be cautious, because recently, the vampires have been very active and may have infiltrated among us.

If you encounter similar difficulties later, you can always go to the town’s guild to find me. Even if I’m not there, other adventurers will provide help.”

When the villagers heard the news, their anxious hearts finally settled, and their faces broke into joyful smiles. They rushed forward to greet Alice, handing over the gifts they had prepared—

“These vampires have kept all of us awake at night, but today, they’re finally over. Alice, you truly live up to your reputation as the ace of the Rekserum Guild—you settled this chaos so quickly.”

“Alice, this is our family’s grape wine. Please take some with you. Although we’re poor and can’t pay a high fee, our intentions are sincere—please accept them!”

“I heard Alice has a young daughter? Then take our sheep with you. Fresh sheep’s milk is very good for children!”

Alice felt a little embarrassed facing the enthusiastic villagers. She didn’t really need these things, and she hadn’t come here expecting any return.

“Alice! Alice!”

Lucia called out from the crowd, finally managing to push her way forward. Her cheeks were flushed from the effort.

Because the guild had recently seen a surge in commissions, there was a shortage of adventurers, forcing Lucia—the receptionist—to step in and work. Considering Lucia’s weak strength and lack of experience, she was only assigned to assist Alice, helping with minor tasks.

Moreover, apart from Merlin, no adventurer in the Rekserum Guild was as strong as Alice. Having Lucia by her side was much safer.

“Alice, the sun is already setting. We need to hurry, or we won’t make it back to Rekserum before nightfall.”

The carriage, which had been empty on the way here, was now packed with villagers’ gifts.

Alice didn’t want to take them, but she couldn’t refuse the villagers’ enthusiasm. If she didn’t accept, she’d never leave the village.

Lucia flipped through the villagers’ gifts and looked at Alice with teasing words, “You’re really popular, huh? A half-month’s worth of provisions just from this trip.”

“I can’t even use all of this. Take it back to the guild and distribute it to the other adventurers.” Alice sighed helplessly.

“That would be too embarrassing, haha.” Lucia paused, then continued, “Besides, most of the guild’s adventurers are out on missions right now, and there aren’t many people left. Taking it back would be like giving it to Hobbes, that old drunkard.”

“Yeah, everyone’s been busy lately, even you had to come out to work.” Alice smiled at Lucia.

“Of course the receptionist’s job is much lighter. This is my first time handling a commission, and I didn’t expect it to be so tiring. I don’t know how long this situation will last. Before, I only heard that the bloodline had appeared in some eastern kingdoms, but now they’ve infiltrated here too. The queen’s checkpoints at the major ports seem to have no effect at all—the vampires still managed to sneak in.”

Lucia’s tone was full of complaints. If it weren’t for these annoying bloodline creatures, she could have kept working as the receptionist forever.

“Actually, the situation is far more complicated and severe than we imagined.” Alice furrowed her brows, her mind filled with worry.

“Hmm?” Lucia sat up straight, her spirit revived as she asked, “Alice, did you discover something?”

“I’m not the first to face vampires. Back then, the situation was different—much worse than now. At that time, the vampires were only active in France, but now they’ve spread to multiple kingdoms and regions.”

Alice paused, lowering her voice to say, “The bloodline’s harm is already beyond control.”

“That serious?” Lucia gasped, thinking the turmoil was only temporary. “Excluding that small-scale disturbance in France, the bloodline had been wiped out for a long time. Who’s manipulating them in the background?”

“They haven’t disappeared—they’ve just become more secretive. As for who’s controlling them?” Alice lowered her head, deep in thought, guessing, “The bloodline has three primordial ancestors. Dracula died during the disturbance in France, leaving two others. Maybe they’re the ones causing trouble. Of course, I can’t be sure, because there’s also a more terrifying existence—one capable of triggering a global catastrophe.”

“?” Lucia was a little confused. Her worldview was ordinary, and she hadn’t reached the level of being able to interact with the fallen son of God.

“Moreover, the vampires are all gagged. The hidden enemy clearly doesn’t want to reveal themselves.” Alice lowered her head, thinking.

“It sounds like a hunter who doesn’t want to scare away the snakes. If the snake senses the hunter, it will definitely run away.” Lucia said casually, thinking the vampires weren’t deliberately attacking humans but were instead hiding in every corner, living alongside them.

“A hunter who doesn’t want to scare away the snakes?” Alice furrowed her brows, then her eyes lit up as she realized who it was. “Hunter—it must be her.”

“Who?”

“We need to get back to Rekserum before nightfall. Hurry up, I asked Hobbes to investigate the vampires. Do you think he found anything?”

“Hobbes is well-connected, so he should have found something. Also, there’s some good news.”

“Good news?” Alice looked at Lucia in surprise.

“A few days ago, Arnold seemed to have proposed to Rosetti. Maybe they’ll soon officially enter the marriage hall. These two finally got together, which is really enviable. Future countess and all that.” Lucia genuinely thought they should have been together long ago, but it took three years.

“They’re getting married? Really? That’s great.” Alice nodded with a smile, her gaze slowly drifting toward the carriage window—

Arnold and Rosetti found their true love. What about me?

Three years have passed, and everyone around me has changed, but I’m still stuck in the same place.

Merlin, are you okay?

Brothers, updates are coming! More updates!

I only got home this afternoon, finally back. I can continue writing for you all.

I’ve been offline for a few days, so I apologize to everyone!

title: Chapter 6 — Source of Calamity
content:
Chapter 6 — Source of Calamity

Volume 37 · Chapter 6

In the Adventurers Guild of Rekxum, Hobbs had many maps spread out in front of him, sipping alcohol while using his quill to mark various information on them.

By rights, Hobbs, being a Black Iron adventurer, should have been out working, but Old Taylor thought he was too weak, who could barely hold his own in a fight, and it was better to keep him in the guild to gather useful intelligence.

Accurate and useful intelligence could potentially save an adventurer's life in a mission, which was the value that Hobbs could not be replaced by.

Three years later, Hobbs looked no different, but he had become much more serious, putting more effort into his work.

Since most adventurers had already gone out on missions, the guild was quite quiet, far less lively than usual.

After winning the championship in the three-year-old competition, the Rekxum Guild had become renowned, and as the top guild in the industry, they had the most commissions, but with the demon race's threats worsening, they were short-staffed and had to transfer work to other guilds to share the burden.

Old Taylor, the Guildmaster, stood with his hands on his back, leaning in close to Hobbs as he saw him marking many X symbols on the maps, and asked curiously, "Hobbs, what are you doing?"

"Me?" Hobbs scratched his itchy forehead with his quill, answering with a snort, "I'm marking all the locations and times when vampire attacks on humans occurred, and compiling all the information I've gathered."

Old Taylor, the Guildmaster, was a bit confused, but he believed that Hobbs, though careless at times, wouldn't do something meaningless in a critical moment, "Do you think this will reveal something?"

"Exactly, at least it can reveal the early action patterns of the vampires and their recent movements." Hobbs grinned, "I see, you're quite clever, Hobbs. If you can uncover the vampires' background, that would be great."

"I can only do my best, as my abilities are limited, and I can't know everything." Hobbs paused, self-deprecatingly, "Compared to other adventurers, I can only do this kind of behind-the-scenes work. Sometimes, I even envy other adventurers."

"Don't say that, your role is irreplaceable, at least that's what I think." Old Taylor, the Guildmaster, patted Hobbs' shoulder approvingly, "Your ability to gather intelligence is better than many adventurers. You can pull adventurers back from the brink of death unnoticed, and because of you, I've had less pressure managing the guild."

"Ha ha, flattered, Guildmaster." Hobbs smiled sheepishly, changing the subject, "Has Karl returned yet? He's been gone from the guild for one and a half years."

"No, he's been training in the harsh northern lands to hone his skills. If he hasn't made a qualitative leap, he probably won't be returning." Old Taylor, the Guildmaster, sighed.

"Karl and I are about the same age, but he's still like this, a person with boundless energy." Hobbs commented.

"The new members joining the guild are getting stronger one by one, I think he's not willing to give up easily, after all, he was once the top adventurer of the guild." Old Taylor, the Guildmaster, though he didn't say it out loud, he was very supportive of his son's efforts in cultivation.

"Don't you want to not lose to the current young people? Interesting." Hobbs shook his head.

"It's already late, and I don't know if Alice and Lucy will make it back? If not, you can go home to rest, you can continue working tomorrow. I heard your wife is very strict, and I don't want you to be embarrassed when you go back, you should spend more time with your daughter and wife." Old Taylor, the Guildmaster, smiled understandingly.

"That's okay, I'm used to it." Hobbs patted his knee meaningfully.

"By the way, I've only seen your daughter, but I've never seen your wife, we've known each other for so long, I always feel like something is missing, actually, you can take some time to bring your wife and daughter to my home for a family gathering." Old Taylor, the Guildmaster, extended an invitation for a family gathering.

Hobbs raised his eyebrows, became very hesitant and cautious, but still remained calm, "I can bring my daughter, but my wife probably can't."

"Why? Is there any difficulty? It's just a simple dinner." Old Taylor, the Guildmaster, asked confusedly.

"My wife is very shy, she becomes very tense and embarrassed when she sees strangers, family gatherings are such joyful things, but for her, it's a kind of torture, sorry." Hobbs politely declined.

"I see, I was being impertinent." Old Taylor, the Guildmaster, had to abandon the idea, and he didn't suspect anything either, as Hobbs had joined the Rekxum Guild only a few years before Alice.

As the sound of carriages approached the guild, Alice and Lucy finally arrived.

Old Taylor, the Guildmaster, immediately went up to greet them, asking, "How's the situation? Is it resolved?"

"Yes, there's no problem, the village only had three vampires, and their strength was weak." Alice answered truthfully.

"That's good, the appearance of vampires in the Rekxum region is not a small matter, Lord Austin has been very tense these days." Old Taylor, the Guildmaster, relaxed, secretly sighing in relief.

Lucy sat down on the chair shakily, then groaned and complained, "Grandpa, I don't want to go on a mission tomorrow, let me rest for a few days, I'm exhausted."

"What are you exhausted for? It's all Alice working hard, right?" Old Taylor frowned, thinking his granddaughter was too spoiled.

"Pfft!" Lucy scoffed, having experienced a taste of an adventurer's life today, she didn't want to experience it again, it was more comfortable being a display girl.

Alice walked over to Hobbs, asking quietly, "Hobbs, are there any results?"

Hobbs looked up, picked up the map marked on the table, and after examining it for a while, handed it to Alice, "There are some unexpected findings, take a look."

Alice took the map and examined it carefully, with the locations and times already marked, the results were clear, "The blood race is spreading from the east?"

"Exactly, I've collected all the information about the blood race attacking humans, and found that the vampires had already started their activities three years ago, initially only in some eastern regions, and it was three years later that they spread to our area." Hobbs lowered his head, drawing a conclusion, "It's clear that their purpose is not to slaughter humans, but to be searching for something, which is why they try to conceal their traces and hide among humans."

"Three years ago, and it's only now that it's revealed, what are these monsters conspiring for?" Old Taylor, the Guildmaster, thought deeply.

Alice stared at the map in her hands, her expression became serious, and she confirmed her thoughts, "It's true, the source of the calamity is Cain, he's searching for the original sinner, to reclaim the divine power, and complete the final transformation."

There will be two more updates! I will do my best! It's much faster to write with a computer nearby.

title: Chapter 7 — Gradually Clearing Up (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 7 — Gradually Clearing Up (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 37 · Chapter 7

Alice was basically certain that the massive appearance of vampires was directly related to Cain; she was searching for the other two blood clan progenitors. If Cain retrieved all the undying power and completed his final transformation, the devastation caused would be unprecedented—perhaps not smaller than Behemoth three years ago, and possibly even more severe. Alice frowned with worry, thinking of Merlin again; if he were by her side, she wouldn't be so anxious.

"What exactly are these monsters looking for? Going to such great lengths?" Old President Taylor was baffled.

"I'm not sure, but it must be something important, and they're worried about alerting the prey," Hobbs said in a speculative tone, continuing to pick up another map from the table and passing it over. "Alice, take a look at this; maybe you'll find something new."

"Another one?" Alice took the other map, noticing it marked locations of recent vampire attacks, densely circled with a black feather pen. "What does this mean? Hobbs, can you explain?"

"Can't you tell? This is good news," Hobbs said meaningfully, a mysterious smile on his face.

"Good news?" Alice looked at the map again. Every black circle represented human deaths—where was the good news in that?

"Exactly. I collected vampire attack incidents from the past six months, organized and investigated them uniformly. I discovered that the frequency of attacks in the Kingdom of Britain and some other regions is rapidly declining," Hobbs paused, then reasoned aloud. "This proves our previous estimate that things were worsening was wrong. On the contrary, the situation is improving. I speculate that within a year, the threat of vampires might completely vanish—though this is limited to Britain and a few nearby nations."

"Oh~" Lucia immediately stood up, her face beaming with joy and excitement. "This is good news! We can finally bid farewell to these busy, bitter days!"

"The vampire threat will just disappear naturally? That sounds a bit unreal. Do you think they'll leave on their own within a year?" Old President Taylor was concerned and hadn't lowered his guard.

"Vampires feed on human blood; they can't just leave easily. Hobbs, your speculation isn't rigorous," Alice thought the same, feeling vampires had no reasonable motive to voluntarily leave Britain and the surrounding regions.

"If vampires found what they were looking for, wouldn't it be normal to leave? Their goal was always to find something," Hobbs paused, speaking with full confidence. "Alice, look closely at the distribution of recent vampire attacks. Maybe you'll find the answer."

Alice lowered her head again, looking at the map in her hand, then widened her eyes, noticing something peculiar—
The places marked with black circles were densely clustered in one region: several nations led by the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
This map represented the distribution of recent vampire attacks, meaning the vampires were likely converging toward the Austro-Hungarian Empire's territory!
Alice's brows furrowed. She suspected whether the two blood clan progenitors Cain sought were hidden in that region led by the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
"Could it be that what the vampires are looking for is right there..."

"You're right. Recently, the number of vampires here has dropped rapidly, while the area around the Austro-Hungarian Empire has increased. Clearly, the vampires are all converging on the same place," Hobbs stood up, drained his cup of strong liquor, and drew his conclusion. "Perhaps the hunters have already found the snake's lair and are preparing a capture plan."

Alice lowered her head, looking at the map in her hand, her heart unsettled for a long time—
What had been said was all speculation; she couldn't fully confirm that the blood clan progenitors were hiding near the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
However, Hobbs's intelligence was valuable. Things were gradually becoming clear. Perhaps recently she needed to travel far and investigate carefully.

"Mom!"
