Little Chris scampered out from the landlady's house, her little carrot legs bouncing as she pounced into her mother's arms, rubbing her face nonstop.
With work temporarily wrapped up, Alice hurriedly took her adorable daughter home, wanting to spend more time with her in the evening.
For three years, the kind landlady had been helping take care of Chris. Every time Alice went out to work, she left her daughter with the landlady.
Alice didn't know why, but the landlady doted on Chris immensely. Anyone unaware of the truth would think Chris was the landlady's granddaughter without a single discordant note.
The love and care the landlady gave Chris rivaled Alice's own maternal love; she even proactively offered that if Alice was busy, she could always send Chris here.
Alice felt the landlady was old and had no other relatives nearby, so subconsciously she treated Chris as her own granddaughter. It was only natural.
A small female dog named "Flower" also burst out of the house, barking happily around Alice, circling her nonstop.

"Alice? You're back?" The landlady walked out of the house slowly, looking somewhat older than before, her back nearly too bent to straighten. Seeing Alice return, her face was filled with smiles.

"I just got back too. Sorry to trouble you again with watching Chris." Alice held her daughter, her eyes full of apology.

"No trouble at all. I live alone, and having Chris keep me company is a good thing—she's brought much joy to my boring life." The landlady indeed hoped Chris could keep living here.

"Hasn't she caused you any trouble? After all, she's been quite disobedient at home." Alice asked curiously, a bit worried that her daughter might let loose when she wasn't around.

"Mmm!" The little girl looked up, pouting. "Chris is very well-behaved! She wouldn't cause trouble anywhere! Hmph~!"

"Ha ha, Alice, you're overthinking it. Chris is a very well-behaved girl." The landlady dispelled Alice's doubts.

"Good." Alice sighed in relief, scowling at Chris. "You really make me worry. At home you're always going against me."

"I didn't do it!" Chris made a face, burying her head in her mother's chest, huffing.

"Alice, was your work smooth today? No trouble?" the landlady asked curiously.

"Nothing wrong, everything went smoothly. It's just that the situation is complicated now—vampires haven't been completely eradicated. If you don't have to go out tonight, please don't wander around casually to avoid danger." Alice earnestly warned.

"I'm just an old woman about to be buried. Getting targeted by vampires? How honored." The landlady laughed. If she wasn't afraid of the Demon Lord, what was there to fear from vampires?

"You're joking. Better safe than sorry." Alice warned again.

"I know. But Alice, your face looks more tired than usual. Is it really stressful without Mr. Merlin around?" The landlady's eyes showed concern.

"A... a little." Alice answered awkwardly.

"If I'm not mistaken, Mr. Merlin left over three years ago, right? Why hasn't he come back? Did something happen?" The landlady asked tactfully.

Alice's expression grew melancholy. She lowered her head, wanting to speak but stopping. It really wasn't convenient to say. She didn't know how to answer—

Not only had Merlin not returned, but in three years, not even a single letter.

Alice had no idea about Merlin's situation among the demons, nor what he had gone through.

Even...
She didn't know if the words the fairies brought back were true.

title: Chapter 8 — All-Around Enhancement (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 8 — All-Around Enhancement (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 37 · Chapter 8

Three years felt incredibly long to Alice, enough to wear away anyone's patience completely.

Late at night, Alice would occasionally wonder if Merlin would never come back.

Alice was unwilling to believe such a thing; even if she had to deceive herself, she would firmly believe that Merlin would definitely return to her and their daughter's side, and would not leave so easily.

Alice hesitated for a while, then could only dispel the landlady's doubts by lying.

"Merlin's hometown had some problems, and dealing with them would be troublesome, so it would take a long time."

"Has Mr. Merlin written to you?" the landlady pressed on.

"Of course he has. He sends letters home every month, so he might be back soon." Alice's smile was very strained.

"Well, that's good. Actually, being apart for so long isn't good for a couple; their feelings might develop problems." The landlady spoke with the tone of someone who had been through it before.

"It won't be. Our feelings..." Alice thought for a moment and answered with certainty—"

"It's not that fragile. This separation is only temporary."

"Merlin will come back. He promised me."

Night fell, the bright moon hung high, and the starry dots lit the path home.

Alice held her adorable daughter, preparing to return home and let the little one rest well for a few days.

Chris seemed to be playing with her little friends today, her small mouth talking nonstop about some amusing anecdotes.

However, Alice was somewhat distracted, because she had been thinking about Merlin lately, causing her mood to be very unstable.

Alice's mind was full of the landlady's words just now—long separation causing problems in feelings? That wasn't without reason.

After all, people change constantly, old friends around her were changing too, so what about Merlin?

Would three years have changed Merlin's mindset, made him change his mind about returning, and choose to stay among the demon race forever?

Alice couldn't get an answer, so she could only passively believe Merlin wouldn't lie to her—there must be a reason he couldn't come back.

"Big Sister Mimi has been so annoying lately. She's grown so tall, taller than me by a head. Now she calls me a shorty every day. If I don't grow a bit more, she won't play with me. Hmph!"

Little Chris lay in her mother's arms, constantly complaining about her little friends, especially complaining about her height, because the other friends had all grown so much, while she had no change at all.

"Is that so?"

Alice lowered her head, looking at her daughter, thinking that Chris had indeed shown no change over three years, no physical growth—this might be related to her origins. After all, she wasn't pure human; she had half demon blood.

As everyone knew, demons, though inferior to elves, also had long lifespans far exceeding humans. Three years was very long for humans, but for demons it was still very brief.

This was probably the reason for Chris's slow growth. One couldn't measure by human age; one had to look at demon age. The little one was still in infancy; it would take two hundred years to become an adult.

"Don't worry about such things. You'll grow up eventually, but not now."

"Really? Then I'm relieved. I'm so envious of Big Sister Mimi, she can grow so tall~" After receiving her mother's comfort, Chris's mood improved a lot, but her expression was still somewhat sad. "Mom, I miss Dad a bit. When will he come back?"

Alice's delicate body trembled; she had to stop walking and look at her daughter in her arms. She had deceived Chris countless times already, and she no longer knew how to explain to her daughter—

This time, Alice had no answer at all, not even a comforting lie.

Late at night, Chris fell asleep to her mother's story.

Alice put down the storybook, covered her daughter with a blanket, extinguished the oil lamp, then her stomach led her to the study, where she picked up a pen and letter paper.

She wasn't writing to Merlin, because in demon territory, letters were almost impossible to deliver unless there was other contact.

Alice hoped to numb herself with work, temporarily forgetting the impact of Merlin's departure. She had always done this.

Regarding the vampires, Alice couldn't put it out of her mind. She worried that one day it might escalate into a massive disaster, threatening everyone's safety.

Alice still remembered Cain's appearance. That harmless little girl had nearly killed her; the danger level was no less than facing Behemoth directly.

After obtaining Hobbs's intelligence, Alice judged that the current situation was no longer something adventurers could interfere with casually, but required nations to unite and prepare in advance.

If things went well, perhaps they could strangle the disaster in the cradle, avoiding a completely uncontrollable situation.

Fortunately, Alice wasn't just a Purple-Gold adventurer; she was also a foreign Thorn Knight, able to communicate directly with the royal family, possessing a certain authority.

Alice intended to write directly to Queen Elizabeth, telling her about Cain, the vampire secret, and Hobbs's analysis—all to the Queen.

Having Queen Elizabeth personally contact the Austro-Hungarian Empire, informing them of the impending danger and preparing in advance.

If circumstances allowed, Alice wanted to assist the knights of the Austro-Hungarian Empire in exterminating the vampires, preventing the disaster from happening.

However, things probably weren't that simple, because greed was endless.

Deep within the Demon City in the Sand Sea, the deepest part of the Seventh Demon Lord Palace.

The surroundings were dimly lit; only a beam of light from the dome shone on the pitch-black demon.

This was the confinement room. The surrounding walls were solid black gold; escaping from here wasn't easy—

Merlin had been isolated from the world for three years, not taking a single step out. He had always been trying to control the demon blood within, avoiding his consciousness being swallowed, becoming a machine that only knew how to kill.

This was something Merlin asked for himself. He didn't want to accidentally hurt his companions. Vivian and Lilith would visit him once a week through the door crack to check his condition.

After three years of effort in darkness, Merlin finally had gains. He began to reclaim control of his body and conquer the demon god blood, making it his own.

In his demon form, Merlin's powerful body trembled. Dense vascular patterns on his skin lit up instantly, gradually fading the pitch-black appearance. The demon god blood gathered entirely at the shocking scar on his chest and was sealed away.

Merlin, back to his normal appearance, had his eyelids tremble slightly. He suddenly opened his eyes, his gaze like scorching flames, flashing the light of clear red rubies. The intense fluctuation blew away the surrounding dust!

After Behemoth's death, Merlin inherited the demon god's power. He not only became the new demon god but also received comprehensive benefits—

Merlin's already formidable body was strengthened again by the demon god blood!

He could even control his demon form and demon god power at will, like a normal demon!

The Earth Spirit within him was also enhanced by the demon god blood's nourishment, and gravity magic climbed to its peak!

Most importantly, regarding Merlin's own curse. Though not completely shaken off, under the effect of demon god blood, the curse was greatly alleviated.

Previously, Merlin needed to constantly slay Saint-tier and above powerhouses to guarantee the curse wouldn't activate for a period.

But now Merlin didn't need to search for prey so urgently. Seizing the life force of one Saint-tier powerhouse was enough to keep him safe for half a year without harm.

This was the power of demon god blood. It wouldn't let its master, Merlin, be easily threatened, strengthening the life force he desperately needed!

title: Chapter 9 — Face to Face
content:
Chapter 9 — Face to Face

Volume 37 · Chapter 9

The sky was overcast with dark clouds. In the cemetery of the Demon City, Merlin stood alone, gazing at the tombstones of demons who had perished in Behemoth's turmoil.

Besides Beelzebub and Leviathan, two Demon Lords, there were many other demons: Miranda, Blackman, Dru, Podom.

Merlin stood among the rows of tombstones, looking at each familiar name, filled with regret and even self-reproach.

That so many companions could perish in Behemoth's turmoil was something Merlin had not anticipated; to rescue the monarch sealed within the Demon-Sealing Flask, nearly all demons had gambled their lives.

The demons who survived were truly fortunate; many had fallen during the turmoil. The demon race's losses in this war were second only to the devastating Holy War of old.

Fortunately, Vivian and Pope Gioegen had reached a private agreement, granting the demon race breathing room in the Sand Sea, time to develop and recover their strength.

Gioegen was not a man of his word, but the Church had suffered no less, losing many of its prized trump cards; to regroup, it was unsuited to wage war on the demon race again.

The Holy Church had governed diligently over these three years, constantly expanding its scale, recruiting powerful figures as believers and inducting them into the Temple Knights, recovering some of its losses.

Yet the demon race was not so fortunate; demons grew far slower than humans, requiring two hundred years to cultivate an adult demon, consuming even more energy.

Fortunately, the remnant demon race could rely on the Sand Sea's natural barrier to resist the vast majority of scheming humans; without large-scale extermination campaigns, they would be hard-pressed to pose a threat.

With Behemoth destroyed, the seven Demon Lord Palaces had lost their purpose, and the demon race underwent large-scale integration, forming a completely unified front.

With Vivian as the new leader of the demon race and the other Demon Lords as vice-leaders, a new hierarchical system with clear class distinctions emerged, making the Demon City its sole stronghold.

As the only Divine Realm cultivator, Vivian's elevation to leader was only natural given the demon race's reverence for strength; the remaining Demon Lords had no objections.

Even Samael hoped Vivian would shoulder the heavy burden of reviving the demon race like Belial once had, freeing it from the predicament of being besieged on all sides.

The situation the demon race faced now was hardly better than after the Holy War; Vivian's shoulders bore a heavy burden, and she spent less time with Merlin and Lilith than before.

Merlin averted his gaze and looked up at the gloomy sky, unable to describe the taste in his heart, especially upon learning he had killed three loyal subordinates; a sense of guilt welled up within him.

"Sorry, I didn't expect things to turn out this way. Truly, I am unsuited to be Demon Lord; I cannot place the collective interest above all else. Honestly, haven't you all always thought I was incompetent?"

"No need to apologize. They weren't killed by you; Behemoth manipulated you." Asmodeus strolled over, stopping beside Merlin, a meaningful smile on his face as he scanned the names on the tombstones. "So you're here. Had me searching for you for a good..."

"Anything wrong?" Merlin asked curiously.

"Nothing much. Just came to see an old friend. You've been in solitary confinement for three years without showing your face, so I came to check on you." Asmodeus looked at Merlin.

"What's there to see? Still the same as always." Merlin spread his hands.

"Heard you've controlled the Demon God Blood? How do you feel now?" Asmodeus examined Merlin's body, indeed restored to his original appearance.

"Fair enough." Merlin touched the top of his head with a helpless expression. "I can't fully recover to how I was before. Small horns have grown on my head and won't recede. Though hidden by my hair they're not obvious, but they feel weird."

"You'll get used to it eventually. After all, you're a demon at heart; it'd be strange not to have horns, wouldn't it?" Asmodeus teased.

"True enough. I just can't get used to having two lumps on my head." Merlin felt that after being transformed by the Demon God Blood, his demonic aura was now very pronounced; his originally thin demonic bloodline had evolved.

"You came here just to look at the dead subordinates?" Asmodeus looked at the tombstones again.

"Mm, I feel a bit guilty." Merlin said with a complex tone.

"After being controlled by Behemoth, I killed many old subordinates too, even Samael." Asmodeus paused, speaking seriously. "But it doesn't concern us. The lucky ones who live must keep moving forward and not bear this meaningless pressure. They didn't die for us, but for the survival of the entire demon race, just like in the Holy War before, when demons fell batch after batch beneath the blades of the Holy Spirits, forming walls of corpses to guard the Demon Lord Palaces."

"I understand your reasoning, yet I still feel ashamed for my incompetence." Merlin replied softly.

"Heh, hearing your tone..." Asmodeus chuckled dryly and asked in a low voice, "Are you planning to leave?"

Merlin hesitated. Now that the Demon God Blood was controlled, it was time to leave—to see Alice and his daughter. He had indeed thought of this, so he nodded. "That's right."

"What a pity. I held a sliver of hope, thinking you'd cut ties with humans and return completely. Looks like I overestimated you." Asmodeus lowered his head and patted Merlin's shoulder—

"I can only wish you luck, Merlin."

In the study of the Demon Lord Palace, Orobas, son of Belial, held a paintbrush, recording the scenery outside on his canvas. His completely absorbed demeanor, as if dedicating himself entirely to art, made him oblivious to everything around him.

Though Orobas had once been Behemoth's accomplice, it was because he had been deceived, not by his own intent.

Thus Orobas was forgiven among the demon race. Vivian did not mistreat him, even granting him monarch-level treatment.

Now the demon race was short on soldiers and officers. Plus, Orobas was Belial's son and could take over Belial's old followers; it would be foolish to settle old scores later.

Furthermore, Orobas was the rightful heir of the Demon City. With Vivian as leader of the entire demon race, she needed his support.

Orobas's paintbrush suddenly stopped. Sensing an overwhelmingly oppressive aura, he turned sharply and saw Merlin leaning against the corner, staring at him with an emotionless gaze.

"Is that you?!"

"Me." Merlin nodded, then asked in a meaningful tone—

"Aren't you the traveling fortune-teller? Why are you interested in painting too?"

title: Chapter 10 — Passing the Message (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 10 — Passing the Message (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 37 · Chapter 10

"How long have you been here?" Orobas thought uneasily, unsure how long Merlin had been watching from behind.

"For a while. Seeing you so absorbed in your painting, I didn't dare to disturb you." Merlin answered truthfully.

"Eh?"

Orobas stared in astonishment, widening his eyes. He knew the studio door was closed and only one window was open, so there was no way to tell how Merlin had gotten in.

Moreover, Orobas was fairly confident in his senses; he hadn't detected Merlin standing behind him all that time, which was rather terrifying. If the person who came in was an assassin, Orobas might die without ever knowing why.

Orobas felt a chill down his spine and cold sweat breaking out on his forehead. Confused by Merlin's intentions, his heart was extremely uneasy.

"You... came to find me for what?"

"Nothing, just wanted to chat with you." Merlin looked at Orobas without approaching. "I didn't expect you to be Beelzebub's son. At first I really thought you were a traveling fortune-teller; you had no trace of demonic aura at all."

"I'm sorry to have deceived you. I was carrying out my father's... no, Behemoth's orders, to investigate your situation in the human realm so I could strike you down at the Seven Kings' meeting." Orobas hid nothing and confessed what had happened.

"I see. You've caused me quite a bit of trouble; I was almost doomed forever." Merlin narrowed his eyes, still clearly angry.

"That wasn't my intention. I had no courage to defy my father's orders, even if he was a false father." Orobas lowered his head, speaking with shame. "Are you here to kill me? That's only right. I've committed an unforgivable error and deserve the harshest punishment. To still be alive is truly a miracle.

"I do intend to. I very much want to kill you, to vent my resentment. If not for you, perhaps Behemoth's matter wouldn't have turned into the worst outcome, and my subordinates wouldn't have died for me." Merlin's tone turned icy, his killing intent toward Orobas obvious.

"As expected. I can't be forgiven; I don't deserve it." Orobas slowly closed his eyes. He had no confidence of defeating this opponent who had killed Behemoth; Merlin's power completely overwhelmed him, and he hadn't even noticed Merlin sneaking into the studio all that time.

"However, you were deceived, and you've come back in the end. Now it seems, your mistake was naivety—willingly trusting your father unconditionally. That's foolish." Merlin paused, then spoke in a heavy voice. "Now the demon race needs to recover its strength; it's unsuitable for more sacrifices. I very much need your assistance. My subordinates have already sacrificed their lives for the demon race. If I kill you, their deaths will have been meaningless."

"Your experience and that of your subordinates makes me feel ashamed. I know my apologies are useless, but I hope to be forgiven." Orobas frowned, speaking in a low voice. "I don't fear death; I fear dying for having made a mistake. I was strictly educated by my father since childhood. Making mistakes is something I cannot tolerate.

"Too pathetic. Your father isn't necessarily right; he once reflected on himself too." Merlin recalled Beelzebub imprisoned in the Sin Domain, pitifully reflecting on himself only at the end of his life.

"Ha, impossible. My father is emotionally cold and wants to control everything; he would never reflect on his own mistakes. Since childhood, I couldn't express my thoughts; only by obeying my father completely would I gain recognition. Behemoth deepened his control over me, turning me into a tool that had abandoned thinking." Orobas's smile was ugly; his large single eye dared not look directly at Merlin.

"Actually, I've seen your father's soul." Merlin said suddenly.

"Impossible? You're joking, right?" Orobas looked up in astonishment, thinking Merlin was making fun of him.

"I'm not joking. Your father's soul wasn't erased by Behemoth; it was imprisoned in the Sin Domain. After I was thrown in there, I found it." Merlin explained calmly.

"Is that so?" Orobas was somewhat bewildered. He knew what the Sin Domain was, but hadn't expected his father's soul to have been imprisoned inside all along.

"Before your father's soul dispersed, he asked me to pass on a few words to you." Merlin took a deep breath and organized his words—

"He says he's willing to give you freedom. If you're willing to stay with the demon race, inherit everything of his.

"If you want to leave, he won't stop you; he allows you to seek the life you want."

"Freedom is the most precious gift he could offer. Which will you choose?"

Orobas's body trembled visibly; his eye rims turned red, sadness spreading across his face, his mind going blank.

He couldn't imagine these words coming from that strict father; they were completely out of character.

Orobas lowered his head, his mood in chaos. For a moment he forgot how to answer Merlin's question, standing there dumbly.

"I don't know..."

Merlin shook his head and turned to leave, leaving Orobas alone here. He thought this guy needed quiet.

He could tell Orobas was a man without much will of his own; most of the time he needed others to help him decide.

This flaw was fatal and had led to Behemoth's matter turning bad.

But this was Orobas's own business; Merlin didn't want to interfere with his thoughts, leaving it all to how Orobas decided.

"Merlin!" Orobas called out to Merlin, walking up slowly. "Are you leaving?"

"How did you know? Divination?" Merlin's tone was sarcastic, though he wondered how everyone knew when I myself had never publicly stated it.

"Not divination. Your leaving is something many demons are clear about; it's no secret. The moment you stepped out of the isolation chamber, everyone understood." Orobas explained calmly, because Merlin hadn't been able to leave before only because his demon blood was unstable and threatened those around him. Now the Demon God blood was controlled, and nothing could restrict Merlin anymore.

"I see. Yes, I'm leaving. The demon race has no immediate danger; what's needed is steady management. Developing farmland isn't something I'm good at; I can't provide any help." Merlin shook his head, feeling staying was a waste of time. He'd rather go back to see

title: Chapter 11 — The Title: Working for a Living, It's Not Embarrassing (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 11 — The Title: Working for a Living, It's Not Embarrassing (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 37 · Chapter 11

The Light Dragon of the Vatican, originally a guardian soaring above the temple, was devoutly worshipped by the faithful.

Even within the Church, Aweis held a unique status, hailed as a sacred beast that had submitted to the great Goddess of Light.

In truth, Aweis's standing among dragons was merely average, far from the mighty reputation spoken of in rumors.

This was similar to the Ice Dragon Marixun, both noble dragons who craved pleasure and abandoned their kind to accept offerings from weak humans.

After all, Aweis had no voice among dragons and had to endure the hot-tempered Flame Dragon King, carrying out its orders.

Why not leave the dragon clan and join the Church instead? Every day people would bring food and drink, and countless would kneel before it in reverence.

The work wasn't hard either—just fly into the sky, occasionally let out a roar, let the believers feel its draconic majesty, and scare them into kneeling motionless.

Although this life was boring, it was comfortable! Aweis understood well the saying "better a rooster among hens than a phoenix among dogs"—with food and shelter secured, why serve the Flame Dragon King?

Unfortunately, that lifestyle ended on a certain day. The Light Dragon Aweis suffered a crushing defeat at the First Demon Lord Palace and has never escaped since.

It was when Merlin had just ascended to the position of Demon Lord. The Church, like it had been injected with chicken blood, and Geigen heard that the new Demon Lord was just a minor demon he could have killed anytime—his confidence soared!

So he organized a subjugation force, placing the Light Dragon Aweis at the forefront, planning to recapture the First Demon Lord Palace and uncover all the demons' secrets.

The last time they had taken the Demon Lord Palace, they held it only briefly before other Demon Lords arrived to reinforce, and they had no choice but to retreat quickly.

This had always been Geigen's regret—he couldn't uncover more secrets. But this sudden opportunity made him reckless.

Unfortunately, the subjugation force failed spectacularly. Aweis was beaten black and blue by the newly appointed Demon Lord Merlin, kneeling in the dirt begging for mercy, until finally its wings were severed and it was locked away behind the blood pool seal.

The sacred dragon that once circled above the temple, receiving countless bows and worship, was now locked away in the First Demon Lord Palace as a guard dog—an ironic twist that made people sigh.

This was a disgrace to the proud Light Dragon Aweis. Its self-confidence was dealt a heavy blow, and it seemed nothing in the higher dragon clan was more pitiable than it.

Three years ago, due to the chaos stirred up by Bismuth, the demons abandoned the Demon Lord Palace and made the Demon City their final home. Aweis, who had been watching over the blood pool seal, was transferred here as well.

However, an awkward situation arose—Aweis had become completely useless. It used to guard the blood pool seal, but now Bismuth was dead and there was no need to guard it anymore.

Right, poor Aweis had been a guard dog for so many years, and even it didn't know the way out—it faced unemployment.

Aweis's pride was struck again. Not only had it failed to be the Church's sacred beast, now it couldn't even be a guard dog—this was the heavens mocking it!

After all, it was a proud sacred dragon, a higher-class dragon. How could it fall to such a state of unemployment?

Aweis felt a bit afraid, because it clearly understood its situation. If it was no longer useful, then it was a question of life and death—the demons wouldn't keep a useless mouth to feed.

Recently, Aweis had overheard some conversations from the food-delivery demons, which filled it with dread.

Demon A: "What use is this big lizard? It eats so much—ten pigs a day! Who can afford to feed it? It's just a useless mouth!"

Demon B: "Demon City is short on supplies, we can't afford it. But we could fatten it up like a pig—plump and round. Just wonder how dragon meat tastes."

These words from the demons caused Aweis to go without sleep for three days and nights, afraid that it would wake up in a cooking pot. It stopped eating, hoping that if it grew thin enough, it might escape death.

The Light Dragon Aweis curled up in the dark cave, bound in chains. Although its white wings behind it had grown back, this atmosphere made its spirit even more tense, often letting out mournful cries, lamenting the injustice of fate.

Footsteps echoed, and Aweis suddenly opened its golden eyes, quickly sitting up to make itself appear stronger, hoping to instill fear in the demons and deter them from making advances—like a cobra hissing at its enemies.

But upon closer inspection, it was not the usual food-delivery demon, but the terrifying figure that had awakened it from countless nightmares—the Third Demon Lord, Merlin!

Aweis's pupils constricted sharply, trembling with fear. The tiny Merlin exerted a terrifying pressure, making its speech incoherent.

"Y-you...!"

"Long time no see. I thought you were already dead. I have to admit, your vitality is truly stubborn."

Merlin wore a mocking smile, finding this big lizard quite amusing.

"Shh!?" Aweis felt insulted, suppressing its fear and putting on the air of a mighty dragon, "Hmph! You lowly Demon Lord, have you come to mock me? Although my body is enslaved by you, my heart and soul remain free. You can never fully conquer me, and you'll never make me surrender under pressure!"

"If you hadn't been obediently guarding the blood pool seal all these years, eating so happily every day, I might have almost believed you were a dragon with backbone. Too bad, you're not. I know you well." Merlin shrugged, having long seen through Aweis's adaptable nature—facing any adversity, it always adapted quickly, truly a carefree type.

"How ridiculous! Dragons eat iron and drink steel—one meal without food won't starve them. My appetite is so good because I'm building up strength, preparing for the day I defeat you and reclaim my dignity!" Aweis snorted, its body honest but its mouth never yielding, after all, it was a proud dragon with limits.

"Is that so? Then you'd better work hard." Merlin didn't take Aweis seriously at all, since Saint-tier beings were simply too weak for him. "I'm here for other business anyway, and I need your help."

"Ah ha~ Did I hear that right? The almighty Demon Lord who looks down on everyone needs my help?" Aweis puffed up its head, forgetting its slave status, "As a generous, beautiful, and proud dragon, I'll reluctantly listen."

"I need a dog—one of those cute, obedient ones that children love. You should be able to transform into that, right?" Merlin asked tentatively.

"Ah...?!"

Aweis was struck as if by lightning, frozen in place. A million wild horses galloped through its mind, trampling its pride back and forth.

Another dog?! I'm a great sacred dragon! How could I...

Wait!

It seems I could agree to this condition and follow Lucifer the Third, that way I won't be eaten by the demons.

After all, the cruel demons can't tolerate this useless guy like me. Better to seize this opportunity and leave.

No! How could I bow to the evil Demon Lord? I'm a proud dragon! My ancestors' honor won't allow me to agree to such a disgraceful thing!

Aweis's face darkened immediately, its golden eyes filled with rage, almost spewing fire that would drown Merlin.

"You lowly Demon Lord, is trampling on my dignity amusing to you? I am one of the noble sacred dragons! You can kill me, but you cannot humiliate me! Even if you put a knife to my throat, I will never agree to this unreasonable demand!"

Merlin drew the demon sword Banri Garan from his waist, pressing it directly against Aweis's throat, then tilted his head, "Hmm?"

"Tell me, what breed do you want? Small, medium, or large? Whatever form you like, I can become it, hehe~"

(*￣3￣)╭(╥╥)╭─╣─╣─╝～

title: Chapter 12 — New Journey
content:
Chapter 12 — New Journey

Volume 37 · Chapter 12

The next day, Merlin was in his room, wiping down the demon sword Banri Garan, making final preparations before his departure.
He spent the whole night organizing his gear, planning to set off early the next morning and leave Demon City.
Thinking that he would soon see Alice and his adorable daughter, Merlin couldn't sleep all night, his heart full of anticipation.
Banri Garan had returned to its former appearance: a red scabbard, the blade full of nicks and rust, losing much of its former killing intent.
This weapon left by the prophet had not degraded; instead, it changed with Merlin's condition.
Only when Merlin invoked the demon god's blood would Banri Garan's latent power be reawakened, restoring it to a pitch‑black, sharp state.
This was a good thing for Merlin, after all, in the Behemoth incident many people had already seen Banri Garan's true
appearance, and if he swaggered about with it, it might cause unnecessary trouble.
Merlin put down the handkerchief, looked at the spotless Banri Garan, nodded satisfied, then picked up his pack and slung it on his back,
and kicked the husky lying on the ground with his foot.
"Aweis, that's enough, let's set off."
"Huh? You're leaving already?"
The holy dragon Aweis had already transformed into a husky; outwardly a goofy large dog, inwardly a proud dragon.
Following Merlin out of Demon City, this place of right and wrong, Aweis felt this was the best choice at present, allowing him to continue living.
Otherwise, the useless Aweis would inevitably provoke other demons' displeasure and might even become their meal.
Although staying by Merlin's side lacked dignity, it was still far better than dying here.
Moreover, Aweis had been captive of the demons for so long that returning to the church was nearly impossible, and Pope Jiogen would not trust him.
Wanting to restore the life once worshipped by countless people is virtually impossible.
For the dragon race it's even more impossible—beating Aweis to death wouldn't let him go back, and he'd have to endure the temperamental Blaze Dragon King, which is worse than death.
It would be agonizing.
Aweis could also be considered a pragmatic fellow; following Merlin might not be bad, at least he'd have a sturdy thigh to cling to.
"You're a demon lord, yet you're mingling in human lands so openly—really, is that alright?"
"I've lived in human lands before, basically no problem, don't worry."
Merlin glanced at the pseudo‑artifact silver bracelet on his wrist, a gift from Europa, which has the effect of masking his aura.
Even if his demonic aura is strong now, as long as he constantly wears this, it's hard for people to notice his demonic identity.
After all, without this silver bracelet the effect is powerful enough to deceive even Merlin, and it's what allows Europa to walk in human lands.
as his reliance.
"You've always lived in human territory?" Aweis wore a husky‑like foolish expression, his heart startled— a demon lord mingling among humans, is that any different from a tiger hiding among sheep? Fortunately he wasn't discovered, otherwise the human lands would have been scared to death.
"Exactly, what's the problem? Can't I live in human lands?" Merlin looked down on Aweis, questioning him from a superior position.
"I didn't mean it that way," Aweis said, a cold sweat beading on his forehead, muttering, "Demons are humanity's enemies—I have to admire your courage; if discovered, the consequences would be unimaginable."
"Wouldn't it be better to keep a low profile? In human lands I'm just a miserable wage slave." Merlin spread his hands, speaking self‑deprecatingly.
Aweis trembled all over, thinking that a mighty demon lord was actually a wage slave—this was shocking; he had already sunk low, and he hadn't expected
"Cough... uh, you made me look like this—what exactly are you planning to do?"
"You'll find out soon enough," Merlin replied mysteriously, unwilling to tell Aweis now.
Actually Merlin was thinking of bringing a gift back for his daughter, because Chris often mentioned the landlady's dog and was enthusiastic about pets like cats and dogs.
So Merlin planned to give his daughter a pet; after three years apart, showing up empty‑handed wouldn't do, and he felt he, as a father, ought to do something.
He chose Aweis because the fellow is easy to control, has no ill intentions, and his strength is passable; besides being a pet, he could also serve as a bodyguard.
In that light, the holy dragon Aweis is indeed the best companion for Chris; he never imagined that leaving Demon City would be jumping from one pit into an even deeper one, and the proud holy dragon would become the little one's dragon nanny.
In Aweis's husky eyes lay suspicion, his fur bristling with tension, his heart uneasy—
Is it really that mysterious?
I have a feeling this isn't going to be good.
I hope I haven't boarded a thief's ship.
Merlin spent last night talking at length with his mother Vivian, making his stance and thoughts clear.
Although Vivian tried to stop him, she couldn't change Merlin's resolve and had to reluctantly agree.
Vivian well knew that Merlin was no longer the little puppet she once pushed around; he now had his own thoughts and was hard to fully obey.
Besides feeling deep regret, Vivian had to accept this reality and had already made preparations.
As a mother, how could Vivian not see it? Merlin's heart was no longer among the demons; he yearned for a new life.
Vivian thought that since she couldn't stop this, she might as well go along and fulfill Merlin's wish.
Merlin isn't abandoning the demon race or giving up his demonic identity; he simply wants to leave Demon City and return to his small family—this is only natural, and Vivian had promised him three years ago that once he could control the demon god's blood, she would let him go.
Outside Demon City, Merlin shouldered his luggage, brought the husky, and bade a final farewell to the demons who had come to see him off.
"If you run into any troublesome trouble, let me know; no matter how far, I'll rush back as fast as I can."
"With me around there's nothing to worry about; when you're out there, take good care of yourself," Vivian said earnestly.
"I know,"
Merlin watched Vivian, words on the tip of her tongue but unspoken; as a transmigrator he always felt a distance with this mother, unsure how to broach the subject.
But one thing is certain: Merlin feels deep gratitude toward Vivian; without her care he could not have survived in this perilous other world.
"If you're going to say something mushy, just forget it—I can't stand it, you know I'm not a gentle mother." Vivian smiled, speaking solemnly, "I know you'll leave sooner or later; this is something every mother experiences. You don't need any psychological burden; as long as you're happy, I'll be satisfied."
Merlin lowered his head, remained silent for a long while, then said, "Thank you for your understanding."
"Hurry up, or Lilith will come after you, insisting on coming along—do you want me to become a lonely widow?"
"Please take care."
Merlin nodded, gave Vivian a slight bow, then took Aweis—now in husky form—by the leash and stepped into the vast desert, beginning his new journey.

title: Chapter 13 — Meeting (Bonus)
content:
Chapter 13 — Meeting (Bonus)

Volume 37 · Chapter 13

Watching Merlin's retreating figure, Vivian sighed, feeling an emptiness inside her chest, as though something important had been lost.

But she understood that once children grew up, they always had to leave their parents and venture out into the world on their own. It was an unavoidable thing.

Abaddon had been standing quietly by her side the whole time. Seeing Merlin leave, he couldn't help but ask softly, "Your Majesty, is this really for the best? Allowing Prince Merlin to leave may not be a good thing. With him here, we would be more than enough to handle every danger."

"This is unavoidable. Do you want me to make Merlin give up his wife and child? I cannot do that." Vivian paused before continuing, "Besides, Merlin doesn't have to stay away forever."

"But Prince Merlin is a power capable of defeating the Ancient Gods. It's not wise for him to get too close to humans. As your heir, you should put the interests of the demon race first." Abaddon disagreed, thinking that having Merlin stay was the best outcome. As for that child born to a human, it was hardly worth worrying about.

"I believe there's nothing I say that could make Merlin stay. So don't waste your efforts." Vivian spoke with deep meaning.

"Why? If you were a little firmer in your attitude, perhaps—" Abaddon hesitated mid-sentence.

"Haven't I told you about the third prophecy of the Prophet?" Vivian asked her subordinate.

"That's right, you only told me the first two prophecies." Abaddon nodded.

"Because the content of the third prophecy is quite strange and doesn't seem particularly significant, it's easy to overlook. However, its contents are related to Merlin's future fate." Vivian lowered her voice.

"Oh? It's related to the Prince's fate?" Abaddon frowned in surprise, disbelief clearly written across his aged face.

"The third prophecy states that the Child of Prophecy will leave the demon race, and nothing can stop—" Vivian spoke in the calmest possible tone, finishing the Prophet's final prophecy.

"What?!" Abaddon's eyes widened in shock, his mind unable to calm down for a long time. He increasingly felt that the demon race's Prophet was some kind of monstrous existence — capable of seeing even futures like this! Such precise prophecy made people wonder if the Prophet could see everyone's destiny.

"That is why I choose to believe the Prophet and not interfere excessively with Merlin's choices. The Prophet's prophecies are all considered with the demon race's future in mind. Perhaps Merlin leaving here is not necessarily a bad thing." Vivian said firmly.

Abaddon fell silent and said nothing more. He too was willing to believe the Prophet's words. After all, the demon race's escape from Behemot's claws had been due to these surviving prophecies.

"Brother! Wait for me! I want to go with you!" Lilith had just learned that Merlin was leaving and immediately stamped her foot in anxiety. She quickly packed her luggage and rushed over, wanting to go with Merlin.

Vivian facepalmed, feeling a headache coming on. She reached out and grabbed Lilith, saying sternly, "You cannot go. Stay obediently in Demon Castle."

"Why?! I want to go with Brother!" Lilith pouted resentfully. Living with her domineering mother every day, she had long grown tired of it.

"Because your strength doesn't qualify you to leave Demon Castle. Once you break through the Saint-tier, I'll consider it." Vivian gave her daughter an empty promise.

"Tch!" Lilith bit her nails, her frustration reaching its peak.

How come! I refuse to accept this!

Thinking about my brother getting cozy with that despicable human woman makes me too angry to sleep!

No way! I'm leaving Demon Castle too!

Within the British Royal Palace, Queen Elizabeth had already received a letter from Alice, learning everything about the Vampire Clan and the current dangerous situation.

Queen Elizabeth promptly contacted the Emperor of Austria-Hungary that night, summoning the royal guard knight Dais to prepare for subtly probing into the matter.

Leading Dais through the palace corridors, Mesfield headed toward the conference room to meet Queen Elizabeth directly.

*Cough cough.* Dais coughed violently from time to time, his face pale and bloodless, looking utterly frail.

Mesfield cast him a worried glance, half-feeling Dais would cough up his lungs. "Are you alright, Sir Dais?"

"I'm fine. This is just an old problem, nothing to be surprised about."

Dais managed a faint smile. For three years, his health had been steadily worsening. He often coughed throughout the night and couldn't sleep. At one point, he had even felt his days were numbered.

Fortunately, the empire had been secretly researching vampires with Countess Báthory's help, and there had been some progress. Perhaps it could improve Dais' precarious condition.

That was probably Dais' only hope for survival. Otherwise, with his current state, he wouldn't last long.

"An old problem? Sir's health has always been poor?" Mesfield asked in confusion.

"That's right. My body has always been weak. Surviving until now can only be considered heaven's blessing." Dais offered a polite smile.

Mesfield didn't press further, only deeply puzzled. Why would someone in such poor health continue serving as a royal guard knight? Under normal circumstances, they should be suspended for proper rest. Was Austria-Hungary really so short of talent that they needed a sick person to hold things together?

Under Mesfield's guidance, Dais was led to the Queen's conference room. Elizabeth had already been waiting for some time. She wanted to know one crucial thing — were the two founders of the Vampire Clan actually in Austria-Hungary?

"Your Majesty, Sir Dais has arrived."

"Beautiful Queen, it is my honor to receive your personal audience." Dais bowed slightly, his knightly manners very pronounced.

"Please, take a seat." Elizabeth gestured to Mesfield to bring over a chair. "It must have been quite a journey for you."

"Not at all. Receiving your audience is truly an unexpected honor." Dais sat upright in the chair, looking somewhat stiff. After all, Elizabeth was the Queen of Britain, holding supreme status. Every gesture between the two represented their respective nations.

Mesfield conveniently prepared a cup of black tea. Dais accepted it with thanks, then shifted the conversation. "Forgive my bluntness, but may I ask why Your Majesty summoned me?"

"Recently, vampire attacks on humans have occurred frequently across the world, posing a tremendous threat to us. I wonder what you think of this?" Queen Elizabeth asked indirectly.

"Between us, our country faces the same problem. Vampires' activities have become increasingly rampant. Our Emperor has been unable to sleep at night because of this, so he formed a specialized squad to hunt down vampires, doing everything possible to protect the safety of our citizens. We have already seen some results, and the situation is basically under control. However, completely eradicating the vampire threat would likely require considerable effort." Dais answered in a very official tone — less like a knight and more like a press spokesperson.

Elizabeth furrowed her brows slightly. She found Dais rather slippery and difficult to handle, so she went straight to the point —

"You're lying. Actually, your situation has already reached its worst, correct?"

title: Chapter 14 — Concealment
content:
Chapter 14 — Concealment

Volume 37 · Chapter 14

Desmond shuddered, his face turning a marked shade of discomfort, and his eyes darted away.

"Your Majesty, I must assume you're joking? We are perfectly capable of managing the current situation. There's no need to worry about any dire circumstances."

"You should be more concerned about yourself, if you ask me. As far as I'm aware, the Kingdom of Britain has been having quite a headache with vampires lately."

"If you'd like, the Austro-Hungarian Empire would be more than willing to offer assistance in helping Britain eliminate the bloodline."

"Are you hiding something? Why won't you tell us the truth?" Elizabeth's stern questioning.

"I'm afraid I don't understand what you mean. I'm not sure what misunderstanding has arisen, but in fact, the Austro-Hungarian Empire is extremely secure." Desmond spread his hands in a gesture of helplessness.

"But the facts are completely opposite to what you say. According to my recent investigations, the vampires have already begun to leave the eastern regions and are converging toward the territory of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. Shouldn't you be the one who's worried?" Elizabeth shot back.

"It seems Your Majesty's investigation has some misconceptions. In fact, the bloodline's objective is quite clear—just like the turmoil in France three years ago, they hope to establish their own nation-state. There's no truth to the idea that they're surrounding the Austro-Hungarian Empire. Our land has no soil suitable for the bloodline to survive in. France, on the other hand, would be ideal." Desmond explained with a smile, trying to avoid raising any suspicion toward the Austro-Hungarian Empire.

From Desmond's perspective, the current situation was quite favorable. The vampires had no reason to gather toward the Austro-Hungarian Empire. Moreover, even Britain had seen signs of vampire activity, which conveniently proved a point—that Cain was truly unable to find Lady Batrice and was wandering around like a headless fly. As long as no word got out, both Batrice and the Austro-Hungarian Empire would remain in a position of absolute safety.

Even if Cain were the son of a god with power rivaling the divine, he wouldn't be foolish enough to make enemies of all of humanity. That would only accelerate the unification of human nations.

"It seems you're not willing to share your secrets. Are you perhaps planning something in secret?" Elizabeth asked with a meaningful tone.

"What do you mean? Britain and we are both members of the Human Alliance. When facing unknown foreign threats, we are trustworthy allies. Regarding the bloodline, there are no secrets between us." Desmond replied smoothly, though inwardly he wondered if he had let something slip. Why had Queen Elizabeth concluded that he was hiding something about the bloodline?

"Since you agree that we're all members of the Human Alliance and should unite against foreign threats, I'll ask you directly." Elizabeth paused, locking eyes with Desmond. "The bloodline originally had three ancestors. Dracula was destroyed three years ago, leaving two remaining. Has the Austro-Hungarian Empire had any contact with the remaining bloodline ancestors?"

Desmond's smile froze for a moment, his heart skipping a beat. He couldn't believe the Queen of Britain knew about this? Normally, no outsiders were allowed near Lady Batrice. Where had she gotten this information?

"Are you not understanding? Let me be more direct. Are you in possession of the bloodline ancestors, hiding or detaining them?" Elizabeth stared intently at Desmond's expression, searching for any clue, but found nothing.

Desmond's smile tightened slightly, his hands unconsciously gripping the armrests of the chair until deep indentations formed. Under immense pressure, he thought: Damn it! Who leaked the secret? If the Kingdom of Britain found out, the plan to study the vampires might be compromised!

No way! I can't admit it no matter what! I have to deny any connection between the kingdom and the vampires!

Desmond took a deep breath, trying his best to appear calm and composed, and answered with a tone of helpless resignation.

"There's no truth to any of that. I must admit, Your imagination is quite vivid. Would you really think we have ties to the bloodline?"

"Isn't that the truth? The vampires are clearly searching for the two remaining ancestors, aren't they?" Elizabeth pressed further.

"The vampires need human blood to survive. The current situation has nothing to do with searching for the two ancestors. They're simply hungry for food." Desmond desperately tried to deny the facts.

"Desmond, you're a knight of high honor. Lying is not a good habit." Elizabeth paused and continued, "Frequent vampire attacks on humans can easily escalate into a great threat. This is a disaster for both of us. I hope you can be honest, show the sincerity befitting a member of the Human Alliance, and not hide crucial secrets. It's the right thing to do to nip potential dangers in the bud."

"I don't understand why you have such a big misunderstanding. Everything you've mentioned is mere speculation, completely inconsistent with the facts." Desmond stood up slowly, preparing to leave, and said, "In fact, it's you who should be the one showing sincerity."

Originally, Queen Elizabeth had wanted to use this opportunity to verify the information provided by Alice. If it was true, she would need to unite with other kingdoms in advance and launch a campaign to exterminate the bloodline.

However, the Austro-Hungarian Empire represented by Desmond completely refused to acknowledge anything, making the plan to exterminate the bloodline full of obstacles and unable to prevent the impending disaster.

After the war with the demons, Britain had temporarily lost its strength and didn't want to suffer any further blows. If possible, it hoped to eliminate all disasters in advance and safeguard the kingdom's interests.

After Desmond left, Mesfilld turned to the worried queen and couldn't help but ask, "Could the information provided by Miss Alice have been wrong?"

"No," Queen Elizabeth's expression darkened as she looked at the chair Desmond had just been sitting in, with deep finger impressions left on both armrests.

"The information provided by Miss Alice is flawless. The real problem lies with the Austro-Hungarian Empire."

"They clearly don't want to admit their connection to the bloodline and are trying their best to conceal the truth."

"They're probably worried we'll mess with their cake."

"Cough, cough, cough!"

In the palace corridor, Desmond leaned against the wall, coughing violently, his face extremely pale, and a layer of cold sweat breaking out on his back.

This meeting with Queen Elizabeth had left him terrified. He couldn't calm down for a long time afterward.

He hadn't expected Queen Elizabeth to know so much about the kingdom's secrets. He even suspected there might be a British spy within their ranks.

Desmond breathed heavily, his gaze growing sharp. He realized that after returning, he needed to have a serious talk with the royal family.

The secret of researching the vampires must not be known by other kingdoms.

The secret of eternal youth and immortality belongs to the Austro-Hungarian Empire. No other force is allowed to lay a hand on it!
