title: Chapter 15 — Unbelieving (Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 15 — Unbelieving (Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 37 · Chapter 15

Des returned to the Austro-Hungarian Empire, appeared before the emperor, and told the royal family in full about what had happened in Britain.

Among the human kingdoms, the Austro-Hungarian Empire was a great power, its prestige and strength not inferior to Britain's.

That a grand event like the Adventurers' Competition could be held here fully demonstrated its standing.

Sixty years ago, the empire had always been divided, until the weaker side was conquered, forming today's situation.

With its vast lands and brave, battle-hardened army, the empire quickly established itself and became a regional hegemon.

The entire empire was strictly hierarchical from top to bottom; almost nothing could bypass the ruler, and the concentration of power was far more severe than in other kingdoms.

Regional great nobles held no authority; even the size of their private armies was strictly controlled, and exceeding the limit immediately meant treason.

Soldiers of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, wherever they served, had only one object of allegiance—the emperor, whose army was the guarantee of his rule.

Such excess would never lead to the situation in the Spanish Kingdom, for the old emperor absolutely would not allow any great noble to challenge his position.

Unfortunately, the old emperor had his flaws—his obsession with power had bordered on madness.

In the old emperor's eyes, emotions were nothing but insubstantial things, far less tangible than the power in his hands.

So he had no heirs. To outsiders this seemed dreadful, but he relished it, avoiding the risk of succession disputes and making his power more secure.

Rumors said the old emperor had once had an affair with a maid, impregnating her, but the cold-blooded man immediately ordered her executed without mercy.

Of all the rulers of human nations, the old emperor of the Austro-Hungarian Empire was the only one capable of remaining utterly indifferent to all emotions.

But the old emperor was an ordinary mortal who could not cultivate; humanity's maximum lifespan was barely a hundred years—fleeting to the other races.

With time passing, the old emperor had lost his former vigor, becoming a frail old man, faintly sensing the threat of death's approach.

So the old emperor's only dream now was to obtain immortality; the desire to live had quietly eclipsed the taste of wielding power. He valued Lady Bathory and the vampires, hoping to gain vampire-like vitality without becoming a monster.

High in the hall, the old emperor sat majestically upon a throne of pure gold, looking down at Des; his aged face revealed no trace of sorrow or joy.

Des knelt on one knee and slowly recounted the events in Britain. "That is roughly how things stand. Queen Elizabeth seems to have discovered something?"

"Do you mean we have British spies here?" the old emperor asked in a deep voice.

"I'm deeply suspicious now. After all, Queen Elizabeth knows far too much." Des replied respectfully.

"I think you're overthinking this, Des. If that little girl knew we were researching vampires, she wouldn't summon you—she'd come straight to me to demand a share." The old emperor closed his eyes and spoke slowly. "But she does know a great deal about vampires. She likely hopes to extract more secrets from you. Your refusal to confirm anything was the right call."

"The secret of immortality is an imperial secret. It cannot be shared with anyone else." Des said solemnly.

"Exactly. Immortality will become the empire's most precious treasure, something many have dreamed of since antiquity." The old emperor agreed.

"However, there is something about what Queen Elizabeth said that troubles me." A trace of worry showed in Des's eyes.

"What?"

"Elizabeth said the vampires are drawing closer to the Austro-Hungarian Empire. I investigated privately, and the vampire attacks on humans this past half-year have indeed multiplied many times over. Other kingdoms seem to be shaking off the vampire menace." Des frowned and offered his boldest deduction. "Could it be that the vampires have discovered we are harboring Lady Bathory?"

"It remains uncertain. Perhaps the vampires have altered their strategy, realizing that scattered searches are inefficient, and have begun pooling their efforts to secretly comb every nation where Bathory might be hiding—that seems far more plausible." The old emperor leaned on the armrest of his throne and spoke slowly. "Our secrecy has always been impeccable. Only you and a few researchers can access Lady Bathory, and we conduct strict identity checks every day. Vampires could not possibly reach her."

"But we cannot guarantee those researchers won't be bribed, Your Majesty. We should exercise additional caution." Des felt uneasy, especially since Elizabeth already knew so much. Exposure of Bathory's hiding place was certainly not impossible.

"Rest assured. Their families are already under control. If Bathory's secret is exposed, they will all die. When faced with bribes, they should worry far more about their own safety and that of their families." The old emperor had prepared in advance, binding everyone to the same cart—everyone dies together if things go wrong.

"In truth, you are the only possible weak link, Des. You have no family, no ties of any kind. Only you are most likely to recklessly blab the truth without any reservations."

Des stared wide-eyed in shock, never expecting to be suspected. He had served the old emperor for many years and knew all too well just how cold-blooded the man was. Once suspected, trust was nearly impossible to regain.

That blazing heart gradually turned to ice. Des never imagined things would come to this. To protect the empire, he had served faithfully for years despite his deteriorating health, only to receive not a single ounce of trust in return.

It was hard for Des to accept. He had devoted the best years of his life to the empire, only to meet such an ending. Any knight, no matter how loyal, could be driven to madness.

"Your Majesty, I am faithfully devoted to you and would never betray the empire. I swear upon the soul of a knight—"

"I know you are loyal—at least, on the surface. But emotion is an exceedingly cheap thing. Your loyalty is far less trustworthy than raw power, is it not?" the emperor countered coldly.

"Respected Your Majesty, what must I do to earn your trust? I have devoted myself body and soul to the empire, asking for nothing in return."

Des struck his chest, his voice growing agitated. "For your sake, my health has declined steadily. I could have resigned and retired home to recover, but I did not. I simply wished to remain by your side and share your burdens."

"Your spirit of selfless devotion earns my admiration. However, for the sake of the greater picture, I cannot fully trust you. I sense my own health deteriorating by the day. I must obtain the power of immortality. I will not allow any mishap under any circumstances." The emperor gave a subtle signal, and a maid emerged from the corner carrying a tray, upon which sat a cup of greenish liquid—a peculiar-looking "wine."

"This is a slow-acting poison, specially prepared for you."

"Come, let me see your loyalty in action, Des."

title: Chapter 16 — Struggle (Monthly Ticket Extra)
content:
Chapter 16 — Struggle (Monthly Ticket Extra)

Volume 37 · Chapter 16

"If your loyalty isn't false? Then drink it. I'll give you the elixir to stay alive, giving it to you regularly—it's for the kingdom's future.

The old emperor's cold words reached Dast, hoping to firmly bind him to his carriage to prevent him from having any thoughts of betraying him.

After all, the other participants in the research all had weaknesses under the old emperor's control, but Dast's son had no attachments whatsoever and might act out of control.

If Dast drank the slow-acting poison wine in front of him, the old emperor could feel at ease that his loyal royal guard knight wouldn't betray him. Dast's body, mind, and spirit were all selfish—he wouldn't gamble with his life.

The old emperor placed his hope for survival on the bloodline. Even if he made his most loyal subordinate drink the poison wine, he wouldn't allow any possibility of unexpected outcomes.

Clearly, the desire for survival had already conquered everything. The old emperor walked this path further and further, unable to let go of the empire he had built with his own hands.

Among all the human nations, the Austro Empire's history was indeed very brief, hardly matching the longevity of many ancient kingdoms. Moreover, the old emperor had no heirs, so death would take away all his former glory.

Not every king and their personal guard knights got along well. Cases like the old emperor and Dast were common, while Queen Iliana and Mespfield were an exception.

Willing to entrust the kingdom's only—unique artifact to Mespfield, showing how much trust Queen Elizabeth placed in her knight—it was almost like giving her life to Mespfield.

But the old emperor wasn't like that. As he aged, he grew increasingly suspicious of those close to him, always harboring a sliver of doubt about his advisors, believing they would harbor ill intentions when he was at his weakest, then seize everything that belonged to him.

So Dast's loyalty was worthless in the old emperor's eyes, and it was destined that he would become a tragedy—the knight not receiving trust was essentially a death sentence for his entire knightly career!

Yet this act of distrust, however, caused Dast's loyalty to develop a tiny crack, making him begin to question whether spending his entire life serving the old emperor was worth it?

Dast's physical condition was terrible. Even the slow-acting poison wine would cause irreversible, severe damage to him. It seemed harmless, but it was pushing him toward a dead end.

Actually, Dast was very clear—researching vampires, creating an immortal elixir of eternal life, his hopes were bleak. For three years, there had been almost no significant progress.

The old emperor's death was virtually certain. If he drank the poison wine, the old king would die, and without an antidote, he would die too—essentially making him his own grave companion.

Dast stared at the green, tempting "wine" before him, feeling disgust to the extreme. He could offer his loyalty, but he didn't want his fate to be tied to the paranoid old emperor's.

"I . ."

"What are you hesitating about? Are you saying all that before was false? " The old emperor asked sternly, sensing his personal guard knight was being disobedient. Obviously, this wasn't a good sign.

"Not at all. My loyalty to you is as pure as a gemstone, without any blemish. " Dast raised his head, sincerely saying, "I hope you can reconsider this decision. My current physical condition doesn't allow me to drink this wine."

"You don't drink it, you won't earn my trust. I'm even a bit suspicious you " the old emperor squinted his eyes, meaning significantly, "are you a traitor from the Kingdom of Britain? Did you reveal secrets to Queen Elizabeth?"

"I would never do that even if I were to die! I'm willing to swear on my knightly soul—why won't you trust me? Doesn't my oath have any value at all?!" Dast bit his teeth, his voice turning into a pleading shout, hoping the old emperor would change his mind. Without him, the Austro Empire would crumble in minutes. The old emperor's rule had already weakened visibly before everyone's eyes. That he could still sit on the throne was relying on countless knights like Dast.

"You and I aren't children—how could we believe in such idle words? It's like children's promises that can be easily revoked, having absolutely no effect. " The old emperor's expression eased, coaxing him to say, "Don't worry about your body. If the bloodline's secret research succeeds, you can be the first to try it, and all problems will be solved."

Dast bit his lip, feeling melancholy inside. The old emperor was still calculating on him at this moment, being the first to try sounded nice, but he was just an experimental guinea pig! One's own body could become a monster, likely to be abandoned at any time.

"Drink it—this is an order. Only by binding everyone's interests together can safety be ensured. You should understand this logic. " The old emperor spoke with an authoritative tone, plunging the two of them into an icy situation.

Dast seemed to understand. Not giving his life to the old emperor meant he could never gain trust. Serving loyally for so many years, he was only a sacrifice for the royal family.

The old emperor felt Dast was acting strangely, clearly resisting his command. Fortunately, he had prepared in advance, tapping his fingers three times on the throne's armrest—

Thump! Thump! Thump!

Suddenly, countless fully armed palace knights surrounded the hall, including many knights with strong abilities, not needing Dast's weakness.

Everyone tightly gripped their weapons, staring at Dast's every move. If he made any move of resistance, he would be surrounded and killed.

The atmosphere in the hall suddenly became tense, weapons drawn. The old king wasn't surprised—he was suspicious even of his own biological child, so naturally he would suspect Dast might rebel him.

Under heavy pressure, Dast showed a pitiful smile, his loyal heart broken, raising both hands to drink the "wine" before him in one gulp—

Clearly, he was being forced. Dast returned to this place, continuing to personally guard Baroness Batou. Inside, however, came the sound of severe coughing.

"Cough... cough... cough... cough..."

Dast looked at the blood on the white handkerchief, feeling sad because, having drunk the slow-acting poison wine, his body couldn't take it anymore.

If he had endured it before, he could have lived another ten years. Now, damaged by the slow-acting poison wine, he might only have less than two years left.

Dast could already see his death approaching, rapidly closing in. As a knight, he felt utterly defeated, never gaining trust even until death.

It was as if Dast were a foolish donkey, attracted by fresh carrots in front of him, but ended up dying slowly, all his sacrifices having no effect.

"What's wrong with you? Your face is even worse than before, looking like a corpse. " Batou knew her guardian well, having been together for three years—she couldn't escape his every move.

"I don't need your sympathy. " Dast coldly said. He agreed with Batou's words. He wasn't even worth being compared to the dead—a discarded diseased dog.

"Lord Dast, could you get me some food? Animal blood has limited effect on me—I need human blood. " Batou lay on her bony cage, her breathing very weak, having been—by groups of people, bled, and had organs cut out. Her condition improving was rare, having endured three years of torment, "I haven't been able to drink human blood for a month. This kind of life I've had enough of—better to be killed by the hidden."

Dast's eyes flickered, an idea forming, and once it appeared, it became unstoppable. Since he had already lost his future, why continue being a knight?

Someone like the old emperor, who was universally betrayed and hated, didn't deserve his loyalty. Perhaps resistance was the only way out.

Dast made up his mind, directly approached Batou's cage, rolled up his sleeves, and thrust his arm into the bone cage, his gaze sharp as ever.

"If you're hungry, then drink my blood."

Batou was shocked, crawling up from the ground, staring blankly at Dast's arm, "Are you serious?"

"Of course. " Dast answered with a definite tone.

"Ha." Batou laughed, revealing her sharp fangs, teasingly saying—"Check chapter 76 for the latest updates"

"I told you long ago—you'll end up regretting this."

title: Chapter 17 — Treason
content:
Chapter 17 — Treason

Volume 37 · Chapter 17

A vast, endless white world stretched out before Cain, with nothing but her in it. It felt like being in a state of primordial chaos, an age before anything had been born, filled with loneliness and desolation.

Cain looked around, trying to find an exit, when she unexpectedly heard a familiar voice echoing in her ears—

"Your birth was an accident. Aber was my only spiritual anchor. You really don't need to exist."

"Goodness often comes with evil, and you are the evil seed that came with Aber's birth. From the moment you were born, you were sinful."

"So no matter how hard you try, you'll never measure up to Aber. You're unnecessary. It's best if you just disappear."

Cain's usually calm face twisted with anger. These words were exactly what that once-lofty "mother" had said to her, directly negating everything she had ever been.

Goddess Mary had originally wanted to create the purest, most innocent child, using her deceased sister as a template and as her own spiritual anchor. But Cain was an unexpected birth, more like an afterthought, completely opposite in nature to Aber, and the very thing Mary most despised.

As the goddess had said, goodness always came with evil, and that was unavoidable. Cain and Aber were meant to coexist. But because of Mary's forced interference, Cain developed jealousy for her sister Aber, which eventually led to their mutual destruction.

Cain was cursed by her mother and sealed in a holy vial for countless eras, losing her freedom and enduring the torment of a craving for blood. The last shred of hope she had for her mother was consumed, and her only motivation now was to avenge her mother.

The anger on Cain's face faded, replaced by an eerie calm. She looked down and said coldly—

"I don't need anything from you. I've had no love for you for a long time. All I have left is endless hatred."

"Wait for me in heaven. We'll meet again."

"Master! Master?"

A series of calls echoed, and Cain slowly opened her eyes, waking up from her sleep.

There was Dickert, looking excited and eager to see her, but her mood wasn't good.

"What's the matter?"

"Good news! Good news! If it weren't for good news, I wouldn't dare to disturb you while you're resting."

Dickert said, beaming with excitement. Under his management, the bloodline had grown stronger and stronger, even taking over several human cities. All of these would soon be the wealth of the Plague Dickert, bringing the dream of establishing a bloodline kingdom closer to reality.

Being able to gain so many benefits from Cain, Dickert had worked hard for her, and if Cain were to leave, he would inherit all of her "legacy."

"What good news?" Cain looked at Dickert. For the past three years, there had been no news of Bartholomew, and her patience was running thin.

"I got information from a man named Old Ho, a dealer in information. We don't need to spend a lot of effort searching all the human kingdoms anymore." Dickert said excitedly.

"Oh? Where is it?" Cain asked, surprised.

"Budapest, the capital of the Austro-Hungarian Empire." Dickert answered confidently.

"Is the information accurate?" Cain didn't believe it, thinking it was just some gossip Dickert had heard somewhere.

"Probably accurate." Dickert smiled awkwardly.

"Probably accurate? Hmph!" Cain scoffed and continued, "I want an accurate answer, not some probability game. You can't even be sure, what's that good news for?"

"I've heard that this man named Old Ho is very powerful. Many people who bought secret information from him haven't had any problems. So the information is highly reliable!" Dickert explained seriously, having heard the name "Old Ho" often during his days as a thief, and he was praised as someone beyond human understanding.

"Information dealers are all useless. The information they sell is worthless." Cain looked down on these dealers who sold secondhand news.

"Master, Old Ho is not ordinary. During my days as a thief, I often heard about him from information dealers. He is the only one among information dealers who can guarantee the accuracy of the information." Dickert paused and said quietly, "Moreover, the source of this information is very suspicious!"

"Hmm?" Cain showed a hint of doubt, "How so?"

"According to the information, it seems to be leaked by the royal guards of the Austro-Hungarian Empire." Dickert answered seriously.

"Royal guards?" Cain finally showed some interest, thinking the reliability of the information had increased. Royal guards were directly under the command of the royal family, and if they were willing to leak such information, it was equivalent to treason. Why would they take such a risk, and what did they want?

"That's right! Coincidentally, I recently ordered the vampires to gather towards the Austro-Hungarian Empire, preparing for a carpet-bombing search. And then this information appeared, there must be a connection!" Dickert narrowed his eyes and said with certainty, "I have an eightiethousand percent chance that Bartholomew is hiding in the capital of the Austro-Hungarian Empire!"

Cain fell into thought. Combining all the clues, the Austro-Hungarian Empire seemed increasingly suspicious, and it was also in the same direction where Bartholomew's scent had disappeared three years ago—

"Prepare, we'll leave tonight. The Austro-Hungarian Empire will soon no longer exist."

"Even if we dig three feet deep, we'll find Bartholomew."

Several days later, at night, the capital of the Austro-Hungarian Empire was as usual, peaceful, with no one realizing that danger was approaching. No one took Elizabeth's warning seriously, and no one had prepared in advance. This provided the best conditions for the vampires' attack, with many people still asleep.

Dickert secretly gathered a large number of vampires, hiding in the night, quickly approaching Budapest. Even inside the royal city, vampires had already infiltrated, preparing to launch a combined attack to quickly take over the place.

In the darkness, countless crimson eyes glowed, more dazzling than the stars in the sky!

This once-prosperous city that had hosted the Adventurers' Competition, might soon disappear from the map, and the entire fractured empire would also collapse.

In the dungeon, Des had already taken off the armor symbolizing his knighthood, sitting on a chair in plain clothes, sharpening his sword—

Des had been prepared for this. After becoming a vampire, the slow-acting poison lost its effect, and even his long-suffering body had recovered. Tonight, he would end the life of the old emperor with his own hands, stripping away all the glory of knighthood.

title: Chapter 18 — Abandonment
content:
Chapter 18 — Abandonment

Volume 37 · Chapter 18

The gathered vampires launched their most ferocious attack, charging into defenseless Budapest. Vampires that had long infiltrated the royal capital also sprang into action under Dickteping's command. They killed the soldiers guarding the city gate and flung the gates of Budapest wide open to the invading vampires. The prosperous city was set ablaze in a short time, and the sky was filled with the phantoms of vampires, emitting piercing shrieks at the helpless people. Most people were still asleep, unaware of what was happening before them, and countless died outright in their sleep. The night patrol soldiers had no time to sound the alarm before being impaled and killed by the vampires' thrown spears; the situation was completely one-sided. Because the old emperor was already suspicious, the whole empire was teetering on the brink, as if it would collapse instantly under the vampires' onslaught. The vampires roamed as if in an uninhabited land, indiscriminately slaughtering Budapest's residents, greedily sucking human blood; for this day they had long awaited. If the old emperor had not been so suspicious and had tried to make a pact with Elizabeth, heeding his subordinates' advice, perhaps what is happening now would not have occurred. But there are no 'ifs'; the Austro-Hungarian Empire, which was already a short-lived state, will tonight have its final period drawn by the vampires themselves. The startled kingdom knights, without even having time to don their armor, immediately organized a counterattack, but the opportunity was already lost; half of Budapest's land fell completely under vampire control. The royal exclusive knight order was also directly blasted to death by Dickteping's flame‑magic great gun; not a single one could stand against it, because the strongest knight, Dice, had already betrayed, driving the kingdom into the abyss—. Flames engulfed the entire royal city; the horrific scene was no different from the British capital falling into demon hands. The firelight illuminated the land as if it were daytime, while thick smoke rose to form oppressive clouds overhead. Angry and terrified cries rose and fell; prosperous Budapest perished in history tonight. In the dungeon, Lady Bathory trapped in the bone cage panicked, her face pallid as she looked around; she heard the shouts of slaughter outside, clearly some great upheaval had erupted. Lady Bathory was terrified, wondering if she would face any danger, but imprisoned she could do nothing but wait in the cage for death! Besides the tumultuous sounds, there came the occasional scrape of a blade being sharpened; not far away, Dice, having taken off his armor, was polishing his beloved sword, making final preparations. Such a bizarre sight made Lady Bathory even more uneasy, for Dice's demeanor had been strange these past days—he had lost his former vigor and become as silent as a walking corpse. Not long ago, Bathory, while drinking Dice's blood, turned him into a vampire, thinking this stiff knight would betray the empire and side with her. But Dice merely sought the vampires' immortal power; he had no intention of obeying Bathory, and instead grew ever colder toward her. Dice rubbed his thumb along the sharp blade, a cold gleam lighting his face as he revealed a long‑absent smile, saying, 'Can—' 'Dice! What's happening out there? Why is it so noisy? Answer me!' Lady Bathory shouted excitedly. 'They're vampires; they've broken in.' Dice answered succinctly, not minding to elaborate. 'Vampires? How could that be!' Bathory's face showed utter disbelief, 'Didn't you say they would never find me?' 'That's how it should be, but I sold the information to an information dealer, so now they know.' Dice said frankly. 'It's you?!' Bathory stared wide‑eyed, scolding, 'You dare deceive me! Why? I've done almost everything you told me to! What else are you dissatisfied with?' 'I have no grievance against you; what I resent is the empire, which wanted to starve me to death, so I smashed the cooking pot together—let nobody be well off.' Dice said bluntly, having already forgotten all knightly virtues, shedding his burdens, and feeling an unprecedented lightness. 'It's not me who's persecuting you, right?' Bathory's eyes filled with pleading, hoping for Dice's help, 'Please, take me away from this damned place; if I stay I'll surely be found!' Dice gave Bathory a cold glance, then asked calmly, 'Why should I help you?' 'I gave you immortal power! Your healthy body now is my doing! Shouldn't you repay me?' Bathory widened her eyes, thinking she still had a chance to escape here. 'Ah, yes, I'm quite satisfied with this body; I've countless times wanted to escape the torment of illness, and now I've realized my dream, thanks to you.' Dice looked at his hands, savoring his healthy body, having escaped the constraints of knightly doctrine; he considered himself reborn, which is why many adventurers would rather rough it than serve the royalty, seeking precisely this. 'Exactly! Exactly! It's me who helped you; you should take me out of here! Rest assured, as long as you help me, I can give you more—perhaps even share Cain's undying divine power!' Bathory's eyes shone with excitement; now all she needed was to be taken away, and she would do anything. 'Sorry, though I am now a monster, that doesn't mean I'll stand with you; we are not the same.' Dice sheathed his sword, put on his coat, and walked straight out of the dungeon without looking back, 'Left to your own devices, poor Bathory.' 'Dice! You worthless, untrustworthy bastard! You'll die badly! You'll pay for your actions! Your soul will never find rest!' Lady Bathory cursed Dice wildly, unaware that he had already abandoned his knightly identity, and that credibility was worthless in his eyes. Dice's silhouette quickly vanished into the distance; Bathory remained alone in her bone cage, despair etched on her face as she listened to the slaughter outside. Though she wanted to flee this damned place, when her hands touched the railings made of holy spirit bone, the pain nearly made her faint. Bathory collapsed, nearly dead, her hands blackened and burned by the holy spirit bone, making it impossible for her to escape the cage on her own. Suddenly a shadow fell over Bathory; she lifted her head hopefully, but instantly turned ashen and frozen in place, her lips moving without uttering a word. Cain looked down on the pitiful Bathory, his smile laden with meaning, like a death‑seeking wraith whispering in her ear—'Do you really think you can escape?'

title: Chapter 19 — Regicide
content:
Chapter 19 — Regicide

Volume 37 · Chapter 19

Lady Bathory saw Cain's figure, her heart plummeted into an ice cellar, feeling death approaching, leaving her mind blank.

"

"You've made me search for so long, it turns out you relied on this method to evade my detection?" Cain lightly touched the holy spirit bone cage with his fingertips, which originally had excellent restraint against dark creatures, but turned to ash and scattered at her light touch, "It's a pity that aside from masking your aura, it has no other use; it cannot protect your safety."

Ugh. Lady Bathory's people stared wide-eyed in horror, thinking even they couldn't escape this cage, Cain easily destroyed it, the holy spirits' bones were useless!

"The ones who deceived me, only you remain; I can finally reclaim all my undying divine power and complete the final metamorphosis. No matter how hard you strive, you cannot change the inevitable doomed fate; fleeing merely grants you three extra years of life." Cain showed a sympathetic gaze, looking at the weary Lady Bathory, presumably she endured much torment to evade pursuit, but what good is that?

"I apologize! I apologize for what happened back then; I never intended to deceive you, it was all Dracula's own doing! I really had no choice!" Lady Bathory clung to hope, wanting a chance to live, "Please forgive me, I'm willing to do anything for you! Please!"

"What use is apologizing now? I never intended to forgive you; even if you had released me from the holy vial, you three would still be unable to escape death. How could a god share power with lowly humans?" Cain looked down at the panicked Lady Bathory; such a weak creature, yet she has survived till now, somewhat ironic.

", I beg for your forgiveness, I have no intention of opposing you! Such a lowly wretch like me does not deserve your strike!" Lady Bathory trembled all over, prostrated on the ground, lacking even the courage to meet Cain's gaze.

"Is begging for mercy all you have to say as your last words? How boring." Cain's gaze was icy, akin to looking at a corpse; he could not accept Bathory's plea for mercy.

"

Lady Bathory hadn't finished speaking when Cain seized her neck, lifting her from the ground; before the true ancestor she had no strength to resist—

"Go join your former companions in hell."

In the Austro-Hungarian Empire's palace, it had already been overrun by crowds of vampires; the servants were terrified, their souls scattered, unable to attend to anything else, snatching precious items from the palace and fleeing in all directions.

The knight order serving the royal family was nearly wiped out before the Diket plane; hardly any knights could return alive to continue guarding the palace, the empire's collapse trend could not be halted.

Under the cover of a few loyal knights, the old emperor stumbled out of the bedroom, seeing Budapest engulfed in a sea of fire, he broke into lamenting wails.

What on earth is happening?! What exactly occurred? Why have vampires invaded my palace?

"Your Majesty! Hurry and leave! This place can no longer be defended! The vampires' assault is too strong! We are unprepared! We cannot possibly kill these monsters!"

"Could it be that heaven wishes my demise?! If I had known this day would come, I should have heeded Elizabeth's advice and prepared in advance; I wouldn't have ended up like this!" The old emperor felt deep regret, unable to comprehend why the blood clan would target him; his mind filled only with thoughts of temporary refuge, then mustering the kingdom's armies from all regions to retake Budapest, "Damn monsters! Wait for me! I will lead the empire's finest knights back to retake it!"

"Your Majesty, rest assured! The knights will give their all to help you reclaim the capital; please follow us through the secret passage to leave here. If the vampire main force arrives, we won't be able to escape!" A knight, sweating profusely, supported the old emperor, thinking that at such a moment there's no point in venting resentment; it's crucial to flee and save one's life.

"Where is my loyal knight Dice? With such a major incident, why is there no trace of him?! If he were here, retaking Budapest would be imminent!" The old emperor, at this moment, recalled his strongest personal guard knight.

"We haven't seen Captain Dice; we don't know where he went. Perhaps he is on the front lines fighting the vampires, buying us time to escape." A knight replied.

Upon hearing the situation was so urgent, the old emperor dared not delay; he immediately ordered the knights nearby to shield him, proceeding along the kingdom's secret passage, hoping to slip out before the vampire main force stormed the palace.

Since the palace's founding, the old emperor had anticipated this scenario; thus he had constructed a nearly kilometer-long underground passage beneath the palace, leading to the outskirts of Budapest.

The knights held torches, guarding around the old emperor, continually advancing through the dark passage, but due to the emperor's advanced age, their progress was slow, making it difficult to quickly leave the danger zone.

Suddenly, a blurry figure appeared before the knights' eyes, startling them into cries, thinking the vampires had discovered the secret passage and set an ambush ahead of time!

"Protect His Majesty!—

At the command, the knights gathered before the old emperor, tension reaching its peak; even the emperor's face turned pale, he dared not breathe loudly.

Dice slowly stepped forward, aided by the dim yellow glow of the torches, the knights finally saw his face, instantly overjoyed, exclaiming repeatedly.

"Captain Dice?"

Seeing it was Dice, the old emperor relaxed, feeling safer, and spoke gently, "Oh, it's you, Dice! Come shield me as I leave this damned place! Once I muster the entire empire's armies, I will help you retake Budapest!"

Dice wore a grim visage, silent, steadily advancing; his eerie behavior drew the knights' attention, many instinctively went on alert, sensing that today's captain was off.

"Captain Dice! What do you want?!"

Dice's face revealed a ferocious expression, his eyes flickering with killing intent; he swiftly drew his sword and slashed, in an instant cutting down all the knights guarding the old emperor, blood splattering onto the walls!

He was originally the kingdom's strongest knight; killing the old emperor was as easy as taking something from a bag—how could these knights possibly be his match?

The old emperor was stunned, bloodless as he gazed at the knights' corpses on the ground, unable to believe his eyes; his most loyal knight had betrayed him.

"Dice! What are you doing?!"

"What am I doing? Isn't it obvious enough? Your Majesty." Dice held a blood‑dripping sword, relentlessly pressing toward the old emperor, feeling exhilarated, finally no longer needing to endure the emperor's foolishness.

".You .You are betraying! Violating the loyalty a knight ought to have!" the old emperor staggered backward, his face etched with terror.

"Loyalty? What is that? Can it be eaten?" Dice narrowed his eyes, replying in an extremely vicious tone—

"From the moment you forced me to drink that poison, my useless loyalty was already tossed into the trash."

title: Chapter 20 — In Full Splendor
content:
Chapter 20 — In Full Splendor

Volume 37 · Chapter 20

The old emperor's heart "clunked" as he realized the cup of wine was the final straw that toppled the crumbling empire into the abyss.

"Did you bring the vampires outside?"

"Yes, I personally sold the information to the intelligence brokers to bring you down from the throne," said Dais.

The old emperor's expression was incomprehensible, and he asked in surprise, "Why would you do that? The empire's fate is intertwined with yours. What's in it for you?"

"There's nothing in it for me. For someone who's on the brink of despair, the empire's fate doesn't matter anymore," Dais replied without emotion.

"You're insane," the old emperor growled, but he couldn't provoke Dais, still hoping to calm him down and secure a chance to live.

"Even if I'm insane, it's because you pushed me to do it. For me, giving up the knight's burden might not be a bad thing. I've never felt this free before," Dais said meaningfully.

"I think there's some misunderstanding between us, Dais," the old emperor's gaze softened, and he said quietly, "I never forced you, nor did I intend to harm you. All decisions were made for the greater good. Only by keeping your life in my hands could I ensure the information wouldn't leak out, and everyone would be at ease, right?"

Dais scoffed, having long since grown tired of the old emperor's selfish attitude, which was why the empire had never been able to escape its fractured state.

"I never expected the poisoned wine would drive you to this point. If I had known you'd turn out like this, I would have never let you drink the poison. I would have found a more gentle way to satisfy everyone," the old emperor said, spreading his hands and looking apologetic. "I apologize for my foolish actions. I hope you can forgive me. I won't pursue the mistakes you've made. Now, help me escape Buda, rally the troops, and pretend nothing happened, okay?"

The old emperor offered a very tempting proposal and was very correct. At this moment, the most important thing was to bring Dais over to their side, not to oppress him.

Only then could the old emperor continue to live, then use Dais' strength to rally the troops within the empire and reclaim Buda.

In the face of this utilitarian monarch, there were no friends worth trusting, only those who would never betray him for the sake of their own interests.

But how could Dais possibly accept this? If he had sold the information to the intelligence brokers beforehand, he might have chosen to accept the old emperor's apology.

Now, Dais had no way back. Not only had he given up the honor of a knight, but he had also abandoned his human identity. There was only one way back for him, and that was death.

"Too late!" Dais grabbed the old emperor by the throat and pushed him against the cold wall, his face twisted in fury. "Why didn't you cut off your arrogant head earlier? Why are you only now feeling remorseful? Are you afraid of me?"

"Dais, stay calm!" the old emperor was being choked, struggling to breathe, his face turning purple and white.

"You've sacrificed almost everything for me, yet I can't even earn your trust. My body is already at its limit, yet you forced me to drink the poison? Why!" Dais was furious, nearly snarling, "Why didn't you trust a knight who risked his life to maintain the empire for you? Why did you treat me like an enemy? Why are you so cruel?"

The old emperor couldn't answer, and he didn't know how to soothe Dais' anger. He felt his consciousness fading, and he was about to be choked to death.

Desperate, the old emperor drew his dagger from his waist and stabbed it into Dais' chest without hesitation. He saw that Dais wouldn't die, and he couldn't escape Buda alive.

Dais looked down at the dagger in his chest and his expression became blank. He couldn't believe that the old emperor would plan to kill him at this moment. To have any hope for such a person was the greatest foolishness.

The old emperor was released, and he took deep breaths, seeing the dagger stuck in Dais' chest. He couldn't help but laugh triumphantly and mockingly said, "Hahaha, Dais, you're still too naive. You ask me why? Because you're foolish. Foolish people should be exploited, drained of all their value, and then discarded like a used rag. You're already a discarded piece of junk, even though you played me for a fool, it doesn't matter. I will rally the entire empire's troops and reclaim my throne, while you will die here as a cold corpse. No one will remember your achievements; they will only remember you as the disgrace of knights, the betrayer of the empire, and even after death, you will be spat upon as garbage."

"It's a pity that you're the one who's dead," Dais looked up, his eyes red with blood, and he pulled the dagger out of his chest and stabbed it into the old emperor's chest.

The old emperor was pale, clutching his chest and trembling, unable to believe what he was seeing. Why hadn't the dagger in his heart killed Dais?

"I'm not human anymore, Your Majesty," Dais said, pushing the dagger into the old emperor's heart and ending his life.

As a vampire, how could he be killed by a normal dagger? This was also the reason he couldn't go back.

This one-sided massacre continued until the next day, when the shadows of the mountains on the horizon turned red, indicating that dawn was approaching. A few lucky people managed to escape Buda, while most perished under the fangs of the vampires and would never wake up again.

The once-bustling Buda became a wasteland, with the flames only beginning to subside the next day, and thick smoke filled the sky.

Looking at the approaching dawn, the vampires felt some panic, as they couldn't move in the sunlight, and they had to find something to hide behind, waiting for the night to come.

Dikter reported the victory to Gehenna, Buda had fallen into the hands of the bloodline, and they had also found the ruler's corpse in the secret passage. They would use this as the center and expand outward, establishing a vast bloodline kingdom.

However, Gehenna had no interest in such matters. Her eyes were only on revenge. After killing Countess Bathory, all the undead divine power had been reclaimed, and she could now evolve into her full form at any time.

In just a few days, Gehenna would fully integrate the last of the undead divine power and undergo a transformation, restoring her status as a godchild and achieving a terrifying leap in power. This outcome was already predetermined and could not be stopped.

Gehenna closed her eyes and felt her body, finally experiencing her completeness, with no weaknesses or shortcomings. She could now proceed with her final revenge plan.

"Master, we've achieved a great victory, but we need to rest. The sun is about to rise, and we need to hide," Dikter said cautiously. He felt that Gehenna was becoming more and more terrifying, and he had to suppress all thoughts of betrayal. He had no courage to stab in the back, because he believed that now Gehenna had transcended the limits of the mortal world and become a terrifying monster that crossed levels!

According to common sense, such a terrifying existence as Gehenna should not appear in the mortal world.

With the recovery of all undead divine power, plus the power of Merlin and Alice, Gehenna was now even stronger than she had been before. This gave her the confidence to challenge her mother!

PSI I

This month, I will definitely make up for the three extra days to reach fifteen days, so you can rest assured!

title: Chapter 21 — Legs Give Way
content:
Chapter 21 — Legs Give Way

Volume 37 · Chapter 21

“Sunlight isn’t scary; there’s no need to avoid it.” Cain looked at the fiery red horizon, a plan forming in his mind.

Dickteping felt embarrassed to speak, thinking sheepishly, You’re not afraid of the sun, but other vampires would be burned to death by sunlight.

“Let’s start the ritual here, the final step to enter Heaven.” Cain glanced around and went straight to the center of the imperial palace.

“What are you planning to do?” Dickteping didn’t know what Cain intended; after each ancestor is dealt with, one normally needs some time to digest.

“Just watch.”

Cain’s eyes narrowed; he slammed his hand hard against the floor beneath him, and the whole land of Budapest trembled.

With a thunderous roar, the earth split, the royal city was instantly destroyed and plunged into the abyss!

The tremendous noise woke countless nearby birds, which fled in fright, and a scorching breath burst from the ground!

Cain used his power to force the land to move; Dickteping sat down stunned, feeling the ground beneath him constantly rising!

After a few minutes, amid the ruins of Budapest, a magnificent black volcano appeared, scorching magma accompanied by thick smoke shooting toward the sky, sealing the heavens with dark clouds, letting no sunlight through, forcibly creating an environment suitable for vampires to live in.

Budapest, which was about to dawn, instantly turned back to night; as long as Cain is here, sunlight can never shine here. After experiencing panic, the vampires saw that sunlight was no longer a threat and cheered toward the newly appeared volcano; Budapest has practically become a homeland tailor-made for them.

At the volcano’s crater, a huge black magic circle emerged, continuously rotating; the sacrificial ritual is already ready.

Dickteping lowered his head, gazing at the enormous black magic circle beneath him, faintly seeing the scorching magma flowing at its base, and asked, “What is this?”

“Don’t be surprised; this is the ritual to open the Gate of Heaven, and also my final step to return to Heaven.” Cain slowly turned around, speaking gloomily—

“Your task is to capture humans and throw them into the volcano to be killed; opening the Gate of Heaven requires many sacrifices.

“I will forge a stairway to Heaven from countless human souls.”

On another note, Merlin didn’t go straight to Britain; instead, he detoured to his homeland, the Death Swamp.

Because the demon race had already completed its integration, after the Death Swamp was abandoned, there were no demons left; they had all been gathered in the Demon City of the Sand Sea.

“Human”-“Dog” suddenly appeared on this barren land, looking somewhat out of place.

Merlin didn’t come here to revisit old grounds; he headed straight for the Despair Canyon in the Death Swamp, wanting to visit an old friend before returning to Britain.

After entering Despair Canyon, the Holy Dragon Aweis was stunned; he had never seen such a perilous place—everywhere were poisonous miasma traps, plus many dangerous demon beasts.

If he weren’t tightly following Merlin, Aweis felt that coming here would surely get him killed horribly; many fierce demon beasts were no weaker than him.

“Hey! Lucifer, what the hell is this place?” Aweis lowered his head, his dog hair standing on end, his nerves stretched to the limit.

“Maybe it’s our demon race’s holy ground? In the past, no demon dared to casually step into this place.” Merlin replied.

“Even if you don’t say it, I know nobody would just wander in here; such a dangerous place—unless one has lived long enough, who would set foot here?” Aweis said anxiously.

“I’ve been here before, and I even made a decent friend.” Merlin thought of “King Kong,” whom he hadn’t visited in a long time; besides seeing his old friend, he also had some questions to ask.

“What are you doing here? You’re not deliberately looking for trouble, are you?” Aweis said sarcastically, thinking Merlin must have lost his mind.

“Talking at length has nothing to do with you; although this place is dangerous, there are some good things that can temper the body and increase its magic resistance—I think you should give it a try.” Merlin said meaningfully.

“Huh?” Holy Spirit Aweis pricked up his ears, his expression turning weird, “Hmph! Don’t think that giving me a little favor will make me wholeheartedly work for you; you’re overthinking—I can be a noble dragon~”

“Ha, hearing such words from a dog’s mouth is kinda funny~” Merlin gave a dry laugh and continued, “Anyway, my demands on you aren’t high—just learn to cheer up my daughter, and if there’s danger, remember to step forward; that’s your task. Though you’re indeed weak, training your body here still has its benefits.”

“I’m a dragon, not a pet! Forcing me to submit to you is bad enough, but you actually want me to fawn over a little brat? If I really gave in, I’d be a disgrace to dragonkind!” Aweis’s mouth was very hard; he absolutely refused to admit he’d submitted to Merlin, yet his body was honest, trotting behind Merlin with a wobble.

“You’ve picked up a great bargain—following me is better than staying in Demon City waiting to be eaten. After being imprisoned so long, even returning to the Church won’t earn you trust; you can’t go back to your former life.” Merlin had seen through Aweis; this holy dragon, aside from following him, had no other choice.

“Hmph! Even if you’re right, so what? I serve you, not your daughter; I hope you understand that.” Holy Dragon Aweis said coldly.

“My daughter is very cute.” Merlin said softly.

“Huh? Really cute? Really?” Aweis widened his eyes, then shook his head, “No, no, no—this isn’t about cute or not; I’m a great holy dragon! Even if I died, I could never lower myself to coax a little child.”

“Be careful—even the insects here could kill you.” Merlin, uninterested in listening to Aweis’s nonsense, quickened his pace.

Holy Dragon Aweis panicked, forgetting his dragon’s dignity, frantically wagging his dog tail.

“Wait for me! Don’t leave me behind—isn’t it just to cheer up your daughter? I can do it!”

“Look at how my tail wags! Besides being a pet, I can also be a floor‑cleaning janitor.”

Merlin and Aweis made it before nightfall to the center of Despair Canyon, where several black mountains stood, majestically connected.

All around was silence; Merlin surveyed for a long time but found no trace of King Kong, feeling puzzled—normally, magical beasts are highly sensitive to intruders on their territory.

Suddenly a tremendous roar rang out; waves of sound wrapped in wind uprooted the tall trees here, the earth rumbled, and something monstrous was rapidly approaching!

“Lucifer! Something’s wrong! Run!” Holy Dragon Aweis’s fur stood on end, like a hedgehog on high alert, his eyes filled with terror—

“This aura isn’t that of an ordinary magical beast; it’s completely unlike the ones we met on the road!

It’s simply… just like a beast that luckily survived from the age of the gods!”

“No, I’m already feeling my legs go weak.”

title: Chapter 22 — Bold Idea
content:
Chapter 22 — Bold Idea

Volume 37 · Chapter 22

Aewis's teeth were chattering wildly; if Merlin hadn't been nearby, it might have already turned tail and fled.
The overwhelming pressure forced Aewis to crouch on the ground, staring in terror at the direction the roar came from.
Although Aewis had never seen a magical beast that survived from the Age of Gods, this aura somewhat resembled that of the dragon clan's leader when he was alive.

“Lucifer! Didn’t you hear me speaking? If you don’t run now, it’ll be too late! Are you trying to get yourself killed and drag me down as a shield?”
“Don’t be so afraid; it’s my friend, the master of this region,” Merlin replied calmly.

“Friends? What a joke! How could a magical beast befriend a demon? They’re nothing but mindless savage beasts!” The holy dragon Aewis frowned, thinking Merlin must have gone mad, deliberately coming here to provoke such a terrifying existence—

A stout black chimpanzee descended from the sky, landing and kicking up a violent wind that gouged a deep pit in the canyon floor.
King Kong appeared much as before, save for a few new scars—clearly left over from battles with other captured beasts.

Merlin looked at the mighty King Kong, a faint smile spreading across his face as he remarked, “You’ve gotten a lot stronger than before, huh? Looks like quite a few magical beasts have suffered.”

“Huh?” Aewis lay trembling on the ground, thinking, “No way… Does Lucifer really know this magical beast? I’ve only heard that only higher‑species magical beasts can communicate, and this black chimp doesn’t look like a higher‑species magical beast at all.”

King Kong lowered its body, bringing its massive nostrils close to Merlin to sniff carefully, as if confirming his identity. Suddenly its eyes lit up, and it excitedly pounded its chest with its fists, booming like thunder—
“Whoo‑whoo‑whoo‑whoo‑whoo~!”

“Ha, Merlin let out a slight sigh of relief, thinking that if he hadn’t seen him, King Kong would have forgotten him—apparently he’d been overthinking; even if King Kong is a magical beast, its memory isn’t that terrible.”

“Lucifer, how did you come to know this big guy?” Aewis shivered, asking, unable to fathom why this black chimp would show kindness to Merlin.

“I met him when I was young; back then I came here for training, and this fellow was my reliance in the canyon.” Merlin gave a thumbs‑up, pointing at the exuberant King Kong.

“There’s actually such a good thing?” Aewis gasped, for being able to tame such a powerful magical beast before one’s eyes is the wish of countless people, and in any nation it would be a guardian‑god‑like existence.

After King Kong reluctantly calmed down, it finally noticed the Erha beside Merlin; since Aewis seemed too weak in its eyes, it disregarded the dragon’s majesty.
For King Kong, the Despair Canyon held far more prey stronger than Aewis—so a holy dragon falling into this canyon was merely a snack in the mouths of all manner of magical beasts.

King Kong stretched out its huge hand, plucking the tiny holy dragon Aewis from the ground and holding it up for close inspection, as if a person were picking up a cockroach with their fingers.
“Lucifer! What is it doing?! Quick, save me!” Aewis was terrified, on the verge of fainting at any moment; even if it recovered its dragon form, it would be no match for this giant gorilla.

“Don’t be afraid; it won’t hurt you,” Merlin soothed Aewis, believing King Kong should have no interest in it, since Erha wasn’t on its menu.

“Really? Really?” Aewis anxiously stared at King Kong, inwardly pleading for the gorilla to spare him.
Yet things turned out a bit beyond Merlin’s expectation: although Erha wasn’t on King Kong’s menu, curiosity is a trait shared by all species, and it certainly didn’t mind sampling the flavor.

Then King Kong opened its massive jaws and shoved the holy dragon Aewis inside in one gulp, with cries of alarm echoing from its throat—
Aewis: “Lucifer!!! I#@￥%”

Merlin:

The sun slowly set, and the peril‑filled Despair Canyon returned to silence.
Aewis the holy dragon regained its true dragon form, its body slick with King Kong’s saliva, lying limp and powerless on the ground.
Its eyes were hollow and void, endless dread seeping into its heart; it felt defiled, no longer pure.
Just moments ago Aewis had brushed past the gates of hell, only to be spat out by King Kong’s mouth in disgust, unable to tolerate the foul stench the giant lizard emitted.
After trying it, King Kong lost all interest in Aewis entirely, deeming dragon meat unpalatable and inferior to the taste of magical beasts.

King Kong sat in a little nest piled with straw, its towering bulk like a small hill, occasionally letting out grunts from its nose.
Merlin stood on its shoulder, watching the afterglow of the sunset; he hadn’t been here in a long while, and the familiar scenery had changed somewhat, prompting him to marvel at how swiftly time flies.

“Long time no see—how’s life been for you here?”
“Whoo‑whoo.” King Kong patted its own biceps, then raised a thumb to indicate it was doing well, and pointed at Merlin.

“As for me? I’m doing fine too—after leaving, I successfully completed my revenge and reclaimed what was mine, all thanks to your help.” Merlin patted King Kong’s thick neck.

King Kong shook its head, pointed at itself, then kept waving its hands, yet raised a thumb for Merlin.
Merlin barely grasped King Kong’s meaning: it was saying that none of this had anything to do with it; everything was achieved solely by Merlin’s own efforts.

“Whoo‑whoo‑whoo‑whoo.” King Kong pointed at Merlin, then at the ground beneath its feet.
“Oh~ … Actually I have nothing else; I just came to see you.” Merlin paused, then added, “Besides, I have a few questions I’d like to ask you.”

King Kong scratched its head, indicating it wasn’t clear what Merlin wanted to know, and that a special trip here wasn’t necessary.

“You’ve actually seen the demon race’s prophet in person, right? Or rather, you know it.” Merlin had once tried asking this question, but back then he hadn’t received a definite answer.

After hearing that, King Kong fell silent for a long while, continually scratching its head as if trying to grasp Merlin’s meaning. Although it can communicate with humans, its wisdom is truly low, nowhere near that of the powerful elemental magical beasts.
It is certain that, while King Kong may not rank as high as an elemental demon king, its strength is hardly inferior—after all, it is a magical beast that survived from the Age

title: Chapter 23 — The Release
content:
Chapter 23 — The Release

Volume 37 · Chapter 23

Merlin asked this question not out of random guesswork, but because he had a vague feeling about it.

Two of the three prophecies left by the seer were related to him, and especially the third-day prophecy, which seemed to be tailor-made for him. Combined with his experiences in the God's Ruins, it reminded him of the danger here, allowing him to barely escape from the ruins.

Especially the simple Chinese characters left on the torn cloth, which made Merlin deeply terrified, and he couldn't help but doubt that there was another traveler before him.

Merlin didn't want to believe in so many coincidences, and why was he unconsciously covered by the shadow of that distant seer?

So Merlin had to come up with this bold idea, after all, he was also a traveler, and he had some understanding of science fiction.

Gold just kept silent, and he didn't know how to express his meaning clearly to Merlin, which was obviously very difficult.

Merlin closely watched Gold, paying attention to every little movement of it, perhaps a subtle action could reveal a surprising secret.

After a while, Gold finally gave a strange reply, pointing to the sky and nodding, which seemed to be an affirmative reply.

"Uh?! Is it me?" Merlin was shocked, his mind was in chaos, wondering if the seer was himself or if there was another person who looked extremely similar to him. He couldn't have appeared in the distant era of the gods!

Just as Merlin was in a mess, Gold added another reply, pointing to the ground and shaking his head, this time denying Merlin's identity?

"Ah?! ??"

Merlin was confused, completely unable to understand what Gold wanted to express. First, he acknowledged himself as the seer, and then denied it? Gold's contradictory answers really put Merlin in deep confusion, and he couldn't find the real answer—damn it, what does Gold mean? Is this answer so difficult to answer? Nodding and shaking one's head represent what?

Merlin frowned, hoping to get an accurate answer, so he reorganized his words and tried to ask, "What does it mean? Am I really the seer?"

Gold started scratching his head, even he was confused and didn't know how to let Merlin understand what he was expressing.

Merlin sighed helplessly, looking down, it seemed that even Gold himself couldn't express it clearly, and it would be difficult to get the real answer.

But from Gold's reaction, Merlin was sure that he was absolutely connected to that seer.

Perhaps in the depths of the unknown, the seer of the demon race was protecting Merlin, which is why prophecies were left for him.

As for why many prophecies were related to Merlin, perhaps in the distant era of the gods, the seer had already glimpsed all of Merlin's fate.

Merlin and Gold lived in the Valley of Despair for two and a half months before Aivis successfully strengthened his body and decided to leave.

A white giant dragon emerged from the scorching lava, soaring in the sky, its scales shimmering like metal, dazzling and eye-catching.

Following Merlin's guidance, Aivis found the hidden black giant tree in the depths of the valley, using the tree oil to nourish and forge with lava, strengthening his body.

In just half a month, Aivis' strength had significantly increased, transforming from Saint-tier to Zong-tier, and even possessed the same anti-magic traits as Merlin, making him a nightmare for mages.

After the transformation, Aivis was ecstatic, even though he wasn't a match for the Flame Dragon King, his new magical dragon body could still hold its own against the dragon leaders.

"I feel my body is very light and full of magical power! I never thought I could strengthen my body to this extent!" Aivis spread his dragon wings and landed gracefully in front of Merlin, looking at his new body with satisfaction. It was much stronger than before, almost like he had been reborn.

Following Merlin for just a few days and already receiving such great benefits, Aivis couldn't help but admire his initial choice. At least, clinging to Merlin's leg meant he could drink and eat well.

This was much better than in the church, where the Pope, Jorgen, was stingy and only satisfied Aivis' vanity with formalities, providing no real benefits.

But following Merlin was different. Although it seemed subservient on the surface, the benefits he received were all tangible! Aivis wasn't stupid, he knew the difference, even if he didn't admit it with his mouth, his body would always be honest.

"How about it? Do you feel good?" Merlin felt that Aivis' dragon scales were like gemstones, almost like he had put on a new outfit, and he was also satisfied.

"Cough! Cough!" Aivis looked embarrassed, feeling a bit conceited, and quickly adopted a proud attitude, saying with a hard mouth, "It's fine, I didn't expect such a brutal body-forging technique to have such an effect. It's decent enough."

Merlin smirked, thinking that this stupid lizard was being greedy, "Following me is good, right? It's better than you being drunk and sleepy in the church, isn't it?"

"Hmph!" Aivis snorted, arguing, "I didn't seek your help voluntarily, it was you who forced me, although you are a bit better than the church~"

"A bit better? Don't you remember who was following you two months ago, eagerly following you to see that mysterious ancient tree, and couldn't be dragged away~" Merlin said with a mocking tone.

The Saint Dragon Aivis blushed, feeling humiliated, "This is temporary restraint, for the sake of future freedom, I have to compromise. Although my body is enslaved by you, my soul will never be!"

"Haha" Merlin laughed, thinking that Aivis was like an old antique, no matter how bad he was, he wouldn't give up his noble dragon pride.

Actually, Merlin was willing to help Aivis a little, because this guy was honest, after being enslaved by demons, he still obeyed the agreement and guarded the blood pool for a long time.

Even after growing new wings, he didn't have any thoughts or actions to escape, although his mouth was always unwilling to submit, and he often boasted to the demons, but there was no substantial damage.

In addition, there was an incident where Merlin was not present, and his daughter Chris was kidnapped, which made him realize that he and Alice might sometimes be unable to protect Chris, so a strong guardian was needed to stay with Chris.

Initially, Merlin thought of Gold, but this ancient demon was very attached to its homeland and didn't want to leave the Valley of Despair, so Aivis took advantage of this opportunity and became the best choice to guard Chris.

Therefore, Aivis' strength couldn't be too weak, it had to be able to deal with most dangers. Considering this, Merlin reluctantly agreed to help Aivis, and having a pet for Chris was secondary, the main priority was selecting a bodyguard!

"We are leaving now, Gold, take good care of Chris."

In the distant United Kingdom, the dwarven kingdom.

The Dwarven King was carefully wiping his valuable treasures with silk, treating them like his own dwarves with great care.

Suddenly, the ground began to shake violently, and the bottles and jars on the counter shattered, the Dwarven King cried out in distress.

"Oh! No! Damn it! What's happening?"

The Dwarven King rushed to the balcony, and he saw that in a certain position in the Golden City, a beam of divine light pierced the sky, which was quite impressive—

The key to killing Cain, the murderous sword Mistral, was forged today!

title: Chapter 24 — The Mistling
content:
Chapter 24 — The Mistling

Volume 37 · Chapter 24

In the dwarves' golden city, a fierce blazing light shot straight into the sky, causing a violent tremor, like a sharp sword blade slicing the heavens, the strange sight visible for hundreds of miles!
Although no one knew what exactly happened in the golden city, an inexplicable pressure kept spreading, and everyone could feel that something terrifying had been born!
The light pierced the sky, forming a rainbow that spanned the sun; countless dwarves stopped their work and lifted their heads to gaze at the various odd phenomena.
After countless epochs, that legendary secret treasure long lost—the great killer that had taken the lives of many ancient gods—Mistartin reappeared!
Who would have thought that, after the Gods Era had passed for so long, someone would still attempt to forge a powerful artifact? After all, the era has changed; many things differ from the Gods Era, and forging an artifact is nearly impossible to succeed.
The church once poured tremendous effort into trying to create a true artifact befitting the present age, but ultimately failed, only managing to forge the inferior pseudo‑artifact Scarlet Enchantress.
This shows how difficult it is to obtain a genuine artifact—not just by piling materials and possessing superlative forging skill, but also requiring favorable timing and location.
The dwarf king gazed at the brilliant light, his anger welling up from nowhere; recalling his expensive collection that had just been smashed, he felt a pang of heartache and gritted his teeth, muttering—
“Who the hell did this? I will surely twist his head off!”
“Your Majesty, just now the guards reported that this disturbance is related to Master Balin; the light came from Master Balin's smithy.”
“What? Master Balin?” The dwarf king's heart gave a thump, his expression somewhat embarrassed, “Oh, then it's fine, retreat.”
“Really okay? Master Balin caused such a big mess.”
The dwarf knight hesitated, thinking that given the dwarf king's temperament he would surely punish severely the culprit behind the disturbance, yet upon hearing it was Master Balin he swallowed his anger back.
Obviously this dwarf knight did not know that the dwarf king fears not Master Balin, but the demon lord standing behind Master Balin!
In the past, the dwarf king would certainly have harshly punished Master Balin, venting all his anger, but now he can only tuck his tail and act like a person; he has not forgotten how Merlin pressed him to the ground and rubbed him, and even succeeded in defeating the elemental magic beast guarding the gold essence.
If the dwarf king were not an idiot, he would surely not lightly provoke Merlin this 'bandit'; moreover, Merlin and Master Balin seem to have a good relationship, punishing Master Balin, lest Merlin come again, he estimates his treasury's possessions would not be safe.
Having lost the gold essence, the dwarf king to this day still cannot forget, often sighing late at night; Merlin's 'bandit' silhouette has long become an indelible shadow in his heart, and if possible he hopes never to see that face in this lifetime.
‘Take that… just treat this as if it never happened, retreat!’ the dwarf king angrily barked, continuing to gaze at the light tearing the sky, muttering—
What is Balin up to? Causing such a big commotion
The strange spectacle lasted about a few minutes before disappearing; all the light converged and gathered in the small hut of the smithy.
Actually Master Balin was also very embarrassed; he had not expected that the emergence of Mistartin would cause such a huge disturbance, nearly frightening him into unconsciousness.
After the freshly forged Mistartin had caused a commotion and finally calmed, it lay still immersed in the icy, piercing water, no longer releasing its pressure.
The Balin father and son in the smithy secretly let out a sigh of relief; fortunately the disturbance was brief, otherwise they would not know how to settle this.
Bali climbed up from the ground, secretly gazing at Mistartin in the water, and asked cautiously, “Father, has this guy finally calmed down?”
“Looks like it; good that after the artifact emerged it only released pressure, not caused an explosion, otherwise my smithy… well, perhaps the whole golden city would be flattened.” Master Balin picked up the towel around his neck and kept wiping the cold sweat from his forehead.
“This thing's emergence is too exaggerated; where is it a weapon? It's basically a monster waking up. I've been learning forging techniques from you, Father, for so long, yet this is the first time I've encountered such a situation.” Bali's mood remained unsettled for a long time; the strange spectacle Mistartin had just emitted was enough to refresh his cognition.
“Don't say it's your first time encountering this; even I am experiencing it for the first time. Originally, when an artifact is forged it is this terrifying.” Master Balin furrowed his brows seriously, yet his eyes hinted at a hint of excitement; he had always been passionate about forging, and the
quality of the product is the sole standard for measuring a blacksmith's worth.
Without exaggeration, the Mistartin just forged is Master Balin's finest work, second to none, a masterpiece capable of shocking the world!
Ordinary people probably cannot fathom Master Balin's current mood; obtaining the finest materials and forging a timeless treasure is incredibly lucky for any blacksmith.
Master Balin's eyes actually glimmered with tears; his heart toward Merlin held only endless gratitude, willing to give him a chance to fulfill his dream.
“This is my life's masterpiece; afterwards I could never forge anything better, even if I die I would have no regrets.”
“Father, don't say that; you should feel happy instead.”
Fairy Phyllis lifted the bowl on her head, excitedly circling the roof; just now, because of Mistartin's pressure, she had been frightened into hiding—
“Did it succeed? It must have succeeded! Quick! Quick, pick it up and have a look!”
Master Balin smiled, lifted Mistartin from the water with a fresh towel, wiped away the remaining droplets, and instantly a cold gleam shone!
Even though Mistartin at this moment has not yet been sharpened, the light it emits is still frightening, giving the illusion of one's spirit being split apart!
Fairy Phyllis had to close her eyes; she felt uncomfortable, her head also began to ache, as if a knife were pressing on her forehead—indeed it is a divine artifact! Its emitted light possesses terrifying deterrence!
Freshly forged Mistartin is silver‑white, its shape almost identical to a katana; the gleaming blade resembles a bright mirror, clearly reflecting the entire smithy.
Although it looks extremely thin, like a sheet of paper, its hardness exceeds imagination, after all the materials are extremely rare.
Overall, the feeling it gives can be described in just two words—
“Sharp!”

title: Chapter 25 — The Place Where the Story Begins
content:
Chapter 25 — The Place Where the Story Begins

Volume 37 · Chapter 25

Mistertin is so thin that it seems unnecessary to sharpen it, because as soon as it comes out of the furnace it is already a naturally perfect weapon! Master Balin's heart could not be calm; he had no doubt that this Mistertin could pierce any form of defense, and solid things were nothing but paper before it. According to the legends of the Age of Gods, Mistertin possesses the power to slay gods; the god-slaying sword is also called the fatal blade, able to destroy all resurrection and regeneration, preventing the dead from rising again. Those slain by Mistertin, whether gods or demons, will completely vanish, with no chance even to become undead—that is the terror of the fatal blade. The fairy Feri flutters around Mistertin nonstop, exclaiming, 'Such overwhelming pressure—I dare not even approach closely, for I feel as if I would be stabbed the moment I get near.' 'Congratulations, Father!' Bart lifted his head, eyes full of excitement, 'With this work, your achievements can stand shoulder to shoulder with those of our ancestors!' 'No, still far from it.' Master Balin wore a helpless expression, feeling deeply disappointed; Bart's forging skill cannot compare to it, he cannot see the technique, yet after observing Mistertin he realized his own great shortcomings, unable to match the true forger of Mistertin—his forging technique is not even in the same dimension. 'Far from impossible? Father, did you see wrong? I think this weapon is already perfect, hardly different from the god-slaying sword of the Age of Gods in legend.' Bart scratched his head in confusion, unable to see where the difference lies. 'Compared to the true Mistertin, this blade has obvious flaws, which I cannot make up for.' Master Balin slowly closed his eyes, unable to help admiring that the ancestors were still superior; he had spent his life honing his forging skill, yet could not catch up to the great ancestors. 'Why?' Bart frowned, examining Mistertin closely, wondering if his father had gone senile. 'Although this Mistertin can approach the true god-slaying sword infinitely, its quality still falls short of the genuine article by a considerable margin—this is an insurmountable chasm for me, so no matter how close this blade comes to the genuine article, it will ultimately remain only a demigod weapon and cannot become a true divine artifact; although the quality differs by only one level, the difference is enormous.' Master Balin explained slowly, his heart filled with regret. 'We followed the secret method on the blueprint exactly, using the same materials, yet the finished product is completely different—where did we go wrong?' Bart wondered. 'The problem is not with the blueprint or the materials, but with me.' Master Balin sighed, speaking low, 'My forging skill is still insufficient; forging looks simple, but every hammer strike has its subtleties. With the same materials and method, I cannot forge a true Mistertin—this is the gap between me and the ancestors.' Bart fell silent, watching the gleaming silver Mistertin, he asked no more, for he understood that—being able to forge a demigod weapon is already his father's limit. Bart believed that if his own father could not forge a divine artifact, then after the Age of Gods it would be unlikely for new divine artifacts to appear, at least mortals could not achieve it. However, Mistertin being able to approach the genuine article infinitely could also be considered as giving Merlin an explanation. Two months later, the world situation changed again; following Dikteping's orders, the blood clan occupied Budapest, causing the Austro-Hungarian Empire to split and fall under blood clan slavery. Under Cain's protection, the former Budapest became the new Eternal Night Empire; although Dracula had died, his dream and shadow never dissipated, but instead grew ever more intense. A towering volcano rose over the ruins of Budapest, the ceremony to restart the Gate of Heaven had already begun; to assist Cain in returning to Heaven, all citizens of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, regardless of status, were enslaved and continually shoved into the volcano to be burned alive, becoming sacrifices for the ritual. The eerie sight made one's flesh crawl: countless people lined up, forced by vampires to jump into the volcano; after death, their souls were sucked into a huge black magic circle in the sky, countless people struggled in the magma, letting out horrific screams, yet no one stepped forward to resist. The enslaved humans had clearly become numb; from the moment vampires captured them, they lost all hope—even a weak vampire could command over a hundred humans, driving them with whips to leap voluntarily into the flames. More than half of the Austro-Hungarian Empire's human population was slaughtered; the surviving natives could only flee everywhere, yet still could not escape the claws, because the number of required sacrifices was far from enough—reopening the Gate of Heaven would demand a price beyond imagination! Even Dikteping felt terrified, thinking the cost of opening the Gate of Heaven was too great; at least half of humanity's nations would have to be destroyed for it to be possible, thus Cain would surely become the world's public enemy, facing the crusade of all mortals. Yet Cain cared nothing for this; she only wanted to return to Heaven to reason with her mother—killing everyone, becoming the world's public enemy—these were trivial matters, she feared no one who would come to crusade against her. Dikteping thought Cain had gone mad, his eyes fixed only on avenging himself against his mother, never considering the vampires; once Cain left, the painstakingly built Eternal Night Empire would surely be torn apart by humans. But Dikteping had no choice; his fate was bound to Cain's, he had lost all retreat and must obey her commands. Dikteping believed that as long as Cain did not leave the mortal world, the blood clan he had painstakingly established would temporarily be safe; taking this opportunity to develop quickly, perhaps after Cain's departure the blood clan would still have a foothold in the mortal world, just as demons guard the Demon Lord Palace, leaving humans with no good recourse. Under Cain's pressure, the blood clan soon began to strike at neighboring countries, even marching across the world, continuously capturing humans and sending them in an endless stream to the volcano as sacrifices, causing human disappearances to occur frequently; some remote villages vanished overnight. All nations had long sensed the gravity of the situation, secretly organizing troops to launch the largest-ever crusade against Cain, who hovered over the ruins of Budapest. This was an unprecedented event, and also the moment when the scattered human nations were most closely united—compared to demons, Cain had truly become the world's public enemy! What had the Church done in these two months? They remained silent, even held a pilgrimage province, and proclaimed that Cain was an emissary of Heaven, that the opening of the Gate of Heaven would let mankind once again witness the goddess's miracles and other confusing statements. In fact, Pope Geoffrey had made it clear he did not want to wade into troubled waters; having just barely recovered a mouthful of blood, he now faced a war against the Son of God.
