Although Cain is portrayed as evil in the scriptures, she is still the daughter of the Goddess, a significance far beyond ordinary, giving the Church ample excuse not to join the fight. Moreover, Cain's target is not the Church, which let Pope Geoffrey secretly breathe a sigh of relief as he busied himself maintaining the surface peace and prosperity of the Holy City. At this moment, on the coast of the British Orkney Strait. Merlin once again stepped onto this familiar soil with the Holy Dragon Aweis, gazing at the beach where he and Alice had once landed, feeling as if worlds apart—this is where the dream began— 'Three years 'I have finally returned! There will be an extra update later. Oh, right, the plot where Mistertin is lost is utter nonsense; I never intended to write such a thing, it's meaningless. What you most want to see now is the male and female leads reuniting for sweet moments, Merlin drawing his sword versus Cain drawing his sword, right?

title: Chapter 26 — Very Understanding
content:
Chapter 26 — Very Understanding

Volume 37 · Chapter 26

The sky had gradually grown dim. The town closest to the Orkney Strait was called Wickheim, a small city with a very prosperous fishing industry.

Here used to gather a large number of stationed legions, plus a solid fortress, used to resist the attacks of the First Demon Lord Palace in the north and prevent demons from landing.

But because three years ago the demons made a great migration, all going to the Sand Sea, the legions here had already been transferred away, leaving only an empty fortress.

Now Wickheim has become a genuine border town; without the soldiers of days past, it has become much desolate——

"Human and Dog," walking on the road to Wickheim——

After several days of raft navigation, Merlin planned to rest here for a few days, then head straight back to Rexham as quickly as possible to see Alice.

Merlin looked around at the scenery, and all sorts of memories flooded his mind. After snatching Alice's inherited Hero armor, the first human town he had ever entered was Wickheim. "This place really hasn't changed at all, it's just become much desolate. In the past, you could always see merchants coming and going on the road."

"You've been here before?" Avis asked in surprise.

"Of course. After leaving the demon race, most of my time was spent living in this kingdom." Merlin answered casually.

A drop of cold sweat slid down Saint Dragon Avis's forehead. He thought, if Lucifer lives here, can the Queen of Britain really sleep peacefully? Fortunately, it hasn't been exposed, otherwise how many people would be scared into madness?

"When there are other people around, remember not to speak." Merlin reminded him.

"Why? On what grounds can't I speak?" Avis felt somewhat displeased inside. Does he even want to deprive me of the right to speak?

"Because right now you are a husky. A dog should act like a dog. I'm afraid you'll speak human words and scare others. Oh right! Don't reveal yourself in front of my daughter either; just let her think you're an ordinary dog." Merlin emphasized, not wanting Chris to discover that a great dragon was staying by his side.

"That's too much, isn't it? If I don't speak, I'll suffocate to death." Avis protested, feeling this job wasn't exactly easy.

Merlin stopped walking and squatted down, grabbing Avis's dog head, and said meaningfully, "If you find it too difficult, I don't mind sending you back to the Demon City. Being slaughtered and eaten by demons is more refreshing than suffocating to death."

"Uh!" Avis's whole body of dog fur stood on end, he instinctively shivered, and would rather die than return to the Demon City, grinning foolishly——

"Hehe, I was joking."

"It's just not speaking, right? I can do it."

"As a proud dragon race, I also disdain communicating with low-level creatures~"

Just as Merlin intended to continue scolding Avis, a carriage slowly drove over, with a middle-aged man dressed as a merchant sitting on it, his face very ugly-looking, seemingly having been upset about something?

Merlin furrowed his brow slightly, feeling something was a bit abnormal. It was almost dark, how could there still be merchants leaving Wickheim? Normally, they should stay inside the town to rest and set off again at dawn.

The middle-aged merchant saw Merlin, so he stopped the carriage and kindly reminded him, "Travelers? Don't go to Wickheim anymore, it's already sealed off, no outsiders are allowed to enter. While it's not dark yet, quickly find a nearby village to stay."

"Ah? Did something happen?" Merlin had gone straight from the Demon City to the Death Marsh, all isolated areas, he didn't know at all what was happening in the world recently?

"Are you a savage living in the forest? How can you know nothing?" The middle-aged merchant was quite surprised, thinking he had met a visitor from outer space. The Blood Race's disaster is causing such a commotion, yet there are still people who don't know?

"Um..." Merlin thought for a moment, weaving a lie, "I live in a very secluded small village, I only came out recently, so I'm not too clear."

Avis raised his dog eyebrows, looking at Merlin with disdain, thinking this guy is really full of lies. What small village, that's a demon nest! A Demon Lord talking quietly with a human, what an eerie scene!

Merlin looked down at his wrist; the bracelet Orobos gave him really did work. As long as he wore it, no human would discover he was a demon.

The middle-aged merchant still felt it was strange. Even in the most secluded village, they should know about this. Vampire attacks on humans often happen in remote, secluded places, not in densely populated capitals. But he didn't think much more. "Since when, everywhere there are signs of vampires. Frequently human corpses sucked dry are found. The problem cannot be solved for a long time, and the situation instead worsens. The distant Austro-Hungarian Empire was conquered by the vampires. They began constantly capturing humans as slaves, without mercy throwing them into volcanic mountains to burn to death. Some villages even disappeared overnight. Now everyone is very afraid. Vampires mixed in the crowd are hard to discover. To prevent similar situations from occurring, Wickheim chose to seal the city and refuse any outsiders."

Merlin frowned tightly, only then learning some current events, so he lowered his head to think. He hadn't heard news of vampires for a long time. Why, after only three years, are they coming out again swaggering and causing trouble? Did something turbulent happen inside the Blood Race?

"You'd better be careful. Don't walk around after dark. Without the sun's protection it's very dangerous, you could bump into wandering vampires at any time!" The middle-aged merchant dared not linger, rushing to find a place to stay before dark, quickly driving away.

"Wait!" Merlin wanted to ask something more, but found the middle-aged merchant had already gone far, "Tsk! Only way is to go to Wickheim and see the specific situation."

"Truly interesting." Avis snickered, feeling it was somewhat interesting——

"A mere human reminding the Demon Lord to be careful?"

"Once night falls, who is the prey is still uncertain."

When Merlin and Avis arrived at the gate of Wickheim, they were indeed blocked by a crowd of guards guarding the town, saying they absolutely would not allow them to enter.

"The Baron issued a decree today. To protect the safety of Wickheim, recently refusing all outsiders, please leave."

Merlin pointed at the sky, awkwardly saying, "It's almost dark, can't I just go in and stay for a night?"

"No! This is the Baron's order!" The soldier said seriously. Merlin was obviously not the first outsider driven away today.

"I'm

title: Chapter 27 — Keep Them Out
content:
Chapter 27 — Keep Them Out

Volume 37 · Chapter 27

Avis exclaimed, tilting his dog head involuntarily. No way? This guy is a Demon Lord, and to sneak into Wickheim he’s using any means? But with Lucifer’s protection, there’s indeed no need to fear the threat of vampires. The soldier, hearing Merlin’s words, felt bewildered, scrutinized Merlin carefully, and replied, “I don’t think you’re here to apply for a guard position; you seem more like a wanderer whose head is full of schemes to get into Wickheim. Sorry, that’s not allowed—no guard unit would recruit someone like you.” Avis gaped in shock, thinking these foolish humans must be idiots, completely unaware of what they’ve just turned down. This is the protection of the demon monarch—normally something people would beg for! “Huh?” Merlin frowned, wondering if it was because he could only serve as a guard for three days, and these soldiers took him for a scrounger trying to mooch food and drink in Wickheim. “Really, won’t you consider it at all?” “What’s all the commotion here?” Hearing the voice, they looked over and saw a man in neat clothing, escorted by a crowd, stepping out of Wickheim’s gate and approaching Merlin, continually sizing him up. Observing his attire, anyone could tell he was a nobleman—the twisted little mustache on his face was quite distinctive. Indeed, upon seeing this man, the soldier immediately stood straight and respectfully greeted, “Baron! This is Baron Boen, who governs the entirety of Wickheim, his family having tilled this land for generations, the most prestigious noble here. Baron Boen stared at Merlin for a while, his eyes showing a hint of impatience, and demanded, “What’s going on?” The soldier hurriedly leaned in to Baron Boen’s ear and relayed Merlin’s desire to enter Wickheim. Baron Boen nodded, understood the situation, looked again at Merlin, and said, “Sir who has come from afar, I apologize for the inconvenience, but the lockdown of Wickheim is for the safety of the townsfolk, so for half a month no outsiders may enter. As for hiring guards, we no longer need them, because we have received the goddess’s favor—Father Mata Solis, returning from the Vatican, will take charge of Wickheim’s security. With him, we don’t need to increase the number of guards.” “A priest returning from the Vatican?” Merlin couldn’t help but frown; he knew that priests’ main work wasn’t combat but preaching, and it was the Holy Knights who represented the Church’s military might—relying on a single priest to guard a town sounded rather foolish. “That’s right, this is Father Mata Solis. He’s been at the side of the Cardinal for many years, an outstanding student. Now that he’s completed his studies and returned home, he’s begun to give back to his hometown, spreading the gospel of the goddess.” Baron Boen proudly introduced the young man beside him: Father Mata Solis stepped forward, clad in a white robe emblazoned with the church insignia, holding a staff and scripture, his expression haughty. “Yes, I will do everything in my power to protect the safety of our hometown. Mary will never abandon her children; I am the beam of light the goddess casts upon the mortal world. Evil vampires before me will have nowhere to hide.” Merlin looked at the young priest, sensing his faint aura, and could tell that at best he was only mid-tier. Perhaps in a backwater like Wickheim that might be passable, but viewed against the world it’s nowhere near enough—at most he could handle an ordinary vampire. If the invading forces were numerous, this clueless young priest would instantly become fodder, incapable of any resistance. You’re merely a priest. “What’s wrong? Sir, are you questioning my ability?” Father Mata Solis’s face darkened; since returning from the Holy City he’d been lavished with praise, his ego swollen, leaving no room for criticism from an outsider. In a place like Wickheim, he even felt a sense of being above ten thousand people. “That’s right, I am questioning your ability.” Merlin was equally frank, bluntly saying that relying on a priest to guard the town was unreliable—if it were the Holy Knights, that would still be acceptable. “What qualifications do you have to question me? I’ve studied under the Cardinal in the Holy City for years—I’ve memorized every passage of the scripture, learned exorcism magic, and even had close-quarters combat with vicious demons.” Father Mata Solis seethed inside, thinking, “How dare a wandering outsider dressed like a vagrant dare to question me?” “You’ve fought demons?” Merlin was surprised, thinking this young priest had no experience whatsoever, utterly unseasoned—basically a fresh graduate whose head is full of textbook theory, lacking any real-world practice. “Of course!” Father Mata Solis’s expression turned somewhat arrogant: “Three years ago, during the Holy City’s defense battle, I personally slew a terrifying demon and even received the pope’s commendation~” Merlin gave a dry chuckle, thinking, “Ah, that’s from back then. Behemoth, in his assault on the Holy City, threw all demons—strong or weak—onto the front lines as cannon fodder. So the demon the young priest likely killed was just a lowly grunt. What’s there to be proud of? And the papal commendation? Worthless.” Avis, who knew the full truth, couldn’t bear to watch, covering his dog eyes with his paw. After so many years in the Church, he knew exactly what sort of people priests are— “Good heavens! This young priest is nothing but a frog in a well! In front of a true Demon Lord, bragging about killing a mere grunt demon—what’s there to brag about? If you told him the Demon Lord stood right before him, he’d probably faint on the spot. No wonder the Church produces priests like this—stubborn and corrupt, unchangeable.” “You killed a demon and received the pope’s commendation?” Baron Boen widened his eyes in admiration, exclaiming, “No wonder you’re the Cardinal’s star pupil—Father Mata Solis, you are practically the glory of Wickheim! Everyone will be proud of you.” After being praised by the baron, Father Mata Solis felt a bit smug, looked Merlin up and down, and said with a sharp tone, “Now you know the gap between us, don’t you? I’ve seen plenty of self-important outsiders like you—nothing but people trying to satisfy their desires by any means. Wickheim has no welcome for country bumpkins like you.” Merlin chuckled, not offended, thinking that if you weren’t hot-blooded you wouldn’t be young—“Well then, Father, how do you plan to deal with the vampires?” “That’s none of your concern; I have plenty of ways to deal with evil vampires—holy water baptism? Or reciting scripture? If that fails I can use exorcism magic.” Father Mata Solis brimmed with confidence, sneering, “And you? Is that blade on your waist just for show? Or maybe for cutting wheat? And you brought along a ridiculous hopping dog—how laughable.” Hearing this, Avis instantly bristled; Merlin could call him his dog, but nobody else could. His fur stood on end, he bared his sharp fangs, and inwardly he cursed, “This clueless fool dares to mock me! I’m a noble dragon!” Merlin kicked Avis, tossed aside the notice he was holding, and gave a meaningful smile, saying, “Well, there’s nothing more to say. I can only wish you gentlemen good luck.” Avis followed Merlin away, turning back to take a deep look as Wickheim’s great gate slowly closed. He shook his head at these foolish humans, who would rather trust a half‑baked young priest than believe in the invincible Lucifer. They will never know what is being kept out at the door, and will likely have to pay for their ignorance.

title: Chapter 28 — Karma (Monthly Vote Bonus)
content:
Chapter 28 — Karma (Monthly Vote Bonus)

Volume 37 · Chapter 28

Forced by circumstance, Merlin and Avis had no choice but to spend the night camping in the wilderness several kilometers away from Wickheim.

They planned to rest for one night and head directly to the next town the following morning, hoping they wouldn't run into anything like a town lockdown.

A bonfire rose, making this desolate wilderness the only source of light——

Merlin kept adding firewood to the flames, his expression thoughtful. A few suspicions were taking shape in his mind.

Dracula was already dead, and the remaining two Vampiric Progenitors certainly wouldn't have the guts to cause such a massive disturbance.

From how the Lamias sought out the God Ruins, it was clear they deeply feared Cain coming after them.

So the current situation was likely in turmoil——Cain had already killed the Lamia and another Progenitor, and was now performing some kind of evil ritual, which is why he needed to keep capturing humans and throwing them into volcanoes to be burned alive.

Aside from this, Merlin couldn't think of any other answer. Cain absolutely needed a massive number of humans, otherwise there'd be no reason to be this疯狂.

Avis lay beside the bonfire, snorting through his nose a bit resentfully. "Those foolish humans actually rejected your protection and chose a young priest who only knows how to talk big on paper."

"No choice, right? Should I go shouting that I'm the Demon Lord? This isn't humanity's flaw, it's a problem shared by all races——easily deceived by their own eyes. They'd rather believe the illusions they see with their eyes than accept the truth hidden in the mist." Merlin replied dismissively, not caring much about the matter.

"I've lived in the Church for a long time. Many priests are exactly like this——stubborn! Pedantic! And unwilling to let go of their useless faith~"

Avis snorted through his nose and continued. "Faith is clearly a tool used to deceive people, yet they deceive even themselves. They believe to their dying breath that noble faith can save their lives."

"What difference does knowing the truth make? People will always believe whatever they want to believe." Merlin said quietly.

Avis lifted his dog-like head and gazed at the sky. "By all rights, humans are so weak, lacking any real advantage compared to other races, and should never usher in their own era. Yet Maria ended up winning in the end. So humans won, how ironic."

"Being powerful doesn't guarantee the last laugh. Examples of the weak defeating the strong are everywhere. Weren't your dragon clan always proud of your strength? Yet you've never truly thrived." Merlin replied with a smile.

"I heard it's because the损失 during the Age of the Gods was far too great, causing you to lose your chance. Otherwise, humph humph~" Avis snorted triumphantly twice.

Swish swish swish——

The sound of footsteps rustling through the grass drifted over on the evening breeze.

Such faint movements shouldn't have been detectable, but both Merlin and Avis possessed formidable perception.

Merlin suddenly raised his head, looking into the pitch-black wilderness, his brows furrowing. "Who's there?"

Avis caught the scent in the air. Although it wasn't a real dog, the dragon clan's sense of smell was a hundred times more powerful than a hound. "There's a bloody stench. Someone wandering in the wilderness this late is most likely not anything good."

"And you're insulting yourself too?" Merlin glanced down at Avis.

Avis: "???"

"Hush——"

Several hundred meters away from the bonfire, a fully blue-skinned vampire was standing at the edge of the grass, relieving himself, pouring out the excess fluid from his body.

Although the membrane wings on his back were folded away, they were still conspicuous, and his physique was far stronger than a human's. A trident was planted beside him.

"Hurry up, hurry up, or I won't catch up with the main group——"

The vampire muttered, his body trembling violently in the night wind, letting out waves of pleasurable groans. He then put his member back into his pants and hurriedly tied his belt.

Just as he was preparing to take flight and catch up with his companions, he suddenly felt an overwhelming gravitational field press down upon him, and he crashed straight from the sky, unable to even crawl.

The vampire screamed in agony as cracks echoed from his bones. A pair of leather boots appeared before his eyes. He timidly raised his head and saw Merlin's expressionless face.

"A human?"

"Unexpected——I actually ran into a lone unlucky bastard." Merlin's smile deepened as he considered how to torment this poor wretch.

"Uh!" The vampire's face paled in shock, unable to comprehend why someone would exist in the middle of nowhere this late at night, let alone effortlessly suppress him. Clearly not a weakling. He bitterly regretted his terrible luck——even taking a piss could land him against an immovable object.

Merlin slowly crouched down, eyeing the vampire. "Why are you here?"

"I——" The vampire, unsure whether to be fearful or suspicious, decided to intimidate the human before him into letting him go. "Do I need to tell you? Hmph! A mere human dares to threaten me? You're nothing but a flock of lambs."

"Oh?" Merlin nodded toward Avis and commented, "Unexpected. This guy has some backbone, doesn't he?"

"Let me go right now, or you're dead! If the others discover I'm missing, they'll definitely come looking. When that happens, you'll be facing a siege——certain death!" The vampire curled his lips in a smirk. "We vampires possess immortal bodies. No matter how severe the injuries, we can recover. You can't do a thing to me. It's still not too late to let me go now."

"How impressive——this guy dares to threaten me?" Merlin said with genuine surprise. He thought, no wonder——after all, vampires possess powerful regenerative abilities. That's the confidence they have even when cornered.

"What's wrong, human? Scared yet? Drop your creepy magic right now!" The vampire commanded in a show of bravado.

Avis looked at the vampire with a hint of sympathy in his eyes, thinking: *Scared my ass! This guy is definitely dead meat!*

"What a pity." Merlin grabbed the vampire by the hair, forcibly lifting his head. Demonic flames surged across his own face, revealing a demonic countenance as he asked in a raspy voice——

"Open your eyes wide and look carefully——am I human?"

The vampire's pupils rapidly contracted as a terrified scream echoed through the wilderness.

Meanwhile, the town of Wickheim was already engulfed in flames. The nocturnal vampire raiding party had successfully broken in.

They bound every human they encountered, planning to secretly transport them all to the volcanoes in Budapest as sacrifices before dawn.

Originally, vampires only dared to raid small villages, as it was less likely to attract attention. But due to Cain's ever-increasing appetite, they were forced to risk attacking towns, accelerating the进程 of restarting the Gate of Heaven.

Fortunately, the alarm had sounded early. Most of the townsfolk had been woken from their sleep and, seeking庇护, had all gathered in the town's church, hoping the "powerful" Father Matusoli could dispel the evil darkness.

The vampires continued to close in on the church, even entering the Goddess's domain. People of faith cried out in constant prayer, hoping the Goddess would descend a miracle to save this pitiful crowd.

Baron Born hid in the back, trembling with terror, his cold sweat drenching his sleep robe. He had placed all his hopes on Father Matusoli.

Because he trusted Matusoli, Baron Born had cut costs rather than expand his escort detail, resulting in the soldiers being quickly annihilated and the populace left unprotected.

Baron Born silently regretted his decision. If he'd only trusted that foreigner and recruited more guards——he was ultimately paying the price for his ignorance and stupidity.

"Father!"

"Hurry and think of something!"

"You are our pride, and Wickheim's only hope!"

Now leaving a hook here for Phoenix, to fill this thread later.

It's just a small side quest, maybe a few episodes with some seasoning thrown in——won't interfere with the main plot.

There's no point explaining further. Just take an example to understand.

Does holding your poop longer make it more satisfying when it finally comes out?

Hold it too long, and it becomes a sickness. Don't hold it long enough, and it's diarrhea.

Hold it just right, and it's pure bliss.

title: Chapter 29 — Foolish
content:
Chapter 29 — Foolish

Volume 37 · Chapter 29

The people of Weckheim had pinned all their hopes on Father Matasole alone, hoping he could drive away the night-attacking vampires.

However, this Father Matasole had already been scared stiff, his face bloodless, his body trembling like chaff, and the heavy tome in his hand was hard to hold.

It was obvious that Matasole was still too young, having almost no practical experience. Most of his methods for dealing with dark creatures were still at the theoretical stage.

Recalling the only demon he had killed—it had been badly wounded by other Holy Knights and was on the brink of death; otherwise, he would never have been allowed to claim the credit.

Right, Father Matasole was exaggerating his achievements. In reality, he was not outstanding, not brave, and had faced evil monsters face-to-face only a few times.

The reason he left the Vatican and returned to this border town of Weckheim was that he had been eliminated in the Holy City, and could only do itinerant preaching work.

Virtually all truly excellent priests had stayed in the Holy City, continuing to study beside several red-clad bishops, and would never come to a place like Weckheim.

Father Matasole widened his eyes, nervously swallowing saliva. With his mid-level power, he could at most entangle an ordinary vampire, and might even have a chance of winning.

Yet tonight's situation had exceeded everyone's expectations. The vampires attacking Weckheim this night were not only numerous but also formidable in strength.

It was clearly a meticulously planned operation. To abduct all the humans in Weckheim to Budapest, the vampires had made ample preparations.

And the leader was actually a Saint-tier vampire! Its body was far larger than other vampire nobles, and it had four arms, with prominent fangs that were thick and long!

This was the first time the vampires had decided to attack a human gathering place to capture more human sacrifices. The appearance of a Saint-tier vampire among them was not strange.

The humans huddled together, hiding in the church, surrounded by the night-attacking vampires. Evil shadows flickered with crimson light in their eyes, laughing mockingly.

In the vampires' eyes, all the humans here were lambs awaiting slaughter, prepared as sacrifices to be secretly sent to the volcano. Within a few days, no powerful kingdom knights would come to rescue Weckheim.

The burly Saint-tier vampire stepped forward, releasing a wave of pressure. Everyone present human felt they could hardly breathe; many fell into despair and wept bitterly, constantly praying for the Goddess's protection.

At this moment, even those who were not believers began to place their hopes in the illusory deity, which only made the vampires' arrogance more rampant!

"Ugh!" Father Matasole was near mental collapse, constantly retreating. In front of the Saint-tier vampire, he couldn't muster the slightest fighting spirit! How could he also not understand why a place like Weckheim, which was so backward, would produce a monster above Saint-tier?

Baron Bourne realized the situation was wrong. If even Father Matasole was more fearful than himself, did that mean Weckheim was doomed? "Father! Are you not a beam of divine light spread by the Great Goddess in the mortal world? Do not fear them! Be brave! If you retreat, Weckheim is finished!"

"But—" Father Matasole was about to speak, thinking his three-legged cat exorcism skills were impossible opponents for a crowd of vampires!

"You have many methods for dealing with evil monsters, why not use them now? What are you hesitating about?" Baron Bourne was immensely disappointed, recalling the outsider he had met before dark fell. No wonder that person had questioned Father Matasole; it turned out he had seen through this fellow's untrustworthiness all along! If only I hadn't been blinded!

Right! Let's drive Father Matasole to a dead end; he can only grit his teeth and go up. Taking out a bottle of holy water from his person, he randomly threw it at the nearby Saint-tier vampire.

Holy water indeed had some restraining effect on dark creatures, but the effect was negligible; it was impossible to repel evil spirits. Otherwise, the attack on the Holy City by demons wouldn't have forced the Holy Knights to go up and fight.

The Saint-tier vampire's body was slightly corroded by the holy water, emitting thin white smoke. For this monster, this damage was like an itch—meaningless, saying it had no deterrent effect.

"No effect? Not... it shouldn't be. The grimoire clearly says this can drive away evil spirits." Father Matasole frantically flipped through the grimoire, wanting to confirm it properly.

Father Matasole's stupidity was undoubtedly exposed. In the midst of battle, would the enemy give you time to read a book? As Merlin had expected, the young priest had no experience, merely someone who had learned some theoretical exorcism knowledge.

Seeing this, Baron Bourne instantly sucked in a cold breath, instinctively and slowly closing his eyes, thinking, It's over! Father Matasole simply cannot deal with vampires. How could I pin the hopes of Weckheim on such a person?

The Saint-tier vampire was enraged and suddenly lunged, grabbing Father Matasole's neck and lifting him from the ground.

Surrounding vampires emitted a dull mocking voice; it was obvious they were amused by Father Matasole's stupidity, and they were actually thinking of using holy water to drive them away?

Father Matasole struggled constantly, feeling he could not breathe, his face turning purple, yet he could not escape the claws. "Filthy monster!

Let me go!

The Saint-tier vampire narrowed his eyes, applying a bit more force. With a "crack," Father Matasole's neck was broken, and his body was thrown to the ground like garbage, to be devoured by other hungry vampires.

Everyone was scared stiff, fearing the vampires even more. Screams and cries rose and fell. Even Baron Bourne could not withstand the blow, sitting on the cold floor with his butt.

In the Goddess's church, evil monsters could kill humans at will. What great Goddess? What devout faith? Everything was worthless!

Just as the vampires continued to close in on the pitiful humans gathered together, the church's roof was suddenly broken open, and a vampire, not knowing who had thrown it from the sky, happened to be pierced through the chest by the Goddess statue's scepter!

"What?!" Baron Bourne lifted his head, not knowing what had happened? Thinking that people outside were still stubbornly resisting?

The vampire pierced by the scepter was dying, blood dyeing the Goddess statue red. "Enemy attack!"

The vampires in the church immediately became alert, beginning to scrutinize their surroundings, preventing a sudden attack.

Theoretically, all the resistance forces in the town had already been eliminated; there should be no one capable of resistance.

Moreover, Weckheim was in a remote area; even if there were support, it couldn't arrive so quickly!

The vampires couldn't figure it out, who exactly was making trouble with them, daring to defy death?

Hosh—

Merlin jumped down from the hole in the church roof, glanced at these pitiful "lambs," and joked, "Quite lively, this is like the Weckheim I came to before."

"Ah, Baron Bourne, seeing Merlin's figure, suddenly became stuttering, an uncontrollable tremor in his heart. It's you!"

"It seems you all aren't having much luck~" Merlin scanned the vampires present, meaningfully saying in a deep tone— "Beg me, beg me, and you can be saved. Don't go praying to any deity.

Those high-and-mighty beings have no mercy, sitting on God's throne, mocking your stupidity."

title: Chapter 30 — Appearance (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 30 — Appearance (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 37 · Chapter 30

Baron Boen stared at the suddenly appearing Merlin, still half doubtful in his heart, "Can you really do it?"

If I can't handle this group of vampires, why would I have come back? Besides, do you have any other choice? Mo Meilin.

Staring at the corpse of the young priest on the ground, he coldly snorted and said, "Do you choose to keep believing in that priest?"

Er! Baron Boen, faced with the incessantly approaching vampires, truly had no choice, and pleaded, "Please save Wickham!"

"I heard your humble plea, alright, I can make an exception to help you—open your eyes and see what is called"

"true talent?"

Merlin slowly closed his eyes; as his words fell, the vampires gathered in the church trembled their membranes and surged upward, baring fangs and claws.

, their expressions ferocious, they wished to tear apart the outsider who had suddenly appeared!

The leading Saint-tier vampire was even more ferocious, seizing a sharp bone blade, roaring as it charged at Merlin, everything in its path being

crushed; each step it trampled could shake the earth to pieces!

More than twenty vampires surrounded Merlin in a ring, their illusions sealing off all dead ends and escape routes, like a wolf pack conducting a

body hunt, the atmosphere instantly tightened to the point where people could hardly breathe!

Helpless people instinctively closed their eyes, not wanting to see the gruesome, bloody scene; most thought Merlin was seeking death!

Facing a siege by a group of vampires, the chance of survival is extremely low!

Only Baron Boen was unwilling, praying for a miracle; although he stared wide-eyed at Merlin, his heart had already risen to

his throat.

"You bunch of lowly sewer rats, do you really deserve to be called dark creatures?"

"Pa—"

Merlin's finger snap echoed outward, a terrifyingly powerful gravitational space unfolded, instantly enveloping each vampire.

Boom, boom, boom—successive thunderous blasts; all the attacking vampires felt a crushing pressure in an instant and were ruthlessly suppressed.

onto the ground!

More than twenty deep pits appeared; the battle ended, the vampires were crushed to bone and flesh by the gravitational space on the spot, becoming patches of

blood-fused mud!

Although the flesh and blood continued to wriggle, trying to repair their shattered bodies, under this degree of heavy blow, the regeneration speed

is extremely slow.

After the church fell silent again, people slowly opened their eyes to see the vampires turned into meat paste, and they all revealed expressions of disbelief.

, unable to believe what their eyes had seen; this seemingly ordinary outsider turned out to be such a powerful figure!

This... this

Baron Boen stared, mouth agape, unable to speak; the group of blood kin led by the Saint-tier vampire was instantly

overwhelmed in an instant, his feelings like riding a roller coaster—exciting—

, what terrifying strength this is! The powerful Saint-tier monster before him had utterly no ability to fight back!

"In the snap of a finger, the enemy vanishes to ashes? If I hadn't seen it with my own eyes, who would believe it?"

Even the kingdom's knights couldn't possibly do something like this!

He... he, just what divine being is he?

Baron Boen lifted his head, gazing deeply at Merlin's figure; although he isn't worldly wise, he has some experience—someone like Merlin who

can crush Saint-tier monsters is truly someone he's encountering for the first time.

This can't be blamed on Baron Boen being a frog in a well; it's the true portrayal of most people, for Wickham itself is a remote town of the British Kingdom.

a remote small town, encountering a Saint-tier powerhouse is as unlikely as winning the lottery.

Although Baron Boen is a noble, he is ultimately neither a warrior nor a mage, making it hard for him to come into contact with the top-tier powerhouses of the world.

Being misled by a young priest and losing his bearings is not strange.

"Your Excellency, just who are you?"

"Me?" Merlin turned his head, thought for a moment, took out his black iron adventurer's certificate from his pocket and wore it, saying, "A nobody black iron adventurer from"

Setherm, unknown and insignificant black iron adventurer.'

"Er!" Baron Boen frowned, suddenly feeling a myocardial infarction.

"Is this a joke on me?"

Merlin stayed two nights in Wickham, didn't linger long, and then prepared to continue onward to Setherm.

Although Merlin is concerned about the current vampire situation, seeing Alice and his daughter is more important.

These days Merlin has been treated like a king in Wickham, with people often coming to gawk and bringing lots of food and drink.

This left Avis somewhat confused, wondering what homage these humans were paying to the Demon Lord—truly spooky!

To Avis it felt like a flock of little sheep actively running up to the big gray wolf, vying to offer themselves.

Such a bizarre scene inevitably made Avis doubt the dragon's birth—could this still be the Demon Lord? No, it doesn't seem so!

Although many hope Merlin can stay in Wickham forever, obviously that's unrealistic.

Merlin shouldered his pack, taking Avis with him as he left Wickham; Baron Boen led a large crowd to see him off, the scene bustling.

Not lively.

This made Merlin feel somewhat uncomfortable; he didn't really like such chaotic scenes, and since he wasn't a leader sent down to inspect, why bother?

?

"Go back, I don't need you to see me off."

"We are all grateful for your protection of Wickham; we hope that if you have the chance, you can come back again, and we will warmly welcome you!"

Baron Boen paused, feeling grateful, and said, "Incidents like vampire night raids happen almost every night; I don't know how many

similar towns and villages to Wickham, destroyed overnight by monsters; meeting you is our fortune."

"Next time you won't turn me away at the door?" Merlin asked back.

"Misunderstanding! All misunderstanding, Mr. Merlin." Baron Boen's old face turned red, feeling very ashamed about the previous events, "I want you to

apologize, for I was too foolish."

Merlin smiled, turned and walked away directly; he was pressed for time and had no leisure to waste here.

"Wait a moment! Mr. Merlin!" Baron Boen shouted hurriedly.

"What else? I'm not staying; don't waste effort." Merlin frowned, feeling impatient.

"I know Wickham can't keep you, but please accept our gratitude; you're an adventurer, and I know the adventurers' customs." Baron Boen produced a small black box, holding it out with both hands to Merlin, "Your strength has deeply impressed me; I'm sure your commission is not small"

"we here are poor and remote, indeed unable to produce anything valuable, but this is a treasure left by my great-grandfather; it should"

"have some value; I hope you will accept it."

"Oh?" Merlin took over the dark self, opened it and found an ancient-looking ring, pitch black, not seeming like anything valuable—

"what the heck is this thing"

"a family heirloom?"

One week later, in the British royal palace.

On Queen Elizabeth's desk lay piles of recent documents about vampire attacks, each copy needing her personal

review and approval.

Such intense work left Elizabeth exhausted, not daring to rest; her sleep was severely insufficient, and dark circles appeared on her face.

The whole kingdom was thrown into chaos by the vampires, leaving no time to handle other matters; surely other human nations are the same.

Thus.

Elizabeth wrote furiously, her quill seeming to leave trailing strokes as she carefully examined the reports sent from all over the kingdom.

Reports.

"Your Majesty! Not good! Something big has happened!" Mersfield burst in from outside, not knocking, his face showing fear and excitement.

","Someone reported! Just now, that... cough cough! Sorry, it's Elgin the Great Swordsman who has appeared in the capital!!!"

Click—

Queen Elizabeth's feather pen snapped in response; she abruptly lifted her head, staring at Mersfield without blinking.

E("△°I)

title: Chapter 31 — Exposed
content:
Chapter 31 — Exposed

Volume 37 · Chapter 31

Merlin, accompanied by Aivis, passed through the capital of Britain; as soon as they entered the city, countless eyes were watching them.

Queen Elizabeth had long issued an order: if Merlin's trail were found within the kingdom, do not act rashly for the time being, and must notify her as soon as possible.

Merlin's identity as the Demon Lord had already been known to Elizabeth; allowing a demon king to roam the realm would be an extremely frightening prospect.

Recalling that the capital had once been seized by Mammon and other demons, Queen Elizabeth still shivers to this day and will not allow this to happen again.

However, because Merlin had lived in Britain without causing any serious harm, Queen Elizabeth's attitude toward him is now complicated.

Merlin lowered his head and weaved through the crowd, fiddling with the ring gifted by Baron Borne. He had been pondering it for several days, yet had never found anything special about this blackish ring. It looked like an ordinary iron ring, perhaps a bit old, barely able to be considered an antique, but it had no value to Merlin—

No way? The thing Baron Borne sent is just a trinket, maybe a betrothal token from his great-grandfather? After all, nobles have many romantic histories, and such stories spread through streets and alleys; it's quite common.

Merlin speculated in his mind, deciding to put it aside for now, to study it properly later; selling it as an antique would only fetch a few gold coins.

Aivis suddenly stopped, turned back, and noticed several faces that had been following him; this aroused its suspicion.

It looked around; all were human silhouettes. Forced to act, it began to bark like a dog, hoping Merlin would become alert.

“Wang wang!” “Hm?”

Merlin glanced at Aivis, then suspiciously looked behind, realizing something was off, but couldn't determine who was following him.

He pondered, thinking that in Britain he had no enemies; who would care so much about a black iron adventurer?

Just as Merlin was hesitating whether to bring a few people over to interrogate, a commotion erupted in the capital's market; a squad of knights swiftly approached and surrounded him.

“Zizhong Flower Knights?” Merlin surveyed the many knights before him, sensing ill intent, “What business?”

“By order of Her Majesty the Queen, we invite you to sit in the palace for a moment.”

The Zizhong Flower Knights appeared very tense, their hands never willing to leave the sword at their waist, fearing that Merlin might suddenly act.

Merlin slightly furrowed his brow, realizing that something was not simple: having a group of kingdom knights invite him? The air was thick with gunpowder.

Aivis couldn't even breathe, thinking, “Shit, did Lucifer cause something? That's why the knights came after me; now I'm ready to eat the fruit!”

In the palace's conference room, the sound of a table being slapped echoed; the situation was contrary to Aivis's expectations, completely different from what he had imagined.

“What does that mean? They actually had a group of knights escort me here, giving me no dignity?” Merlin glared at Queen Elizabeth, feeling displeased.

“No, no, no, I— I didn't mean that. I just have some important matters to discuss with Mr. Merlin.” Queen Elizabeth, on the verge of tears, had originally intended to adopt a hard stance after seeing Merlin, but after preparing a long speech, Merlin slapped the table and she forgot it all, collapsing like a deflated balloon, utterly lacking intimidation.

“Hmph! I'm not someone who fusses over trivialities; otherwise, you wouldn't have a good life!” Merlin snorted, continuing, “Even if you are the Queen of Britain, what does that matter? Do you think your wings are hard enough to challenge me? Naïve. Don't forget, who rescued you from the dungeon? Who generously helped you hold the throne? You still owe me a huge debt, and you haven't repaid it yet!”

“Uh! Seeing what you say, how could I possibly be at odds with you?” Queen Elizabeth hurriedly rose, standing behind Merlin, repeatedly pounding his back with two small fists; the queen's dignity and authority vanished instantly, turning into a maid who gets bullied every day. “Calm down; having the knights bring you here was also something unavoidable.”

“???” Aivis looked strange, its dog mouth almost falling to the ground; it thought, “Did I see correctly? The Queen of Britain, how could she be so subservient before Lucifer? Cheer up! You are a ruler of a nation! Don't be so spineless! No wonder Lucifer can roam the human realm for so long without trouble; even the ruler has yielded to it!”

Merlin's mood finally improved a bit; he opened his hand to Elizabeth and asked, “What exactly is the matter? I'm very busy right now; I can't help you clean up any mess.”

“The reason I had the knights intervene is because I fear you.” Queen Elizabeth answered seriously.

“Hmm? That's perfectly normal. Didn't you fear me before? Your sister had tried in countless ways to eliminate me, probably to the point of sleepless nights.” Merlin smiled calmly, thinking that Elizabeth's fear of him was normal, but the two had reached a consensus.

“That’s different, Mr. Merlin.” Queen Elizabeth paused, then said seriously, “Let us be honest for a moment; you are Demon Lord Lucifer III, and I already know that.”

“!!!” Aivis's little heart was again frightened; no way? The Queen of Britain knows Merlin's true identity? No ruler can tolerate…

No ruler can tolerate a Demon Lord in their own realm; the risk is too great for anyone to bear!

Merlin's heart went “clunk” as his demon identity was known to Elizabeth; this was unexpected.

But if Elizabeth can say it so openly, it means the matter isn't that serious.

After all, Elizabeth is a clever person; such matters can be discussed, and tearing each other's faces is no benefit to anyone.

Merlin tried to calm his own feelings, no longer hiding, and answered honestly.

“That’s right, I am your neighbor, the first Demon Lord of the North, Lucifer III.”

“.” Queen Elizabeth inhaled sharply; although she had known for a long time, hearing it spoken directly from Merlin's mouth felt entirely different.

“Where did you learn of this?” Merlin asked, suspecting that Elizabeth had been secretly investigating him all along.

Elizabeth wanted to speak but stopped, awkwardly answering, “Do you often spit on my knights?”

“The one called Missfield the female knight?” Merlin frowned, suddenly realizing, feeling a bit regretful—

“Tsk! I guessed it was her; indeed, was it still exposed?”

“If I had known this earlier, I shouldn't have been spitting on one person; cough cough.”

(=w=;)

title: Chapter 32 — Advancing Towards the Source of Calamity!
content:
Chapter 32 — Advancing Towards the Source of Calamity!

Volume 37 · Chapter 32

Merlin sighed, feeling there was nothing left to hide, and said, "Now that you know my identity, what exactly do you plan to do? Are you going to drive me out of Britain?"
Avis widened his eyes, thinking that if a normal ruler's mindset were applied, Merlin would definitely be driven out, after all, who would allow a time bomb to stay by their side?
"At first I really felt panicked, thinking you posed a great threat to my kingdom and that it was very likely to repeat the demon invasion." Queen Elizabeth answered truthfully.
"You're not wrong to think that, after all Mammon caused irreparable trauma to Britain, making mutual understanding impossible." Merlin nodded, feeling it was natural for the queen to think that way.
"But because of one person, I've changed my mind; now I believe I can have a good talk with Mr. Merlin, and perhaps we can clear up our misunderstandings." Queen Elizabeth shifted her tone.
"One person? Who?" Merlin frowned, thinking such a person must be very knowledgeable about the demon race, aside from those church folks, it seems no one could do that.
"It's Miss Alice; her sincerity dispelled my doubts, and I'm willing to believe what she says." Queen Elizabeth answered seriously, having learned many unknown demon secrets from Alice, as well as things closely related to Merlin, which gave her a deeper understanding of him.
"Alice?" Merlin slightly frowned and asked, "What did she say?"
"A lot; I basically know everything about you. The demon race isn't a monolith, and you stand out among demons. I'm deeply grateful for everything you've done for Britain; without your behind-the-scenes help, we might not have easily retaken the capital occupied by demons." Queen Elizabeth, knowing Merlin's covert actions—though not direct aid—said it played a decisive role in ending the war between humans and demons.
"I never thought of helping you; I just don't want the demon race to fall into a dangerous abyss, so ending the human-demon conflict is merely helping my own kin." Merlin showed no appreciation, despite his close relationship with the queen, both sides have their own positions.
"I understand, and I'm well aware of your contributions to maintaining peace, so I'm willing to believe you aren't an ambitious warmonger like Demon Lord Mammon, with no intention to harm humans." Queen Elizabeth said slowly.
"Don't be so confident—how could you see through my thoughts?" Merlin replied with a cold snort.
"If you truly had the ambition to enslave humanity, Britain wouldn't exist anymore, would it?" Elizabeth said lowly, thinking that with Merlin's power, destroying a human empire wouldn't be difficult; it's just a matter of whether he wants to do it.
"So, are you willing to fully trust me then?" Merlin asked in surprise.
"It's not that I trust you; it's Miss Alice who trusts you. If we compare you two as one person, Miss Alice is the kind side of your heart." Queen Elizabeth had already seen through Merlin: as long as Alice exists, even if Merlin is a demon lord, he won't act recklessly. Rather than Merlin leading Alice, it's Alice who subtly influences Merlin, continually pulling this fearsome demon lord toward the lawful good camp.
""Merlin doesn't want to acknowledge Alice's place in his heart, but he patiently asks, 'What exactly do you want?'"
"To be frank, I hope you can remain in the Kingdom of Britain." Elizabeth voiced her thought; from the start she had this idea, she's no fool—knowing Merlin isn't a threat, not keeping him would be a disservice to herself. If such a powerful figure as Merlin could stay in Britain, the benefits would far outweigh the drawbacks; any astute ruler would make that choice, not lightly giving up such a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.
"!!?" Avis gaped, utterly unable to fathom Queen Elizabeth's thinking, musing that keeping Lucifer would be like making a deal with a tiger—this is a great demon lord nobody can control! He clearly lacks Elizabeth's insight, unable to see the subtle relationship between Merlin and Alice.
"Mr. Merlin, I won't divulge your affairs, will keep all secrets, and won't disturb your life; however, I do not permit any demon other than you to enter my territory at will. I hope you can understand." Queen Elizabeth stated her condition, having learned from Alice that Merlin is an anomaly among demons; trusting him doesn't mean trusting other demons, especially given Mammon as a precedent—we must guard against that.
"Elizabeth, your little scheme is quite clever—keeping me here, are you trying to make me work for you? Don't dream; I won't obey anyone." Merlin slowly rose, warning, "My staying or leaving doesn't require others' consent; you and I aren't equals. I hope you realize that."
Elizabeth remained silent, her hopes dashed, yet she still had a roundabout solution: as long as Merlin could stay and continue living in Britain.
"I don't have time to keep chatting; I'm leaving, farewell." Merlin walked straight out of the conference room door, rejecting Elizabeth's suggestion, because he won't allow a mere kingdom ruler to stand above him, though he also saw through the queen's底线—Elizabeth had no recourse, lacking the courage to turn faces.
"Are you going back to see Miss Alice? Forget it, she's not in Rexham." Elizabeth suddenly said.
"Huh?"
"Miss Alice set out for Budapest a few days ago, preparing to subjugate the enemies stationed there."
Merlin and Avis swung open the palace hall doors; just now he learned the latest news—Alice had actually left Britain a few days ago.
The situation became complicated, as Alice decided to go subdue the dangerous Cain, which is very perilous.
Although Alice's divine artifact can restrain vampires and she has the strength to defeat a second-generation demon lord, wanting to triumph over Cain in his current peak form is nearly an impossible task.
Even Merlin, without Mister Poison, cannot completely kill Cain, let alone Alice.
Merlin stood before the palace gate, pondering carefully; he guessed that for such a perilous mission, Alice would definitely not bring her daughter, and would surely go alone.
However, Elizabeth just told Merlin that nearly all human nations have joined this subjugation, including the Thorn Knight Catherine and some volunteer adventurers, who are in the same party as Alice.
But Merlin clearly recalls that Cain mastered his own sword-drawing technique, slew Mammon, and reclaimed all his immortal power; thereafter his strength likely reached an unfathomable level, possibly rivaling the true primordial beast Behemoth.
Countless subjugation forces heading to Budapest are as good as going to their deaths; they struggle even to overcome Mammon, let alone face the monster personally crafted by the goddess.
Avis: "Lucifer, where are we headed next?"
Merlin: "Budapest."

title: Chapter 33 — The Collapsing Female Knight (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 33 — The Collapsing Female Knight (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 37 · Chapter 33

"Ah?" Avis stared blankly, asking in surprise, "Aren't we going to Rexham first?"

"There's something more important now, so returning to Rexham will have to be put on hold for now," Merlin replied in a low voice. The situation on Alice's side was very urgent; he had to rush over there as a priority. As for his daughter's side, there shouldn't be any problems for the time being — Alice would certainly have arranged things properly for Chris before leaving, so there was no need to worry.

"Rushing from here to Budapest will take half a month; it's quite far," Avis frowned. Having traveled for so long, it really wanted to rest for a while.

"Aren't you a dragon? Your flight speed shouldn't be slow, right? It'd be best if we could catch up to the crusade team that departed a few days ago," Merlin figured that with Avis carrying him to Budapest, it shouldn't take half a month.

"What!?" Avis glared with wide eyes, all its dog fur standing on end. "I'm a noble dragon! Not your mount! What do you take me for?"

"What's the difference? A pet and a mount are the same thing, aren't they?" Merlin couldn't understand why Avis was being so stubborn.

"They're completely different! Treating me as a mount is an insult to me! I absolutely won't agree to it!" Avis bared its teeth, truly unable to endure Merlin's contempt.

"Ah~ what a pity then. Alice seems to know orthodox dragon martial arts and magic, having received the inheritance from your first clan leader. I was hoping she could give you some pointers, but too bad," Merlin said meaningfully.

"Then what are we waiting for? Let's set off right now!" Avis instantly went wild like it had been injected with chicken blood, wagging its dog tail furiously. "So what if I'm a mount? Absolutely no problem! Not to brag, but in terms of flight speed, only the Storm Saint Dragon can match me! All other dragons are no good~"

"Hah, weren't you unwilling? Can't let go of your pride as a dragon~" Merlin said with a face full of disdain.

"Hmph! Even if my body submits, my soul will absolutely never acknowledge being a mount!" Avis held its head high.

"This again..." Merlin curled his lip, truly looking down on this two-faced guy.

Not far away, Mesfield glared at Merlin's back with incomparable ferocity, wishing she could rush up and hack this bastard to pieces right now.

She had already learned of Merlin's multiple identities; she never expected this unremarkable Black Iron adventurer to be the Great Swordmaster Elgin.

They had clearly brushed past each other several times before, yet Mesfield had never discovered any flaws — thinking about it made her teeth itch with anger!

Recalling how they had once sat together eating late-night snacks in the dead of night, she felt incomparable horror! She had actually sat down quietly to eat with her lifelong enemy? What a surreal thing!

Since the Great Swordmaster Elgin was a Demon Lord, that mysterious black-robed person who had been beside him back then was probably also a Demon Lord!

She had sat together with two Demon Kings, shooting the breeze in the middle of the night — if she told anyone, probably no one would believe it!

Mesfield gritted her teeth, making a "kaka" grinding sound; her current mood was a mix of shock and fear.

Merlin felt Mesfield's "fervent" gaze, turned around and spotted this female knight, and immediately scratched his cheek awkwardly. "Long time no see, Miss Knight."

"Uh!" Mesfield hadn't expected Merlin to greet her first, and cursed this thick-skinned bastard inwardly. "Who's 'long time no see' with you? We're not familiar at all! You filthy maggot, why are you still alive?!"

A few black lines slid down Merlin's forehead; from Mesfield's reaction, he knew she must have learned the truth — otherwise her attitude would have been much more amiable.

"I don't know where I offended you? Why are you speaking so viciously to me?"

"Stop playing dumb here! Don't you know what you've done?!" Mesfield's expression held some shame, and a hint of red. "You did such excessive things to me! You haven't forgotten all of it, have you?!"

"???" Avis's expression turned strange, thinking what's going on — could it be this lady knight also has a thing with Lucifer? Aha! I knew Lucifer wasn't anything good! As expected, my guess was right!

"Sigh," Merlin sighed, feigning difficulty. "Miss Knight, I'm already married, my kid is old enough to run errands, you have no chance — give up."

"!!!" Avis was shocked again, wondering — could it be this lady knight is throwing herself at him? Does this Lucifer guy have that much charm?

"What did you say?!" Mesfield's face flushed red with anger, instantly feeling like she had a brain hemorrhage. She hadn't even said anything yet, and this thick-skinned bastard started twisting things around. "That's not what I meant?!"

"Then what do you mean? Miss Knight, let me go — we're impossible. Stop peeping at me with that fervent gaze..." Merlin raised his head, gazing into the distance, and said shamelessly, "I'm the man you'll never be able to get~"

Avis's dog head shook, its gaze toward Mesfield becoming weird — thinking, no way? Is it really this stimulating?!

"You you..." Mesfield clenched both fists, her whole body trembling, her face red as a monkey's butt. "Although I was mentally prepared, I never expected this bastard's face-skin thickness to exceed my imagination!"

"Oh? Thanks for the compliment, you're saying I'm generous and magnanimous, right? I get it~" Merlin nodded approvingly.

Mesfield's face darkened; she had no way to deal with Merlin — couldn't beat him in a fight, couldn't win in a verbal spar. Was there anything more stifling than this?

"You've humiliated me again and again — you should apologize to me!"

"I humiliate people with my strength — why should I apologize?" Merlin said with righteous confidence.

"Ah?" Mesfield was rendered speechless by the retort, grinding her teeth as she cursed, "Arrogant Demon Lord! You've blinded everyone's eyes, making them think you're a hero, but you can't blind me — just wait and see, I absolutely won't let you off easily!"

Avis's expression was complex; in its eyes, it always felt like Lucifer and this female knight had some ambiguous relationship, but it didn't know what exactly had happened. Maybe Lucifer had led her on then abandoned her, making this valiant female knight hold a grudge. That philandering Lucifer, relying on his face that could tire humans to death — just how many ignorant young (middle-aged and elderly) women had he deceived?

Seeing Mesfield furious yet helpless against him, Merlin felt a bit of pleasure in his heart.

It must be that Queen Elizabeth had instructed Mesfield not to cause trouble for Merlin.

Otherwise, with Mesfield's personality, even knowing she couldn't win, she would still fight Merlin to the death for her dignity—

"Sigh, this charm of mine with nowhere to place it — why can't she forget me? I'm guilty~"

"Although I'm not interested in you, I do appreciate your taste in underwear — especially that black thong."

"However, I think that transparent gauze one in your wardrobe is more exciting — it suits you very well. Wonder if you're wearing it right now?"

title: Chapter 34 — Fainting
content:
Chapter 34 — Fainting

Volume 37 · Chapter 34

You. You're talking nonsense.

Mersfield was greatly startled, wide-eyed, staring at Merlin with an unbelievable gaze, his heart pounding like a drum.

Damn it! This cursed demon must have a clairvoyance! How does he know what underwear I wear?

This is impossible! It must be my imagination, but why does it know so much?

Mersfield's face turned red, his expression like that of a wolf on the prowl, frantically shielding his chest and private parts, fearing Merlin might indeed have clairvoyance.

Merlin grinned and intended to humiliate the female knight, making himself a dream she would never forget, "To be honest, we slept together, though I resisted, you still dragged me to bed. Now, thinking about it, I feel deeply humiliated, *hmpf*."

"! ! ?" Avis widened his eyes, his mood unexpectedly excited, "Oh, I knew it! Of course, things aren't that simple. Seeing this knightly lady, I never imagined she was so lustful in private?"

"Mersfield pointed at Merlin, coldly scolding, "You're defaming me! You cursed demon, are you trying to sully my reputation? You're so vile!"

"Don't you remember that night?" Merlin closed his eyes, continuing with a sympathetic expression, "You encountered a golden-haired boy, then brought him to your home, and spent an awkward night together~"

"Uh! No way? Mersfield's delicate body trembled violently, shocked to the point of fainting, vaguely recalling something!"

"That's right, the golden-haired boy was me. I accidentally ingested a time elixir and turned into a child, so when you insisted on hugging me to sleep, I was also embarrassed." Merlin's expression was strange, reluctant to reveal this, but Mersfield was a bit pushy.

Mersfield stood frozen, unable to believe her ears, doubting if she had heard correctly, her heart rate even stopping.

Oh my! This isn't true! The golden-haired boy I thought was kidnapped by human traffickers, was actually this scoundrel!

I didn't know that boy was the infamous swordmaster, just thought he was a child, what's the big deal?

A kidnapped child, who needed maternal care, was what I did out of compassion.

No! Why did such a shameful thing happen to me? I might as well die!

No! Even if I die, I won't drag this scoundrel down with me!

Mersfield's face turned red as if boiling, showing signs of a heart attack, humiliated by Merlin, even her last dignity was trampled.

Her mind was in chaos, forgetting Queen Elizabeth's advice, her only thought was to fight Merlin!

Mersfield drew her royal sword from her waist, ki like a tidal wave erupted, shaking the palace.

"Damn scoundrel, even if I die, I'll die with you!"

The surrounding knights saw the situation was out of control, Mersfield was enraged, and they all rushed to hold her back, preventing her from doing something irreversible.

"Mersfield! Calm down! Calm down!"

"Don't take it out on that man! There's grass everywhere in the world, why die on one tree?"

"Don't be impulsive, Mersfield! You're still young, who hasn't experienced a few setbacks in love?"

Mersfield, listening to the surrounding advice, became angrier, almost spitting out blood, her vision blurred, and she fainted on the spot.

"*Hmpf*!" Merlin shook his head, saying in a sighing tone, "Tsk, my cursed charm~"

Avis looked at the unconscious Mersfield, feeling a bit of sympathy.

He thought the knightly lady was so devoted that even death wouldn't keep her apart from Merlin, what a strong resolve!

However, things were completely different from what Avis thought.

A few days later, in the secret sky ship from Britain to Budapest, Alice was polishing her sword in the corner, preparing for the upcoming battle.

This ship was provided by the Rothschild family's son Jacob, filled with soldiers and knights from Britain, planning to meet up with other royal troops in Budapest to jointly attack the vampire, Cain.

However, the troops from Britain encountered some minor issues on the way, the sky ship malfunctioned, and it took the whole night to repair before continuing the journey, delaying for about a day.

Perhaps the troops from other kingdoms have already arrived in Budapest, gathering around the volcano, preparing for all the reinforcements to arrive, and then unite to attack the vampire hiding in the volcano.

The participants in this campaign were not only the elite knights from various kingdoms but also many adventurers who voluntarily joined the team.

Vampires indiscriminately captured humans, which had touched the interests of neutral parties.

Many familiar faces were among them, such as the half-elf adventurer from Manchesters, Zikathiro. After failing in the adventurer competition three years ago, he had been diligently practicing, without any slack, hoping to further improve his skills. Now that he had made some progress, he wanted to try his hand at it, and he heard that the kingdom was about to attack the blood race, so he began to select willing warriors to join, and thus he signed up.

But when Zikathiro saw Alice, his mood dropped significantly. His memory was still stuck in three years ago, thinking Alice was a realm-level strongman, and progress was impossible to surpass her, but she was now a pseudo-god master, an existence that could wrestle with the Demon Lord, and also a guest of honor in the British kingdom, holding the noble title of foreign thorn knight.

This was unacceptable to Zikathiro, who had worked hard for three years, yet couldn't surpass his former rival, and was even far behind, which was completely unfair!

Zikathiro would never know that sometimes luck is also a form of strength, years of hard work might not surpass the favored child of fate, who can achieve everything with a single stroke of luck.

This shouldn't be the case! Why did I, after three years of hard work, become even worse? Is it because I haven't worked hard enough?

Yes, that's right, I must be even harder on myself!

Although Alice appeared to be casual about training, who could see the effort she put in behind the scenes? Maybe even a hundred times more than me.

Zikathiro looked at Alice polishing her sword, his eyes shining with admiration, unable to help but silently admire in his heart.

How amazing, Miss Alice, you are the example for all adventurers, and I must also work a hundred times harder!

Look! To prepare for the battle, Miss Alice is polishing her sword non-stop, wanting to be in the best condition to face the enemy!

She must have a perfect plan, and even a god child is not worth her attention. This is the attitude of a pseudo-god master.

However, the reality was not as Alice thought. Her face was a bit pale, and her hand polishing the sword was trembling, the surface calmness was all a facade.

It's time to face Cain, and Merlin is not with me this time.

What should I do? I'm so nervous.

E(°△▲°II)

title: Chapter 35 — Ambush
content:
Chapter 35 — Ambush

Volume 37 · Chapter 35

Alice had not forgotten. If not for Merlin, she might have died at Cain's hands three years ago.

That seemingly harmless little girl was actually a true ancestor with terrifying strength! She wondered what that creature looked like now.

Alice had originally wanted to avoid this matter, but the vampires' activities were growing increasingly rampant. At this rate, they would eventually threaten all human nations, and perhaps even Rexem would not be spared.

So Alice had gritted her teeth and joined this crusade. Though she lacked full confidence in defeating Cain, with strength capable of overcoming the Second Demon Lord, perhaps she could put up a fight.

Alice glanced at her companion, the petite pseudo-dragon warrior Elia, who was devouring a roasted lamb leg with voracious appetite, tearing at it without any chewing, swallowing the meat whole as if drinking water.

Many of the accompanying knights and adventurers could not understand why Elia's tiny stomach could consume a month's worth of rations for the entire party, leaving not even a crumb of bread behind, causing the whole group to face severe food shortages before even reaching Budapest.

Since Master Gregory had been transformed into a woman by the backlash of ancient magic, his physical condition remained highly unstable, so he did not join this crusade. Instead, he sent his student Elia, hoping to help Britain defeat the massive threat lurking in Budapest.

"Burp~" Elia looked up and let out a burp. After having swept through more than half of the skyship's food stores, she finally showed signs of being full. Many people secretly breathed a sigh of relief. Fortunately, some scraps had been left from this glutton's mouth; otherwise, they would have been eating dirt for the rest of the journey.

Alice looked at Elia, feeling exasperated. Why did this permanently child-sized dwarf patient have such an enormous appetite? She could devour more than half an army's rations alone. She was simply not someone an ordinary person could afford to feed.

Ever since the Battle of Britain, Alice had barely seen Elia. Compared to three years ago, this girl seemed largely unchanged. Though her strength had not improved much, her appetite had grown considerably.

Noticing Alice's gaze, Elia thought for a moment, then wore an expression of great reluctance as she held out the half-eaten roasted lamb leg. "You want it?"

"No no no! I don't need—" Alice saw the teeth marks all over the lamb leg and could hardly bring herself to eat it.

*Heh.*

Elia smiled with relief, thinking Alice had been trying to steal her food.

With her current strength, Alice was arguably the strongest person on the crusade team.

Even Elia would no longer look down on Alice as she used to.

"Miss Alice, you're so amazing. It's been three years, and you've already reached the pseudo-god realm, the same level as my teacher."

"Just luck." Alice replied without elaborating further.

"But your figure hasn't changed at all. My teacher has a much hotter body than you, hehe~" Elia said without any filter.

"Ugh!" Alice frowned, her mood instantly souring. "You're not much better yourself, still looking like a little shorty."

"Hmph!" Elia snorted, not wanting to provoke Alice. "I can sense the dragon aura radiating from you. It's completely different from three years ago. Did something good happen to you?"

"What's the point of telling you?" Alice answered calmly.

"You've advanced to a true dragon warrior, haven't you? I can smell the气息 of my own kind~" Elia studied Alice, suspecting she might have found genuine black dragon blood.

"You guessed correctly. I completed my transformation three years ago. Unlike you, a half-hearted amateur, I am a true dragon warrior — the kind that can fly~" Alice raised an eyebrow, secretly mocking Elia as a ground dragon incapable of flight.

"Where did you get genuine black dragon blood? My teacher searched for a long time without any results." Elia puffed out her cheeks, filled with jealousy, thinking Alice's luck was absolutely explosive.

"In a canyon in the Kingdom of Spain. Unfortunately, it self-destructed. If you're still looking for black dragon blood, there's virtually no chance." Alice answered truthfully. In fact, she was now the last and only surviving true dragon warrior.

"Tch! I see. No wonder you've reached the same realm as my teacher. Don't get so smug. Perhaps my teacher can create black dragon blood even closer to the real thing. In that case, I might not be worse than you~" Elia felt deeply unconvinced. As long as Teacher Gregory was still alive, she still had hope of becoming a true dragon warrior.

"Then good luck to you." Alice said in a nonchalant tone, never regarding Elia as a rival. She changed the subject. "By the way, I heard Little Johnson also joined this crusade. Why haven't I seen him on this ship?"

"Johnson that brat? You've known him long enough to know he's directionally challenged. Getting lost is his常态. Who knows where he is right now, probably completely disoriented. He definitely hasn't boarded this skyship." After eating her fill, Elia took out her pillow and immediately lay down. "Eat your fill and then sleep — what a divine life~"

Soon, Elia's snores filled the air. Alice withdrew her gaze and thought of Little Johnson, feeling certain that this arrogant brat had gotten lost somewhere along the way.

Alice was deeply worried. This crusade did not seem to be going smoothly. Few of the people on this ship were reliable. She wondered if they could defeat Cain.

Katherine, clad in magnificent silver-white knight armor, slowly approached and asked softly, "Miss Alice, are you alright? Your complexion looks a bit poor."

"I'm fine, just a bit worried." Alice's expression was troubled.

"Worried about what?" Katherine asked curiously.

"Worried whether we can defeat Cain. I've seen it before. To be honest, with the people on this ship, defeating Cain will be difficult." Alice answered with a heavy tone.

"You are the strongest person on this ship, and even you think so. The problem is indeed serious." Katherine paused, then continued, "However, we are not the only ones crusading against Cain. Other kingdoms have also sent their own teams. If we unite and fight together, there may still be a chance."

"Perhaps you're right." Alice managed a faint smile.

"Before we reach Budapest, you should rest. Don't worry, I'll be responsible for everyone's safety. This ship has been set up with a defensive barrier. There won't be any danger."

Late at night, the skyship sailed steadily through thick fog that obscured their direction.

They did not know that at this very moment, the skyship was already above the Budapest region!

Clearly, Alice and her companions were not the first team to come for the crusade. The vampires were well prepared.

Alice suddenly opened her eyes from her sleep, sensing a terrifying power rapidly approaching. She burst out of her room and shouted, "Everyone wake up! We're under attack!"

Before her words had even finished, a massive explosion rang out. Flames instantly engulfed the skyship, and the defensive barrier was shattered to pieces!

Countless people died in their sleep. The scorching flames devoured the entire skyship, lighting up the night sky with towering inferno.

A vampire bathed in flames floated in the sky, slowly lowering the smoking hellfire great lance in her hand.

Dikte had been waiting for this moment, intending to ambush and intercept the team coming to crusade against Cain. Alice and her group were the final batch.

"Done!"

"Another group of hopelessly foolish humans."

title: Chapter 36 — Encountering Heavy Injuries
content:
Chapter 36 — Encountering Heavy Injuries

Volume 37 · Chapter 36

The airship departing from the Britain Kingdom exploded on the spot, its massive hull torn apart and consumed by flames.
These past days, extermination teams from various nations have continually arrived, continually interfering with the ritual to restart the Heavenly Gate.
In order to preemptively stop the extermination teams of various nations, Dickteping has already ambushed many along the way, succeeding repeatedly.
Britain's extermination team suffered heavy losses, countless knights and soldiers vanishing instantly; hardly anyone could have survived the blast.
As Dickteping was planning to head to the next location to continue ambushing other extermination teams, a green light flashed in the sky, accompanied by a Saint-tier pressure descending; numerous vines like giant hands slammed down fiercely toward Dickteping!
Boom——
Dickteping was caught off guard, like a burning fly, and was slapped straight to the ground!
The Eighth Thorn Knight Catherine's silhouette slowly emerged; she seemed to have successfully escaped the explosion's danger, and without hesitation she immediately launched a counterattack.
Catherine slowly descended from the sky, her wary eyes fixed on Dickteping, faintly sensing that his pressure was extremely strong, his strength at least one tier above hers, completely different from the vampires she had encountered before.
Dickteping slowly got up from the ground, rubbing his sore neck, and said in a low voice, 'Who would have thought a mouse would escape? How unexpected.'
Catherine narrowed her eyes, having learned some top-secret intelligence from the queen, and vaguely deduced his identity: 'You're the lackey beside Cain, aren't you? Possessing the bloodline of a high-ranking vampire and also wielding the power of elemental magic beasts? Three years ago you were the thief who stole the Flame Demon from the Frankish Kingdom.'
Oh? Dickteping replied, quite surprised, 'You know quite a lot; you've investigated me so thoroughly.'
'Information among allies is shared; knowing your background isn't difficult.' Catherine answered calmly.
'What do you intend to do? Noble knight, are you going to kill me?' Dickteping asked in a provocative tone.
'You are originally one of the targets that must be dealt with in this extermination; even if you don't come to us, we will find you.' Catherine said frankly, 'The extermination mission isn't only aimed at Cain; it also targets his lackeys, especially someone like Dickteping, a close confidant. Many attacks on human towns are inseparable from him.'
'I think you've got it wrong; I'm not the prey, you are. My strength can completely overwhelm you—can't you see the gap between us?' Dickteping said mockingly.
'I can see it, but the fact that I'm standing here proves I have enough confidence to deal with you.' Catherine's calmness was somewhat inexplicable; normally, upon realizing the disparity, one would choose to flee quickly.
'Foolish knight, I see you're deliberately seeking death; well then, let me bite through your throat and taste the blood of a female knight.' Dickteping licked his lips, inwardly craving blood.
'This deserted environment is practically heaven's gift for choosing your grave.' Catherine looked around, correctly confirming whether anyone else was present.
'What are you looking for? Perhaps seeking help from other companions? Give up; I've been lying in ambush here for a long time, and most of your team will die under my firearm.' Dickteping said confidently.
'Dealing with you doesn't require companions; I'm merely checking if there's a third pair of eyes around. If there are others, I really wouldn't be able to execute my move.' Catherine said seriously, seemingly not joking.
'Blatant lies!' Dickteping glared, his whole body engulfed in blazing flames as the Flame Demon's power surged wildly; he raised his Flame Demon Great Gun and launched a bombardment at Catherine, shouting, 'Disappear!'
