Boom! With a tremendous roar, the Flame Demon's flames spewed from the barrel, forming a scorching tongue of fire several meters long!
Dickteping poured all his power into the weapon, intending to blast Catherine to bits, leaving not even slag!
The enemy's strength far surpassed Catherine's; the Flame Demon's cannon could hardly be resisted!
Only saw Catherine, with a wave of her hand, construct a barrier spell; golden light walls appeared out of nowhere, three layers thick, isolating the surging cannon fire outside!
However, facing the powerful Dickteping, the defensive barrier could not withstand much time; the three light walls quickly developed numerous cracks, becoming perilously unstable!
Catherine still maintained her extraordinary calm, spitting out a black ring from her mouth and swiftly placing it on her left index finger; a strange deathly power erupted instantly!
The Apocalypse Magic Ring representing 'death' is Catherine's greatest reliance; its terrifying deathly power can directly dismantle an enemy's soul, imparting the meaning of death upon them.
Wielding such a powerful divine artifact, Catherine naturally exercises extreme caution; she would never use it when others are present.
Now facing the stronger Dickteping, Catherine unhesitatingly activates this magic ring; the power disparity between them, under the artifact's effect, is directly reversed!
The Apocalypse Magic Ring emanates deathly power, spreading like a virus and rapidly corroding everything around Catherine; even the flames cannot escape fate, being completely suppressed!
'What is this?' Dickteping exclaimed, eyes wide with shock, only feeling a massive black shadow surging from Catherine's body, like a grim reaper continually harvesting life!
The deathly power of the Apocalypse Magic Ring struck in the blink of an eye, engulfing Dickteping in thick darkness; he struggled desperately and shouted, but his throat could emit no sound, as if he had entered a pitch-black world of death!
Dickteping's soul and body were severed by the deathly power; his sinful soul struggled in the dark vortex, ultimately being torn apart alive!
In the face of the artifact's power, Dickteping had utterly no means to resist, especially against the mysterious Apocalypse Magic Ring.
Dickteping's corpse lay on the ground, unmarked by any injury, yet he was already dead; even the vampires' formidable regenerative ability was useless, for a body without a soul is merely a corpse.
The next morning,
'Miss Alice? Miss Alice! Wake up!'
Catherine searched the vicinity all night, only finding the unconscious Alice; everyone else had completely disappeared. The airship had been destroyed by Dickteping, most knights should have perished, with only a few survivors.
'.Alice slowly opened her eyes, soreness spreading through her body making her frown, 'Where is this?'
'Probably the outskirts of Budapest; we were attacked last night and the airship was destroyed.' Catherine said softly.
'I recall now; last night some unknown force attacked, and I wanted to warn everyone, but it's already too late.' Alice remembered the events before she fainted.
'There's nothing to be done; last night's enemy was very strong, and the defensive barrier I set on the airship was breached, causing many deaths.' Catherine said helplessly.
'Anyone survived? Zikailo, Ailya, and the other knights and adventurers?' Alice asked urgently.
'Sorry, I searched the vicinity all night and only found you.' Catherine lowered her head, answering seriously, 'Most likely perished in the airship explosion last night.'
'How could this happen?' Alice frowned, thinking they hadn't even seen Cain yet and already suffered a heavy blow; what now?
'However, Zikailo and Ailya should be able to survive; their strength is sufficient to cope with last night's turmoil.' Catherine paused, then suggested—
'We should now hurry into Budapest; once they wake up, they should head straight to subjugate Cain.'

title: Chapter 37 — Perfect Monster
content:
Chapter 37 — Perfect Monster

Volume 37 · Chapter 37

The massive black magic circle in the sky above the volcano in Buda-Pest grew even larger, getting closer and closer to successfully reactivating the Heavenly Gate.

Mountains of corpses littered the ground, and beneath the volcano, the flags of various kingdoms lay in ruins. Every team that came to challenge Cain was defeated by him, their deaths gruesome.

Conquering the God's Child in their prime was an illusion, a task doomed to fail.

Instead of defeating Cain, the crusading forces only provided more human sacrifices, accelerating the reactivation of the Heavenly Gate.

The last team to stand against Buda-Pest was the British crusading force. They had lost the power to unite.

After being ambushed by Dictator, the British crusading force suffered heavy losses, with only a few survivors.

As Catherine had guessed, Zikathiro and Alice barely survived and came directly to Buda-Pest to challenge Cain.

Now, Cain stood alone on the mountain of corpses, expressionless and lonely, observing Zikathiro and Alice.

In these past few days, countless people who called themselves "human strongholders" had come to challenge her, and even she couldn't remember how many there were.

These people were undoubtedly famous figures from various kingdoms, either elite knights of the royal family or renowned adventurers.

While they were once looked up to and admired by many, they were no match for Cain, who could dispatch them as easily as cutting vegetables.

"This must be God's Child Cain, right?" Zikathiro, whose strength had improved significantly three years ago, felt an unprecedented pressure when he saw Cain.

"Should be, but there's a discrepancy with the intelligence. The intelligence said Cain was a girl, how did she suddenly become a mature woman?" Alice was puzzled, as the information she had received didn't match Cain's current appearance.

After recovering the last part of her immortal power, Cain completed her evolution, changing from a girl to a mature woman. Her height and face had matured, and her ample chest couldn't be mistaken for a girl's.

This was Cain's true form. She had never been a little girl; her body had temporarily regressed due to the loss of immortal power.

In the calm atmosphere, there was an underlying killing intent. Zikathiro and Alice both felt the pressure emanating from Cain, who was not just a god but an ultimate being that shouldn't exist in the mortal world.

Alice, who had always considered herself superior, began to have doubts. "Should we really go? We're just two people, and we have no chance of winning, do we?"

"There's nothing we can do. We've been targeted by her, and there's no time to escape now." Zikathiro replied quietly.

Both of them had some regrets. They had hoped to find other royal crusading forces in Buda-Pest to join and fight against Cain together.

However, they realized how dangerous the situation was when they found that all the royal crusading forces had been annihilated upon arrival.

Cain looked at them for a while and asked, "Are you humans who came to challenge me?"

Alice swallowed hard and shouted, "Yes! What's the problem?"

"Interesting. Before, there were thousands of elite troops, but now, you're just two people. What happened to the rest?" Cain found it amusing, wondering if all the human crusading forces had been killed by her, leaving only some insignificant stragglers.

"What's the difference if it's just two people? You monster, are you mocking us?" Zikathiro's eyes sharpened.

"I think you're here to play, not expecting two mice to challenge me. Look at the corpses at my feet." Cain pointed to the mountain of corpses, saying, "Among them are some who are stronger than you, but they still couldn't change their fate of death. Do you think you can?"

"We know we can't defeat you, but surrendering won't save us either." Zikathiro hesitated and continued, "A monster who doesn't fear becoming the world's enemy can't have mercy. As described in the myths of the Holy Church, you represent pure evil."

"You've done your research for me, right. Correct, praying to me is useless. It's better to become a sacrifice for the ritual."

"You're dreaming!"

Zikathiro couldn't withstand the immense pressure and launched the first attack. Golden-colored magic power surged within his body.

Shadows spread rapidly, and countless black shadow arms grew from the ground, charging towards Cain.

Alice gritted her teeth. The current situation was hopeless, and they had to cooperate to have any chance.

Thus, Alice entered the Dragon Fighter state, with heavy dragon armor appearing, and her body pores emitting death warnings.

Just as Alice was about to act, a hot flow splashed onto her face, and she touched it to find it was warm blood.

Alice's pupils contracted, and she looked at her side in confusion, only to see that Zikathiro had become a headless corpse, standing straight, with blood gushing from the severed neck like a bizarre flower.

The scene fell into silence. Before Alice could act, Zikathiro was instantly killed by Cain, and she didn't even see the attack coming. Her companion had died mysteriously.

"Good, much weaker than I imagined, boring." Cain remained in the same position, having not moved at all, and killed Zikathiro from a distance with ease. Such a move would make any opponent terrified.

Alice's brain went blank, unable to generate any counterattacking thoughts, feeling that Cain was a terrifying monster from another dimension, completely beyond her ability to defeat.

The enormous gap between them filled Alice with deep despair. She might as well have the thought of moving, and she would end up like Zikathiro, instantly killed.

Now, Cain seemed to have become an incredibly large giant, with shadows looming over the tiny Alice, threatening to collapse her spirit at any moment.

No! I can't win against such a monster. How did such a terrifying being appear? What is the Heavenly Realm?

"Are you afraid? I smell your scent, meek, cowardly, desperate." Cain looked down on Alice, speaking in a condescending tone.

"Correct, fearing me is the normal reaction of mortal beings."

"The home you love is just a garden for the gods."

"Since the era of the gods, humans have never controlled their own fate."

title: Chapter 38 — Mother-Daughter Conflict
content:
Chapter 38 — Mother-Daughter Conflict

Volume 37 · Chapter 38

"Now, do you understand how foolish the idea of opposing me is?"

Cain looked down at Aelia, his contemptuous gaze as if a god were looking down at a tiny ant, without a trace of emotion.

The outcome for these people was already visible, given that crusade teams had been dispatched successively from various kingdoms.

Even Cain was somewhat puzzled—why did humans refuse to accept being sacrifices and instead rise up to resist?

By Cain's understanding, weak humans daring to rebel against the divine was an extremely foolish notion.

They had always been slaves from start to finish, and even their current prosperity was granted by that Lord of Heaven.

Aelia's eyes were utterly vacant, with not a single spark of resistance in her heart. Whether she had even heard Cain's words was unclear.

"Pay the price for your ignorance, insignificant human."

Cain slowly raised one finger, and a razor-sharp ice spike formed at his fingertip before shooting forth like a bullet, aimed straight at Aelia's brow.

Aelia stood expressionless and dazed. Zikatielou's death had long since frightened her senseless, reducing her to a living target completely unresponsive to the incoming ice spike.

Tink—

A sharp ringing sound rang out. At that critical moment, Alice arrived and deflected the ice spike with her slender sword!

Thankfully Alice and Catherine had arrived. Otherwise, Aelia would certainly have died without any chance of survival.

Catherine paused and saw the woman sitting atop a mountain of corpses. Many familiar faces lay in gruesome states—renowned knights and powerful warriors.

The countless bodies piled into a mountain of corpses seemed to serve as Cain's throne, which sent a tremendous shock through Catherine, making her heart tremble violently.

"What a bloody method. Is this really Cain?"

Aelia barely snapped back to her senses and saw Alice's resolute back. In startled surprise, she called out, "Miss Alice?"

Alice looked up and stared directly at Cain atop the corpse mountain. This was completely different from the harmless little girl in her memory—she was now a living demon incarnate!

She wasn't entirely sure what Cain had experienced or why he had become like this. But she could clearly sense that the current Cain was far stronger than before!

If Alice had once felt there was even a possibility of defeating Cain, now there was not a shred of hope for victory. Cain had become a complete entity, even more powerful than his former self!

From their brief exchange just now, Alice had already discerned something. As Merlin had said, Cain had learned their magic and also Merlin's sword-drawing technique. There was absolutely no weakness to exploit.

"You're indeed still alive," Aelia's emotions calmed somewhat.

"You and Zikatielou should have waited for us instead of coming here directly." Alice glanced at Zikatielou's corpse, feeling helpless inwardly. Wasn't this just like the Calabash Brothers going one by one to their doom?

"We originally thought a large number of crusade teams had already gathered here. Who would have guessed they were all wiped out?" Aelia gritted her teeth, feeling that the crusade teams from other kingdoms also had flaws in their judgment.

"Pull yourself together. Don't let fear take hold of you, or you'll become prey to be slaughtered at will." Alice reminded Aelia.

"I-I understand," Aelia replied with an awkward expression, recalling her dazed state just now—it truly had been pathetic.

Cain fixed his gaze on Alice, especially on that familiar face, and couldn't help but narrow his eyes. "I didn't expect you to come too. Long time no see, dear Mother."

"Mother? What's going on?" Catherine frowned, startled.

"Don't call me Mother! It makes me sick!" Alice gritted her teeth and said angrily, "If I had known you were a dangerous monster, I would never have temporarily taken you in!"

Catherine looked at Alice, then at Cain, confusion rising in her heart. What exactly was happening? Did Cain and Miss Alice know each other? No wonder she knew so much about vampires.

"How cold-blooded, Mother. Have you forgotten? The days when you carefully nurtured me." A deep smirk appeared on Cain's face. He harbored not an ounce of gratitude toward Alice, only seeing her as foolish.

"Shut up! The various crimes you've committed must be paid for! The fact that I ever cared for you is my shame!" Alice solemnly drew a clear line. On matters of principle, she would never make the mistake of being lenient.

"I never expected you to be so heartless. Perhaps I should have killed you back then without hesitation. Pity I felt pity and spared you." Cain folded his arms, his expression turning cold. "To be honest, I regret it now."

"You felt pity? I don't believe a word of your nonsense." Alice's body went tense. Her experience of nearly dying at Cain's hands had shattered all her fantasies. "Stop this! Cain! No one can bear the consequences of opening the Heavenly Gate! You will bring unknown disasters upon the mortal realm!"

Although the Church constantly preached that the Goddess of Heaven was kind and lawful, Alice had come to a conclusion through her own experiences—

Whether the Goddess and the Holy Spirits were kind or not was far from certain!

How could deities of the higher planes possibly stand alongside ants?

The various so-called good deeds of the gods undoubtedly had deep, underlying motives—they were not without selfish interests.

In their eyes, the ants of the mortal realm were merely insignificant existences. If they were bothersome, they could simply be removed without bearing any cost.

If the Heavenly Gate were to open again, an uncontrollable situation would arise, making it impossible to predict what the Holy Spirits of Heaven would do.

Only by keeping the mortal world and the various divine realms independent and non-interfering would yield the best outcome. At least then both humans and other races could decide their own fates.

"Do ants care about catastrophic floods after they die? I'm simply returning to the place where I was born. This place has nothing to do with me."

Cain answered coldly, then glanced at the massive volcano behind him. "Almost there. I can return to my homeland and see my true mother!"

"You won't succeed!" Pressure surged from Alice's body. Her gorgeous dragon warrior armor materialized, and a pseudo-divine dragon aura constantly radiated outward—far stronger than Aelia's by a wide margin!

Aelia and Catherine had no intention of letting Alice fight alone. Together, they launched an attack against Cain—

Catherine did not use her divine artifact. Instead, she kept her secrets hidden and deployed a dual wind-thunder barrier, attempting to confine Cain and restrict his movements.

Aelia unleashed dragon breath toward the sky. A fierce wind swept up pebbles, and a spectacular sandstorm roared toward Cain!

"Annoying pests, get lost to one side first!" Cain's gaze hardened. Using his thumb, he nudged the demon sword Tirfing at his waist aside, and a surging wave of murderous sword intent pressed down on both of them!

"Careful!"

Aelia knew Catherine's strength was inferior to her own and deliberately stepped in front, taking the full force of the murderous sword intent!

The sword energy storm easily slashed through Aelia's pseudo-dragon warrior armor, nearly costing her life outright!

"Miss Aelia?!" Catherine caught the unconscious Aelia. A profound fear rose in her heart. Even if she used the Apocalypse Magic Ring, she still couldn't defeat this monster. The enemy's strength far exceeded her estimates! If she continued to fight, she feared she would only distract Alice and add to her burden.

"Cain!!"

Alice had already closed in on Cain, forcing him to have no time to deal with two insignificant ants. Charging magic power and fighting spirit into one strike, she drove her sword hard toward his heart.

But Cain showed no panic whatsoever. He extended two fingers and pinched the incoming blade, his contemptuous demeanor identical to Merlin's—

"You're still as weak as ever, Mother."

title: Chapter 38 — Urgent! Urgent! Urgent! (Bonus Update for Monthly Tickets)
content:
Chapter 38 — Urgent! Urgent! Urgent! (Bonus Update for Monthly Tickets)

Volume 37 · Chapter 38

Cain's finger trembled slightly, and Alice instantly felt as if she had been electrocuted, being shoved back tens of meters. Alice barely stabilized her stance, shocked in her heart, sensing the huge gap between false god and true god; even getting close she couldn't gain any advantage! Being able to, with just two fingers, withstand the sword she had just infused with power—her physical strength may not match Merlin's, but it's quite close. Cain looked at his finger, which was still emitting a faint white glow from being scorched by the Hymn of Light, feeling somewhat surprised—- "So this is your confidence? But what use is it?" The scorched finger healed in the blink of an eye; as a true ancestor, Cain not only fears no sun, but his regenerative ability far surpasses that of ordinary vampires. Alice furrowed her brow, originally intending to deal a fatal blow to Cain with the Hymn of Light in her hand, but before such terrifying regenerative power, she began to doubt whether she could even kill Cain. Catherine felt waves of worry; the power gap between Alice and Cain was enormous—if Alice couldn't defeat Cain, the crusade would be declared a failure. What will happen after the Heavenly Gate is opened? No one can predict; foolish masses might be duped by the church into a situation where the church completely rules the human nation. Alice knew there was no retreat; she could only grit her teeth and charge again, the steel dragon wings on her back trembling, emitting a piercing roar, countless ice blades intertwining like a flood that embraces all rivers, surging forward! "You really are someone unwilling to give up, huh." Cain's mocking laughter echoed; he raised his hand and imitated her, summoning a torrent of countless ice blades that collided wildly with Alice's ice blades!- Ice shards flew sideways, the two torrents of ice blades clashed, shaking the earth with rumbling, Budapest's temperature plummeted below zero! Alice gritted her teeth, frantically driving the countless ice blades, yet still couldn't gain any edge—instead Cain gained the upper hand. The surging frozen torrent kept pressing on Alice; Cain seemed not to have gotten serious, his face still bearing a contemptuous smile. Even using the same move, Alice was still no match for Cain; the difference in strength was plain to see! Alice gave up direct confrontation, planning to rely on technique to find an opening—she leapt up, diving from the sky, her slender sword tracing silver arcs like a thread cutting through the night sky, straight toward Cain's head! "Ridiculous swordsmanship~" Cain spread one hand, a massive ice wall suddenly appeared out of thin air, forming an insurmountable sighing ice wall between him and Alice! Creak—— Alice's blade could only leave shallow traces on the ice wall, unable to break through, and was flung back, her sword arm also feeling sharp pain! Cain not only learned Alice's skill but surpassed her in strength; the fused ice crystals he created were harder than Claudia's! Alice desperately shook her steel dragon wings to stay aloft as much as possible, then divine power began to surge, she shouted loudly. "Stop!" With Alice's shout, the world entered a frozen state, time ceased flowing, Cain became an immobile ice sculpture! Alice raised her Hymn of Light, activating the artifact's ability; the Holy Spirit Legion appeared in the sky, guarding her side. At this moment Alice resembled a valkyrie descended from the heavens, vigorous and spirited, leading the Holy Spirit Legion to annihilate evil spirits! Alice's sharp gaze flashed as she swooped down from the sky; under the blessings of countless holy spirits, she instantly drew all her inner power and unleashed the third style "Open Heaven"! This was Alice's all‑or‑nothing gamble; she had no other choice—if she didn't do this, she would only be slowly tortured to death by Cain. If Alice defeated Cain within the frozen time, she would have won—at least the Hymn of Light would inflict unimaginable heavy damage on Cain! But if she failed, Alice would become fish on a chopping block, her magic and battle spirit both exhausted, leaving her with no ability to resist at all. The steel dragon wings emitted thunder‑like ripping sounds as Alice reached Cain's face; her eyes firm, without hesitation she thrust the sword she had poured all her strength into toward his chest! "I won!" Just as her words fell, an abrupt change occurred—— Cain instantly dispelled the frozen time; in a world where time could not flow, two beings capable of simultaneous movement appeared—ultimate controllers of cold! Seeing Cain slightly turn his body, he easily dodged Alice's deadly sword, his face still wearing a triumphant smile, as if everything was under his control. "! ! ?" Alice looked bewildered; her Open Heaven sword thrust into empty air, her exposed side completely visible to Cain, utterly unable to comprehend how, with the world still frozen, Cain could still act— What is this? Time should have stopped flowing; Cain clearly hadn't broken free, so why could he move freely in my domain?! "Truly a shame—everything you can do, I can do too~" Cain lightly snapped his fingers; with a "pop", Alice's frozen time was directly touched by him, and everything around returned to normal. Alice stared wide‑eyed; Cain also possessed the ultimate law of "Frozen Time"—something she had never imagined. She had always regarded "Frozen Time" as her trump card for countering strong foes, never expecting it to be useless against Cain. "Hehehe, enjoy the torment." Cain's smile grew thicker; he flicked his finger lightly, and Alice shot backward like a cannonball, slamming hard into the ruined city wall! With a bang, the wall cracked, Alice was embedded into it, blood trickling from the corner of her clenched teeth. "???" Catherine tended to the unconscious, wounded Elia; the battle between Alice and Cain she couldn't follow, feeling like much was missing—this is the aftereffect of Frozen Time; observers cannot know what happened inside the frozen time. Alice endured the pain throughout her body, trying to pull herself free from the icy wall, but her strength was exhausted, she couldn't muster even a bit of energy; even her Dragon Fighter battle armor dissipated, unable to persist any longer— It's over! Against Cain, I have no chance of winning! Whoosh whoosh whoosh, successive tearing sounds rang out as several ice swords pierced Alice's body, making her cry out; she was tightly pinned to the wall, unable to move. Cain slightly bowed, adopting the exact same sword‑drawing stance as Merlin, his eyes locked on Alice, feeling it was about time to finish. "Stay there as a living target; I enjoy hunting mice like this*, last words—goodbye forever~" He drew his sword; a murderous sword aura exploded outward, sweeping and cutting everything in its path, leaving horrifying blade marks, compared to a straight strike aimed at Alice pinned to the wall! The power of this draw was very close to Merlin's ultimate technique; even Mammon was slain by it, let alone Alice who couldn't block it! Urgent urgent urgent—— Just then, a roar tore the air; a blade descended from heaven, landing precisely between Alice and Cain! Boom boom boom, a thunderous explosion rang out; the murderous sword aura from the draw fell into chaos, being mysteriously scattered, failing to kill Alice. As the rolling gaze slowly faded, an ancient long blade was planted in the ground, rusted and notched—indeed it was the demon sword Banri Garan!

title: Chapter 40 — Temperature
content:
Chapter 40 — Temperature

Volume 37 · Chapter 40

“Hmm? Caiyin failed to eliminate Alice, so he immediately furrowed his brow, his gaze fixed intently on the demon sword Banri Garan plunged into the ground, finding it somewhat familiar.

Alice, still shaken, slowly opened her eyes. Seeing Banri Garan, she gasped, her voice filled with disbelief. “No way… could it be…?”

“Roar—”

A tremendous dragon’s roar echoed across the sky. A pure white, holy dragon flapped its colossal wings, soaring over the ruins of Budapest, its immense shadow casting over everyone below.

The sudden appearance of the white dragon left Catherine utterly astonished. She watched the dragon’s silhouette fly past, her mind brimming with questions. A dragon? Where had it come from? Why did it resemble the Dragon of Light that had once hovered above the Holy City’s cathedral?

“Edwards!” Alice exclaimed instinctively, recalling that this creature had always been imprisoned in the Demon Lord Palace within the Swamp of Death, never having appeared again.

A figure leapt from the dragon’s back, descending rapidly into the center of the battle. After days of continuous travel, Merlin had finally returned at the most critical moment!

“Him? The Great Swordmaster of Elgin!”

Catherine’s eyes widened in sheer shock, her heart pounding with alarm. She had heard whispers about Merlin’s secrets, including the identity of the Demon Lord. Of course, this knowledge was limited to those close to Elizabeth; the vast majority of people knew nothing of it.

The youngest ruler of the demon race had suddenly joined the fray. Perhaps a great shift was about to occur. After all, this would be a battle between monsters.

Catherine had some understanding of Lucifer III. Though young, he was seemingly the most powerful among the demon race. With the Demon King’s help, the outcome of this crusade was now uncertain. No one could be sure which side would ultimately prevail.

“Haha~” Seeing Merlin, Caiyin felt no fear. Instead, a rare excitement gleamed in his eyes. “So it’s you! I knew you’d come! My dear Demon Lord father~”

Merlin shot Caiyin a long, deep look. Though his appearance had matured greatly, his aura remained unchanged. This was the same creature who had used their kindness, nearly causing Merlin and Alice’s death. The culprit.

Memories of living with Caiyin filled Merlin with revulsion. He had freed Caiyin from the seal, yet instead of gratitude, Caiyin had tried to harm him. This was something Merlin could never tolerate. Every time he thought of it, his teeth ached with rage. He could never fully swallow this grievance. Today was finally the day to settle the score.

However, Caiyin held little interest for Merlin at the moment. He pulled Banri Garan from the ground, turned, and swung several swift slashes, shattering the icy wall and freeing Alice.

Catherine, witnessing this, vaguely understood. No wonder this Demon King had rushed back from afar—it was for Miss Alice. Had he truly fallen for a human? The Queen’s prediction had been correct.

Merlin helped Alice to her feet, cradling her in his arms, and quickly checked her injuries. Fortunately, they were not fatal, and he finally breathed a sigh of relief. “Good. I thought I might be too late.”

Alice was about to speak, but seeing the deep concern in Merlin’s eyes, a wave of warmth filled her heart.

Initially, Alice had been full of resentment toward Merlin for his three-year absence. But now that he had truly returned, most of her anger melted away. If it weren’t for genuine feelings, who would forgive someone again and again?

Looking at the familiar face she had dreamed of countless nights, Alice had prepared so much to say, yet now she couldn’t utter a single word. She wasn’t angry with Merlin anymore; it was just that the man she had yearned for had suddenly returned, leaving her bewildered, unable to tell if this was reality or a dream.

“Uh, this…”

Merlin felt awkward. He had imagined many scenarios for meeting Alice again, but this was one he had never anticipated.

“Hey, what’s this mean? I did come back as promised, didn’t I?”

“Although it was three years later, which is a bit excessive.”

“But I had no choice! Who knew the demon god’s blood would be so hard to control?”

“Alice must be angry with me. Yeah, that’s definitely it.”

Merlin frowned, unsure how to explain. Having their relationship left unresolved for three years was something no one could endure.

“Are you… angry with Alice?” he asked, stammering slightly, feeling an inexplicable panic. He should have been on the moral high ground, unleashing a barrage of criticism on Merlin.

“Then give me some reaction! Joy or anger, anything! What’s with this complete silence?” Merlin gave a wry smile, genuinely unable to read Alice’s thoughts.

“Humph!” Alice puffed up her cheeks in irritation, staring at Merlin with a resentful gaze. “You knew to come back? I thought you’d hide in Demon Castle forever!”

“You’ve got it wrong. I ran into some trouble; otherwise, I wouldn’t have stayed in Demon Castle so long.” Merlin sighed helplessly; explaining this would be complicated.

“The message I sent through the fairy said I’d definitely return, but it was three years later! What were you even thinking?” Alice said, her face red with委屈.

Merlin’s expression was complex. He thought, “So it was really that excessive? Yeah, three years of silence, leaving only the words ‘I’ll definitely return’—that wasn’t very responsible. But Demon Castle is isolated from the world; even writing a letter was a luxury.”

“Do you know how I spent these three years with Chris? I told her you’d come back countless times, until in the end, nothing I said convinced her anymore. You’re the one who caused this!” Alice stared into Merlin’s eyes, her face contorted with anger.

“I’m very sorry, but I am back, aren’t I? I kept my promise.” Merlin gave a thumbs-up, shamelessly praising himself.

“Is that even the same thing?” Alice nearly fainted from anger. She had expected Merlin back within a year, not three. Who knew how much her confidence had been shaken during this time?

Merlin exhaled deeply, gripping Alice’s hand tightly. “Alice, forgive me. I promise, I will never leave you easily again. Believe me.”

“Um…” Alice’s face gradually turned red, dazed by the sugar-coated bullets, her gaze flickering away. “Not again… I’m not angry, or forgiving, or anything…”

“It’s just… it’s just that I want to be able to touch your warmth whenever…”

title: Chapter 41 — Sword vs Sword (Monthly Ticket Extra)
content:
Chapter 41 — Sword vs Sword (Monthly Ticket Extra)

Volume 37 · Chapter 41

"Alice."

Merlin suddenly froze, rarely did he hear Alice speak so candidly, though her words were somewhat euphemistic, their meaning was still clear.

Their relationship had changed significantly since their last separation, both having realized their feelings for each other, but they had yet to confess their true intentions.

The sweater Alice had knitted for him while staying up all night, and the embrace Merlin gave her before parting ways, were enough for even the most obtuse to realize each other's feelings and attitudes.

"Don't stare at me like that, we can talk about other things later, now isn't the time for that." Alice blushed intensely, unable to raise her head, she instinctively pushed Merlin away.

"I understand, I'll explain why I couldn't come back sooner." Merlin gently took Alice's hand, whispering, "Rest well, I'll handle that person."

Alice didn't continue speaking, her heart pounding, knowing that it wasn't the right time to vent three years of resentment, yet she couldn't help but vent her frustrations on Merlin.

Merlin slowly approached Cain, looking at this former "daughter," he remained calm, knowing that Cain was a powerful and ruthless monster, far different from the one he had first encountered.

"Another meeting, Cain."

"Indeed, another meeting, Dad." Cain smirked, his smile mocking.

Merlin frowned, the term "Dad" made his skin crawl, it was unbearable, "You're disgusting, don't call me that, I've never acknowledged you as my child."

"Tsk tsk, what a pity, I was hoping to reminisce about our family, but you and your mother are just as cold-blooded as parents can be." Cain shrugged, displaying a fake sense of disappointment.

"There's no family bond between us, only hatred, I was deceived by your innocent appearance and considered adopting you, little did I know you had no gratitude, and even wanted to kill us!" Merlin paused, continuing, "I've wanted to retaliate against you countless times, thank you for giving me this opportunity."

"An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth? Not bad for a petty demon, this fits your Demon Lord identity well. The old you, both in appearance and heart, didn't seem like a demon at all, but now you have a hint of it." Cain looked into Merlin's eyes, saying slowly, "After obtaining your swordsmanship, I was indeed shocked by your terrifying strength. How boring is it to refine swordsmanship to such an extent? Its power can even rival that of the gods. I've since realized that you must have encountered some ancestor of the demon race."

"What do you mean?" Merlin was surprised, he had indeed been told that the person he had encountered in the Despair Canyon was a great seer respected by the demon race.

"The demon race's seer, who once single-handedly slayed countless ancient gods, bringing about the twilight of the gods, I heard from my mother that this person, like you, also uses a swordsmanship so powerful it defies belief. You must have learned it from that seer, right?"

Cain felt he had touched the truth, besides that, he couldn't understand why Merlin, the youngest Demon Lord, possessed such a powerful swordsmanship, it was beyond belief.

Even if Merlin had been refining his swordsmanship day and night since birth, it would be impossible to reach such heights in just two hundred years, let alone two thousand years!

It seems Cain didn't understand what a "transferee" was. These individuals are often born with special abilities, and Merlin was no exception.

"? ? ?" Merlin was confused, wondering if the demon race's seer also used swordsmanship? But they should be of a different kind, I was born with special skill points.

"If you remain silent, then it's true, I'm grateful you taught me such a powerful swordsmanship, giving me the confidence to face my mother!" Cain now possessed the abilities of freezing time, swordsmanship, and the power of the immortal, giving her the confidence to challenge the goddess head-on, believing she had touched the heels of the gods.

"You're merely a mediocre imitator of mine, you'll never surpass me, that's certain." Merlin gripped the hilt of his sword, saying seriously, "I don't know what your conflict with the goddess is, that's none of my business, I only know you'll pay for what you've done, are you ready to face your death, Cain?"

"Interesting, I am a god! Do you really consider yourself a seer? !"

As soon as the words left his lips, both men launched their attacks simultaneously, their steps and movements identical!

Even Merlin felt a moment of surprise, as if he were fighting his own reflection?

Cain was a perfect imitator, possibly the one who had studied Merlin's swordsmanship most thoroughly, and might even surpass him!

Unfortunately, Cain was Merlin's enemy, if she were Merlin's student or apprentice, she might be the most likely to inherit all of Merlin's skills.

Bang! The two powerful sword techniques clashed violently—

The two divine artifacts clashed, Banri Garan and Tirfing sparking brightly, followed by a terrifying explosion. The ground shattered and trembled, dust and fire surged into the sky, even the magnificent black volcano was halved, hot lava erupting!

The magic circle of the Restart Heavenly Gate trembled, suffering some damage, its light dimming slightly, unable to withstand the residual power of their confrontation!

Ordinary strong fighters would only be able to destroy buildings, but Merlin and Cain were on a scale that seemed to want to destroy the sky and earth?

A crater resembling a giant meteorite impact gradually appeared as the smoke dissipated, the two standing in the center, engaged in a fierce battle, the situation seemed tense, neither had gained an advantage!

Catherine's forehead was drenched in cold sweat, she was stunned by the confrontation between the two, feeling a deep sense of admiration—

It's too strong, such a level of combat is no different from the wars between the gods!

Even if I use the divine artifact Heaven's Initiation Ring, I wouldn't be able to defeat either of them!

The rumors were indeed correct, Lucifer the Third is the most powerful Demon Lord!

To be precise, he has already transcended the identity of a Demon Lord, being the closest to a god in the mortal world, able to stand toe-to-toe with Cain without falling behind!

Catherine felt deep terror, how small and insignificant she was in their presence? The black iron adventurer's badge she wore was particularly ironic, her Ujie Knight identity now seemed shameful.

Merlin's gaze tightened, he quickly sheathed Banri Garan, sending Cain flying into the air!

Then, he quickly drew his sword, the entire action seamless, without any hesitation!

"Bri-la!"

Cain's head was severed, she hadn't even seen Merlin's movement, her head was simply chopped off.

"What!??"

"I told you, you're merely a mediocre imitator, far from me!"

PSI I

The male and female leads are almost at one blood, let's give everyone a heads-up.

Then, then that thing—

title: Chapter 42 — Killing Time
content:
Chapter 42 — Killing Time

Volume 37 · Chapter 42

"No use! No use! No use! You can't kill me!
Cain's pupils contracted, he shouted excitedly, the severed head flying in midair suddenly grew crimson tendrils, connecting with the headless body.
Seeing Cain's back bulge with huge black membranous wings, he soared into the sky, quickly widening the distance from Merlin.
The wound on his neck healed in the blink of an eye; even if his head were chopped off, it would be impossible to kill her!
"Tch! Really can't kill it, huh."
Merlin furrowed his brows, facing the same situation as when he dealt with Dracula—although he could defeat Cain, he couldn't kill the opponent.
Relying on tremendous regenerative ability, Cain could completely wage a war of attrition, slowly draining Merlin until victory.
Dracula at least had a weakness; even if he could quickly repair bodily injuries, he would still fear sunlight.
But Cain is different—she can move freely in sunlight, and with her immortal divine power, she hardly has any weakness!
Facing such an opponent, Merlin felt a bit nauseated, like trying to swat a fly that he couldn't hit, and it was extremely annoying.
He recalled the materials he had given three years ago to the fairy Feyri; after all this time, he didn't know if Mister Tin had finished forging them yet.
If there were a weapon like Mister Tin that could seal regenerative resurrection abilities, Merlin would be confident in ripping out all of Cain's tendons in a short time.
Catherine felt a wave of worry in her heart; even beheading couldn't kill Cain, so ordinary methods against vampires likely wouldn't work. If the battle couldn't be ended swiftly, the scales of victory would tip back toward Cain's side!
Cain touched her slender neck, not a scar left, and said proudly, "Wow, your draw speed is actually much faster than mine—looks like I can't fully copy your iaijutsu. But it doesn't matter; I can't change the fact that you'll lose. You only have one life, while I am immortal~"
"Wipe that smug look off your face—you'll be the one lying here forever." Merlin thought of other alternatives; although immortality was hard to deal with, there should be some weakness.
"You try every means to kill me; when you're exhausted, that'll be your death!"
Cain unfurled her crimson membranous wings, divine power surging unrestrained, accompanied by rumbling thunder, nine colossal flaming skulls appeared in the sky!
Their eyes flickered with red light, bones clacking together, emitting a "ka ka ka" sound, sending chills down one's spine!
"Come keep playing with me, don't think about escaping—I won't give you any chance!"
Merlin's face darkened; his thoughts were seen through by Cain. He had considered that if he couldn't kill Cain, he might as well find a chance to escape with Alice, then return with Mister Tin to deal with Cain—that would be the safest approach.
He carefully examined the dark magic formation above the volcano; reactivating the Heavenly Gate might still take some time, enough for Merlin to make a trip to the Southern United Kingdom.
But since Cain had already spoken, she obviously wouldn't give Merlin any chance to leave; today someone must die here!
Nine burning giant skulls plummeted from the heavens like meteorites, smashing toward Merlin!
Temperature spiked suddenly, the ground showed faint signs of melting, the skulls' piercing shrieks shook people's minds into a daze!
Merlin's expression turned grave; he suddenly drew his sword, a murderous sword aura slicing the incoming skulls into pieces, exploding into a line of fire that set the sky ablaze red.
Before Merlin could catch his breath, Cain seized the moment he hadn't yet readied his hand blade, instantly appearing before him, swinging her blade straight at his neck!
"Hahaha! Die!"
Merlin suddenly raised the demon sword Banri Garan in his hand, opting not to sheath it but to swiftly unleash a second strike.
Cain's arm wielding Tyrfing was severed, tracing an arc in midair before falling to the ground with a "pat."
Merlin's demon blood surged; half his body was corroded, entering a half-demonic state, his power rapidly rising—
His eyes flickered with demonic fire, and the demon sword Banri Garan in his hand also changed shape amidst the flames, revealing its true pitch-black form.
"What are you laughing at?"
"!!?"
Cain froze for a moment, realizing that even without Merlin drawing his blade, his swordsmanship was still unfathomable, especially under the enhancement of demon god blood!
Alice felt her heart tighten seeing Merlin's appearance, recalling events from three years ago, inexplicably frightened!
"Tch!"
Cain turned into a phantom, flashing behind Merlin, using her body to bind him, then she grinned, revealing sharp fangs, and viciously bit toward Merlin's neck!
Since she couldn't win with brute force, Cain could only play dirty, planning to suck Merlin's blood dry and deprive him of his strength!
But Merlin had prepared in advance; he rotated the demon sword Banri Garan in his hand, reversed his grip, and thrust the blade along his own neck toward the one behind him—
"Sss!
The blade of Banri Garan accurately pierced Cain's mouth, straight through her skull, rendering her unable to speak.
"Feel the heat of demonic fire!"
As Merlin gave a low reprimand, Banri Garan ignited a scarlet demonic flame, then erupted explosively!
The raging demonic flame poured straight into Cain's mouth, rapidly spewing outward behind Merlin!
Cain's immortal body, under flames comparable to the sun's temperature, turned to ash; the distant mountain ranges vanished, scorched into boiling lava!
"This! ! !" Catherine stared wide-eyed in horror at the land turned to lava, astonished by the power Merlin displayed—
What immense flame is this? If not withdrawn in time, the whole of Budapest might become a sea of magma! Under this attack, could Cain possibly still survive?
Whoosh—
The severed Cain arm on the ground suddenly twitched, gripping the demon sword Tyrfing, swinging straight toward Merlin!
Merlin's heart jolted; he had forgotten about this, quickly sidestepping to avoid the sharp blade that scraped past his cheek!
Cain's ashes gathered together, forming a skeleton, then new flesh grew, and in the blink of an eye she recovered, merging with the incoming right arm.
This astonishing regenerative speed would have left ordinary enemies despairing, who would have the will to keep fighting Cain?
"Hahaha, openings are starting to appear? Just as I expected, I've already seen your expression at death—how many more times can you hold out?"
Merlin wiped the blood from his face, as Cain said—when his strength runs out, he probably won't be able to keep resisting Cain's assault; this is dangerous!
Alice clenched her fists silently, sweating for Merlin—really no way? I've already killed Cain twice.
Suddenly, a blue light streaked across the sky, and the fairy Feyri's voice rang out—
"Merlin!
"I have your delivery, come sign for it!"

title: Chapter 43 — The Balance Tilts
content:
Chapter 43 — The Balance Tilts

Volume 37 · Chapter 43

Fairy Ferri flew swiftly to the center of the battlefield with her small satchel on her back, her cicada wings trailing a long tail of light.

After Master Barin finished forging Mistilin, Fairy Ferri took up this semi-divine artifact, thinking to seek Merlin's whereabouts.

Merlin lifted his head and saw Fairy Ferri darting toward him, his heart suddenly stirred——

Ferri? Has Mistilin already been forged? How timely.

Huh? Where did this little guy come from? Cain narrowed his eyes, vaguely sensing something was off; this clueless fairy might be bringing something to Merlin?

Seeing Cain glaring up at her from below, Fairy Ferri felt a twinge of fear; otherwise rashly approaching Merlin, she could only keep circling in the sky looking for an opportunity.

Cain gripped the hilt of Tyr's Edge, harboring the thought of killing Ferri; although he didn't know what the fairy intended to give Merlin, he would not allow his plan to encounter unexpected circumstances.

Suddenly! Cain's form shifted into a wraith, thinking to fly toward the tiny Fairy Ferri, killing intent surging, temporarily setting Merlin aside, to deal with this sudden little pest!

Er! ! ! Fairy Ferri was terrified, wildly zigzagging in the sky in an 'S' pattern, trying to shake off Cain's pursuit, but his speed was unbelievably fast!

Stop it!

Merlin leapt up, instantly appearing beside Cain, and swung his blade fiercely at him to prevent him from harming Ferri.

Cain gritted his teeth and immediately drew his blade to block; the vibration from the clash echoed throughout the sky.

The two plummeted together from the sky, entering a stalemate.

Phew~

Fairy Ferri let out a breath, wiped the cold sweat from her forehead, not daring to approach carelessly; only under the premise of ensuring her safety did she hand Mistilin over to Merlin——

One could see Ferri taking Mistilin out of her dimensional satchel; her tiny frame was still smaller than this weapon, looking rather comical.

Ferri hoisted Mistilin over her head like a strongman, wobbling as she aimed at Merlin's position, then threw it with all her might!

Merlin! Catch!

Although this parcel‑delivery method is embarrassing and a bit irresponsible, it's already the limit of what Ferri can do.

This little guy doesn't want to be a courier and risk his life; it's not worth it.

Mistilin flashed with silver light as it spun in the air, swiftly falling toward the ground straight for Merlin.

!!?

Cain's eyes flashed with vigilance; seeing how much Merlin valued this weapon, he knew it was of great importance and must not fall into Merlin's hands. Anxious, Cain shook off Merlin, flaring his crimson blood wings to boost his speed to the peak, hoping to snatch Mistilin first!

Merlin furrowed his brows, releasing a terrifying gravity space against Cain; with a 'bang', he slammed her down from the sky.

Cain was pressed flat to the ground, feeling as if several mountains weighed on him; he gritted his teeth in anger, his whole body beginning to tremble.

Don't even think of stopping me!

Cain let out a loud shout, emanating a blood explosion from himself that instantly shattered the gravity pressing on him, then shot back up into the sky!

Merlin gasped in surprise; to so easily break free from the gravity field, Cain was the first!

Cain successfully seized Mistilin; as soon as it was in his hand he felt a strange fluctuation, realizing this weapon was extraordinary—no wonder Merlin had fought desperately to stop him.

No way? Fairy Ferri covered her face, her eyes full of embarrassment; the parcel she'd meant for Merlin had been intercepted by Cain—what now?

I see, this is your trump card, something specially made to deal with me—too bad, now it belongs—Cain hadn't finished speaking when a tearing sound rang out; a thin sword of radiant lament shot forth, piercing his palm, and Mistilin began to fall again!

The pierced palm smoked with thin white vapors; holy power continually scorched the wound, making Cain furrow his brows in pain as he glared hatefully at Alice below.

Alice gasped for breath, her state still utterly exhausted, yet she managed a successful sneak attack, preventing Cain from seizing Mistilin.

Merlin deployed a gravity field, swiftly snatching Mistilin into his hand—this moment——

It announced Cain's doom!

Tch! Cain snarled, grinding his teeth; his right hand healed instantly as he gazed at Merlin holding Mistilin, feeling an unprecedented threat.

Merlin examined Mistilin in his hand; lightly stroking it, he sensed waves of 'sharp' aura—it was indeed a rare blade.

It seems Master Barin truly lives up to being the contemporary finest smith, able to fully utilize the materials he gathered, successfully resurrecting a divine artifact of the age of gods.

However, Merlin could still discern that Mistilin, compared to the true form of the demon sword Banri Garan, was slightly inferior in quality.

Still, Merlin hadn't set his expectations too high; he hadn't hoped Master Barin could forge a true divine artifact—just being able to help him deal with enemies possessing resurrection and regeneration would be enough.

Your time is up, Cain!

Don't get cocky; even if you have that blade, you still can't beat me! Cain scolded from above, still believing he had a chance to win.

Then let you truly feel—what exactly is the difference between us in the same drawing technique?

Merlin slightly bowed, assuming the stance for a drawing slash, his eyes locked on Cain in the sky, taking a deep breath to let his whole body relax.

The more so, the greater the pressure Cain feels; if we truly decide victory, it likely takes only an instant—unable to withstand the pressure, one is destined to become the loser!

Cain also assumed a drawing stance in the sky, his eyes sharp, his demon sword Tyr's Edge trembling constantly, emitting a bewitching hum.

Their gazes seemed to collide in midair like sparks; the outcome of the next clash would be decided in an instant——

Boom!

The two launched their attacks almost simultaneously, their wraith‑like forms swiftly converging on the center of the sky.

The ground beneath Merlin's feet was shattered into spider‑web cracks that instantly began to spread!

Cain's blood wings behind him tore the sky apart, producing a visible distortion in space!

The killing intent radiating from both sides made the few onlookers feel a chill, as if two gamblers were locked in a stare‑down!

Ah!

Cain's eyes shifted; mid‑draw he used Frozen Time, dragging the whole world into a still, icy void.

Merlin turned into a lifelike ice sculpture, suspended in midair, deprived of all ability to act.

Yet Cain continued to approach, his Tyr's Edge faintly flashing with a deathly light!

Frozen Time truly is a divine art, capable of instantly altering the outcome of the battle——

Cain gained a tremendous advantage, the scales of victory continually tipping.

Merlin is in peril!

title: Chapter 44 — Slash (Monthly Ticket Added Update)
content:
Chapter 44 — Slash (Monthly Ticket Added Update)

Volume 37 · Chapter 44

In this situation, it seems no one can save Merlin; Cain almost has victory in the bag!
Even if Merlin's draw speed is faster than Cain's, under the effect of frozen time, this advantage is completely gone!
Cain gripped his Tyrfing tightly, rushing toward Merlin at breakneck speed, his eyes unable to hide the excitement of impending victory over beauty——
“Let me chop off your head and toss it into the lava to celebrate properly!”
At the critical moment, Alice suddenly appeared, re-summoning the Dragon Warrior armor and rushing to Merlin's side!
In this frozen world where time has stopped flowing, Alice can also act, so she naturally won't stand by.
“Not happening!”
Alice swiftly drew her sword, desperately stabbing at Cain, trying to buy time until the frozen time effect ends and Merlin will regain
freedom.
“How is that possible? A mere pseudo-god realm, how could one use divine power twice in a short time?”
Cain frowned, sensing something off; Alice can only act in the frozen world when she is using frozen time.
She can act within it.
But Alice clearly just used it once; a pseudo-god almost cannot use divine power twice in a short time—there are strict limits.
That's correct.
Upon close observation, Alice's body emitted waves of green light, clearly not her own power, containing surging life force!
Life force!
Cain stared wide-eyed, his mind momentarily drifting; this strange power felt eerily familiar, as if
he had returned to the heavenly realm of old——
“Life divine power! No! Impossible! Why do you possess Abel's life divine power!”
The two children created by the Goddess Maria were each granted different powers, but because Cain was disliked, he received
the cursed undying divine power.
While Abel, the child favored by the Goddess, received the most orthodox power, the life divine power sharing the same source as Goddess Maria,
which has the ability to repair and create all things.
Cain knows his sister's power to the bone; even a trace of its scent can make her recall her days living in heaven.
days.
Cain halted, his mind lost in confusion, unable to understand why Alice possesses Abel's life divine power; obviously this is
having received Abel's blessing!
During the time in the Kingdom of Spain, when Alice fought the black dragon and was severely wounded, Chris tended to her day and night, and the life divine power was
subtly stored within Alice's body.
Now, drawn by the heavenly power emanating from Cain, it manifested successfully; Alice felt nothing, thinking her own power had
returned in a short time?
Little did she know, the power she is now using is not her own, but rather she employed Chris's life divine power to unleash frozen time.
.
Indeed, Chris was once also a heavenly divine child, another child created by Goddess Maria—Cain's sister—
Abel!
After Cain killed Abel, Abel reverted to a lifestone used to create life, falling from heaven to the mortal world, landing precisely at the
entrance to the elves' secret realm, blocking the elves' passage.
This lifestone of creation remained at the secret realm's entrance for countless ages, finally awaiting Merlin and Alice, who re-conceived new life
—life, which is now Chris.
Although Abel has died, Chris has inherited everything from Abel; calling her a rebirth is not an exaggeration.
This is also why the landlady treats Chris so kindly; she, as one of the Seven Archangels Raphael, once had a good relationship with Abel in heaven and also greatly favored this innocent divine child.
However, Chris is not truly Abel; she is merely the child of Merlin and Alice, and those divine children's experiences have for her
completely faded away, and she cannot recall them anymore.
Once again sensing his sister's aura, Cain's thoughts fell into chaos; he hovered blankly in midair, his eyes filled with doubtful uncertainty.
Alice didn't catch what Cain was muttering; seeing him dazed and immobile, she seized the opportunity, thrusting her fine sword with all her strength
at the enemy's head!
“!!!”
Cain came to his senses, turning his head aside, but Alice's blade still sliced his cheek, blood spraying everywhere!
Alice felt frustrated, only a hair's breadth away; if she had successfully pierced Cain's head, it would have inflicted heavy damage.
Cain's eyes flashed with anger; the thought of slashing Alice to death flashed through his mind, but he abandoned it in an instant.
“Get out of my way! Don't interfere! After I finish off Merlin, I'll interrogate you about everything!”
Cain slapped Alice's chest; a bloody shockwave erupted, blasting her straight down from the sky.
Alice's Dragon Warrior armor shattered instantly, she hit the ground hard, coughing up blood, suffering severe injuries.
Why does Alice possess Abel's blessing? The answer is obvious—she's still alive! I didn't completely kill her!
Cain thought, deciding to let Alice off for now, then after dealing with Merlin, he would cruelly torture Alice to extract
Abel's whereabouts.
Regarding Abel, Cain's hatred toward her is no less than that toward his mother; jealousy turned into hatred, tormenting her day and night.
.
This sister who stole all his maternal love will not die; Cain will never reconcile, believing his descent into ruin is entirely due to his sister Abel.
.
“Cough
Alice tried to rise again, but the pain in her chest made her suck in a cold breath; she could no longer support Merlin, yet
the frozen time hasn't ended, Merlin remains in danger, making her anxious!
Cain turned his gaze back to Merlin, assuming a draw stance, charging at Merlin with fierce momentum, not hiding the killing intent in his eyes,
and in this frozen world, Merlin could not possibly be her opponent.
*Alice rapidly thought of solutions, but the situation was already beyond salvage; her severely injured body could be of no help,
“It's time to end this, arrogant Demon King!” Cain's visage twisted, his Tyrfing ringing as it was drawn!
At the critical moment—crack crack crack——
“Impossible!!?” Cain's expression froze; even his draw slash hesitated for a beat.
Merlin's ice sculpture cracked, and then the frozen world where time could not flow collapsed instantly; he regained his freedom!
Scorching heat waves surged forth; Merlin was completely corroded by demonic blood, revealing a terrifying demonic form, with multiple pairs of black wings
bursting forth!
Merlin is the perfect inheritor of the demon god Behemoth; calling him a true demon god is not an exaggeration, as the ancient god's bloodline can overwhelm mere
divine children; escaping from frozen time is no surprise.
However, Cain's blade is already drawn; he still holds a huge advantage, likely able to strike Merlin down first—whether he can turn the tables from a disadvantage remains unknown!
“I've already won! I'll take your head!” Cain jeered arrogantly.
“!!!” In his demonic form, Merlin was too passive, drawing his sword at light speed to meet the foe, yet he was still a beat slower than Cain.
Cain's blade aimed straight at Merlin's neck; Merlin's blade likewise aimed at Cain's throat; both abandoned all defenses,
seeking each other's lives; the outcome of the draw would be decided in an instant——
Cain: “Slash!”
Merlin: “Slash!”

title: Chapter 45 — Ending in Regret
content:
Chapter 45 — Ending in Regret

Volume 37 · Chapter 45

Mistilin and Tir Feng's blade light - - flashed past, and their draw-sword duel ended in an instant!

Looking at Merlin and Cain in the sky, Alice's heart rose to her throat, she was extremely nervous, not knowing who would win in the end.

Both of their draw speeds were extremely fast, to the naked eye almost impossible to see clearly, as if they both struck each other's neck at the same moment!

Catherine widened her eyes, feeling doubtful. According to her judgment, Cain should have won, after all, he struck first and held a huge advantage; for Merlin to strike back would be difficult, at least he would need overwhelming strength to do so.

As a Thorn Knight, Catherine wasn't a swordsman either, and could only make such a reasonable judgment, which seemed fine.

But if a swordsman expert looked, Merlin's draw, though he was second, was at least ten times faster than Cain's.

The outcome was really hard to judge--

“Pila!”

Merlin's chest wound suddenly burst open, blood flowing freely; fortunately, the demon blood had strengthened his flesh, so this seemingly shocking wound was not fatal.

In his demon form, Merlin's physical strength was extremely formidable, his perception equally keen; in that instant, by slightly adjusting his posture, he successfully dodged the fatal slash aimed at his throat!

Even so, Merlin could not completely avoid Cain's desperate attack; his chest suffered heavy damage, after all, Cain's draw technique came from Merlin, making it impossible for the enemy to easily evade.

If Cain's draw technique could be refined a bit more, making that slash at Merlin's chest go a little deeper, it would definitely threaten Merlin's life, the blade would tear his heart apart!

Cain clutched his neck, continually stepping back, his eyes flashing with disbelief; he couldn't understand why, despite copying Merlin's draw technique, the gap was so huge.

Even though he held absolute advantage, he was still counter-killed by Merlin's single slash; such a blink-of-an-eye duel deciding victory, striking back after the opponent's move was almost impossible!

Merlin's slash was so fast that Cain couldn't even see it clearly; he only felt a silver light flash before his eyes, and half of his throat was severed.

The crimson blood wouldn't stop, dripping from between his fingers; his face turned ashen, the unwillingness in his eyes about to spill over.

Cain desperately used his Undying Divine Power to heal the fatal wound on his neck, but Mistilin's ability sealed it tightly, preventing any healing.

Any wound caused by Mistilin cannot be healed by any means; even resurrection and regeneration abilities would be sealed as well.

“I won, Cain.” Merlin sheathed the silver Mistilin, looking at Cain and slowly said, “Maybe you weren't wrong, but you angered me; this is your biggest mistake, you should pay for your actions.”

“.You .” Cain tightly covered his neck, looking at Merlin with eyes full of hatred, blood flowing more and more, already unstoppable, “.I still haven't .”

“Still want to return to Heaven? Give up, you have no chance left.” Merlin paused, speaking with self-reproach, “You being able to stir up trouble again is my fault; I shouldn't have let you out.”

“No, Abel Abel still not .”

Cain's neck was already broken; speaking was extremely difficult, and no one could understand what he wanted to say.

In his final moments, Cain still envied his sister Abel, extremely wishing she could continue living while he would completely disappear.

His wish remained unfulfilled; the fire of hatred in his chest could not be extinguished even in death, leading to a gloomy end.

Cain's gaze gradually scattered; his beautiful figure fell from the sky into the volcano he himself created, swallowed by the scorching hot lava.

The black magic vortex constantly rotating in the sky shattered into specks of light with Cain's death, and the plan to reopen the Heaven's Gate was declared a failure.

Merlin breathed a little easier; this might have been the most dangerous battle of his life, and he should be glad that Cain's learning ability had limits.

Although Cain's strength might not match that of the demon god Behemoth, the Draw Slash and Time Freeze gave him such a boost that he almost became a rival to Merlin.

No wonder Cain gained the confidence to oppose his mother; obtaining the Draw Slash and Time Freeze gave him extra capital, at least enough to contend with the ancient gods.

Cain had become this strong only because he gained a bit more confidence for revenge; so as the main god, Maria, just how powerful is she?

Merlin didn't think about that much; the Heavenly Realm and the mortal world were isolated, mutual interference not easy, and this wasn't something he should worry about.

Alice dragged her fatigued, heavily wounded body up, seeing the sky's clouds disperse and sunlight shine upon Budapest; those Cain's lackeys had nowhere to hide and were burned to death.

“It's finally over; the remaining vampires can only hide in the darkness, barely clinging to life.”

“How about it, Alice? Indeed, without me by your side, you're completely useless~” Merlin turned around, saying proudly.

“Ah?” Alice frowned, displeased, saying, “What are you proud of? Without my help, you would definitely lose!”

“Don't be insincere; admit it, you need me.” Merlin raised his eyebrows.

“Tch!” Alice pursed her lips, not wanting to argue with Merlin.

“Wow, you actually won? This nearly impossible task succeeded.”

Catherine looked after the unconscious Elia, her expression blank as she gazed at the sky, feeling unreal; she had just witnessed a god-slaying battle—

Elgin Greatsword—no, he should be called the arrogant monarch of the demon race.

This guy's power is terrifying; I can't think of any way to defeat him.

If he were a friend, that would be fine, but as an enemy, that's truly

I hope we never have to face a day where we must fight this guy.

After this disaster ended, the reinforcements that arrived began cleaning the battlefield, eliminating the vampires hiding in dark corners.

Merlin and Alice planned to leave Budapest and head straight to Rexham to pick up their daughter and go home.

After all, the little one misses her father dearly; Merlin wanted to get back to Rexham sooner, then have the family reunite.

Alice had the same idea; she would bring Merlin back, give the woman a big surprise, and this time they wouldn't need to lie to get by.

The fairy Frey had no intention of staying in the human realm; she wanted to return to the United Kingdom to keep drinking and bragging with the dwarf Barli.

“Are you really leaving now? Won't you come play in Rexham for a bit?” Merlin asked, feeling Frey had helped a lot, so he should bring her home to entertain as a guest.

“Forget it; what's fun in the human realm? I don't like dirty human adults; kids are better, at least they don't have the stench of sin.” Frey pinched her nose, saying she didn't want to get too close to humans; Merlin is a demon, so he's an exception.

“1”

“By the way, about this Mistilin, Master Barin has something to tell you.”

title: Chapter 46 — Misfortune Upon Misfortune
content:
Chapter 46 — Misfortune Upon Misfortune

Volume 37 · Chapter 46

“What? Merlin curiously inquired, not knowing what Master Balin wanted to tell him.” “Master Balin said, this sword is his lifetime masterpiece, hoping you use it properly. Although it's only a semi-divine artifact, it can approach the true Misteltein infinitely, the ability gap isn't too big, this is the limit he can achieve.” Fairy Feyri recalled Master Balin's words, wanting to show that he had already done his best, forging a divine artifact, which he lacks the ability for.
“Really? I understand.” Merlin nodded, lowered his head to look at his waist Misteltein, indeed he could feel the quality gap, but he wouldn't blame Master Balin, the latter doing his best was already quite good.
“I merely helped Master Balin a little, yet I got his full assistance in forging my Misteltein, obviously a gain; I should give Master Balin some return in any case.”
Merlin thought: taking Master Balin's lifetime masterpiece away would surely break the craftsman's heart; every freshly forged item is like a child to a smith, into which he pours great feeling.
So Merlin secretly decided, took out the recently confiscated demon sword Tirfing, handed it directly to Fairy Feyri, and said seriously: “Feyri, take this to Master Balin and tell him it's my little token; I won't let him help me for nothing.”
“What is this?” Fairy Feyri frowned, clearly sensing an ominous aura emanating from Tirfing, making it feel very uncomfortable.
“It's a divine artifact from the demon race, a treasure left by the demon god Behemoth, the demon sword Tirfing.” Merlin replied.
“Eh! This is a true divine artifact?!” Fairy Feyri was startled, examining Tirfing closely: “Merlin, you don't need to do this; you previously helped Master Balin get past the dwarf king's difficulties, and helping you forge Misteltein is already the best repayment. Moreover, that's only a semi-divine artifact, yet you now give Master Balin a true divine artifact—isn't that a huge loss? Besides, Master Balin would feel psychological pressure, unable to repay your kindness.”
“For a smith, there's nothing happier than studying forging techniques; taking this true divine artifact to Master Balin for thorough research might possibly let his forging skills leap forward.” Merlin looked at Tirfing in his hand and continued: “Besides, I and those around me hardly have any use for this thing; giving it to Master Balin is truly making the best use of it, the only way to let this demon sword exert its maximum value.”
“Is that so?” Fairy Feyri, half-understanding, slowly took the demon sword Tirfing, preparing to store it in her dimensional bag and then bring it back to Master Balin's smithy.
“One thing, you must tell Master Balin: absolutely do not use this divine artifact, because it will bring misfortune to its user.” Merlin warned in a very serious tone.
“What?! Really?!” Fairy Feyri was frightened badly, almost wanting to toss the demon sword Tirfing away immediately!
“Don't be so nervous; as long as you don't use it, there shouldn't be any problems; the misfortune seems merely a legend, though . Merlin hesitated, actually not sure how true that legend is, and added: “All users of Tirfing indeed have never met a good end—Behemoth was imprisoned for several epochs and finally slain, Mammon likewise died an untimely death, and as for Cain, you've already seen what happened.”
“No way?! That scary?” Fairy Feyri shivered, isn't it that whoever uses Tirfing is destined to die? No one can escape this misfortune!
“So it's better to be extra cautious; Master Balin merely using it to study forging techniques should be fine.” Merlin added in his mind, “Probably?” He wasn't sure either, but he couldn't just discard Tirfing—after all, it's a priceless divine artifact.
“Alright, I'll convey everything to Master Balin, goodbye!” Fairy Feyri nodded, vibrated her cicada wings behind her, and turned into a blue streak of light that vanished.
Merlin exhaled, his mind calmed considerably; it seemed like exchanging a divine artifact for a semi-divine one, a profit, but actually he was thinking long-term—.
Merlin did not want to become Tirfing's user, referencing Behemoth, Mammon, and Cain; whether the legend of misfortune is true or not, he didn't want to take that risk, so he kept Tirfing.
Merlin's luck was already bad enough; becoming Tirfing's user would be misfortune upon misfortune, something he could never accept.
Secondly, Master Balin's forging skill is indeed superb; the church once spent countless efforts and only managed to produce a pseudo-divine artifact like the Scarlet Enchantress, showing how high Master Balin's forging realm is—perhaps just one step away from forging a true divine artifact. Thus giving Tirfing to Master Balin is the way to maximize this demon sword's value; by studying the artifact's craft, he could discover the methods of forging divine artifacts in the Age of Gods, raising his own forging skill by a tier. Moreover, it shows Merlin as very upright and generous, repaying kindness; in moments he could make Master Balin moved to tears, his gratitude flowing like an endless river; once Master Balin learns the forging of divine artifacts, Merlin could have him forge divine weapons or armor for him—wouldn't that be just a matter of chatting and laughing?
Merlin nodded, very satisfied with his own two-birds-one-stone plan; obtaining a true divine artifact from Master Balin, who would willingly work for him unpaid—just thinking about it made him burst out laughing.
“What are you laughing at?” Alice asked in surprise.
“Just remembered something happy~” Merlin spread his hands, showing a harmless appearance.
“Huh?” Alice looked puzzled, then suddenly noticed the husky at Merlin's feet: “Right! I've been wanting to ask—where did this dog come from? Why does it keep following you?”
“This?” Merlin lowered his head to look at Aegis, thinking Alice's lips aren't tight; if she let her daughter know there was a giant dragon by her side, it might frighten her, so he chose to conceal it: “It's a dog I raised in Demon City; I recalled Chris isn't very fond of small animals, so I brought it back as a gift for her.”
“You raise a dog?” Alice stared at the husky again, puzzled; Merlin seemed not to have a hobby of raising dogs, but she didn't think much of it: “I didn't expect you still remember Chris.”
“Of course, how could I not love my daughter?” Merlin answered righteously.
Aegis covertly sized up the human woman before him, concealing his dragon might as much as possible, actively cooperating with Merlin's act to continually probe Alice's strength—.
This human woman's strength is impressive! She can totally be compared to that bastard Flare Dragon King! It seems Merlin wasn't lying; that trace of pure dragon aura obviously came from personal instruction by the original clan leader. I don't even qualify to receive such orthodox inheritance, yet a mere human can... It makes me furious! Am I living worse than a human? Damn it! o(TT)o
Next episode, cough cough, feelings have reached the blooming moment, you all understand~

title: Chapter 47 — Our Relationship
content:
Chapter 47 — Our Relationship

Volume 37 · Chapter 47

Aivis felt very wronged inside, feeling that he had failed as a dragon, and even a human had received the favor of the first clan leader.

Alice slowly squatted down and stroked the fur on Aivis's neck, speaking in a tone of coaxing a pet, "Stretch out your paws, be good."

Aivis bared its own canine teeth, angered, thinking to itself that I am a high-value dragon! Not a dog! Dream on making me act like a dog to please you!

So Aivis raised its proud dog head on purpose, deliberately dodging Alice's hand, posing an aloof and noble look. After all, it is one of the Holy Dragons—it would never easily lower its pride, of course except for Merlin, which it cannot resist.

"Huh? What's wrong with this dog? Not friendly to people?" Alice furrowed her brow, muttering with an unsatisfied tone.

Hearing Alice say that he was not smart, Aivis immediately flew into a rage, baring his teeth at Alice. If he hadn't promised Merlin not to speak human language, he would have loudly asked where he was not smart?

"This." Merlin embarrassedly smiled and explained, "After all, it has been living with demons, so it might not be adapted to the human scent?"

"Is that so? But it's fine to have it accompany Chris, right? I heard that this breed of dog is not smart." Alice showed the concern of an old mother, feeling that Aivis, this chihuahua, is still a bit too big.

"Absolutely no problem, it is very smart, believe me if you don't." Merlin lowered his head and looked at Aivis, squinting and asking, one plus two equals how many?

Aivis rolled its eyes, under pressure having to obediently answer this stupid question, showing its brain had no problems to its future owner, "Woof woof woof!"

"Really calculated that?" Alice felt quite surprised upon hearing three dog barks.

"How about it? Didn't I lie to you?" Merlin raised an eyebrow.

"It's fine for Chris to have a pet, she indeed likes the dog at the landlady's house." Alice reluctantly agreed to Chris keeping a pet, and then suddenly thought of something, questioning, "Right! When you came over, didn't you bring a dragon? Seems like the legendary Holy Dragon Aivis."

Aivis immediately perked up its ears, its mood becoming excited. If Alice herself discovered its identity, then it wouldn't need to keep acting like a dog!

Oh no~, it seems this human woman is very sharp, right! I am the Holy Dragon Aivis! Once hovering above the Holy City Temple, the symbol of light!

Aivis widened its dog eyes, praying that Merlin would mess up, at least it could stand above this human woman as a dragon elder, isn't that more comfortable than acting like a dog?

"That is indeed Aivis, but it just came to bring me here, and then it would return to the Demon City by itself." Merlin feigned calmness and said.

"Really? Has the Holy Dragon completely surrendered to your race now? Can be called at will by you." Alice harbored some doubt in her heart; she knew dragons' personalities are very proud and would not easily submit.

Aivis's eyes flashed with tears, excitedly thinking, I didn't! My noble soul will never submit! It turns out this human woman's chest is a bit small, but she still has some brains.

"What's the problem? After Aivis was imprisoned by us, it hasn't suffered abuse, we are not bad to it." Merlin answered with a clear conscience, his face not turning red at all from speaking.

Aivis looked at Merlin with its dog eyes open, feeling dissatisfied in its heart. It hasn't suffered abuse? Kept in an underground blood pool for many years, and finally the demons wanted to eat me! That's called being good to oneself?

Alice looked down at the chihuahua, her eyes flashing with dense suspicion, and couldn't help but mutter in her heart. - Perhaps the Holy Dragon that once guarded the church has now surrendered to the demon race?

The British team began to return, and Merlin and Alice prepared to go to the nearest port with a group of knights.

Because Merlin gave Catherine a huge shock, she dared not be negligent at all, and specially called for a comfortable carriage for Merlin and Alice.
