Catherine certainly did not want to cause Merlin to be dissatisfied due to inadequate hospitality, as this was not something she could afford.

This made Catherine's pressure double, feeling greater than subduing Cain, the companions were the Demon Lord! And the terrifying existence that defeated the Son of God! On礼仪, there could not be the slightest negligence!

Aivis also behaved appropriately, seeing that the two hadn't seen each other for a long time and had many things to tell each other, it simply didn't act as an electric light bulb, but stayed outside the carriage, consciously acting as a lookout hunting dog.

Seeing there was time now, Merlin also no longer hid the things from three years ago, and told Alice about his life in the Demon Lord Palace, hoping to get her understanding.

It's not that Merlin didn't want to come back earlier, but out of consideration for the safety of Alice and Chris, he couldn't return to be by their side.

"The situation is like this, I waited in the sealing room in the Demon Lord Palace for three years, constantly fighting against the demon god blood in my body, until I could completely control it and be able to walk out of the sealing room."

Alice sat beside Merlin, not interrupting his narration, but quietly acting as a listener, feeling Merlin's three-year experience.

Originally, Alice had a bit of resentment in her heart, after all, Merlin disappeared for three years with just one sentence, which couple could endure such a thing?

But after listening to Merlin's account of his experience, Alice's resentment dissipated, and she actually felt some sympathy for Merlin, feeling he also was not easy.

"So, I am sorry, in that situation, I couldn't return to your and Chris's side. If the demon god blood eroded my consciousness, I would become a pure killing machine, the first one to hurt would be you and Chris." Merlin paused, speaking with an apologetic tone, "Just like when I was controlled by Behemoth back then, you should know."

"Don't talk about these things anymore, it's already past." Alice took a breath, feeling that Merlin returning was the best result.

"Yeah, it's already past." Merlin also sighed, "Seeing you and Chris safe and sound, the heart I was finally hanging up can be put down."

"What do you mean? Do I need someone to worry about me that much?" Alice furrowed her brow, her face writing dissatisfaction. "Just because I'm not by your side, many times in the quiet nights, I am very worried." Merlin's face had a smile.

"Stop talking to yourself, I don't need you to take care of me, even if you don't come back, I will continue living with Chris, I don't need you!" Alice crossed her arms, saying the opposite of what she meant, actually she also worried about Merlin's situation in the quiet nights, but she would never say it even to death.

"You misunderstood, my meaning is..." Merlin paused, speaking gently, "Without you by my side, I cannot adapt."

"Huh?" Alice lifted her head to look at Alice, her face flushed with two red clouds, then hurriedly lowered her head, speaking sarcastically, I am not your playmate! You can't adapt to having what relationship with me? Originally... originally our relationship is very strange, to, what relationship

Merlin became puzzled, silent for a long time without answering, he also felt that his relationship with Alice was very strange, enemy? Friends? Or something else?

Alice lowered her head, not willing to break the silence in the carriage, but her heart very much hoped Merlin could give a positive answer, this doubt tangled in her heart for three years.

"We should... Merlin nervously swallowed, using a probing tone to softly answer—

"Lovers, right?"

title: Chapter 48
content:
Chapter 48

Volume 37 · Chapter 48

This is the answer Merlin arrived at after carefully thinking everything through: willing to give and take, even risking his life to protect the other person—what else could this be if not lovers? Perhaps they weren't lovers at first, and they didn't even find each other pleasing to the eye, but as time passed and they got to know each other, their attitudes quietly changed. Although Merlin thought Alice was a meddlesome idealist and he looked down on such people from the bottom of his heart, that didn't conflict with his desire to be with her. Over the years of gradual acquaintance, like water wearing away stone, Merlin noticed every little thing Alice did, and even that foolish hero from before was subtly changing him. Merlin thought it would be hard to find another girl like Alice who understood him and silently devoted herself to him; the most suitable person was right before his eyes, and nothing could make him happier than this. It was as if on a beach strewn with beautiful shells, Merlin picked up Alice's one, nodded, and decided she was the one; even if there were many more beautiful shells, he would never come back to this beach a second time. This was Merlin's true feeling: he hoped Alice would accompany him for the rest of his life; if his dream was to break the curse and then find a secluded utopia to live in seclusion, now it had become taking Alice along to get away from the hustle and bustle. Merlin couldn't fathom what Alice was thinking; he felt her attitude toward him was hot and cold, hard to read, so he sneakily glanced at Alice beside him, seeing her head lowered and not saying a word— What's going on? Didn't Alice hear what I just said? Is my expression not clear enough??? Alice lowered her head, her ears flushed red, her fingers tangled together, countless chaotic thoughts surging in her heart. Are we lovers? Merlin originally thought that, so our thoughts are the same. Does this count as a confession? After that we'd do some intimate things, like ordinary lovers. Alice's cheeks flushed crimson; after thinking for a long time she still didn't know how to respond, so she could only nod with a voice like a mosquito." Merlin looked at Alice in surprise, his eyes darting about, embarrassed, and asked, "You feel the same way, don't we? We really are... like lovers or something." "I didn't think that way." Alice turned her head away, blushing, and muttered, "Is this you confessing to me?" "That..." Merlin rubbed his hair, his hands having nowhere to go, revealing his inner embarrassment, "If you think so, then it is." Alice froze for a moment, joy welling up inside, but she still said, "What a casual confession." "Casual?" Merlin stared for a moment, then cleared his throat and said solemnly, "Cough cough! That Alice, I—" Alice didn't let Merlin finish; she lifted her head, covered his mouth with her finger, and said, "No need, I already know." Merlin looked at the shy Alice, surprised, and asked, "You know? When?" "I'm not an idiot; when you suddenly hugged me before leaving last time, how could I not know what you were thinking? It's only you who thought I didn't realize, idiot." Alice pouted and said in an annoyed tone. "Right, that's how it is." Merlin felt embarrassed inside; it seemed his nervousness was unnecessary, Alice had already seen through his petty thoughts. Alice's eyes darted, two blushes rose on her face, like she was being coquettish as she leaned her head on Merlin's shoulder, huffing and refusing to speak. "Alice?" Merlin glanced at her, wondering what she was thinking. "Why are you only saying this now? Couldn't you have told me earlier?" Alice whispered plaintively. "I don't know what you're thinking." Merlin replied with a wry smile. ↓￥1F48 "Idiot!" Alice lightly jabbed Merlin with her elbow, dissatisfied, saying, "I've hinted at you several times already, and you had no reaction at all." "Really?" Merlin asked in confusion, truly not having noticed. "So you're just a slow-witted guy, really, the more I think the angrier I get." Alice frowned. "Anyway, the result is good, right?" Merlin glanced at Alice leaning on his shoulder, "I thought you always disliked me." "I didn't; it's all just you overthinking." Alice paused, then asked quietly, "Does choosing me really not matter? After all, being with you would get you rejected by other demons." "I know, but it's fine; I can leave the demon race—this is my own choice." Merlin replied in a serious low voice, then teased, "I just don't know if you'd be willing to take in this poor guy who got fired like fried squid." Alice lifted her head, looked into his eyes, felt a little moved, realizing that for her sake Merlin seemed to be under great pressure. She hadn't expected Merlin to go this far for her, forcibly suppressing the other demons' opposition and insisting on leaving the demon city. Since Merlin was willing to go to such lengths, what did Alice have left to worry about? Her concerns had already dissipated like smoke. Merlin "Don't worry, nothing will happen." Merlin paused, then said softly, "Alice, meeting you is my luck; actually even if you don't agree to be with me, I won't let you go—this is what I've decided, and no one can stop it."1 " ." Alice's eyes showed a bit of tenderness, her face flushed like a ripe cherry, her heart feeling as if Merlin were holding and protecting her in his arms; she really liked this Merlin. "Alice Merlin moved closer to Alice, stared into her eyes, hesitated a moment, then actively kissed her lips. The closed space filled with a pink atmosphere; the two entered that state, accompanied by rhythmic breathing and moans, their souls and bodies merging together— Tonight is destined to be a sleepless night for both of them— Outside, Avis lay slumped on the carriage, half-asleep, when suddenly he perked up his dog ears, looked over in surprise at the carriage where Merlin and Alice were. He saw the carriage trembling slightly, with a mysterious rhythm, swaying left and right like a cradle, occasionally a faint embarrassed sound came through. Although the sound wasn't loud, Avis's dog ears were so sharp he heard it crystal clear; his expression was embarrassed, he felt a bit impatient— Damn! Do we have to do this? Just met not long ago and can't help but go at it like dry wood and fire? Can't holding out kill you? Can't we wait until we get back to talk about it? No wonder he's a belly full of dirty tricks, Lucifer, rushing to see this human woman—indeed he had no good intentions~ (O1O0)

title: Chapter 49 — Black Box
content:
Chapter 49 — Black Box

Volume 37 · Chapter 49

The next day, the party had finished their preparations and could reach the nearest port to sail back to the Kingdom of Britain that very day. Catherine came to check on Merlin and Alice’s condition, wanting to give them advance notice and prepare to continue the journey. However, Catherine knocked on the carriage door for a long time outside, but no one answered, leaving her puzzled about what was happening inside. “Mr. Merlin, Miss Alice, are you in? We’re about to depart,” she called. The carriage interior was silent; Catherine frowned, wondering if something had happened. In her urgency, she considered breaking in to investigate. Suddenly, the dog that had been guarding the carriage, Hatuqi, began barking “woof woof woof,” as if warning Catherine not to break the door. Catherine halted her raised fist, bewildered, looking at the Husky, wondering what was wrong with the dog—why was it barking like that? Could thieves have sneaked into the carriage? That seemed impossible. Avis was frantic, wishing she could speak human words, issuing a warning in her heart, still wanting to break in? Did the female knight not want to live? That dog‑couple had been tossing all night; it was strange they could even get up now. Catherine silently lowered her fist, abandoning the idea of breaking in, but she couldn’t just stand there wasting time—she needed to get back to Britain soon. What was going on inside the carriage? Avis secretly sighed in relief; thankfully this female knight wasn’t a hothead, otherwise angering Merlin would be troublesome, after all, being disturbed and waking up grumpy are pretty much the same. Recalling the intermittent sounds from last night, Avis felt a bit embarrassed, causing her to stay awake all night, filled with resentment toward Merlin, yet unable to lash out. While Catherine hesitated, the carriage door finally opened, and Merlin and Alice stepped out, both looking embarrassed, clearly having just put on their clothes, still somewhat disheveled. “Ah, Lady Catherine? What’s the matter?” Merlin asked awkwardly, fastening the buttons on his chest. Alice’s face was flushed, her eyes darting as she hurriedly tidied her somewhat messy hair. Catherine wasn’t stupid; seeing their expressions and disheveled state, she could guess what had happened last night. It was perfectly normal to notice; Catherine wasn’t surprised—a lone man and woman alone in a carriage, what else could they be doing? Moreover, Catherine believed Merlin and Alice were essentially a married couple, so not having that kind of life would actually be strange. Still, Catherine hadn’t expected them to be in the carriage, but after a moment’s thought she relaxed, especially after hearing that Merlin had been away from Britain for over three years and the couple hadn’t been able to meet. As the saying goes, absence makes the heart grow fonder; after three years apart, upon reuniting, a spark can easily ignite in the heat of the moment, and the carriage is far more comfortable than the wilderness. Catherine glanced elsewhere, not wanting to make them too embarrassed, then cleared her throat twice and answered in a solemn tone, “We’re about to set out, so I came to inform you two—there shouldn’t be any inconvenience, right? If there is, we can stay here a few more days to rest.” Merlin glanced at Alice, recalling how intensely they’d been tangled the night before, his old face flushing instantly, “I suppose… it should be fine, right? Alice, what do you think?” Alice’s face reddened even more, her eyes showing embarrassment, she shyly exclaimed, “What are you asking me for? Of course it’s fine, what’s inconvenient?” “Then you two get ready,” Catherine nodded, took a few steps, then turned back, lowering her voice, “Better tidy up your appearance—you two look a bit messy.” After Catherine left, Alice couldn’t help but cover her flushed face, mortified inside, “I’m done for, utterly humiliated.” “Cough cough!” Merlin, thick‑skinned, thought it was nothing, reassuring, “It’s fine, I swear I’ll be gentler next time—believe me.” Alice shuddered, her face burning, ears red, recalling last night’s frenzy, her legs still weak, she couldn’t help but jab Merlin hard with her elbow, “It’s all your fault, you jerk! I’ll remember this!” “Really? You’re holding a grudge that badly? You weren’t like that last night.” Merlin’s expression grew meaningful, thinking, “Last night you were just a little wildcat, now you’re all prim and proper—women’s hearts are unfathomable.” “How dare you say that?” Alice flushed, jabbing Merlin’s chest with her finger, “I last night must have been possessed by a ghost.” “What? You want to freeload? Well, I’ve lost big—I’m a disgrace to the gigolo world~” Merlin said with a worried face, adopting a victim’s pose. “You… you…” Alice was speechless, her liver aching from Merlin’s anger, she hadn’t even said anything yet, yet she was first blamed— “What do I want? I want you to take responsibility!” Merlin twisted his mouth, declaring righteously, “Sigh~; before last night I was still a pure‑hearted man, but then I got defiled—I’m in agony, I’m suffering~” “You… you… stop stealing my lines, okay?” Alice snapped, her lines all taken, leaving her wordless. Merlin pulled Alice into his embrace, kissed her forehead, and said, “All right~ we’re married, aren’t we?” Alice stared, then muttered angrily, “Damn thing, always picking the sweet‑sounding words.” Avis squatted nearby, bewildered, feeling the dog food beside her suddenly lose its aroma, thinking— “These two are completely unfathomable.” Chrono, once the world’s strongest adventurer, unfortunately lost to Merlin in the Adventurers’ Grand Tournament three years ago. His true identity is an otherworldly spy who infiltrated the mortal realm, seeking the black box that can open the gate to the otherworld, searching everywhere. The otherworld has existed since ancient times—though not as old as the mortal realm, its appearance predates both heaven and hell, more like an attendant that arose alongside the mortal world. It lies within the world’s fissures, a rule‑less special zone where its creatures feed on the mortal world’s fighting spirit and magical energy. Subtle rifts connect the mortal and otherworld, allowing fighting spirit and magic to seep through, nourishing the strange beings there. Yet the otherworld’s barrenness exceeds imagination; it cannot sustain too many of its inhabitants, and as it continually contracts, destruction is inevitable. The otherworld’s king will not sit idly by; his dream is to breach the barrier with the mortal realm, letting his people live there—the only way to avert annihilation. Chrono bears this mission, to save the otherworld and countless peoples, spending decades sleeplessly searching for the black box, the sole passage between mortal and otherworld. Heaven rewards the diligent—Chrono succeeded, finding the long‑sought object in the collection room of a certain Captain Dennis— On a pitch‑black night, Chrono fled from Captain Dennis’s house, eyes gleaming with excitement, head down, sprinting wildly. In his arms he held the stolen eerie black box, the very thing taken from the chaotic sea that cannot be opened. “Got it! I finally found it—my people can leave that damned otherworld and come to the mortal realm’s joy…”

title: Chapter 50 — Dark Movements
content:
Chapter 50 — Dark Movements

Volume 37 · Chapter 50

After shaking off his pursuers, Klauno arrived in a desolate wilderness, eager to open the black box.

He cut his own wrist, letting his blood flow onto the black box.

Suddenly, the black box seemed to activate, growing eerie eyes on its surface, then slowly opening.

Even Merlin, who had tried every method, couldn't open it, yet Klauno did it effortlessly - the key was the blood of an otherworldly creature.

With a loud "boom," a brilliant light burst from the black box, shooting straight into the sky!

The light churned the winds, gradually forming a massive purple-black vortex in the sky, as if connecting to a gate of another world!

If Merlin and Captain Dennis were present, they would be extremely shocked - the vortex in the sky was identical to the one above the Chaos Sea!

The heavens changed color, the massive upheaval causing space to tremble continuously. Fortunately, this was in a remote wilderness; otherwise, countless people would have been startled awake from their dreams.

Klauno spread his arms, kneeling on the ground, his eyes fixed on the purple-black vortex in the sky, as if performing some evil ritual.

"Open! Gate to the other world! My people can finally escape their doomed fate!"

A round of applause came from behind Klauno, instantly making him feel an inexplicable pressure, as if being stared at by a hungry, ferocious dragon!

Klauno's back turned cold, and he quickly turned around, tightly gripping his staff, staring into the endless darkness behind him.

The sudden situation made Klauno dare not be careless - he had already been cautious, so how could someone have followed him? This was very unusual!

"Who!? Come out!"

Two figures slowly emerged from the darkness, a man and a woman.

The man was burly, with the head of a wild leopard, his entire body covered in glossy black fur - he was a beastman!

The woman had a fiery, slender figure, her perfect curves accentuated by a black leather outfit, her pink hair adding a touch of cuteness and playfulness.

What was eerie was the golden eyes gleaming in her gaze, emitting a terrifying dragon aura.

They were members of the strongest dark guild, Phoenix - the former Human King Sarret, and the exiled Dark Holy Dragon, Hesie!

Hesie was the only female among the holy dragons, her talent unmatched, far surpassing the Flame Dragon King, and the first dragon to enter the pseudo-god realm.

However, due to her vicious personality and conflicting views with her kin, she even dared to call Nidhogg "Great Father," enraging the first clan leader Alphard, who then exiled her from the dragon tribe, never allowing her to return.

Before Hesie left the dragon tribe, Alphard had always considered her the best candidate for the next clan leader, cultivating her as his successor.

After leaving the dragon tribe, Hesie was accepted by the dark guild Phoenix due to their similar nature, becoming a core member and swearing loyalty to the nearly divine guild leader.

The two appearing here wasn't a coincidence - they had been watching Klauno all along, waiting until he found the black box and opened the interdimensional gate.

Clearly, the materials needed to create the Philosopher's Stone must come from another world; otherwise, Phoenix wouldn't have targeted Klauno, now engaging in a dark guild's infighting.

Klauno broke out in cold sweat, unsure of the duo's origins, and questioned, "Who are you?"

"We are members of Phoenix." Sarret replied coldly.

"Dark guild people?" Klauno was shocked, not daring to provoke them. Sarret was manageable, but the seductive woman beside him gave off an overwhelming pressure. "Do you two have business with me? I don't seem to have any grudges with you."

"Grudges are irrelevant. Your master has already been marked as prey by our guild leader, and that's enough." Sarret said in a low voice.

"Your other world is just a vassal of the mortal realm, born from the sinful borderlands between worlds." The Dark Holy Dragon Hesie said solemnly, her demeanor righteous. "To uphold love and justice, to protect world peace, we will eliminate you on behalf of Phoenix~"

Klauno snorted, finding it laughable. "The dark guild also protects world peace? That must be a fake dark guild. We don't seem to have conflicting interests - plunging the world into chaos is exactly what you want, isn't it? Our goals are the same."

Sarret bared his fangs, slightly enraged. "Don't compare us to other dark guilds - they're not worthy. Who says we want the world to fall into chaos? Our wish is to let the world evolve, eliminate all the weak, and create a new era of ultimate perfection and fairness, where everyone can live better in an evolved world, with no distinction between strong and weak. This is something you can't understand."

"Enough nonsense, let's get straight to the point. We're here to plunder." Hesie spread her hands, not wanting to waste words with an otherworldly dog. "You choose - end it yourself, or let us do it?"

"Either way, it's death."

Klauno narrowed his eyes, feeling immense pressure. He knew he was in a desperate situation, unsure why the dark guild had targeted the other world.

Now that the interdimensional gate was open and couldn't be closed, the situation forced Klauno to fight with his back against the wall, hoping to survive.

Relying on the otherworldly creatures' ability to absorb magic and qi, he might be able to defeat the two strong enemies before him.

Klauno made up his mind, staring at the duo, and as a cold wind blew by, he swiftly raised his staff to strike first.

"You won't get your hands on the other world! I won't let you in!"

Boom! A massive pressure erupted! A giant claw mark materialized in the air, splitting Klauno's body into pieces!

The former strongest adventurer was instantly killed before Sarret, without even a chance to scream, his body falling into a pool of blood.

The otherworldly creatures' ability to absorb magic and qi didn't activate - it seemed Sarret and Hesie had long prepared countermeasures.

Hesie looked at Klauno's corpse, shaking her head. "Tsk tsk tsk, poor guy. Choosing to end it himself could have at least left a whole body~"

Sarret gazed at the alchemical claw gauntlets on his hands, shimmering with black-red light. "That Flamel guy usually acts like a madman, but his creations are unexpectedly useful."

"Those supposedly fearsome otherworldly creatures can't even withstand his alchemy."

title: Chapter 51 — Return
content:
Chapter 51 — Return

Volume 37 · Chapter 51

Heci frowned, her tone disdainful. "Flamel is only impressive at alchemy stuff. At best he's just a human. The only reason he could join Phoenix is because he can refine Philosopher's Stones."

"You can't say that," Beast King Saret said fairly. "Humans are weak, but they have excellent talents and can reach a certain height within a hundred years, making up for their short lifespans." He knew that as a dragon, Heci was already incredibly powerful and had every reason to look down on other races.

"Useless. The one who lives to the end is the winner. A short lifespan is an unbeatable weakness for humans." Heci didn't care about Saret's words. She looked up at the interdimensional gate open in the sky and said slowly, "Stop wasting time. Before the gate closes, let's head to the other world and bring back the Interdimensional King's eyeballs."

"Just the two of us?" Saret asked worriedly and nervously. "Isn't that a bad idea?"

"What's wrong with that?" Heci asked confused.

"Maybe we should wait for backup and enter together. It'd be safer." Saret paused and voiced his concern. "We just took out some minions, but entering the other world means facing the Interdimensional King directly. He's the ruler of the world's seams. For safety's sake, don't rush in."

"What's the Interdimensional King? Just some monster surviving in the seams. Not hard to deal with." Heci said carelessly, thinking Saret was being overly cautious and unnecessary.

"But... the Interdimensional King became the ruler of the seams, so his strength must be extraordinary. Even with Flamel's alchemical weapons, we might not guarantee victory." Saret thought for a moment and whispered, "I think dealing with the other world requires the Guild Master to come personally. He has the power to destroy the entire other world."

"What?" Heci's eyes showed disbelief. She shook her head. "Saret, you're too weak. Your level is too low. You haven't seen true power. I don't need the Guild Master to handle the Interdimensional King. I'm enough."

"That's not safe. I advise you not to do this," Saret cautioned.

"Hmph. That's why you're just a small fry in Phoenix. You'll never reach the core circle." Heci sighed helplessly, like a newbie talking to this max-level veteran about how scary Slimes are. What a joke?

"Being careful is never wrong. Your arrogance will get you into trouble someday." Saretze thought this confidence would ruin Heci.

But dragons always have this flaw.

"Less talk. I'm one of Phoenix's Three Greats, a dragon genius named Heci Igor. The other world poses no threat to me." Heci turned and walked toward the interdimensional gate. "If you're so scared, stay here and wait for me. You're just my baggage-carrying lackey anyway."

Saret's face darkened. He was annoyed but couldn't lash out, because Heci was indeed powerful and a core member of the guild—

A Dark Holy Dragon vs. the Interdimensional King, ruler of the seams? The chance of victory felt slim.

Forget it. I'll follow and see. Maybe Heci will run into trouble.

The other world was different from the mortal realm. There was no sun, only a pitch-black world. Everywhere were cracks of other dimensions and wandering monsters.

Mysterious energy ran rampant here, easily grinding people to dust. Souls would become mindless puppets, devoured by the other dimensions.

No wonder the monsters here wanted to leave this hellhole. It was completely unsuitable for survival, full of unknown dangers everywhere!

Yet in this other world stood a magnificent palace—the Interdimensional King's residence, the only decent building here.

The Interdimensional King was the first monster born in this dimension, appearing with the rift itself. It was the ruler here, devouring magic and martial energy from the mortal world, and feeding on other monsters.

Rumble—

A deafening roar shook the world. The magnificent palace was engulfed in black flames. Monsters fled in terror.

The dragon's aura spread constantly, keeping monsters away. They had never been invaded by a mortal creature before.

"So this is the Interdimensional King? Completely pathetic, just as I thought."

Heci sat on the Interdimensional King's throne, looking down at the massive corpse, its arms severed. Its true form was a multi-armed humanoid monster whose every move could shake the entire other world.

Unfortunately, it couldn't withstand Heci's attack and was instantly killed. The Dark Holy Dragon's breath was so powerful it pierced through its chest as easily as slicing tofu.

"So this is the powerful Interdimensional King you mentioned? Saret?"

*Saret's forehead dripped cold sweat. He had witnessed everything. The Interdimensional King wasn't weak—Heci was far stronger, completely overwhelming, the fight had no suspense at all!

"I already told you. Your level is too low, Saret. What you think is strong isn't strong at all." Heci said leisurely, giving Saret a proper lesson.

Saret had no reply. He thought: No wonder Heci was one of the guild's Three Greats. With such strength, she deserved it. What about the other two? Were they as terrifying?

The Beast King dared not think further. He was just an ordinary member, far below the Three Greats. What kind of existence was the rarely-seen Guild Master?

No one would believe it. Saret had been in Phoenix for so long but never seen the mysterious Guild Master. Only the Three Greats and early members had seen the Master's true face.

"So relaxing. Going out is like a vacation." Heci jumped onto the Interdimensional King's corpse head, plunged her hand into its eye socket, and ripped out the huge eyeball—

"Got it. Finally can go back and report."

"Looks like making the Philosopher's Stone, just need a few more rings now."

Meanwhile, Merlin and Alice had returned to Lexham. The carriage slowly stopped in front of the landlady's house.

As they dismounted, they heard Chris playing, her voice coming from the landlady's yard.

"Hua Hua, come here. You're being naughty again. Careful, no bones for you tonight."

Hearing his daughter's lively voice, Merlin felt a bit nervous. He couldn't describe the feeling in his heart—

I've been gone so long. Will this kid resent me?

What do I do? I'm dying of nervousness!

How to face Chris's resentful little eyes.

title: Chapter 52 — Father and Daughter
content:
Chapter 52 — Father and Daughter

Volume 37 · Chapter 52

Alice noticed Merlin's complexion wasn't good, so she whispered, "What's wrong?" "Nothing, just nervous." Merlin replied anxiously. "It's just that I'm about to see Chris; what do you have to be nervous about? Seeing one's own daughter is normal for a father, isn't it?" Alice muttered, puzzled, not understanding why Merlin was flustered. It had been three years since she'd seen her own father; surely Chris would be overjoyed to see him. "I haven't shown my face in three years, after all. I keep feeling like I've done something wrong, a strong sense of guilt—Chris won't have forgotten me, will she?" Merlin's worries were written all over his face. "Oh? You even know you made a mistake? I thought you never reflected on yourself." Alice sneered from the side. "You'll also reflect properly." Merlin answered embarrassedly. "Don't worry, you not coming back for three years was unavoidable; Chris will understand you, and besides, this kid mentions you every day—she could never forget you as her dad. Hurry up and catch up; I still want to give Chris a surprise." Alice tugged at Merlin's sleeve, comforting him not to think too much. "Cough cough." Merlin cleared his throat twice to ease the awkwardness, then lowered his gaze to the husky at his feet and whispered quietly, "Aweis, you'll soon get to meet my daughter—you'd better behave and try to cheer her up as much as possible." "Hmph! Don't think I'll submit to a little brat; I'll just casually go along with it, and you still want me to grovel and flatter a little monster? What a joke—where am I supposed to put my old face?" Aweis lowered his voice, emphasizing, "I am a proud holy dragon; making me lower my head would be the death of me." "Tsk! You'd better drop that arrogant attitude; if my daughter isn't happy, you won't get anything good either." Merlin warned sternly, making it clear that if he felt unwell, Aweis wouldn't have a good time either. "Aweis broke out in a cold sweat on his forehead, thinking, 'No wonder he's a ferocious Demon Lord—if I don't obey, he'll probably try to kill me.' This feeling of being threatened is so humiliating!" "Merlin? Who are you talking to?" Alice turned back in surprise, seeing Merlin standing there like a log, not intending to catch up. "No, you must have misheard." Merlin put on an innocent smile. "Huh?" Alice glanced suspiciously at the husky, didn't think much of it, and said, "Hurry up, don't let Chris get impatient…" In the landlady's yard, the little one was playing with a little *flower named "Flower", completely unaware that the parents had returned. Little Chris threw the ball far away, then kept coaxing, "Flower! Bring that ball back~" The little *flower looked puzzled at the ball thrown far away, glanced at Chris, and kept wagging its tail, seemingly not understanding Chris's meaning. "Hey, Flower, you're so dumb—how many times do I have to tell you?" Little Chris could only run over herself to pick up the ball and place it at her feet, saying, "This is how you play, got it?" The little *flower immediately sat up, lifted its paw to clap for Chris, wagging its tail even more vigorously, as if thinking Alice would have it perform a ball‑fetching trick worthy of encouragement. Chris's little head was full of question marks; she felt something was off—had her and Flower's roles been reversed? Shouldn't the dog be the one cheering her up? "Chris!" Alice's call rang out; Chris's eyes lit up, she instantly forgot all her worries and toddled toward the garden gate. Seeing her mother's figure, little Chris felt delighted—she could finally go home with Mom and had lots of things to tell her. "Mommy~ Mommy~" Alice squatted down, opening her arms, wanting to get close to her daughter after not seeing this little cutie for a while. But Chris ran halfway, suddenly spotted Merlin standing beside Alice, and her eyes widened in disbelief. The little one made a 90‑degree turn, left Alice aside, and lunged at Merlin, clinging tightly to his thigh. "Daddy? Daddy! Daddy!" "Come on, let me see if the little princess has grown taller?" Merlin bent down, lifted Chris from the ground, noticed she was a bit heavier than three years ago but not much changed. This made Merlin a little puzzled, but he soon realized—because of his demon blood, Chris's growth would be slow, so no change in three years was normal. Little Chris kept tugging at Merlin's cheeks with her hands, feeling like she was dreaming, a bit unreal, her voice trembling as she said, "It's really Daddy!" Merlin didn't resist, letting her tug at his face, and replied indistinctly, "Genuine, don't pull—I'm not wearing a mask." "!!!" Chris covered her red little face, feeling happiness come too suddenly, with no warning, saying she'd just come back, "Daddy's back~" "Yeah, I'm back." Merlin nodded, carefully observing Chris; even if he hadn't been there, Alice had looked after the girl J L very well. "What's wrong with this kid? Why doesn't she believe I'm back?" Alice hadn't been the first to hug her daughter; her empty arms felt awkward, so she put her hands behind her back and thought, "I've failed—this daughter is as good as raised for nothing, now that she has a dad she forgets Mom, damn it! Why?" "As a parent, am I not a hundred times better than Merlin?" Continuing to make Alice look ugly, she glared at Merlin with an unpleasant expression, not giving a good answer. "Why else? It's all because you didn't come back for three years, making her think she was dreaming!" "Is that so?" Merlin looked at Chris again, his guilt heavier, feeling that not seeing his daughter for three years was terrible. "No, it's not like that—it's because Mom kept telling me Dad would be back soon, and now he really is, I feel like I haven't even woken up yet, hehe~" Chris rubbed her little face, her head feeling dizzy. "Ha ha~ looks like it's not my fault, it's yours, Alice." Merlin felt relieved, his smile gradually turning smug. "Hey! You two, teaming up against me as soon as you meet?" Alice flared up, hands on her hips, retorting, "Why would I lie to Chris? It's not because you're this jerk, Merlin!" Merlin felt a twinge of sourness; even seeing his daughter, she wouldn't believe he'd really returned, and in a sense his responsibility was great. He hadn't accompanied Chris for three years; compared to Mom Alice, this dad had seriously neglected his duty, feeling ashamed. "I take responsibility, but Dad won't easily leave you from now on—believe me, Chris." "Daddy~ zhong" Chris snuggled into Merlin's embrace, desperately inhaling the familiar scent—today was his happiest moment in three years! Alice watched them from the side, her heart full of relief, and didn't disturb them; Chris had finally seen Merlin, so they should be allowed a quiet moment together. Merlin gently set Chris on the ground, then called to Aweis behind him, speaking mysteriously— "Actually, Dad brought you a gift this time; guess what it is?"

title: Chapter 53 — WTMTB
content:
Chapter 53 — WTMTB

Volume 37 · Chapter 53

“What’s up?” little Chris asked in a cute voice, her heart full of anticipation, not knowing what gift Dad had brought back. Aweis, in the form of a Husky, saw Merlin calling him and, reluctantly, walked over, sizing up Chris, then proudly lifted his dog head. Don’t look at Aweis now submitting to Merlin and agreeing to be a pet—having him fawn over a little brat is really too much for him; he absolutely refuses to let go of his pride. “Wow~” Chris’s eyes sparkled with stars; it was her first time seeing such a huge dog, far bigger than Huahua by who knows how many times, looking like a wolf. Chris, being short, didn’t even reach the height of the Husky’s head; to her, such a big dog already counted as a beast to look up to. Aweis glanced sideways at Chris, thinking, Is this Lucifer’s daughter? She looks… actually pretty cute, huh? No way! Don’t be fooled by this little brat’s appearance—this is the Demon Lord’s child, maybe just as wicked and shameless as Lucifer; I can’t afford to mess up in front of this little imp! “How about it? Do you like it? This is the dog Dad raised back home, specially brought back to be your pet.” Merlin said mysteriously, guessing the little one could never imagine that he’d have a dragon as her pet~. “I like it!” Chris nodded like a pecking chick; she already liked the landlady’s dog, and now she had her own pet, though the little one was still hesitant, because Mom wouldn’t let Chris keep a pet, saying it’s too dirty. Aweis widened his dog eyes in surprise, his face bewildered as he looked at Alice, inwardly shouting Who’s dirty?! I’m not just some stray dog—I’m a giant dragon, and I’m super clean, okay? “This” Alice wanted to speak but stopped; it wasn’t that she didn’t allow Chris to keep a pet, but that she herself was too busy, with no spare energy to care for a pet, and looking after Chris was already exhausting. Besides, Chris is still so young that she probably couldn’t properly care for a pet; if you can’t treat a little life well, then you shouldn’t keep one—this is good for both the young daughter and the little life, so a blanket ban on pets at home is most suitable. “Mom isn’t forbidding you to have a pet; she’s just worried you can’t handle the responsibility of being an owner, got it?” “Huh?” Chris tilted her little head, half‑understanding. Alice squatted down and said earnestly, “If you really got a pet, could you take good care of it? Mom and Dad won’t help you raise it.” “I can! I’ve been looking after Huahua all along, I have tons of experience!” Chris lifted her little face, stubbornly answering, clearly wanting to take Aweis home. “Are you sure you can take good care of it, even when it’s sick you’d stay by its side?” Alice doubted, feeling Chris was still too small to have that ability. “Mm‑mm‑mm~” little Chris kept nodding, instantly falling for the big Husky; petting it would surely feel better than Huahua. “Alright then.” Alice nodded helplessly; since Chris had made her stance clear, she wouldn’t say more, and would later use any issues as a chance to properly educate her daughter. After getting Mom’s consent, Chris happily spun around on the spot, eager to approach the tall Husky. Dad, does it have a name? “Name? If I just called him Aweis, that’d be too obvious, so I need another name—this one’s Wangcai! Yeah, that’s it—he’s Wangcai! Hahaha.” “What a lame name—did you dig it out of a money hole?” Alice rolled her eyes, despairing at Merlin’s naming skills; it sounded like it didn’t belong to this world at all. “I’ve always called it that; the meaning is ‘attract wealth and treasure,’ and it should come from some mysterious Eastern name.” Merlin gave a vague answer. “Such a corny name—if the dog could understand, it would surely be ashamed and faint.” Alice thought the dog was too pitiful. Aweis’s eyes glistened with tears; he thought resentfully, Exactly! What a tacky name! I’ve long since lost patience with Lucifer’s taste! “Wangcai? What a weird name.” Chris thought for a moment, laughed happily, “But it actually sounds pretty nice~” Aweis frowned, unable to stop himself from mentally ranting, Not nice at all! No wonder—being Lucifer’s woman, her taste is on the same level! This is hopeless; this kid’s already been led astray by Lucifer! Chris noticed the Husky standing before her, cold and aloof, completely unlike Huahua’s warm attitude toward people; she felt a bit disappointed, “Dad, it doesn’t seem to like me? It’s not wagging its tail—normal dogs wag their tails.” “Who said it doesn’t like you? It’s just a bit slow; this breed has that trait, it’s rather dull.” Merlin said soothingly, then glared fiercely at Aweis, as if saying— “What do you mean? Want to die? Dare to be so cold to my precious daughter—believe it or not, I’ll send you back to Demon City as ingredients!” Aweis shuddered, terrified; his dog tail behind him swept like a broom, flicking away the dust under his rear. Chris showed a satisfied smile, reached out her little hand, wanting to train her pet, “Come on, put out your paw.” Aweis’s face showed extreme reluctance—how could I, a great holy dragon, now be made to play with a little brat and have to cheer her up? This is like grinding his last dignity into the dirt. So Aweis turned his head away, adopting an aloof pose, letting the dragon that usually soars in the sky act like a dog—if I say stretch out your paw, I stretch out your paw, then wouldn’t I lose face? “Huh?” Merlin’s death‑stare came again, thinking this guy’s a bit disobedient—maybe my intimidation isn’t enough yet? Aweis grew nervous again, his eyes darting; under pressure he reluctantly stuck out his dog paw and placed it in Chris’s palm, constantly comforting himself inside— It’s just for a living, not shameful; being a dog for a little brat is still better than Merlin, at least I’m a bit freer~ “Dad, Wangcai is awesome—I taught Huahua for ages and she never learned it, but Wangcai gets it right away!” little Chris’s eyes shone, her cheeks flushed with excitement, feeling she might have the talent of a pet trainer? “Ha, Merlin gave a dry chuckle, thinking This isn’t an ordinary dog—it’s a holy dragon, my little princess, naturally possessing considerable wisdom; he’s just playing with you,” “Although Wangcai is smart, he’s not very obedient; if worse comes to worst, we’ll just stew him and eat him.” Aweis lowered his head in fright, realizing Lucifer was warning him, afraid he wouldn’t properly accompany the little girl before him; given Lucifer’s personality, he could actually do something like that. But who knew Chris would immediately object—she threw her arms around Aweis’s neck, puffed out her little mouth, and said angrily, “No way! Wangcai is my pet now; Dad can’t just eat him, and he’s smart, well‑behaved, and hasn’t done anything wrong—how could you bear to?” Chris shielded Aweis with her small frame, her cheeks rubbing against his soft fur, her little hands constantly scratching his neck; rubbing him really felt countless times better than Huahua. For a moment Aweis felt a touch of emotion; his cold gaze softened a little— This kid may have poor taste, but she’s nothing like Lucifer; she’s willing to use her tiny body to protect a lowly pet. She’s practically a little angel~ And, this technique is awesome—rubbing me feels so great. No way! I’m going to lick this super cute little Mengli to bits, prprprp

title: Chapter 54 — This Marriage
content:
Chapter 54 — This Marriage

Volume 37 · Chapter 54

Chris had been getting along with Huahua, that little female dog, for a long time, and had plenty of experience petting dogs; a light scratch‑scratch on the little female dog would make it involuntarily expose its belly. Aweis wore a happy expression, moved close to Chris to let her pet him, and inexplicably felt a strong sense of comfort; he even couldn't help rolling on the ground, exposing his white belly—. Feeling so good, is this what being petted feels like? It's much more comfortable than scratching an itch; I never expected this little guy to have this talent~. Aweis looked at the young Chris with newfound respect, thinking this kid was much easier to get along with than Lucifer; maybe having her as a pet would be a real cushy job. As a noble holy dragon, after leaving the church there were no good days; every day he had to stay on guard against those demons, living a miserable life. But Aweis seemed to see a ray of light in Chris, subtly and continuously drawn to her, even feeling an urge to protect this little guy. After leaving the church, Chris was the only one willing to approach Aweis with a kind attitude; this gave the depressed Aweis a little island where he could rest a bit, incredibly precious. Not everyone would risk their life for a dog, but Chris stood out; with her small frame she seriously wanted to protect him. This move successfully touched Aweis; he couldn't figure out why the vile, shameless evil Lucifer would have such a kind, adorable daughter, like a little angel. Aweis secretly formed an idea: since Lucifer is so hard to serve, it's better to follow the little guy; when Lucifer gives him a hard time, someone will have his back—how nice! What is the pride of the dragon race? It can't be eaten as food, and besides, following such an adorable little master is far better than those stiff church priests; this move isn't a loss! Aweis had already tossed aside the so‑called pride; though he wasn't a lolicon, being beside the little angel was enjoyable, and he most liked approaching pure, kind souls. Moreover, Aweis sensed that Chris was somewhat different, emanating a mysterious warm power; after she gently stroked him, his fatigue vanished, leaving him spirited. “Woof woof woof!” Hehe, he’s so lively, Dad . Chris kept petting Aweis’s white belly, thinking that just moments ago the dog was aloof, now it had surrendered; I’m really a genius pet‑trainer! Aweis was overjoyed, rolling wildly on the ground, hoping Chris would pet him a bit longer, showing no trace of a dragon’s dignity. “Huh?” Alice felt a hint of doubt; she had observed this husky for a long time, always silent, never showing any enthusiasm toward people, so why did his dog nature surface in front of Chris? Merlin watched Aweis rolling all over the ground, feeling bewildered, sensing this wasn’t the holy dragon he knew—had he already surrendered so quickly? This was completely unlike what he imagined. Aweis excitedly got up from the ground, stuck out his tongue, and licked Chris’s little face fiercely, making the little guy extremely itchy. “So itchy~” Chris wiped her face, immediately put on a serious look, “Sit nicely.” Aweis immediately sat down, his dog tail wagging nonstop; after contact with Chris, he felt his inner power stirring, becoming more active than before. He couldn’t figure out what was happening; he wondered if the little guy had inherited some of Lucifer’s power that could stimulate bodily potential. “Dad, am I strong? Will I be able to become an animal trainer someday?” little Chris asked proudly, striking a pose of seeking her father’s praise. Merlin smiled without speaking, thinking where’s the strength? This guy isn’t just obeying me out of fear, starting to work honestly? But Merlin noticed the sly glint in Aweis’s eyes, suddenly sensed something off, recalling Aweis’s earlier reaction—. Wait! Is this guy really that easy to subdue? Even if his body is obedient, his mouth surely won’t give in. Could it be that Aweis is enjoying this? No way, could this bastard be a lolicon? No, Aweis is so proud, he couldn’t possibly have any improper thoughts toward humanoid beings. Merlin stared at Aweis, pondering various possibilities, wondering if bringing him back was a mistake; this guy’s gleeful appearance was definitely not normal! “Cough cough! Wangcai actually never really listens; when the chance comes, I should give him a good beating—using fists is the most useful against dogs.” Aweis heard this and his fur stood on end; he was frightened by Merlin’s words, even though he had been behaving as a pet, why was Lucifer still dissatisfied? Chris immediately stepped in front of Aweis, puffed out her little mouth angrily, and said dissatisfiedly, “Dad, don’t do that—Wangcai is my pet from now on, you can’t hit him; only I can.” Merlin was at a loss for words, seeing his daughter’s earnest expression; he had nothing to say, for if his daughter came to dislike him it would be terrible. Aweis felt a secret delight deep inside; he earnestly licked Chris’s little shoe with his tongue, while his gaze flicked to Merlin, thinking triumphantly— You didn’t expect that, Lucifer—this is my escape route! You who love your daughter so much surely don’t want to be disliked, right? So I’ll lick your daughter to death, build a deep friendship, and completely shake off your enslavement of me! Will I end up submitting to you? Your daughter is ten thousand times stronger than you, Lucifer! “Dad wouldn’t hit Wangcai; I was just joking.” Merlin’s stiff smile comforted his daughter, wondering what Aweis was getting proud about; I originally planned to have him accompany her, so wouldn’t think that just because Chris protects him he’d escaped my grasp—no way! Aweis had already forgotten his earlier resistance; he once thought being a dragon nanny was a humiliating job, but after meeting Chris he felt the job wasn’t so bad. Little Chris finally relaxed, patted Aweis’s dog head, then called over the little female dog Huahua, putting on a mature‑adult act, speaking in an old‑fashioned tone. “Huahua, this is Wangcai; Wangcai, this is Huahua; from now on you two are good friends—get along well.” Aweis glanced at the little *, feeling contempt inside; “Hah! What a joke—I’m a noble holy dragon soaring the skies; how could I befriend an insignificant little female dog? Does this little * not fear me? As soon as I release my dragon aura, this dog will drop dead!” Chris tilted her head in puzzlement; the husky returned to its aloof demeanor, though Huahua seemed very enthusiastic, yet obviously didn’t grasp the meaning of her words—. Only see little ** Huahua turn her rear toward Aweis, wiggling her tail, as if saying “come in”. “! ! ?” Aweis stared wide‑eyed, mouth agape, unable to speak, his head buzzing as if struck by lightning! Chris: “Dad, what does that mean?” Merlin: “Don’t ask—asking just means I approve this marriage.”

title: Chapter 55 — Blessing (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 55 — Blessing (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 37 · Chapter 55

Merlin was gloating on the side, never expecting that the landlady's little female dog happened to be in heat; upon seeing the tall, sturdy husky, it instinctively wanted to mate.
Merlin almost laughed out loud, having no intention to stop it; thinking of the high-and-mighty holy dragon being given autumn glances by a little female dog, he found it quite amusing.
"Ah ha! Avis! I never thought you'd have a day like this! The landlady's lovely young lady has already sent you a marriage proposal; why don't you respond?"
Even if Merlin didn't know what Avis was thinking right now, he could guess roughly; he estimated Avis was so angry he might cough up blood, and wished to blast the little female dog with a single breath of dragon breath.
However, Merlin thought for a moment; Avis's husky incarnation must be extraordinarily handsome among dogs, so it's no wonder it attracts other opposite-sex counterparts.
Alice's face turned red; she pulled Merlin's hand and said sternly, "What do you mean agreeing to this marriage? Don't corrupt the children."
"Cough cough!" Merlin gave two light coughs, speaking in a tone of watching the spectacle: "This is an inevitable stage of life's reproduction; how is that corrupting the kids? Besides, I think Wangcai and Huahua are a great match, I agree~"
Avis was furious, his dog fur all standing on end; he thought, "Shameless Lucifer, is humiliating me really that enjoyable? You're a match for my grandfather! If you've got the guts, come at me!"
"After all, I am also a holy dragon; to end up being the object of a little female dog's heat is a tremendous disgrace!"
"This interspecies love, Avis cannot accept; Merlin still sneers from the side, making him grit his teeth in hatred, as if releasing dragon might to make the little female dog retreat."
"Just as Avis was torn, a 'creak' sounded; the house door slowly opened, and the landlady's elderly figure stepped out, gently placing her broom outside, as if she had just finished cleaning the house."
"The landlady raised her head, saw Alice, and her smile wrinkled together: 'Miss Alice, you're back? You didn't even give a heads-up.'"
"'I just got back myself, preparing to pick Chris up home, thank you for your help looking after her these days,' Alice said with a slight bow, feeling deep respect for the landlady, who had been a great help while she wasn't with Chris."
"'We've said it many times, you don't need to be so polite with me,' the landlady replied with a smile; upon occasionally seeing Merlin, her expression shifted slightly: 'Mr. Merlin?'"
"'Just pretend I wasn't here, landlady.'"
"Merlin also bowed slightly; he had heard from Alice that the landlady had helped look after Chris, and both of them owed her a favor; even though the landlady is an ordinary person, Merlin would show her extra respect and not be too casual."
"This elderly person doesn't know how much longer she can live; Merlin feels her lifespan may be short, and he can't help but feel a sense of melancholy."
"Merlin and Alice have lived in this person's house for several years, and they inevitably develop some fondness for the old lady."
"If the landlady passes away, not to mention Alice, even Merlin would feel that life might be missing something."
"Merlin thinks he isn't someone who dwells on the past, but emotions are something he cannot control; including those familiar faces in the guild, he will care about them more."
"The landlady's expression gradually returned to normal, and she sighed, 'You've finally returned; you haven't shown your face for three whole years—I thought you wouldn't come back to Rexham.'"
"'How could that be? I wouldn't leave easily,' Merlin glanced at Alice and whispered, 'There's someone very important here.'"
"Alice's face turned red; she knew Merlin was hinting at her, but saying such things in front of the landlady still made her feel a bit embarrassed."
"'I see; do you know that over these three years, Miss Alice has almost constantly been thinking of you?' the landlady asked softly."
"'Huh? Is that really the case, Alice?' Merlin glanced at the Alice beside him."
"'No no no! That's not true, it's exaggerated!' Alice's face flushed red as she frantically explained, but it dwindled to a mosquito-like whisper: 'I really didn't—'"
"'Miss Alice is just too shy to admit her inner feelings, but I can clearly see that every time she comes to pick Chris up home, she sighs; even your daughter, upon learning you can't return, feels equally low-spirited. For this mother and daughter, you are truly important; please, Mr. Merlin, take note—you are not alone, you have your own family; as a husband, you should shoulder your responsibility and not appear again with a three-year absence, which would be a severe blow to the marriage.' The landlady paused, then continued in the tone of someone who's been through it: 'Miss Alice loves you, that's why she's waited three years for you; in fact, you're draining her affection for you.'"
"'Alice remained silent, not saying a word, turning her gaze elsewhere; deep down she still harbored a tiny bit of resentment toward Merlin.'"
"'I feel sorry for my three-year absence; you're right, I bear great responsibility.' Merlin did not rebut the landlady, thinking her words made sense."
"'Mr. Merlin, I'm glad you understand my words; I believe you will surely become an excellent husband and father.' The landlady held her little dog close, speaking meaningfully: 'I heard from Miss Alice that you returned to your hometown to handle some important matters; I don't know if you've finished them yet?'"
"'Well... Merlin didn't know how to answer for a moment, then said tactfully, 'Of course, although these are very troublesome matters, they've all been settled; I'll stay in Rexham long-term as before.'"
"'Then that's good.'"
"The landlady nodded, showing a look of wanting to speak but hesitating, due to whether she should reveal that a demon lord might come to assassinate Chris."
"However, the landlady doesn't want others to know she was once a holy spirit; if she spoke of it, there would be a risk of exposure."
"Looking at Merlin's demeanor, he likely has no idea of the dangers Chris has faced; that demon lord named Asmodeus hasn't revealed anything about himself."
"The landlady decided to forget about it, treating it as if it never happened; perhaps it was just a minor incident during internal turmoil among the demons."
"'Granny! Look at my pet, I also have a doggy~' Chris's petite figure was already riding on Avis."
"'Oh~, what a cute dog.' The landlady replied with a smiling glance; in one look she saw through Avis, thinking 'Is it a giant dragon? It seems not just a pet.'"
"'Hehe~*' Chris felt a bit proud, discovering that Wangcai was sturdy enough to even be ridden like a horse, giving her far more fun than Huahua."
"'Mr. Merlin, Miss Alice, seeing you two reunited makes me happy; I wonder if we could get a little closer? You should know I love seeing loving couples; it reminds me of my youth, endlessly nostalgic.' The landlady looked at the two, speaking gently: 'Tonight, could you give me a good dream?'"
"'This' Alice hesitated."
"'What's that? The landlady's wish is easily fulfilled, of course no problem.' Merlin grabbed Alice's hand, then interlocked their ten fingers."
"'??? Alice looked at Merlin in surprise, lowered her blushing cheeks, and rested her head on Merlin's shoulder.'"
"'You really are well matched, I'm satisfied.' The landlady noticed some subtle changes and said meaningfully——"
"'Compared to three years ago, it seems you no longer have any barriers between you?'"
"'Indeed, have you accepted each other? How should I put it?'"
"'Happy newlywed life~'"

title: Chapter 56 — Hidden Danger
content:
Chapter 56 — Hidden Danger

Volume 37 · Chapter 56

Merlin brought Chris home and stayed with her for a long time before the little girl finally fell asleep, unsatisfied.

Clearly, one night was not enough to release the long-buried longing in Chris's heart.

Chris told her father about every single thing that had happened to her over the past three years.

Although they were all very boring things, Merlin still listened quietly, knowing that his daughter needed a listener.

Finally, the little girl ended up leaning on the husky's body and fell asleep. The warm body of Ivy made her feel very comfortable.

Merlin took a deep breath, carefully picked up the sleeping Chris, then kicked Ivy's foot and said in a cold voice, "Don't pretend to sleep, you damn thing, don't get too full of yourself. Don't think that because I have my daughter protecting you, you can do whatever you want."

Ivy rolled over and got up from the ground, smiling awkwardly and saying in a low voice, "You misunderstood, Lucifer, I don't have that intention. Keeping promises is my strength. Since I promised to be your daughter's pet, I won't back out. Do you think I did anything wrong? I'm even more beloved by my master than a real dog is, look at how much your daughter likes me~"

"Uh, that's right," Merlin was speechless. Ivy was so hardworking in forced business, wasn't it her own request? If Chris didn't like Ivy, why did I bring it out of the demon city?

In a certain sense, Ivy was excellent in completing the task. Not only shouldn't it be scolded, but it should be praised. The proud saint dragon, willing to lower its status to make a small child happy, was already very rare.

However, Merlin still had a few complaints, so he lowered his voice and said in a warning tone. "You can listen to Chris when you're not around, but if I'm here, you'd better listen to me. Understand?"

"Of course, I can still judge properly. I'm submitting to you, not your daughter." Ivy nodded.

Merlin finally relaxed a bit. It seems that my concerns were unnecessary. I thought Ivy would be very reluctant to take care of Chris, but she was so active.

This seems a bit abnormal. Where did the arrogance of the noble saint dragon go? Shouldn't they resist to the end for their honor?

"Do you like my daughter?"

"Nonsense, who doesn't like a little angel? Should I like a scheming pope or a vile and dishonest demon lord?" Ivy looked at Merlin with disdain, obviously disagreeing with Merlin's opinion.

Merlin's body trembled, and he asked in a low voice, "Old man, aren't you a pedophile?"

"Damn it, Lucifer, what do you think I am?" Ivy gnashed her teeth and responded angrily, "I am a dragon representing light and purity. Don't put your perverted ideas on me. It's an insult to my dignity, and I can't tolerate it. You can distort my will, but you can't touch my bottom line."

Merlin was speechless. Ivy seemed to be right. After knowing this guy for a long time, the most intolerable thing is slander. Okay, I was wrong. I can apologize, but you're very abnormal. You don't like taking care of small children, right? Even if it's because I forced you, I don't believe it."

"Won't it be? Lucifer, with your abilities, can't you feel the power contained in your daughter?" Ivy asked in surprise.

Merlin suddenly stopped, and answered hesitantly, "The power of life?"

"That's right. The power of life is the root of creation and the original power that exists in the world before its birth. It is from it that everything has evolved." Ivy looked at Chris sleeping in Merlin's arms and said meaningfully, "Your daughter is constantly releasing this power, especially when in close contact. This feeling is most obvious at first. I also didn't understand at first, but after she touched me, my magic power was boiling inside. It must be stimulated by the power of life. As long as I stay by her side, my body and soul will be nourished."

"So is that the case?" Merlin was very surprised. I've been with Chris for a long time, but I've never had this feeling. Is it because I don't have magic power and qi? Alice seems to have not noticed it either, "No, right? Alice and Chris have been together for a long time, but they don't seem to have this feeling."

"Merlin, you're a demon, right? Humans are the most insensitive to external stimuli among all races, even dogs are not as sensitive as humans. The sense of dogs is thousands of times that of humans. You can imagine how bad humans are at perceiving subtle changes. Ivy paused and said in a speculative tone, "Moreover, your daughter's power should become more and more obvious as she grows older. It should be very difficult to perceive at first."

After listening to Ivy's explanation, Merlin understood a little bit. Before, I could feel the power of Chris, which delayed the pain brought by the heart curse.

If Chris can continue to grow and become strong enough, can she completely solve my hidden danger? It seems very possible.

However, Chris is still too young. It's unrealistic to wait for her to become strong enough. It's a very long process.

"That's why you changed your attitude. It's no use without profit, right?"

"That's only part of the reason. The main reason is" Ivy paused and looked at him with a heartbroken expression, "It's very painful to see a kind and pure little angel fall into the claws of a vile demon lord. I can't just watch it happen."

"What do you mean? She's my daughter. Don't say I might kill her at any time." Merlin frowned and said suspiciously, "Are you a pedophile?"

"Nonsense!" Ivy argued angrily, then changed the subject and asked, "Is this really the child born to you and that human woman? It's completely different from you two. It shouldn't have the original power of life."

"Oh? Do you have something to say?" Merlin hesitated. The birth of Chris was indeed very strange.

"As far as I know, the person who controls the law of life is the main god who dominates the heavens. Only she can have and control the most original power." Ivy said meaningfully.

"So you mean" Merlin narrowed his eyes and realized what Ivy wanted to express.

"Are all my guesses, don't be so tense. Ivy paused and continued to say in an advisory tone.

"Lucifer, you'd better be careful. Don't let your daughter come into contact with any undead creatures."

"As she grows older, she may become more and more dangerous."

"Because of the power on her body, hell will go crazy. No undead can resist the temptation to be revived."

title: Chapter 57 — The Great Masseur, Merlin
content:
Chapter 57 — The Great Masseur, Merlin

Volume 37 · Chapter 57

Merlin listened in silence, his gaze falling on Chris in his arms, a faint worry rising in his heart. Could Chris's power attract the covetousness of villains? As she grows older, it becomes harder to conceal. "Merlin, who are you talking to?" Alice peered over, seeing Merlin holding Chris and standing there in a daze. Ah, Merlin glanced away, embarrassed, replying, "I was just talking to myself with Chris." "Huh?" Alice noticed her daughter already asleep, drool trickling from the corner of her mouth, "She's already asleep, so don't disturb her." "I know." Merlin nodded, gently laying the little one on the bed and carefully tucking the blanket over her— No matter what, I cannot let Chris face any threat; I must keep all danger away. Could it be a necromancer? It seems Chris has never come into contact with any undead, so there's no need to worry for now. But what about the future? If there's truly no way, I can only hide with Chris and live in seclusion. But just now, what did Avis mean? Could Chris have some direct connection with that goddess? As Merlin pondered, the sleeping little one grabbed his finger and murmured in her dream, "Daddy, hee—" Merlin jerked awake, his expression turning grave, deciding not to tell Alice about this, lest it make her uneasy. What am I worrying about? No matter where Chris comes from, she is my daughter, carrying my and Alice's blood. Late at night, the couple sat in the living room, still awake. Alice handed Merlin a cup of hot tea, puzzled, asking, "What's wrong? Your face looks a bit grim—do you have something on your mind?" Merlin startled, lifted his head, thought for a moment, and temporarily set aside his worries about Chris, after all, his daughter is still safe for now. Even Avis only sensed the primordial life force after having close contact with Chris; outsiders never get that chance. "Nothing, what could I possibly have on my mind?" "Huh?" Alice, somewhat sensitive, lowered her voice, "We ... are husband and wife, right?" "Of course, why suddenly ask like this?" Merlin's smile gradually turned sinister as he reached out to restrain Alice's waist, thinking she needed him to do household chores? But who knew Alice furrowed her brows, swung a fist and hit Merlin's nose, dissatisfied, saying, "Behave yourself." Merlin had to release Alice, covering his sore nose, bewildered, asking, "What are you doing?" "This is my line; Chris is in the bedroom, waking her would be bad." Alice paused, then poked Merlin's forehead several times, "With Chris at home, you'd better behave properly, don't entertain foolish thoughts, lest you corrupt Chris—I won't let you off the hook." "That's true." Merlin nodded glumly, the sense of responsibility as a father welling up in him, "I thought you wanted..." Alice bit her lip, her face flushed, she whispered softly, "What are you thinking about? Filthy! I never thought about that..." "Really? Between husband and wife we should be honest." Merlin retorted, suspicious. "I'm not saying I don't want to, but I have to distinguish the occasion; I can't abandon my dignity as a mother, humph!" Alice huffed, turning her head away, her ears reddening. "Then I see, I also don't want to ruin the image of a proper father in Chris's eyes." Merlin said agreeably. "Forget it; in Chris's eyes, you're never a proper dad anyway." Alice's gaze held a hint of disdain. "No way?" "You're lying." "Well then, Alice, watch how I deal with you." Merlin directly grabbed Alice's waist, pressed her down beneath him, his hands roaming to her itchy spots, continually teasing. "Hahaha, stop stop, Alice is itchy unbearable, she lets out bursts of laughter." "Still dare?" Merlin lifted his head, looking down at Alice, his face smug as he questioned. "Alice panted lightly, her chest rising and falling, the thin sheer nightgown slightly disheveled, her white shoulders exposed— A vague flirtatious atmosphere began to spread, causing Merlin and Alice's minds to drift a little, their eyes locking, sending out thick waves of longing. Although they weren't novices, in the close rubbing they still found it hard to restrain rising desire, a thought forming to deepen their feelings. Alice's gaze was like water, exuding a tender, sweet affection; any man seeing that look would feel his heart soften, longing to pull her into his arms and cherish her. For a moment Merlin seemed to see it, he gently stroked Alice's flushed cheeks, worried about waking the daughter in the next room, trying to hold back but finding it difficult. "Alice" "Merlin" "No, Chris is right next door, forget it." "Maybe we can keep our voices down." Alice clearly hesitated, unsure how to handle the situation, yet deep down she felt a hint of pleasure at being held by Merlin, greedily savoring that heat. Merlin took a deep breath, decided to give it a try, so he tenderly brushed aside the hair on Alice's forehead and slowly leaned toward her trembling— "Eh? Mom and Dad, what are you doing?" A childish voice rang out; Merlin and Alice stared wide-eyed, bodies stiff, maintaining the awkward man‑on‑woman pose. The scene fell into extreme embarrassment; the little one's eyes fixed straight on Mom and Dad, sucking her finger, face full of puzzlement. Merlin and Alice had no choice but to freeze like statues, hoping the cute daughter would ignore them—as long as the couple wasn't awkward, the awkwardness would fall on someone else. "Mom and Dad, what are you doing? Why aren't you speaking?" little Chris tilted her head, bewildered, wondering what game this was. Merlin sprang up from the sofa, put on a fatherly smile, and changed the subject, "You woke up? Are you hungry? Dad will make you a late‑night snack." Seeing Merlin trying to slip away, Alice shoved herself back, one hand covering her flushed face, the other gripping Merlin tightly, refusing to let him flee, her thoughts in turmoil— "Shameless Merlin! Don't try to run! Leaving me alone in front of Chris, how am I supposed to explain this to her?!" Yet despite her innocence, the little one wasn't stupid; she bluntly asked again, "Mom and Dad, what were you just doing?" Merlin's expression turned *awkward*, forced by his daughter's questioning, his scalp tingling, changing the subject useless, a spirit of relentless questioning taking over. In desperation, Merlin immediately sat behind Alice, began to massage her shoulders, pretending to be serious— "What else can Dad do?" "Just now Dad was giving Mom a massage."

title: Chapter 58 — Great Loss
content:
Chapter 58 — Great Loss

Volume 37 · Chapter 58

Merlin energetically lifted Alice's shoulder and asked seriously, "How is it? The pressure is pretty good, right?" Alice coughed twice, her face flushed with embarrassment, replying, "Not bad, congratulations on learning a survival skill—no need to be a host." "Pfft!" Merlin nearly spat out a mouthful of old blood, his feelings a mixed bag, thinking, "Even if I don't become a host, could I become a masseuse? Don't look down on me!" "Dad, are you going to give Mom a massage again? Hmm?" Chris tilted her little head, her mind filled with question marks, sensing something off but unable to put it into words. "What are you looking at? Go back to sleep obediently." Merlin put on a stern facade, hoping the little one wouldn't keep staring. "I was actually getting sleepy, but seeing Dad give Mom a massage woke me up—I want to see exactly how Dad massages Mom." Little Chris showed no fear of her father's stern look, even waddling forward, her eyes wide open, staring at that pair of pure, innocent big eyes, making Merlin and Alice feel embarrassed, as if they really had to— in front of their daughter— rub— Alice's shoulders at night? Not to mention Alice couldn't sit still, even Merlin couldn't bear it, yet they weren't like the innocent daughter learning bad habits at such a young age, already understanding some strange things. Merlin felt goosebumps all over from being stared at by his daughter, forcing a faint smile, "Chris, be good, go back to sleep. What's there to watch me massage your mom?" "Yeah, go back to sleep. Mom and Dad will come keep you company." Alice also chimed in, her eyes darting around guiltily. "Nope, I want to watch Dad give Mom a massage—again, the way Dad was pressing onto Mom just now, it feels so weird~" Little Chris's cowlick on her head shook excitedly, her curiosity overcoming everything. *Merlin was at a loss for words, thinking, "Is this the end? Being stared at by my daughter, surely my pose with Alice just now was weird? Even if Chris is just a kid, she could sense something odd!" Alice covered her flushed face, having mentally cursed Merlin from head to toe; if it weren't for him constantly teasing her, how could she make such a rookie mistake? "Mom and Dad, what's wrong? Why don't you demonstrate once so I can learn too~" Chris smiled innocently, completely unaware how wicked her words were. "Um... um..." Merlin hesitated, then started lying, "The way I just massaged your mom is rather special; you're too young to learn it, we'll talk about it later." "Why?" Chris's eyes filled with a hint of disappointment, like a curious baby probing for answers. "Because... because this is a massage between adults; kids can't learn it, and if they try forcibly, they might end up wetting the bed every day." Merlin spoke solemnly while spouting nonsense. Alice thought Merlin was getting more ridiculous, and she jabbed him hard with her elbow, feeling he was clearly corrupting the child. Merlin rolled his eyes, thinking, "What else can I do? I'm left with no choice; first I'll try to curb Chris's curiosity, then we'll see." "Bedwetting?" Chris's eyes finally became hesitant, recalling how her mother would scold her when she wet the bed, so she became a bit timid, "Well, I guess I won't learn then—bedwetting is smelly." "That's right." Merlin let out a sigh of relief, marveling that his skill at deceiving kids had leveled up. Before Merlin could fully relax, Chris dropped an astonishing line: "Can Dad give Chris a massage too? Mom seemed happy just now, I want to try it as well." Merlin: "!!" Alice: "???" After hearing that, both stared at Chris in disbelief, never imagining such wicked, perverse words would come from their own daughter's mouth. Little did they know Chris understood nothing; she was simply voicing her honest thoughts, and she really was curious about what Dad had been doing while pressing onto Mom just then. "Who... who was happy ah!?" Alice felt as if struck by lightning, her face burning red, her voice like text: "I I didn't—" "But I just—" Before Chris could finish, Alice clapped a hand over her daughter's mouth, speaking sternly, "Don't talk nonsense; what you just saw were all hallucinations. When you wake up tomorrow, you'll forget it." "Mom's back again, I just want to experience the massage Dad just gave Mom." Chris waved her little fists in protest, feeling adults always dismiss her words. "No way, Chris, don't joke like that." Merlin replied with a stiff smile. "Why not?" Chris pouted, unconvinced, "If Mom can, why can't I?" "Because... because your mom and your grandmothers will immediately kill this big mourning—" Merlin's voice trailed off awkwardly, feeling the topic had slipped beyond his control; he certainly had no father-complex tendencies, just treating Chris as a clueless kid, as the saying goes, children's words are innocent. "What is 'great loss'?" Merlin: "Go to sleep!" Alice: "Go to sleep!" The little one was forcibly sent back to the bedroom, a single person lying on the bed, hard-pressed by the parents who had driven her back. Chris was so angry she couldn't sleep, pounding the blanket covering her with her tiny fists, tossing and turning in bed. Aweis watched the sleepless Chris, his eyes showing a hint of sympathy, thinking helplessly— Ah, it's all curiosity's fault; earlier he kept biting your pant legs and couldn't be stopped, yet you insisted on going out and getting a face full of dust. Little Chris turned over, gazing at the husky under the bed, curiously asking, "Wangcai, what were Mom and Dad doing just now?" Aweis rolled his eyes, thinking inwardly, What else could they be doing? A lone man and woman, making tea and fire—poor little angel has become an annoying lightbulb. "So annoying, why do adults always lie? Clearly I saw it, yet they keep saying I hallucinated—could it really be my fault?" Chris's cowlick on her head twisted into a question mark, unaware she'd done anything wrong. Aweis looked at Chris, sympathizing, thinking, What could be wrong with you? People grow up and become dirty; lying becomes routine; your parents, to ease their embarrassment, just dumped the blame on you—how pitiful~ "I think I just made a mistake, upset Mom and Dad—what should I do?" Chris pulled at the blanket, revealing a troubled expression. Seeing this, Aweis stretched out his dog paw, relying on his large size, gently patted Chris's head, as if comforting her, telling her not to dwell on it. Chris froze, looking at the pet just adopted today, feeling delighted, "Wangcai, you're so gentle—indeed I can't tell Mom and Dad the secret, I can only whisper it to you."
