Aweis's old face flushed red, feeling proud, "Oh ho ho~, of course I'm gentle, and I'm the only one who can patiently be a confidant for a little kid's worries; those irresponsible parents can't compare with me!" Chris stared blankly at Aweis, feeling as if, after being patted on the head, she had become the pet while the dog became the owner. The little one grew angrier the more she thought, got up, grabbed Aweis's head, and rubbed it vigorously, muttering— "I—I am the master~" "You mustn't get carried away, Wangcai." 9(@'^Q)f

title: Chapter 59 — Ghost Talk
content:
Chapter 59 — Ghost Talk

Volume 37 · Chapter 59

A few days later, a continuous barrage of celebratory cannon fire rang out. Today was the wedding day of Arnold, son of Count Austin, Lord of Rexham, and the adventurer Rosetti.

Quite a few people from the small town had gathered in Rexham's church to watch the ceremony.

Especially the close friends and relatives of the newlywed couple — almost all of them had shown up to offer their most sincere blessings.

Arnold stood before Rosetti in an impeccable formal suit, his face flushed with embarrassment as he kept scratching his head, looking extremely nervous.

This was the most important moment of his life; his mood was naturally indescribably stirred, as if he had been dressed up into an adult overnight.

Arnold was also someone who could pick things up and let them go. After giving up his pursuit of Alice, he realized what he truly needed.

He slowly began to face his feelings for Rosetti squarely.

Rosetti wore a wedding dress and looked much more mature than before. She had put away her sexy demeanor, instead exuding a reserved beauty.

She held a bouquet of flowers with her head lowered. Although she wasn't shy like Arnold, she was equally moved, enveloped in warm happiness.

Rosetti had waited for this day for a long time. Over these three years, her relationship with Arnold had heated up rapidly, and they had finally successfully entered the marriage hall.

Although Rosetti always joked about being the future countess, those who knew her well understood she wasn't after wealth and glory — she had secretly loved Arnold for many years.

The two had known each other for a long time. That they could reach the step of marriage naturally earned them many people's blessings.

The elderly priest flipped through the scripture, looked down at the two newlyweds, and asked in a solemn tone.

"Mr. Arnold, are you willing to take this woman as your wife? To love her, be faithful to her, whether she is poor, sick, or disabled, until death do you part."

Arnold: "I am willing."

"Miss Rosetti, are you willing to take this man as your husband? To love him, be faithful to him, whether he is poor, sick, or disabled, until death do you part."

Rosetti: "I am willing."

"Then congratulations to you both. May the great Goddess bless you forever."

Arnold mustered his courage and kissed Rosetti before everyone's eyes. The wedding guests all rose to their feet, offering the newlyweds thunderous applause and their most sincere blessings.

Count Austin stepped forward and embraced his son, repeatedly patting Arnold's shoulder and speaking earnestly — seemingly offering words of encouragement.

Arnold's younger sister Jenna stood quietly beside Rosetti, uncharacteristically not causing any trouble. She knew this day held great significance for her elder brother; it was a day worth commemorating.

Merlin clapped along numbly, feeling the pacing was a bit fast. He completely couldn't understand how these two had inexplicably gotten married. Just what had happened in the three years he wasn't here?

Until yesterday, Merlin knew nothing about Arnold marrying Rosetti. It wasn't until Arnold's sister Jenna came running over with an invitation that he learned the lord's foolish son was getting married!

"What exactly is going on here? Alice—"

"What do you mean what's going on? Arnold and Rosetti are lovers who finally became a couple. Is there a problem?" Alice retorted in puzzlement beside him.

"How did those two end up together? I feel like a patient who just woke up, completely clueless about everything that happened over the past three years." Merlin's head was a mess.

"Rosetti liked Arnold all along. It's just that her excessive enthusiasm scared Arnold off. As long as Arnold was willing to get to know Rosetti a little, he'd realize she's a good girl. Their marriage isn't surprising at all." Alice answered in a low voice, thinking Merlin didn't seem to understand anyone in the guild deeply except Hobbs.

"So that's how it is." Merlin nodded, recalling he'd heard some rumors about Arnold and Rosetti, but never expected the two would actually end up together. "Alice, let me ask you something."

"What is it?" Alice looked at Merlin in surprise.

"Seeing your former pursuer marry someone else — how do you feel right now?" Merlin asked with ill intent.

"Hah." Alice gave a dry laugh, wanting to tease Merlin. "What do you think I feel?"

"How would I know?" Merlin spread his hands.

"Sigh, I regret rejecting Arnold back then." Alice feigned a serious expression.

"No way? Do you have some dissatisfaction with me?" Merlin clutched his chest, feeling an indescribable discomfort.

Alice burst out laughing, then answered seriously, "I was joking. Seeing them get married, I genuinely feel happy from the bottom of my heart.

After all, the one marrying Arnold isn't me — it's Rosetti."

"Is that so?" Merlin scratched his head, hesitantly asking, "You said you rejected Arnold back then... you didn't do it for me, did you? After all, my... you know~"

"Tch!" Alice shot Merlin a fierce glare, saying discontentedly, "What nonsense are you spouting? I never had feelings for Arnold to begin with. When I rejected him, you weren't even in Rexham yet. Besides, back then you were the world's number one scumbag in my eyes — I hated you to death."

Merlin felt a few black lines slide down his forehead. He said awkwardly, "Come on, it's not that bad. I didn't do anything to you, did I?"

"Shut up. Just thinking about it makes me angry all over. I still can't figure out why I got targeted by a scumbag like you in the first place?" Alice grumbled inwardly, unable to understand why she'd become entangled with Merlin, unable to cut ties since that Demon Lord Palace crusade.

"Maybe that's because you're rather special?" Merlin answered after some thought.

"Special?" Alice's face flushed slightly as she probed, "Wh-where am I special?"

"It's not easy to say." Merlin hesitated.

"What do you mean? Just say it. What can't be said?" Alice stared straight into Merlin's eyes, pressing him.

"If I say it, you can't get angry."

"I'm not that kind of person."

"The flatness of your chest is something I've rarely seen in my life, so you're very special."

"Hmph!" Alice's blood instantly rushed to her head. She grabbed Merlin by the collar, looking like she wanted to give his eye socket a punch.

"Stop! Didn't you promise not to get angry?" Merlin glared at Alice righteously.

"You—! Hmph!" Alice let go of Merlin, seething silently.

"Don't take it seriously. Actually, I—" Merlin paused, then sneakily wrapped his arm around Alice's waist and whispered, "The first time I saw you, I felt a sense of familiarity. I kept feeling like we'd met somewhere before."

"Impossible. We couldn't have met before." Alice glanced at Merlin, thinking this guy was spouting smooth talk again.

"Not necessarily. Maybe we met in a past life, and maybe we were even lovers. That's why I think you're special." Merlin waggled his eyebrows.

"Lovers in a past life?" Alice's eyes grew flustered. She lightly poked Merlin with her arm, her face flushing red as she said irritably—

"You'll say anything that sounds nice, you smooth-talking big liar. I won't believe your ghost stories, hmph~!"

title: Chapter 60 — Friend
content:
Chapter 60 — Friend

Volume 37 · Chapter 60

Everyone stood up and applauded, offering their blessings to the newlyweds. Unfortunately, Chris was too short, and even on tiptoes she couldn't see, her anxious little face breaking out in sweat.

Alice, seeing this, picked Chris up from the ground. This was the little one's first time witnessing a wedding scene; to her, everything was full of novelty.

"Mama, what is Aunt Rosetti wearing? It looks so pretty~" Chris asked in a childish voice, quite interested in Rosetti's formal attire.

"That," Alice smiled, looking down to answer her daughter, "that's a wedding dress, something everyone wears when they get married. Maybe you'll have the chance to wear one in the future."

"A thing for weddings?" The little one sucked on her finger and asked puzzledly, "Then did Mama ever wear one?"

Alice hesitated before responding, "Not yet."

"What a pity. Mama must look wonderful in a wedding dress~" Little Chris said very seriously, unable to stop herself from imagining how her mother would look in one.

"Very lovely, do you think?" Alice looked up at Rosetti on the stage, a trace of envy showing in her eyes. "Maybe so."

Merlin suddenly paused, glanced at the newlyweds on stage, and said softly, "Alice, how about we also have a wedding?"

"Huh!? " Alice froze, then replied hesitantly, "Don't you think that's unnecessary?"

"Won't you feel regretful?" Merlin asked, somewhat uncertain.

"We haven't exactly just gotten together. In our friends' eyes, we've already been married for several years. A wedding might not really suit us." Alice shook her head.

Merlin was about to say something but stopped, thinking that from other people's perspective, he and Alice already seemed like an old married couple, and a wedding did seem rather superfluous.

But seeing how envious Alice looked of Rosetti's wedding dress, Merlin felt his sense of responsibility as a husband stirring—he really wanted to fulfill her wish.

"Marriage does need a bit of ritual, but isn't that not the most important thing?" Alice asked with a smile.

"Alice..." Merlin paused and had to nod. "You're right. Maybe we no longer need a wedding to witness each other's feelings. After all, enduring affection is the best confession. Actually, in my heart, a real wedding doesn't look like this."

"Doesn't look like this? Then what is a real wedding?" Alice asked curiously.

"It should be that even until the last moment of my life, I am still by your side. That is a real wedding. It's not just a ceremony—it's a vow that both people truly believe in." Merlin looked at Alice and said slowly, "As long as two people who love each other are together, then every day is a grand and magnificent wedding."

"Hmm..." Alice's cheeks flushed slightly, unsure of how to respond. Normally, those words would be extremely cheesy, but at the moment, they carried a different flavor.

"However..." Merlin's face showed a knowing smile as he deliberately teased Alice's curiosity.

"However what? Don't leave me hanging like that." Alice glared at Merlin discontentedly.

"Even if you never wear a wedding dress, I can still imagine how stunning you'd look in one~" Merlin's gaze drifted toward the distant Rosetti. Without a doubt, Rosetti was the most beautiful person here today, but that could in no way shake Alice's place in his heart.

"You..." Alice's cheeks turned crimson, her heart a mess from Merlin's words. "You're being extra cheesy today."

"Well? Were you moved?" Merlin asked, eyes bright and animated.

"No, I was actually grossed out." Alice frowned and answered.

"Pfft! Then I won't say it anymore. How boring~" Merlin sighed, greatly disappointed.

"I-I didn't mean that!" Alice tugged at Merlin's clothes and glared at him angrily. "Occasionally... occasionally saying stuff like that is fine."

Little Chris's ahoge wobbled back and forth. She had no idea what her parents were squabbling about—

Not in the slightest. The adult world is incomprehensible.

After the wedding ceremony concluded, everyone gathered on the lawn outside the church for a meal. The air was filled with the aroma of roasted meat and fine wine.

"Arnold, Rosetti, blessings to you both."

Merlin raised his glass, gently clinking it against theirs, and offered his congratulations—though who knew whether a Demon Lord's blessing would have the opposite effect.

Arnold and Rosetti both wore happy smiles on their faces. In the past, Merlin would often make somewhat improper jokes with Arnold, but not today. Merlin set aside his usual carefree attitude—after all, Arnold was the protagonist of the day and deserved to be taken seriously.

"Merlin, you actually managed to make it back? I thought you wouldn't be able to attend my wedding." Arnold was very happy to see Merlin. They hadn't seen each other in three years, but it seemed this guy hadn't changed at all.

"How could I not show up for a friend's wedding? I specially rushed back for you." Merlin told a white lie; he couldn't exactly admit he'd only just found out about the wedding a few days ago.

"Really? You don't happen to have just returned to Letheram recently, do you?" Arnold asked, his face full of suspicion.

"What are you talking about. Given our friendship, would I lie to you?" Merlin asked sternly in return.

"I see, my mistake, haha~" Arnold laughed foolishly, feeling that Merlin was already being a very good friend by willing to rush back for his wedding.

"By the way, Merlin, you and Alice haven't had a proper wedding, right? When do you plan to get officially married?" Rosetti asked in a teasing tone.

"What do you mean 'officially married'? We already got married ages ago." Alice paused, then said proudly, "Compared to you two who've only been married for a few years, we're far ahead of you."

"Exactly!" Merlin immediately wrapped his arm around Alice and answered earnestly, "We're already an old married couple."

"Hmm? I see." Rosetti's smile held deep meaning. She knew more or less what was going on—it seemed Merlin and Alice had already gone from a fake relationship to something real and had acknowledged each other.

"I knew it. You two were definitely already involved long ago." Arnold's expression turned weird.

"Your wording is really unpleasant." Merlin frowned. What did he mean by 'involved'? It wasn't like that at all.

"Then we won't disturb you any longer. We have quite a few things to attend to." Rosetti nodded slightly in greeting and pulled Arnold away to greet other guests.

After the two left, Merlin let out a breath of relief. Before he could fully relax, someone draped an arm around his shoulder, and the strong smell of alcohol hit his face.

Hobbs had spotted Merlin and enthusiastically approached, wanting to have a proper chat with his old friend and catch up about everything that had happened over the past three years.

"Merlin, you damn guy, you actually came back?! Come, come, come, let me give you a kiss! Do you have any idea how much I missed you?"

"No no no, cut it out." Merlin looked at Hobbs' scruffy, beard-framed lips and refused with full dread—

"Hobbs, you damn—"

"You creepy old pervert."

title: Chapter 61 — Regular Customers
content:
Chapter 61 — Regular Customers

Volume 37 · Chapter 61

“We should drink well today, to make up for what we've owed over these three years.” Hobbes said, beaming. “Good, you guy.” Merlin pushed Hobbes aside, glanced at him, “You haven't changed at all?” “What could change? I'm just idling away in the Adventurers Guild every day.” Hobbes gave a self-deprecating laugh. Alice stood aside silently, thinking that in the Adventurers Guild, probably only Hobbes and Merlin had a close relationship, after all they were always hanging out together. “Mini sister~” Little Chris saw her playmate, happily waved her hand, eager to show off her new pet. Mini was still a bit shy, always hiding behind Hobbes, peeking with her little head to size up Chris's parents, thinking there wouldn't be any familiar kids here, but didn't expect Chris to be here as well. Merlin looked at Mini, noticing the girl had grown a lot; calculating the time, she must be seven or eight now, looking much more mature, losing some childishness, he said, “Hobbes, your daughter is already this big?” “Of course, kids grow fast; you haven't been back for three years, so you're surprised.” Hobbes said in a teasing tone. Merlin gave an awkward laugh, thinking his own daughter was indeed a bit embarrassing; all her friends had grown up while she was still in the toddler stage? “Chris doesn't seem to have grown much either; looks like nutrition isn't keeping up, you should pay attention.” Hobbes glanced at Chris, his drunken eyes somewhat unfocused. “Well... my daughter will grow up sooner or later.” Merlin gave a vague answer, not wanting to explain further, he slowly squatted down, “Mini, do you still remember me?” Mini shrank back behind Hobbes and whispered in a tiny voice, “Uncle Merlin.” Merlin laughed heartedly, happy inside; although he hadn't returned for three years, Mini still remembered him. “Captain? What captain?” Hobbes asked, puzzled. “Never mind, haha.” Merlin gave an embarrassed smile, thinking his past as a melon squad captain should be forgotten; as Mini grows up, she'll realize it was just a game kids played. “Dad, I want to go play with Chris.” Mini asked softly. “Go on, go on.” Hobbes nodded. So the two little ones took the husky Avis and went off to play away from the adults. Chris couldn't resist showing off her dog, even riding on Avis, demonstrating the pet's various uses. Although Mini had grown quite a bit, like Chris she had a strong interest in small animals, and they had a lot in common. Just as the kids left, a call came from not far away; Lukiya was seen walking slowly, holding her grandfather's arm. “Mr. Merlin, when did you come back?” “A few days ago, maybe.” Merlin scratched his head, thinking that at Arnold's wedding, everyone was familiar. “You finally came back, abandoning Alice and her mother and disappearing for three years—you're really an irresponsible scumbag!” Lukiya said without hesitation, directly blaming Merlin. Alice laughed beside him, turning her head away, thinking that what Merlin had done, in many friends' eyes, was already equivalent to being a jerk. Seeing Alice not helping him out, Merlin forced himself to say, “I didn't do it on purpose; because of various things, I couldn't come back.” “What could you possibly be busy with? Even being busy can't compare to your platinum-ranked adventurer wife?” Lukiya said with a scornful look, thinking a bronze-ranked adventurer normally has nothing to do, where would there be any busyness? Merlin was at a loss for words; what had happened to him was indeed hard to explain. “Alright, Lukiya, don't give Merlin a hard time—he's back, isn't he?” Elder Taylor, the Adventurers Guild president, hurriedly stopped his granddaughter, looked at Merlin, and said, “I heard from Alice that your family had some trouble; is it all resolved now?” “Yeah, it's all over. Now I...” Merlin looked at Alice beside him, smiling, “I need to spend more time with Alice to make up for my mistake.” “That's good; the Adventurers Guild really needs you.” Elder Taylor was tactful, not pressing Merlin further, just leaving it at that; regardless, it's good that Merlin can return to Rexheim. “You still have a bit of conscience, do you know how hard it is for Alice to raise a child alone?” Lukiya spoke up for Alice, feeling indignant. Seeing this, Hobbes thought that given Lukiya and Alice's usual relationship, they would surely blast Merlin for his three-year absence, so he spoke up for his lady friend to vent her frustration. So Hobbes hurriedly patted Merlin's shoulder, smiling, to help him out, saying to everyone: “Merlin and I haven't seen each other in a while; you guys keep chatting, we're going to find Price for a few drinks~” “Yeah, yeah, let's go have a few drinks.” As soon as the words fell, Merlin and Hobbes quickly slipped away, leaving the crowd with bewildered expressions. “These two irresponsible guys, getting together surely means no good.” Lukiya said with a suspicious face, full of resentment, “Alice, you'd better keep an eye on Merlin and not give him a nice look.” “It's fine, we're already fine.” Alice said with a bashful face; now she's satisfied with Merlin, so there's no resentment. “Good grief!” Lukiya covered her forehead, her eyes showing a bit of sympathy— “It's over, you've been brainwashed by Merlin's honeyed words.” Having avoided Lukiya's criticism, Merlin let out a breath, wiped the sweat from his forehead, “Phew, thanks, thanks, Hobbes, you get me~” “Of course, Lukiya just loves to stick up for the underdog, especially against guys like you who are irresponsible, full of malice.” Hobbes said with a wicked grin. “Tch! Who's the irresponsible guy? Not me, I didn't do anything.” Merlin rolled his eyes. “Merlin brother!?” The Rexheim guard captain Price, seeing Merlin, felt happy inside; “We haven't seen each other in ages; today we definitely must not stop until drunk! Without you, my drinks with Hobbes have lost much flavor.” “Long time no see, Price.” Merlin still had a deep impression of this guard captain, although he's not exactly proper and tends to be timid when things happen, but his nature is not bad. “It's a shame; if Helena's secret cottage were still around, we could go find some fun tonight.” Hobbes said regretfully. “Yeah, Helena inexplicably closed her shop; now we don't know where she went, nor if she's forgotten us old regulars.” Price recalled the king, really missing those (demon) girls. “Forget about the secret cottage.” Merlin's mouth twitched wildly; he couldn't believe three years have passed and this bunch of old reprobates still can't stop thinking about Helena. Helena now stays in Demon City, guarding beside Asmodeus, focusing on handling Demon City's affairs. Who has the time to think about these two old guys, Hobbes and Price?

title: Chapter 62 — Towering Above All Beings
content:
Chapter 62 — Towering Above All Beings

Volume 37 · Chapter 62

At the wedding, Captain Dennis held a glass of champagne and looked around, finding no familiar faces, and felt a moment of awkwardness.

Since this was the wedding of Count Austin's son, Captain Dennis had come on behalf of Duke Powei, bringing gifts and blessings from the Rose Family.

Captain Dennis slowly turned around, deciding to pass along a few words from Grand Duke Rose before leaving the wedding venue. But then, he happened to spot Merlin drinking with two older men not far away, and his heart lightened. He walked over, wanting to chat with Merlin.

"Mr. Merlin, I didn't expect to see you here. It's been such a long time."

"Hmm?" Merlin glanced over and smiled. "Oh, it's you, Captain Dennis? Come, come, have a drink with us."

"Haha, I never expected Mr. Merlin to still be so approachable. No change at all after all these years," Captain Dennis said with a sigh.

"Hey, you flatter me," Merlin shook his head. If he had any airs, how would he be mixing with this bunch of humans?

"Captain Dennis? That name sounds familiar." Price furrowed his brow, searching his memories.

"Can't be wrong. It's that person from the Powei family, the first one to return alive from the mysterious chaotic seas. It caused quite a stir at the time." Hobbs had a good memory and remembered the incident.

"So you already know about them?" Merlin thought for a moment and politely helped introduce. "Captain Dennis, these two are Price and Hobbs, my drinking buddies."

"Nice to meet you." Captain Dennis took off his hat and bowed slightly, then continued. "No need to speak of the past anymore. The fact that I survived that desperate situation was thanks to Mr. Merlin's help."

"What? Wait, no way. Merlin, you had that kind of ability?" Price was utterly confused. In his eyes, Merlin was just a freeloader clinging to his wife's coat tails, not much better than himself.

"I see. Merlin, you've made me look at you in a new light," Hobbs said with a drunken smile.

"Let's not dwell on that, it's boring." Merlin waved his hand. He had already forgotten about such a minor favor. "How did you end up here, Captain Dennis?"

"I came representing the Rose Family. The Duke has been extremely busy lately and couldn't attend Count Austin's son's wedding in person," Captain Dennis said helplessly.

"Oh~" Merlin nodded, suddenly remembering two familiar people. "How are Cecilia and Kael? Are they doing well?"

"All is well. Miss Cecilia has grown a great deal and often accompanies the Duke to handle various matters. She's already a capable successor who can stand on her own." Captain Dennis lowered his head and smiled as he added, "As for Kael, he may become the Rose Family's son-in-law in the future. The Duke favors him greatly, and I see indications of that sort of intention."

"???" Merlin was startled and looked up in astonishment. "What!? Cecilia and Kael...?"

"Yes, I believe it would be a fine match for Miss Cecilia to wed a loyal knight. Perhaps the Duke thinks the same," Captain Dennis said quietly.

"Has it come to mating season for the sows again? Everyone's going into heat all of a sudden," Merlin muttered.

"Uh, Mr. Merlin, that's rather harsh phrasing. Miss Cecilia and Kael grew up together and know each other well. I think it would be far better for her to marry Kael than some frivolous noble scion," Captain Dennis emphasized.

"You have a point. I always suspected those two had something going on. As expected~" Merlin offered silent blessings for the pair in his heart, then changed the subject and asked, "How have you been lately?"

"I'm the same as ever, but..." Captain Dennis hesitated, then lowered his voice. "But the black box you gave me was stolen recently."

"The black box?" Merlin frowned, momentarily unable to recall.

"That unopenable thing you brought back from the chaotic seas." Captain Dennis reminded him.

"Oh!" Merlin's brows relaxed, then he asked in puzzlement. "That thing couldn't even be opened by me. At best it's an old antique. Who would go out of their way to steal something so unremarkable?"

Captain Dennis looked hesitant, unsure whether he should tell Merlin about this. After a moment of silence, he spoke. "Half a month ago, a mysterious thief broke into my home and stole that black box. I searched for a long time with my men, and finally found it in the wilderness. But the box had already been opened, completely empty inside, and the thief was dead as well, his body torn apart, as if attacked by a beast."

"Hmm?" Merlin raised his eyebrows. Captain Dennis's words caught his attention. The thief was able to open that black box, and his death might be connected to it?

The most puzzling part was... "Captain Dennis paused and said in a deep voice, "that thief was not human."

"Not human?" Merlin grew increasingly confused, sensing this matter was probably more complicated than it appeared.

"Correct. It was a creature I had never seen before. Its internal organs were entirely different from humans. Anyway, it was very strange," Captain Dennis recalled.

"Could it be an alien race?" Merlin guessed.

"Impossible. I've traveled north and south for so many years; what alien races haven't I seen? But that thief, I had truly never heard of. Even in death, its body possessed some bizarre ability. Upon contact, it continuously drained my strength." Captain Dennis answered with certainty.

"Continuously draining strength?"

Merlin bowed his head and thought. Such a unique ability—he had indeed encountered it before, in those chaotic creatures he had once faced! Moreover, that black box also came from the place where chaotic creatures gathered. There might be some connection!

"Did you keep the thief's corpse?"

"Of course. Due to how bizarre it was, I had the corpse properly preserved." Captain Dennis answered truthfully.

Merlin nodded. Captain Dennis's home was in Wales, not far from Wrexham. It was entirely feasible to go take a look—

"Captain Dennis, why not stay a few days in Wrexham? I can help you investigate this matter."

******

Vast desert, within the pitch-black obelisk.

A spiral staircase led straight to the tower's peak, with thick stacks of books everywhere.

Rather than calling this the Dark Guild's den, it was more like a magical library.

In the center sat a massive alchemy furnace, the very one Bartoli had once made for Flamel.

It was filled with all sorts of strange materials—ores, poisonous insects, herbs—all soaking in viscous blood.

To craft the true Philosopher's Stone, this furnace contained the blood of every type of mortal creature, burning fiercely alongside the other materials.

Blindfolded Lorig stood there, broom in hand, dutifully working as the cleanup crew, sweeping dust throughout the obelisk while keeping a constant watch on the alchemy furnace.

In order to help his father, the Red Beard Pirate, take vengeance, Lorig had chosen to join Phoenix and become one of their members, placing his hopes upon that overwhelmingly powerful guild master.

Lorig stopped cleaning, looked up toward the top of the obelisk, and silently tightened his grip on the broom, a spark of hope kindling within his heart.

That man, who was nearly divine—would he be able to defeat Lucifer III?

After all, someone capable of subjugating so many terrifying beings to serve him must have already become an existence that transcended all living creatures.

title: Chapter 63 — The Eerie Guild
content:
Chapter 63 — The Eerie Guild

Volume 37 · Chapter 63

The son of this pirate learned the true identity of his father's killer from an information dealer known as "Old Huo". It was none other than the Demon Lord he had once seen, Lucifer III. After learning the truth, Luoqili felt unable to accept it; facing immense pressure, he repeatedly wondered—could he possibly be unable to help his father take revenge? After all, a terrifying monster like a Demon Lord was not something he could handle. Even with the Medusa's Eye, Luoqili had no confidence at all; he had already suffered a great loss against Mammon. Unwilling to accept defeat, Luoqili could only seek help from others, fixing his goal on the remaining dark guild, "Phoenix". Moreover, Luoqili himself had prior contact with Phoenix, having interacted with the orc king Sarret, making it easy to connect with them. Hearing that Phoenix's mysterious chairman possessed near-divine power, perhaps capable of defeating that young Demon Lord, Luoqili abandoned his pirate crew, devoted all his wealth to Phoenix, and successfully joined. However, Phoenix is the strongest dark guild; it could never accept someone as weak as Luoqili, whose strength didn't even meet the threshold for membership, and the guild never welcomes the weak. Thus Luoqili appeared to be a member of Phoenix, yet he was merely a fringe figure, only able to barely serve as Flamel's assistant while occasionally sweeping the obelisk. Luoqili seemed honest on the surface, but inside he was deeply resentful, desiring to enter Phoenix's core and shed his fringe status there. He very much wanted to meet that mysterious chairman, to perform well in front of him and perhaps gain a chance to participate in various important meetings.

At that moment, Heshi and Sarret returned from outside. Luoqili hastily put aside his thoughts and put on a smile. "Lady Heshi, Lord Sarret, welcome back. I don't know how the matter went." "Hmph, that's not something you should ask, human." Sarret snorted coldly; deep down he still resented Luoqili, this ambitious person, entering Phoenix, but since the chairman agreed, he could do nothing. Luoqili gave an embarrassed smile, not daring to retort Sarret; here he had no status, and dared not bring up the unpleasant past with Sarret. "Is it only you here? Where did everyone else go?" Heshi frowned, asking. "I'm not quite sure either." Luoqili answered embarrassedly; anyone here could be casually pulled out and he couldn't afford to offend them, so he dared not ask what they were doing. "Tch! Useless thing, what's the use of you joining Phoenix? I really don't know what the chairman is thinking; surely there's something wrong with his head." Heshi said displeased. "His head is full of using us to get revenge for his father, unaware of how foolish his father really is—just a lowly pirate." Sarret bluntly evaluated. Luoqili's face instantly darkened; he silently clenched his fists, veins bulging all over, unable to tolerate others insulting his father, yet now he could do nothing; here anyone could order him around.

"You're back? How did it go? Have you already gotten the eyes of the Otherworld King?" Flamel slowly descended from the spiral staircase, gently closed the book in his hand, and smiled at Heshi and Sarret as he watched them. "Nonsense, I went out—what could possibly fail to get done? Are you doubting my power?" Heshi glared at Flamel. "You misunderstand; after all, your opponent is the Otherworld King." Flamel showed no fear of Heshi, even though she was one of the three top figures in the guild, yet he was irreplaceable—without him, who could produce the Philosopher's Stone? "You and Sarret are the same, just frogs in a well; I've already wiped out the Otherworld, so next time don't bother me with this—it's boring." Heshi finished speaking, then pulled the enormous eyeball of the Otherworld King from her spatial ring, saying, "Come on, don't you want to inspect the goods?" Flamel glanced at it a few times and knew it was genuine; it seemed the Otherworld King really had been slain by Heshi. "No need, as a noble dark dragon, how could I deceive anyone?" "You little brat know how to talk." Heshi paused, then continued, "Since I've already brought back the Otherworld King's eye, is the Philosopher's Stone now only missing the final ingredient?" "Exactly, we still need four Awakening Magic Rings; they are the keys to unlocking truth, but we need to discuss this properly." Flamel was only one step away from fulfilling his wish—"Meeting tonight, don't be late."

Deep in the night, atop the dark tower, all members of Phoenix had gathered, sitting cross-legged before a cluster of flames. Although Phoenix is the strongest dark guild, it differs in that its members are few. Excluding fringe individuals like Luoqili, there were only nine in total. But these nine "people" should not be underestimated; each had considerable background, and if placed outside they would be formidable powers capable of shaking a region. Besides the genius alchemist Flamel, the dark dragon Heshi, and the benevolent king Sarret, there were also— the fourth knight of the Thorns who fled Britain, a necromancer, Solorok; once a purple‑gold adventurer who spread plague and ruined the four northern nations, a criminal, Hippocrates; a candidate for the Wrath Demon Lord, who lost the struggle for the Demon Lord throne to his brother, Samuel's younger brother, Alam; the fifth apostle from Hell, who in life had personally founded the most terrifying assassination organization and was also the teacher of the former kingdom's dragon‑riding thief, Hassan Sabbah; and another, a relatively young boy with a warm, gentle smile, sitting among the fearsome crowd, appearing out of place. One could hardly believe that such a seemingly kind, pure‑innocent boy was also a member of the dark guild. His name was Erikson; he possessed a unique telepathic ability, allowing him to speak directly into another's mind. Even when facing realms beyond the mortal world—such as the Otherworld, Hell, or Heaven—Erikson could still establish contact. This was Erikson's unique ability: unrestricted by time or place, able to communicate with all things; though it seemed of little use, it was the core of Phoenix. Because among those present, only Erikson could contact the mysterious chairman, relaying the chairman's intentions to everyone. Lastly, naturally, was that mysterious chairman Phoenix himself—present, though no one had seen his true face, only knowing his power was terrifyingly immense, as he watched everyone from the darkness. Among them, the dark dragon Heshi, the Wrath Demon Lord Alam, and the Hell relic apostle Hassan Sabbah were the three top figures of the guild, their strength and influence far surpassing the others.

The harmless boy Erikson slowly opened his eyes, fixed his gaze on the burning flames before him, and softly said— "Everyone, the chairman has already issued the next instruction."

title: Chapter 64 — Mysterious President (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 64 — Mysterious President (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 37 · Chapter 64

Erikson's words had barely faded when everyone's gaze converged upon him, leaving the young man feeling awkward.

Obviously, even though he was a member of the Dark Guild, he couldn't adapt to this place, especially not with this bunch of ruthless individuals.

However, Erikson simply thought these people weren't bad; they were just extremely extreme in their ways.

Everyone shared a common goal: to create the Philosopher's Stone and use the "Wishing Machine" to fulfill their desires.

Indeed, the Wishing Machine represented the three goddesses of fate in alchemy: the past, present, and future.

These goddesses were not ancient deities; they existed even when the world was in chaos. They had no thoughts, only weaving the fate of every individual, embodying the will of the world.

They could also grant wishes, with the Philosopher's Stone serving as the key, akin to a coin for the Wishing Machine—a single coin could only fulfill one wish, and wishes already granted by others could not be repeated.

This was to maintain the balance and stability of the world, as many things were unique and could not be duplicated.

However, using the Philosopher's Stone to make a wish was not the only method; one could also make a wish to the three goddesses at the cost of their life, ensuring the wisher's demise.

Those who made a wish to the three goddesses and survived, regardless of the method, would forge a divine seal, the only way to obtain one.

With a divine seal, one would achieve the status of a prime deity, equal to figures like Odin, Satan, and Mary, and gain incomparable rule power, becoming a participant in the construction of the world.

That's why Phoenix, who was determined to obtain the Philosopher's Stone and make a wish to change the world, could also become a prime deity, making no one able to resist such temptation.

"Did he say something?" Hecate asked curiously, eager to know what Phoenix's command was.

"Next, we must find the Four Apocalypse Rings to create the Philosopher's Stone, and everyone in the guild must take action," Erikson relayed Phoenix's words.

"Everyone must take action?" Sarret hesitated before continuing, "That's fine, who knows where the Apocalypse Rings are? We're short-handed."

"Short-handed?" Solroch, the fourth knight of the thorn, raised his head and whispered, "I can send my undead to search."

"With just a few skeletons of yours, you'll be cleaned up by the Holy Church people before you even leave the Great Desert," Hassan Sabbah mocked from the side. Once a human, he became a demon after becoming a herald of Hell, naturally having no good opinion of Solroch, a mage who manipulated the undead.

"Hassan, do you have any suggestions? As a demon's pawn, you're not one of us," Solroch narrowed his eyes.

"Little demon, speak to me politely, and I can kill you anytime," Hassan Sabbah responded in a low tone.

In truth, most of the people present had their own ambitions, hoping to use the Philosopher's Stone to fulfill their own desires.

For example:

Hassan Sabbah, who had submitted to Satan to become a herald of Hell, was not satisfied and wanted to use the Philosopher's Stone to break free from his undead identity and truly live again.

Hecate also had great ambitions, not for the evolution of the world, but to forge a divine seal and become a greater existence than the ancient dragon Nidhogg.

Flamel was not interested in the "Wishing Machine" but was fascinated by the essence of alchemy, wanting to create the Philosopher's Stone and reduce the three goddesses of alchemy.

Alram, who had not obtained the Demon Lord's position, was resentful and wanted to become the strongest demon, then defeat his brother Samiel and return to the demon race.

Solroch's ambition was even more terrifying; he sought the truth of death and wanted to become a new Hell lord, like Satan, which could only be achieved by the three goddesses.

Hippocrates was more straightforward and had no great ambitions, simply joining the Dark Guild to escape the constraints and enjoy the pleasure of killing, which made him very satisfied, a madman with a disease.

Looking at them, it seemed only the straightforward orc king Sarret and the young Erikson were loyal and fully supported Phoenix's ideal of a completely equal new world.

Most members had their own ambitions and naturally scoffed at Phoenix's ideal, even mocking the leader in their hearts as a fool, too naive, and such a utopia was impossible.

These people could gather together only because of the "Wishing Machine," which was what they wanted to pursue; otherwise, Phoenix would have disbanded long ago.

"I'm fed up," Alram raised his head, his demon horns glowing red in the firelight, "Everything has to go through Erikson, why can't the leader appear in person and talk to us?"

"That might be because the leader has his own reasons and has to hide, but he is always watching us, and we can hear everything he says," Erikson explained.

"Nonsense!" Alram stood up, his temper as fiery as his brother Samiel's, and scolded, "Since joining Phoenix, I have never seen the leader's true face, and we are all sitting here like madmen, as if we are obeying a non-existent leader!"

"Well," Erikson showed an awkward smile, unsure how to respond.

Everyone fell silent, looking at the young Erikson, not just Alram, but everyone in the room had the same question in their minds, which Alram had just expressed.

Phoenix often held meetings, with everyone sitting around the campfire, listening to Erikson relay the leader's words, wondering where the leader was hiding.

Staying up all night here, sitting in a circle, wasn't it like an eccentric cult ritual? Alram's outburst was understandable.

"Erikson, today the leader must appear, we have had enough of you playing games here," Alram showed a grotesque face.

"That's right, the leader should come out in person and talk about this, we joined the guild to obey him, shouldn't he show his face and see us?" Solroch said seriously.

"Don't be so suspicious, what I say is true, the leader can see us and hear us," Erikson was desperate, feeling overwhelmed by the situation, and his position in the guild might not even be as good as that of Lochi.

Suddenly, the campfire in front of them rose, a power not inferior to the divine realm filled the room, making everyone's faces pale and gasping for air.

This powerful aura was stronger than anyone present, and even if they all joined forces, they might not be able to resist it.

Erikson helplessly spread his hands, scanning everyone with his eyes, speaking in an innocent tone—

"See for yourselves, what did I say?

"The leader is everywhere, always watching us."

"Your recent actions have angered him, and he might bring down punishment."

"The leader's methods are well-known; his anger, no one can withstand."

More and more!

Actually, I also feel guilty, everyone came here, and a single update feels a bit guilty.

title: Chapter 65 — Divergence
content:
Chapter 65 — Divergence

Volume 37 · Chapter 65

The room fell silent, everyone lowering their heads. No one dared to stand up and question the Guildmaster’s authority again—no one wanted to face his wrath.

Alam, who had just been fuming with rage, slowly sat down and fell silent, beads of cold sweat trickling down his forehead. That mysterious pressure was far stronger than anything his brother, Samiel, could muster.

Alam’s doubts grew. The Guildmaster, Phoenix, was likely no human—more like an existence from a higher plane. Otherwise, how could he be so enigmatic, never even appearing in person?

“Let’s just forget what happened earlier, shall we?”

“I didn’t mean anything by it either. It was all Alam’s fault for stirring things up.” Hassan al-Sabah didn’t hesitate to throw Alam under the bus.

“Yeah, I had nothing to do with it either.” Solrock quickly distanced himself as well.

“Tsk! You two bastards!” Alam’s face twitched with rage, the muscles in his cheeks jumping violently.

“Forget it. The Guildmaster just issued a warning—no need to dwell on it.” Erikson spoke calmly, making it clear the Guildmaster had no intention of holding anyone accountable.

The tension in the room eased slightly. To break the awkwardness, Hecate stepped forward to shift the topic:

“So, about the discussion earlier—are we really supposed to mobilize everyone to find the Four Apocalypse Rings?”

“Yes, that’s the Guildmaster’s intention.” Erikson paused, his tone serious. “This time, every member of the Guild must act. We need to ensure we retrieve all four rings successfully.”

“But we don’t even know where these rings are! Finding them could take years—maybe even decades. Doesn’t the Guildmaster have any clues to guide us?” Sarret asked, suspicious that the Guildmaster would order a full mobilization without any leads.

“Of course. The Guildmaster is omniscient and has already prepared everything. He already knows the locations of the Four Apocalypse Rings.” Erikson nodded with a smile.

“Oh? What exactly does the Guildmaster know?” Hassan al-Sabah couldn’t resist pressing further.

“The Four Apocalypse Rings represent Death, Plague, Famine, and War. Each is in the possession of different individuals, and retrieving them won’t be easy—it’ll take some effort.”

Erikson crouched slightly, then slowly revealed the locations of the rings:

“The Death Ring is in the hands of a knight named Katherine from the British Kingdom. She’s not particularly strong, but she’s backed by the kingdom itself—taking it from her might mean going to war with them.”

At the mention of Katherine’s name, Solrock—once a traitorous knight of the British Kingdom’s Thorn Order—felt an unexpected familiarity. He never expected to hear this old friend’s name again, especially as a target.

Solrock had no fondness for the British Kingdom. He had once tried to kill the queen and seize the throne for himself, but failed. Still, he harbored some lingering affection for his former comrades, despite their naivety and weakness. After all, they had shared the same pot of food, the same training grounds, and the same fate as orphans chosen for the Thorn Order.

Even Solrock, a merciless knight, couldn’t help but feel a flicker of nostalgia when recalling those training days with his brothers-in-arms. It was the only soft spot in his heart.

He lowered his head, not wanting anyone to see his thoughts. A pang of pity rose for Katherine—if only she would surrender the Death Ring willingly, everything would be so much simpler.

“The Plague Ring is currently with a rogue knight named Des. He murdered his master, the Holy Roman Emperor, and fled to his homeland. This man won’t be hard to deal with—he has no allies.”

Hippocrates, cloaked in black, lifted his head. His sealed crow mask made him look even more unsettling. He wasn’t interested in Des—only in the Plague Ring.

Once a top-tier adventurer, Hippocrates had always specialized in plague magic, chasing the destructive power of disease and counting deaths as his achievements.

He had never been welcome among his peers, who feared both the plague and the unpredictable nature of his magic. Even Hippocrates struggled to control it, often causing mass casualties by accident. He was constantly suppressing his own power, which was why he had joined the Dark Guild in the first place—he couldn’t stand the constraints of rules.

Hearing about the Plague Ring, Hippocrates was eager to witness the divine artifact’s plague energy. Maybe he could learn something to refine his own magic further.

“The Famine Ring is far more difficult to obtain. It’s hidden in the elven secret realm of the Southern Union, worn on the skeleton of the elven god, Corillon. It’s what keeps the continent from being swallowed by the abyss beneath the deep sea. Taking it won’t just mean facing the elves or Corillon’s lingering spirit—it’ll mean war with the entire Southern Union. If we remove the Famine Ring, the continent will lose its support and be consumed by the sea, leading to their complete annihilation.”

Hecate and Sarret raised their heads in shock. The Southern Union was their homeland. Knowing it was doomed, they couldn’t help but feel the weight of it.

Hecate frowned, struggling with the decision. Though she despised the elves, she couldn’t bring herself to want them dead.

Sarret’s expression darkened with emotion. He couldn’t accept this. It was the opposite of what he wanted—his homeland, his home, was being destroyed.

“How can this be? Is there no other way? Can’t we find a solution to save the Southern Union?”

“I’m sorry, I don’t know. I’m just relaying the Guildmaster’s words.” Erikson responded awkwardly, sympathizing with Sarret. After all, the beastkin were also part of the Union.

“What other way? The Four Apocalypse Rings are essential for crafting Philosopher’s Stones. Do you really think there are two Famine Rings?” Flamel sneered, his dream of witnessing the truth of alchemy now obstructed by Sarret’s stance.

“Even if we take the Famine Ring, can’t we find a way to save the Union from sinking? That’s my homeland,” Sarret said, his voice trembling with emotion. “I refuse to accept this!”

“I beg you—give my homeland a chance to survive.”

“If we have to destroy my homeland, maybe I should never have joined you in the first place.”

title: Chapter 66 — Seizure Plan
content:
Chapter 66 — Seizure Plan

Volume 37 · Chapter 66

The moment Sarret finished speaking, every member's face darkened, their gazes toward it brimming with hostility.

Phoenix isn't an organization just anyone can join whenever they please; how could someone come and go as they wish?

Sarret knew its words would provoke dissatisfaction, but it had to fight for its homeland.

"Sarret, what do you mean? Are you trying to defy the Guild Master's will? Don't forget why we gathered here!" Alram lifted his head and said coldly, "To realize the ideal of absolute fairness, a world where no one suffers bullying, paying a price is necessary! We can't abandon it just because of one person's opposition!"

"Yes, for the sake of our shared ideal, the price is mandatory. Forget destroying my homeland — even if you took my own flesh and blood as a sacrifice, I wouldn't object. Everything is for the Guild Master's noble ideal." Hassan-i Sabbah rasped in agreement.

"Shut up! Sarret, I understand your feelings, but compared to realizing a world of absolute fairness, what does the destruction of the United Kingdom matter? You shouldn't be emotional. Don't forget, one of the conditions for joining Phoenix is to completely abandon your past. The United Kingdom has nothing to do with us anymore." Hesi said with a cold face; for the sake of its own ambition, it had abandoned its own kin, clearly afraid of destruction.

This group of people, each harboring ulterior motives — few were truly willing to be driven by that mysterious Phoenix Guild Master, yet on the surface they loved to invoke the "Guild Master's ideal" to ensure the Philosopher's Stone production plan proceeded smoothly.

Odom, Hassan-i Sabbah, and Hesi were the Guild's three pillars. Since they had already declared their stance, everyone else's objections could basically be ignored; Sarret fundamentally could not stop the United Kingdom's doomed destruction.

Cold sweat beaded on Sarret's forehead. Unwilling to give up just like that, it hoped its fellow countryman Hesi would stand with it. "Hesi, we both come from the United Kingdom. At a time like this you should be opposing this. Don't you care about your own people at all?"

"The dragon race might as well disappear already. I'm not like those fools. I believe in the great black dragon Nidhogg; they're all traitors." Hesi paused, then said indifferently, "Natural selection, survival of the fittest. The dragon race exited the stage of history long ago. Besides, the United Kingdom itself is just a huddle of heteromorphs trying to avoid elimination. They're not worth saving. You should wake up, Sarret."

You!! Veins bulged on Sarret's forehead. Lectured by Hesi until it couldn't retort, it could only grit its teeth and fall silent. To save the United Kingdom, it would have to find a way itself; Hesi was completely unreliable.

"This matter isn't up for discussion. No reason can obstruct our plan to create the Philosopher's Stone. No matter how great the cost, it's worth it." Hesi said coldly.

"Th-then I'll continue." Ericson swept a glance over everyone's expressions, his own turning grave. "This last War Ring — I'm afraid it'll be the hardest thing to obtain. It's in a Demon Lord's hands."

Everyone looked up, their eyes strange as they turned to Alram. This meant the Guild would have to contend not only with human kingdoms and the heteromorph alliance, but possibly not even spare the demon race.

Alram frowned. He hadn't expected a demon to be involved, and a Demon Lord at that. "Which Demon Lord?"

"Lucifer III." Ericson answered in a low voice.

"In that brat's hands, huh." Alram's expression grew heavy, a thread of pressure rising in his chest. "Is he in the Demon City?"

"No, the Guild Master said he's already left the Demon City and is living in the Britannia Kingdom." Ericson answered truthfully.

"Not in the Demon City? That's good. If he were still there it'd be too troublesome." Alram paused. Right now all demons were gathered in the Demon City; for him to go alone and seize the War Ring was nearly impossible. Even the three pillars working together would face enormous difficulty, what with Vivian, a Divine Realm expert, holding the fort, plus a host of Demon Lords including his own brother standing guard.

"Alram, what do you mean? Are you also going to speak up for your own kind like Sarret?" Hassan-i Sabbah questioned sternly.

"You misunderstand. Why would I speak for my own kind? I'd love nothing more than for the demon race to be utterly destroyed." Alram narrowed his eyes and continued, "If the War Ring were in the Demon City, we might as well give up now. The Demon City is currently an unshakable fortress. All the Demon Lords are gathered there. Even if we all mobilized, getting the War Ring would be very difficult."

"You haven't been with the demon race for a long time. How do you know so much detail?" Hesi asked suspiciously.

"I left, but that doesn't mean I won't go back. The demon race has always had my spies; I'm aware of every move." Alram replied quietly.

"In that case, Lord Alram is determined to obtain the War Ring?" Solrock asked with deep meaning.

"Not necessarily. Let me give the conclusion directly." Alram looked at the assembled members and said heavily, "The probability of forcibly seizing the War Ring from Lucifer III is zero. Not a single person here is his match."

At those words, everyone's expression shifted. Even Alram, who always looked down on everyone, had admitted defeat. Who knew what kind of monster this Lucifer III was?

By seniority, Alram — a second-generation demon — should be Lucifer III's senior, yet he feared this third-generation Demon Lord so much!

Hesi wasn't convinced, suspecting Alram was talking nonsense. "You're joking, right? No one is his match? Is he really that strong? You're not deliberately exaggerating here to protect your kin, are you?"

"Exaggerating? Hah! Lucifer III defeated the Demon God Behemoth." Alram looked at Hesi with a mocking smile. "That's an ancient god on par with the black dragon Nidhogg you worship. Can you defeat the black dragon? No, right? Probably only the Guild Master stepping in personally could fight this youngest Demon Lord to a draw."

Hesi was instantly struck speechless, unable to rebut, and muttered, "What kind of freaks are you demons?"

"The Guild Master isn't available, so we have to figure it out ourselves." Ericson wore a very troubled expression.

"Then aren't we screwed? We can't miss a single one of the four rings." Flamel's face was utterly disappointed.

"I said the probability of a frontal seizure is zero. I didn't say other methods are impossible." Alram shifted gears. "Knowing the enemy is strong yet still insisting on a head-on clash — besides a reckless fool, who would do that?"

"Oh? You really do have a way." Flamel's expression eased slightly.

"Leave this to me. The task of retrieving the War Ring — besides me, no one is up to it." Alram said with certainty.

"Lord Alram is going for the War Ring. What about the rest of you?" Ericson looked curiously at the others.

"Plague Ring — I'll take it." Hippocrates said in a hoarse voice.

"I can retrieve the Death Ring. I know Britannia better." Solrock thought that since they had to strike at old friends, it was better he go himself; at least he wasn't as ruthless as the others.

"The rest of you head to the United Kingdom together. Dealing with the heteromorphs' king won't be simple; we'll need more manpower." Ericson shrank his neck and said obsequiously, "No objections, right?"

Sarret's face was frosty. It was extremely dissatisfied with the Guild's decision, yet utterly powerless. Its resolute heart began to waver —

No! I must secretly notify the United Kingdom to prepare!

If possible, let some of my clansmen escape first.

■To Be Continued
