title: Chapter 1 — First One in Hand (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 1 — First One in Hand (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 38 · Chapter 1

Gulgul, gulgul—
Dais downed the pot of pig's blood in one gulp, watching the children practicing their swords, recalling his own childhood self here.
He had already returned to his hometown, severed ties with the fallen Austro-Hungarian Empire, and become a teacher who taught the children martial arts.
Since being turned into a vampire by Lady Bathory, he had to be careful everywhere, lest the villagers discover his monster identity.
To quell his thirst for blood, Dais could only substitute pig's blood; he did not want to harm the children nor the enthusiastic elders.
Dais hoped to completely forget his memories of serving the Austro-Hungarian Empire, to start anew, and if possible, to remain a teacher in his hometown forever—that would already be quite fortunate.
Yet every night Dais dreamed of the Austro-Hungarian emperor's expression at death; though it was unavoidable, he could not forgive his own betrayal.
Now Dais no longer considered himself a knight; even with familiar people, he kept silent about past events, not wishing those who looked up to him as a role model to be disappointed.

The children's movements were uniform, sweat pouring like rain, as they practiced the most basic thrust in swordsmanship, having forgotten how many days they had drilled this simple motion.
Many children felt vexed, thinking that after following Teacher Dais for so long they had yet to learn true skill, daily thrusting only.
“Teacher, what use is this thrust?”
“Yeah, Teacher, we want to learn real swordsmanship.”
“Exactly! Just like you, able to defeat magical beasts.”
A chorus of complaints rose and fell; Dais smiled, recalling his own childhood complaints about such things.
Dais lifted his head, seeing the sun set, finally able to shed his robe and step out from the shadows to move.
“You don’t understand; the thrust is the foundation of foundations. If you can’t even use a basic thrust well, how can you learn other sword techniques?”
“I’ve seen many people whose foundations were not solid, ultimately losing their lives in life‑and‑death battles, and even their strength stagnating for decades.”
“These are the prices paid for neglecting the basics; blind pursuit of power only leads down the wrong path, while steady progress lets you go farther.”
“You’re still young; you’ll understand this someday.”
The children glanced at each other, half‑understanding Dais’s words, not quite grasping them.
At their age, wanting to become independent swordsmen still leaves a long road ahead.
“It’s getting late; go home now. Be here promptly tomorrow to continue training.”
The children bowed to Teacher Dais, then, amid laughter, left the crude training ground.
Dais stared at the disordered field, shook his head, and began tidying up alone, still thinking about what to prepare for the children’s training tomorrow.

Suddenly a chilly wind blew, Dais felt an unfamiliar aura and instantly became alert!
He saw, outside the training ground’s gate, a figure who had appeared at some point, clad in a black robe, a crow mask on his face emitting heavy breathing.
“Doctor?” Dais exclaimed in surprise, shouting, “Who are you? There are no patients here.”
“Dais, former imperial guard of the Austro‑Hungarian emperor, who later betrayed and personally killed his master, then fled and vanished without a trace.” Hippocrates slowly lifted his head, his dark eyes fixed tightly on Dais, “So you were hiding here, becoming a sword‑instructor? A wretch who betrayed the knight’s spirit—what qualifications do you have to teach others? Ridiculous.”
Dais’s body jolted; he instantly drew the sword at his waist, angrily demanding, “Who are you exactly? Could you be the kingdom’s pursuers?”
“No, I have no relation to the already‑fallen Austro‑Hungarian Empire, nor am I here to hunt you down.” Hippocrates paused, then frankly said, “I am Hippocrates, a member of the Dark Guild Phoenix.”
“Hippocrates?” Dais frowned, unable to recall who he was; the identity of a Violet Gold Adventurer was always mysterious, so it was no surprise he didn’t know.
“Actually I’m not a famous adventurer either; you can call me a Plague Mage.” Hippocrates gave his other title.
“Eh! Plague Mage?!”
Dais stared wide‑eyed in shock; now he finally knew who the man was—wasn’t he the Violet Gold Adventurer who decades ago spread disease and ruined the four northern nations?
Because he abused his power to slaughter innocents, that Violet Gold Adventurer was expelled by the Association and remains a top‑rank fugitive to this day.
No wonder he vanished for so many years—he had actually joined the Dark Guild Phoenix and rarely shows his face.
Dais grew tense; the other was a merciless killer, and he couldn’t fathom why the Dark Guild had taken notice of him.
“I know who you are—a wanted criminal hunted by many nations, the madman who destroyed the four northern lands.”
“Exactly, I am a madman; in a sense we are alike, aren’t we?” Hippocrates paused, then continued, “Both of us despised the constraints of rules and regulations, finally rose in rebellion—you were oppressed and ultimately killed your own sovereign with your own hands; I was discriminated against and forced to suppress my power, until I could bear it no longer and faced my true self; I admire you greatly.”
“We are not alike, and your admiration is not a good thing.” Dais frowned, speaking sternly, “I have nothing to do with the Dark Guild Phoenix; please leave immediately—I do not welcome you.”
“I can leave, but please hand over the Plague Demon Ring.” Hippocrates locked eyes with Dais.
“How do you know about that?!” Dais’s heart jolted—this was his secret, never told to anyone.
“It’s a treasure I found by accident in childhood, always kept on me.”
“Our great guild leader knows all; nothing escapes his eyes.” Hippocrates explained, “Hand over the ring, and you may continue living.”
“Dream on!” Dais refused Hippocrates’s suggestion; he could never part with that treasure.
“You cannot control it; I can see you were once plagued by disease—this is not something you should possess. One who cannot command disease will be corroded by the plague, his body eaten away until death.” Hippocrates said solemnly.
“None of your business!”
“Then truly…”

Dais’s Saint‑tier fighting spirit erupted; without hesitation he thrust his sword at Hippocrates, who had once been a powerful Violet Gold Adventurer and must not be underestimated.
Hippocrates took off his glove, revealing a pale, withered palm, lightly touching the blade of Dais’s incoming sword, instantly corroding it to ash.
Dais failed to notice in time; the plague’s power followed the blade onto his hand, beginning to incessantly attack his innards, causing him excruciating pain.
“This is your own doing!”
In desperation Dais instantly produced the Plague Demon Ring, slipped it on, and the terrifying artifact’s power burst forth, lunging at Hippocrates—
“I don’t want to kill you, but you force me!
“Even if you kneel tonight begging for mercy, I will not let you leave alive!”
*Pffft!*
Hippocrates drove his silver dagger into Dais’s chest; Dais’s body turned to ash, utterly destroyed.
The evening breeze whispered, lifting Dais’s ashes and revealing the green Plague Demon Ring, flickering with an eerie light.
“Things went even smoother than I imagined.”

title: Chapter 2 — Joke
content:
Chapter 2 — Joke

Volume 38 · Chapter 2

A merchant ship was slowly approaching.

The Fourth Thorn Knight Solrock and Demon Lord Aram stood on the deck, gazing at the continent of the Kingdom of Britain.

Since their targets were in the Kingdom of Britain, after discussing, they decided to go together, ensuring they could bring back the two rings of Death and War smoothly.

"Going after your former companions, how do you feel about that?" Aram asked curiously.

"I'm calm," Solrock replied.

"Really? Not even a little reluctant? After all, you fought side by side before." Aram loved to pick at others' scars.

"So what? Since joining Phoenix, I'm no longer a knight. If Catherine refuses to hand over the demon rings, I'll kill her myself." Solrock said seriously.

"Cold-blooded enough. Though I don't particularly like humans, I admire you." Aram said meaningfully.

"I stopped being human long ago. Among those who study the undead, how many still keep their physical bodies?" Solrock looked at Aram, as if hinting at something.

Aram was startled, looking Solrock up and down, suddenly understanding. "So that's it. You're the same kind as Hassan."

"What about you? Can you go through with it when it's your own kin?" Solrock asked in return.

"Of course. I'm a criminal who cut off my own brother's head. How could you suspect me?" Aram frowned, feeling somewhat displeased.

"I don't know what you want by joining Phoenix. You make me very suspicious." Solrock's gaze was cautious; after knowing each other so long, he still couldn't see through the demon's thoughts.

"To realize the president's great ideal and create a brand-new world of absolute equality." Aram answered without flinching.

"Do you think I'd believe such nonsense? You want to return to the demon race and reclaim what was rightfully yours." Solrock voiced his own speculation.

"You're right, that's exactly what I'm thinking. But you probably didn't join Phoenix just to realize the president's ideal, right?" Aram paused and added, "Not just us, those guys all have their own ulterior motives. Who would willingly be driven by a president who won't even show his face, if not for summoning the Goddesses of Fate?"

Solrock didn't refute it; it was indeed true. The people in the guild joined Phoenix for their own benefits. "But the chance to make a wish only comes once."

"That's something to consider later. Before the Sage's Stone summons the three goddesses, we can still be trusted companions." Aram said softly.

Solrock remained silent, beginning to think about how to seize the only wish opportunity for himself.

Night fell upon the capital.

Today was the memorial day for several Thorn Knights. The scene of the demons' night raid from years ago was still vivid in mind.

Due to being busy with food affairs during the day, Mesfield had no time to pay respects to her former companions, so she went alone to the cemetery at night.

She prepared flowers, recalling her former companions; vivid familiar faces flashed through her mind.

Mesfield sighed at how things had changed in just a few years; among the Thorn Knights, only she and Catherine remained.

When she arrived at the cemetery, Mesfield discovered someone had arrived even earlier, standing before a tombstone holding flowers—

"Catherine? Why are you here too?"

"Today is Morrison's memorial day. You can come, so why can't I?" Catherine slowly turned around.

"I didn't mean that. I thought you had already come during the day." Mesfield replied awkwardly.

"I came with the queen during the day, but I wanted to come alone for a look." Catherine said meaningfully.

Mesfield suddenly remembered something, her expression turning melancholy. "Morrison is such a pity. After he left, the knight order became so much quieter."

"Yeah, he was never a well-behaved person, causing trouble everywhere and making quite a few jokes." Rarely, a smile appeared on Catherine's face. "When he was young at the monastery, he was afraid of being found wetting the bed, so he burned the sheets, and accidentally burned down the stable. He went three days without dinner."

"I didn't know so many interesting things happened when you were young." Mesfield looked strange, gazing at Morrison's tombstone.

"We're different after all. You were born into a knight family, while we grew up in orphanages. You must have had few friends as children, right?" Catherine asked curiously.

"Not exactly. I followed the queen when I was young; she... counts as my friend, right?" Mesfield answered in a low voice.

"That's wonderful. Growing up with the queen, she trusted you so much, willing to entrust her life to you." Catherine's tone carried a hint of loss.

"Uh!" Mesfield noticed the change in Catherine's attitude and quickly said, "Her Majesty the Queen also trusts you. She's the same with all knights. Don't think too much."

"I wasn't thinking much, and I'm not jealous. I'm just envious of you. Growing up beside the queen, your relationship goes beyond that of lord and knight." Catherine emphasized.

Mesfield was speechless. She and Elizabeth had indeed transcended the master-servant relationship, becoming more like sisters.

"To live up to the queen's trust in you, you should shoulder greater responsibilities. Possibly, you won't be able to pursue your own happiness in this life." Catherine's tone revealed a trace of sympathy.

"Pursue my own happiness?" Mesfield was surprised, shaking her head repeatedly. "No no, I won't get married."

"Don't you have someone you like?" Catherine asked with confusion.

"Someone I like?" Mesfield's mind suddenly flashed the ugly face of the great swordsman Elgin. She shook her head immediately. "No, you're mistaken."

"Is that so? Looks like I was overthinking." Catherine averted her gaze.

"Could it be... you have someone you like???" Mesfield asked curiously, unable to resist starting to gossip.

Catherine looked at Morrison's tombstone in silence, as if she had already told Mesfield the answer.

Mesfield was startled, gradually realizing that Catherine and Morrison had grown up together, and secretly developing feelings was only natural.

But Morrison was already dead. Catherine's secret would never be conveyed.

"I've been paying attention to that person all along, but the other party seems to have mistaken my concern for sisterly care. So I buried the secret deep in my heart forever."

Mesfield didn't know how to comfort Catherine, afraid that her straightforward nature would make her say the wrong thing and hurt the other person.

Catherine suddenly laughed, looking at Mesfield beside her, and said slowly in a tone like she was joking.

"Maybe I'll be buried here too. Then I could meet him again. After that, Her Majesty the Queen would need you to take care of her."

Mesfield was stunned, her face turning somewhat ugly. After hesitating for a moment, she replied seriously—

"Stop it. This kind of joke isn't funny at all."

title: Chapter 3 — Words Turn into Prophecy (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 3 — Words Turn into Prophecy (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 38 · Chapter 3

After Messfield left, Catherine stayed for a while longer, then slowly placed the flowers in her hand before the grave and prepared to leave.

Suddenly, a pale skeleton burst from the soil and grabbed Catherine's wrist, sending her face draining of color!

In that instant, wails like the cries of ghosts rose through the cemetery, cold winds sweeping around.

*Whoosh!* Ghost fires of eerie blue ignited, surrounding the entire cemetery and forming a barrier cutting it off from the world.

The skeletons of the knights seemed to come alive, crawling out of their tombs one by one, their hollow eyes fixing on the lone Catherine.

A layer of cold sweat beaded on Catherine's forehead as she felt as though she'd entered hell itself — the dead knights stood before her, clearly someone was targeting her.

Morrison hung tattered in rotting clothes, his flesh long since decayed, his bones creaking with each movement, making one's flesh crawl!

Catherine's expression grew complicated, wondering who would dare mock Morrison's remains — this was disrespect toward the dead.

"Long time no see, Catherine."

"Sorlock."

Sorlock's figure slowly appeared, a bizarre smile on his face, waiting until after Messfield had left before daring to show himself.

Catherine immediately gripped her magic wand, glaring at him with hostility, trying to read his intentions.

"What are you doing here? After betraying the kingdom, do you even have the face to return?"

"Don't say that, we were once companions who trusted each other. If you won't welcome me, at least why resort to sarcasm?" Sorlock said in a tone of helpless grievance.

"Who are your companion? You are our disgrace! You aren't welcome here!" Catherine reprimanded without mercy.

"Fine. I thought that after all this time, we could have a proper chat. Guess I was overthinking it." Sorlock continued, clearly disappointed, "I can leave, but... you need to hand over the Death Ring."

"Huh!" Catherine's expression tensed up. She hadn't expected her secret to be exposed — she'd been so careful!

"Hand it over, Catherine. I don't want to kill you, don't force my hand. That item is very important to me," Sorlock said frankly.

"Impossible. I won't hand it over to someone who joined a dark guild. Who knows what you'll use it for?" Catherine refused sternly.

"It seems there's no need for negotiation then. I'll have to finish you myself. Don't worry, I'll make it quick — more merciful than any enemy."

Sorlock's gaze turned fierce. Countless skeletons around him seemed to receive orders, all moving at once and lunging toward Catherine.

Flames of ghost fire flickered in their empty sockets, their ghastly forms radiating a hunger for fresh flesh and blood as they closed in around Catherine, as if afraid the meal would be gone if they delayed.

Catherine's expression darkened. She slammed her magic wand hard against the ground, completing a barrier spell in an instant. An invisible shockwave radiated outward, shattering the skeletons to pieces!

Sorlock waved his wand, his profound magical power surging forward. The scattered bones took flight, surrounding Catherine in the center and shooting toward her —

"Die!"

*Swish swish swish!* Sharp whistling sounds of splitting air rang out as bone fragments flew like razor-sharp swords, plunging Catherine into a dire predicament!

In terms of power, Sorlock surpassed Catherine. In a contest of magic, she had no chance of winning!

In desperation, Catherine spat out the Death Ring from her mouth and quickly slipped it onto her finger.

Immediately, the artifact's deadly power erupted outward from Catherine, engulfing Sorlock in an instant.

"What — what is this?"

Bathed in the Death Ring's radiance, Sorlock's spirit suffered unprecedented devastation, his eyes gradually dimming.

Catherine exhaled in relief upon seeing Sorlock's rigid corpse lying before her, feeling a weight lift from her chest as she prepared to report the matter to the queen.

But disaster struck without warning — the bones covering the ground suddenly trembled again, rising straight toward the sky and wrapping around Catherine. Sharp bone spurs pierced deep into her flesh!

A skeleton dragon wreathed in blue flames materialized from thin air. Its tattered dragon wings emanated an overwhelming aura of death, making Catherine feel as though she couldn't breathe!

"You thought you had defeated me? Foolish. This flesh is merely a vessel — I have long since become an eternal undead. Death means nothing to me. Your ring is useless against me."

Sorlock's voice emanated from the soul fire within the skeleton dragon. As a necromancer, he had long abandoned his physical body, becoming nothing more than an undead creature!

Catherine was tightly gripped in Sorlock's claws, unable to speak, her terrified gaze fixed on the skeleton dragon before her as despair filled her heart.

"It's over, Catherine."

Along the way, Messfield had sensed the terrifying aura of death emanating from the cemetery direction and immediately realized something had gone wrong.

She rushed back without rest, but unfortunately arrived a step too late and couldn't prevent Catherine's death.

The cemetery lay in ruin. Catherine's body was twisted into a grotesque shape, lying amid a sea of white bones.

Messfield's expression was dazed, her whole body trembling. She stumbled toward Catherine and collapsed to her knees.

Her breathing was heavy as she reached out to gently stroke Catherine's cold face. What just happened... the words had already come true —

"Catherine..."

Merlin followed Captain Dennis back to his home and saw the shredded corpse.

Since this corpse devoured people's power, no one dared to touch it casually.

Merlin had to handle it himself, suppressing his disgust as he pieced together the mangled body until he could clearly see the face —

"Cronos!?"

Merlin was stunned. He'd assumed it was some unknown chaotic creature, but it turned out to be the former strongest adventurer!

So Cronos was indeed a chaotic being from another world, lurking among humans and plotting who knew what all along.

Only now did Merlin learn the truth, his mind a whirl of confusion about what had happened to Cronos, the interdimensional spy.

"Cronos? Could it be that strongest adventurer, Cronos?" Captain Dennis asked beside him, puzzled — he'd never met that mysterious adventurer.

"Yes, that's him." Merlin nodded.

Captain Dennis drew a cold breath. "He wasn't human!? He was a monster hiding among us all along? Who killed him? Was it black eating black? If an ordinary person had killed him, they'd surely be making a big show of it. Removing a potential threat is an honorable deed."

"That's quite possible, but who exactly..." Merlin frowned, wondering —

Which dark force had targeted a chaotic being?

And for what purpose had they killed Cronos?

Meanwhile, in Rexham.

Outside Da Vinci's home, an uninvited guest had arrived.

Demon Lord Aram had witnessed Merlin handing a ring to Da Vinci shortly before leaving, a discovery that filled him with wild excitement.

He could retrieve the War Ring without even clashing with that young Demon Lord — so effortless!

It seemed Merlin didn't understand the ring's purpose at all and was having others help research it.

Merlin had been gone for several days; there was no way he could return to Rexham so quickly. This was the perfect moment to strike!

A grin spread across Aram's face as his twin sharp claws glinted with cold light, inching ever closer to Da Vinci's home.

"I never expected... retrieving the War Ring would be this easy?"

title: Chapter 4 — The Gear Turns
content:
Chapter 4 — The Gear Turns

Volume 38 · Chapter 4

Da Vinci was at home, carefully studying the ring Merlin had given her. The table was covered with various bottles and vials of alchemical materials.

Intricate magical arrays enveloped the small ring, continuously unraveling its internal secrets.

After several days of research, Da Vinci gradually found her way, becoming increasingly convinced that this ring was no ordinary piece!

As fierce flames burned, the ancient ring's surface slowly melted, shedding its black color to reveal a corner of bright red—

“This is...?”

Da Vinci's eyes widened in horror. The change in the ring confirmed her suspicions exactly.

This wasn't some ancient, ordinary ring at all—it was one of the Four Apocalyptic Demon Rings!

Someone must have coated the demon ring with a concealed substance to hide the truth, making it hard for others to discover!

Da Vinci put down her tools, picked up the War Demon Ring, and adjusted her glasses. A flood of alchemical knowledge surged into her mind—

The Four Apocalyptic Demon Rings were essential materials for creating the Philosopher's Stone, and the Philosopher's Stone had intricate connections with the mysterious Three Goddesses.

Perhaps I can use this ring to research the true method of creating the Philosopher's Stone!

Suddenly, Da Vinci's head was struck violently. She blacked out instantly, unaware that Alam had sneaked in.

Alam picked up the War Demon Ring from the floor and smiled smugly. Retrieving the War Demon Ring had been far too easy, almost unbelievable.

He had originally thought it would be the hardest to recover and had prepared many strategies, but he had completed the task without using any of them.

"Got it. I wonder how things are going with Thorlock?"

Alam's gaze fell on the unconscious Da Vinci on the floor, and he considered killing her to cover his tracks. Even if Merlin wanted to investigate, it would be very difficult.

However, Alam suddenly noticed the books on the workbench and found them familiar. He picked one up and saw it was—

"Democritus's Alchemical Notes"

Alam looked at Da Vinci again with suspicion. The reason it was familiar was because Flamme had also carried a copy of this notebook, saying it was a summary of his teacher's alchemical experiences.

By rights, a teacher's experience notes should only be shared with their own students. Could it be that this person and Flamme were from the same school, and their relationship was very close?

After a moment's hesitation, Alam abandoned the idea of killing her, letting Da Vinci go as a favor to Flamme.

Flamme was the only alchemist who could create the Philosopher's Stone. Alam didn't want to have any conflicts with this man.

"Hmph, consider yourself lucky to have saved your life."

In the Holy Tree Palace, the Elf King struggled on his bed, drenched in cold sweat that soaked the sheets beneath him.

He suddenly jolted awake from his sleep, sat up straight, gasping for breath, his eyes呆滞 and his entire body trembling uncontrollably.

After many years, the Elf King had once again had a prophecy dream of the extinction of the alien races. This time, it felt more real than ever, even showing a few blurry figures approaching.

"It's over. The prophecy has begun. Fate cannot be defied."

The Elf King muttered to himself. He knew the terrifying aspect of fate was that it was unchangeable. What was arranged would inevitably happen.

He had once again foreseen the extinction of the alien races, proving that the gears of fate had never stopped turning and that the time for the prophecy to come true had arrived—

What should I do? No matter what I do, I cannot change the arrangement of fate. Can the last pure land of the alien races not be protected?

If possible, I can only prepare in advance to ensure that part of the alien races can survive and pass on their legacy.

"Your Majesty!?" Shiruf heard the commotion inside the room and immediately rushed in when she sensed something was wrong with the Elf King. Seeing the Elf King in a state of extreme shock, she hurried forward, "What's wrong with you?"

"I had a prophecy again. I saw the prophecy of the extinction of the alien races once more," the Elf King said gravely.

Shiruf sweated coldly, frightened out of her wits. "Did you make a mistake? Because you've been overworked recently."

The Elf King shook his head. He also wished it was a mistake, but it wasn't. "No, it's real. This prophecy feels more real than ever. I feel the fulfillment is very close, possibly within half a month."

Shiruf was stunned, not knowing what to do. She knew the Elf King's prophecies were no joke. That meant the kingdom's destruction had already begun counting down. "Your Majesty, don't panic. We must have a way to get through this! We can... we can ask for Merlin's help. He definitely can!"

"No, it's too late," the Elf King shook his head, giving a bitter smile. "These are all things arranged by fate. You can escape for a while, but not forever. It will always happen. It's better to face it directly than to keep avoiding it."

"Your Majesty, don't give up! I and the other elves will fight with you until the very end!" Shiruf said emotionally.

"That's the most foolish thing you could do. You must survive. Only you can protect Shirley's safety. An old man like me should have long vanished into the dust of history." The Elf King paused, his tone resolute. "I was born on this land, and I will die buried here."

Shiruf felt不甘, but she could understand the Elf King's willingness to sacrifice himself for his people.

"Don't tell Shirley about this yet. I'm afraid she might act emotionally," the Elf King looked up, gazing at the dark and oppressive palace ceiling, and said softly—

"Go away. I'm already tired."

As the Elf King had prophesied, the ship carrying the Phoenix Guild had already approached the continent of the United Kingdom.

The night was dark, and the countless stars above seemed dim. A few dark shadows loomed like giants over the heads of the alien races.

Hasan Sabah收回 his gaze, the ghostly fire in his eyes flickering, "We're almost there. Are everyone prepared?"

"Of course. I can't wait to twist the head of the Blazing Dragon King off~" Hesee said with a meaningful tone.

"I want to visit the dwarf's territory. There might be many rare alchemical materials there," Flamme had already made up his mind to plunder the dwarves' wealth.

The harmless-looking young man Erikson placed his hands on his temples, communicating with other guild members remotely, "I just received the news. Hippocrates, Alam, and Thorlock have all been taken care of. The three rings are in our hands!"

"Oh? That's great news. We can't fall behind. Let's quickly get the Famine Demon Ring," Flamme was overjoyed. The dream of creating the Philosopher's Stone was just one step away.

Among the people present, only the former king Sarret had a pale face, gazing at the long-unseen homeland before him; his heart was extremely complicated—

Could it really not be saved?

title: Chapter 5 — Slaughter
content:
Chapter 5 — Slaughter

Volume 38 · Chapter 5

Saret lowered his head, silent, longing in his heart to save his homeland from destruction, but he was insignificant in the guild and had no way to change the mysterious chairman's decision.
He truly admired Chairman Phoenix's ideal of absolute equality, but the price was the destruction of the United Kingdom, which was obviously hard to accept.
"Taking back the Famine Ring is my job; a mere Elf King is no match for me." Hassan Sabah looked at everyone and continued, "Hessi, Flamel, Saret, you go kill the leaders of the other alien tribes to prevent them from coming to reinforce."
"That's easy, but you better act quickly; now we only lack the Famine Ring, and our mission can be completed." Hessi said solemnly.
"Yeah, why not let Hessi go with you? Going alone might be dangerous." Flamel expressed some concern, not wanting the mission to fail.
"Are you talking to me, the greatest assassin in history? I'm not only skilled at assassination; theft is my forte, with countless ways to retrieve the Plague Ring." Hassan Sabah said confidently.
Ericsson looked at his companions, couldn't help pointing at himself, "Then... what about me? What should I do?" "You don't need to do anything; just carry our luggage. Besides being able to contact other members, what else can you do?" Hassan Sabah had never expected such a petty Ericson; in battle he was utterly useless.
"Completely like a logistics person," Ericson lowered his head in disappointment. "Saret, Hassan Sabah looked toward the Benevolent King, saying meaningfully, "When facing your own kin, won't you be soft-hearted? Don't forget, you are a member of Phoenix; you should obey the guild's orders. If you defy, even if the chairman spares you, I won't let you off."
Saret broke into a cold sweat on his forehead, gritted his teeth and nodded, indicating his stance, but deep down he began to plot other things; betraying his kin was something he could not do.
In the dwarven kingdom's golden city, within the palace. The dwarf king played with the demon sword Tirfing in his hand, loving this artifact dearly, even holding it while sleeping. Not long ago, the dwarf king learned from a spy that Master Balin had obtained a treasure, and immediately conceived the notion of taking it for himself. For a dwarf king who loves collecting various treasures, Tirfing possessed immense allure, almost to the point of forgetting tea and meals. Even knowing it would offend Merlin, he couldn't resist seizing the demon sword Tirfing and making it his own. The dwarf king gently wiped Tirfing with smooth silk, more meticulously than he cared for his wife, having cast all affairs behind him.
"Good, good thing! A true divine artifact, only I am worthy to possess; placing it with Master Balin is simply a waste of heavenly treasure!" "Your Majesty, that's not right? This is a gift from the Demon Lord to Master Balin; you shouldn't have taken it." a dwarf subordinate said softly.
"Rob? Who robbed? I'm merely temporarily safeguarding it for Master Balin; such a precious item, keeping it in Master Balin's smithy is unsafe; only my treasure vault can guarantee absolute safety." The dwarf king defended himself, saying even if Merlin came to accuse him, he had prepared his excuses. "*How long do you intend to keep it for Master Balin?" the dwarf subordinate asked doubtfully. "Why so much nonsense? This obviously depends on my mood." the dwarf king replied shamelessly.
The dwarf subordinate frowned, a faint unease rising in his heart, "But Master Balin said this artifact is dangerous, bringing misfortune to its user; please, Your Majesty, be cautious." "Rest assured, who would believe such nonsense? It's just that old coot Balin wanting to keep the demon sword for himself, deliberately spouting alarmist talk to make me give it up." The dwarf king analyzed logically, continuing to stroke Tirfing, "Misfortune? Bullshit misfortune! I am now the master of the demon sword; let me see who can punish me!"
Just as his words fell, a pool of black sludge slowly seeped from the cracks in the palace floor, then gradually solidified into the shape of a hound, with four scarlet eyes! The dwarf king was startled, leaping from his throne to stare at the bizarre black hound, "What the hell is this thing?!" The black hound bared its teeth at the dwarf king, its mouth suddenly swelling to several times its size, spewing a large amount of alchemical bombs from its mouth! "This this this?!" The dwarf king tried to flee, but it was too late; with a thunderous boom, the palace instantly turned to ruins.
Although Flamel himself was weak in strength, his alchemy was immensely powerful, easily dispatching the dwarf king. Flamel's appearance emerged in the ruins; he crouched to pet his alchemical beast hound, a smile growing on his face. "Well done, not bad for my little treasure~" The alchemical beast wagged its tail, enjoying Flamel's stroking, then ran to a pile of rubble, unearthed the demon sword Tirfing and presented it to its master. Flamel examined the demon sword Tirfing, his eyes flashing with delight; he had only intended to loot the dwarves' ore materials, but unexpectedly gained an extra prize— "A divine artifact? Good stuff, it's mine now."
In the dragon territory, lava spewed from volcanoes continuously flowing outward, the gloomy clouds growing ever more oppressive, seeming not a good omen. The Blastflame Dragon King gazed at the scorching lava, pondering how to make the dragon race stronger—this was the task given by the White Dragon Alfard. With the black dragon Nidhogg's complete death, Alfard's lingering soul also dissipated, making him the supreme leader of the dragon race, the entire burden of the clan resting on his shoulders. The Blastflame Dragon King felt terrible; he noticed the dragon numbers dwindling, a trend hard to stop, as if an invisible pair of hands were clutching the throat of the dragon race's fate? "How exactly can we let the dragon race flourish again?" "This is fate's choice; why won't you accept reality?" "You're talking nonsense." The Blastflame Dragon King suddenly opened his golden eyes; a female voice came from behind him, unknown who was speaking to him. This is the core of the dragon territory, outside many dragons stand guard, impossible to enter silently! So the only answer: the dragon guards have all been **ed, and the enemy strides boldly before him! The Blastflame Dragon King abruptly turned, his whole body's fur bristling with alarm, he saw that familiar silhouette—none other than the outcast once expelled from the clan— "Igor!" "You traitor of our kind, do you still have the face to return?!"

title: Chapter 6 — Divine Bone (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 6 — Divine Bone (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 38 · Chapter 6

"Long time no see. Congratulations on becoming clan chief~"

Heshi appeared before the Explosion Flame Holy Dragon. Though her words were congratulatory, her tone was dripping with mockery.

In her view, the Explosion Flame Dragon King's desire to revive the dragon race was nothing short of delusional.

"Hearing your voice makes me sick. You should disappear forever and never appear before me again." The Explosion Flame Dragon King spoke through gritted teeth.

"Have you got it wrong? I came all this way to visit, and you're not the least bit welcoming?" Heshi asked with feigned surprise.

"What did you come back for? A freak like you was already expelled from the dragon race. There's no place for you here!" The Explosion Flame Dragon King was utterly rude.

"How regrettable. I was going to kill you, and I still had a shred of reluctance. But since you put it that way, I have no psychological burden anymore~" Heshi rubbed her slender neck, her gaze turning cold.

"Kill me? You'll need real skill for that. Who knows where you've been all these years? Have you actually improved at all?" The Explosion Flame Dragon King's face was gloomy.

"I think you know perfectly well that I've always been stronger than you. If I hadn't left, how could the position of clan chief have fallen to you?" Heshi's tone was sarcastic. "The current me is a member of the Dark Guild, and in the future I may even surpass Nidhogg, the creator of the dragon race."

"I never expected you to be so base as to sell your life to a filthy organization like the Dark Guild. You truly are a disgrace to the dragon race!" The Explosion Flame Dragon King glared furiously, speaking through gritted teeth. "Where did the once-proud you go? Don't you have even a shred of shame?"

"Do you think I'd have something like that?" Heshi paused, her words heavy with meaning. "Everyone was deceived by Alphard. What's wrong with serving our creator Nidhogg? You insisted on pursuing so-called freedom, and the result was the clan's vitality was severely damaged, with no possibility of ever rising again. Give it up. Weak clansmen are destined to be eliminated. Only outliers like you and me can survive."

"Shut your mouth! Don't bewitch people with fallacies in front of me! Scum like you has no right to judge Alphard!" The Explosion Flame Dragon King's body surged with scorching flames, already provoked. "If Clan Chief Alphard hadn't fought for our chance to determine our own destiny, we'd all be slaves enslaved by the Black Dragon! Without a shred of dignity!"

"Fool. Dignity is worthless." A mocking smile curled Heshi's lips as she spoke slowly. "The United Kingdom has already been targeted by the Dark Guild. This land is about to sink, and you have no way to stop it. I'll personally bury you here. I hope you can still cling to your pathetic dignity until death~"

"Don't even dream of it!"

The Explosion Flame Dragon King let out a furious roar, swallowed by a tsunami of raging flames, revealing his true form—

Amidst the howling fire, a colossal crimson fire dragon covered in scales appeared. Its wings unfurled, whipping up a firestorm!

The Explosion Flame Dragon King swung his massive tail, striking Heshi hard and sending her flying like a cannonball, crashing into volcanic rock.

"As expected, this is more interesting!"

Heshi was unscathed, a contemptuous smile still on her face. Having gauged the Explosion Flame Dragon King's strength, she was brimming with confidence.

Dark light enveloped her. Unwilling to be outdone, Heshi revealed her true form as well — a pitch-black dragon rose into the sky, its scales like knives!

Its eyes were crimson, its wings gleaming with a metallic luster. Every movement caused space to tremble violently!

Heshi opened with a Dark Breath at her opponent, and the Explosion Flame Dragon King countered with the same technique. The powers of flame and darkness collided violently, triggering an astonishing explosion in midair!

Dark Holy Dragon VS Explosion Flame Holy Dragon—

Two beings of nearly equal strength, both at the Pseudo-God realm. Their struggle would not yield a victor quickly.

Sylph had already received news that other demi-human territories were under attack, so she immediately rushed to the Sacred Tree Palace to report to the Elf King.

But the moment Sylph pushed open the palace doors, she suddenly felt gusts of cold wind, carrying a thick stench of blood!

Sylph's heart skipped a beat. Realizing something might have happened, she gripped her sword and entered the palace step by step, warily scanning her surroundings. Cold sweat trickled down her cheeks.

She searched for a long time but found no suspicious figures. Instead, she discovered the Elf King sitting upright on the throne with eyes open, gaze fixed straight ahead.

Sylph dropped to one knee and hurriedly reported, "Your Majesty! Something's happened! Other demi-human territories have been attacked! We need to go support them!"

The Elf King didn't move a muscle, still staring straight ahead, as if he hadn't seen Sylph at all.

"Your Majesty? What's wrong with you?" Sylph had an ominous premonition. The Elf King seemed very strange.

The Elf King remained unresponsive, like a withered tree — lifeless and listless. Even hearing Sylph's urgent report, he didn't react in the slightest.

Summoning her courage, Sylph approached the Elf King's side. The smell of blood grew stronger. She lightly touched the Elf King's shoulder — *hiss—*

A red line appeared on the Elf King's neck. His entire head had been severed, falling from the throne like a ball!

"Ah!" Sylph covered her mouth, horrified, eyes wide with fear! She never imagined this could happen. The Elf King was dead, just like that!?

Actually, Hassan-i Sabbah had already been here. As the once-strongest assassin, now granted the power of a Hell Apostle, his strength was even greater than before.

The Elf King had once sacrificed his own power to keep the Alliance Continent from sinking. His strength had long since fallen far from its peak, regressing severely.

Hassan-i Sabbah was one of the Guild's Three Pillars, a Pseudo-God expert. The Elf King couldn't even defeat his own brother Ashudor. How could he possibly be a match for Hassan?

Keeping the corpse intact, leaving only a red line on the Elf King's neck — clearly Hassan-i Sabbah had finished the opponent in a single strike. His assassination art was terrifyingly powerful!

Sylph nearly collapsed. Her eyes reddened as she slowly knelt beside the Elf King's headless corpse, fists clenched tight, silently resolving herself.

It seems the prophecy cannot be stopped. Then I must protect Princess Sherry's safety!

Hassan-i Sabbah and Erickson had already successfully infiltrated the elves' holy land, finding the cavern containing Corellon's bones.

Gazing up at this god who once ruled an era, even as mere remains, he possessed an awe-inspiring pressure beyond imagination!

"So this is the dead Elven God? This pressure is truly extraordinary. Though not equal to Satan, it's very close."

Hassan-i Sabbah felt a hint of tension. Before him lay the skeleton of an Ancient God. Even in death, its will would linger here.

But Hassan-i Sabbah had seen the far more terrifying Hell Ruler Satan. Clearly, Corellon's strength fell short of a True God possessing a Divine Spark.

"Lord Hassan! Look quickly!" Erickson was overjoyed, pointing at the skeleton on the throne, shouting excitedly—

"That's the Famine Magic Ring, worn on its hand!"

PSI 1

Less combat, not because I'm cutting corners, but to accelerate the pacing and improve your reading experience.

If I'm not mistaken, what you all want to see now is—

The mysteries left by previous foreshadowing, all being revealed step by step.

So we'll proceed in this direction. Faster pacing makes for a more comfortable read.

Let's calculate: if combat descriptions took two or three chapters, these plot points would need 20+ chapters to finish — 50,000+ words of just fighting.

That's meaningless. You'd definitely get sick of it. It's far less comfortable than accelerating the pace, with every chapter advancing the story.

I'm not cutting corners. I believe the current stage needs faster pacing to quickly present what you want to see.

And at this stage, all battles are one-sided — realm suppression. Everyone knows the results. Writing endless fight scenes serves no purpose.

The only somewhat close match is Heshi and the Explosion Flame Dragon King, so that gets a bit more detail. The rest just need the outcome stated.

Take Hassan and the Elf King — pure strength suppression. Nothing much to say. Better to accelerate the plot and get to the gripping foreshadowing reveals sooner.

Most

Brothers, still got votes in hand?

title: Chapter 7 — Destined to Perish
content:
Chapter 7 — Destined to Perish

Volume 38 · Chapter 7

Hasan Sabbah also noticed the gray ring on Corelon's skeletal remains. It was the power of this ring that upheld the continental landmass of the Allied Kingdom, keeping it from sinking into silence.

But if the Demon Ring of Famine were removed, it would trigger an unprecedented catastrophe. This land where the outsiders lived would plunge into the deep sea, and the kingdom would be destroyed along with it.

"As long as we retrieve it, all four rings will be collected. We're truly lucky!" Erickson said excitedly, rolling up his sleeves and stepping forward to pluck the Demon Ring of Famine right off.

"Wait! Don't be careless!" Hasan Sabbah stopped Erickson, his tone taking on some gravity.

"Lady Hasan, what are you doing? There's no one here but us." Erickson scratched his head in confusion, not understanding why Hasan was so tense.

"Who says there's no one else? You brat, you're too rash. If you approach carelessly, you might end up dead." Hasan Sabbah warned.

"Surely not?" Erickson felt a cold sweat drip down his forehead, frightened. "Could there be some kind of机关 or trap here?"

"Not traps. That person hasn't completely dissipated yet." Hasan Sabbah stared directly at Corelon's skeletal remains. It was inherently an undead being, extremely sensitive to souls. The Elf God Corelon appeared to be dead, but his remnant soul had not completely vanished—it still lingered here, much like White Dragon Alpha's condition.

"I... I see..." Erickson shivered, his gaze fixed on the motionless skeleton upon the throne.

"Lord Corelon, I believe you can hear us. We have no intention of disturbing your eternal rest. We merely hope you will hand over the Demon Ring of Famine." Hasan Sabbah spoke loudly.

For a long time, the remnant soul of Corelon possessing the bones never responded, ignoring Hassan—this mere hellhound.

In terms of status, Corelon, as the ruler of the Elf Era, could never consider someone like Hasan worthy of attention, let alone granting him the privilege of communication.

Furthermore, Corelon at this moment was only a remnant soul, possessing partial memories of the Elf God, not Corelon himself.

"Disregarding me?" Annoyance rose in Hassan's heart. He had lowered himself, only to be ignored. The other party was clearly humiliating him.

"What should we do now, Lady Hasan?" Erickson asked nervously.

"What else can we do? We'll just have to force it." Hassan answered with no small amount of helplessness.

"Will that be alright? That's the Elf God we're dealing with," Erickson said, deeply worried.

"It's only a remnant soul. There may still be a chance. Compared to the real Elf God, the gap is quite significant." Hassan Sabbah decided to give it a try. He had finally made it this far; if he didn't take the Demon Ring of Famine, it would be a great waste. "Stand back. I don't want you caught in the crossfire later. Watch my commands carefully, and if things go wrong, leave immediately."

"Understood!" Erickson quickly nodded, stepping backward continuously, his eyes filled with deep unease.

Hassan Sabbah's gaze was fixed on Corelon's skeletal remains. From his sleeve, he drew two serrated daggers, emitting an overwhelmingly dark aura of death.

"Hundred Shadows Stranglehold."

Before the words had even finished, Hassan Sabbah dissolved into the shadows. Immediately afterward, a hundred identical shadow figures appeared, densely packed throughout the cave.

Its true body seemed to be hidden among these hundred shadows, or perhaps all the shadows were illusions—no one could see through the secret.

As the most powerful assassin in history, Hassan had many disciples and left behind numerous assassination techniques that very few could fully master.

The Hundred Shadows Stranglehold was Hassan's proudest ultimate skill, with countless powerful figures having perished by its hand!

Suddenly, all a hundred shadows moved simultaneously, leaping up from the ground and completely surrounding Corelon's skeletal remains.

It was as if a hundred Hassans had acted together at once, coordinating with each other to form a deadly kill阵!

"Retreat, insignificant—"

Corelon's voice rang out through the cave like a bolt of thunder, making everyone's heads buzz.

The Demon Ring of Famine in hand erupted with ten thousand rays of light, and the deity's oppressive pressure filled the entire narrow space!

Hassan Sabbah's shadows were instantly dispelled, forced to reveal their true bodies. Panicked, it cried, "Run!"

But once a deity is angered, escape is nearly impossible. Corelon would absolutely not let go of this tiny undead who dared to challenge him.

Hassan Sabbah's skull, concealed beneath his black robe, was pierced through by an invisible force. The soul fire in its eyes flickered and died, and it was killed on the spot!

Only Erickson remained in the cave. He had already been terrified out of his wits and collapsed onto the ground—

"T-this th—"

Meanwhile, the elves had been organized and were preparing to board their ships, leaving the homeland that was about to be destroyed.

Sylph was strictly carrying out the tasks entrusted to her by the Elf King, doing everything she could to ensure her people could continue living, while also protecting Shelly.

Shelly, kept in the dark, had no idea what was happening. No matter how much she pressed Sylph for answers, the latter refused to tell her.

Perceptive as she was, Shelly faintly sensed something was unusual, especially since she hadn't seen her father from beginning to end, which made her deeply uneasy.

So Shelly stubbornly refused to leave the elf territory, pressuring Sylph to tell her the truth. "What exactly is going on? Why are we leaving like refugees?"

"Your Highness, please stop pressing me. Once you're on the ship, I will tell you everything." Sylph anxiously pulled at Shelly. If they didn't leave soon, it might be too late.

"I won't! Sylph, I order you to tell me!" Shelly said with a serious expression.

"...I can't tell you yet. His Majesty gave explicit orders." Sylph was under tremendous pressure. The Elf King had said that based on Shelly's personality, learning the truth would cause her to act emotionally and refuse to leave.

"If you don't tell me, I'm not going anywhere." Shelly stubbornly lowered her head.

"Your Highness..." Sylph was nearly at her wit's end. Biting her lip, she said, "The Allied Kingdom is under attack and will be destroyed. His Majesty's prophecy has come true. We must leave here to ensure at least some of our people survive!"

"Huh?" Shelly raised her head in shock, saying in disbelief, "No way... Could there be a mistake?"

"No, it's all true." Sylph responded with utmost seriousness.

Shelly looked at the elves continuously fleeing, realizing the severity of the situation. "Where is Father? I need to see him! We'll leave together!"

"His Majesty... has already passed away." Sylph answered softly. She didn't want to deliver this news to Shelly.

"What...?" Shelly suddenly froze, her face draining of color. "P-passed away? How is that possible? You're definitely lying to me, right?"

Sylph's expression grew grave, and she shook her head. She was barely maintaining the last shred of composure.

Shelly's eyes dimmed. Having lost her mother, and now losing her father—such a fragile blow was impossible for her to accept.

She refused to believe this reality, turning to head back toward the Holy Tree Palace, convinced her father must still be there.

"I'm going to see Father! He must still be alive. You're lying to me!"

"Your Highness, forgive me." Out of necessity, Sylph knocked Shelly unconscious, then carried her in her arms, sighing. "Please don't blame me. You are the royal bloodline's only survivor. You must live."

Clap, clap, clap—

A round of applause rang out. Flamel slowly emerged from the darkness, watching Sylph and Shelly with keen interest, accompanied by his loyal alchemist hound.

"A parting of life and death... What a touching scene."

"Unfortunately, it's destined to end in tragedy."

"Don't tell me you actually think you can survive."

title: Chapter 8 — Hard to Trust
content:
Chapter 8 — Hard to Trust

Volume 38 · Chapter 8

Sylph's heart jumped, she clutched Shirley in her arms and demanded, "Who are you?" "I am Flamel, who honestly tells you that I bring you the fate of destruction." "You bunch of bastards, you will surely meet retribution someday." Sylph gritted her teeth, thinking that if she tried to escape, although the frail human before her wasn't very aggressive, he might be able to swagger in here, surely possessing considerable strength. "Retribution? What is that? Just excuses the weak use to comfort themselves." Flamel stroked the fake sage's stone on his neck, speaking meaningfully, "Let me guess—you're currently thinking of how to escape, right?" "!!!?" Sylph stared wide-eyed, her thoughts completely guessed by the opponent, now she's in trouble! "I knew it, unfortunately I won't give you a chance. The ship you intend to use for escape actually has a bomb I secretly placed~" Flamel stretched out his hand and snapped his fingers— Boom boom boom! A huge explosion sounded, firelight dyed the distant sky red, exactly the direction where the escape ship was docked! At this moment many elves had already boarded the ship, countless innocent elves were blown to death. Fortunately Sylph and Shirley were not on the ship, otherwise they would likely have been blown to pieces in the explosion! Sylph felt horrified; the opponent wouldn't leave any way out, clearly intending to exterminate them completely. She glared at Flamel, eyes filled with bloodshot veins, wishing to rush forward and fight the enemy to the death, but Shirley was still unconscious in her arms, so she dared not act rashly. Those ships were the hope for the clan's survival; now they were destroyed, meaning most of the elves would perish in this catastrophe! "You despicable villain! You won't die well!" "Hehe~ thanks for the praise." Flamel weighed a gold alchemy bomb in his hand, wore a satisfied smile, and mercilessly threw the bomb at Sylph and Shirley. The bomb detonated in midair; flames and shockwave shattered the earth, instantly engulfing Sylph and Shirley—obviously they couldn't survive. Flamel was about to head to the elf clan's secret realm to check the situation when he suddenly sensed something abnormal— The smoke cleared, and before Sylph and Shirley appeared a figure—it was the Beast King Sarath! Just at the critical moment, Sarath had protected Sylph and Shirley, which is absolutely not something a dark guild member should do. "You're the Beast King?!" Sylph exclaimed, her mouth unable to close. "Are you alright?" Sarath turned his head to look at Sylph and Shirley, seeing they were unharmed he breathed a slight sigh of relief. He had betrayed the guild, returned to the beastmen clan, and instead of launching a massacre, he led his people in evacuation. After arranging things roughly, he began to aid other clans, coincidentally encountering Sylph and Shirley. The elf clan is the center of chaos, casualties are heavy; if possible, he hopes to protect more elves to survive. The United Kingdom is an alliance of multiple races, sharing honor and disgrace alike; he will not solely look after his own people. Sylph responded blankly, hurriedly asking, "You weren't satisfied with the alliance's system before, you left this place voluntarily—why did you suddenly return?!" "It's a long story; now is not the time to discuss these matters." Sarath replied coldly, his black fur bristling, guarding against Flamel opposite. "Sarath, are you crazy? Did you forget your mission? How could you protect those two elves!" Flamel shouted angrily. "I'm not crazy; I simply cannot abandon my kin, sorry." Sarath said expressionlessly. "Do you know what you're doing? The consequence of betraying the guild is only a dead end!" Flamel frowned, speaking sternly, "If I kill those two elves, I can pretend this never happened." "I can't do that." Sarath said sincerely. "Tch!" Flamel's forehead veins bulged as he gritted his teeth, "You damned traitor! You betrayed our shared ideal! The guild leader will absolutely not let you off!" "If realizing our shared ideal requires slaughtering my kin, then I would rather give it up!" Sarath bared his fangs, making it clear he would fight to the end. Sylph stared dumbfounded, a sense of fear rising in her heart; from their conversation it was obvious they were allies—could the Beast King also be one of the enemies?! "I will take the guild leader's place to eliminate you, this traitor!" As Flamel's words fell, the alchemy hound beside him opened its mouth, spewing a large number of alchemy bombs, which it hurled at Sarath! Sarath bared his claws; dark claw shadows flashed out of nowhere, tearing the incoming alchemy bombs to pieces! The violent explosion flattened the surroundings; the alchemy beast hound instantly turned into a barrier, shielding Flamel within. When the blast's aftershock faded, Flamel saw that Sarath had already fled with the two elves, nowhere to be seen; he was so angry his eyelids twitched. "Sarath, don't think you can escape; once the guild finishes handling everything, that will be your death day!" Suddenly a wave of heat hit; from the direction of the elf clan's holy ground, magnificent flames shot straight into the sky, gradually forming an undying phoenix that burned continuously, emitting a cry like an eagle! The earth beneath let out a mournful wail; all things in the world slowly melted as scorching magma surged up from underground! The elf clan's territory was shrouded in raging flames; this scene matched the elf king's prophetic dream exactly. A familiar pressure loomed over heaven and earth, pressing Flamel so hard he could barely breathe, even giving him the urge to kneel and worship— This familiar aura is the guild leader! Why would the guild leader appear here? Sylph clung to the unconscious Shirley, following Sarath as they fled quickly; her heart filled with unease. "We... where should we go?" "Leave by ship; this place will soon fall silent." Sarath answered calmly. "But... the elf clan's ships have been destroyed, we have no spare vessels." Sylph furrowed her brows. "Go to the beastmen clan's harbor; I have prepared many ships, enough to bring a large number of people to safety." Sarath had already readied everything; now he only needed to protect as many surviving different races as possible. "Really?" Sylph couldn't fully relax; her gaze toward Sarath was full of vigilance. The reason was precisely what had just happened—she couldn't trust this Beast King who had disappeared for so long. He might be colluding with the enemy, perhaps even jointly planning this disaster! Sylph lowered her eyes to look at Shirley in her arms; to prevent having just escaped the wolf's den only to fall into the tiger's den, she forced herself to ask: "You and that human just now—are you in cahoots?" " " Sarath paused, his expression complex as he looked at Sylph, fell silent for a moment then replied— "I will be honest about everything, but not now. "If you still want to live, then please believe in me." 弹

title: Chapter 9 — Grudge
content:
Chapter 9 — Grudge

Volume 38 · Chapter 9

Hexi clutched her grievously wounded abdomen and sucked in a sharp breath. In the battle against the Raging Flame Dragon King, she had been nearly killed.

Thankfully, she had won the final victory; otherwise, it would have been her lying dead here, not someone else.

The corpse of the Raging Flame Dragon King lay sprawled on the ground, its dragon body shattered into pieces, blood and scalding magma mingling together.

Hexi glanced at the severed head of the Raging Flame Dragon King, a flush of irritation in her heart, and grit her teeth, muttering through them.

"Trying to take me down with you? Keep dreaming. How could I possibly fall at your hands?"

A trace of hatred flashed in Hexi's eyes, and the searing pain from her abdominal wound made her wince in agony.

She had thought she could easily dispatch the Raging Flame Dragon King, never expecting the creature to fight to the death and nearly cost her her life!

Suddenly, the earth beneath Hexi's feet began to tremble violently, steadily sinking. Seawater surged up from somewhere unknown, and upon contact with the scalding magma, it erupted into massive clouds of steam—

Hmm?

Has the Ring of Famine already been obtained?

Looks like Hassan al-Sabbah's side went smoothly.

Rumble, rumble. Accompanied by tremendous noise, the Continental Land of the Allied Kingdoms was slowly sinking.

One after another, lifeboats scrambled to escape. The non-human races gazed upon their destroyed homeland, their hearts heavy with desolation.

The Elf King's prophecy could indeed not be avoided—it had come to pass. The gradual extinction of the non-human races seemed to be an unavoidable fate.

Fortunately, some of the non-humans had survived, avoiding the danger of their lineage being severed. How they would continue to live in the future was a severe test for them.

Under the organization and direction of the Orc King, Sarat suggested they first seek refuge with the human kingdoms friendly toward the non-humans, and then figure out how to rebuild their homeland.

This ran counter to the original wish of the Elf King, who had united the non-human races. They had kept their distance from human territories precisely to avoid endless conflicts between the non-humans and humans.

But now, the surviving non-humans seemed to have no other choice. They could only place themselves under the protection of humans, hoping to find enough living space to continue繁衍 and prosper.

The Orc King had an idea: he hoped to leverage the precious heritage of the non-human races to strike a deal with the Queen of Britain, swear fealty, and obtain a fief large enough for the non-humans to survive.

Unfortunately, this maneuver was extremely difficult. Whether that queen would even trust them was uncertain, and moreover, the issue of territory was a red line that no kingdom could afford to touch.

The Orc King decided to give it a try, since the Kingdom of Britain was located in the north, separated from other nations by sea—an ideal place for the non-humans to rebuild their homeland, far removed from most conflicts.

"Gone… our home is gone…" Master Balin hung his head, tears streaming down his aged face. The word "sorrow" was utterly inadequate to express what he felt at that moment.

"Don't be sad, father. We're still alive, and that's already lucky enough," the dwarf Bahl said, taking out a handkerchief and handing it to his father to wipe his tears.

"Exactly! Being alive is better than dead! We can still rebuild our home!" The fairy Phoebe floated in the air, cheering up the companions around her.

But her reddened eyes still betrayed her true feelings.

"We may have escaped, but many precious things are forever buried in that land. This truly is an unprecedented catastrophe." Master Balin was a man deeply attached to his home, and the sinking of his homeland dealt him a heavy blow.

Bahl and Phoebe fell silent at once. No one wanted to be forced from their homeland to seek a path to survival, yet none of them knew what their future held.

Silve cradled the unconscious Shirelli and sat in a corner, her expression grave, her heart filled with unease.

Could the home-less elves ever rise again? That remained an unknown.

Although the Elf King was dead, Silve pinned all her hopes on Shirelli. As long as she was alive, the elves would have a pillar to rely on.

"Can we really rebuild our homeland?"

"We certainly can." Sarat stood beside her, gazing afar at the dark sea. "Humans once were so weak that they were nearly driven to extinction. Yet they have since thrived again. Why can't we?"

Something stirred in Silve's heart, and she asked with suspicion, "Will that Queen of Britain really be willing to accept us? Will she be willing to grant us a piece of land?"

"The Kingdom of Britain is one of the few friendly allies of the Alliance. That queen has always been renowned for her kindness and sincerity. I think she won't kick us when we're down." Sarat reasoned. In truth, however, he himself was uncertain, for most rulers were two-faced hypocrites.

"What if she refuses us?" Silve frowned worriedly. The surviving clansmen currently had nowhere to set their feet.

"The likelihood of refusal is slim. We can offer her some of our inherited arts—for example, the magic of your elf race, or the martial techniques of our orc race. These can all serve as bargaining chips." Sarat bowed his head, analyzing. "Furthermore, we can swear fealty to her. Three years ago, the Kingdom of Britain suffered a demon invasion and was severely damaged; it has yet to recover its strength. Refusing us would not be in that queen's interests. As long as she agrees to accept us, granting us a fief is only reasonable."

Silve thought it over and found the words of this late-arriving Orc King somewhat reasonable, so her unease subsided somewhat. "Now can we talk about your relationship with those people, Your Orc Kingship?"

"This…" Sarat's expression grew serious. He turned around and gazed at the Allied Continental Land slowly sinking into the seabed, then slowly confessed everything—

"This all stems from the Elf King unilaterally deciding the destiny of the Alliance, violating the voting system agreed upon by the original nine leaders."

"I despised his attitude, as though he could see the future and placed himself at the center. The non-human Alliance appeared seemingly solid, but in reality it was not equal."

The next day, during daylight hours, the members of Phoenix had already boarded the return voyage.

"What!? Sarat that bastard betrayed us!?" incredulity was written all over Hexi's face. She had underestimated this Orc King's courage.

"That's right. He rescued two elves from my hands and then fled." Flamel answered truthfully.

"Foolish creature. He's dead meat. The Guild Master will never let him off. Phoenix is not a place you can just come and go as you please." Hexi's tone grew somewhat sympathetic; in her eyes, opposing the guild for the sake of his clan was about as foolish as one could get.

"Why would Senior Sarat do such a thing? The Guild Master will surely be furious." Erikson's expression was filled with worry.

"His clan is more important than the guild. That was exactly what he said with his own mouth. He must pay the price." Flamel said coldly.

"That's not something we need to worry about. The Guild Master will handle this matter." Hexi paused, then asked curiously, "How did you obtain the Ring of Famine?"

"This is all thanks to Lord Hassan." Erikson pulled out the green Ring of Famine, his eyes welling with tears. "If not for Lord Hassan perishing together with the remnant soul of the Elf God, we would never have obtained the magic ring. Lord Hassan is truly someone worthy of reliance."

Flamel kept a poker face on the surface, but his heart suddenly skipped a beat, a trace of resentment stirring within him. He stared at the youth before him, who seemed harmless as a lamb—

Why was he lying?

My intuition is not wrong. The aura emanating from the Sacred Land was that of the Guild Master.

There were five companions in total. Sarat and I went to deal with the other non-human leaders.

Hassan and Erikson went directly to the Elf Sacred Land. But now Hassan is dead, and only Erikson survived?

Could it be…

title: Chapter 10 — Parents Are True Love, Children Are an Accident
content:
Chapter 10 — Parents Are True Love, Children Are an Accident

Volume 38 · Chapter 10

Merlin returned to Rackham, but upon hearing from Alice that Da Vinci had been attacked, he hurried over to check on her.

Da Vinci had bandages on her head, and she bowed her head toward Merlin, apologizing with deep pits in her cheeks—

"Mr. Merlin, I am very sorry. Your ring was stolen by someone."

"Huh?

Merlin furrowed his brows. He had originally thought of asking Da Vinci to help him research it properly, but he never expected it to be stolen?

This made Merlin's mood very displeased. He had always been the one stealing other people's things, and now the tables were turned.

"Who did it?"

"I don't know either. I passed out directly." Da Vinci's speech was a bit awkward; she only remembered her head suffering a heavy blow, "However, when I woke up, I felt a faint demonic aura inside the room."

"Demon?

Alice was taken aback, and subconsciously looked toward Merlin, "Could it have been a demon?"

Merlin said nothing, and his heart was also uncertain. In principle, demons had no reason to attack Da Vinci. After all, it still came down to that ring!

"I'm very sorry, Mr. Merlin, for failing to keep your belongings safe," Da Vinci said, feeling guilty in her heart. She believed the ring being stolen was her responsibility.

"It's okay, Miss Da Vinci, don't blame yourself. It's not your fault."

"Yeah, Miss Da Vinci, it's fine..."

Alice agreed from the side, thinking to herself: Who cares about a ring compared to a life? Besides, Da Vinci didn't lose it on purpose.

Suppose that robber not only stole the ring but also killed Da Vinci. Then the guilty ones would be her and Merlin.

After all, Da Vinci had nothing to do with this. It was Merlin who asked her to help research the ring, which dragged her into it.

"Miss Da Vinci, does that ring have any problems?" Merlin asked with deep meaning, thinking that if it were an ordinary ring, it probably wouldn't attract others' greed.

Very big. Da Vinci emphasized her tone and continued, "That ring is one of the Four Heavenly Demon Rings. Looking at its characteristics; it should represent war."

"The Four Heavenly Demon Rings?

Merlin was surprised. He didn't know alchemy, so he wasn't clear on what this meant.

"That's right. Besides containing the power of a divine artifact, the demon rings are also indispensable materials for crafting the Philosopher's Stone. In alchemy, they are precious treasures that are hard to come by, although their surface is plated with a special substance, concealing their true appearance." Da Vinci answered truthfully.

"Huh"

Merlin was suddenly stunned, feeling like he had lost out big time. So that seemingly ordinary ring was actually a divine artifact and a rare treasure! No wonder someone came to snatch it!

Merlin had actually researched it since 2 already, and giving it to Da Vinci hadn't held much hope, but to think it would be an ace from the start!

Merlin pounded his chest in anger, stomping his feet in frustration. If only he had burned it with demonic fire when he first got the ring. A duck in his mouth could fly away!

"I M._."

"What's wrong?

Alice was startled by Merlin's reaction, thinking that even if the ring was lost, the reaction shouldn't be this big?

Merlin suppressed his irritable mood and said seriously—

"I must get this ring back."

On the way home, the two of them kept thinking about who had stolen the ring.

"Since Da Vinci sensed demonic aura, the thief must be someone from your demon race, right?" Alice speculated in her mind.

"It shouldn't be. My clansmen are all stationed in the Demon City, and there's no reason for them to leave. Moreover, my mother never mentioned the Four Heavenly Demon Rings, and she wasn't very interested in them either. On the contrary

Alice saw Merlin's hesitant look and追问, "What's the 'on the contrary'?"

"Isn't Da Vinci saying that the demon rings are necessary materials for crafting the Philosopher's Stone, and are treasures in alchemy? I think it's likely an alchemist or organization that stole the ring." Merlin stated his guess.

"But how does Da Vinci's sensing of demonic aura explain that?" Alice curiously asked.

"Demons living outside the demon race aren't just me. Some demons were exiled because they committed mistakes. Of course, the number is very few." Merlin answered.

"So you're still planning to find that ring?" Alice's expression was strange, suspecting that Merlin might want to leave alone again?

"Of course. It was originally my thing. If it was stolen, I can't just sit here silently! Impossible!" Merlin's face was ugly, explaining, "This ring is a divine artifact, not some cheap thing. Even if I'm extravagant, I won't just let it go like that."

"Do you have a plan?" Alice asked softly.

"I'll let the guild help me collect a list of exiled demons, one by one, and I'll definitely find a clue." Merlin had calculated in his mind, planning to go back to the Demon City.

"So you're planning to leave again?" Alice's face was unsightly, and she was full of resentment in her heart.

Merlin realized something and looked at Alice beside him, "What do you mean 'I'm planning to leave again'? You're not going with me, are you?"

"Huh? Alice's mood improved a bit, affecting a composed look, "I never said I'd go with you."

"Well, then I won't bring you, you stay home and watch the kids." Merlin answered ruthlessly.

"Wait a minute!

Alice grabbed Merlin, glaring at him with puffed cheeks, "At a time like this, shouldn't you beg me a few more times?"

"Pah! Who would do such a troublesome thing?" Merlin rolled his eyes.

"If you beg me once more, I'll definitely agree!" Alice said seriously.

"So troublesome." Merlin sighed, lowering his voice, "Together?"

"Hmm~" Alice lifted her hair, haughtily saying, "Since you've invited me so sincerely, I'll reluctantly agree."

"Damn it! Get lost! I resign!" Merlin shook off Alice and quickened his pace.

"Merlin!

Alice caught up with Merlin and gave him a throat-strike, "You this heartless rascal, do you not love me anymore?

Do you have no patience for me now!"

". I didn't mean that, dear wife, you misunderstood me." Merlin dropped a cold sweat on his forehead, thinking

The "rascal" hat he wouldn't wear.

"- Investigating this matter isn't impossible, but what about Chris? As a father, you should consider your daughter more." Alice scolded with a face full of anger.

"I've considered it, couldn't the landlady help take care of her for a few days? She's a lonely old person, quite pitiful." Merlin said righteously.

"Bothering the landlady every time—do you think anyone is as thick-skinned as you?" Alice gritted her teeth.

"It won't take much time to track down the thief, plus you don't see that the landlady is very lonely, needing someone to accompany her." Merlin emphasized seriously.

"Alice hesitated.

"On the surface, we're tracking down that thief, but actually Merlin whispered near Alice's ear, "This is a honeymoon trip, dear."

"Honeymoon trip?

Alice's gaze was startled, and her face unconsciously flushed red, her heart stirring

"If it's a honeymoon trip, then it's fine,"

Tracking the thief doesn't take much time.

The landlady is also lonely and needs company."

"Is it a honeymoon trip, then—"

"There's no problem then, let's depart tomorrow~"

The poor little guy was kicked away by unscrupulous parents. Indeed, spouses are true love, and the child is just an accident.

On the side, Chris, who was playing with a dog, sneezed, and her whole body began to tremble.

Ives swayed his dog tail, looking at Chris in doubt, suspecting the little guy had caught a cold? So he went over to rub against her.

"Chris, are you sick?" Mini asked with concern.

Not sick. "Little Chris frowned, the hair on her head like a straight antenna—

"Chris has a bad feeling, though~"

"Must be a big bad guy scheming against good Chris!"

title: Chapter 11 — Surfacing (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 11 — Surfacing (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 38 · Chapter 11

"Alice nodded. 'You found something at Captain Dennis's house?' she asked.

'That's right,' Merlin frowned and whispered, 'I saw the body of Klowno.'

'What?!' Alice gasped, thinking of the adventurer with the deformed appearance. 'He's dead?'

'Yes, he was torn apart into pieces, and I don't know who did it,' Merlin was still puzzled about this matter and continued, 'but I found out a secret. Klowno wasn't human; he was a creature from another world, and it's highly likely that he was a spy hiding in our world.'

'Huh?' Alice was stunned, finding it incredible. 'There are such things?'

'His body had the ability to absorb power, which is similar to those chaotic creatures,' Merlin paused and said slowly, 'Dennis and I both believe this was a case of black-on-black, where ordinary people killed the alien spy. Normally, they would announce it publicly, but until now, there's been no news, which suggests that the perpetrators didn't want to take credit for it, and they're probably not good people.'

Alice lowered her head and muttered, 'What happened? Why were they targeting Klowno? He hid his identity for so long, and it shouldn't have been easy to discover him.'

'It's probably because of the black box. Klowno stole the black box I brought out of the Chaos Sea, which even I couldn't open, but others managed to open it. Dennis said there was nothing inside, it was empty,' Merlin recalled Captain Dennis's words and wondered what happened that night when Klowno died. 'What was in the black box?'

'I don't know how I would know,' Merlin guessed, 'but it must be something very important to the other world.'

'Recently, things have been quite unsettled, with all these strange and bizarre incidents happening.'

'I couldn't agree more.'

Just as they reached the door, they saw a man in a state of distress, standing at the door and refusing to leave. It was Chaplain, the Knight Commander of the Wisteria Knights, that middle-aged man who had once asked for Elkin's signature on his sword. Chaplain saw the two returning and was overjoyed, rushing forward. 'Miss Alice, you're finally back. And who is this?' Merlin looked puzzled.

'Chaplain seemed embarrassed, wondering if Merlin was holding a grudge, as he was of a high rank and didn't know that Merlin was Elkin,' Chaplain continued, 'You're a forgetful noble, I came to the Kexum to interrogate you three years ago, about the undead infestation in Dunby County.'

'Oh, it's you, you old boy,' Merlin finally remembered.

'Chaplain nodded humbly, his attitude very submissive, because of Alice's high status, even if Merlin was a 'softie,' he couldn't afford to offend her.'

Alice had met the Wisteria Knights before and was familiar with Chaplain. 'Chaplain, what are you doing here?'

'Miss Alice, there's been a major incident. Queen Elizabeth wishes to see you as soon as possible,' Chaplain said seriously.

Alice frowned, feeling something major must have happened. 'What happened?!'

'The Black Phoenix, a dark guild, has been very active recently, collecting something called the Magic Rings, and they've been causing trouble everywhere. Kathrine has fallen heroically,' Chaplain said solemnly.
