'Kathrine?!' Alice knew Kathrine well, she was a serious person who didn't smile much, and now she's dead.

'Oh? That woman,' Merlin also remembered her, his mood turning somewhat perplexed. 'Wait, you said they're collecting Magic Rings? The Four Magic Rings of the Apocalypse?'

'It seems to be that name, I wasn't very clear, it was a half-orc named Sarret who said it in front of the queen.'

'Black Phoenix? Dark Guild?' Merlin's eyes widened, and suddenly, many unrelated things seemed to connect, forming the truth. His War Magic Ring might also have been taken by the Black Phoenix. Who among the exiled demons joined the Dark Guild?

Chaplain swallowed nervously and revealed another shocking piece of news. 'Additionally, there's the latest news. The Black Phoenix has destroyed the Southern United Kingdom, and the land of the orcs has completely sunk into the deep sea. The surviving orcs are now seeking refuge in Britain.'

'Alice: !!!'

'Merlin: ???'

With all the clues pointing to the Black Phoenix and the Southern United Kingdom experiencing such a major incident, Merlin and Alice didn't waste any time and set off for the capital the next day to gather more detailed information and learn about the inner workings of the Black Phoenix.

As for Chris? She was sent to the landlady's place to be taken care of. The little girl seemed to have a premonition, though she was unhappy, she had no choice.

At the Knight Cemetery, Mesfield stood in front of Kathrine's tombstone, she hadn't left here for days.

Mesfield regretted in his heart, why didn't he stay with him that night, maybe everything could have been changed.

As Kathrine's words came true, she was also buried here, next to Morrison.

Perhaps in the world of the dead, they could express their feelings to each other and become a couple who loved each other.

Mesfield was very sad. Twelve Wisteria Knights died, ten of them, and one turned traitor.

Strictly speaking, she became the last remaining Wisteria Knight, as if a curse was hanging over the entire knightly order.

Queen Elizabeth was with Mesfield, hoping she could go back and rest properly.

'Go back, Windsor, death is something everyone will experience, don't dwell on it, I'm sure Kathrine wouldn't want you to.'

'I know, I just feel so helpless, it's so unfair for Kathrine,' Mesfield regretted Kathrine's death.

Queen Elizabeth remained silent, unsure of how to respond.

'A knight should die at the hands of the enemy, not at the hands of their comrades, I can't accept that Kathrine left in this way.'

Mesfield's voice was filled with anger, she clenched her fists and shouted, 'Solrock, this traitor must be punished! I will go to avenge Kathrine and punish the Dark Guild!'

'I will find a way, you should calm down now,' Queen Elizabeth was concerned about Mesfield's state, fearing she might do something foolish.

At that moment, Chaplain came over, kneeling on one knee to report, 'Your Majesty, Miss Alice has arrived.'

'Are you Merlin?' Queen Elizabeth asked.

'Yes, we came together,' Chaplain nodded.

'I know, I'll be there right away.'

See, how fast it went, straight to the point.

If everything was written in detail, it would take about 30 episodes to get here.

Is that the case?

title: Chapter 12 — Seeking the Truth
content:
Chapter 12 — Seeking the Truth

Volume 38 · Chapter 12

Merlin and Alice had already arrived at the conference room to wait, and not long after, Queen Elizabeth and Melfield rushed back.

"You're finally here, Miss Alice." Queen Elizabeth stepped forward and naturally nodded to Merlin in greeting. "Mr. Merlin."

"Hmm." Merlin nodded, as if in response, without saying much.

Melfield, following behind Queen Elizabeth, wore an unfriendly expression and glared angrily at Merlin. He thought to himself: that detestable man again! Did Her Majesty personally invite him?

Merlin broke into a cold sweat, his eyes flickering about as he pretended to be innocent. He certainly didn't want Alice to know about the many times he had humiliated Melfield. Who knew if this jealous vase wouldn't tip over?

Alice looked疑惑ly between Merlin and Melfield. A woman's intuition told her something was off. Were these two hiding something? The atmosphere was full of gunpowder the moment they met.

"Cough, cough!" Merlin hurriedly interrupted Alice's thoughts and asked solemnly, "Elizabeth, what exactly happened? Can you tell us in detail?"

"Let us sit down and talk. This matter involves very many people..."

After everyone took their seats, the Queen recounted everything that had recently occurred.

After hearing the account, Merlin felt deeply唏嘘. "That guild called Phoenix — they were collecting magic rings from everywhere to create the Philosopher's Stone, and that's what caused the destruction of the Southern Alliance?"

"What cruel deeds. A perfectly fine homeland of a different race, just vanished like that?" Alice lowered her head, feeling regretful in her heart. She hoped the kind Sherry was unharmed.

"That's correct. The survivors from the United Kingdom have taken refuge with me, and they are temporarily settled. But matters of the future still need to be discussed." Queen Elizabeth spoke slowly.

"What exactly is Phoenix's background?" Merlin asked curiously, unable to understand why there would be demons within such an organization.

"They are the strongest dark guild, yet their behavior is very low-key. We know very little about them. But one thing is certain — they are definitely plotting some kind of evil scheme." Queen Elizabeth paused and continued, "From the current situation, Phoenix members come from different factions. There are not only humans but also members of other races. Although the number of members is very small, each one is a terrifying powerhouse. This may well be the most elite organization in the world. Rather than calling it a guild, it would be more accurate to say it is a consortium composed of different factions."

"That sounds unbelievable." Alice paused and countered, "To set aside all disputes and bring together powerful individuals from different factions — the difficulty is far greater than imagined. Who exactly is their leader?"

"This dark guild is named after its leader, also called Phoenix. He is said to be the person closest to God. There is very little information about him, and honestly, I'm not particularly clear myself." Queen Elizabeth said awkwardly.

"So you don't know anything either?" Merlin shrugged helplessly. "I thought coming here I'd hear more detailed intelligence about Phoenix and figure out what they're planning with the Philosopher's Stone. Unfortunately, Elizabeth, your intelligence gathering leaves much to be desired."

"Silence! When speaking to Her Majesty the Queen, you ought to be more polite!" Melfield scolded, his face full of anger.

"It's alright." Queen Elizabeth waved her hand, not angry at all. After all, she understood Merlin's personality well. "Perhaps Mr. Merlin should consult others about these matters."

"Others?" Merlin frowned and looked around.

Queen Elizabeth instructed Captain of the Knights, Chapman, to bring over the two leaders of the refugees from other races, so they could answer Merlin's questions.

After a while, Orc King Saret and Elf Princess Sherry arrived in the conference room. They immediately bowed slightly in greeting.

"Your Majesty, noble Queen..."

Merlin's gaze turned peculiar as he glanced at Queen Elizabeth. He thought to himself: the two representatives of other races are so respectful. Had the surviving members of other races already pledged allegiance to the Queen of Britain?

In fact, that was precisely the case. Queen Elizabeth had accepted their fealty, which could be used to make up for the kingdom's strength. It was just that matters of fiefdoms still needed negotiation.

Orc King Saret had requested a piece of land large enough for the other races to survive — this clearly involved the core interests of the Kingdom of Britain, and Queen Elizabeth had to think carefully about it for some time.

Although the surviving members of other races were reluctant to submit to humans, they had no better option. Having lost their homeland, submitting to Britain was still better than submitting to kingdoms hostile to other races.

"There's no need for such excessive courtesy. I merely wanted to ask about Phoe—"

Queen Elizabeth had not finished speaking when she heard a startled exclamation from Alice beside her. Her hand went straight to her sword hilt.

"It's you!?"

"Uh... troublesome human woman?"

Saret had also spotted Alice and was immediately stunned. How could an adventurer be present in the Queen's conference room?

"Fate has a way of bringing enemies together, doesn't it?" Merlin muttered. He hadn't forgotten that during the time he had been turned into a child, this orc had kidnapped Helena... "Do you two know each other?" Queen Elizabeth asked, quite puzzled and confused.

"How could we not know each other? This filthy orc—"

"Miss Alice~"

Before Alice could finish her words of condemnation, Sherry had already thrown herself into her embrace, wearing a sweet smile on her face.

Since her father's death these past few days, Sherry's mood had been deeply depressed. No matter how Sylph tried to console her, she could not shake off the shadow of losing her only family.

But seeing Alice, Sherry felt as though she had met an old friend. Her gloomy mood improved considerably, and she had so much she wanted to tell her.

"Sherry?" Alice suddenly paused, then gently stroked the poor child's hair. "I'm just glad you're safe. I was worried you hadn't managed to escape."

Sherry's expression suddenly darkened, and she sniffled as she said, "Father is dead. I've lost my only family."

Alice froze for a moment, sympathy evident in her eyes. She held Sherry tightly and comforted her, "Everything will pass. Don't keep dwelling on this."

Merlin remained silent, thinking to himself: so that elf king has died? Does this organization called Phoenix also possess the power to destroy a kingdom?

"Then why were you with this orc, Sherry? He's a villain!"

"If I'm not mistaken, weren't you also part of Phoenix?"

Alice glared at Saret with an unfriendly expression and adopted a stance as if she were about to attack at any moment. What had been the purpose of that initial kidnapping of the demon?

Sherry sensed the tense atmosphere and quickly blocked Alice, saying in a pleading tone, "It's not like that! Uncle Saret isn't a bad person. He only made a mistake through a moment of confusion. He was the one who organized our escape from the dark guild's persecution!"

"Huh?" Alice was momentarily flustered, unable to imagine that members of such a vicious dark guild would rescue people in distress. Had they suddenly discovered a conscience?

"How interesting. So they've defected." Merlin laughed out loud. His doubts vanished completely. The answer could finally be revealed — the leopard-like orc before him must have an extremely thorough understanding of Phoenix.

title: Chapter 13 — The Only Chance
content:
Chapter 13 — The Only Chance

Volume 38 · Chapter 13

Watching Alice full of hostility, Sarret bowed his head and had to admit his fault.

After all, it had already betrayed the guild, and now that it needed to protect its clan and continue living, it had to avoid making enemies.

"This human miss, I know you must despise me, but I still want to apologize for what happened back then. I should not have struck your son."

"Huh?" Queen Elizabeth looked completely puzzled. Didn't Merlin and Alice only have one daughter? Where did a son come from?

Alice's expression was strange. She knew Sarret had misunderstood — that was Merlin in the state after drinking the Time Potion, not her own son.

"Who's the son? Just shut up." Merlin's forehead vein throbbed.

"Did I misunderstand? My apologies." Sarret paused and said earnestly, "I just don't want everyone to hold grudges over the past. Back then, I was following the guild's orders. I had no choice but to obey."

"Oh? Then why did you betray the guild?" Merlin asked coldly.

"Because my clan was threatened. I couldn't accept the guild coercing me into harming my own people in order to achieve their goals." Sarret answered honestly.

"So in the end, you're still just a selfish creature. It's fine to harm others, but not your own clan?" Alice said discontentedly.

"That's not it. I used to agree with Phoenix's vision of creating an absolutely equal world, on the premise that only a small price would need to be paid." Sarret paused, then continued, "But I underestimated their ambition. To achieve their goal, they were willing to destroy the United Kingdom and kill every alien race. I couldn't accept that."

"An absolutely equal world? What kind of nonsense is that?" Alice was confused.

"That is an ideal land with no conflicts whatsoever, where everyone is the same, with no distinction between high and low. That was Phoenix's conception, and all guild members would act toward that goal." Sarret explained slowly.

"Sounds kind of nice... but something like that is impossible, right?" Alice found it hard to believe. Only children would entertain such unrealistic ideas.

Queen Elizabeth frowned. Phoenix's members were extremely dangerous individuals. How could they willingly serve some vague ideal? The situation was probably not so simple.

"It can be achieved. This requires the power of the Philosopher's Stone. After making a wish to the legendary Three Goddesses of Fate, reality itself can be changed. If you think of the Three Goddesses of Fate as the book that holds the world's history, then the Philosopher's Stone is the pen that can rewrite it." Sarret stated concisely, hoping the others could understand.

"The Philosopher's Stone? The Three Goddesses of Fate?" Merlin frowned. He had heard those names more than once. "So you're saying you want to create the Philosopher's Stone and use that goddess's power to alter reality?"

"That's correct. That's exactly what Phoenix has always sought to accomplish. That's why, to create the true Philosopher's Stone, they would spare no cost." Sarret nodded, finding the blond man understood quickly. For some reason, he looked somewhat familiar.

"Changing reality? That's impossible, right?" Merlin found the idea quite absurd. If a device like that truly existed, wouldn't life be amazing?

"It's real. In history, there have been three who made wishes to the Three Goddesses and altered reality: Odin, Mary, and Satan. They have all used it." Sarret paused, then continued. "I once read about it in human ancient texts. In the distant age of the gods, the world was not yet divided. All races lived on the same continent. There was no Hell or Heaven. Clearly, someone had altered the original appearance of the world."

"Something like that exists? Unbelievable." Alice lowered her head. She felt the power to alter reality posed a tremendous threat. If it fell into the wrong hands, who knew what disasters it could cause?

"The guild has been preparing to create the Philosopher's Stone all along. In addition to the Four Apocalypse Magic Rings, other materials are needed, such as the blood of all races. Because of this, I set my sights on that exiled female demon and clashed with you all." Sarret's tone was filled with apology.

"I see."

Merlin remembered that Sarret had wanted to kidnap Helena, the Flamel Bureau Adventurers Competition, and the plan to destroy the United Kingdom — all of these were to gather materials for creating the Philosopher's Stone. He now understood almost everything about Phoenix.

"Do you have demons in your guild?"

"Demons? Yes. His name is Alam. I've heard he's a terrifying figure who nearly became a Demon Lord." Sarret answered truthfully.

"Alam? Hah."

Merlin gave a helpless smile. So it was him — a dangerous individual who personally severed his own older brother's head, the younger brother of the Wrathful Demon Lord Samyel. Who would have guessed he'd joined a dark guild?

The so-called promise of an absolutely equal world was certainly a lie. At the very least, a demon named Alam would surely sneer at such a foolish ideal. No doubt everyone in the guild had their own calculations.

"Where is Phoenix's guild? We're going there."

"I'm coming too!" Meisfield suddenly spoke. She still wanted to find Solrock and avenge Catherine.

"No. I don't like dragging burdens along." Merlin looked at Meisfield and rejected her wish to accompany them. "Besides, you're the last remaining Thorn Knight. You should understand your responsibilities, right?"

In fact, Merlin's words were hinting at Meisfield — if she left, there would be no one to guard the queen and the capital's safety. Especially now that so many alien races were taking refuge in the royal capital, Merlin didn't fully trust the orc king Sarret.

No one could be certain the orc king wouldn't lose his mind and take advantage of the capital being undefended to seize the place entirely.

With Meisfield there, at least the orc king would feel a significant deterrent and think twice before acting recklessly.

However, Meisfield's straightforward nature failed to understand what Merlin meant. Instead, she felt slighted —

"Hah! You arrogant jerk!"

In the soaring obelisk, the pirate's son Loki was secretly observing everything happening inside the secret chamber.

All members had returned there days ago and handed over the Four Apocalypse Magic Rings to Flamel.

All the materials for creating the Philosopher's Stone had been prepared. Now they only needed to wait for Flamel to make history and bring the true Philosopher's Stone back into the world.

Loki had been staying here for a long time and had learned many secrets. Unfortunately, he still couldn't participate in the guild's important matters. Everyone excluded him.

This made Loki somewhat regretful. He shouldn't have handed over all the pirate fleet's wealth to Phoenix, because those people hadn't followed their original agreement to help him kill Lucifer III.

Loki felt deceived. He couldn't count on this group for revenge. He had to rely on himself —

The Philosopher's Stone, huh?

Probably the only way to avenge my father. I must seize this opportunity!

title: Chapter 14 — Outwardly United, Inwardly Divided (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 14 — Outwardly United, Inwardly Divided (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 38 · Chapter 14

A strange alchemical circle, bright red, emitted a strong scent of blood.

Flamel held a broom, stained with fresh goat's blood, and added various strange symbols to the alchemical circle.

Others watched from the side, wondering what Flamel was up to?

"Hurry up..."

Flamel paused, wiped the sweat from his forehead, and sighed as he struggled to complete the complex alchemical ritual.

"What is this?" Sollock asked curiously.

"This is an alchemical circle used to summon the Three Goddesses," Flamel said, looking at the central alchemical furnace. "Once the Philosopher's Stone is complete, we can use it to open the door to the Realm of Destiny."

"Is that so? It will take a long time before the Philosopher's Stone is finished," Sollock said, looking at the alchemical furnace.

"No, it should be done soon. It won't take much longer," Flamel replied.

Sollock's eyes burned with intensity as he stared at the alchemical furnace, secretly plotting in his mind. If he could obtain the Philosopher's Stone and fulfill his wishes, he would have to eliminate the others.

Not only Sollock thought this way; others had similar thoughts, their eyes fixed on the alchemical furnace, waiting for the Philosopher's Stone to be completed so they could take it for themselves and make wishes to the Three Goddesses.

Hershey and Aram's gazes clashed in the air, each seeing the other as their most formidable competitor. Both were among the three giants of the guild, and their chances of obtaining the Philosopher's Stone were greater.

Since the Philosopher's Stone began to be made, no one had left the room, all waiting and spying on each other, afraid someone would get ahead of them.

Although the guild remained a whole before the Philosopher's Stone was completed, it had already begun to separate, with mutual calculations.

Those without ambition were only Hippocrates, the simple-minded killer, and the harmless young man Erikson.

"Finally, it's done? What a relief," Erikson said, sighing in relief. "I wonder, if we fulfill the guildmaster's wishes, what will the world be like?"

"Of course, it will be everyone's utopia. I'm sure Hippocrates will also be free to express himself," Erikson said naively.

"Hmph," Aram let out a low chuckle, thinking, "What nonsense! There are indeed fools in the guild."

"What are you laughing about? It sounds sinister," Hershey said, her eyes filled with meaning.

"It's nothing, I'm just happy for everyone because we're about to achieve our shared dream," Aram said, smiling.

"Are you serious?" Hershey narrowed her eyes, thinking, "Old fox, you're quite convincing. I hope you remain calm after the Philosopher's Stone is completed."

"What do you mean? Hershey, do you doubt my loyalty to the guildmaster?" Aram said, staring at Hershey. "I think you're not right. You shouldn't be satisfied with your own desires and ignore us and the guildmaster, right? After all, you don't even spare your own kin, so you shouldn't put us and the guildmaster in your sights either!"

"Hah~" Hershey's face darkened, and she retorted, "I don't want to be called a cold-blooded demon who chops off his brother's head by a heartless monster like you, who has no right to doubt me."

"Ha, it seems that the two of you don't trust each other at all. Then it's easy. After the Philosopher's Stone is completed, why not let me take care of it? That way, both of you will be satisfied," Sollock said, seizing the opportunity.

"What are you? Do you have the right to speak here?" Aram scolded.

"Are you really a lowly human and want to touch the Philosopher's Stone? Do you think you're worthy?" Hershey said, filled with hostility, looking at Sollock.

Sollock's face turned very ugly. Seeing that the Philosopher's Stone had not yet been completed, he could only suppress his anger. He realized that Aram and Hershey were a great threat, and if he didn't find a way to eliminate them, he would lose his chance.

Flamel looked down at the alchemical circle, drawing the symbols, and sighed silently the whole time. He had anticipated the reactions of everyone, but not the rapid division of the guild.

Flamel had already foreseen that once the Philosopher's Stone was completed, there would be fierce fighting.

"No, don't argue," Erikson quickly stood up, saying nervously, "We all gathered here to fulfill the guildmaster's ideal, why do we have to distrust each other?"

"Yes, arguing is meaningless," Hippocrates nodded in agreement.

"Are you already turning your backs on the guildmaster's ideal and not wanting to fulfill it?" Erikson paused, saying seriously, "You must not forget our mission and the significance of Phoenix. A shared ideal does not allow betrayal."

The guildmaster always watches over us, he knows everything we do, and he certainly does not want to see us like this."

Several people's faces changed, and as long as they did not get their hands on the Philosopher's Stone, the mysterious guildmaster still made them fearful.

"Cough cough!" Sollock coughed lightly, saying, "It's a misunderstanding. I have always been loyal to the guildmaster."

"I am too, but I'm just a bit suspicious that someone might betray us in the middle," Aram said awkwardly.

"I agree, it's just that I'm afraid that something might happen, so I'm a bit suspicious," Hershey said, her eyes avoiding.

"Since we can't eliminate each other's doubts, why not give the Philosopher's Stone to me?" Erikson said seriously.

Sollock: "???"

"Are you serious?" Erikson's forehead dripped with cold sweat, saying nervously, "I am the weakest in the guild, and I have no threat, so this way everyone can be at ease."

"I agree," Hippocrates nodded.

Sollock felt that it was better to give the Philosopher's Stone to Erikson than to Hershey and Aram, so that the robbery would be easier. "I have no objections either."

Hershey and Aram looked at each other, hesitated for a moment, and then forced a stiff smile, nodding in agreement. They both had a bit of fear for the mysterious guildmaster. If they didn't agree, they might be suspected of having double intentions.

"This might be the best solution," Hershey said, looking down, thinking about the best time to act.

"Giving it to Erikson, everyone can be at ease," Aram bit his teeth, thinking Erikson was meddling in other people's affairs.

Erikson smiled innocently and confidently, saying, "Great! I will definitely not disappoint the seniors!"

Flamel glanced at Erikson, becoming suspicious. These idiots, haven't they realized the seriousness of the situation yet? This...

After completing the alchemical circle, Flamel stood up slowly, collected everything, and prepared to leave temporarily, looking at everyone and saying, "It's done. I need to rest for a while. Do you want to go together? After all, you haven't seen you rest for many days."

"Yes, you should go rest, and I'll take care of it here," Hershey said hurriedly, wanting to get everyone out of the room.

"I'm not tired. I don't feel comfortable leaving you alone here. It's better to guard the alchemical furnace," Aram said, his words filled with meaning.

"Yell!" Hershey's forehead veins bulged, her thoughts exposed.

"Then I'll go. If the alchemical furnace reacts, call me..."

In Flamel's room, there was a strict isolation magic circle, which not only could block the sound but also isolate the air.

In the center of the magic circle, a small alchemical furnace was placed, and it was burning fiercely. A small, dark stone was visible in the furnace.

As the fire burned, the dark substance on the surface gradually cracked, revealing a bright red interior.

Everyone was deceived by Flamel.

The real Philosopher's Stone was not in the secret room, but in this room.

title: Chapter 15 — Truth and Lies
content:
Chapter 15 — Truth and Lies

Volume 38 · Chapter 15

Flamel took the completed Philosopher's Stone from the alchemy furnace, gave it a gentle squeeze, and the black layer on its surface completely shattered.

The Philosopher's Stone emitted a dazzling crimson glow, which quickly收敛ed into its interior, resembling a ruby, yet its color was far purer.

"Is this the real Philosopher's Stone?"

Looking at the stone the size of a fingernail in his hand, Flamel furrowed his brow, clenching it tightly before glancing down at the fake Philosopher's Stone around his neck.

Flamel could guess that the Philosopher's Stone would cause the entire guild to fall apart, and only one person could hold it to meet the Three Fates.

Although Flamel had no ambitions, he simply wanted to use the Philosopher's Stone to meet the three goddesses of alchemy who represented "truth," fulfilling his own wish.

But he was very clear that no one would believe he had no ambitions and would suspect him of seizing the sole wish-granting opportunity.

Therefore, Flamel saw the current situation very clearly. If he couldn't satisfy his own wishes, why should he hand the Philosopher's Stone over to those greedy bastards?

Flamel had already made his plans and preparations, wanting to use the real Philosopher's Stone to blackmail others. If they didn't fulfill his wishes, no one would get the real Philosopher's Stone.

Flamel slowly crouched down, patted the head of the alchemy beast hound beside him, and fed the real Philosopher's Stone to it. Then he pulled the fake Philosopher's Stone from his neck, intending to process this fake thoroughly to deceive everyone.

"Is this the only way?"

Flamel sighed, looking at his alchemy notes on the desk beside him, which recorded all his alchemy knowledge, including the method for creating the Philosopher's Stone and the alchemy array for opening the Fate Realm.

He fell silent for a long time, recalling a person he could trust, and suddenly had a new idea, deciding to make two preparations—

My plan might fail.

But that person will surely fulfill my wish.

A few days later, the alchemy furnace suddenly shook, and brilliant red light shot out from the furnace.

Everyone in the secret room was startled awake, their faces filled with excitement, obvious to all.

"Did it succeed!?"

"Should be no problem!" Hessey secretly glanced at Alram, ready to seize it.

Of course, the furnace's reaction was all fake. Flamel had placed other substances inside, deliberately making the furnace react so strongly to deceive everyone.

But these people, who knew nothing about alchemy, had no idea, even believing the Philosopher's Stone had been completed and it was time to seize it.

Sorlock's eyes were filled with greed, and he rushed toward the alchemy furnace first, wanting to knock it over and get the Philosopher's Stone first.

It's mine!

Suddenly, a dark binding like a cage wrapped around Sorlock, rendering him unable to move.

"Alram, you're really despicable!"

"Don't get so excited. The Philosopher's Stone isn't something you can take."

As soon as Alram finished speaking, he himself walked toward the alchemy furnace, his eyes burning with intense desire, thinking his wish was finally about to come true.

Unfortunately, Alram had only taken a few steps before being blasted by a dragon's breath, crashing heavily into the wall of the secret room and failing to approach the furnace.

"Cough cough... Hessey, do you want to die?"

"Haha, you brought it upon yourself." Hessey said lightly.

Erikson looked around at everyone in terror, hesitantly saying, "Aren't we supposed to let me保管 the Philosopher's Stone?"

"Sorry, that was just a lie to deceive children." Hessey blinked her eyes.

"Hessey senior, this isn't right," Erikson said nervously.

The door of the secret room opened, and Flamel walked in, loudly addressing everyone, "Everyone, calm down. Let me take out the Philosopher's Stone."

"No way! Who knows if you'll keep it for yourself?" Alram said seriously.

"Besides me, who else here understands the Philosopher's Stone?" Flamel paused, confidently saying, "If you're not convinced, you can open the furnace yourselves. When everything effort is wasted and the result is a failure, don't blame me for not warning you."

Everyone exchanged glances and had to admit it was a fact. The Philosopher's Stone was so precious that if a problem occurred in the final step, no one wanted to see that result.

Flamel's confident demeanor indeed intimidated everyone, forcing them to refrain from taking any rash actions.

"Then you please go ahead," Alram said with a smile, temporarily daring not to offend Flamel.

Flamel coldly hummed, brought his alchemy hound with him, and slowly approached the alchemy furnace, turning his back to everyone. As he opened it, a scorching storm swept through the entire secret room, causing everyone to briefly close their eyes.

When they opened their eyes, a bright red gem was already in Flamel's palm. Everyone stared at it intently, each expression seeming on the verge of going mad!

"This is," Flamel looked at everyone and declared with a decisive tone, "the Philosopher's Stone!"

Flamel lied. This Philosopher's Stone was fake, precisely the processed counterfeit of his original fake Philosopher's Stone, but it was already enough to deceive these alchemy outsiders.

"Philosopher's," Alram swallowed.

"Looks like a gemstone," Hessey examined the Philosopher's Stone.

"Senior Flamel, this Philosopher's Stone seems similar to yours," Erikson suddenly said.

"Seems like it," Sorlock frowned.

Flamel's heart gave a jolt, but he still maintained his composure, saying, "My Philosopher's Stone is fake, but it's already very close to the real one, so it's natural for them to be somewhat similar."

"Originally," Hippocrates paused and asked, "then who should manage this Philosopher's Stone? Perhaps we should follow the original agreement and give it to Erikson. Everyone would feel at ease."

"No way! Erikson is unsuitable," Alram was the first to object.

"Exactly, just because Erikson seems harmless doesn't mean he doesn't have his own thoughts," Hessey also disagreed.

"Everyone else is more suitable than Erikson. How about... drawing lots?" Sorlock suggested.

Just as everyone was arguing without resolution, each hoping to obtain the Philosopher's Stone, Flamel stepped forward and said—

"Give it to Erikson. Giving it to anyone else would make no one feel at ease. Your greed is written all over your faces."

"What do you mean, Flamel?" Hessey's face darkened, her killing intent subtly rising.

"I'm just stating the facts. If Erikson isn't suitable to hold the Philosopher's Stone, then there's no suitable person here," Flamel ignored the angry looks from others and walked up to Erikson, personally handing him the Philosopher's Stone—

Flamel still had a faint hope, which was to negotiate with the head of the Phoenix Guild.

Not asking for anything else, just to meet the Three Fates.

But if the other party refused, then no one would ever know the whereabouts of the real Philosopher's Stone!

title: Chapter 16 — Wipe Out Completely
content:
Chapter 16 — Wipe Out Completely

Volume 38 · Chapter 16

The group gathered in the alchemical circle, ready to open the realm of destiny.

"Next step, Erikson?" Erikson asked hesitantly. "Flameel senior."

"Just wait quietly, the realm of destiny will open on its own," Flameel replied.

Alram and Hecate exchanged glances, clearly both harboring ulterior motives. No one could remain composed in the face of such a massive temptation.

Suddenly, the alchemical circle filled with thick mist, engulfing the entire chamber!

Flameel's alchemical beast, the hunting dog, showed signs of distress, as the true philosopher's stone in its belly had reacted.

When everyone opened their eyes again, the scene before them had completely changed. It was no longer the chamber they had just been in, but a world they had never seen before.

Numerous gears intertwined, clattering as they turned, and in the distance lay vast starry skies. They stood on a massive wheel, in this mysterious and vast world, they seemed incredibly small, as if they were at the heart of a clock.

Is this the realm of destiny?" Sollok wiped a bead of cold sweat from his forehead, the sight before him causing a great shock to his three-dimensional perception.

"Look! What is that?" Hippocrates widened his eyes, pointing in a direction.

Everyone followed his gaze, and saw a towering stone gate standing at the end, with strange carvings on it. It seemed to depict three seductive women.

They wore crowns and robes, and together held up the sun at the highest point, symbolizing something?

"The gate symbolizing truth in alchemy!" Flameel was not calm, his eyes filled with longing. The Three Goddess of Destiny must be inside! Once that door is opened, the true essence of alchemy will be revealed!

"Almost there," Alram stepped forward first, saying coldly, "Erikson, give me the philosopher's stone. No one else can enter that door with the philosopher's stone except me."

"A ridiculous claim. Such a precious philosopher's stone is certainly mine!" Hecate advanced slowly, not hiding her greed.

Sollok beside her also showed signs of greed, secretly extending his bone spikes, ready to kill Erikson and take the philosopher's stone for himself.

At this moment, the philosopher's stone had become a hot potato, and whoever held it would be the enemy. Erikson's life was in danger.

Erikson retreated in fear, pleading, "No. Don't do this. The philosopher's stone is used to fulfill the guildmaster's wishes, not to satisfy personal desires. Don't you think the guildmaster will blame you?"

"Guildmaster, what a worthless coward! He's just a hideous little turtle!" Alram scolded without any politeness.

"That's right! The guy who hasn't shown his face until now, what guildmaster is that? Isn't it fun to play hide and seek?" Hecate was very disdainful.

"Isn't it? Do you really think we're loyal to Phoenix for his ideals? That's just a story to tell children," Sollok also no longer hid his true feelings.

"The guildmaster is angry, and you all won't have a good result!" Erikson said in a panicked voice.

"Ha, guildmaster? Where is he? Call him out! I haven't seen the guildmaster enter the secret realm, which proves he's not here!" Alram paused, his expression twisted into a grotesque one. "Even if it's the guildmaster, he can't peek into the things in the secret realm, right?"

"If you don't want to die, hand over the philosopher's stone, Erikson. Don't you understand the situation now?" Hecate said in a mocking tone.

Erikson suddenly became calm, his gaze sharp, and he said coldly, "I knew you would betray me in the middle of the way. Since you don't believe the guildmaster is here, let's see for yourself."

"What?!"

As the words left his mouth, a strong heat wave hit them, and flames erupted in the realm of destiny, burning fiercely!

A phoenix made entirely of fire appeared in the sky, roaring loudly at everyone!

Then, the flames of the phoenix all rushed into Erikson's body, causing some changes in his appearance. His hair turned into flames, his body grew golden feathers, and a bird-like mark appeared on his forehead.

"Sollok, you can't say anything," Sollok was stunned, the divine aura was exactly like the guildmaster's!

"Isn't it? It's a ghost!" Alram was scared to death.

"You are the guildmaster?!" Hecate widened her eyes, hesitating to take action.

"That's right, I am Phoenix, I've been watching you all along!" Erikson said with fire in his eyes.

"Indeed," Flameel took a deep breath, things were exactly as he thought. He had guessed that Erikson was the mysterious guildmaster.

"So, we've all been deceived? Why?" Hippocrates asked in confusion.

"It's true," Erikson said without any expression, using a condescending tone, "You were all tools I used to collect materials to make the philosopher's stone. Since the philosopher's stone is now complete, you have no value, so disappear."

Erikson's gaze hardened, and the flames engulfed everyone, the high temperature sweeping through the entire realm of destiny!

Alram, Hecate, Sollok, and Hippocrates were almost instantly turned to ashes!

They had no resistance against the phoenix, the gap in power was too great!

Erikson looked at Flameel, extended a finger, pointing at this talented alchemist, and said coldly, "You've done well, Flameel. You've also lost your value."

"Wait!" Flameel shouted, cold sweat beaded on his forehead.

"What? Even at this moment, you're still thinking about begging?" Erikson tilted his head.

"You'll regret killing me! I beg you, don't do this!" Flameel gritted his teeth, trying to fight for his life.

"Guildmaster, I'm different from them. I don't threaten you. I have no ambitions. I just want to enter that door with you. This is my lifelong dream! I won't interfere with anything you do! I just want to see the Three Goddess of Destiny!"

"Flameel, haven't you noticed? Wanting to enter that door with me is your ambition, isn't it?" Erikson said sympathetically.

"Uh!" Flameel's face turned ashen, his last hope shattered.

"How can I allow others to enter that door? Especially..." Erikson's face darkened, his expression icy cold, "you, the terrible alchemist who made the philosopher's stone."

Flameel let out a sigh, as if accepting his fate, and laughed, "It's no use, right? Don't worry, you won't succeed. Your fate won't be much better than ours."

"This is not something you need to worry about."

Erikson mercilessly burned Flameel alive, his body blackened, lying straight on the ground.

The loyal alchemical hunting dog emitted a sorrowful "woo," circling around Flameel's corpse.

After dealing with all the obstacles, Erikson prepared to enter the stone gate, but suddenly heard other voices behind him.

Merlin: "This is the realm of destiny, as Saraiet said? It's indeed extraordinary."

Alice: "Wait for me! Don't walk in so boldly, what if there's an ambush?"

title: Chapter 17 — Rebirth from Ashes
content:
Chapter 17 — Rebirth from Ashes

Volume 38 · Chapter 17

The alchemical hound of Flamel sensed the outsiders, panicked and fled; no one paid any attention to this ownerless dog, and they certainly wouldn't know that it had swallowed the true Philosopher's Stone. Erikson turned his head and saw Merlin and Alice intruding into the Fate Secret Realm, slightly furrowing his brow; at this moment he didn't want anyone to ruin his plans. Merlin and Alice also saw Erikson, and had to stop and size him up, having expected many people to be here, but only one remained. Looking at the ashes covering the ground and the charred corpses unrecognizable as to who they were, Merlin thought for a moment and realized what had happened; after all, according to Sarat's intelligence, the wish opportunity comes only once, so to compete for it, an internal conflict was inevitable. Merlin felt his timing was perfect, saving himself a lot of trouble dealing with others; dealing with a single opponent was much easier. “Tsk tsk, what a pity, it seems everyone except you is dead.” “Merlin, who is he?” Alice asked curiously in a low voice beside him. “No matter how you think about it, he should be the president named Phoenix.” Merlin answered. “He is Phoenix.” Alice furrowed her brows, looking at the boy engulfed in flames, feeling a formidable pressure. “I never imagined that the president of the Dark Guild would be an Ancient God.” Merlin continued in a speculative tone, “His aura is extremely similar to that of an Ancient God, but his pressure is considerably weaker; it seems he is easier to handle than I imagined.” “Strictly speaking, I am not an Ancient God; I am a descendant of an Ancient God. My father is the immortal bird that once perched atop the World Tree, Vedfolnir, who overlooks all beings and knows all things; I am his heir.” Erikson introduced himself calmly. “Descendant of an Ancient God?” Merlin seemed to have heard this somewhere, like it was Little John's father mistakenly thinking he was a descendant of an Ancient God; turns out such a thing really exists? “I know you, Merlin, the youngest monarch of the demon race, and you, Alice Miss, a vessel meant to carry a certain Ancient God's soul.” Erikson said with a meaningful tone. “???” Alice's mind filled with question marks, not understanding what Erikson meant; could he be hinting that she was once the sacrifice designated by the black dragon? “You know quite a lot,” Merlin said with a sneer. “Of course, this is an inherited talent; as long as you stand high enough, everything will be within your sight.” Erikson smiled confidently. “You must know that you are about to die under my blade, right?” Merlin narrowed his eyes, speaking sternly, “You dare to harbor designs against me? Your courage is not ordinary; you will pay the price for this.” “Are you lying? It's not because you're angry about me taking your war magic ring, but because you came abandoning the Philosopher's Stone.” Erikson said with a smile. “I don't deny it; this is a wish opportunity, who could stay calm?” Merlin did not conceal his excitement; he had been moved, perhaps he could wish to touch the heart curse and thereafter be infallible. “No, I am striving to create an absolutely equal world, an ideal beneficial to all; I hope you will cooperate with me.” Erikson painted a grand pie in front of the two. “At a time like this, are you still putting on an act? Your lofty ideal is just a trick to fool children; drop the pretense, it's meaningless.” Merlin frowned. “Don't treat us as foolish; in the face of great temptation, there is no one without selfish motives.” Alice shouted loudly. “Indeed, you've been found out? Even someone like Alice Miss can't be fooled; I've failed miserably.” Erikson sighed. “What are you saying?!” Alice gritted her teeth in anger, is he saying she's easy to fool? Absurd! “It's not wrong what he's saying.” Merlin nodded solemnly. “Merlin! Alice glared at Merlin, dissatisfied. “Talking is useless; since you refuse to hand over the Philosopher's Stone, then don't blame us for being impolite.” Merlin reached toward his waist for the demon sword Banri Garan. “Just with you lot wanting to lay hands on the Philosopher's Stone, don't joke—” As his words fell, Erikson suddenly flung his arms wide, a flame like a mountain roar and sea surge rushed forth, instantly engulfing the two tiny figures. Although Erikson is merely a descendant of an Ancient God, his power is by no means weak, surpassing even Vivian in the divine realm by a notch. The raging flames roared without cease; Erikson unleashed full firepower from the start, leaving no need for either side to test the other— “Stop!” Alice activated Freeze Time, entered the Dragon Warrior state, the gears in the Fate Secret Realm halted their turning, everyone except her was encased in ice! Alice swiftly appeared behind Erikson, her slender sword shedding silver light, she thrust out dozens of consecutive strikes, turning the enemy into a honeycomb! After Freeze Time ended, Erikson's body instantly burst with countless wounds, blood gushing incessantly, yet Alice's swordsmanship failed to kill him. “Tch! A troublesome woman!” “He's still not dead?!” Alice exclaimed in surprise; normally, if an enemy's heart is pierced, they should be cold. “Alice, dodge!” Merlin bellowed, swiftly unleashing a draw‑cut slash; murderous sword aura exploded, rumbling toward Erikson. Alice's vibrating steel dragon wings barely managed to evade; the terrifying murderous sword aura almost grazed her body, directly tearing Erikson into fragments! “What the heck? Even easier than I imagined.” Merlin sheathed the demon sword Banri Garan. “Will there be any mishap?” Alice likewise felt something off. “Hahahaha” A wild, unrestrained laugh rang out; flames gathered in the air, gradually forming a phoenix, the temperature in the Fate Secret Realm rose again! Erikson completely lost his human form, turning entirely into a flame‑composed phoenix, his scarlet eyes gazing down at Merlin and Alice— “Foolish! You cannot kill me! I am a phoenix!” “No matter what method you use to kill me, I can absorb your power, reborn countless times from ashes, growing ever stronger.” “Thank you for the grand gift you sent my way, Merlin! Your draw‑cut technique is a great supplement for me!” “I feel fantastic now; surging power boils constantly within my body, you can no longer defeat me!” “What kind of bizarre ability is this?!” Alice felt a bead of cold sweat slide down her forehead; this seems like an invincible position! “Who said I just now used my full strength? I occasionally hold back a bit.” Merlin gripped the second sword at his waist, namely the Godslayer Sword Mistletin— “In the past, you would have given me a headache.” “But now, at most it will take a little extra effort—”

title: Chapter 18 — The Prophecy Comes True
content:
Chapter 18 — The Prophecy Comes True

Volume 38 · Chapter 18

“Alice! Cover me!”

Merlin sprang to his feet in an instant and bolted toward the sky at blinding speed, where Erikson had transformed into a fiery phoenix.

Alice unleashed her Great Snow Mountain Sword Art, and rivers of pale golden ice swords flooded forward like a tide before soaring skyward!

“What reckless foolishness!”

Erikson vibrated his flameshaped wings, unleashing the oppressive pressure of the Divine Realm and forming a barrier of raging fire!

The ice swords were like mud calves entering the sea; nearly every single one melted away before they could even approach the flame barrier.

Just as Erikson was about to counterattack, he noticed a faint, barely discernible figure flickering before the stone gate in the Destiny Secret Realm—

Loki! Did this rat also seize the opportunity to slip in?

Even a lowly pirate’s son dares to covet what’s mine. Preposterous!

Wait… Loki’s wish.

I see. How much ambition could a man blinded by hatred possibly have?

Perhaps I’ll do him a favor on this one and draw those two’s attention for him.

Just don’t let me down, Loki.

Erikson withdrew his gaze and danced through the air, raining down a skyfull of fire to pull Merlin and Alice’s attention entirely onto himself.

“So… is behind this stone gate the abode of the Three Goddesses of Fate?”

Loki stood before the massive stone gate, gazing up at its mysterious patterns with hunger in his heart, and gently touched the surface with his finger.

A heavy aura of antiquity washed over him, and the mottled marks covering its surface seemed to recount tales of when the world was still chaos.

Rumbles echoed as the stone gate slowly creaked open a narrow fissure just wide enough for him to squeeze through, as if welcoming him?

Loki was stunned. He had assumed a Philosopher’s Stone was required to open it. Had he overthought things?

So the Philosopher’s Stone was only needed to enter the Destiny Secret Realm and had nothing to do with this gate at all.

Loki slowly turned around and wore a longfamiliar smile before resolutely stepping inside—

“Lucifer III, the hour has come for you to pay blood for blood.”

Pitch black beyond the stone gate—terribly silent, with only Loki’s nervous breathing.

Cold sweat beaded on his forehead as he had no idea where on earth he was.

Suddenly, candles ignited one by one, spiraling upward in rings until it felt as though he stood among a swarm of fireflies!

Before Loki appeared three grand, pitchblack thrones, each occupied by a profoundly aged female giant!

Unlike the youthful figures depicted on this stone gate, their backs were hunched as if their spines might snap at any moment.

Even stooped, the three giantesses towered well over a hundred and fifty feet tall; humans were utterly insignificant before them.

Their garments were equally strange, resembling the shamans of ancient tribes, their wrists and necks hung with jumbled trinkets, and pitchblack robes completely concealed their faces.

Loki was paralyzed, gazing up at the three giantesses without daring to breathe. Could these be the legendary Three Goddesses of Fate!?!

“That’s right. We are the three goddesses who weave the destinies of all living beings, embodying the will of the world.”

The three giantesses did not move their lips, yet their voices appeared from nowhere, carrying a triple reverberation that constantly echoed through the pitchblack space.

“Huh!” Loki widened his eyes in shock. I didn’t say anything out loud. How do they know what I’m thinking?

The Three Goddesses of Fate: “There is nothing strange about that, Loki.”

“?” Loki nervously swallowed, his mind churning with disbelief. They even know my name!?!

The Three Goddesses of Fate: “We understand every person’s destiny. Yours was woven by us according to the world’s will.”

“Wh… what is my destiny?” Loki summoned his courage to ask.

The Three Goddesses of Fate: “We are under no obligation to answer your questions, little one.”

“Tch!” Loki grit his teeth and said heatedly, “I demand you grant my wish! You should be able to, right?”

The Three Goddesses of Fate: “Of course. That is our work. We do not refuse anyone who comes here. Though fate has already been arranged by the will of the world, those who reach this place are granted the chance to take control of their own destinies.”

“Then bring it on!” Loki clenched his fists, steeling himself.

The Three Goddesses of Fate: “However, you do not possess a Philosopher’s Stone. If you make a wish without one, the price will be your life. Are you truly ready for that?”

“My life!?!

Loki was taken aback. He had no idea about this. He lowered his head and pondered deeply, his expression wavering.

To avenge my father… at the cost of my life?

If I refuse, I’m afraid I’ll never get another chance at revenge!

The mighty Lucifer III cannot be defeated by someone like me.

What if I choose to resurrect my father instead? No! I’d still die, and we still wouldn’t be reunited!

We’ve already been crippled and broken by Lucifer III’s persecution. We must make him suffer punishment—even if it means we all go to hell together!

Loki gritted his teeth. He had no other choice. The hesitation on his face vanished, and he lifted his head to respond loudly.

“I’m ready! Please fulfill my wish!”

As soon as his words fell, light flickered before Loki, and an ancient, pitchblack crown materialized, intricately carved with exquisite patterns that resembled ancient runes.

On the inside of the crown, three lines of text were carved. Clearly, Loki was not the first to request wearing the crown—

“I wish for myself to become overwhelmingly powerful, so that no one in this world can ever defeat me.”

“I wish to control all life and creation, so that, to fulfill my sister’s wish, humble humanity may flourish.”

“I wish to take hold of the souls of all things. I will not allow foolish Maria to dominate alone. Only I am the one humanity should worship!”

From top to bottom, the three wishes were respectively those of Odin, Maria, and Satan when they wore the crown, forever inscribed on its interior.

Loki was honored to be the fourth person about to wear the crown. Unfortunately, without a Philosopher’s Stone, he was destined to die after making his wish.

He examined the words inside the crown and felt a hint of puzzlement. Raising his head, he looked toward the three goddesses, hoping for answers.

The Three Goddesses of Fate: “These are the wishes granted to those who came before. The wishes of successors cannot be the same.”

“Ah… I see.”

Loki stared at the pitchblack crown in his hands, licked his dry lips, and, trembling all over, placed it upon his head. The bandages before his eyes fell away, revealing the serpentlike Gorgon eye of Medusa—

Lucifer III, you’ll never guess it, right? The one who successfully kills you will be me!

Loki, the pirate’s son! Remember this! This is the price you must pay for killing my father!

Blood debt repaid in blood!

“Merlin Lusifir—let us go to hell together!”

The Elven King’s prophecy had finally come true at this very moment!

title: Chapter 19 — The Arrival
content:
Chapter 19 — The Arrival

Volume 38 · Chapter 19

# 来临 / Coming

Merlin and Alice were locked in combat with Ericson and had not noticed that the inconspicuous Lodgere had already walked into that mysterious stone door.

Ericson was calculating in his heart that if Lodgere could make his wish quickly and eliminate the troublesome Merlin, then the remaining Alice would be no match for him at all.

"It's useless! No matter how many times you kill me, it will only make me stronger!"

In his phoenix form, Ericson swung his flames of the wings, instantly stirring up a fierce firestorm!

Countless golden ice swords formed a torrent, constantly assaulting the flames, but they struggled to break through Ericson's defense.

"Tch! Can't do it?" Alice grit her teeth, unable to deal any substantial damage to Ericson.

"Vanish!" Merlin had taken the opportunity to close in on Ericson, and without any hesitation he drew his blade—

Mistilteinn flashed with brilliant silver light, its sharp aura striking terror into all who felt it!

Ericson was split cleanly in two right there on the spot, completely unable to withstand a single strike from Merlin!

"Useless. Useless, useless! I can—ugh!?"

Ericson still wanted to be reborn a second time from the ashes, but he suddenly discovered that his resurrection ability could not be used at all, completely sealed away.

"It's over." Merlin landed back on the ground and slowly sheathed Mistilteinn.

"Impossible!" Ericson's eyes widened in horror, his body swelling continuously until it exploded in the sky, never to awaken again from the ashes.

Suddenly, Merlin's consciousness began to blur, his eyes losing their luster, his body swaying unsteadily for a few moments before he collapsed onto the ground.

Lodgere's wish had been fulfilled. Merlin's death came without any warning, as if his very life had been stripped away in an instant.

"Merlin?" Alice frowned and slowly approached Merlin's side, thinking he was pulling a prank. "What are you doing?"

Merlin gave no answer; the entire person was cold and lifeless.

"Stop joking around like this. Is this funny?" Alice put her hands on her hips and continued, "You don't really think I'd fall for that, do you?"

"Merlin" still gave no answer whatsoever, lying on the ground like a dead object.

At that moment, Alice finally realized something was wrong. She hurriedly squatted down, lifted Merlin, and checked his condition—only to find that his heartbeat had completely stopped. This made her so anxious that she began to cry.

"Merlin! Merlin, wake up! Don't scare me like this!"

"Don't leave me..."

Alice kept shaking Merlin, but the Merlin whose life had been deprived showed absolutely no reaction. Her eyes turned red, her face ashen—

What happened? That guy earlier shouldn't have been able to kill Merlin. Who actually did this?

For someone to suddenly die out of nowhere—this method was very much like some sort of curse or dark magic.

Alice looked around and her gaze fell upon that ancient stone door, where she noticed a gap that had opened at some unknown time. Inside, there seemed to be some kind of magical power, constantly tempting her.

"Could it be—"

When Merlin opened his eyes again, the realm of fate had already disappeared, and he was still in the chamber of the obelisk.

Everything around him was extraordinarily quiet, as though all events had already come to an end. He couldn't figure out what he had experienced.

He only knew that after killing Ericson, the world around him had spun wildly, and then in an instant he was staring at the chamber ceiling.

"What's going on?"

Merlin slowly got up, feeling waves of pain in his head. He slowly climbed to his feet and patted off some dust from his clothes.

After surveying the area, he discovered that the alchemy circle that had been here before had vanished, and both Lodgere and Alice were lying motionless on the ground.

"Who is this guy?"

Merlin walked over to Lodgere and remembered who he was—wasn't he the pirate who had originally wanted to kidnap Helena to use as a bargaining chip?

He never expected that this guy was also a member of the dark guild Phoenix. Merlin had thought the two of them belonged to completely different factions.

After a quick inspection, Merlin realized that Lodgere was already dead, yet there were no wounds on his body at all, which looked very strange.

"How did he die?"

Merlin frowned tightly, unable to come up with an answer, so he had no choice but to go to Alice's side and prepare to wake her up to return to Rexem.

It was regrettable that this trip had yielded no results at all. He had originally hoped to walk through that stone door and see what secrets lay behind it.

Unfortunately, he had inexplicably fainted, and even the realm of fate had vanished without a trace.

Merlin squatted down and poked Alice's cheek with his finger, noticing that her body felt somewhat cold.

"Alice, wake up. Alice, we should head back."

Alice lay motionless on the ground, with tear marks still lingering at the corners of her eyes. She looked extremely peculiar.

"Alright then, is this a prank? If so, I won't hold back."

Merlin reached his hand toward Alice's waist, planning to torment her with tickling. He refused to believe she could still pretend to be dead in front of him.

He knew this was something Alice found unbearable. Every time he touched one side of her waist, Alice would laugh uncontrollably.

Merlin laughed as he tickled Alice's waist, but discovered she had no reaction at all, like a dead person. This was thoroughly abnormal.

"Alice?"

Merlin's expression became alert. He patted Alice's cheek with his hand and then checked for her breath.

He suddenly discovered she was no longer breathing at all. Merlin's face instantly changed, his heart convulsing uncontrollably—

"Damn it!!!"

Inside the secret basement of the Holy City Temple.

Over the past three years, Pope Georg had begun to secretly alter the church's beliefs, shifting from worshipping Mary to revering Satan, the ruler of Hell.

In order to help Satan take control of the mortal world as soon as possible and get everyone to accept the worship of the Lord of Hell, Georg wanted to request the aid of Hell.

Georg hoped that Satan could send the other apostles from Hell to the mortal realm to help him accomplish his plans.

Unfortunately, the gates of Hell were very difficult to open, and there were numerous restrictions on opening them, so Georg's wishes could never be realized.

However, half a year ago, a mysterious person came knocking, and Georg's wish finally became achievable—

He was the former kingdom's prince, Copeland.

After escaping from the prison in Britain, Copeland had been searching for apostles active in the mortal realm, hoping to borrow the apostles' power to help him revive the former kingdom.

Copeland had seen apostles long before. When he was young, he personally witnessed his father forging a contract with a hellish apostle, successfully establishing the powerful former kingdom.

Therefore, Copeland was very familiar with the aura of apostles. As long as he could face them in person, he could detect the nauseating stench of the undead emanating from them.

Half a year ago, Copeland came to the Holy City to evade pursuit from the kingdom of Britain. This was a sacred religious site, and the kingdom's soldiers dared not act recklessly here.

By chance, Copeland saw Pope Georg giving a speech during a festival, and he immediately detected the scent on the other person—this was an apostle from Hell.

Copeland felt utterly shocked. Was the mortal realm's spokesman who worshipped the Goddess of Light actually a creature of Hell?

So Copeland secretly contacted Pope Georg, and the two hit it off immediately, deciding to cooperate—

Copeland knew how to open the doors between the mortal world and Hell, allowing a large number of hellish apostles to flood into the mortal realm.

And Pope Georg also promised that as long as he unified the faith of the mortal world, reviving the former kingdom would be a simple matter of minutes.

After six months of preparation, a massive ancient door appeared at the center of the chamber—

The gate to Hell that had been destroyed by Merlin had been successfully repaired.

Tonight was the moment when the apostles of Hell would descend.

title: Chapter 20 — Hell's Messengers
content:
Chapter 20 — Hell's Messengers

Volume 38 · Chapter 20

“Is it possible to summon even the great i ] of Hell? Pope Jiogen examined the gate carved with grim skulls, which looked especially eerie, with faint wails drifting from within. He was unsure whether he could pass through this gate to summon Hell's powerful apostles to the mortal world to aid him in accomplishing the grand task of unifying faith. “Don’t worry, this is a secret method passed down in our family; originally it was used to summon the Hell Burning Legion, so summoning an apostle should certainly be possible.” Kopofel said confidently; besides him, probably no one knows how to connect the mortal world and Hell, unless one thoroughly studies the former kingdom's canon. “Your Holiness, please don’t forget what you promised me: help me destroy Britain and revive my kingdom. “I will not go back on my word; as long as the apostles descend to the mortal world and completely destroy the faith left by the Goddess, reviving your kingdom will not be difficult.” Pope Jiogen paused, then continued, “We are all serving the great Satan; as long as we unify people’s faith, the world order will change—I will oversee religion, and you will become the king of the new world. Kopofel’s eyes were full of anticipation; even if this is the big pie Jiogen drew, it still has enough appeal, “Then I’ll first thank you for your generosity.” “No need.” Pope Jiogen waved his hand, sighing, “This world no longer needs Maria’s protection; stingy as she is, she gives nothing to humanity, only sits high in heaven looking down on our suffering. Satan can give what she never can. “You’re right.” Kopofel nodded deeply, lowering his voice, “Please begin calling the apostles; I think they’re ready.” Pope Jiogen slowly approached the great “] and muttered the strange incantation; the wails of the resentful spirits inside grew fiercer! Boom boom boom, the Hell’s gate began to tremble, slowly opening to reveal a bottomless black vortex, as if connecting to the world of the dead. “Come forth! Apostles of Hell, to fulfill the great Satan’s dream, I need you to contribute your power! The aura of the undead grew denser; Kopofel could barely keep his eyes open, feeling several powerful pressures. “This pressure is even more terrifying than the entire Hell legion combined! Black mist continually poured out from the Hell’s gate], quickly filling the secret chamber and rapidly spreading outward. Before long it had spread over half of the holy city; people screamed in terror and fled, but could not escape death’s fate! Within the black mist countless resentful spirits flickered, madly devouring human souls; the entire holy city had become a banquet for the resentful spirits! Suddenly! Several silhouettes flickered within the gate; they had no flesh, only stark white bones, with the fire of the undead flashing endlessly in their black eye sockets— 1、V、VI、V- Four apostles descended, slowly walking out from the Hell’s gate, many of whom were familiar opponents of Merlin. Seventh Apostle VII, Dracula, after death submitted to Satan and gained rebirth. Sixth Apostle VI, Ashmodor, King of the Dark Elves, decided to betray his soul in order to awaken once more. Fifth Apostle V, the alchemist Democritus, thanks to his excellent alchemical talent, was highly valued by Satan. First Apostle, the original Pride Demon Lord Mephistopheles, to take revenge on the Goddess of Light, stood on Hell’s side. All Hell’s apostles have become undead, favored by Satan, their power far greater than in life—this is the grace of the Hell’s ruler. Pope Jiogen is the last Eighth Apostle VlI, Hassan Sabah is the Second Apostle JI, while the Third and Fourth Apostles did not appear. Kopofel gazed at the throng of undead, swallowing nervously, able to feel their immense power; if they could assist, unifying faith would not be difficult. Together they could easily destroy every human kingdom, leaving only those willing to serve Satan to build a new world of faith in the undead. Especially the apostle before him, Kopofel felt his heart pound; that surging immense pressure was even more terrifying than the combined pressure of the other apostles! “Welcome, fellow brethren, thank you for answering the call.” Pope Jiogen paused, then continued, “We are all loyal servants of Satan, so we must strive for our shared ideal; next I need your assistance to drive out the Goddess Maria and establish the great Satan as the sole faith! “Idiot, we didn’t come to help you; we have other missions.” Dracula said gloomily. “Exactly, unifying faith is not the top priority now; we must first kill Merlin Lucifer.” Ashmodor stated his purpose. “Merlin? ” Pope Jiogen wondered in his heart why Hell would target Vivian’s son, so he asked, “Is there a reason?” “Satan’s Majesty is about to hold a wedding; to ensure the ceremony proceeds smoothly, Merlin Lucifer must be eliminated.” Democritus replied. “Satan’s Majesty is getting married? I didn’t know—who is it?” Pope Jiogen looked puzzled; the exalted ruler of Hell, who has he taken a liking to? “Eighth Apostle, you only need to fulfill the task assigned by His Majesty in the mortal world; no need to inquire about other matters.” Ashmodor said in a reproachful tone. “I understand.” Pope Jiogen felt a cold sweat trickle down his forehead; he could not afford to offend anyone here. “Having us come to eliminate Merlin is truly picking the right people.” Democritus said excitedly. “Yeah, I’ve dreamed of killing this guy; otherwise my hatred would never fade.” Dracula clenched his bony hand. “This is Satan’s Majesty’s chance for us to take revenge! Nothing compares to this precious gift.” Ashmodor’s ghostly fire flickered as he looked at the silent figure ahead, “First‑Apostle, am I right?” Mephistopheles arrived and said nothing; no one knows what this once‑most‑powerful Demon Lord is thinking. “Mephistopheles, the one you must kill next is your grandson—won’t you hold back?” Ashmodor said meaningfully, “If you can’t bring yourself to do it, we can help.” The other apostles turned to Mephistopheles, this silent First Apostle is the strongest, yet his thoughts are inscrutable. Kopofel looked at the skeletal figure with horns on its head, his heart leapt— It is Mephistopheles! The legendary strongest swordsman of the demon race? I never imagined he too had become a Hell’s apostle! Having him deal with my descendant—would that be a problem? PSI Will it be soon? I think it’s fine. This long‑web novel of this word count should about finish. I like to wrap things up when they’re good; being able to finish now is a good thing. Continuing would also be possible, but the story would surely lack excitement, like an old woman’s shoe‑cloth. As I write, readers would leave, making it pointless. If readers drift away, my new book would have no one to look at it. If everyone knows I’m a big water‑bag, my career would be over.

title: Chapter 21 — Acting Alone (Monthly Ticket Extra)
content:
Chapter 21 — Acting Alone (Monthly Ticket Extra)

Volume 38 · Chapter 21

Are you talking to me, the demon race leader who defies the heavens? Mephistopheles' azure flames in his eyes flickered slightly, uttering a bewildered question. “So what? We've all become hell's lackeys, still clinging to the glory before death? How laughable~” Asmoday sneered. “You've got guts, pointy-eared biped.” Mephistopheles said in a low voice. “What did you say? If you hadn't become an apostle early, I would have feared you.” Asmoday's tone turned hostile. Pope Jiogen sensed the atmosphere was off, quickly stepped in as a mediator, smiling. “Come on, don't we share a common goal? Let's set aside our prejudices and unite—how great would that be?” “This old geezer doesn't seem to welcome us much.” Asmoday said gloomily. “Yeah, the first apostle seems very attached to his former status.” Democritus said sarcastically. “Is the demon lord above us? We're all just Satan's dogs anyway.” Dracula whispered quietly. Coppefell's face looked grim, thinking it's over; these guys are all apostles but they can't seem to cooperate. Can my dream of reviving the old kingdom really come true? “Dogs?” Mephistopheles raised his head, slowly looking at his companions behind him, “You are indeed dogs, but I am not.” “Don't argue, stay united, First Apostle, don't provoke the other apostles—maybe you still need help.” Pope Jiogen said humbly. “Are you saying I, the demon king, need your help?” Mephistopheles used his ancestral skill, tilting his head to mock. “, not, I mean just in case, we'll inevitably run into some trouble.” Pope Jiogen grew less confident, faintly feeling this first apostle is not to be provoked. Suddenly, Mephistopheles lunged, drew the bone dagger from his waist, and slashed at everyone present!—— Dagger! Pope Jiogen, Coppefell, and the other apostles were all chopped into pieces, dying instantly! Mephistopheles slowly retracted the bone dagger, looked down at the severed limbs and carnage, and said meaningfully: “True demon lords walk alone, needing no one's help—you're insulting me.” Asmoday's soul fire burned weakly, still clinging to life on the ground, he cursed angrily. “Foolish Mephistopheles! You dare slash your blade at fellow apostles, acting so recklessly—Satan Majesty will never forgive you!” “Too bad, I've never feared Satan; in my eyes he's forever that hesitant opportunist.” As soon as he finished, Mephistopheles stomped out Asmoday's soul fire with his foot, sending the dark elf king to die once more. Silence returned to the secret chamber, but outside the human screams never ceased. After forcibly opening the gates of Hell, the once-prosperous holy city has become a mortal purgatory. Mephistopheles alone walked toward the exit of the secret chamber, muttering to himself: “Dealing with Merlin, I alone am enough—you're just a burden.” Rexelum, Merlin brought Alice's corpse back, and it quickly became known to the other guild members. They all came to Merlin's house to check, finding Alice's body icy cold, nobody willing to believe it. Chris's eyes swelled from crying, desperately using her rudimentary healing to pour life force into her mother's body, but it had no effect. Alice wasn't wounded; she had lost her soul—something no healing can fix. In the yard, Merlin sat on the steps by the door, hearing Chris's sobs echo from inside, his heart sank to the depths, never before feeling such despair. Merlin's expression now was like a stone statue, devoid of any ripple; he cannot shed tears, cannot show the slightest panic, cannot reveal any weakness. Deep down Merlin knows he is his daughter's only reliance; if he breaks down, what will become of Chris? She's still so young. Lin that . “Arnold didn't know what to say, only able to comfort: “Grieve and move on.” Merlin suddenly lifted his head, anger nearly bursting from his eyes, “What are you saying? Alice isn't dead.” “Uh! ” Hebnov was startled, his mouth naturally clumsy, now even more at a loss for words, “I didn't mean that.” “Yeah, what are you saying? Alice, she's still alive!” Rosetti beside him frantically gestured to her husband, hinting he should say Alice lives forever in everyone's hearts. “Ah right! Alice is just unconscious now, she'll wake up sooner or later, right, Merlin?” Hobbes beside him was anxious to death, thinking given Merlin's state, who knows what impulsive thing he might do—if oil catches fire, the whole British Kingdom might have to follow him to the grave! “I will save Alice, don't worry everyone.” Merlin said seriously, knowing they meant no harm, but he won't easily believe Alice just left like that. “Mr. Merlin.” Lucia lowered her head, speaking softly, “I understand your feelings, but the dead cannot be resurrected.” “Lucia!” Chairman Taylor sternly rebuked, “At times like this don't point out reality—your granddaughter can't read the room!” “What's wrong with me? Speaking the truth won't do, are we supposed to let people live in a dream, never emerge from the shadows?” Lucia retorted angrily, feeling she's not wrong; Alice's death also grieved her, losing a friend to talk with, but Merlin will eventually have to accept this reality—dwelling in kind lies achieves nothing. Lucia doesn't want to lose Alice and fall back into her former decadent lifestyle; she's finally shaken off her bad habits, becoming a responsible father. So Lucia believes Merlin has accepted reality, shouldn't wallow in self-pity after losing his wife, shouldn't ignore others, and should also consider little Chris's thoughts. Chairman Taylor, angered by his granddaughter's low EQ, raised his cane and tapped her head twice, “No nonsense at times like this.” Lucia covered her head, looking wronged, pressed her lips shut, feeling everyone here except her are bad people. “Lord Merlin, Lucia meant no harm, please don't take it to heart.” Chairman Taylor sincerely apologized. “It's fine.” Merlin shook his head, knowing Lucia is always blunt, that straightforwardness is also good. The silent Da Vinci suddenly spoke, “Actually, Miss Alice can still be saved.” Everyone looked at Da Vinci with shocked eyes, thinking resurrection basically impossible, yet a sliver of hope rose— “You're not joking, right, Da Vinci!” z( A° I))

title: Chapter 22 — Raphael
content:
Chapter 22 — Raphael

Volume 38 · Chapter 22

"I never like joking." Da Vinci said with a serious face, "Miss Alice's cause of death is very strange, and it has a great relation to the Fate Secret Realm, so I can make a bold guess: Miss Alice very likely made a wish to the Three Goddesses of Fate without the Philosopher's Stone, so the price should be her life." "Like the Three Goddesses granting a wish?" Merlin lowered his head, feeling this was possible, "The benevolent king named Sarit indeed said such a thing." "I don't know what wish Miss Alice made, but it must be very important, otherwise she wouldn't risk making a wish to the Three Goddesses without the Philosopher's Stone." Da Vinci said in a speculative tone. "Could it be related to another person?" Merlin suddenly recalled another corpse, feeling things became much clearer. "Another person?" Da Vinci asked doubtfully. "It's a man named Lochiri; after I woke up I also found his corpse, just like Alice, with no wounds, dying mysteriously." Merlin answered truthfully. Hobbs' face suddenly changed, his eyes darted, he lowered his head heavily, as if thinking of something? Hearing the name "Lochiri", others became doubtful, they had never heard of this person. "Could it be that two people made wishes before the Three Goddesses? We can't confirm this for now." Da Vinci furrowed her brow, then shifted tone, "However, Miss Alice can still be saved, as long as we obtain the Philosopher's Stone and reopen the Fate Secret Realm, we can do it, but unfortunately I don't know how to set up the alchemy array to summon the Three Goddesses, nor the Philosopher's Stone." "Do you mean this?" Merlin suddenly took out a red gemstone and handed it to Da Vinci, "This is what I found in Alice's palm." Da Vinci widened her eyes, examining the red gemstone closely, her hands trembling a bit, but she quickly calmed down, "This is a fake Philosopher's Stone, Mr. Merlin." "Fake?!" Merlin was startled, thinking that because this stone is fake, Alice sacrificed her life to make a wish to the Three Goddesses? "Although it's fake, it's already very close to the genuine article; this level of alchemical technology is astonishing, as far as I know, only my senior brother can achieve this." Da Vinci recalled Flamel. "Flamel?" Merlin frowned. "Yes, he's a madman obsessed with alchemy; I believe he might eventually create a true Philosopher's Stone." Da Vinci, although not particularly fond of Flamel, admired his talent. "I think he's already dead; Phoenix killed all the other members to seize the Philosopher's Stone." Merlin sighed, feeling deeply disappointed. Da Vinci was at a loss, now she truly had no way. The hope that had barely been ignited was extinguished again; Merlin sighed, feeling vexed. "Everyone go back, I'll think of a way." Everyone looked at each other and could only silently leave; at this time Merlin needed to calm down. Hobbs gave Merlin a meaningful glance, thinking it was because of me? I didn't expect that pirate's son to actually manage it; things have already exceeded my expectations. Merlin lowered his head, veins bulging on his hand, looking shocking; at this moment he was extremely furious, but didn't show it in front of others— He didn't hate the enemy, but hated his own inadequacy. No matter how strong, he couldn't even protect his own wife, only able to sit here helplessly. In the room, Chris's crying never ceased, continuously transferring life force to her mother. The little one was already exhausted; if this continues, her strength will be drained and her body will also deteriorate.
