The landlady couldn't bear it any longer, saying softly, "Chris, that's enough, it's useless." "No! I want to wake Mom, I don't want Mom to leave me!" Chris stubbornly replied, rubbing her small face against her mother, hoping she could open her eyes. "Your mother will wake up, believe me, if she sees you like this, she definitely won't be happy." The landlady said gently. "No! You're all liars! I will never believe you again!" Chris clenched her small mouth, tears like broken beads falling onto her mother. Merlin returned from outside, gently patted his daughter's shoulder and said softly, "Enough, Chris, Dad will think of a way." Chris excitedly turned her head, loudly questioning, "Mom will definitely come back, right? Not like the grandmothers who can only see her in dreams? Mom is still alive, right?" Seeing his daughter crying tears, Merlin felt as if his chest had been struck by a hammer, his whole body trembled once, making it hard to breathe. Merlin was speechless, his mind went blank, completely unaware how to answer his daughter's question, only able to stay silent. He finally understood how hard it was for Alice to raise a child alone; having been away for three years, Alice probably also didn't know how to answer her daughter's question. Late at night. Chris finally fell asleep from exhaustion, crawling into her mother's blanket, like a little koala hugging Alice's cold corpse. Merlin sat beside her, face grim and silent, got up to cover her with a blanket, intending to go ask Da Vinci about the Fate Secret Realm. But suddenly the room door opened, the landlady entered holding an oil lamp, glanced at the sleeping Chris, and said softly— "Mr. Merlin, could you step out for a moment? I have something I want to say." The two went outside; the landlady leisurely placed the oil lamp beside them, unsure where to start? Merlin looked at this elderly old man, puzzled about what she wanted to say, couldn't help but ask first. "You're looking for me, what's the matter?" "Can't I just come see you if there's nothing wrong? Young Demon Lord." The landlady's smile held deep meaning. "!! ?" Merlin's whole body jolted, startled into opening his mouth but unable to speak. "Don't be so surprised, actually I've known all along." The landlady pointed at Merlin's waist at the demon sword Banri Garan, continuing, "I've seen this thing before, when it was worn by Mephistopheles; you must be the current First Demon Lord, right?" This Merlin lowered his gaze to his own demon sword Banri Garan, thinking that those who can recognize this are old-timers who have had contact with the demon race. So Merlin quickly composed his shocked expression, his demeanor turned much more serious, he lowered his voice and asked, "So who are you?" "Now I'm just an old woman about to return to the earth, but before I was one of the Seven Great Holy Spirits, representing myself as Raphael."

title: Chapter 23 — Container (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 23 — Container (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 38 · Chapter 23

The heavenly realm, created by the chief god Maria, is a magnificent palace floating above white clouds, where the life she created resides. It is the homeland of the holy spirits, a pure land that no one is allowed to violate. After the ancient holy war ended, the surviving holy spirits returned to the heavenly realm; although they failed to completely annihilate the demon race, they dealt a heavy blow to the enemy. At the moment when the vast majority of holy spirits were celebrating the victory, one holy spirit was unhappy and considered the war meaningless—this was Raphael. After returning to the heavenly realm, Raphael began proclaiming that no matter how many holy spirits died in this war, the lofty goddess would not even glance at them; this was purely a quarrel mixed with personal grudges. It seemed that after being slapped by Michael, Raphael felt no fear, but instead intensified his accusations against the goddess's various sins, declaring that waging war was not something the ruler of the heavenly realm should do. The piercing voice finally reached the ears of Goddess Maria, so she specially summoned Raphael to ask what exactly dissatisfied her. Michael and Uriel pressed Raphael together as they came to the main hall of the heavenly realm, preparing to punish him for his nonsense—Maria lay in a rocking chair, not turning her head, fully focused on reading a book, and coldly asked, 'Raphael, I heard you are dissatisfied with me lately; is that true?' Raphael, pressed to the ground, angrily lifted his head, gritted his teeth, and said, 'Exactly! I am very dissatisfied with you!' 'Why? What wrong have I done?' Maria asked, her back to Raphael. 'You should not have launched the holy war! The heavenly realm should not interfere in mortal affairs! That place has nothing to do with us!' Raphael said solemnly. 'I was once the leader of humanity, and now I have become the chief god; what is wrong with leading humanity toward prosperity?' Maria countered. 'Because you are the chief god, you should not interfere in the mortal world! The mortal world does not belong solely to humanity but also to countless other races; you cannot change the course of history according to your own preferences!' Raphael gritted his teeth and said earnestly, 'You are not only the leader of humanity, but also the leader of all life in the mortal world! Forced interference goes against the will of the world! One day you will pay for this; the former chief god Odin is a precedent!' Michael and Uriel, hearing Raphael's words, were somewhat moved and indeed thought she was right, but the goddess is the ruler of the heavenly realm and does not allow others to hold opposing views. 'So what? Leading humanity toward prosperity is my sister's wish; she gave her life for it—are you asking me to betray her?' Maria slowly closed her book, her tone already tinged with anger. Raphael gave a dry laugh and said with anguish, 'Again it's your sister—so many holy spirits died for you in the war, are they not worth more than your sister's single wish?' Maria fell silent for a moment, then replied in a low voice, 'I do not deny that I am your creator; your lives naturally belong to me.' Michael and Uriel bowed their heads; this statement was especially piercing, but they lacked the courage to resist and could only remain silent. 'I am deeply disappointed in you; I regret being given life by you.' Raphael furrowed his brow, his heart filled with despair, feeling that Maria's actions might repeat history, ending like Odin's. The divinity bestowed by the three goddesses is less a representation of power and authority and more like a curse—no one will have a good outcome. 'The demon race has long been running amok in the mortal world; they deserve punishment. We are upholding justice and eradicating evil; the fallen holy spirits are honorable warriors who brought light to the mortal world—why do you oppose this?' Maria asked curiously. 'Upholding justice? Eradicating evil?' Raphael gave a helpless smile, 'That is your lie; I know what you are thinking.' 'Oh? Do tell.' Maria showed some interest. 'You hate demons because your sister died at a demon's blade, so your main goal in launching the holy war was to annihilate demons; for your personal grudge, those dead souls are merely the burial offerings of your anger!' Raphael bluntly exposed Maria's noble-sounding lie. Maria said nothing, only her face grew somewhat ugly. 'You established the era of human prosperity, but it is not solely for your sister's wish, is it?' Raphael paused, then continued, 'I know you have been trying to repair your sister's fragmented soul, planning to place it into the womb of some unfortunate mortal woman, waiting for her soul to naturally awaken and regain all memories, so that the age of humanity would be more suitable for your sister's happy life, while other non-human races are merely dispensable background.' The faces of the two holy spirits beside them changed; they looked at Maria, thinking this was something only a madman would do—just for a dead sister, to go to such lengths? 'Great master, is that so?' Michael asked, frowning. Uriel remained silent, never opposing whatever Maria did. Maria remained silent for a long time, wearily leaning back in the rocking chair, and coldly pronounced, 'Lock Raphael up; let him out only when he is willing to repent.' Raphael, who had mustered the courage to reveal the facts, was mercilessly abandoned by Goddess Maria, thrown into a lightless dungeon guarded by a giant holy spirit. No one knows how long passed, but the ashen-faced Raphael finally gave up on Maria completely, angrily tearing out his white holy spirit wings from his back, renouncing his status as a holy spirit. Raphael's blood stained countless holy spirit bones beneath his feet as he stumbled out of the prison and fled that isolated island. 'I will never again serve that selfish, self-serving god, even if he is my creator.' Late at night, the stars sparkled. Merlin listened to the landlady's tale, his heart unable to calm for a long time; it turned out that the holy spirit wings discovered on Alice's trial island came from Raphael, and by chance they also activated the power of the Slender Sword's Bright Lament! 'Having heard all this, you must be bored, right?' the landlady said with a hint of apology. 'No, your resolve to abandon everything fills me with admiration,' Merlin replied, swallowing his saliva, and asked, 'Since you already knew my identity early on, why didn't you make it public?' 'I have given up my holy spirit identity, so naturally I have little connection to the heavenly realm; demons are no longer my enemies.' The landlady paused, then said meaningfully, 'Moreover, I can see that Miss Alice has some affection for you; why would I want to be the villain who tears apart a loving couple?' Merlin nodded; this was his first peaceful conversation with a holy spirit, and he was astonished—these beings could actually communicate, contrary to his belief that they only acted according to the goddess's will. 'Miss Alice, too, is no ordinary person; from the moment I first saw her, I knew everything.' Raphael said softly. Merlin recalled Cain's oil paintings and suddenly had a few guesses. 'Yes, Miss Alice,' the landlady said, looking into Merlin's eyes, revealing an unknown secret— 'She is the soul container of the lucky goddess Teresa.' 'Their souls are symbiotic.'

title: Chapter 24 — Unavoidable
content:
Chapter 24 — Unavoidable

Volume 38 · Chapter 24

Merlin stared wide-eyed, listening to the landlady's words, as if all the puzzles wrapped around his heart had suddenly been solved.

How could Alice have abilities that ordinary people couldn't understand?

How could Alice receive recognition from the divine artifacts of the heavens?

How could Alice's face appear in the painting left by Cain?

It turned out that Alice was the deceased sister of the Goddess of Light, inheriting her appearance and power.

Merlin bowed his head, these words gave him an unprecedented shock. His mind was in chaos, he didn't know where to start thinking.

"Actually, I've been observing Alice, about her being the soul vessel of Theresa, I haven't told anyone, you're the first." The landlady said seriously.

"So Alice is the Goddess Mary's sister?" Merlin frowned, feeling a bit difficult to accept, loving the sister of the number one enemy?

"Yes, but also no." The landlady's answer was ambiguous.

"Ah?" Merlin suddenly felt confused.

"Before Theresa's incomplete soul is repaired and Alice successfully recovers her memories, Alice is just Alice, but if she recovers her memories, then she is Theresa. This is the Goddess's plan." The landlady said slowly.

"She is already the main goddess, reviving her own sister requires such elaborate measures?" Merlin frowned, reviving someone should not be difficult for the main goddess, right?

*Mr. Merlin, it seems you don't understand death deeply enough. Reviving someone is extremely difficult and requires an unimaginable cost. What Satan did is not true revival, but a corpse forcibly awakening. This is not what the Goddess wants. The landlady paused, then continued, "Souls are very fragile things, repairing them requires enough patience. Theresa's soul will gradually repair itself as Alice grows. Maybe one day, a trigger will come, and their souls will merge, Alice will be Theresa, and Theresa will be Alice."

"You mean..." Merlin tried to understand the landlady's words, "Alice will have memories of two lives? They are the same person."

"That's right, in a way, this also counts as a kind of revival." The landlady nodded.

Merlin finally sorted out all the things, tonight he heard too many secrets, he probably couldn't sleep.

Why did you tell me these things?

"Because Alice's personality is much better than her sister's, I think Alice is fine even if she doesn't recover her memories. Moreover, I think the Goddess's plan has failed. Alice is now of this age, and she has not recovered Theresa's memories, and it is unlikely that she will in the future. This is no longer a secret, so I can tell you." The landlady said in a speculative tone.

Merlin bowed his head, his thoughts were simple, Alice was Alice, what did Theresa have to do with him?

"Mr. Merlin, you don't have to be too anxious, I will find a way to wake Alice up." The landlady said seriously.

"You have a way?" Merlin said with great enthusiasm, his heart once again burning with a flicker of hope.

"You can't help, I know you are powerful, but the main goddess is not ordinary, it's not something you can defeat." The landlady looked up at the vast starry sky and whispered, "I will return to heaven and tell the Goddess about this. She will certainly not let Alice be ignored. Hell is Satan's territory, only a main goddess with a divine form can defeat a main goddess. Besides Mary, no one can bring back a soul from hell. As for the vast life force, it needs the water flowing from the roots of the World Tree. Unfortunately, the World Tree has been cut by your demon race's seer. Mary is the only one who can currently control the law of life. No matter what method, bypassing that Goddess who is so high above, is almost impossible."

Merlin frowned, his mind was troubled, at this time he was powerless, but he couldn't refuse the landlady's good intentions.

"That's all I can do."

The next day, a luxurious carriage stopped at Merlin's door, followed by a group of wisteria knights.

This grand procession obviously belonged to the royal troops.

Elizabeth had heard about Alice's incident and rushed to Rekxum at night to pay a personal visit.

After seeing Alice's condition, Elizabeth felt very sorry, followed by endless anxiety and fear.

Alice was an important task to restrain Merlin, now that she's dead, Merlin has become a dangerous factor that cannot be controlled!

Elizabeth looked panicked, thinking about whether to sell the pot to pay off the money she owed Merlin, she couldn't give Merlin a reason to rebel.

The group left Merlin's house, Elizabeth organized her words for a long time, and said softly, "Mr. Merlin, don't be too sad, I will help find a way after I go back."

"Merlin smiled and said calmly, "You don't have to say that, you're not a fool, I know you have your own position as queen, coming to comfort me is already enough."

"Is that so? But I still feel sorry for Alice." Elizabeth was honest.

"I understand, you're a kind person." Merlin nodded.

"Please accept this." Elizabeth took out several valuable crystal cards, looking nervous like she was paying protection money.

Merlin looked at the crystal cards for a while and shook his head, "Queen Elizabeth thinks I really need this? You're looking down on me a bit, don't you know what I'm thinking? Don't worry, I won't do anything that will make you worry."

"It seems I'm too vulgar." Elizabeth awkwardly took back the money and bowed slightly, "Then please take care of yourself, if you need anything, please come to the capital at any time."

Macefield looked on the side with a strange expression, by rights, she should hate Merlin very much, but seeing his wife's death, her heart couldn't help but have a few sympathies.

Macefield, who came with the queen to visit, couldn't say anything for a long time, and was about to leave, so she stammered and comforted.

"Are you okay?"

"I am a warrior,

"Shouldn't you be strong, right?"

title: Chapter 25 — Refusing Kindness
content:
Chapter 25 — Refusing Kindness

Volume 38 · Chapter 25

Merlin watched Mesfield's hesitant expression and laughed, finding the female knight quite amusing.

"You're laughing? Is there something wrong with what I said?"

Mesfield frowned, assuming Merlin was mocking her, and she had even gone so far as to try to comfort the other person.

"There's nothing, I just didn't expect you to comfort others as well." Merlin put away his smile.

"Hmph!" Mesfield scoffed, sarcastically saying, "This is all because of Alice's face, do you think I'll show you any kindness? I'd rather tear you apart!"

"Oh? So that's the case." Merlin hesitated, then said quietly, "Then let's forget about it, don't force yourself, I really dislike sympathy that's given to me."

"You! Hmph!" Mesfield's eyebrows tightened, and she was furious, turning her head and walking away. "Take care of yourself."

After most of them had left the courtyard, the timid Sherry dared to sneak up, looking a bit tense. "Merlin sir."

"What? Do you also want to say something like sympathy to me?" Merlin had a smile that wasn't quite a smile.

"No, Merlin sir, I want to help you." Sherry's gaze became firm, as if she had made a decision. "Please take this."

"Hmm?"

Merlin took the scroll that Sherry secretly handed him, which looked quite old, and was shocked when he opened it—it was one of the three forbidden magic rituals of the elves, the ritual used to revive the dead, the Elven Wail!

Merlin's eyes widened in surprise, looking at Sherry's eyes, and after calming his emotions, he asked, "What do you mean?"

"I want to save Alice, I'm willing to make a sacrifice." Sherry answered in a serious tone.

Merlin frowned, knowing that the Elven Wail ritual was very dangerous, requiring the consumption of a large number of souls and using an elf royal family member as a sacrifice!

This forbidden magic ritual could be said to be extremely inhuman, using countless lives to exchange for the revival of one person.

Who would use such a forbidden ritual, except for ruthless and cruel people?

Merlin didn't expect Sherry to give him something so precious, and even to save Alice, she was willing to sacrifice herself, which was too crazy.

"Sherry, are you crazy? This thing is incredibly valuable, if it falls into the hands of someone with evil intentions, it will definitely cause a disturbance."

"I know, Merlin sir, this thing has no value to me anymore, I'm alone in this world, what's the point of living?" Sherry hesitated, then looked up, saying sincerely, "So I want to do something meaningful in the last moments of my life, you all took my life, so now I should repay you."

"The repayment we want is not this way, Sherry." Merlin shook his head.

"Please take it, Merlin sir, don't you want Alice to open her eyes again? Besides our race's forbidden ritual, do you have any other way to save Alice?" Sherry spoke excitedly, hoping to be successful.

Merlin was speechless, staring at Sherry's eyes, feeling very confused in his heart. Logic told him it was wrong, but the shortcut to saving Alice was right in front of him, could he not be moved?

In fact, Merlin was indeed moved, using the Elven Wail ritual would bring Alice back to him quickly, without having to beg that high and mighty goddess.

However, Merlin hesitated for a long time, and ultimately, reason triumphed over desire, and he returned the parchment to Sherry, refusing to save Alice in this way.

"Take it back, Sherry."

"Merlin sir!"

"I know you mean well, but I can't accept this way." Merlin shook his head, smiling and refusing Sherry's help.

"Why? Sherry doesn't understand why Merlin refuses such a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity!"

"Because, I'm not evil to the core, and more importantly..." Merlin hesitated, saying in a helpless tone, "You should know Alice's character, if I revive her using the Elven Wail, she will definitely hate me for life, Alice is that kind of person, she doesn't like to transfer her own pain to others, this is not helping her, but insulting her soul."

Sherry was stunned, feeling that Merlin was right, with Alice's character, how could she accept the sacrifice of so many innocent people?

"Sherry, I understand your feelings of losing your parents, but you're being too selfish." Merlin's expression became very serious.

"I know my father used his life to protect me, but you don't cherish it, and instead want to end your life in this way, that's not right." Merlin sighed, saying slowly, "If the Elf King were still alive, he would be very disappointed with you, you've made all his efforts meaningless, I'm also a father, so I understand the Elf King's feelings at the time of his death."

Sherry lowered her head, having to reflect on herself, and she, who was originally very fragile, only wanted to escape, never thought about inheriting her father's legacy and leading the elves to continue living.

Merlin patted Sherry's shoulder, speaking in a grandfatherly tone, and said with great emphasis—

"Live on, you're not alone, those elves who survived can all be led by you."

At night, the Queen's troops had already left, and the small town of Rekxum had returned to peace.

After putting Chris to sleep, Merlin was alone in the courtyard, restless, looking at the night sky—

I wonder if the landlady has already gone to the heavens?

The landlady said that the gate of the heavens was above the kingdom of France.

Was it the huge bronze door I saw before?

Merlin kept thinking, regretting handing the matter over to the landlady alone, he should have gone together.

But Merlin, as a demon, going to the homeland of the saints, was bound to cause trouble, and it was likely to cause a conflict.

Suddenly, a fireball flew over the sky of Rekxum, crashing to the ground, and the blue flames instantly illuminated the night like daytime!

Merlin suddenly frowned, his thoughts interrupted by the sudden situation, looking at the burning flames in the distance, feeling very uncertain.

Meteor? No! This feeling of the dead is what's going on!

The burning ghost fire faded, and a skeleton slowly crawled out of the deep pit, and the black, deep eyes suddenly glowed with eerie red.

Mefistopheles slowly stood up, his bones rattling, looking around the small town, muttering to himself—

"Merlin, where are you?"

title: Chapter 26 — I am your grandfather (monthly ticket bonus)
content:
Chapter 26 — I am your grandfather (monthly ticket bonus)

Volume 38 · Chapter 26

The sudden, massive tremor woke countless residents of Rexem Town from their sleep in the dead of night.

Count Austin immediately led his guards over to investigate the explosion and see what on earth had happened.

Arnold had grown quite a lot and knew how to help shoulder his father's burdens, so he followed along behind the count alongside his new wife, Rosetti.

When they reached where the "meteorite" had fallen, they found Elder Taylor and his granddaughter Lucia already there, along with quite a few others, all standing around the enormous crater peering down into it.

Since Carl had been training in the Extreme Cold Lands and hadn't returned, Elder Taylor naturally took on the role of town guardian and arrived here immediately.

Da Vinci furrowed his brow slightly, staring at the demonic skeleton standing inside the crater, as a wave of fear rose within him. "A demon's undead?"

Hobbs caught sight of the mark on Mephisto's forehead and his eyes darted around nervously. He couldn't help but step back, terrified of being discovered.

Even Hobbs himself hadn't anticipated that an Apostle of Hell would suddenly appear in Rexem. This meant Hell was no longer peaceful—the passage between the two worlds had opened!

"Elder Taylor! What's going on?" Count Austin asked in a panic.

"Undead! Undead have appeared in town!" Elder Taylor replied.

"What!?" Count Austin stepped closer and saw Mephisto's undead looking around as if searching for someone. Good heavens! Why were there undead appearing on my territory?

"What should we do now? We can't let undead threaten the town's safety." Rosetti became extremely tense.

"Should we have the guards charge together and eliminate it quickly?" Arnold said to his father.

"Exactly! One undead is nothing to be afraid of."

"No! Acting rashly will doom the entire town!"

Before Count Austin could even speak, Elder Taylor sharply rebuked him. He glanced at everyone present and said calmly, "This demon's undead is no ordinary creature. I can feel the pressure radiating from its body—it possesses terrifying strength, the likes of which I have never seen in my life."

"No matter how many people we send up there, they'll only be throwing their lives away. This is meaningless sacrifice!"

"It hasn't shown any malice yet, so let's not provoke it carelessly!"

"Then what should we do? We can't just let it stay here, can we?" Count Austin grew anxious, worried that one undead would attract countless more.

"I feel like it's looking for something. If it finds it, it should leave." Elder Taylor said with a grave expression.

Mephisto hadn't spotted Merlin. Instead, it found itself being mobbed by humans like some kind of monkey, and resentment began to swell within its heart. Roaring with a voice laced with battle energy, it bellowed—

"Merlin!!"

Fierce sound waves spread out in all directions, making everyone's ears ring. Weaklings among the onlookers simply fainted on the spot under the force of those shockwaves!

"How… how terrifying is this power!" Elder Taylor sucked in a cold breath. In this situation, all he could do was pray the town wouldn't suffer any casualties.

Lucia lowered her hands from her ears and asked in confusion, "Was it just calling out Mr. Merlin's name?"

"Could… this undead know Merlin?" Arnold was equally bewildered.

Mephisto's鬼火 flickering eyes swept across the crowd of onlookers, and by chance it spotted Hobbs hiding at the back. Its gaze shifted slightly.

"That person…

Just as Mephisto was about to go investigate directly, Merlin finally arrived. "What happened?"

"Mr. Merlin, this undead seems to be here because of you." Lucia explained.

"Here because of me?"

Merlin frowned, studying the demonic undead. A demon? Could it know me?

"I'll go down and take a look."

"It's dangerous, don't do this!" Lucia tried to stop him anxiously.

"It's fine, leave it to me."

Ignoring everyone's protests, Merlin jumped straight into the crater and came face to face with Mephisto.

The two stared at each other for a while, sizing one another up. Since Mephisto was little more than a set of bones, no one could discern what it had looked like in life. Eventually, Merlin broke the silence first.

"Who are you? Are you looking for me for some reason?"

Mephisto examined Merlin for a long time, the flames in its eyes flickering constantly. Clearly, its emotions were in great turmoil.

Perhaps it was seeing its grandson and feeling stirred within, or perhaps something else entirely.

Mephisto opened its jaw but couldn't find the right words to say. Instead, it let out a sigh heavy with meaning.

"Sigh… I never would have guessed. Never would have imagined. It's actually you. I didn't discover this secret even until my death. My future grandson is—

Sigh!"

"????" Merlin furrowed his brow, his mind completely filled with confusion. What on earth is this guy babbling about?

"Only now do I understand what you meant back then." Mephisto slowly raised its head and gazed at the night sky.

"Aren't we strangers? What did I say?" Merlin spread his hands innocently.

"You always refused to accept my challenges, saying there would be a chance later and we could meet again. So that's what you meant." Mephisto threw its arms wide and cried out loudly, "Fate! Everything is arranged by fate! We are all chess pieces on this board! No one can escape it! Who would have thought we'd meet again in this manner?"

"Ah???" Merlin was completely dumbfounded, utterly unable to understand what this undead was spouting nonsense about.

"Worth it! Everything was worth it!" Mephisto lowered its head and stared directly at Merlin, speaking in a deep voice. "To wait for this day, I had no choice but to abandon all my dignity and submit to Satan, exchanging for the eternal persistence of my consciousness. I've regretted my choice countless times—but today I understand. All the付出 was worth it!"

"Um… Merlin had absolutely no idea what was happening. After pondering for a long time and still not comprehending, he could only awkwardly say, "Sorry, I have no idea what you're talking about."

"You don't understand?" Mephisto countered, then seemed to realize something and let out a helpless sigh. "I see. That's a pity. You are merely a chrysalis that hasn't yet turned into a butterfly."

Merlin was beginning to lose patience with this rambling undead. Getting straight to the point, he demanded, "Stop saying things nobody can understand. My patience is limited—I won't stand here going crazy along with you. Who exactly are you!?"

"Hmph." Mephisto snorted coldly, emphasizing, "I greatly admire your personality. However, that's no way to speak to your grandfather. You clearly haven't learned demon race etiquette, have you?"

"Grandfather? What grandfather? Are you insane?" Merlin hadn't even grasped the seriousness of the situation. Not only that, he thought the other party was insulting him—wanted to be his grandfather?!

"Doesn't remember me at all?" Mephisto sounded somewhat dissatisfied, concluding it must be that rebellious girl Vivian who rarely mentioned him—

"Merlin, I am your grandfather—"

"Mephisto Luciferfel."

title: Chapter 27 — The Strongest Swordsman
content:
Chapter 27 — The Strongest Swordsman

Volume 38 · Chapter 27

Ah? Merlin was suddenly stunned, somewhat at a loss, standing there blankly, “What are you joking about?” “Do I need to joke?” Mephistopheles retorted. Merlin furrowed his brow, his mind a blank; anyone suddenly faced with the countless deceased ancestors of Guanyin would have roughly the same reaction. “From your reaction, Vivian rarely mentions me, huh?” Mephistopheles paused, his tone tinged with anger, “That rebellious girl, she may have completely forgotten me.” *That. Merlin’s mind was in utter chaos, he had no idea how to converse with this ancestor, “Perhaps we should sit down and talk; many things seem to be in disarray.” “Talking is useless, come fight.” Mephistopheles slowly drew the bone knife from his waist, pointing at Merlin solemnly, “I have waited for this day for a long time; other matters hold no interest for me.” “Wait, you want to fight right away?!” Merlin looked bewildered, “Is there something wrong with your head, Grandfather? It doesn’t seem easy to talk; shouldn’t we exchange information first and clear everything up?” “There’s no need for that; from the moment I saw you, all my doubts have been resolved.” Mephistopheles answered coldly. Merlin shook his head helplessly, thinking, You’ve figured it all out, but I know nothing! Why has my grandfather become an undead seeking me? And he wants to slash me right off the bat? “Draw your sword, I won’t hold back.” Mephistopheles’ tone was serious, intending to strike here. Merlin glanced at the people behind him, constantly chattering, and said helplessly, “Let’s go outside the town; if you want to fight, I’ll oblige you.” Outside Rexhelm Town, Merlin and Mephistopheles stood far apart, gazing at each other, a thick smell of gunpowder began to spread; the others stood far away on the city walls, watching the duel. Merlin was Rexhelm’s little-known first stronghold; perhaps only he could handle this powerful undead before them. Everyone’s hearts rose, even though part of them knew Merlin was extraordinarily strong, this opponent was unlike any other—not only blessed with Satan’s divine power, but also the former First Demon Lord! To the eyes of this group from Rexhelm, this was their first time seeing a battle of this level; they feared they would never witness a second such encounter in their lifetimes. “Did you all hear what they just said? That demon undead claims to be Mr. Merlin’s grandfather, doesn’t that mean—” Rosetti didn’t dare continue. “Doesn’t that mean Merlin is also a—” Arnold supplemented his wife’s sentence, a hint of fear flickering in his eyes. “We’ve been living with demons for this long?” Lucia’s face turned pale, frightened badly, “Good heavens, who would believe such a thing if it got out?” “If Mr. Merlin is a demon, then what is the purpose of his long residence in human lands?” Da Vinci likewise felt fear, but instead of showing it, he posed the question. Faced with this doubt, everyone chose silence; no one could guess the answer. They hadn’t even noticed the demon among them, so how could they guess why Merlin had stayed in Rexhelm all this time? Chairman Taylor lowered his head, worry welling up, because he could no longer tell whether Merlin was friend or foe; although the adventurers’ rule is not to ask about origins, having a demon as an adventurer was unprecedented! Count Austin, as lord of Rexhelm, had been frightened silly, his mind filled with the invasions of demons that the United Kingdom once suffered, “What should we do? Rexhelm has a demon! Should we send an urgent report to Her Majesty the Queen? This is a huge matter!” Among those present, perhaps only Bus remained completely calm, having long known everything. Merlin stared at his grandfather’s undead, speaking seriously, “I think we should sit down and talk properly, rather than engage in meaningless fighting here.” “This isn’t a fight; it’s a duel where we stake our lives.” Mephistopheles’ ghostly fire flickered in his eyes, “I have endured humiliation and burden for far too long to wait for this day.” “Why do you hold such great hostility toward me? When I had memories, you were already dead; we never had any conflict, did we?” Merlin hoped to end this meaningless struggle. “Shut up and draw your sword.” Mephistopheles had no patience to sit down and talk with Merlin; he only wanted to fulfill his dream, to win this duel that had been dragged across several eons! “I—” Merlin had just begun to speak when Mephistopheles could no longer restrain himself, launching a fierce attack with incredible speed! From afar, just seeing the swing of the blade, in the blink of an eye the sharp bone knife’s edge had already reached Merlin’s face, pressing him into danger! Before Merlin, Mephistopheles had always been the strongest swordsman among the demons, his strength and swordsmanship surpassing all the first demon kings. Looking through history, Mephistopheles might be the only one who could exchange a few blows with Merlin in swordsmanship. Merlin’s heart leapt in shock; he had clearly underestimated his grandfather, whose strength exceeded any opponent he had faced before! Even the ancient god Behemoth, in terms of oppression, paled compared to Mephistopheles, whose power faintly already stood above the ancient gods! According to some historical records Merlin had read, descriptions of this ancestor were nowhere near this formidable; obviously he had gained Satan’s blessing, his power elevated another level! So what kind of supreme deity could make Mephistopheles submit, and how mighty must it be? Merlin’s pupils contracted; he had to dodge quickly, yet still a few strands of his hair were cut, his head nearly severed. He finally realized this grandfather was serious, not joking, coming to take his life! Before Merlin could catch his breath, Mephistopheles’ second strike followed, aiming straight at his fragile neck, killing intent looming! “Tsk!” In this situation Merlin had no choice but to strike back after the opponent’s move, launching a counterattack; in the flash of lightning he drew his sword and swung at Mephistopheles. A fierce, murderous sword aura surged forward, straight at Mephistopheles, enough to shatter his bones into countless fragments! But the ghostly blue fire in Mephistopheles’ eyes surged, as if he had anticipated Merlin’s move; he swiftly raised his bone knife to block, his body slightly turning aside, using soft force to guide Merlin’s sword aura! Faced with Merlin’s hard, overpowering draw‑slash technique, Mephistopheles did not choose to meet force with force; instead, unexpectedly, he chose to overcome hardness with softness, continually dispersing the power of Merlin’s draw‑slash in other directions! Merlin’s blade slammed heavily onto Mephistopheles’ bone knife, yet unexpectedly slid along the curved blade’s edge to the side, the earth trembling and cracking, a terrifying gouge carved beside the enemy’s feet! “!!?” Merlin’s heart pounded; he had failed to inflict any substantial damage on Mephistopheles—this was the first time he had encountered such an opponent— relying on superb swordsmanship, he had successfully neutralized the draw‑slash he prided himself on— terrifying. Mephistopheles truly deserved his reputation as the strongest swordsman of the demon race!

title: Chapter 28 — Broken Ass (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 28 — Broken Ass (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 38 · Chapter 28

Merlin was somewhat bewildered. The power of his slash remained, but Mephistopheles' bizarre parry had redirected all the force to the other side.

This soft, mushy technique was indeed very unique—not brute-forcefully bouncing the power away, but slightly deflecting its reverse direction. If an ordinary person could hardly see through the method, but as a transmigrator, Merlin had a fierce sense of déjà vu—something like overcoming softness with hardness, wasn't that "Tai Chi"? He wouldn't clash head-on with powerful enemies, but would instead unload the incoming force and redirect it elsewhere.

Mephistopheles slowly raised his head, staring straight into Merlin's eyes, and said in a low voice, "I haven't been practicing my parry sword technique in vain. I've studied your drawing technique for a long time, and now it's finally proven useful."

"? ? ?" Merlin was astonished. Mephistopheles had studied him for so long? What did that mean? Logically speaking, they weren't even from the same era.

"I hope you can show me some real skills. Don't disappoint me."

As soon as the words fell, a sharp bone knife appeared in Mephistopheles' left hand. He also became serious, intending to win with his full strength.

Mephistopheles had always been skilled with dual blades. The sharpness of his swordsmanship would leave enemies unable to parry, giving them the illusion of fighting two opponents. Only when facing a true strong enemy would Mephistopheles use his dual-blade technique. For today's duel, he had prepared for a long time.

Mephistopheles swung both hands simultaneously. The angles of the two bone knives were extremely tricky, instantly bursting forth with surging sword energy, far more violent than before.

"Tch!"

Merlin had to quickly retreat. Even with his speed, he couldn't escape the kill net woven by the dual blades. Arms and waist were both cut.

"What are you doing? Only this level? Pathetic."

Mephistopheles spoke with sarcasm, hoping Merlin would show his true skills. Like this, he was still far from meeting his expectations.

Merlin looked down at his wounds. Thankfully they weren't too deep and nothing serious, but the swordsmanship Mephistopheles displayed still left him very surprised.

Mephistopheles charged forward again. The slashing of the dual blades was like a storm, instantly increasing Merlin's pressure!

Merlin countered with a draw, but was blocked again by Mephistopheles using the same method, not giving him any chance at all.

"So annoying!"

"Useless. This parry technique was specially designed to counter you. I've run through it in my mind countless times."

Mephistopheles' gaze froze, thrusting the bone knife in his left hand directly at Merlin's abdomen—a clearly fatal strike!

In a desperate moment, Merlin's demonic blood surged. The scorching hot air wave blasted Mephistopheles flying!

The people on the city wall, seeing Merlin's terrifying demonic form, screamed in fright and were at a loss.

Arnold stuttered, pointing at Merlin and unable to speak.

"Demons!" Lucia widened her eyes, thinking she had been joking with demons every day, and felt a chill!

"Is that the true appearance of Mr. Merlin?" Da Vinci had a complex expression.

Count Austin went mad on the spot, clutching his head and exclaiming, "It's over! Rexham is doomed! Just looking at this, it's definitely not an ordinary demon!"

Mephistopheles barely stabilized his figure. Seeing Merlin's demonic form, he sighed, "That's right. This is what I wanted. Come! Let me see your true power!"

Demon Merlin looked at Mephistopheles. His voice became hoarse as he slowly said, "I see. Defeating you isn't difficult. There's a saying: chaotic punches can kill the master. I wonder if you've heard of it?"

Merlin meant that Mephistopheles' parry technique had limits. It couldn't block crushing-level power. No matter how high the skill, it's afraid of kitchen knives—the same principle.

"Less talk. Try it boldly." Mephistopheles took his stance.

Merlin gripped the hilt of Banri Garan. After demonization, the flames began to spread and burn the blade, revealing the true nature of the blade's qi.

Suddenly, Merlin disappeared from his spot and instantly appeared before Mephistopheles. Without a word, he drew his sword and slashed. This time was different—the direction changed to the right.

The ghost fire in Mephistopheles' eyes jumped. Under the demonic form, Merlin was indeed different. His power suddenly increased several-fold, his eyes almost couldn't keep up!

However, Mephistopheles remained calm. This duel had been run through in his mind countless times; he could guess all situations.

Mephistopheles raised the bone knife in his right hand again to parry, wanting to redirect Merlin's drawing force so it couldn't hurt him.

"Right hand again?" Merlin said coldly.

This time, a problem appeared. The drawing force of demonized Merlin was too huge, instantly blasting Mephistopheles away!

Demon fire exploded, instantly swallowing Mephistopheles. The flames spread continuously, melting the nearby mountain, burning through from the middle.

Lava rolled. Even the people on the city wall felt an unbearable heat wave—

"I-I..." Arnold widened his eyes, sat down on his butt from fright. Originally... originally Merlin's power... so terrifying? He's not a kept man!"

Lucia was shocked, covering her mouth, not knowing what to say. Her heart was in a mess. Mr. Merlin was too strong, right? He seemed stronger than Alice. Originally everyone wasn't lying. I used to joke that he was a useless man who hugged his wife's thigh every day. He won't hold a grudge, will he?

"My heavens." Elder Taylor secretly gasped, again and again having his worldview refreshed. He knew Merlin was strong, but didn't expect it to be this strong! Far beyond his imagination. Even this demon undead wasn't a match!

"This???

"Father! Father!

Count Austin was scared unconscious on the spot, rolling his eyes and losing consciousness. Rosetti hurriedly squatted down to check on him.

In Count Austin's eyes, such a terrifying demon was in Rexham. Wouldn't his territory turn to ash in a minute? Destroying Rexham was underestimating Merlin. If he wanted to, one person destroying a country wasn't a problem.

Mephistopheles' whole body was burned bright red. He climbed out of the lava again, clearly injured. He was satisfied with this result.

"Correct! Should be like this! This is the duel I've been looking forward to! Indeed I didn't wait in vain for so long..."

If Merlin continued attacking fiercely, he could easily defeat Mephistopheles. But he suppressed the demonic blood and ended the demonization.

This left Mephistopheles very confused, so he shouted, "What do you mean?"

"Crushing with power is dishonorable. Besides, you're my grandfather. I don't want to defeat you with such means." Merlin answered seriously.

"Silly! Give me your full strength! Otherwise the humiliation I suffer in hell becomes meaningless!" Mephistopheles shouted loudly.

"You seem to not understand my polite words at all? Then I'll be more direct." Merlin paused, speaking with a blank expression. "Against you, I don't need to use my full strength at all."

title: Chapter 29 — Urgent
content:
Chapter 29 — Urgent

Volume 38 · Chapter 29

"What did you say!?"

Mephisto looked somewhat disheveled, instinctively gripping the twin blades in his hands, an endless anger stirring within him.

Merlin refusing to fight at full strength was clearly an insult to Mephisto, something he simply could not accept.

"Give me everything you've got! Are you pitying me!?"

"No, I admire you. I admit that in terms of swordsmanship, I am inferior to you. If I were to win by brute force, it would be meaningless. So I will defeat you with sword technique." Merlin explained quietly.

"You have a lot of nerve." Mephisto勉强 accepted this reason, raising his twin blades again. "Come then, it's time to decide this."

Merlin slowly unfastened Misteln, tying the god-slaying sword separately to the right side of his waist. After preparing everything, he drew his blade into a ready stance, his right hand firmly gripping Banri Garan.

Mephisto's two bone blades trembled constantly, ghostly blue flames erupting continuously, completely shrouding his body. The overwhelming pressure surpassing even ancient gods roared like a mad lion, directed ceaselessly at his enemy.

An inexplicable pressure swept through the surroundings, making those on the city wall struggle to breathe. Nobody dared to blink, fearing they might miss important details —

Suddenly, the distant mountains turned fiery red as the morning light gradually rose, slowly casting its rays onto the two figures.

Almost at the exact same moment, Merlin and Mephisto both launched their attacks, closing the distance between them instantly!

Mephisto's entire skeletal frame creaked and rattled, his twin blades aiming for性命, striking straight for Merlin's neck. Before the blades even came down, the sharp aura had already left a red mark on Merlin's neck!

Merlin did not defend or dodge. Instead, he pressed forward recklessly, showing no regard for his own head being separated from his body, choosing to face head-on the killing blade net woven by Mephisto, quickly drawing his sword and slashing!

"It's useless!"

Mephisto's right-hand bone blade danced, once again assuming a bizarre parrying stance, successfully deflecting Merlin's strength so that his blade struck his right side instead.

However, this time Merlin did not stop his attack. Before Banri Garan could even be retracted, he swiftly drew again, pulling out Misteln from the right side of his waist and striking at the defenseless Mephisto!

Double consecutive draws — inspired by Mephisto, Merlin had attempted this for the first time and achieved good results. This confirmed his suspicion: whether with his left or right hand, he possessed the power of iaijutsu!

Crack — — -

Mephisto was destroyed on the spot, bones scattering across the ground, his skull cracking and rolling across the floor. His soul fire grew extremely faint, reduced to nothing more than a tiny flame.

This strongest demon race swordsman was indeed powerful, but unfortunately, he was only the strongest of the past. Since Merlin's birth, that title had likely already been quietly taken elsewhere.

Merlin stood before the ground covered in skeletons, wielding twin blades. His appearance bore a striking resemblance to what Mephisto must have looked like in his youth; he even saw a hint of his own reflection in him.

"Did you figure it all out, Mephisto?"

"Yes." Merlin nodded, slowly returning both swords to their scabbards, speaking softly. "Every parry used your right hand. Your twin-blade technique hasn't reached its peak, has it? Your left hand can't perform a parrying sword technique, or if you can use it, it's not as perfect as your right."

"It seems I've been seen through after all." Mephisto's laughter was filled with resignation, his tone becoming much more relaxed. "Very well. To be able to complete this duel, I am already satisfied. I finally have no regrets. Having existed in a half-dead state as an infernal apostle for so long, it was all worth it."

"Why did you want to duel me right from the start?" Merlin demanded.

"Because of a promise made long ago. If I don't fulfill it, I won't find peace even in death," Mephisto replied.

"Huh...?" Merlin furrowed his brow, thinking — a promise? A promise with someone else?

"My time is running short. There are some things I must tell you." Mephisto's soul fire flickered, already teetering on the verge of extinction.

"Do you know Alice? I heard her calling out your name in hell, apparently with great urgency."

"Alice!?" Merlin heard the name and cast all other doubts aside. "You saw her? She is my wife!"

"So that's how it is. Then you must hurry. Satan is about to hold a wedding, to marry your wife." Mephisto paused, then continued. "Right now, before the gate to hell in the basement of the Holy City's temple closes, you still have a chance to go to hell and stop this."

"Satan is going to marry Alice!?" Merlin felt as though struck by lightning, a faint sensation growing at the crown of his head like grass sprouting. "Why has things come to this!?"

"Listen to me!" Mephisto barked loudly, speaking gravely. "You must depart as soon as possible and arrive before the wedding. Although your wife refused, Satan is after all the ruler of hell, and no one can defy him. He will likely force the matter."

"Tch!" Merlin's brows tightened, his anger clenching his fist white-knuckled. He thought — things are getting worse and worse. Will I ultimately have to fight the Supreme God?

"You'd better be careful. The infernal apostles seem to live right beside you. I'm not certain about this, but it feels familiar." Mephisto said anxiously, his soul fire no longer able to sustain itself.

"What!?" Merlin's head snapped up in shock. An infernal apostle has always been by my side!? Who is it!?

"Finally, it makes me happy to see you. Farewell."

"Hey! Wait!"

Mephisto's soul fire completely extinguished, and no matter how Merlin called out, there was no further response.

In his final moments, Mephisto had conveyed important matters to Merlin, hoping to provide him some assistance.

Merlin stood like a stone statue where he was. After hearing Mephisto's news, his heart remained deeply unsettled —

An infernal apostle by my side? Who is it? Could Mephisto have been mistaken?

None of that mattered now. What was important was Alice.

I can't keep waiting for news from the landlady anymore. I must personally go to hell and stop all of this!

---

The following day, Count Austin, terrified beyond measure, used an emergency communication item overnight to contact the royal capital.

He reported everything that had happened the previous night to the queen, and also truthfully revealed Merlin's identity.

Count Austin was deeply unsettled. A demon appearing in his domain was something that could shake the entire kingdom!

Especially since Britannia had previously suffered a demon invasion, and everyone's fear had not fully dissipated — mentioning demons alone could change anyone's complexion.

Having witnessed Merlin's strength, Count Austin, as the local lord, found himself utterly incapable of handling the situation.

That opponent was a terrifying demon who could destroy the nation with a mere gesture. How could a minor lord like Count Rexem possibly resist?

Count Austin hoped the kingdom would dispatch a knight corps, and preferably that the First Knight Mestfield would also come to support them. Only then might there be a chance to save Rexem.

But after receiving the queen's reply, Count Austin became utterly perplexed —

「I have received your message. I understand you must be very anxious right now, but I ask that you completely forget about this matter and pretend it never happened.」

"Huh...?"

"What does that mean?"

title: Chapter 30 — Vigilance
content:
Chapter 30 — Vigilance

Volume 38 · Chapter 30

Vigilance

Early morning, Chris sat beside her mother, still not awake.

The little one still hadn't given up, pouring life force into Alice every day, hoping she could wake up.

This made Chris extremely exhausted. Merlin wanted to stop his daughter's meaningless actions, but it had no effect at all — her stubborn nature was completely inherited from Alice.

Husky Avus had been accompanying the little one all along. Seeing Chris's tired appearance every day, he felt great sympathy in his heart.

But he wasn't allowed to speak, so he could only keep wagging his dog tail, trying to make Chris feel a little better.

Avus, lying by the bedside, heard the door open. He suddenly opened his eyes and chased straight out, seeing that Merlin already had his pack slung over his shoulders and was preparing to leave —

"Merlin! What are you doing?"

"I have an urgent matter. I must leave." Merlin stopped and looked back.

"Are you going to abandon your own daughter? She's still so young, who will take care of her?!" Avus felt utterly disappointed in Merlin. He thought to himself: as expected of a demon, no sense of responsibility whatsoever. How could he abandon his own child at a time like this?

"I'll find someone else to help look after her for a while." Merlin replied.

"Others will never be her parents. It's completely different. What are you really going to do? How can you leave your own daughter at a time like this?" Avus's tone grew angry. The little one was so pure and kind — how could Merlin bear to do such a thing?

"I want to rescue Alice. Only then can Chris recover." Merlin answered truthfully.

"Rescue a dead person? What do you plan to do?" Avus's attitude softened slightly. Chris was pouring life force into Alice every day; sooner or later her body would break down.

"I will go to Hell and retrieve Alice's soul." Merlin's eyes were resolute. He was already prepared.

"What!??" Avus's eyes widened in terror. He wondered if he'd heard wrong. "Have you gone mad?! No one can take a soul away from Hell!"

"How will I know if I don't try?" Merlin gave a weary smile, turning the question back.

"Hell is the realm of the dead, a completely unknown world. Its master would absolutely not allow you to do this — you would die!" Avus urged anxiously. "Isn't there any safer way?"

"I have no other choice, Avus. I must go." Merlin lowered his head and added, "While I'm away, make sure to protect Chris. Don't let anyone hurt her."

"I... I understand." Avus nodded blankly.

"It's all in your hands from now on. I will come back." Merlin let out a long breath and turned to leave directly.

Avus watched Merlin's departing figure, his heart filled with mixed emotions. He felt great sympathy for Chris, still lost in sleep —

A happy family of three had been reduced to this. Fate was too cruel to mankind.

But Merlin couldn't possibly succeed, right?

Because there had never been a single successful case of bringing a deceased soul away from Hell.

At the Guild, the atmosphere was somewhat oppressive. Merlin's terrifying image from the previous night lingered, impossible to shake.

Everyone harbored a worry — was Merlin friend or foe?

Such a powerful demon present in Rexham made everyone deeply uneasy.

Especially since Merlin hadn't said a single word the previous night and went straight back, making the crowd even more puzzled.

"Ahem... Could Merlin be... a demon race spy, waiting for the right moment to annihilate us one by one?" Rosetti swallowed nervously.

"That doesn't make sense. With Mr. Merlin's power, he could destroy us anytime. There's no need to wait for an opportunity." Da Vinci replied gravely. From Merlin's behavior the previous night, he could have destroyed all of Britain without any problem.

Rosetti fell silent, puzzled. "What is Merlin thinking? We simply can't figure him out."

"Perhaps he's staying here for some other reason?" Da Vinci speculated.

"Oh!" Luqia's eyes brightened. A new idea formed in her mind. "Could it be that the demon has fallen in love with a human? Alice captured Merlin's heart, which is why he's been staying in Rexham this whole time!"

"Luqia, you've read too many love stories. Your head is full of interspecies romance. Is that even possible?" Rosetti rolled her eyes. "Demons always hold themselves in high regard and look down on us. In their eyes, we're the same as livestock. Would livestock fall in love with you?"

"Why not? Mr. Merlin is spending every day with Alice now. Without love, is that possible?" Luqia retorted defiantly. Apart from her underdeveloped chest, Alice was a beauty. How could she not capture Merlin's heart?

"That was later. At first, it was completely different. The Guild Master must know — initially, the two of them were like enemies." Rosetti continued to stress. "Since Merlin is a demon, he might have some enormous conspiracy!"

Guild Master Old Taylor remained silent. He was also deeply worried. If Merlin was indeed a spy planted by the demon race among humans, it would pose a massive threat to the entire kingdom.

"Why is everyone so tense? Haven't we grown quite familiar with Merlin already? We've drunk together, boasted together. Though he's a demon, he's never harmed us, has he? Perhaps Merlin has no ill intent at all." Arnold stood up, feeling that everyone was overcomplicating matters. Even if Merlin was dangerous, hadn't they lived together peacefully for so long?

"Merlin is a demon! Three years ago during that disaster, how many people died at the hands of demons? Have you forgotten so quickly?" Luqia countered.

"Yes... Merlin is ultimately a demon." Rosetti's expression was deeply unsettled.

"Hobbs! Why don't you say something? Don't play dead at a time like this. You and Merlin have always had a good relationship — what do you think?" Arnold asked loudly.

"Huh? What?" Hobbs seemed to wake from a dream. He wasn't sure what he'd been thinking about just now.

"Hobbs, what's wrong with you? You seem distracted lately." Arnold frowned.

"Sorry, I haven't been getting enough sleep lately, haha." Hobbs laughed it off.

"What do you think about Merlin?" Arnold asked again.

"Merlin? Well..." Hobbus furrowed his brows. "I can't really put it into words. I just feel very worried about my own safety."

Creak —

The Guild door opened. Merlin walked in with his pack on his back. Everyone's faces changed dramatically, their eyes filled with deep vigilance and fear.

Merlin's gaze swept across the crowd. He understood what was happening — his identity had been exposed, frightening them all.

The atmosphere in the Guild instantly grew tense. Everyone stared at Merlin's every move, but no one had the courage to speak first.

The eerie silence made Merlin somewhat uncomfortable. He slowly approached Rebus, drained the remaining liquor from his cup in one gulp, then wiped his mouth —

"What's wrong, everyone?"

"Are you afraid I'll eat you?"

title: Chapter 31 — Stepping Through the Gates of Hell (Bonus Chapter: Monthly Votes)
content:
Chapter 31 — Stepping Through the Gates of Hell (Bonus Chapter: Monthly Votes)

Volume 38 · Chapter 31

Merlin spoke in a teasing tone, trying to appear relaxed so as not to put pressure on others. Everyone stared at each other, noticing that Merlin was just as usual, as if last night's events had never happened. Then Arnold, this blockhead, was the first to stand up and break the silence, bluntly asking— "Merlin! .You you ." "I I I what I?" Merlin looked helpless. "Not! "Arnold, nervous, misspoke, then coughed twice, "Cough cough! Are you a demon?" "As you see, yes, I am a demon.* Merlin nodded, not continuing to hide. Everyone's faces changed somewhat, the oppressive atmosphere eased considerably, Merlin's willingness to admit his identity proved he could be someone to sit down and talk with. If Merlin wanted to slaughter Rexel Town, there would be no need to come here, just like usual drinking and chatting with everyone— Upon this, everyone's emotions steadied considerably, they all looked at Merlin, hoping he could explain this matter clearly. "Since since you are a demon, why have you been living here all along?" Arnold continued. "Because I was exiled, I could only leave the demon race and live outside; initially I wandered around, even worked as a waiter in a small village chief's place, then followed Alice here, becoming an adventurer, after all this profession is not only free but also earns quite a bit of money." Merlin temporarily set down his pack. "Exiled?" Da Vinci showed some doubt. "I am the master of the First Demon Lord Palace, also known to you all as Lucifer the Third; for certain reasons, I was expelled from the Demon Lord Palace by the demon race's Elder Council." Merlin explained sincerely. "You, you are Lucifer the Third? Master of the Northern Demon Lord Palace!" Chairman Elder Taylor exclaimed excitedly, knowing that in the northern kingdom's private swamp there is a gathering place of demons. "Have you really killed indiscriminately, slaughtering countless Holy Temple Knights of the Holy Church?" Lucia also couldn't help but ask. "Have you violated a female Hero? That 233rd Hero, is he already dead?" Rosetti also curiously asked. Merlin suddenly felt his head swell, completely unsure how to answer everyone's questions, only able to signal everyone to be quiet, then he said himself— "Everyone, don't be so agitated, I know you're all uneasy because of my current mood. "But I promise I won't just kill people casually, nor will I threaten the kingdom's safety. "As for the questions you raised? Most are rumors, only a few are true." Everyone stared at each other, originally the rumors and the true Lucifer the Third are not quite the same; thinking of Merlin's usual appearance, it's indeed hard to equate him with a murderous maniac. "That is to say, Mr. Merlin is not a demon race spy, and has nothing to do with the demon invasion three years ago?" Da Vinci continued. "It cannot be said to be completely unrelated, after all I am also a member of the demon race, but the demon race is divided into two factions, conservatives and radicals; the war was sparked by the radicals, and with internal turmoil in the demon race, the flames of war were completely extinguished, otherwise the war would not have ended in such a short time." Merlin paused, then slowly said, "Now the demon race has abandoned the original Demon Lord Palace, taking development as the primary goal; the probability of launching another external war has become very small." After Merlin's explanation, everyone's expressions eased a little, as long as no demon invasion of human homelands occurs again, it's fine. "That... Mr. Merlin, you really have no way to return to the demon race?" Lucia asked curiously, thinking that even if Merlin was exiled by the demon race, as a former Demon Lord, returning should not be difficult. "I can go back, but here there are people more important to me; for Alice and the child, I must stay." Merlin lowered his head, his gaze sweeping over everyone— "I must have frightened you all, but I understand, after all having a demon lurking nearby would make anyone uneasy. "But don't be afraid, here I am just Merlin, an ordinary adventurer, not a Demon Lord. "I hope you can treat me as before, not feel fear just because of my demonic identity." "Really?" Arnold asked tentatively. "Of course." Merlin nodded. Arnold steeled himself to approach Merlin, tentatively giving him a light punch on the chest to see his reaction? Merlin glanced at Arnold, not taking it as anything, nor getting angry. Arnold then completely relaxed, his tone extremely excited, saying— "You all just saw that? I just punched the Demon Lord, the Demon Lord didn't even dare to squeak, I feel I could brag about this for a lifetime!" Arnold's joke immediately caused laughter to erupt in the Adventurers Guild, the atmosphere lightened considerably, the pressure in everyone's hearts dissipated like smoke. The guild members have known Merlin for not just a day or two, they are familiar with his personality, seeing he is not a bloodthirsty demon, they finally felt at ease. "I even recommended a job to the Demon Lord; among all the Adventurers Guild's barmaid posters, only I have this courage." Lucia laughed proudly. "What's that? I once even flirted with the Demon Lord; it seems the Demon Lord isn't as scary as imagined~" Rosetti felt this was a precious memory hard to forget, saying it out loud maybe nobody would believe. "? ? ?" Arnold had a head full of question marks, feeling like maybe there's a bit of green on his head? "Joking aside, I still request everyone not to spread this matter; if it causes any disturbance it would not be good." Merlin said in an admonishing tone. "Don't worry!" Arnold patted Merlin's shoulder, thumped his chest, saying, "Our lips are sealed, we won't say anything, come on, come on, let's sit down and have a good drink, I'm very curious about your demon race, can you tell us something interesting?" "Let's talk later; I didn't come here to drink, I have other matters." Merlin smiled and refused Arnold's invitation. "Other matters?" Arnold suddenly startled. Merlin approached Chairman Elder Taylor, speaking sincerely, "Chairman, I need to leave for a while, could you please look after Chris?" Now the landlady has already left Rexel, heading for the Heavenly Realm; if Merlin is not here, Chairman Taylor is the most suitable to look after Chris. "Of course, but ., where are you going?" Chairman Taylor felt Merlin looked anxious. "You don't need to ask, this is my own affair; I don't want to drag you into it." Merlin's expression turned serious, he did not intend to tell unrelated people about his upcoming journey— Going to Hell is extremely dangerous; to retrieve Alice's soul, I may have to oppose the Supreme God, this is unprecedented. The good and kind people of Rexel have no need to wade into the mud from the start. So Merlin chose to conceal it, alone to face the ruler of Hell. Over a month later, Merlin arrived at the Holy City, which had become a land of the dead, corpses piled like mountains, survivors few and far between. Following the clues given by Mephistopheles, he discovered in the underground secret chamber of the temple a Hell Gate that had not yet been closed. Standing before the gate, Merlin heard the cries of the undead, he took a deep breath, resolutely stepped inside— He suddenly recalled a line from Dante's Divine Comedy: "Abandon all hope, ye who enter here."

title: Chapter 1 — Countdown
content:
Chapter 1 — Countdown

Volume 39 · Chapter 1

Hell, a world of darkness and fire, is the land of the dead, the final resting place of souls.
In history, only one living person has ever come here: the Spear Hero Olivier, who came to save his wife. He failed, unable to escape; Merlin is now doing the same thing as Olivier, and whether he will succeed remains unknown.
Hell is divided into nine layers; the lowest layer is called Ice Hell, where there is a vast ice lake beneath which countless souls are frozen. They are of no race; after death they all face Satan's judgment. The souls frozen here are deprived of their seven senses, forever unable to escape, suffering eternal cold torment. Anyone who falls into the ninth layer of Hell has, without exception, committed grave sins in life—betrayal! Either betraying kin and friends, or betraying their lord or kingdom. They gather in the ninth layer of Hell to endure the most terrifying punishment Hell can offer, never able to rise again. Satan's hounds take perverse pleasure in smashing the rulers of Ice Hell, splicing together different bodies to form grotesque ice sculptures, satisfying the Hell Lord's taste for the bizarre—this is an insult to traitors, such as pressing the queen's jade peak against a male slave's chest, or stuffing a king's head into a pig's rear, and so on—unimaginable strange ice sculptures.
At the center of the ice lake stands a majestic black temple, Satan's dwelling, the absolute center of Hell, where many powerful undead gather.
At this very moment, deep within the temple, Alice is dressed in a black wedding gown, locked inside a golden cage. All around is pitch black; she cannot see anything at all. Alice's breathing is uneasy and constricted; she huddles in a corner of the cage, her heart filled with waves of fear, a look of helplessness. She does not know where she is; she merely woke up to find herself in the golden cage, already changed into a black wedding gown. This leaves Alice completely bewildered. Only after meeting the so-called ruler of Hell, Satan, does she realize she is truly dead. Alice tries to escape the cage, but any touch brings a deep stabbing pain; all her power has been mysteriously stripped away, making escape impossible. Not knowing how long she has spent in the cage, Alice can do nothing but give up resistance, curling up inside and waiting for fate to decide her fate.
Regarding her choice in the Fated Secret Realm, Alice feels no regret, nor does she fear death—only sorrow. 'Will I never again be able to see Merlin and Chris?' she wonders. 'How are they now? Have they already buried me?' Without her by her side, Chris will surely be heartbroken; I haven't even finished telling her bedtime story. What is Merlin thinking? Will he weep for me? Will he not quickly find a new love? Probably not, but that silver‑tongued fellow really makes me uneasy. Ah, it seems I may never see them again.'
Alice stares blankly at the twelve oil lamps outside the golden cage, her mind full of questions, occasionally using memories of the past to numb herself and ease her loneliness.
Suddenly, a huge shadow looms in the darkness—only a single eye, yet it emits a bewitching red light that catches the heart, its gaze filled with intense obsession. 'Teresa, have you made up your mind? If you agree to marry me, I will grant you freedom and make you the mistress of all Hell.' Alice's body trembles; she slowly rises, stares directly at the immense shadow, and boldly declares, 'I am not Teresa! I am Alice! You have mistaken me!'
A strange, eerie laugh echoes; Satan does not believe Alice's words. 'Don't deny it—I know you are Teresa, the woman I have long dreamed of.' 'Shout!' Alice grits her silver teeth, having explained to Satan countless times, yet he insists she is that so‑called Teresa. 'I have no reason to conceal anything; I have never even heard the name Teresa. How many times must I explain before you understand?'
'You and I share the same scent, and even our looks are—identical; I will not be mistaken.' Satan pauses, his tone tinged with a hint of pleading, 'I have pursued you since the age of the gods; if it weren't for that hateful demon prophet, you would already be my wife. After all this time, my feelings for you have not changed in the slightest—does that not prove anything? I love you more than anyone else; I am willing to swear that I will care for you for life, for all eternity.'
'What does this have to do with me? I am not Teresa! I already have a husband—his name is Merlin! I could never marry you! Your affection means nothing to me!' Alice shouts angrily from inside the cage, never imagining she would be stared at by a pervert other than Arnold; the men she attracts all seem to have some psychological issue.
Faced with Alice's tirade, Satan falls silent for a moment, as if recalling something unpleasant. After a long while, he speaks again, his voice no longer enthusiastic but now laced with coldness—
'You really haven't changed at all; you once said similar things to me.' 'What is your husband anyway? Do you still miss him?' 'Useless; perhaps he is already dead.'
'What?!' Alice's eyes widen in shock, as if realizing something; she demands, 'Did you do something?' 'I won't tell you. Since you are so cold‑hearted and unwilling to accept my proposal, I must continue to win your heart.' Satan pauses, then continues, 'I want your person, by any means necessary.'
'You?!' Alice is at a loss, faced with this psychological deviant she has no recourse; moreover, he especially enjoys self‑gratification, as if he had done something extraordinarily impressive, and not accepting him is seen as not appreciating his efforts. 'Do you see the twelve oil lamps before you? This is your last time.' Satan looks down on Alice; as the master god, he has countless ways to obtain her. Since he cannot win her heart, he must resort to force—
'The oil lamps will go out one by one; when all are extinguished, your consciousness will come under my control.' 'I will make you agree to the lewd union, holding a grand wedding before countless souls of the dead.' 'We will spend a wonderful night together and beget excellent offspring.' 'You yourself may not realize how beautiful you look in the wedding dress I prepared; I am almost impatient for the wedding to arrive soon.'
'Eh!' Alice gasps in shock, her gaze fixed on the twelve oil lamps outside the cage; fear seizes her heart— the flame of the first oil lamp flickers wildly and goes out first. The countdown begins!
A terrifying murderous aura erupts; a blade slashes fiercely! The three-headed hell hounds guarding the gate are instantly split in two! Their massive bodies crash to the ground, blood pouring everywhere, devoured by endless flames. Satan's war‑hound, which had just been savagely lunging at Merlin to tear him apart, loses its life in an instant. This beast does not even know who it faces; it still thinks it is dealing with the same easy‑target as those who came to Hell before. Merlin sheathes his blade, his eyes sweeping over the dark, fiery world before him, his resolve hardening—
'Alice, I have come.' 'Wait for me!'

title: Chapter 2 — Stop
content:
Chapter 2 — Stop

Volume 39 · Chapter 2

Hobbs returned home late, his expression heavy with concern. The First Apostle of Hell, Mephistopheles, suddenly appeared here, making him feel very uneasy. He didn't know what had happened in Hell, and there was no news at all. He just felt that his peaceful life was coming to an end.

After returning home, Hobbs went to his bed and found that his daughter, Mini, was already asleep. He gently caressed her face, praying silently, "Please, don't let anything happen. It's best to be like this now."

Looking at Mini's sleeping face, Hobbs' mood gradually calmed down, and a few smiles appeared on his face.

"You seem to be enjoying your life in the mortal world very much."

Hobbs' body trembled, his face turned pale, and large beads of sweat rolled down his forehead. He stiffly turned his head slowly.

He discovered that the darkness behind him had been completely consumed by an endless abyss, and a ghostly flame was burning fiercely.

Hobbs quickly stood up, bowed his knee sincerely, and responded in a trembling voice, "Great Master."

"You haven't completed the task I assigned you properly. You should have stirred up conflicts and consumed the strength of the mortal world, making the powerful ones fall into Hell and become my servants," Satan said, his tone filled with the flavor of reproach.

"I have been diligent in fulfilling your instructions, not a moment has been neglected," Hobbs replied nervously.

"That is Mini?" Satan asked, noticing Mini sleeping peacefully.

Hobbs' heart skipped a beat, and he quickly replied, "No, it's an orphan I picked up."

"Oh?" Satan remained silent for a while and continued, "You are my servant, yet you are still so kind, which surprises me."

"It's just something to do to pass the time," Hobbs said, his expression worried, fearing that Satan might harm Mini if he didn't obey.

"You haven't forgotten, have you? Your wife is still suffering in Hell, and if you don't obey me, you should know what will happen to her," Satan said, his tone threatening.

"I understand," Hobbs bit his lip, knowing that Satan was scolding him.

"Your mission in the mortal world is temporarily over. Come back quickly, there is something for you to do," Satan said, his tone commanding.

"What is it?" Hobbs didn't want to return to Hell.

"The young Demon Lord Merlin has entered Hell. Go and stop him, otherwise, your wife will die at his hands," Satan said, his voice low and mocking. The darkness in the room quickly faded, and Hobbs stood there, his eyes filled with disbelief.

Merlin... went to Hell? Was it for Alice?

This is bad.

That night, Hobbs used some means to ensure that Mini wouldn't wake up easily. Then he took Mini and directly went to the house of Elder Taylor, knocking on the door.

Elder Taylor was still awake at this time and was a bit surprised to see Hobbs.

"Hobbs? What are you doing here?"

"Is Lucy not at home?" Hobbs asked curiously, glancing inside the house.

"She is temporarily staying at Merlin's house, with Chris," Elder Taylor explained, and I am the only one here at the moment.

"Is there something wrong?" Hobbs lowered his head, his expression becoming complex.

"What's the matter, Hobbs? You don't look good," Elder Taylor felt that Hobbs was not the same as usual.

"I actually have a request. I hope Elder Taylor can help me," Hobbs said, his tone hesitant.

"What is it?" Elder Taylor became serious.

"Please take care of Mini. I have something to do and must leave Rexum," Hobbs said.

Elder Taylor was stunned, as his home had almost become a daycare center for Rexum, but recently, he had been asked to help take care of children.

However, Elder Taylor felt very strange because Hobbs rarely needed to leave Rexum. Was something serious happening?

"What's going on? Do you need my help? Just speak up."

"Hobbs pretended to be embarrassed and explained, 'This is a matter you shouldn't interfere with. I and my wife had an argument, and she left home in a huff. I need to go and bring her back.'"

"Oh~" Elder Taylor immediately understood, as domestic issues were not something he was good at interfering with, "I understand. Don't worry, I will take care of her. As I said, what can't be resolved between a husband and wife? You should be more considerate of your wife a little."

"Yes, yes, it's all my fault," Hobbs nodded repeatedly, reminding himself, "Please take good care of Mini until I return."

After Hobbs left, Elder Taylor took Mini into Lucy's room and planned for her to stay there. However, when Elder Taylor was helping Mini get into bed, he noticed that she was wearing Hobbs' black iron adventurer's certificate.

Elder Taylor was shocked. This item is used to prove identity, how can it be worn by a child?

Recalling Hobbs' expression when he left and his unusual behavior, Elder Taylor finally realized that something was wrong. He rushed outside but found that Hobbs had already disappeared into the night, as if he had never been there.

"Hobbs, what's going on?"

In the secret weapon library of the Holy Temple in the Holy City, the Hell Gate was open, and there were no guards. A figure entered here, and it was Hobbs, who had just left Rexum.
