He slowly approached the spear named "Crimson Beauty," which had not found a new owner since Joan of Arc and was stored here.

Hobbs picked up the red spear and gently caressed it. The spear body trembled slightly, as if it had met an old friend, making him extremely excited.

He took a deep breath and suddenly gripped the spear firmly, dancing it skillfully in circles, trying to find the familiar feeling.

After a long time, Hobbs looked up, his expression sharp and resolute, obviously the eyes of someone who had gone through countless battles.

"Merlin, don't walk my path."

"You can't succeed, I will personally stop you."

content:
Chapter 3 — TITLE: Settling Accounts <<<BEGIN SOURCE>>> SOURCE TEXT: <<<END SOURCE>>>

Volume 39 · Chapter 3

Twelve oil lamps had already gone out more than halfway, with only the last three still burning. The moment Alice's consciousness was about to dissipate was imminent.

Fortunately, Merlin had not wasted a single moment and pressed straight for the Ninth Layer of Hell.

After felling multiple vile spirits guarding the layers below, Merlin successfully entered the Seventh Layer of Hell —

This was the place where the cruel were imprisoned. Most people born with a tyrannical nature throughout history had been gathered here, primarily kings and high nobles.

After all, most of those in high positions of power had ample conditions to brutally oppress the common folk, so they made up the largest population in this layer.

What greeted Merlin's eyes was an endless lake of blood, within which drowned the bone remains of countless sinners. Their flesh had long since corroded away completely, and skull after skull floated upon the surface of the blood pool from time to time.

Merlin had no boat, and when it came to crossing the River Styx, that helmsman Charon had been personally dealt with by Merlin's own hand.

In his desperation, Merlin tried wading across the endless river of blood before him. Fortunately, the blood pool was not deep — it could only reach his waist. With that, Merlin finally felt reassured and kept walking forward. Leaving this place meant entering the Eighth Layer of Hell, and the palace where Satan resided was already very close.

Suddenly, Merlin felt someone grabbing his foot from beneath the blood pool, which sent his heart racing. He drew Banri Garan behind him and, regardless of consequences, prepared to plunge it hard into the bottom of the pool to eliminate whoever was blocking his path.

Since arriving in Hell, Merlin had encountered too many unknown monsters, all of them incredibly ferocious. They were the lackeys who pledged allegiance to Satan, and one careless move would leave him trapped here forever.

So Merlin was extremely cautious, always on guard against unknown dangers. But this time he hesitated, his sword hovering in mid-air, refusing to fall — because the "enemy" at the bottom of the pool had already surfaced of its own accord. It was —

"Teacher Merlin?"

"Miranda!?"

Merlin saw Miranda's soul. Unlike the scattered bones floating around her, her body remained relatively intact, with less severe corrosion.

Considering when Miranda had died, it had been roughly three years ago. Such a short time was not enough to completely corrode a soul.

From this, it seemed that those who fell into the Seventh Layer of Hell would endure the pain of corrosion until their consciousness completely vanished — and before that complete corrosion, there was no relief.

For Miranda to end her suffering, it would probably take decades. This was undoubtedly a torment beyond ordinary imagination.

And once a soul fell into Hell, it lost all the power it had possessed in life, becoming prey at the mercy of others.

Only those undead who willingly submitted to Satan would regain the strength they had in life, and if Satan favored them, they would receive the blessing of a Principal God, greatly increasing their power.

Those chosen apostles were exactly like that — undoubtedly the lucky ones in Hell. Unfortunately, they were the rare minority; the vast majority would suffer inhuman torments in Hell.

Satan was the absolute ruler of Hell, controlling the souls of the dead. But Merlin was an exception — he had not died. He was a living person walking through Hell.

Merlin was deeply shocked to see Miranda and could not understand why someone as kind as she would be here enduring torment?

Although Miranda was a demon, Merlin believed she had not committed any unforgivable crimes, nor did she deserve to suffer the agony of the blood pool's corrosion.

"Miranda, why are you in the Seventh Layer? Have you done something cruel?"

"No, I came here on my own to see my brother," Miranda quickly answered.

Merlin suddenly paused, and then understood. Belial was indeed cruel among the Demon Lords, so it made no sense that she would end up here.

"Your brother is here too?"

"Yes. His situation is far worse than mine. He endures beatings and curses every single day," Miranda said sorrowfully, lifting her head. "Teacher Merlin, please help us. Save my brother. We are about to go mad here. There is no way to end this cruel torment."

Merlin's heart softened. Although he was here to rescue Alice, he could not simply ignore what was happening before his eyes.

"Where is your brother?"

"Not far from here. He is bound to a tree by the ruler of the Seventh Layer, whipped mercilessly every day," Miranda cried.

"Who is the ruler of the Seventh Layer?" Merlin asked. He already knew that each layer of Hell had a warden, and he had already dealt with several blockers along the way.

"Mammon! It's Mammon! He sold his soul and submitted to Satan, then flaunted his authority cruelly, taking pleasure in torturing my brother," Miranda bitterly accused.

"Mammon? He is actually the ruler of this layer!?"

Merlin frowned. There were too many acquaintances from the Seventh Layer, he mused. But that Mammon would fall into the Seventh Layer of Hell and submit to Satan as a lackey — that did not surprise him at all.

Because that was exactly the kind of creature Mammon was — brutally pressuring the weak and groveling to the strong. He appeared utterly without dignity, but in truth it was simply his way of getting by.

However, hearing that Mammon, now a ruler, used whips to torment his former companions was something Merlin could not tolerate. What was there to be proud of about being a dog?

"As expected of Mammon. I still slightly underestimated the depth of his shamelessness. Take me to him."

In the center of the blood pool lay the only small island, topped with a withered tree.

And the soul of Belial was bound there, the sound of cracking whips ringing out from time to time.

Mammon's appearance had changed drastically. Countless undead heads grew from his body, making him look particularly hideous.

This Demon Lord of Greed had abandoned all dignity, begging Satan for forgiveness, and in return received the position of Warden of the Seventh Layer along with the restoration of his former strength.

The swinging whip came to a halt. Mammon panted heavily, his flab trembling, and took a swig of strong liquor, intending to rest for a moment —

"Belial, do you look down on me that much?"

"Submitting to Lord Satan is far more comfortable than soaking in a blood pool~"

"Look at me. Don't you envy me? Unfortunately, you no longer have that chance."

Belial kept his head lowered. His body had already been lashed open, revealing pale bone beneath. Slowly, he raised his head.

"You are truly a disgrace to demons. Would I envy you? Don't make me laugh. You really are hopeless — acting so superior even after becoming a dog."

"What did you say?" Mammon's expression twisted狰狞, raising his whip once more. "If you had supported my expansionist policy back then, would I have ended up like this today!? It's all your fault, you foolish conservatives! It's all your fault! I will slowly whip you into meat paste, and then eat you as an appetizer!"

"Stop it!"

The shout rang out suddenly. Mammon froze, turning to look, and a look of disbelief spread across his face.

"Lucifer?"

Merlin glared at Mammon and silently tightened his grip on the hilt at his waist. Miranda, terrified, shrank behind him.

Belial raised his head in astonishment and saw Miranda. In a panic, he called out, "Miranda! Why have you come here? Leave quickly!"

"Brother! I'm here to save you!" Miranda called out loudly.

"Lucifer — why are you appearing here!?" Belial was extremely puzzled.

"Need I ask? Lucifer is already dead! He followed in our footsteps and came to Hell as well!" Mammon's eyes widened, his expression growing extraordinarily agitated, as though this were a gift from heaven —

"Lucifer! You have ruined me! You are partly responsible for what I've become!"

"How does Hell feel? Have you discovered that you've lost all your power?"

"That's right! You are no longer that young Demon Lord who once shook the world — you are now just another undead spirit of Hell!"

"This is wonderful! I never thought I would have the chance for revenge. Let's settle this score properly."

title: Chapter 4 — Plea (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 4 — Plea (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 39 · Chapter 4

*Let go, Mammon, look at how ugly you look now Merlin had a solemn expression, never expecting that Mammon would hate himself so much even after death. "Stop putting on an act in front of me! If it weren't for you stopping me, would my plan have failed?!" Mammon's expression was ferocious, resentfully saying, "You traitor who secretly communicates with humans, even after falling into Hell you're still pretending?" Merlin didn't answer; it seemed Mammon didn't realize he wasn't dead at all, still thinking he and it were the same, having arrived in Hell after death, "I am a traitor, then what are you now? Serving Satan without dignity, showing off against former comrades, your heart is as ugly as yours, inside and out the same." "Shut up! You're not qualified to blame me!" Mammon angrily whipped his whip, lashing toward Merlin— a crisp sound; Merlin didn't dodge at all, a red mark appeared on his face. "Merlin teacher?" Miranda beside him felt shocked, not knowing what Merlin was thinking. "Are you satisfied? Your death is somewhat related to me; this whip is my doing." Merlin's eyes burned like torches, thinking Mammon was killed by Cain, while he himself was the one who released Cain, making the causality hard to untangle now. "Satisfied? If I don't torture you to the point of wishing for death, how could I be satisfied? One whip is like settling scores? You're dreaming!" Mammon swung his whip again, lashing toward Merlin, still thinking Merlin was just a soul fallen into Hell, with no power to resist him, making his whip merely for show. Merlin was quick-eyed and quick-handed, grabbing the whip Mammon swung, and scolded, "I warn you, don't push your luck; now release Beelzebub, and I can spare your life!" "Haha, interesting, you won't think you're still alive, will you? You're no longer a Demon Lord, just a stray dog fallen into Hell, and you dare to negotiate with me?" Mammon's grin gradually became wild. "Tch!" Merlin suddenly jerked the whip, hauling Mammon's huge body up and then slamming it hard into the blood pool on the other side. Boom! A loud roar, Mammon screamed in pain, the calm blood pool rippled with waves— "Merlin?" Beelzebub felt something was off; logically, dead people coming here would have their former strength stripped, why can Merlin still resist? "Mammon coughed up from the ground, eyes filled with disbelief, "Why? Why can you still resist me? "Mammon, open your eyes and look well, am I really a dead person?!" Merlin shouted. "Huh!" Mammon saw Merlin's reflection in the blood pool; a spirit cannot have a shadow, you're not dead!" "Of course, I came here as a living person!" Merlin said solemnly. "How is this possible? When did Hell and the mortal world become connected?" Mammon had no idea about the Hell's gate, his face showing a hint of panic. "You're just one of Satan's many lackeys, the most insignificant; it's normal not to know." Merlin said bluntly. "You! Mammon felt anger rising, seeing Merlin appear in Hell, he still felt a bit of schadenfreude, but upon realizing Merlin wasn't dead, he instantly became jealous. This young Demon Lord who caused his own fall into Hell not only didn't die, but is freely hopping around in Hell—who could bear that? If Merlin were to become depraved like Mammon, Mammon's heart would become unbalanced, eventually turning entirely into hatred toward Merlin. "I want you to die! Lucifer!" Mammon's eyes bloodshot, the bones in the nearby blood pool all trembled, piling onto his body, quickly fusing together! In just a few moments, Mammon turned into a massive monster covered in bones, like a human centipede, wildly churning in the blood pool! Mammon opened his bloody maw, lunging at Merlin, the entire Seventh Layer of Hell echoing with the most vicious curses: "You, who have become Satan's lackey, are no longer fit to exist." Merlin silently watched the furious Mammon, without a word drew his blade, a murderous sword aura exploded, the rending storm shredding the huge Mammon into countless fragments! Mammon merely restored his former strength, without receiving Satan's blessing; in terms of power, he might even be weaker than those Hell apostles who have been blessed. "Merlin, you" Mammon was utterly unwilling, but before his final curse could be spoken, he breathed his last; dying in Hell means existence completely erased— Miranda rescued Beelzebub from the withered tree, throwing herself into her brother's arms. "Brother!" "I'm fine, don't cry." Beelzebub gritted his teeth, enduring the pain throughout his body, constantly comforting his weeping sister, not wanting to let Miranda feel sad because of him. "Thank you, Lucifer." "It's nothing, just a small effort." Merlin replied lightly. "Why are you here?" Beelzebub asked. "Merlin wanted to speak but hesitated, feeling no need to hide anymore, 'I came to save my wife.' "Is that the human woman? Beelzebub looked at Merlin's eyes, already knowing the answer, 'I had a vague guess, you really did fall for a human.' "If you want to say something to dissuade me, just forget it." Merlin looked at Beelzebub. "No, I'm already dead, what's the point of dissuading? You won't listen anyway." Beelzebub paused, then continued, "That human woman, aside from a bad temper, is passable enough; after all, she has no ill intentions, how did she die?" "It's a long story; I'm not sure of the cause of death yet." Merlin shook his head. "Not possible at all." Beelzebub sighed, then asked, "How is the demon race now?" "Behemoth is already dead; all demons have abandoned the Demon Lord Palace, gathering instead in Demon City." "That puts my mind at ease; as long as the demon race retains a spark, the future will blaze again." Beelzebub's expression relaxed considerably. "Shall I take you out of here?" Merlin asked. "It's useless; even if you bring our souls out of Hell, we can never live again, we'll only become wandering souls." Beelzebub refused Merlin's kindness. Merlin suddenly recalled that to be resurrected, besides bringing back Alice's soul, he also needs a tremendous amount of life force. Even if he brings Beelzebub and Miranda out of Hell, without immense life force they still cannot revive. According to the landlady, Chris possesses vast life force, but it's still far from enough to resurrect the dead. Nevertheless, bringing Alice's soul out of Hell at least fulfills one condition for resurrection; coming to Hell isn't entirely useless. "That truly—" "Lucifer, can you help us?" Beelzebub pleaded in a beseeching tone. "What?" "Please, just erase us completely."

title: Chapter 5 — Seduction
content:
Chapter 5 — Seduction

Volume 39 · Chapter 5

"What nonsense are you saying, Beelzebub?" Merlin thought he had misheard; Beelzebub actually wanted him to completely exterminate him, just like killing Mammon. "I will be serious, Merlin," Beelzebub paused, his calm tone as if he had already accepted his final fate, "The undead cannot leave here on their own, nor can they commit suicide; take a good look at the bones floating here." Merlin looked around; those unlucky ones corroded clean by the blood pool could no longer be identified. The undead cannot rely on themselves to end their lives; they must endure the torment until their consciousness completely dissipates, unable to escape the pain. "You see? Those piles of bones are my and Miranda's ending," Beelzebub said, holding Miranda seriously, "This process is painful and lengthy; you're still alive, unable to understand our feelings; rather than endure endless torment, it's better to give us a quick end." "No! I didn't come to do this!" Merlin firmly refused Beelzebub's request, really unable to bring himself to do it. "Merlin, this is our choice; we won't blame you; what you need to do is free us from pain; do you really want to watch our siblings suffer and die here in torment?" Beelzebub spoke sincerely, hoping for release. "Sorry, I can't," Merlin lowered his head; although Beelzebub made sense, he felt immense psychological pressure, guilt impossible to erase. "Merlin teacher, please help us," Miranda also pleaded, being able to die together with her brother is already the best outcome, "My brother and I will eventually die here; if you refuse to help us, we'll have to endure prolonged torment until our bodies completely rot to gain release; this process is too long, we can only passively choose to endure." Merlin frowned sternly, saying, "Why must I do this?" "Besides you, no one can do it; we won't hate you, only feel genuine gratitude," Beelzebub said with a smile. Merlin exhaled, his arms partially demonized, he pried open a section of the demon sword Banri Garan at his waist, and scorching flames instantly burst forth! The intense heat scorched the seventh layer of Hell; the blood pool surged, nearly boiling! Beelzebub and Miranda, siblings, embraced in the flames and were instantly turned to ash. The high temperature of Banri Garan would instantly incinerate them; before they could feel pain, they'd be turned to ash. Merlin tried to lessen the siblings' pain; he didn't know if what he did was right or wrong, only feeling his guilt weigh heavily— Farewell. Sorry I couldn't save you; the only thing I could do was end your suffering.

Satan's palace, Alice in the golden cage stared intently at the oil lamp before her. Another oil lamp went out again; at this moment only two lamps remained burning. This meant Alice's time was running short; when all the lamps went out, her consciousness would vanish and she would marry Satan as his wife. Time became extremely urgent; Alice's mood grew tense as the lamps dwindled, and she couldn't help but start wild speculations— How much time is left with the last two oil lamps? What should I do? How can I escape this predicament? Merlin, does he know my situation? No, even if he did, what difference would it make? This is hell; only the dead can come here. It seems Merlin really isn't coming back this time; do I have to accept the fate Satan has arranged for me? Alice's eyes lost their luster as she curled up in the corner of the cage, silent; although she felt deeply low, a sliver of hope still remained. After all, Merlin always returns at the most crucial moments to be by Alice's side; perhaps this time will be the same— even if he's in another world, he'll rush over to save her. "Our wedding is drawing near; how do you feel now?" "You're dreaming! I will never marry you!" Alice stood up and shouted at the suddenly appearing Satan; for this pervert, she felt no affection. "Heh, I'd like to see how long you can hold to your stance; when all the lamps go out, then you won't have a choice," Satan said smugly. "You won't succeed," Alice gritted her teeth, appearing strong on the surface but inside she had already begun to panic. "Let me guess: do you still harbor a sliver of hope, wishing your husband will come to save you?" Satan asked meaningfully. Alice's heart jolted; she hadn't expected that her deepest thoughts had already been seen through by Satan. "It seems I guessed right, but I advise you to discard this notion, for I have just learned something; do you want to hear it?" Satan's tone began to waver. "Stop pretending here!" Alice frowned. "I could tell you, but it would make you feel very sad; I'm hesitant," Satan said, shaking his head. "What are you hesitating about? Speak!" Alice felt a bead of cold sweat slide down her forehead, wondering if something had happened to Merlin or Chris. "Well," The words had barely left his mouth when Satan lightly gestured in the void, and an incredibly lifelike image appeared before Alice— It was a wedding, seemingly taking place in the British palace, with guests all people Alice knew well. Mesfield wore a white wedding gown, holding Merlin's arm, beaming with happiness. Merlin wore a black suit, continually waving to the guests, his face full of springtime pride. The newlyweds together received the blessing of the British queen, and little Chris personally presented a bouquet to the new mother. Although it was only an illusion, it felt too real, as if it had just happened recently, recorded by Satan. After seeing it, Alice went blank, her expression dazed, her mind in turmoil; she clutched her head and curled up— Has Merlin found a new love? Even my daughter has forgotten me? No! This can't be; it's too fast, everything happened too quickly. "This isn't real! You're lying to me!" "Theresa, my love for you is utterly sincere; why would I deceive you? This is what just happened a short while ago." Satan paused, then continued his seduction, "It's regrettable that not only that man betrayed you, but even your daughter is no exception; the love you've given them is worthless; only I will cherish you, and yet you still don't understand?" "Fake! All of it's fake!" Alice refused to believe; yet deep down she began to waver. "You're so pitiful, Theresa; what's the point of deceiving yourself? Isn't it hard to admit you misjudged someone?" Satan feigned sympathy. Alice's mind was in chaos; she clutched her hair, her face turned pale, her mental defenses crumbling— Did Merlin abandon me without hesitation? Is that true? The relationship between that female knight and Merlin seems to have indeed surpassed ordinary friendship. What should I do now?

title: Chapter 6 — Repeating the Same Mistake (Monthly Ticket Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 6 — Repeating the Same Mistake (Monthly Ticket Extra Chapter)

Volume 39 · Chapter 6

Hell’s eighth layer, the gathering place of fraudsters, is where anyone who told a lie in the mortal world is imprisoned.
In fact, there is no one who has never lied, and the eighth layer of Hell also holds the greatest number of dead.
Merlin saw many spirits lining up along the way, leaping into the boiling oil cauldron—this is the punishment for deceivers.
Plop, plop, plop—
The sound of the great oil cauldron splashing continued without end; from afar it looked like dropping dumplings, sending a chill down one’s spine.
Merlin did not linger here; he rushed straight to the end of Hell’s eighth layer, worried he would not arrive in time to stop Alice and Satan’s wedding.
But upon reaching the end of the eighth layer, Merlin was blocked by a towering wall unlike anything before, unable to proceed to the next layer.
While Merlin was at a loss, preparing to smash the wall by force, he noticed a woman embedded in the wall, only her shoulders and above exposed.
She had golden hair, her dignified countenance giving off a sense of holiness, starkly different from the ferocious spirits commonly seen in Hell.
The blonde woman did not lift her head, yet she could still sense Merlin, speaking patiently, “This is not where you should be, spirit. The eighth layer of Hell is where deceivers are punished.”
“I am not a spirit; I wish to enter the ninth layer of Hell, but the wall around you blocks me,” Merlin explained.
The blonde woman trembled all over; she had seen many lost spirits, but none had claimed not to be a spirit before. She slowly raised her head, “You’re not a spirit?!”
“An apostle?!”
Merlin furrowed his brows, seeing the mark on the woman’s left cheek!
“II”
This signified Hell’s third apostle; having arrived in this region, Merlin finally met a new apostle.
Merlin immediately grew wary, gripping the hilt of his knife at his waist, his eyes flashing with hostility.
“Not a spirit? Then who are you?” the blonde woman questioned, puzzled.
“I am a living person,” Merlin replied solemnly, though he noticed the third apostle seemed gentle, as if one could reason with her.
“A living person? Hell is no place for the living; you should leave quickly, or it will be too late,” the blonde woman urged anxiously.
“I cannot leave; I have come to save my wife,” Merlin paused, then asked, “So do you know how to get through this wall? If not, I will have to destroy you and the wall together.”
“You’ve come to save your wife? What nonsense, another stubborn one,” the blonde woman’s expression grew complex, as if she saw a familiar shadow in Merlin.
“What do you mean?” Merlin pressed, seeing her expression, as if it weren’t only he who had come to Hell to save his wife.
“I advise you to turn back; no one has ever succeeded in taking a soul from Hell, and all that awaits you is endless suffering,” the blonde woman kindly advised.
“Why? How would you know without trying?” Merlin was not convinced.
“You don’t understand—Satan is the ruler of Hell, he controls everything here. To take a soul from here is to oppose the supreme god; can you defeat an existence that transcends all rules?” the blonde woman tried to make Merlin realize what he was doing.
“Why not?” Merlin countered, then slowly said, “You are unlike the other spirits here; what is your name?”
“I am Gwendolin; I should not be here either, for Satan is using me to restrain someone.”
The blonde woman did not hide anything, directly giving her name—she is none other than the wife of the spear‑wielding Hero O’Brien, the beautiful flower of the Holy City!
“Who?”
“My husband, my husband is somewhat like you; he once entered Hell as a living person, trying to rescue me from here, but we failed—Satan deceived us,” Gwendolin said, lowering her gaze at her body fused with the wall, her voice sinking.
“As you can see, because of me, my husband is forever trapped in Hell; he could have left and continued living in the mortal world, yet he stayed for my sake and is forced to serve Satan.”
“So I hope you leave before you sink deeper; perhaps there is still time, so you won’t end up like us.”
“I know your grief over losing your wife, but if you insist on rescuing her, you will surely pay a terrible price.”
Merlin fell silent—he had not expected that besides himself, another living person had come to Hell seeking to take a soul away.
Although Merlin did not know O’Brien’s story, the woman’s fate before him also served as a warning.
Yet Merlin had no intention of heeding Gwendolin’s advice; having already reached the eighth layer of Hell, there was no turning back.
Moreover, Satan’s forced marriage of Alice to him was imminent, and Merlin could not possibly stand by and do nothing.
“Thank you for your warning, but nothing can stop me. I sympathize with your plight, but you are not me, and in my eyes those lofty gods are not invincible.”
“My husband once thought the same, yet reality proved even crueler than imagined,” Gwendolin said solemnly.
“I won’t concern myself with all that; this is my decision,” Merlin paused, then demanded, “Tell me, how do I get through this wall?”
Gwendolin sighed, giving up persuasion, “Kill me, and this wall will naturally collapse.”
“Really?” Merlin tightened his grip on the knife hilt, not caring about anything else, “Then I’ll offend you—no matter what, you are still an apostle of Hell.”
“Could you wait a moment before killing me? Sir, I know I am no match for you, but I wish to see my husband one last time,” Gwendolin pleaded in a beseeching tone.
Such a request, under normal circumstances, Merlin might have granted, for it was not excessive.
But now Merlin’s heart burned with urgency; he wanted to rescue Alice as soon as possible, how could he waste time here?
“Sorry, I cannot waste too much time here; I cannot fulfill your request.”
“Really not possible? Well, in the end it’s just my vain hope,” Gwendolin slowly closed her eyes, as if she had already accepted her fate.
Merlin drew a deep breath, assumed the sword‑drawing stance, prepared to strike down the third apostle before him and open the road to Hell’s ninth layer.
Just as Merlin was about to act, a shout suddenly came from behind, interrupting his move—
“Stop! Merlin!”
Hearing that familiar voice, Merlin jerked his head back, seeing Hobbs standing there with a spear, though he did not know when he had arrived.
“Hobbs? Why are you here?!”
“Sorry, Merlin, I am here to stop you,” Hobbs replied with a stern expression.
“Why?!”
“Because . . . Hobbs wanted to speak but stopped, bit his tongue, and stuck it out for Merlin to see—there, clearly printed—
‘IV’
This death‑laden mark appeared on Hobbs’s tongue, signifying his identity as
Hell’s fourth apostle!”

title: Chapter 7 — O'Brien
content:
Chapter 7 — O'Brien

Volume 39 · Chapter 7

Hobbs,

Merlin stared at Hobbs in front of him, his eyes wide with shock, words failing him, his heart a tangled mess.

He had never dreamed of such a thing. So the apostle that Mephisto said was by his side — it was Hobbs!

This old man who often drank and boasted with him was actually a hound of Hell as well? It completely exceeded Merlin's expectations!

Merlin gritted his teeth, feeling that things had become incredibly complicated. He lowered his head and questioned seriously.

"Why? Why are even you an apostle?"

"Sorry for deceiving you for so long." Hobbs's expression was complex as he continued, "I became an apostle a long time ago. In the mortal realm, I was carrying out the tasks Satan assigned me, stoking conflicts whenever possible."

Gwendoline inside the wall suddenly paused, surprised, and asked, "Didn't you say you wouldn't do bad things in the mortal realm? Why deliberately stir up conflicts?"

*I'm sorry, Gwendoline. I deceived you. Satan wants to expand Hell's power and desires more powerful souls to fall into Hell. I was left with no choice.* Hobbs paused and said softly, *Besides, I did all this for you. If I hadn't done things properly, you would have suffered torture like the other undead. Satan promised me that as long as I completed my tasks, you could leave the wall and be free!*

Gwendoline stood dumbfounded and lowered her head sadly. *Why would you still believe that infamous god? He won't keep his promises. He'll only toy with us endlessly.*

*This time will definitely work!* Hobbs's eyes were filled with obsession as he said firmly, *I swear, although I can't take you away from Hell, I can reduce your suffering!*

Merlin frowned and had already realized something, so he asked, "Hobbs, could she be your wife?"

"That's right, she's the wife I've never shown to anyone." Hobbs lowered his head and said softly, "Merlin, take my advice — call it quits. You can't succeed."

"Hobbs..." Merlin stared at him and spoke loudly, "You've already come this far! And you want me to give up? On what grounds!"

"I was once like you, wanting to take Gwendoline away from Hell, but that's impossible." Hobbs lifted his head and advised, "If you don't want to be trapped in Hell forever like me, you should stop now and accept the fact that Alice is dead!"

"I can't accept that. Don't compare me to you, Hobbs." Merlin's gaze was sharp as he said gravely, "What you cannot do, I can! I will kill Satan and destroy the entire order of Hell, ending the suffering of all the undead!"

"You can't do it. Only a True God can kill a True God. No one can break that rule. I know you're powerful, but True Gods are on the level of world builders — you can't handle them." Hobbs explained, hoping Merlin would realize it was too difficult and back off, avoiding the same fate as himself.

"I don't believe it. How would I know without trying? If you're here to persuade me to stop, then just shut up. I won't listen to any advice." Merlin turned around and looked at Gwendoline. *Now I'm going to destroy this wall and go have a word with this guy called Satan.*

Seeing Merlin about to destroy the wall, which would clearly cost Gwendoline her life — if the wall was damaged, Gwendoline's existence would also be erased.

As her husband, Hobbs could not tolerate this. He immediately gripped his spear, Crimson Temptress, and took a stance ready to fight Merlin to the death.

"Stop it, Merlin! I won't let you do this!"

Hobbs. Merlin glanced back slightly and gave him a look. *You think you can stop me?*

Hobbs stared into Merlin's eyes and suddenly began to laugh, as if recalling past events. *I never thought the little devil who once trembled in terror while clutching his sister would grow to reach this level. I wonder if letting you go back then was the wrong choice?*

*What are you talking about?* Merlin's brows tightened, a bitter taste rising in his heart.

Hobbs wielded his spear skillfully and assumed a stance that was incredibly familiar to Merlin, asking, *You haven't forgotten me, have you? Your Highness, the Prince of the First Demon Lord Palace.*

"Huh!"

Merlin's eyes widened, cold sweat beading on his forehead as his breathing grew heavy.

The stance Hobbs was in now — Merlin knew it all too well. It had startled him awake countless times in his sleep!

This opening posture of the attack was identical to that of the Spear Hero O'Brien!

If Hobbs wasn't O'Brien's disciple, then he must be...

"Hobbs, could it be..."

"That's right. I am the Spear Hero O'Brien, who once drove you to the brink of despair." Hobbs did not hide it but revealed everything.

"You—!"

Merlin's expression changed drastically. Encountering the man from his nightmare again made him unable to remain composed.

How many years had the nightmare of the Spear Hero tormented him? Only he knew best.

He had thought that after the Spear Hero disappeared, he would never encounter him again. But he never expected to meet him once more in Hell!

Merlin's face darkened. He subconsciously clenched his fists, suppressing the anger in his heart.

"Why has your appearance changed so much?"

*To carry out the tasks Satan assigned me, I returned to the mortal realm and could no longer use the identity of the Spear Hero. So Satan personally changed my appearance, turning me into a slovenly drunkard. This did help me deceive everyone.* Hobbs paused and said meaningfully, *Actually, I recognized your identity from the very beginning. I was also surprised that you left the demon race to live in a human kingdom. Having played along with you for so long, I've grown tired of it, Lucifer III.*

*Why didn't you kill me back then?* Merlin demanded in a low tone.

*Because you were too weak back then. Attacking a helpless enemy would sully my name as a Hero. To put it plainly, you weren't worthy of dying by my spear.* O'Brien said seriously.

*Heh.* Merlin let out a sinister laugh as he looked straight into Hobbs's eyes. *How many more things have you been hiding from me? I don't even know whether to call you Hobbs or O'Brien.*

*That depends on your choice. If you leave Hell now, I'm Hobbs. But if you continue deeper into the lower levels of Hell, then I'm your enemy, O'Brien.*

*It seems there's no way out. I can't give up halfway. You want to save your wife, and so do I!* Merlin gripped the hilt of his sword at his waist, looking at Hobbs as if looking at a stranger —

*O'Brien, one of us will remain here forever.*

*It's time to settle things from back then.*

title: Chapter 8 — Choice
content:
Chapter 8 — Choice

Volume 39 · Chapter 8

Both of them stared into each other's eyes, ready to reenact their past duel in hell.

For Merlin, Obrien was his nightmare, an existence he had to overcome.

Although Merlin had some feelings for Hobbes, the one who had drunk with him, he couldn't stop here.

"I can still remember how terrified you looked when you were young, but now you've become a true warrior." Hobbes said in a low voice.

"Forget about the past, Obrien." Merlin said coldly.

Gwendolyn saw the two about to engage in a deadly battle before her eyes, and her heart was extremely anxious.

She wanted to stop this meaningless fight, and didn't want Obrien to do bad things for her sake.

Gwendolyn felt it was all her fault, if she completely disappeared, would Obrien be able to live a better life?

However, the tension between the two grew thicker, and Gwendolyn couldn't find any opportunity to stop them—

The two almost charged at the same time, the collision of their powers causing the eighth layer of hell to shake violently!

Obrien was the last legendary Hero, after him, no Hero could surpass his strength, the legendary Hero era had completely ended!

In the past, Obrien's strength was only half-god, but after becoming an apostle and receiving Satan's blessing, his strength surged, reaching the pinnacle of power that ordinary people couldn't climb, the realm of gods!

For someone who relied solely on bitter cultivation, without any extraordinary encounters or resource blessings, half-god might be the ultimate realm that ordinary people could reach, to improve further, luck was the decisive factor!

Hobbes' long spear danced out countless afterimages, his skilled techniques actually made Merlin feel a bit of pressure, constantly pushing him back.

Merlin dodged continuously, gritting his teeth and glaring at Hobbes, subconsciously turning the tachi at his waist, he was still soft-hearted after all.

Although Merlin's words were merciless, appearing very cold, the memories were still vivid in his mind.

The man before him had accompanied him drinking and boasting every day, comforting and answering his doubts like an older brother.

To make Merlin kill him without hesitation, he would have to put down all his memories and become a cold killing machine.

"Hobbes! Are you serious? You're still alive, do you have to fight to the death?"

"You want to save Alice, so you'll kill my wife and destroy this wall, I won't allow that to happen!" Hobbes' attack became even fiercer as he shouted, "As long as you don't give up on saving Alice, only one of us can live!"

Merlin's cheek was slashed, making him even angrier, "Hmph! Your wife is already dead!"

"That's what I should be saying! Alice is already dead! Why are you so obsessed? In the end, we're all selfish!" Hobbes shouted loudly.

"Nonsense!"

Merlin suddenly drew his sword, using the back of the blade to heavily strike Hobbes, his strength was far inferior to Mephisto's.

If Merlin wanted to take down Hobbes, it would probably only take an instant.

But Merlin wanted to make Hobbes realize his mistake, self-pity was extremely foolish—

Obrien had never asked Gwendolyn about her own wishes, did she want to come back to life? To avoid his own suffering, it was okay to push his wife to the evil side?

These things Obrien didn't understand at all, he simply thought this was love for his wife, he couldn't bear to see his wife suffer in hell.

But Merlin knew this wasn't love, it was Obrien's arrogance from the bottom of his heart!

Hobbes raised his long spear to block, but couldn't withstand Merlin's terrifying strength, and was sent flying, heavily crashing into a giant oil cauldron.

Boom! The oil cauldron collapsed, the half-fried wraiths on the ground writhed continuously, emitting waves of painful wails.

Hobbes endured the burns on his back, staggering to his feet, knowing he wasn't Merlin's match, but to prevent his wife from being completely erased, he had no choice.

"Merlin!!"

"You should calm down, look at your current state, is this what your wife wants to see? Have you ever asked for her thoughts?" Merlin scolded.

"I've done everything for my wife's happiness!"

Hobbes gathered his strength again, frantically pouring power into his long spear Scarlet Demoness, a dazzling red light burst out, completely enveloping him.

At this moment, Hobbes was like a bullet ready to fire, his terrifying strength causing the ground beneath his feet to crack like a spider web!

Hobbes' eyes locked, his feet crushing the land behind him, he charged at Merlin with all his might, in the blink of an eye he was before Merlin, his sharp spear pointing straight at his opponent's throat!

Merlin remained calm, turning the tachi in his hand, the blade's edge gleaming, it seemed he was about to get serious!

Merlin's ghostly figure slightly shifted, his long knife slashed down, cutting Hobbes' long spear in two!

Immediately after, Merlin punched Hobbes in the face, pressing the knife against his neck, saying coldly.

"You're not my match, continuing to fight is just humiliating yourself."

Hobbes' face turned ashen, he was completely no match for Merlin, he could see that Merlin had been holding back.

"Kill me, Merlin, you've won."

"Do you think I don't dare to?" Merlin frowned, the knife leaving a blood mark on Hobbes' neck.

"Stop! Don't hurt him, please!" Gwendolyn shouted loudly, "Aren't you trying to enter the ninth layer of hell to save your wife? Then kill me instead!"

"Gwendolyn!" Hobbes was shocked, pleading, "Merlin, spare my wife, I'll do anything you say."

Merlin frowned, this made things very difficult, Gwendolyn and the wall were one entity, this wall was also blocking his plan to save Alice, he didn't want to be the villain, but the current situation required him to make the right choice.

"Enough, Obrien, don't do bad things for me anymore, I don't want to see you like this, I'm very disappointed in you," Gwendolyn said tearfully.

Hobbes wanted to explain, but didn't know where to start.

"I still like the old you, cold outside but warm inside, a kind person, you shouldn't become Satan's dog, helping him do evil in the mortal world." Gwendolyn paused, feeling immense pressure, "If all of this is for me, then it's better to let me go early, I don't want to implicate you, making you forever unable to escape Satan's control."

"Gwendolyn, no... it's not like that." Hobbes' lips moved.

"I'm already satisfied to see you again, Obrien, don't continue doing bad things, live well, this is my own choice, I hope you respect it." Gwendolyn's tone was like saying her final goodbye—

"That Mr. Merlin, please do it.

"I hope you can succeed in saving your wife, don't be like us..."

"Repeating the same mistakes."

title: Chapter 9 — Heavenly Realm (Monthly Ticket Extra)
content:
Chapter 9 — Heavenly Realm (Monthly Ticket Extra)

Volume 39 · Chapter 9

"Gwendolin!"

Hobbs screamed until his voice cracked, but it couldn't change the outcome. He couldn't stop Merlin; he could only watch helpless as his wife vanished before his eyes.

With Merlin's hand rising and the blade falling, Gwendolin—the Flower of the Holy City—collapsed along with the despairing wall, and the path to the Ninth Circle of Hell revealed itself.

Hobbs clutched his broken spear tightly, wanting to fight Merlin to the death and stop Gwendolin from disappearing.

But then he remembered her resolute gaze in that moment—she had clearly already made her peace with accepting her fate.

Under Gwendolin's own choice, Hobbs simply didn't have the courage to twist his wife's final wishes. He fell to his knees like a puppet stripped of its soul, sobbing uncontrollably.

Hobbs thought perhaps Merlin wasn't wrong. It had always been him, stubbornly forcing his own ideas onto Gwendolin, believing it was love for his wife.

But the pressure he brought upon Gwendolin was far too great. Seeing her husband become Satan's lackey, stirring up strife in the mortal world, she had fallen into self-doubt—had it been because of her that O'Brien had walked this dead-end path? She couldn't absolve herself of blame for the tragedies brought by the strife either.

The crushing pressure had finally snapped that last thread, leading Gwendolin to choose self-destruction. Only by disappearing completely could O'Brien possibly begin a new life.

Gwendolin saw her own disappearance as liberation for her husband, and at the same time, a selfless act of love. She hoped O'Brien would live well, not be held back because of her.

Merlin sheathed his sword and glanced back at Hobbs, kneeling on the ground in utter devastation. There was a flicker of pity in his heart.

But Merlin didn't show any softness. Instead, his face turned grim, his tone utterly flat as he spoke:

"This was Miss Gwendolin's own choice. For her, it was liberation. There is no reason to grieve."

"You thought everything you did was for her own good, coming from a husband's love."

"But it was all your own fantasy. What you brought Miss Gwendolin wasn't love—it was an unbearable weight of pressure."

"Hobbs, you never once considered what Miss Gwendolin herself wanted. Everything was imposed upon her by force!"

"If there's no mutual respect, then isn't marriage merely one person unilaterally dominating the other?"

"Shut up, Merlin! Since when do you get to lecture me?!" Hobbs raised his head, so furious he nearly ground his teeth to dust, glaring at Merlin with hatred. "You killed my wife just to save Alice! No matter how splendid the prophecy, it can't cover up your selfishness! I hate you!"

"You haven't understood Miss Gwendolin's final words at all." Merlin paused, then continued. "You say I'm as selfish as you? You're wrong."

"Isn't that right?" Hobbs demanded, his face flushed red.

"I could have used a simpler method to resurrect Alice, provided I was willing to sacrifice countless other lives." Merlin shrugged helplessly. "But I refused that method."

"Why would you refuse? Don't you want to resurrect Alice that badly?" Hobbs's expression turned confused. A normal person wouldn't reject such an option, even at a cost.

"Because I know Alice wouldn't like it. If she were awakened at the cost of countless lives, she would despise me." Merlin looked straight into Hobbs's eyes and emphasized, "That is the difference between us. I consider my wife's wishes. You don't."

Hobbs froze, standing in place, his heart in turmoil. Those words left him speechless.

Merlin shook his head, turned, and left for the Ninth Circle of Hell, leaving a dazed Hobbs behind.

"Take care of yourself, Hobbs."

"Out of consideration for the fact that you let me go once, I won't kill you. We're even now."

---

The Heavenly Realm. Since the Landlady had already lost her status as a Holy Spirit, returning here had taken considerable effort.

Gazing at the white expanse around her, the Landlady's eyes filled with tears. It had been a long time since she'd seen her homeland.

Clouds drifted across the sky, and seven white jade-like temples connected to one another, forming a spectacular floating continent!

The scale of the Heavenly Temple was more beautiful than Odin's garden from back then, and it radiated an irresistible majesty!

This was the seat of the Heavenly Ruler, an independent realm hovering above the entire world, symbolizing the supreme divine authority!

Suddenly, a flash of light, and two Holy Spirits robed in ornate silk gowns arrived here. Multiple pairs of pure white wings sprouted from their backs—clearly of extremely high rank among the Holy Spirits.

Michael and Uriel. Both were among the last surviving Archangels, and after Raphael departed, they had been heavily relied upon by the Goddess, tasked with maintaining the security of the Heavenly Realm.

"Raphael?" Michael slowly descended, surprised to see the Landlady. "Why have you returned?"

"Your appearance..." Uriel saw the deeply aged Raphael and could tell her remaining lifespan was nearly exhausted. Even so, she was once a companion, and he couldn't help but feel a pang of emotion.

"Long time no see. I thought you wouldn't recognize me." The Landlady smiled self-deprecatingly.

"Not at all. Look at yourself—why did you have to question the Goddess? You must have suffered a great deal in the mortal world." Michael asked with concern.

"It's fine. Living in the mortal world these past years has helped me better understand mortal suffering, and has only strengthened my original convictions." The Landlady harbored no regrets about her decision. Leaving the Heavenly Realm had taught her many things.

"You!?" Michael was at a loss for words. He had thought Raphael had come back to soften, but she was still as stubborn as ever. "Raphael, it seems you haven't properly reflected on yourself."

"Why should I reflect on myself? I'm not the one who's wrong. The Goddess is." The Landlady retorted firmly.

"Raphael, you shouldn't be like this. You've lost your Holy Spirit status. If you don't return to the Heavenly Realm, you will surely die one day." Uriel frowned and said seriously, "Right now you only need to admit your mistakes to the Goddess, and you can surely return to the Heavenly Realm. The Goddess will also help repair your Holy Spirit body. Wouldn't that be better?"

"Uriel, I have never feared death. You underestimate me too much."

The Landlady's words left both Archangels speechless. They had been hoping in vain for so long. The Heavenly Realm was currently short on powerful Holy Spirits and very much needed Raphael's return.

However, seeing Raphael's attitude, both Michael and Uriel felt deeply disappointed. Having seeped into the mortal world for so long, she hadn't changed at all—in fact, she had only become more entrenched.

"If you're not back to admit your mistakes, then why have you come to the Heavenly Realm?" Michael demanded.

"Take me to see the Goddess. I have something very important to tell her."

---

In the garden of the Heavenly Realm, Maria lay on a rocking chair basking in the sunlight, her white veil drifting with the wind, as if she were taking a nap.

Michael and Uriel brought the Landlady along, and the two knelt on one knee respectively. Only the Landlady refused to kneel.

In fact, she had already left the Heavenly Realm and sworn not to pledge allegiance to the Goddess again, so of course she wouldn't bow down.

"Raphael, why have you returned? Have you finally agreed to admit your mistakes?"

"No. There's something I want to tell you—Miss Alice's soul has fallen into Hell."

Maria, reclining on the rocking chair, though facing away from the Holy Spirits, suddenly opened her eyes wide. Her deep gaze resembled the vast stars!

---

Write fast and I'll say I'm phasing it off, not detailed, trying to finish quickly and bail.

Write slow and I'll say it's filler, dragging out the pace, deliberately milking money here.

This novel is really hard to write!

title: Chapter 10 — Come Home With Me
content:
Chapter 10 — Come Home With Me

Volume 39 · Chapter 10

Merlin successfully entered the Ninth Layer of Hell. Upon arriving at the frozen lake, he was stunned by the scene before him.

Countless ice statues stood in all directions, their shapes grotesque and bizarre, with many even composed of stitched-together body parts from different species and humans.

These ice sculptures formed a bizarre forest of human forms, sending shivers of unease down Merlin's spine.

What kind of taste did that Satan have, placing so many human ice statues here?

These poor souls were all traitors during their lifetimes, with no exception, and would continue to suffer the torment of the biting cold even after death.

Merlin saw a magnificent castle at the center of the frozen lake. That must be Satan's lair, and Alice was likely there.

He took a deep breath, tightened his grip on the sword at his waist, and slowly stepped into the forest of ice sculptures, his gaze alert to all sides.

Just as there had been managers in the previous layers of Hell, the Ninth Layer probably had one too. He had to be careful.

Merlin looked at the lifelike faces around him, his nerves on edge, feeling as though countless eyes were staring at him.

Why could these people not even find peace after death? Was this all some rule set by Satan?

"Hey, are you new here? Could you help me? Please."

At the call, Merlin stopped and saw a human head hanging from an ice sculpture speaking. Its expression was exhausted, looking half-dead.

"What's your name?"

"My name is Days. I was once the Knight Commander of the Austro-Hungarian Empire." The head answered honestly.

"Austro-Hungarian Empire?" Merlin was startled, thinking that kingdom had long been destroyed in the chaos caused by Cain and was now split into two nations that could never coexist. "What do you need help with?"

"Help me find my body. I don't want to be hung here forever. I want to be whole again." Days said in a pleading tone.

Merlin looked around. Too many people here were frozen in ice, and many were dismembered. Finding the person's body would be far too difficult. "I can't. I have something urgent to do and can't waste too much time. Think of another way."

Merlin didn't linger and walked straight toward the castle at the lake's center, ignoring Days' pleas.

He didn't know this man at all. There was no need to waste time for a stranger. Seeing Alice was far more urgent.

Days watched Merlin's departing back, despair overwhelming him as he shouted loudly, "Don't go! Don't leave me! Help me!"

Merlin continued onward, growing closer to the castle. He expected nothing to happen, but along the way, he spotted a familiar figure on an ice tree.

Alice's teacher, Clodgia, was encased within the ice tree, almost merging with it, her body pierced by several bone-chilling ice spikes.

Merlin stopped before Clodgia, at a loss for words, his heart a tangled mess of emotions.

Clodgia was like a mother figure to Alice, so Merlin couldn't simply ignore her.

Clodgia's eyelids trembled, and she slowly opened her eyes. She was surprised to see Merlin. "You?"

"Are you alright?" Merlin asked, debating whether to free Clodgia from this torment, as he had done for the Beelzebub siblings.

"You still have the face to appear before me?" Clodgia lowered her head, gritting her teeth. "I thought you would take care of Alice. And what did you do? You sent her falling into Hell. You've failed completely as a husband."

Merlin lowered his head, unsure how to respond to Clodgia. Indeed, he had no grounds to argue. "I... I am at fault. You're right."

"I often hear Alice crying out for you here. My heart is about to break. She calls your name. Do you know how important you are to her?" Clodgia paused, then continued her accusations. "And you? You didn't do anything. You failed to protect her completely, sending her to this tragic world."

"I never expected things to turn out this way. I still haven't figured out how Alice died," Merlin said, frowning with deep regret. "If I could turn back time, I would never have brought Alice along."

"There's no medicine for regret in this world. Honestly, I also regret giving Alice to you. I should have taken her away back then. But Alice was no longer a child. She had her own thoughts, and I couldn't force her. Her wish was to stay by your side." Clodgia frowned deeply, recalling the past. If she had completely cut Alice off from the outside world, would everything have changed?

"I know I was wrong, so I won't argue no matter what you say. I will find a way to bring Alice back." Merlin's tone was resolute.

"What way? How can you bring her back?" Clodgia asked in confusion.

"I will take Alice's soul out of Hell, then figure out a way to make her awaken again." Merlin answered.

"That's impossible. No one can take a soul away from here. Even if you somehow succeed, you cannot bring Alice back from the dead." Clodgia shook her head.

"I can do it. Please trust me. Otherwise, I wouldn't have come here." Merlin's gaze locked onto Clodgia's eyes.

Clodgia sighed. Alice had already fallen into Hell. What good was blaming Merlin now? Better to try treating a dead horse as if it were alive. Perhaps there was still a sliver of hope.

"Then I can only entrust it to you. Don't let me down again."

Raging demonic flames erupted, burning Clodgia and the ice tree together to ashes, sparing her eternal torment.

Inside the castle, Alice's mind went blank. Ever since Satan had fabricated those lies, she had been like a soulless shell, curling up in the cage and staring vacantly.

Isolated from the world and deceived by Satan, Alice still wanted to firmly believe it was all lies. But as time passed, she inevitably began to waver.

What if Satan wasn't lying? What if Merlin had truly found someone else?

Alice had no confidence at all. Only seeing Merlin could dispel her doubts. But Hell was the realm of the dead. Merlin could never possibly appear here.

Satan was exploiting this information gap, constantly whispering to Alice that Merlin was a faithless man, urging her to give up hope of seeing him sooner.

The last oil lamp outside the cage flickered and suddenly went out.

Alice's face turned ashen, as if she had heard a death sentence. She helplessly buried her face in her knees. The last ray of hope in her heart vanished, plunging her into an icy abyss.

"Hahaha, time's up! Alice, obediently become my wife!"

Satan suddenly appeared. He had finally waited long enough for the moment the wedding could begin. Endless darkness began to spread throughout the great hall, encroaching upon Alice in the cage.

Whether Alice agreed or not, today she would become the Queen of Hell. Satan would erase Alice's consciousness and turn her into an obedient shell.

"It's over. It's all over. Merlin..."

Alice called out softly, her expression unreadable. But her trembling voice revealed her heartbroken state.

With a crash, the castle's grand doors were forcibly breached, interrupting this absurd ceremony.

Satan was greatly alarmed. He raised his right hand and shouted, "Who?! How dare you!"

Alice's eyes widened. She quickly wiped the tears from her face and turned around. A blurry figure slowly walked forward, gradually becoming clear.

Merlin walked into the castle's great hall. He raised his head, his ruby-like eyes blazing with fury that continued to burn.

"I've come to take you home, Alice."

title: Chapter 11 — Face
content:
Chapter 11 — Face

Volume 39 · Chapter 11

"Merlin!"

Alice rubbed her eyes vigorously, wondering if she was dreaming. Her face was filled with shock.

When the last oil lamp went out, she had already given up all hope, convinced she would become Satan's puppet.

But once again, at the last moment, Merlin arrived, bringing color back to her eyes.

However, Alice's joyful expression was short-lived, replaced by waves of worry as she asked loudly, "How did you end up here?"

"Hah, if I didn't show up, would I let you marry someone else?" Merlin retorted with a dry laugh.

"I didn't mean that. You're in Hell, does that mean you've..."

"Rest assured, Alice, I'm not dead. I came directly through the Interrealm Gate to bring you back."

After hearing Merlin's serious response, Alice was taken aback, warmth surging in her heart—

So Satan had been lying all along. Merlin hadn't abandoned her; he had been trying to rescue her the whole time.

"I've been waiting for you, Merlin."

"I know. Come home with me, Alice. I'll find a way to wake you up."

Satan's massive black shadow swayed beside the cage, his burning single eye fixed intently on Merlin, his emotions in great turmoil—

So this was Theresa's husband? If he remembered correctly, his name was Merlin Lucifer, the third-generation ruler of the demon race. He had even sent envoys to win him over, only to be rejected.

But why did this man's appearance seem so familiar? Especially now that he saw him in person, the sense of déjà vu grew stronger!

Logically, they should be meeting for the first time. In this dark, sunless place called Hell, had his memories become distorted?

Satan's mind was clouded with doubts, but for now, he couldn't let Merlin take Theresa's soul away.

"This won't do. This is my domain; I won't let you take any soul away so easily."

As soon as he spoke, a circle of dim blue flames erupted around the golden cage, completely separating Alice's soul from Merlin.

Merlin had to defeat the main god Satan to have any chance of leaving with Alice's soul.

The interrupted wedding ceremony enraged Satan, who now only wanted to tear the man before him to pieces.

"This isn't up to you. I'm taking Alice out of Hell. Anyone who stops me, I'll cut down, even if you're the ruler of Hell." Merlin's voice was icy cold as he gripped the hilt of his sword.

"How interesting. I, the master of all souls, am being threatened by a tiny demon?" Satan's single eye glared, sneering, "Ignorant fool, you don't know your place! You think you're worthy of Theresa? She's mine!"

"I know my wife is loved by everyone, but you bastard want to sow discord between us? You're the one who doesn't know your place!" Merlin cursed angrily.

"Huh? What are you talking about, Merlin?" Alice looked at him with a speechless expression, the atmosphere momentarily awkward.

"Forget it. As the ruler of Hell, I don't need to argue with a small demon. Once I kill you, Theresa will naturally be mine."

Satan extended a withered palm from the shadows, his fingers pointing at Merlin as endless divine power surged wildly, bursting into brilliant light at his long fingernails!

Mysterious black patterns began appearing in the air, each character containing the ultimate truth of the laws, revealing the supreme power of death!

Satan, wearing the crown bestowed by the three goddesses on the Philosopher's Stone, had gained control over the death laws of the world, not only surviving but also obtaining the divine status of death.

The greatest difference between gods and ancient gods was the possession of divine status, which represented the world's strongest power, capable of opening new worlds and creating new rules.

"Let me show you the power of a god!!!"

A beam of light containing death laws shot out from Satan's fingertips, its overwhelming power causing the entire Hell to tremble!

Countless spirits could only cower on the ground, begging Satan to calm his anger, or they would all suffer.

The black light devoured everything in its path, bringing the purest death, with the power of the laws unstoppable!

Boom boom boom—

A violent explosion erupted, engulfing Merlin in smoke and black light, the death power showing no signs of stopping but instead expanding!

"Hahahaha, this is all your fault, little demon~"

"You should reflect on yourself."

"This is the price of provoking a god!"

The death power seemed tireless, continuing its rampage, with Merlin nowhere to be seen, leaving everyone wondering if he was dead or alive.

"Merlin!" Alice was shocked, feeling the awe-inspiring power of the main god. She knew that even Merlin couldn't emerge unscathed from the power of the laws.

"This is the main god? Indeed... indeed impressive."

As the aftershocks dissipated, Merlin's figure reappeared, the ground beneath him pockmarked like the moon's surface.

He knelt on one knee, his right hand covering his left arm, his body bearing numerous wounds being eroded by the death power, turning purple-black.

He had just deployed a repulsive space, trying to resist, but it was instantly dispersed by the death power, leaving him completely defenseless.

Merlin wiped the blood from his mouth, gritting his teeth as he stood up. Defeating Satan would require considerable effort.

"Oh?" Satan looked puzzled, saying in surprise, "Still alive? This is strange. It's the first time someone has survived my attack. You're not ordinary, harder than I imagined."

"Is it my turn now?" Merlin stared straight at Satan, flames erupting across his body as he revealed his demon god form, his multiple black wings spreading wide, his wounds rapidly healing!

"Hahahaha, as expected, your mouth is as hard as your body!"

Satan roared, his fingertips flashing with brilliant light as death bullets shot out in rapid succession!

Though he couldn't instantly kill Merlin, with enough shots, he was confident he could wear him down!

Boom boom boom, the death bullets ravaged the land, but each time they barely grazed Merlin's body!

In his demon god form, Merlin's speed was incredibly fast, his power surpassing even the ancient god Behemoth, making him a formidable opponent.

Satan suddenly felt a hint of pressure, finding Merlin's elusive movements difficult to counter, and he couldn't help but curse loudly—

"Fly around like a fly! Have the guts to face me like a man!"

"Fine!"

Demon God Merlin dodged several death bullets in succession before suddenly appearing in front of Satan, his fist smashing into Satan's face with a loud "bang."

The impact sent shockwaves through Satan's body, causing him to twist and stumble backward, stars flashing before his eyes—

This...?

Could he actually feel pain?

This guy's power... wasn't normal!

title: Chapter 12 — Arrow
content:
Chapter 12 — Arrow

Volume 39 · Chapter 12

Merlin's fist slammed into Satan's face, sending his massive body hurtling backward like a cannonball.

Satan barely steadied himself and glared at Merlin, his mind filled with shock and suspicion. -

Isn't he just a minor demon lord in the mortal world? Then why does he possess power enough to shake the position of a Major God?

I barely scraped together a divine spark after exhausting every scheme — how can a mere mortal demon possibly oppose me!?

This is abnormal. What kind of freak is this?!

Merlin frowned. His punches had dealt no real damage to Satan; even with all his strength, the blows were barely more than irritating scratches.

Unseen, Merlin felt some kind of unique force protecting Satan, like an impersonal game rule that simply could not be ignored.

Merlin did not pause — he pressed the advantage, launching furious punches hoping to find a crack in that mysterious rule-bound power.

Thud, thud, thud —

His relentless strikes hammered Satan's face, pinning him against the wall like a grotesque human fresco.

"Enough! I am the Lord of Hell—"

Satan never finished. Another heavy punch cracked against his jaw, burying his head completely into the wall.

Why? Why aren't my strikes working? Under normal circumstances, an opponent's head would already be pulped. Is it healing ability?

Merlin grew ever more alarmed as he kept hitting. He began to suspect Satan might be immortal — with his own power alone, there seemed no way to defeat him.

Satan gradually regained his composure, adapted to Merlin's relentless barrage, and immediately seized Merlin with his shriveled hand, glaring viciously.

"Don't push your luck, little demon—!"

Demon God Merlin lightly touched Banri Garan at his waist, transformed it back into its original obsidian-black appearance, then drew the blade and released its scorching hellfire!

The temperature inside the castle skyrocketed. Solid walls and domed ceilings began melting and dripping downward.

Satan wailed in agony within the flames. Though unable to suffer harm, the burning pain inflicted by the demon fire was terribly real.

Freeing himself from Satan's grip, Merlin wasted no words and swung Banri Garan down toward his enemy's skull, intent on severing Satan's head right then and there.

But then something unexpected happened —

Countless wandering black runes materialized around Satan, forming a defensive barrier that even Merlin's Iaijutsu could not pierce!

This was precisely why only a Major God can slay a Major God. These wandering black runes carried the power of the Death Law, protecting the bearer of a divine spark around the clock.

Only by becoming a Major God and obtaining a divine spark could one command the Laws. No ordinary being, no matter how powerful, could break through the barrier formed by such Laws — making it impossible to kill a Major God.

"What is this?!" Merlin's eyes widened in shock. He finally understood why he couldn't harm Satan — it was the Law all along!

The murderous sword aura of Iaijutsu and the power of the Death Law collided violently, producing thunderous explosions that shook the entire Hell!

With the fierce blast, a massive crack split the sky above Hell, and howling winds from an unknown space swept across the realm!

The enormous impact sent Merlin flying. He tumbled across the ground, sliding dozens of meters before finally coming to a stop, wisps of white smoke rising from his body.

Even Merlin's Demon God form struggled to withstand the shockwave between Iaijutsu and the Law's collision force. A few more hits like that and every bone in his body would shatter.

*Maria's worry was written plainly on her face. The situation was far from promising.

Merlin grit his teeth and slowly rose from the ground, furious. "So that's how it is. The power of the Laws — a Major God's privilege, huh?"

"Hmph hmph hmph —" Satan let out a string of cold laughter, slowly rising into the air to look down upon the tiny Merlin. "Exactly. The Law is a wall of despair that creatures like you ants can never surmount. As long as the Law shields me, I stand invincible. Do you still believe you can take Theresa away?"

"Pfft!" Merlin realized things had grown troublesome. This meant he was the one being relentlessly beaten while his opponent had some sort of damage-immunity cheat active.

Satan extended his withered hand and pointed toward Hell's sky, conjuring out of nowhere a death star of enormous size that swirled like a black hole, endlessly devouring everything around it!

The death star churned, releasing boundless Death Law power. From afar it looked like a末日 death warning, and its overwhelming aura of death filled all of Hell!

"Vanish, demon ant. The death star will consume all living things — none shall escape!"

Before the words even finished falling, the death star in the sky began plummeting rapidly, roaring down toward the tiny Merlin!

Merlin's expression darkened. The terrifying pressure made every bone in his body rattle with a "crackling" sound!

He raised his head, switched to Mistle, and unleashed a sudden iai draw aimed at the falling death star. The razor-sharp sword aura split the enormous death star cleanly in two!

The collision between Iaijutsu and the Death Law erupted once more. The shockwave left the Ninth Hell in ruins, on the verge of collapse at any moment!

Crack —

Mistle snapped in two. This blade forged by矮人 masters was ultimately only a semi-divine artifact — it simply could not resist a Major God's Law power and was destroyed in one strike.

Merlin dropped to one knee. His Demon God appearance was gradually fading. He panted heavily. Though the death star had not struck him directly, the power of the Death Law had been continuously eroding his body.

He could already feel his body growing weaker by the moment. Areas touched by the Death Law seemed already dead, no longer responding to his commands. If the Law's erosion reached his brain, Merlin would truly perish.

Satan may not have appeared overwhelmingly powerful, but he could erode living flesh like poison — that was the terrifying nature of the Death Law. Within this Hell, everyone, sooner or later, would be completely consumed by the Death Law and ultimately become Satan's puppet.

Alice pressed herself against the cage, watching Merlin from afar, her heart racing with anxiety. At this rate, not only would Merlin fail to bring her away — he would end up trapped in Hell forever, becoming another puppet toyed with by Satan!

"Iaijutsu, demons, Mistle... I remember now who you are."

"Seems I've been in Hell too long. I'd nearly forgotten what a bastard like you looks like."

"It's you. You're the man who stole Theresa from my side! And you still dare to show your face before me? You must die today!"

Satan was muttering to himself, saying incomprehensible things, his body trembling violently as if recalling some dreadful memory?

He clutched his head and shook it wildly, seeming unable to accept this reality. The nightmare that had tormented him since the Age of the Gods — why was it resurfacing now?!

Unable to find answers, Satan could only think of eliminating the dangerously familiar man as soon as possible. So he conjured another terrifying death star, and a crushing pressure descended upon them!

"Why are you appearing before me again? Were you here just to steal Theresa from me once more?! I won't allow it—"

Merlin's brows furrowed deeply. Overwhelming exhaustion crashed over him. The Death Law had already corroded half his body. His mind was consumed with thoughts of what to do next — he barely caught a single word of Satan's babble.

Just as the terrifying death star was about to fall, and Merlin feared he could not withstand it —

*Whoosh* — a sound of sundering air suddenly rang out. A brilliant light arrow shot through the rift above Hell's sky and struck Satan directly between the eyes!

"Ghh—?!" Satan froze mid-motion. Holy power flooded from the luminous arrow into his brain, fiercely scorching his soul—

"Maria!"

"You fucking whore!!!!"

"How dare—"

title: Chapter 13 — Bleeding Too (Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 13 — Bleeding Too (Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 39 · Chapter 13

"How dare you!"

"You actually dare to ambush me!"

"What audacity!"

The light arrow struck Satan's forehead, the noble divine power was forcibly poured into his body, causing him unbearable pain.

For Satan, who mastered the law of death, divine power was like poison, easily threatening his life.

This time, the power of the law did not appear to protect Satan, but mysteriously disappeared, allowing the arrow to strike his head.

The reason was that Maria was also a main god, possessing divinity, controlling the law of life, and could easily ignore the protective law barrier around Satan.

Satan's soul was greatly stimulated, letting out a painful roar, stumbling about like a madman, desperately trying to pull out the arrow from his forehead.

"Maria! You won't die well! I absolutely won't let you off!"

Suddenly, a crack in the hellish sky lit up with a beam of light, the sound of heavenly bells came from within, accompanied by waves of sacred songs.

The song contained the majesty of the heavenly ruler, yet one could feel warmth; the tormented spirits in hell, as if they had received redemption, temporarily forgot their suffering.

Alice looked up, staring at the light in the crack, feeling as if someone was summoning her, a strange sense of familiarity.

"Maria, has heaven also gotten involved?"

Merlin gasped, checking his body, which was getting worse and worse, the erosion of the law of death was still ongoing.

If he didn't leave hell quickly, Merlin would soon be completely eroded, forever trapped in hell as a spirit.

Hell was, after all, the land of the dead, not a place for the living, unless Merlin surrendered to Satan like Hobbes.

On the other side, Satan grew even more frenzied, trying to pull out Maria's arrow, but the eerie arrow only sank deeper.

This was clearly Maria's preparation, a divine artifact arrow specially forged to take down Satan, imbued with the Goddess's law power.

Now, to save Alice trapped in hell, Maria decided to use this secret weapon ahead of time.

Originally, the arrow couldn't enter hell; Maria had planned to use it in a future battle against Satan, catching him off guard.

But unexpectedly, the collision between Merlin and Satan in hell created a spatial rift, giving Maria an opportunity, and the arrow shot from heaven wandered through the chaotic spatial rift, directly reaching hell!

The sacred bell sound from the light in the rift grew louder, each strike making Merlin feel uneasy, and even Satan felt annoyed, unable to endure this sound.

Suddenly, Alice felt the golden cage shaking, a mysterious power pulling at the cage itself, leaving her full of doubt.

The golden cage, carrying Alice, quickly rose into the air, flying towards the light in the hellish sky's rift!

Maria had noticed Alice and decided to bring her back to heaven, unable to leave her in the dangerous hell.

Alice couldn't resist, only able to stand beside the cage, stretching out her hand towards the distant Merlin, calling out loudly—

"Merlin! Merlin!"

"Alice!"

Merlin had just stood up when he fell to the ground, discovering one of his legs wouldn't listen to him, and could only crawl up again, limping as he chased after her.

But in Merlin's current state, how could he possibly catch up? He could only watch as Alice flew towards the light in the rift, soon disappearing within.

Merlin breathed laboriously, watching as the light in the rift gradually dimmed, then completely vanished, even the rift in the hellish sky slowly healing.

Now Alice had just escaped the wolf's den, only to enter the tiger's lair; who knew what the Goddess of Light would do to her?

Merlin had originally planned to take Alice's soul away, then negotiate with the Goddess of Light, but now he had lost all initiative.

"Why, why did it become like this!?"

Merlin sat on the ground, all his efforts in vain, having to plan again from the beginning, his fist pounding the ground in anger, veins bulging on his forehead.

The Goddess of Light suddenly appeared, taking Alice away, something Merlin had never expected, exceeding his predictions.

According to the landlady, Maria's plan to revive Theresa had already failed, so what would that high-and-mighty goddess do to Alice, a failed product?

Merlin didn't dare to think, fearing Maria wouldn't allow this failed product to exist, only willing to keep Theresa's residual soul.

This was the worst possible situation.

Satan crazily struggled for a while, finally pulling out the arrow from his forehead, looking at the killing tool Maria had prepared for him, he roared in anger—

"Maria, wait for me! I will definitely go to heaven to find you myself!"

Satan threw the silver arrow on the ground, then looked around, discovering Alice was gone, which made him even more furious.

"Theresa! Where is Theresa? I've waited so long, just wanting to marry her, and in the end, I got nothing!?"

Merlin let out a dry laugh, tiredly saying, "You brought this on yourself."

Satan noticed Merlin, having lost his beloved, the wedding ceremony ruined, and being ambushed by Maria, all these things combined made him feel unprecedented anger.

Now Satan needed to vent his endless rage, and Merlin became the best target; only by killing the man in front of him would his mood improve.

"It's you! It's all because of you! If it weren't for you, Theresa would already be mine, you took my beloved from me, and now you mock me!?"

"We seem to be meeting for the first time, right?" Merlin said weakly, feeling he couldn't escape this calamity today.

"Shut up! You're the root of all chaos, all tragedies are caused by you, why are you still alive? You should die!"

Satan had somewhat lost his reason, roaring angrily at Merlin, his withered hand pointing at the sky again, the law of death surging violently!

The Death Star, bringing death's end to all things, lit up again, hell once more plunged into Satan's shadow, pain and death spreading wildly!

"Is it all over? How unwilling I am..."

Merlin's body went limp, as if he had lost his soul, this time unable to resist the Death Star's impact, awaiting him was only annihilation.

Suddenly, a broken red spear struck, half of the crimson spear shooting straight at Satan, but was blocked by the power of the law.

"Who! Is there still an ant daring to disrespect me?"

"Of course!"
