A man engulfed in flames, covered in the blessing of semi-divine power, swiftly picked up the arrow on the ground.

He gritted his teeth, leaping up from the ground, the silver arrow in his hand bursting with dazzling light, Maria's divine power instantly breaking through Satan's death law protection!

"Even gods will bleed!!!"

Pfft, Maria's arrow was stabbed into Satan's only eye, blood splattering everywhere, the divine power's light wildly expanding, tearing at his soul.

Satan let out a painful wail, stumbling about, grabbing at the air, this light arrow posing a huge threat to him, like a snake piercing deep into his divine core!

Merlin opened his eyes, shocked by what was happening before him, somewhat unable to believe his eyes, his mind going blank.

"Hobbes!"

title: Chapter 14 — Farewell, Hobbs
content:
Chapter 14 — Farewell, Hobbs

Volume 39 · Chapter 14

"Uaaaaah!!!"

Satan let out an agonizing wail, his body contorting under the divine power. The arrow had struck his one and only eye, robbing him of all sight.

The frenzied Satan began wildly destroying everything around him. The arrow piercing his single eye grew ever more brilliant, steadily advancing toward the center of his mind — his Divine Seat!

"Merlin! Run! If you don't escape now, you'll lose your chance!" Hobbs desperately gripped Mary's arrow, striving to drive it clean through Satan's skull.

"Huh?!" Merlin's eyes shifted. He never expected Hobbs to appear at a time like this.

"Satan deceived me for a long time, and I did many wrong things because of it, so I came to settle the score with him!" Hobbs paused, then gritted his teeth. "This guy is the root of all these tragedies. If it weren't for him, I wouldn't have ended up like this!"

"Hobbs..." Merlin froze, torn within himself about whether to abandon Hobbs there.

"Stop hesitating, Merlin!" Hobbs was practically hanging from the top of Satan's head, gripping the arrow with all his might to keep from being shaken off. "Run! As long as you escape, there's still a chance! Now is not the time to be sentimental! I never needed your sympathy!"

"You won't escape hell! I won't let you go! I'll cut your flesh piece by piece and feed it to the hungry dead!" Satan cursed loudly in rage.

"Merlin!" Hobbs urged again.

"Damn it!"

Merlin grit his teeth, turned, and limped back the way he came, his eyes slightly reddened.

Since Hobbs had already gone this far, staying any longer would only mean his sacrifice was in vain. Merlin had no other choice.

Memories flooded through Merlin's mind like a revolving lantern — scenes of them sitting together drinking were so vivid, leaving Merlin with a storm of emotions...

Farewell, Hobbs.

Goodbye forever, Hobbs!

There probably won't be another chance to drink together, Hobbs.

Actually... I never got around to paying you back for the drinks. Sorry.

"Merlin, now we're truly even."

Hobbs felt guilty about Alice. His friend's departure was somewhat connected to him.

If Hobbs hadn't revealed Merlin's identity to that pirate's son Lockley, maybe the couple would still be alive and well today.

This was Hobbs's own choice. He didn't want to owe Merlin anything, hoping that at the final moment of his life, he could do something right.

Hobbs decided to take responsibility for his mistakes, to achieve redemption for his sinful soul. Only then would he have the courage to face Gwendolyn, who had already left him.

"Satan, why did you deceive me? Was it fun to toy with me? In your eyes, was my subservience worth so little!"

"You're nothing but an ant! Who do you think you are to make demands of me? O'Brien, you've narrowed your path!" Satan roared in anger.

"Is that so? You never expected to die at the hands of an ant," Hobbs paused, saying with meaning, "Today, I will become the first Hero to slay a god."

"You? Are you kidding? Neither you nor that man will escape today!"

As soon as he finished speaking, Satan summoned the terrifying Death Star once more, hurling it toward himself, intending to use a pyrrhic strategy to rid himself of the troublesome Hobbs and Mary's arrow.

Merlin hadn't escaped far yet. When the Death Star caught up, the law of death would engulf him too. Satan was using this mutual destruction tactic to eliminate both of them.

But the initiative wasn't in Satan's hands — it was in Hobbs's. Gritting his teeth, Hobbs concentrated all his strength into his fist and slammed it down on the tail of Mary's arrow, driving it straight into the god's brain.

The Divine Seat deep within Satan's mind was damaged. Struck by the arrow, it immediately cracked with a horrifying sound!

The frenzied Satan instantly fell still, standing like a wooden post, trembling all over.

"This is the price for deceiving me! Satan!"

Boom—

Light surged, and blazing divine radiance erupted from all of Satan's orifices. This fatal arrow had already wounded his Divine Seat!

The entire Hell began to quake violently. The sky shattered like glass, and the earth was being devoured by endless void!

Hell, this world created by Satan, was now on the verge of collapse after its creator suffered such devastating injuries.

Merlin looked back. The Death Star from the sky had already fallen, swallowing both Satan and Hobbs in the same instant!

"Hobbs!"

The remaining devastation overwhelmed him, flames and darkness obscuring Merlin's vision until he could barely see anything.

"Today, our dear old friend Hobbs has left us."

"Though he was usually joking around, not acting like a serious person."

"But whenever it mattered most, he always showed us the right path."

"He was irreplaceable in the guild. He was our source of joy, our best companion."

"Without exaggeration, he was a member of the Laxem Guild family, a dearly loved one, someone we all cherished."

"But there's no need to be overly grief-stricken. Hobbs hasn't truly left us. His presence will live on forever in our hearts."

At the Adventurers' Cemetery, most members of the Laxem Guild had gathered, dressed formally and solemnly to see off Hobbs and fulfill their duties as friends.

President Elder Taylor gave a gentle speech before Hobbs's tombstone. Whenever a guild member passed away, he did the same, seeing off familiar faces one by one.

After the speech, everyone placed the flowers they'd prepared at Hobbs's tombstone, then turned away with heavy hearts.

Little Minnie lingered long after offering flowers to her father, sniffing quietly. She was being brave and didn't cry out loud.

Merlin watched from the side, feeling uneasy, so he gently patted Mini's head and spoke softly.

"It's alright. Your father was a hero. You should be proud of him."

Little Minnie nodded repeatedly, too heartbroken to speak, completely bewildered by what had happened. She woke up one morning and her father was just gone.

Elder Taylor picked up Mini, continuously comforting her. He decided to raise her himself, treating her like a granddaughter — a way of giving Hobbs some closure.

"Let's go, Merlin. It's about to rain."

"No rush. I want to stay a while longer."

Elder Taylor glanced at Merlin, then at Hobbs's tombstone, nodded without pressing further, and slowly led Mini away from the cemetery.

Merlin gazed at Hobbs's tombstone, slowly retrieved his Black Iron Adventurer credential from his chest, and gently placed it before the stone.

The rough little black plate bore faint scratches, vaguely reflecting Hobbs's sloppy drunkard appearance from life, feeling strangely familiar.

Merlin raised his head to look at the sky shrouded in dark clouds, which weighed heavily on his spirit. He suddenly offered a helpless smile.

"Hobbs, if... I mean, if..."

"If there's still a chance to sit and drink with you..."

"How wonderful that would be."

A gap appeared in the churning dark clouds, golden sunlight pouring straight down, landing squarely on the Black Iron credential. The once-rough iron plate now gleamed brilliantly—

Region: Laxem

Name: Hobbs Gerald

Occupation: Unambitious Mage

title: Chapter 15 — Opening Again
content:
Chapter 15 — Opening Again

Volume 39 · Chapter 15

Lexham, early morning.

Da Vinci opened the door, preparing to go to the market to purchase some alchemical materials and continue her experiments.

She stretched and took a deep breath of fresh air, just as she was about to turn back to lock the door, when she discovered a dog crouching in front of it?

Or rather, a bizarre hound with pitch-black fur and six eyes — an alchemical beast that had escaped the obelisk tower after Flamel's death.

"Hmm?"

Da Vinci looked puzzled, reached out and patted the alchemical hound's head, her suspicions growing —

An alchemical beast?

There should hardly be anyone left who still possessed this kind of technology. Who was its master?

The alchemical hound nuzzled against Da Vinci, wagging its tail incessantly, as if trying to convey some meaning, then lowered its head and began coughing violently.

"What's going on?"

The hound's coughing only grew worse, making Da Vinci watch with alarm. It slowly opened its jowls and regurgitated something from its stomach —

A bright red gemstone, and a brown notebook.

Da Vinci frowned and slowly picked up the items from the ground, only to find a familiar name prominently written on the notebook!

Flamel's Alchemical Notes.

Da Vinci's heart skipped a beat. Her gaze locked onto the red gemstone in her hand — a mysterious power was flowing across its surface, causing her eyes to widen instantly.

A Philosopher's Stone? The real Philosopher's Stone!

Da Vinci couldn't understand why the alchemical beast before her had delivered these two things, but she could be certain — this was definitely the intention of her senior fellow disciple.

So Da Vinci hurriedly flipped open the notebook and discovered it contained all of Flamel's alchemical experience, including the correct method for refining a Philosopher's Stone, as well as the secret alchemical阵 for summoning the Three Fates!

The shock in Da Vinci's eyes was impossible to conceal. Every page she turned felt like opening a door to a new world, a wealth of knowledge she had never learned flooding her mind, leaving her unable to digest it all at once.

Flamel truly was a rare alchemical genius, having long surpassed his teacher Democritus and leaving his junior sister Da Vinci far behind, almost reaching another realm entirely!

The notebook recorded many bold alchemical experiments — things Da Vinci wouldn't even dare imagine — and Flamel had almost done them all, acquiring extremely classified alchemical knowledge in the process.

As Da Vinci kept flipping through the notebook, a letter tucked inside fell out. She paused, picked it up, and opened it —

"My dear junior sister, Da Vinci, by the time you read this letter, I am likely already dead."

"To be honest, it's quite embarrassing. Only now, as I write this letter, did I realize that I seem to be entirely alone."

"I have no family or friends, no kindred spirit with whom I can sit and share my innermost thoughts. You are the only person I can trust."

"Therefore, I can only entrust the true Philosopher's Stone and my notebook to you. I hope you will make good use of these things."

"For the sake of this Philosopher's Stone, I have paid a great price — too many people have lost their lives for it. Its cost is far heavier than I ever imagined."

"I know the Philosopher's Stone is an unfathomably filthy stone. Every one of its edges is filled with sin, making one feel sickened."

"But we alchemists must constantly pursue truth. Glimpsing the very end of truth is our lifelong mission, is it not?"

"This notebook records all my alchemical techniques. Many of them are cruel, inhumane alchemical experiments — using human beings as alchemical materials is a commonplace occurrence."

"I'm sure you must despise me, right? I'm willing to accept all the blame. But alchemy, if restrained and tied down, will never go far. Someone must break through every kind of shackle."

"Perhaps all my alchemy is sinful, but no one can deny that these techniques possess tremendous value — enough to advance alchemy once more!"

"I have never feared death. What I fear is my alchemy coming to a complete halt, unable to glimpse the truth at the end."

"I may be dead, but you can continue forward. Treading upon my corpse, explore the pinnacle of alchemy."

"Only in this way will I have no regrets."

After finishing the letter, Da Vinci folded it back up and looked at the Philosopher's Stone in her hand, her expression incredibly complicated.

Without a doubt, Da Vinci also pursued the Philosopher's Stone, but after seeing the bloody refinement methods, she couldn't help but feel shaken.

Da Vinci believed alchemy was meant to bring convenience to people, not to cause bloody slaughter. She wondered if she had been walking the wrong path all along —

"Flamel, I'm sorry."

"I won't continue down your old path. It runs completely counter to the alchemy I hold in my heart."

Late at night, Da Vinci found Merlin and decided to hand over the precious Philosopher's Stone for him to use.

This was the result of Da Vinci's careful deliberation. She had long harbored lingering resentment over the earlier incident where the War Ring had been stolen.

If the War Ring hadn't been stolen, Alice and Merlin wouldn't have been drawn into danger. Da Vinci felt she bore some responsibility.

The two went down to the basement of the Lexham Library, where Da Vinci had already laid out the陣 for summoning the Three Goddesses according to Flamel's notebook.

Merlin looked at the familiar crimson runes on the ground and recalled the day he went to the obelisk tower — the ground there had an alchemical陣 exactly like the one before him.

"Are you saying all of this is true, Miss Da Vinci?"

"Yes. As long as we can appear before the Three Fates and offer the Philosopher's Stone, we will be granted a wish. This is the only way to alter reality — it might even allow Miss Alice to come back to life."

Da Vinci said this with a grave expression. She believed this was the only chance to resurrect Alice.

To prevent any disturbances, she had only told Merlin about possessing the true Philosopher's Stone.

After using this Philosopher's Stone, Da Vinci would burn Flamel's notebook, completely cutting off any possibility of further slaughter.

She didn't want anyone else to pursue the Philosopher's Stone in the future. That would only cause countless tragedies. Things like this kind of sin should best disappear forever.

"This is the true Philosopher's Stone. Take it and walk into the alchemical陣 — that will open the Realm of Destiny."

Merlin looked at the gleaming red gemstone in his hand and couldn't help but frown. He genuinely couldn't tell any difference between this and that fake Philosopher's Stone.

"I don't know much about the Realm of Destiny, so I can't provide much useful information. From here on, you'll need to investigate it yourself."

"Thank you so much — you've been a tremendous help. I don't know how I can repay you, Miss Da Vinci."

"No need. I feel deeply sorry about Alice. If I had guarded that War Ring properly, you two wouldn't have been drawn into danger either." Da Vinci paused and added softly, "If possible, I'd like to make up for some of my failures."

Merlin nodded, without hesitation, and slowly stepped into the alchemical阵. He took a deep breath — suddenly, fierce winds swept through the basement, and mist began spreading continuously —

The Realm of Destiny.

Was being opened once again!

title: Chapter 16 — The Result
content:
Chapter 16 — The Result

Volume 39 · Chapter 16

Da Vinci watched the mist spreading from the alchemy array, her brow furrowing slightly. She had no intention of following Merlin into the Fate Secret Realm, nor did she want to get involved. Da Vinci believed that if she pursued the secrets of alchemy like Flamel, she might also be controlled by desire and create an unpredictable tragedy. Such a dangerous thing, of course, should be avoided as much as possible. Da Vinci had made up her mind not to continue down Flamel's old path.

Da Vinci glanced at Flamel's alchemy notes in her hand, hesitated for a moment, then shook her head and decisively threw the notes into the nearby furnace. Watching the notes burn in the flames, gradually turning to ashes, the precious memories of the alchemy genius Flamel were also completely erased. However, Da Vinci had already memorized the contents completely, and would take these memories to her grave, ensuring that these evil alchemy techniques would never reappear.

Especially since the notes recorded how to summon the Three Fates, if this alchemy fell into the hands of greedy villains, no one could predict what the world would become. So burning Flamel's alchemy notes would prevent others from seeking the Philosopher's Stone and trying to satisfy their ambitions using the Three Fates.

The alchemy hound squatting beside Da Vinci saw its original owner's notes being burned and let out a series of whimpers, anxiously circling in place. Da Vinci squatted down, gently stroking the alchemy hound, and said in a comforting tone, "Everything is already over, this is all for the future of the world. Your owner was led astray by the temptation of fate. Such things will not happen again."

In the Heavenly Realm, in the magnificent garden behind the divine palace. Alice lay unconscious in a golden cage, surrounded by a group of holy spirits. Michael and Uriel looked at Alice in surprise, this being their first time seeing Theresa's vessel. Unexpectedly, her appearance was very similar to Goddess Maria, except for the difference in breast size, they could almost be considered identical!

The two holy spirits knew little about the goddess's plan to revive her younger sister, only barely glimpsing the tip of the iceberg at this moment. The landlady's expression was complex, happy to see Alice successfully rescued from hell by the goddess, but also worried. The landlady couldn't judge how Goddess Maria intended to handle Alice, after all, she was the product of the failed plan to revive Theresa.

The landlady planned to speak up for Alice as much as possible, to make Maria recognize reality, abandon her plan to revive Theresa, and acknowledge Alice as a new life with an independent personality. And considering Alice possessed a portion of Theresa's residual soul, to save Alice and let her return to the mortal world, reunite with her husband and daughter Merlin.

However, these were all the landlady's speculations, the actual situation would depend on Goddess Maria's thoughts. She could only try her best to help. In this Heavenly Realm, Goddess Maria was the absolute ruler, with the power to decide everything, her word was law.

"Great Master, is... is she your sister?" Michael asked, mustering his courage. Maria gave an uncertain response. "This..." Uriel looked bewildered, not understanding the meaning behind Maria's words.

Maria wasn't sure if the plan had succeeded. If Alice could recognize her as her sister, then the result would naturally be joyful. But if Alice couldn't recognize Maria, the plan would be declared a failure, and Alice's fate would become uncertain.

Seeing Alice's current age, Maria felt that Theresa's residual soul should have grown along with the vessel, and it was time to inspect the results.

Alice slowly opened her eyes, her world having changed. From a world of darkness and flames, she had arrived in a peaceful and warm paradise, the contrast was enormous. Alice's memories were still stuck at the moment of being forcibly separated from Merlin, so she quickly got up and looked around.

"Merlin..."

Seeing Alice awaken, Maria's icy expression immediately softened, as if she had seen her kind and innocent younger sister. The deceased Theresa was an unhealable wound in Maria's heart, and only she could make the aloof goddess lose her composure.

A long time ago, when Maria put on the Three Fates' crown, she had been torn between a painful choice - between familial love and greater righteousness. She could have used the power of the Fate Crown to revive her sister. But in the end, she chose righteousness, choosing to wield the power of life and creation, to create an era of human prosperity.

The reason was simple: Theresa had once said that this was her greatest wish, hoping that weak humans could escape their oppressed circumstances. So Maria tearfully gave up the chance to revive her sister Theresa, creating the current human era as her sister had hoped.

As for Satan? Although he claimed to deeply love Theresa, when faced with the Fate Crown, he still chose power and authority. In Satan's heart, Theresa was clearly not as attractive as these two things. Moreover, the Fate Crown's wish opportunity only came once, how could it be wasted on a woman?

Although she had lost the easy chance to revive Theresa, Maria had never given up, which was why the plan to repair Theresa's residual soul had appeared. Maria couldn't hide her excitement, her heart filled with anxiety, as she slowly approached the golden cage, staring tightly at Alice, her lips moving as if to speak but hesitating.

"Eh!"

Alice looked at the silver-haired woman outside the cage, her heart shocked, momentarily wondering if she was looking in a mirror? The woman in front of her looked too similar to herself, except for the eye mask covering her face, revealing only one right eye, which seemed especially eerie.

Alice's thoughts were in chaos, unable to understand where she was or who the one-eyed woman, who looked so similar to herself, was. "Theresa? Is that you?"

Maria's hands trembled as she reached into the golden cage, gently stroking Alice's hair. The usually cold-blooded goddess's eyes now shone with tears. Seeing Alice's frightened reaction, Maria thought her plan had succeeded, and her eyes flickered as she considered how to welcome her sister's return.

But Alice's subsequent reaction made Maria plummet into disappointment, the small flame of hope in her heart completely extinguished. "I'm not Theresa, why does everyone think I am? Who are you? Why do you look..."

Maria's expression stiffened, her eyes losing some of their color, becoming dull and lifeless, returning to her usual aloof and icy demeanor. She quickly withdrew her hands from the cage, retreating in confusion, her eyes reddening as she asked in a sorrowful tone, "My dear... You... You don't recognize... Is that right?"

title: Chapter 17 — Not Possible
content:
Chapter 17 — Not Possible

Volume 39 · Chapter 17

Alice wore a bewildered expression, though the woman before her looked similar, she didn't recognize her and certainly didn't have a twin sister.

The landlady's heart skipped a beat, desperately winking and making eyes at Alice, hoping she could deceive Maria, perhaps there was still a chance to turn things around.

Unfortunately, Alice completely failed to understand the landlady's meaning, instead asking in confusion, "Landlady, why are you here too? Could it be this mortal world..."

Maria turned her head to glare fiercely at the landlady, noticing she seemed to be hinting at something to Alice. Her eyes flashed with intense killing intent.

The landlady's face turned ashen, closing her eyes in resignation as she mustered the courage to say, "Your plan has already failed. Even if you are the great Goddess, you can't simply revive a dead person, especially one who only has a few strands of lingering soul left."

"Shut up." Maria's expression turned ugly, her eyes gradually growing colder.

Alice was taken aback, staring in disbelief at the silver-haired woman outside the cage, thinking to herself, Goddess? Could it be the Goddess of Light, Maria? Oh my, why does she look just like me!

"I know you're extremely disappointed right now, but this is reality. You've already expended a tremendous amount of energy trying to revive Theresa, but it hasn't succeeded. Continuing is meaningless." The landlady spoke righteously.

As Maria's expression grew increasingly terrible, Michael and Uriel both sensed something was off, rushing forward to dissuade the landlady from speaking further, fearing something might happen if she continued.

"Raphael, shut up!" Michael frowned.

"The great Goddess is absolutely right, no need for you to question her!" Uriel chimed in from the side.

Alice's expression grew even more bewildered, thinking to herself, what are these two saints calling the landlady? Raphael? Oh my, what is all this? I'm getting more and more confused!

"I won't! I must speak the truth!" The landlady refused to listen to their advice. If she could be persuaded, she wouldn't have been imprisoned in the first place and eventually abandoned her saint status. "Your plan to revive Theresa has already caused countless tragedies. Can't you see that? Give up, don't continue clinging to this. Personal feelings can't be built on others' suffering. This isn't something a ruler of the world should do."

"I don't want to hear you speak. Get out of the Heavenly Realm, we don't need you here." Maria glared fiercely at the landlady, her divine pressure gradually surfacing.

Under the pressure of the main deity, the landlady found it hard to breathe but still loudly exposed the truth, "Admit it! You couldn't revive your sister. She is Alice and has her own independent personality, a new life!"

"Shut up!"

Maria angrily rebuked, her eyes flashing with ferocity as her divine power erupted, causing massive distortions around them!

The landlady's body was instantly twisted beyond recognition by this invisible force, flowing like mud on the ground.

Maria, provoked into a rage, lost control of her temper and finally couldn't restrain herself from striking down Raphael.

Michael and Uriel turned pale, too frightened to even breathe, watching the meaty pulp that was once Raphael on the ground. They felt immense sympathy in their hearts.

This was one of their own kind, a former comrade who fought alongside them. Losing one meant there would be one less.

As for Maria's actions, the two saint commanders naturally didn't dare speak out. They were all created by Maria, and a single thought from her could end their lives.

"Landlady! What are you doing?!" Alice, seeing the landlady's gruesome death, grabbed the golden cage in protest, but Maria completely ignored her.

Maria took heavy breaths, slowly calming her agitated emotions, her gaze looking down condescendingly at the puddle of flesh on the ground.

"This is all your own doing, Raphael. I warned you, but you repeatedly challenged my dignity. I couldn't continue to tolerate you."

"That's right, she isn't Theresa, but what does it matter?"

"I can kill her, strip away Theresa's lingering soul once more, and restart the revival plan!"

"Try twice if once isn't enough, three times if twice isn't enough."

"No matter how many times it takes, as long as I haven't succeeded in bringing Theresa back to my side, I won't stop!"

"There will eventually be a successful time..."

The Fate Labyrinth, this starry sky where gears intertwined, seemed to hint at the fates of countless people.

Merlin came alone to the ancient, massive stone gate, where the goddess relief on it was vividly lifelike.

He took a deep breath, just about to push open the gate before him, but the door slowly opened by itself.

Darkness, pitch black where one couldn't see their own hand, with only the sound of gears constantly turning.

Merlin didn't hesitate, walking straight in. Candles lit up in a spiral pattern, and three towering giantesses appeared!

They sat on magnificent stone thrones, calmly gazing down at another new visitor, as if they had long anticipated Merlin's arrival.

"Are you the Fates?" Merlin examined the three giantesses, his heart filled with shock and doubt.

"That's right."

The three goddesses responded in unison, their hoarse voices echoing through the space and surging towards the countless extending heights.

"I've heard you can grant wishes?" Merlin asked tentatively.

"That's right, young Demon Lord. This has always been our work, you don't need to doubt it." The three goddesses paused simultaneously before continuing, "However, your wish is probably impossible to fulfill. You want to revive your wife, Alice Clotilde, correct?"

"Ah!" Merlin felt like he'd been seen through, somewhat uncomfortable, but had to ask, "Why? Can't any wish be granted?"

"It can, but wishes made by predecessors can't be repeated by those who come after. It would be a duplication, unable to be inscribed on the Crown of Fate."

"Who made the same wish?"

"It was your wife, Merlin. You once died, and before you, a pirate's son named Lochley wished for your death." The three goddesses paused, continuing emotionlessly, "So your wife donned the Crown of Fate, exchanging her life to bring you back."

Merlin's eyes widened in shock, finally understanding the whole situation. His unconsciousness in the Fate Labyrinth was because Lochley had wished for his death.

And Alice had entered this gate, using her precious life to gain the chance to make a wish, bringing herself back from death.

Merlin shuddered, his eyes growing excited as he slowly closed them, letting out a long breath to calm his emotions.

So it was like this.

"Alice left because of me."

"I should have guessed it earlier. That's just like her."

title: Chapter 18 — Get Ready (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 18 — Get Ready (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 39 · Chapter 18

"Can't Alice really be brought back to life? After all, reviving different people—wouldn't that count as the same wish?"

Merlin tried to play with words, hoping to find a loophole in the Crown of Fate. If he succeeded, who knew? It was uncertain.

"The key of your wish is to bring a dead person back to life. That's very clear. Too vague a wish can't be engraved on the Crown of Fate."

"If you want to become stronger, you must specify in what way? Strength means different things to different people. That's too vague and uncertain."

"I advise you not to try to trick the Crown of Fate with wordplay. It won't work. You think reviving different people isn't still reviving?"

"Naive. Unless your wish can bypass the clear process of going from death to life."

The three goddesses' voices echoed repeatedly, dispelling Merlin's attempt to find loopholes. A wish to bring someone back from the dead had already been used; it wouldn't work again just by changing the person.

Similarly, Rocky had cursed Merlin to death. If anyone could still come here in the future, they could not use the Crown of Fate to specifically kill any one person, by any means.

Wishes like guaranteed victory in battle, creating life, or learning soul control would not appear again either. The Crown of Fate had its own rules and could not be violated.

Merlin lowered his head and thought carefully. Suddenly an outlandish idea came to him, so he asked tentatively—

"Can I ask for Alice from the past to return to my side?"

"Possible. If you understand this wish as resurrection, there's no problem. But think carefully—who exactly would return to your side? That dead Alice and you are in the same timeline; her soul would still suffer persecution."

The three Fate Goddesses hid nothing and told Merlin the results plainly. That was their job.

Now Merlin was completely stunned. Turns out the Crown of Fate could actually do this—alter time and space.

"Does that mean... there would be two Alices? Wow, double the happiness!"

Merlin nodded, thinking this idea wasn't suitable. Though from different timelines, the other Alice would be suffering? Clearly not a good solution.

Moreover, he would harbor an illusion that the suffering Alice was the real wife. An Alice from a different timeline would lack a sense of reality, missing the crucial memories and experiences of this time.

"What should I do?"

Merlin dared not make a wish carelessly. He wanted to seize this important opportunity, but no matter how hard he racked his brains, he couldn't find a perfect way to bring Alice back.

Though he could wish for Alice's soul to return, what good would that do? Just a soul.

To revive Alice again, he'd need a massive amount of life force to heal her. Only then would it be possible.

But could he negotiate with the goddess who controlled the law of life? Not only did Merlin lack confidence, but even the landlady said the odds were slim. They could only try.

Thus the initiative was completely not in Merlin's side, but in that goddess's hands far above. Now Alice's soul had also been taken to the celestial realm.

Recalling his battle with Satan, Merlin felt immense pressure. Only a god could kill a god; he might not be able to defeat Maria and take Alice's soul.

Suddenly, Merlin remembered King Saint Sarite's words. His chaotic thoughts gradually cleared, and he hurriedly asked the three goddesses.

"As long as I have the Philosopher's Stone and survive after making the wish, I'll become a god, right?"

"Correct. But the Philosopher's Stone is only an item to offset the Crown of Fate's price. It has no direct relation to becoming a god. Whoever wears the Crown of Fate and comes back to life, by any means, will be granted divine power and become a god."

"Divine power?"

Merlin stared in astonishment, vaguely recalling what the mysterious man had told him in the cave of the Despair Canyon when he was young.

To master the power of the drawing sword technique, one had to remain on the brink of death at all times, or obtain divine power.

Perhaps divine power could completely root out the curse on his heart—and the opportunity was right before his eyes!

Merlin's heart thumped wildly. He felt he was close to lifting the curse of Asura. Maybe he would return to normal and could continue using the drawing sword technique's power!

"What exactly is divine power?"

The three Fate Goddesses thought Merlin's question wasn't off-topic and could answer him, so they explained unhurriedly—

"Divine power is the proof of a world builder. It contains the power of the primordial creation laws, and each is unique. Two people with the same law cannot exist simultaneously."

"After wearing the Crown of Fate, making a wish, and surviving, one is regarded as a creator-like existence, a participant in building this world, and thus granted divine power."

"The power of the laws within divine power protects the owner. Anyone without divine power cannot harm a divine power owner. This is the privilege of a creator, and also a rule."

Merlin lowered his head. After hearing the goddesses' explanation, he understood. This was a god? Protected at all times. No wonder only a god could kill a god.

When he was in hell, it wasn't that he couldn't defeat Satan, but the law power in Satan's divine power protected him, so Merlin could only make Satan feel pain, unable to harm him.

Divine power was like an invisible barrier, isolating gods from the world and all things, making them lord over all beings. Ordinary rules no longer applied to them.

"So if Alice could be resurrected, she would also—"

"Yes. Your wife would also be granted divine power. This fits the Crown of Fate's rules.

Merlin lowered his head. He understood something. His thoughts became much clearer, no longer lost—

As long as he had divine power, defeating Maria and reclaiming Alice's soul wouldn't be a problem.

This satisfied one condition for reviving Alice. There was a second condition.

That was a massive amount of life force. What if after defeating Maria, this guy would rather die than help him?

The law of life was now controlled by Maria. According to the Crown of Fate's rules, one cannot simultaneously possess divine power of the same law.

That was awkward. But the landlady had said there was another thing with surging life force—the life force flowing from the roots of the World Tree.

But that thing only existed in the Age of Gods!

Merlin raised his head. His expression turned grave. He silently vowed to seize the initiative, not let Maria lead him by the nose.

"I'm ready. I'll make my wish!"

"Are you sure?"

"Sure!

title: Chapter 19 — Return! Era of the Gods!
content:
Chapter 19 — Return! Era of the Gods!

Volume 39 · Chapter 19

Merlin's gaze was resolute, his thoughts crystal clear. If the Crown of Fate could interfere with events, then time-space jumps shouldn't be too difficult.

The three Fates fell silent for a moment, then a fierce wind suddenly erupted around them, causing countless candles to flicker. Mysterious runes floated in the air.

The light flashed repeatedly, and a pitch-black crown materialized out of thin air, slowly descending into Merlin's hands. An inexplicable power emanated from it, inspiring awe.

On the inner surface of the Crown of Fate were engraved the wishes left behind by predecessors, each wish having caused some change in the world. Merlin saw the wishes of Odin, Maria, and Satan, as well as Loki's vicious curse against him.

The last wish, naturally, was Alice's - a wish for Merlin to come back to life.

Merlin's expression was complex, imagining Alice's emotions when she made the wish. She hadn't considered her own life, but had put him first.

"Alice, I'll definitely save you. Wait patiently for me."

Merlin slowly put on the Crown of Fate, took out the true Philosopher's Stone, and said loudly after taking a deep breath.

"I want to go to the Era of the Gods, to stay there for a while!"

As soon as he finished speaking, the Crown of Fate on his head trembled slightly, and a mist dispersed, enveloping Merlin completely.

The Philosopher's Stone in Merlin's hand was disintegrating at a visible speed, turning into specks of starlight that vanished without a trace.

Merlin slowly closed his eyes, waiting to return to the distant past, planning to bring back the spring water from the base of the World Tree in the Era of the Gods.

The Crown of Fate seemed to be activated, emitting a buzzing sound that seemed to pierce through the soul, making it impossible to think.

However, the Philosopher's Stone had already been absorbed by the Crown of Fate, but after a long time, nothing happened.

Merlin furrowed his brow, opened his eyes, and found himself still in front of the three Fates, not having returned to the Era of the Gods.

"What's going on? Why am I still here? Shouldn't I have been sent to the past? Is the Crown of Fate unable to fulfill my wish?"

"It's not that. The reason you can't go back to the past is that the price you paid isn't enough. The Crown of Fate isn't something to be used casually; it requires a value equivalent to your wish."

The three Fates spoke without emotion, revealing the reason for the failed wish. To use the Crown of Fate, one had to pay with their life. Although the Philosopher's Stone could offset part of the cost, it was still insufficient.

"What do you mean? I've already used up my Philosopher's Stone. Why isn't it enough?"

"The Philosopher's Stone can offset part of the cost, meaning the user of the Crown of Fate won't die after making a wish, but it's still a bit short of the crown's power."

"What else do I need to do?" Merlin asked urgently, not having time to waste here.

"Simple, offer one of your eyes. With the Philosopher's Stone, the price will be sufficient."

"Offer one of my eyes?" Merlin was astonished. Using the Crown of Fate would make him a one-eyed person?

"That's right. Odin, Maria, and Satan all offered an eye when they made their wishes. That's the price for using the Crown of Fate, and you're no exception."

After hearing the Fates' explanation, Merlin was stunned. This request was hard for him to accept. He hadn't even started yet, and he had to blind one eye?

Merlin's eyes narrowed, suspecting the three Fates were deceiving him. What if he gouged out his eye and still couldn't return to the past?

Doubts surged in his mind, and Merlin's eyes showed clear hostility as he gripped the knife at his waist, considering whether to kill the three Fates in front of him.

"We know what you're thinking. Don't do something meaningless. Killing us won't help. If we die, your wish won't come true."

"Besides, we're not true gods, but manifestations of this world's will. Even if we die, new replacements will appear later."

"As long as this world exists, we'll never disappear. We'll just change forms and continue our work."

"If you refuse the Crown of Fate's rules and try to break them, that's your choice."

The three Fates sat calmly on their stone thrones, facing Merlin's immense threat without fear, like machines without emotion.

For them, answering the questions of those who came and fulfilling their wishes was just work to be done.

Even if Merlin killed them, it wouldn't solve anything fundamentally. Similar Fates would appear later, continuing the same work.

Merlin slowly released his grip on the knife handle, abandoning the idea of killing the Fates. He had come this far, and regret would mean losing his chance to save Alice.

But offering one of his eyes made him hesitant. Wasn't this self-mutilation?

However, thinking of Alice possibly suffering in the heavens, his heart couldn't calm down.

Alice was willing to give her life for him. What was losing an eye compared to that?

Merlin took a deep breath, pointed at the Crown of Fate above him, and asked the Fates loudly.

"If I offer one of my eyes, will this thing really fulfill my wish?"

"Of course. You've already been killed once by the Crown of Fate. What more do you have to doubt?"

Merlin lowered his head, gritted his teeth, and poked his right hand's fingers directly into his left eye socket. Excruciating pain surged up.

He had to endure it until he dug out his left eyeball!

This was a pain ordinary people couldn't bear. Merlin almost fainted several times, clearly hearing the sound of his fingers rubbing against his eyeball's fluids.

When Merlin finally dug out his left eyeball, countless electric currents flashed through his brain, gradually forming a new divine aura.

Merlin slowly came to from his faint, the intense pain from his left eye jolting him awake.

He covered his left eye, lying on the ground and gasping for breath. The immense pain made his whole body ache. If this still couldn't fulfill his wish, he'd definitely kill those three giant women!

Merlin cursed in his heart, gradually adapting to the pain of losing an eye after a while. With only one right eye left, he couldn't adjust to seeing things for a while, especially judging distances, which became extremely blurry.

Merlin covered his bleeding left eye, trembling as he opened his eyelid, and found himself no longer in front of the three Fates, but in an unfamiliar place.

All around were dense jungles, with towering ancient trees packed tightly together. Even the smallest trees required a dozen people to encircle.

The ground was covered in strange, unknown plants that Merlin couldn't identify.

The sky was obscured by thick foliage, and sunlight couldn't penetrate this dark forest.

The scene before Merlin felt somewhat familiar, similar to the forest in the Valley of Despair, with ancient trees everywhere.

This wasn't surprising, as the forest in the Valley of Despair was well-preserved, almost identical to the natural environment of the ancient era.

Merlin nervously swallowed, dispelling his doubts. He had no doubt he had successfully arrived in the Era of the Gods.

Brothers, I'm going to refine the final outline.

There might be an update today, or there might not be.

As you can see, we're in the final stage.

So, I'll refine the outline to see if there are any problems.

If possible, I want a brilliant ending, not just filling in the blanks mechanically. I want something different.

I just looked at the outline, and if I write it normally, the plot is too dull.

So, I plan to organize it tonight to make the plot more exciting, with more suspense and variables.

The ending will definitely be good, so don't worry.

title: Chapter 20 — Resuming Updates
content:
Chapter 20 — Resuming Updates

Volume 39 · Chapter 20

Merlin hadn't even had time to fully comprehend the unfamiliar world before his head erupted in intense pain.

He clutched his head, wincing in agony as he felt something suddenly appear in his mind?

Gray law runes flickered in and out of visibility on Merlin's body, transforming him from the inside out—

The Law of Destruction, the ultimate destructive force!

Among the many creation laws, the Law of Destruction possessed the most formidable destructive power, with no comparable force to be found.

The emergence of the Law of Destruction often heralded the world's approach to its end, as this destructive force would bring about a fate of destruction.

"God..."

"This is the power of the law granted by the divine?"

"How amazing..."

Merlin gazed at the gray law runes in his hand, which seemed to possess a consciousness of their own as they continuously circled around him.

He felt he could freely command the Law of Destruction, and its power was boundless, with no risk of depletion.

As long as this era continued to function normally, the power of the law's ruler would be eternal—this was indeed sufficient to be considered aberrant.

No wonder those so-called main gods looked down on all living beings with contempt; possessing divinity and commanding the power of the laws meant standing at the pinnacle of the highest dimension.

Merlin recalled something—the mysterious person in the cave of Despair Valley had said—

Now that he had obtained divinity, he no longer needed to be on the brink of death to unleash the full power of his sword technique.

But how could he safely remove the golden cone lodged in his heart?

Rashly pulling out the golden cone might threaten Merlin's life; he had to find a safe method first.

However, this wasn't the most pressing matter. Merlin hadn't forgotten his original goal: to find the spring water at the base of the World Tree and bring it back.

In the era of the gods, the World Tree supported the entire world and nurtured countless ancient gods, constantly absorbing the life spring water from its base to sustain its own life.

Merlin thought that if he were to head to the base of the World Tree, he would inevitably clash with the ancient gods—this was something he had to consider.

Legend had it that the entrance to the World Tree's interior wasn't below, but at the very top, in the realm of the King of the Gods, Asgard—

To reach the base of the World Tree and obtain the spring of life, he would first have to ascend to the peak of the World Tree. The entrance had long been occupied by Odin, who treated the spring water as his own treasure.

Merlin shook his head, putting aside his chaotic thoughts for the time being. For now, he should focus on understanding this era and gradually adapting to it.

Regarding the Era of the Gods, Merlin's knowledge was limited, gleaned only from a few ancient texts and historical records, which were far from detailed—

It was said that the Era of the Gods was a time when gods and humans coexisted, with ancient gods and lower species living together on the same continent in utter chaos and disorder.

The ancient gods stood high above, monopolizing all wealth and capriciously playing with the lives of lower beings.

To these gods, lower beings were nothing more than slaves, mere toys to alleviate their boredom.

Faced with such powerful creators, the lower beings could only cower in submission, devoid of any will to resist.

These were the accounts recorded in some texts, though Merlin wasn't certain of their accuracy. Still, they held some reference value.

Merlin surveyed his surroundings, unable to determine his location. It appeared to be a vast jungle, with dim lighting that felt like the depths of evening.

Normally, anyone who strayed into this forest would easily get lost, but Merlin's experience living in Despair Valley allowed him to judge directions without difficulty.

Considering various factors, Merlin roughly determined which direction to head in to find a straight path out of the forest. Other matters could be dealt with later.

The forest's vast expanse exceeded his imagination. Merlin had been walking in a straight line for a long time, yet he still couldn't see the end.

Merlin was certain he hadn't lost his way, but he had misjudged the situation before him.

This forest was at least dozens of times larger than the one in Despair Valley, making it far from easy to leave.

Without sunlight, Merlin had no idea how long he had been walking in the forest—definitely several days.

Merlin felt the pain in his gouged-out left eye growing worse, failing to adapt to the agony of losing an eye, which only intensified.

The blood on his body had long since congealed, clinging to his face like a layer of dead skin, a ghastly sight!

"Why was I transported to this godforsaken place?"

Merlin muttered to himself, exhausted and hoping to find a water source to clean his hollow left eye, perhaps alleviating some of the pain.

Suddenly, Merlin perked up his ears, faintly hearing the sound of water coming from the northwest. Overjoyed, he hastened his pace.

The sound of water cascading from above grew louder as Merlin pushed through layers of vines and weeds, soon catching sight of a distant waterfall.

"Indeed!"

Merlin was overjoyed, disregarding everything else as he jumped down the low cliff, then walked while stripping off his dirty clothes until he was completely clean.

In the ancient, uninhabited forest, a blond man stood naked, his buttocks exposed as he danced toward the waterfall with abandon!

The scene was bizarre and difficult to look at, with Merlin resembling Tarzan at that moment.

Others might have woven a grass skirt, but Merlin, in the absence of people, simply let loose.

Upon reaching the waterfall, Merlin initially intended to leap in and swim a few laps, but he suddenly stopped, his expression alert as he stared at the ground—

Several pieces of white silk clothing lay on the shore, resembling a female priestess's attire.

To prevent the clothes from being blown away by the wind, their owner had weighted them down.

Merlin furrowed his brow, shocked to discover that someone—specifically a woman—existed in this desolate place.

Unable to discern whether this person was friend or foe, he dared not call out, especially in his current naked state.

Merlin lifted his gaze, scanning the water's surface. He sensed the clothes' owner was nearby, possibly about to emerge at any moment.

Given his appearance, he would undoubtedly be mistaken for a pervert. It would be better to retreat, put on some clothes, and return to talk to this person.

Just as Merlin was about to quietly withdraw, his attention was caught by the white underwear on top of the clothes. He wasn't a pervert, but the underwear seemed somewhat familiar?

Merlin's heart racing, he nervously swallowed and crept forward to pick up the underwear, carefully unfolding it—

A small bear pattern appeared before his eyes, seemingly mocking him. How's it look? s.B!

title: Chapter 21 — Usurpation
content:
Chapter 21 — Usurpation

Volume 39 · Chapter 21

I'm truly seeing ghosts!

Why does someone with the same taste as Alice exist in this era?

It's completely devoid of any aesthetic sense!

Looking at the priest's robe next to me, it doesn't seem like it's for a child, so why would someone wear something so childish?!

Merlin gazed at the underwear spread out before him, his emotions in utter turmoil, never imagining that in this distant era of the gods, there would still be someone like Alice.

Just as Merlin was about to quietly put the underwear down and pretend he hadn't seen it, his hollow left eye suddenly transmitted intense pain, piercing straight to his spiritual core!

"Ow!"

Merlin clutched his left eye, drawing in a sharp breath as his consciousness began to blur. The sudden, overwhelming pain caused him to faint on the spot.

Merlin, still clutching the underwear, lay unconscious on the ground for who knows how long. In the rippling water, a silver-haired girl emerged like a lotus flower.

She seemed just as bewildered as Merlin, having stumbled into the forest and discovered the waterfall by chance, unable to resist taking a bath.

But this girl probably never imagined that someone else would discover this place besides herself.

The girl's face wore a faint smile as she slowly stood up from the water, adjusting her wet hair. Clearly, she was in an excellent mood after her bath.

Transparent water droplets glowed with faint light as they trickled down her snow-white skin, flowing unimpeded over her flat chest.

The silver-haired girl standing in the water pool formed a stark contrast with the surrounding, enclosed forest, giving the illusion that she was the only light in the darkness.

"I didn't expect to find a water source here, perfect for washing off the dirt. I'm really lucky."

The silver-haired girl muttered happily, but then caught sight of the unconscious Merlin on the shore, letting out a startled cry before quickly hiding back in the water.

She slowly floated up halfway, her face flushed with shyness as she warily eyed the motionless Merlin on the shore.

Who is this person? He doesn't look like a good guy.

There are hidden dangers everywhere in the forest, so why would someone come to a place like this?

Judging by his attire, he doesn't seem to be a hunter, more like a vagrant who wandered into the forest.

The silver-haired girl speculated in her mind, too afraid to come ashore. If she did, this man who suddenly appeared might see her naked.

She was extremely anxious, wanting to put on her clothes as soon as possible, but her clothes were near the man. If she rushed ashore, she'd be too embarrassed to show her face again.

The silver-haired girl was at her wit's end. She couldn't stay in the water forever, so she mustered her courage and loudly called out to the unconscious Merlin:

"Hey, could you please leave for a bit?"

I was here first, so let me get dressed and then you can come back, okay?

"Everything should follow the principle of first come, first served, right?"

"Hey! Can you hear me or not?!"

No matter how the silver-haired girl shouted, Merlin remained unresponsive, still unconscious and unable to hear her voice.

After calling out several more times, the silver-haired girl felt despair, wondering if he was intentionally teasing her.

How infuriating! I'm a goddess, and yet I'm being bullied by a vagrant!

Anger flashed in the silver-haired girl's eyes, so she steeled herself and stood up from the water again, covering her chest and lower body with her hands as she cautiously made her way ashore.

When she reached the unconscious Merlin, she realized he had fainted, which explained why he hadn't reacted to her calls.

"I was so scared, turns out he passed out,"

But before the silver-haired girl could catch her breath, she saw that Merlin was clutching her underwear, causing her face to flush with anger and shame.

"Just as I expected, this guy isn't a good person!"

Now Merlin's reputation was irreparably ruined in the silver-haired girl's eyes. He wasn't just bad; he was a scoundrel, a vagrant, and a lecherous villain!

The silver-haired girl angrily snatched her underwear back from Merlin, glaring at his unconscious form as she began thinking of ways to punish this pervert.

"I'll make you pay!"

"There's no power fluctuation, so he's definitely a mortal."

"A mere mortal dares to bully me? How outrageous!"

When Merlin came to again, he found himself in a rather awkward situation, extremely passive.

He saw that he had been labeled as a great villain, with the silver-haired girl using unknown radiant chains to bind him to a tree.

The chains weren't ordinary, emitting a holy aura that made Merlin uncomfortable. Clearly, they were formed from the girl's divine power.

What the...?!

Merlin struggled slightly, discovering he was bound very tightly. Without expending some effort, he couldn't break free.

He looked up discontentedly, scanning his surroundings until he spotted the silver-haired girl standing not far away.

The silver-haired girl had already dressed in a pristine white priest's robe, with a green olive wreath on her head that added a touch of playfulness.

In her hand, she held a whip made from woven branches, cracking it loudly.

"Now that you're awake, how should I punish you?"

The silver-haired girl's face wore a triumphant smile. She had waited for this moment, and although she wouldn't kill him, this villain before her was too detestable. He needed to be taught a lesson.

Merlin's expression was blank, his eyes wide with shock as he stared at the silver-haired girl's face, his mind flooded with questions.

"Alice?"

"Huh? What Alice?"

The silver-haired girl asked in confusion, having never heard the name "Alice" before.

Merlin's eyes widened in realization, quickly regaining his composure as he thought, Of course! This is the Era of the Gods, and Alice hasn't been born yet. But this person's appearance...

"What's your name?"

"Huh?" The silver-haired girl looked puzzled, saying in surprise, "You look human, so why don't you recognize me? No human wouldn't know me. You look like a savage from some deep mountain forest."

Merlin's expression was complex, a hint of understanding in his heart, but he wanted a definitive answer. "That's right, I'm a savage. You're correct."

The silver-haired girl furrowed her brow, introducing herself impatiently, "I am Teresa, the Goddess of Fortune. My sister Maria is the creator of humanity. How's that? Now do you know how noble my status is?"

Merlin's eyelid twitched, his layers of confusion suddenly clearing up. He exclaimed in a tone of realization:

"Indeed..."

"Is this also fate's arrangement?"

Merlin's eyes sparkled with a hint of understanding, but his words were left hanging, awaiting the goddess's response.

title: Chapter 22 — Unreliable Goddess (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 22 — Unreliable Goddess (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 39 · Chapter 22

Teresa couldn't understand Merlin's muttering, thinking this man who suddenly appeared was very strange.
As a human, she didn't even recognize her own human goddess?
However, Teresa didn't care about that; her mind was full of wanting to properly punish this shameless villain.
"Don't change the subject—I've caught you red‑handed, and you still want to bluff your way out?"
"Huh? What caught red‑handed? I didn't do anything."
Merlin said with an innocent face, after fainting from pain he had no idea what happened.
Seeing Merlin still putting on an act, Teresa grew even angrier, thinking that if he sincerely admitted his mistake, the punishment
would be a bit lighter.
"What are you pretending? Do you think I wouldn't know? Just now you were trying to sneak a peek at me."
"Huh? ? ? Merlin's head filled with question marks; after thinking it over he realized, 'Wait! It's all a misunderstanding!'"
"Misunderstanding? You were caught red‑handed and still call it a misunderstanding?" Teresa stroked the vine whip in her hand, speaking sternly, "Desecrating a goddess is a serious crime; fortunately you're facing me—if it were my sister, you'd already be chopped into minced meat."
Merlin rolled his eyes, secretly sighing that he shouldn't have been nosy, and forced a smile: 'Beautiful goddess, it's really a misunderstanding; your taste is similar to someone I know, so I got curious.'
"Excuse!" Teresa shouted, raising the vine whip to give Merlin a beating.
"Don't jump to conclusions—take a good look, do I look like a major villain?" Merlin asked confidently.
"Yes! From head to toe you look like one!" Teresa said decisively.
Merlin sighed, thinking this guy's personality was somewhat like Alice's; when angry, communication basically breaks down.
Recalling Alice, at first she also regarded Merlin as an utterly evil villain.
The scene before her eyes, like
"Goddess, I've restrained myself as much as possible; the reason I can still calmly talk with you is to clear up the misunderstanding."
"Hmph, you're bound and can't move, yet you talk big—I've never seen such a shameless lecher act so self‑righteous!" Teresa said, hands on her hips, fuming.
Merlin narrowed his eyes, speaking with deep meaning: 'You don't really think these chains can bind me, do you?'
"How so? Although my strength isn't great, it's more than enough to deal with you." Teresa lifted her chin proudly.
"If I can't handle other ancient gods, does that mean I can't even deal with a mere mortal?"
"Well, this is all your own doing."
Merlin suddenly clenched his fists, and the light chains wrapped around him shattered instantly into pieces.
These light chains weren't nearly as strong as imagined; Merlin could break free without effort.
"What the—?"
Teresa was startled; this was the strongest magic she could muster, yet Merlin broke free easily.
As the Lucky Goddess, her power is extremely weak, ranking among the lowest of the ancient gods.
However, her sister Maria told Teresa that she possesses a luck beyond ordinary comprehension.
This ability is far more formidable than mere world‑shattering destruction; it can be called being blessed by luck.
Yet Teresa feels no luck accompanying her, cannot use this illusory ability, and even suspects her sister Maria is comforting her with lies.
Because Teresa believes she's no different from others—luck comes and goes, and wanting something doesn't guarantee you'll get it right away.
Teresa collapsed onto the ground, pointing at Merlin, hardly believing her eyes that he could easily break her magic chains, proving his strength far exceeds hers.
"You're not a mortal?"
"According to what you say, I'm a savage." Merlin replied mockingly.
Teresa regretted deeply; had she known, she should have put on clothes and fled, avoiding any involvement with this man.
Merlin leisurely picked up the vine whip from the ground, flashing a ill‑intentioned smile: 'Since I'm a savage, what brutal way should I use on you, Goddess?'
"No, don't, don't come over!"
Teresa let out a scream, continually backing away, but her strength was too weak—she probably couldn't even escape.
In the end, she accidentally bumped into a fruit tree, completely cutting off any retreat, her back pressed against the rough bark.
A leaf slowly drifted down from above onto her head, making this Lucky Goddess, who had previously been putting on airs, look especially disheveled.
Facing Merlin's step‑by‑step approach, Teresa's eyes filled with fear, her hands clutched to her chest, her body curled up trembling.
"Don't! Don't come near me!"
"That's not up to you." Merlin's evil grin grew more wanton.
Teresa was scared to tears, unable to stop imagining what would happen next, fully putting herself in the victim's role, her heart pounding—
"I'm doomed—I'll surely be ruthlessly bullied by you, you great villain!"
"First, my clothes will be violently torn off, then the sinful big hand will grope all over my body."
"Then your disgusting tongue will invade every corner, and finally I'll be forcibly defiled."
"Who knows if you have some special fetish—I'll definitely be played to pieces!"
"? ? ? Merlin's head filled with question marks, thinking even Alice wouldn't have such a rich imagination; this description is too vivid."
"Let me, the goddess, be stained—you must feel accomplished, right? Don't keep coming closer!" Teresa's face turned pale as she shouted in fear, "Watch out, I'll drag you down with me!"
Merlin's face darkened as he approached Teresa, slowly squatting down and extending his 'sinful' hand.
"Ugh!" Teresa's whole body tensed, like a puffed‑up cat rejecting everything around her.
It's all Teresa's fault for having such a rich imagination; even she herself believed what would happen next, but she thought too much.
Then Merlin used his hand to remove the leaf on Teresa's head, then calmly looked at her and said softly—
"I'm not a bad person; you don't need to be so nervous."
"Huh?"
Teresa opened her eyes, staring at Merlin with disbelief, wondering if it was real—this rude man, does he have any thoughts about me at all?
Before Teresa could speak, a fruit from the tree suddenly fell, hitting her squarely on the forehead, putting an end to the farce.
Teresa rolled her eyes, swayed in front of Merlin, and fainted; the Lucky Buff seemed to have no effect.
Merlin furrowed his brow, stroked his chin, and pondered—
This guy
really the Lucky Goddess?

title: Chapter 23 — Interwoven World Lines
content:
Chapter 23 — Interwoven World Lines

Volume 39 · Chapter 23

The campfire rose in the darkened forest. Merlin had bound a rag around his head to cover his missing left eye.

After cleaning the wound on his left eye, Merlin felt much better, at least that piercing pain was no longer unbearable.

He sat on a quiet rock, absentmindedly tossing firewood into the flames, pondering all sorts of questions—

This girl was Maria's younger sister, the Lucky Goddess Theresia. But she seemed entirely harmless, seemingly very different from Maria's personality?

According to the information Mrs. Landlady had revealed, Maria had specifically created Alice as a soul vessel in order to revive her.

She hoped that as Alice grew, Theresia's damaged soul would heal, completing the entire revival plan.

Undoubtedly, Theresia's damaged soul was also part of Alice's composition, but she was终究 not the Alice who had accompanied me.

She didn't possess shared memories with me, nor those important experiences; clearly, she was another person entirely and couldn't be treated as Alice.

But in a certain sense, Alice was the continuation of Theresia's life—that is, Theresia's past life—and there existed an undeniable connection between the two.

If Maria's plan succeeded, would all of Alice's memories disappear? Or would the two merge, with one person possessing memories from both lives?

Perhaps I shouldn't waste time on her but should instead hurry to the World Tree, find the Fountain of Life, and return to the original timeline.

Merlin's gaze shifted toward Theresia, who was sleeping soundly. Under the firelight, his brows furrowed slightly, his heart a tangled mess—

She carried too many shadows of Alice. Aside from lacking memories with me, she was basically the same as when I first met Alice.

Should I just leave her here and walk away? Completely severing ties would be a good choice.

But this girl was so weak that I simply couldn't feel at ease leaving her.

No wonder she died in the future. With such weakness, surviving in an era filled with Ancient Gods was indeed not easy.

Theresia's eyelids trembled slightly as she slowly woke from her coma. She didn't panic and scream loudly; instead, she narrowed her eyes slightly, taking in her surroundings.

Seeing Merlin sitting nearby by the campfire, seated alone on a stone with a thoughtful expression, her mood grew extremely tense.

Theresia glanced down at herself and discovered that Merlin's coat had been draped over her without her noticing. This considerate gesture didn't relax her guard at all—instead, she panicked more—

Good heavens, he even covered me with clothes. Has the aftermath already happened?

I don't even know what happened! This is so miserable!

What kind of Lucky Goddess am I? Is there anyone more unfortunate than me?

Theresia's expression turned desperate, and she subconsciously peeked under Merlin's coat to check inside, finding that her clothes were still on, seemingly confirming that nothing like what she imagined had occurred—

Hmm???

What's going on?

My clothes are all still here?

No way? This big villain really didn't touch me?

Theresia stared at Merlin's back with a complicated expression. At that moment, she felt a hint of失落ness— even a villain as shamelessly bold as him wasn't interested in her. That was too pitiful!

She looked at the coat covering her, and her impression of Merlin improved slightly. Perhaps there had truly been some misunderstanding earlier. He wasn't as vile as she had imagined.

"Awake yet, Miss Goddess?"

Merlin stood with his back to Theresia. He had long noticed she was awake but hadn't called her out on it. However, he had no idea what chaotic nonsense was going through this goddess's head.

Theresia's expression turned panicked. Unsure of how to face Merlin, she simply closed her eyes and continued pretending to be unconscious.

"Stop pretending. I know you're already awake. Is it because you know it was all a misunderstanding and you can't face me?"

Hearing Merlin's mocking tone, Theresia's pride was struck. Biting her teeth, she threw off Merlin's coat, stood up from the ground, and glared at him with her hands on her hips.

"What misunderstanding? You just failed to succeed! Hmph~!"

"Starting to twist words now?" Merlin said wearily, thinking that she was exactly like Alice—refusing to admit her mistakes no matter what.

"Well, I guess I'll reluctantly say you're not that bad of a person. My impression of you has improved, just a little bit." Alice held up two fingers to measure, saying defiantly, "Only a tiny bit. It just proves you still have some conscience and aren't rotten to the core."

Merlin smiled faintly, not expecting Theresia to soften and apologize. After all, perhaps Alice's personality came from this person.

"So... who exactly are you?"

"A barbarian."

"Stop joking! You broke through the chains I condensed with my divine power. Your strength should be above demigod level, right?" Theresia stared at Merlin, extremely curious about his identity. "Could you be in the God Realm? Definitely not an Ancient God, right? I've never seen you before."

Facing these guesses, Merlin smiled without answering. He didn't plan to reveal too much about himself. Besides, he didn't belong to this era, so the fewer entanglements, the better.

Merlin guessed that his return to the Era of Gods wasn't the true past but rather a point along some timeline. This conjecture wasn't baseless—it came from the Three Fates Goddesses.

Of course, when Merlin wished for the past living Alice to be brought back to the correct timeline, the three goddesses replied that two Alice versions would appear, and that Alice, who was suffering in the Heavenly Realm, would not disappear.

This proved that the world might consist of countless worldlines, intertwining with each other, where the progression of time might differ. Merlin had simply arrived at a past point on some worldline.

That is to say, as long as Merlin stayed here long enough and crossed several eras, he might very well meet his other self!

Countless worldlines, each containing a Merlin and an Alice, but their personalities, experiences, and even destinies might have subtle differences.

How many times had Merlin faced choices in his life? Even he wasn't sure. Perhaps the Merlins in other worldlines had made unexpected choices, causing their fate's trajectory to diverge.

On the correct worldline, Merlin and Alice were together. But on different worldlines, due to different choices, Merlin and Alice might not have ended up together—

They might even hate each other to the point of fighting to the death.

Merlin might have married Margaret, or Mayesfield.

Alice might have also chosen someone else, like Arnold, who had once relentlessly pursued her.

All of these were possible. The Schrödinger's cat experiment was exactly like this—in the box of poison gas, the cat could either be dead or alive, producing two possible outcomes.

So Merlin had already realized the key issue. To put it nicely, he was a time traveler; to put it harshly, he was a variable interfering with the worldline. Full of uncertainty—

It was possible that his small actions could trigger a butterfly effect in the future, causing a major upheaval and preventing this worldline from heading in the right direction.

Merlin secretly decided to avoid getting too entangled here, minimizing his impact to the absolute least.

This wasn't only for his own sake but also for the Merlin and Alice of this worldline.

title: Chapter 24 — True Era
content:
Chapter 24 — True Era

Volume 39 · Chapter 24

"You take me for what you wish."

Merlin gave Theresa an evasive answer; he would not admit that he came from the future, nor did he want the Goddess of Fortune to know him too deeply.

If possible, Merlin hoped to remain a mere passerby, interfering with no historical进程 and ensuring the future held no unpredictable events.

"Hmm?" Theresa was puzzled, but still believed her guess was correct. Perhaps Merlin had always lived as a native of this forest. "Someone who can cultivate to the Saint-tier on their own is rare. You do have some talent. Don't tell me you know nothing because you've been hiding in these mountains cultivating all this time?"

"Something like that," Merlin replied in a casual tone.

"Do you plan to stay here forever? Any other plans for the future?" Theresa said meaningfully.

Merlin frowned slightly and retorted, "What do you mean by that?"

"Join us and contribute to humanity's rise! You're human after all, and staying hidden in this forest won't allow you to showcase your talent. Only by leaving here will you see the world. Wouldn't that be good?" Theresa extended an olive branch to Merlin.

Merlin chuckled dryly, thinking that if he were to make himself valuable, it would surely disturb the timeline of this world-line far too greatly, making everyone's fate full of uncertainty.

"What's with that attitude? Just leave this forest with me, and I'll personally recommend you to my older sister. You'll surely be given important duties then. Not everyone can earn my sister's trust, and you should feel honored." Theresa said proudly.

She naturally admired her older sister Maria deeply.

"Are you serious?" Merlin's expression turned strange. He thought: I'm the Demon Lord. I'd serve Maria? That's absolutely ridiculous.

"Of course I'm serious. You may think living in the forest is fine, but once you leave, you might not be able to survive outside!" Theresa said with a grave expression.

"Why?" Merlin asked inquiringly.

"How long have you been hiding in this forest? How can you know nothing?"

Theresa pursed her brows, hands on her hips, sounding exasperated, as if dealing with an antique who couldn't keep up with the times.

"It's because we humans are weak. If we don't unite, we could be destroyed at any moment."

"There are no rules in the outside world. Only strength matters."

"Do you understand what I'm saying?"

Merlin adopted a thoughtful expression, recalling the ancient texts he had seen, and asked curiously, "Is it because the Ancient Gods, relying on their status as creators, freely wreak havoc upon the world?"

"Who told you that?" Theresa seemed to have heard something quite novel.

"Well, I overheard it by chance..." Merlin's gaze flickered away as he answered.

"That's not it! There are too many Ancient Gods, both good and bad. How did it become black-and-white in your mouth?" Theresa paused and argued indignantly. "That's too one-sided. Among the Ancient Gods, there are also those who hope for peace, like my older sister. Despite being a creator of humanity, she oppressed no one and only wished to guide humanity toward prosperity."

Merlin fell silent, thinking: Is Maria really that kind of person? If he hadn't personally returned to the Era of Gods, he would never have known.

Of course, Theresa's words were not necessarily entirely correct. Upon careful reflection, humanity was so weak during the Era of Gods that it couldn't have wreaked havoc on the world even if it wanted to.

So hoping for peace may have been passive. If Maria had been powerful enough, she might have become like the other Ancient Gods and become the source of chaos.

There were too many stories of dragon-slaying warriors eventually becoming dragons themselves. If the world is compared to a cake, it's only so big; it cannot grow larger.

Merlin didn't believe in the possibility of peace at all; he only believed in relative peace. Theresa appeared far too naive and idealistic in his eyes.

"Look at me, I'm also an Ancient God. Do I seem like someone who would wreak havoc upon the world?"

Merlin said nothing, thinking: Your older sister caused a series of upheavals in the future; in a sense, she truly was the root cause of that chaos.

"Some Ancient Gods protect their subjects, while others, as you said, oppress them. Powerful Ancient Gods threaten weak ones to satisfy their own desires. In short, this world is very complicated, absolutely not black-and-white."

Merlin looked away, musing that those ancient texts indeed differed somewhat from the true Era of Gods and could not be fully trusted. The people who recorded them were likely insufficiently objective and公正, mixing in no small amount of their own emotions.

Theresa pressed her palms together in a wishing gesture and said with utter seriousness—

"My wish is simple: that humanity may one day escape its current predicament and become prosperous and mighty."

"So no one will ever be bullied again, nor threatened by those powerful, evil Ancient Gods. Complete liberation!"

"Well? Isn't my wish wonderful? If it comes true, you'll be a beneficiary too!"

"You're terrifyingly naive." A bead of cold sweat rolled down Merlin's forehead. He thought: In the future, Theresa's wish does come true. Humanity does become prosperous and mighty, and yet they begin oppressing other races.

"What do you mean by that? Looking down on me?" Theresa asked angrily.

"No." Merlin shook his head. He wasn't denying Theresa's ideals, but the world's cake is limited. The rise of one race inevitably accompanies the decline of another. That is the rule.

Theresa pouted, realizing she simply couldn't read the man with one blind eye. She felt he held many secrets.

"So... will you leave the forest with me?"

"I can consider it."

Merlin敷衍 answered. He decided to make use of Maria and Theresa to learn more about the Era of Gods, and then formulate a plan to plunder the Spring of Life.

But the naive Theresa failed to notice Merlin's敷衍 tone and took the matter seriously. Her expression showed delight, thinking that bringing back a Saint-tier powerhouse for her older sister Maria would surely earn praise.

"That's wonderful then."

"Allow me to ask a question. Why are you in this forest? Aren't you afraid of danger alone? This place is full of ferocious magical beasts."

Merlin was curious why Theresa dared to enter the forest. He had casually dealt with several troublesome magical beasts along the way.

With Theresa's poor strength, she would easily have become fodder for those beasts. Merlin didn't believe she could have reached here unscathed.

Theresa's eyes showed confusion, and she said with an innocent expression, "Magical beasts? What magical beasts? I haven't encountered any. Everyone says this forest is dangerous, but I think it's fine~"

"???" Merlin secretly swallowed, feeling something was very wrong here. Something must have gone awry.

Was it the Lucky BUFF playing tricks?

It allowed a goofy goose to reach the depths of the forest unscathed, even having the leisure to take a bath.

title: Chapter 25 — Fall into (Monthly Ticket Extra)
content:
Chapter 25 — Fall into (Monthly Ticket Extra)

Volume 39 · Chapter 25

"Actually, I came here to find something deep in the forest that can help my older sister get through her current predicament."

Teresa looked up and recalled what had happened not long ago. Although she was weak, she still wanted to know if she could share some of her sister's burdens.
