"Predicament? What kind of predicament?" Merlin didn't think there was any problem that could stump that lofty goddess.

"The dragon race has always been bullying us. That detestable black dragon Nidhogg demands that we send him numerous young children for his enjoyment, or he will burn down most of our human tribes." Teresa frowned, speaking with a worried tone. "My older sister is trying to figure out a solution. She's so anxious that she looks years older. She not only has to deal with that despicable black dragon, but also with Odin, the King of Gods who lives in Asgard."

"Odin?" Merlin furrowed his brow slightly.

"He's the ruler of this world! Don't you even know that? His subordinates gather a massive number of Ancient Gods, and he possesses absolute ruling power. He has never lost a single battle and has never been defeated in his entire life. He is simply the strongest deity unmatched by anyone!" A deep fear rose on Teresa's face as she continued, "Although King of Gods Odin appears different from the other evil Ancient Gods on the surface and can be communicated with, his methods are equally unacceptable."

"What methods?" Merlin asked curiously.

"The Valhalla. I heard that it's a place where Odin collects the souls of the strong. No one seems to know exactly what he uses them for." Teresa thought for a moment and continued, "As the ruler of this world, Odin requires every race to offer him the souls of their strong warriors. Sometimes even some Ancient Gods can't escape the fate of being sent to Valhalla. Whoever dares to rebel will face utter destruction."

Merlin pondered, wondering what Valhalla was actually used for. He had visited the Ruins of the Gods before and never found any trace of Valhalla. Had it already been destroyed?

"However, this situation isn't entirely without room for maneuver, because Odin has a unique hobby." Teresa's tone turned mysterious.

"What?"

"He likes listening to stories, and he's extremely obsessed with them. If a story is well-told and manages to move him, then you can temporarily avoid offering souls to him." Teresa's expression grew helplessly resigned. "Because of this hobby, Odin has almost heard every story there is, so it's actually quite difficult to move him with a tale."

"What a bizarre hobby." Merlin found it hard to understand. Was it because he'd already reached the peak of the world that he needed novel stories to pass the time?

"In any case, I came here to find a way to help my sister. Our current situation is very dangerous. Odin is demanding the souls of the strong, and my sister can only hold things together for now. But that black dragon has come again. While my sister was in Asgard telling stories, I wanted to handle this nuisance and share some of the pressure. My sister will definitely be proud of me." Teresa said with full confidence.

"What do you plan to do?" Merlin asked.

"Don't ask so many questions. Just follow me. If anything dangerous happens, I'll leave it to you~"

Under Teresa's guidance, Merlin had no choice but to temporarily set aside his plans to leave the forest.

Instead, he followed that unreliable goddess deeper and deeper into the heart of the forest.

Merlin decided that after finishing his business, he would take Teresa with him to leave this forest and learn more through Maria and Teresa.

After reaching the deepest part of the forest, Teresa searched for a long time but couldn't find any trace at all. She could only choose to rest for a bit and continue searching carefully.

"Your left eye... how did you lose it?" Teresa curiously leaned close to Merlin, studying him.

"I dug it out myself." Merlin answered truthfully.

"Huh? Why would you do something like that?" Teresa looked at him as if he were an idiot.

"To save someone." Merlin said nonchalantly.

"Who?" Teresa grew even more curious. If someone was important enough to dig out one's own eyes to save, they must have been very significant, right?

Merlin hesitated, then shook his head. "It has nothing to do with you."

"Hmph!" Teresa pouted and turned her head away angrily. Her expression was strikingly similar to Alice's, which made Merlin stare blankly for a moment. "Fine then. I went through all that trouble answering your endless questions for nothing."

Merlin didn't plan to say much. He didn't want to form too deep a bond with Teresa. The less people in this era knew about him, the better he could avoid interference caused by himself.

Teresa stole a glance at Merlin and said in a tempting tone, "If you're willing to answer me, maybe I'd feel generous and help cure your eye~"

"Really?" Merlin asked in surprise. He felt this was unlikely, since his eye had already been the price paid for using the Crown of Destiny.

"Between you and me, I'm very confident in my healing abilities. Healing the eye you lost would be a piece of cake!" Teresa gave herself a thumbs-up, her eyes shining with full confidence.

Although Merlin was suspicious, he was still quite tempted. One eye was far too inconvenient. So he dishonestly began to deceive the naive girl.

"Then try it. If you can cure my eye, I'll answer all your questions."

Merlin said that aloud, but added "Yeah, right" in his heart. He wouldn't honestly answer Teresa's questions.

Teresa confidently extended both hands, aimed at Merlin's left eye, and released waves of warm light, attempting to make his eye grow back.

However, after trying for a long time, Merlin's lost left eye showed no reaction at all. It simply couldn't be healed.

"What's going on? My Divine Power healing can regenerate even severed limbs. Why doesn't it work on your eye?"

"Looks like your training isn't quite up to par, Miss Goddess. Let's keep looking for what you need."

Merlin sighed. As he had suspected, his lost left eye probably wouldn't return. How could the price of the Crown of Destiny be undone?

As far as Merlin knew, both Odin and Satan were one-eyed. Clearly, it was the price they paid for wearing the Crown of Destiny. If even they couldn't restore their lost eyes, how could he possibly manage it?

As for that Maria he'd never truly met, Merlin didn't need to guess to know she likely had only one eye remaining as well.

Merlin got up on his own and continued toward the deepest part. This made Teresa behind him anxious, and she quickly hurried after him.

"It's not that my skills are lacking! Something must be wrong!"

"Never mind. Even if you can't heal my eye, it doesn't matter much. I'll just get used to it slowly. Let's find what we need and leave this awful place as soon as possible."

"We've searched for so long and found nothing. Now I'm starting to suspect the intelligence was wrong. Maybe I was deceived. I really wish we could find it quickly. Otherwise, that detestable black dragon will surely put even more pressure on my sister."

"That black dragon is nothing. Actually, I can—"

Merlin hadn't finished his sentence when he suddenly felt the ground give way beneath his feet.

The two let out a startled cry and fell into the endless darkness.

title: Chapter 26 — Rude
content:
Chapter 26 — Rude

Volume 39 · Chapter 26

Two people fell from a height at the same time, for some reason one foot slipped? Merlin crashed heavily to the ground, and before he could ascertain the situation, he heard Teresa's startled cry from nearby as they continued to fall deeper into darkness.
Seeing Merlin had no time to think, he leapt into the deeper darkness, drew the long knife at his waist and stabbed it into the wall beside him, then seized Teresa's hand. They clung to the black wall like ornaments hung on it—.
After they temporarily steadied, Merlin and Teresa each let out a slight sigh; it seemed this place wasn't as dangerous as they had imagined. "Where are we?" Merlin gazed at the black surroundings, feeling uneasy, this unease stemming from his ignorance of the Age of Gods. "Could it be... could it all be true?" Teresa's expression was doubtful, she gripped Merlin's hand tightly and muttered, "It must be right, this is exactly the place! My intel was spot on!" "What are you talking about?" Merlin asked, bewildered.
This is the place we've been looking for! The underground palace deep in the forest! It seems we've found the entrance by sheer chance! Teresa exclaimed delightedly, meaning the danger of the black dragon could now be approached.
"What's here?" Merlin scanned the pitch-black surroundings, seeing nothing at all. "A spell, you'll find out soon." Teresa urged, "Let's go up and search this underground palace thoroughly."
Merlin prepared to pull Teresa up, but suddenly realized the situation wouldn't allow it—he saw countless scarlet eyes glowing in the darkness below, like dense tiny red bulbs! Obviously many dangerous creatures lived here; Merlin and Teresa's sudden intrusion had awakened them, which was hardly a good thing. Normally dealing with these monsters wouldn't be hard; Merlin could just transform into his demon form and fly Teresa away, but he didn't want to expose his demon identity.
"Hold onto me." "Ah? ? ?" Teresa's face flushed; she thought Merlin was being oddly abrupt, wondering if this man was too forward. As a goddess, she really didn't feel like embracing a man she'd barely spoken to, finding it hard to accept mentally. "Don't waste time! Quick!" Merlin didn't bother explaining, gave Teresa no time to think, and forcefully hauled her up, holding her tight and taking a deep breath.
Actually, if it were just Merlin himself, he wouldn't have to worry about any danger, but bringing Teresa, this weak goddess, changed things—he had to consider her safety. "Wait... wait a moment! Don't touch me, I—I" Teresa's face turned as red as a ripe apple, waves of masculine scent assailed her, making her heart race and her mind go blank. Among human tribes, she was a lofty goddess; who would dare act as boldly as Merlin? Teresa was like a naïve girl who'd never seen cruelty, completely flustered by Merlin's old‑handed ways, utterly no match for him. Merlin never imagined Teresa's mind would be filled with so many thoughts; his only focus was getting Teresa out of danger and then finding what they wanted in the underground palace.
Merlin's gaze hardened, he held Teresa close, pulled the demon sword Banri Garan from the wall, and the two appeared to be plunging into despair. Teresa stopped resisting, because she had already seen the countless hungry beasts' eyes below, greedily fixed on them; Merlin's rude move was unavoidable. As they were about to be thrown into the wolves' den, the hungry monsters below let out excited roars, Teresa's heart pounded with panic— "Hey! We we are going to be—" "Silence." Merlin stayed calm, silenced the panicking Teresa, and just before contact with the monsters, the repulsive space was triggered! The immense repulsion used the gathered monsters below as a springboard, creating a reaction force that launched the pair into the air, narrowly escaping disaster! The two plump ducks that had been about to be eaten flew away, causing the monsters below to erupt in fury, howling upward and scrambling up the rock wall in pursuit.
They landed on a stable platform—. Teresa was temporarily released, she kept patting her flat chest, still a little shaken from what had just happened. "Close call... a little bit" "Run now, this isn't the time to rest!" "What?!".
Merlin spotted a strange door on the platform, its center swirling with a vortex, looking like a portal. There was no time to think; Merlin grabbed Teresa's hand and kept running toward the portal, trying to shake off the countless monsters behind them. Of course Merlin could slaughter the monsters with his sword-drawing technique, but the surroundings were pitch‑black, he couldn't gauge how many monsters lurked there. If he couldn't kill them quickly, and their numbers were huge, they'd keep coming in waves to stall him—what then? And he still had to protect Teresa; in the heat of battle he'd inevitably be distracted, possibly failing to watch over her. So escaping the monsters' pursuit became the top priority, rather than turning back to clash head‑on with the horde.
The two sprinted toward the nearby portal, the brutal monster horde hot on their heels—. At this moment, what was the unreliable goddess of luck thinking? Teresa's hand was clenched tightly in Merlin's grip; she felt no nervousness about danger, instead she couldn't help but let her mind wander—. "What is this feeling?" "Why is my heart beating so fast?" "I've never felt this way from anyone other than my sister—". Teresa sensed an inexplicable sense of security, as if as long as this man stood beside her, nothing could harm her.
When Teresa came to her senses, she saw Merlin pulling her toward the portal, about to enter, which shocked her. "No! Don't just go in! That gate... isn't right, we might not be sent to the underground palace—" Before she could finish, Merlin yanked her toward the portal; the monsters behind let out angry, exhausted howls, clearly unable to just let them enter. In the pitch‑black darkness where not a finger could be seen, they couldn't tell where in the underground palace they were, nor which level this was.
Teresa slowly crawled up from the ground and complained, "Don't just rush into that portal; it will surely send us somewhere—" "Now we might not even find our way back." "Why bother with that? You're still alive—shouldn't you be thanking me?" Merlin got up and brushed the dust off his clothes. Teresa was at a loss for words; recalling the moment her heart had raced, her face flushed as she muttered—. "You really are—" "A very rude man." o(^~ )o

title: Chapter 27 — Still a Coincidence......
content:
Chapter 27 — Still a Coincidence......

Volume 39 · Chapter 27

"You still dare to call me rude? If I had been just a bit slower just now, you wouldn't even have had the chance to complain." Merlin retorted bluntly, scanning the surroundings, unable to tell where the portal had just taken them. "Where... are we?" "I already told you not to just wander into that portal; who knows where that door would actually send us?" Theresa said, huffing. A look of resentment slowly crept over her face. "When did I ever say that?" Merlin frowned. "Theresa was at a loss for words, thinking she had just spaced out; otherwise she would have surely found the correct route." "So, we're still in the underground palace, we just don't know which level we're on?" Merlin asked tentatively. "Exactly, the layout of the underground palace is extremely complex; one misstep and you can't find your way back. We might already be trapped in here." Theresa said with a sullen expression, thinking that even if they managed to reach the lowest level and complete their goal, getting out would be just as hard. "If we had stayed calm a moment earlier and found the correct door to the next level, we might not have ended up in this awful situation." "The underground palace consists of several layers, each deeply mysterious, easily trapping anyone who enters forever." "The portal seemed like a way out of the immediate danger, but it's also a trap that drives intruders deeper into the perilous depths of the underground palace." Theresa sighed, realizing it was too late to say anything; better to carefully examine their surroundings and find a way to break the current situation. As Theresa's hand glowed with light, continuously shooting upward, it illuminated the unknown underground palace as bright as day, and both of them saw a strange sight— Seven massive stone stelae stood before them, appearing quite mysterious, their surfaces covered in a thick layer of dust, making any blurred inscriptions unreadable. "No way... this is it!" Theresa pointed excitedly at the distant seven massive stone stelae, her face flushed with excitement, her whole body trembling with joy. Merlin was utterly bewildered and couldn't help but ask, "What do you mean?" "This is it! The lowest level of the underground palace! The portal brought us straight here!" Theresa paused, clasped her hands together, and said excitedly, "What's recorded on these stelae is exactly what I've been looking for—we've achieved our goal directly!" Merlin's gaze fell on the seven massive stone stelae, wondering what secret they held that would make Theresa care so much—could it be used against the ancient god black dragon? Surely it must be a priceless treasure. "How wonderful, I never imagined our luck would be this good—even the portal ended up helping us!" Theresa's earlier dissatisfaction vanished; she thought Merlin's rash decision to enter the portal wasn't such a bad thing after all. "I think you have a misunderstanding—it's not us—" Merlin's expression was complex, a bead of cold sweat sliding down his forehead. He felt Theresa was terrifying, far beyond his comprehension—venturing alone into a forest brimming with danger and yet hardly encountering any peril? Just after saying they wanted to find the underground palace, they immediately discovered the hidden entrance deep within? And then the portal's door seemed to have rebelled against the underground palace, bringing her to the lowest level where the stone stelae were placed? Are all these just pure luck? But this guy seems completely unaware of his own abilities. Merlin couldn't believe that good fortune could trigger so frequently; perhaps he thought wishes coming true were just that simple, like a cheat within a cheat. "Don't talk, I need to quickly record the contents of these stone tablets and bring them back to deal with that hateful black dragon." Theresa interrupted Merlin's thoughts, beginning to gather wind magic, intending to blow away all the dust on the stelae. "We have plenty of time; is there really a need to rush?" Merlin said calmly, sitting on a stone, planning to wait until Theresa finished before figuring out how to leave this creepy place. "This is the lowest level of the underground palace, also the most dangerous place. I saw in my sister's diary that a dangerous giant lives here." Theresa paused, then continued, "Its temper is extremely violent; it survives by hunting magical beasts in the forest, and no one wants to provoke it, so we'd better finish up and leave quickly." "Really?" Merlin nodded, aided by the light continually rising from Theresa's hand, the situation of the lowest level of the underground palace gradually became clearer. He slightly furrowed his brow, seeing traces of a giant's life here—tables, chairs, and other household furnishings all present. The seven massive stone stelae were actually just a few pillars supporting a bed! Merlin and Alice, in this dreadful environment, were like two tiny mice, not even as tall as the cup the giant uses to drink water. Not far away, Merlin also saw a stove where scalding hot water was being boiled, and on the chopping board lay the ingredients ready for steaming and cooking. Even a huge kitchen knife as big as a small mountain had been sharpened and was stuck upside‑down on the board, waiting for prey to arrive so it

title: Chapter 28 — Chaos Giant
content:
Chapter 28 — Chaos Giant

Volume 39 · Chapter 28

Merlin had harbored some suspicions before, but this feeling was growing stronger.

Especially seeing the blood pool seal recorded on the stone tablet only confirmed his conjecture!

Merlin simply couldn't believe so many coincidences would happen to him, so there was probably only one answer—

That he was the great prophet of the demon race!

Traveling to the past timeline, ending the era of the gods, setting the wheel of history in motion!

Now, Merlin existing in the Age of the Gods could accomplish all these things, and the historical mysteries were gradually unraveling.

The prophet whose ears had grown calloused from hearing was nothing but a piece of history where Merlin had appeared in the past!

Merlin's expression grew grave, and suddenly he felt his shoulders become abnormally heavy, a immense sense of mission pressing down on him.

If all this was true, then Merlin could no longer follow his original plan of trying not to affect this timeline—he had to get involved.

The answer was already obvious: Merlin needed to participate in the great transformation of the Age of the Gods, pushing the nearly stalled wheel of history once more!

In other words, Merlin had to redo what the demon prophet had done in the Age of the Gods, ensuring the future world history wouldn't undergo major changes!

This task was extremely difficult, because Merlin didn't know at all what the demon prophet had actually done? He only knew some general major events.

How terrifying was the butterfly effect? Merlin knew this well—perhaps in the short term nothing would show, but looking far ahead, small things from the past could cause major changes in the future!

Merlin wasn't sure if he could perfectly replicate what the demon prophet had done? He could only follow his own instincts.

After all, the former prophet, who was Merlin from another timeline, was still himself in a sense.

Without major upheavals, any Merlin would make roughly the same choices.

However, Merlin still felt immense pressure—if by some chance he chose wrong, this timeline might head straight for destruction, completely deviating from the correct fate track.

"So that's how it is, looks like setting up the seal isn't that hard~" Teresa had memorized the method for constructing the blood pool seal in her mind, turned around and said, "Alright, let's go."

Merlin stood there like a soul-less puppet, not hearing Teresa's call beside him, his thoughts extremely chaotic, his mind full of how to make history proceed in the right direction?

"Hey! What's wrong? Can you hear me?" Teresa waved her hand in front of Merlin.

Merlin snapped back to reality and said awkwardly, "Done? Let's go."

"Hmm?" Teresa found Merlin's reaction a bit odd, but didn't think much of it, chasing after him, "Do you have something on your mind? Your face looks terrible."

Merlin's brows furrowed, he didn't answer Teresa's question, silently making a decision in his heart—

Thinking so much now was useless, he had to follow his instincts.

As long as I myself have no problems, the choices made by intuition are mostly correct.

No matter which timeline's Merlin he was, he was himself, and absolutely couldn't be affected.

The two decided to leave the giant's kitchen first, get away from the last floor of the dungeon, and figure out a way to escape.

But just as they reached the kitchen door, they suddenly heard sounds coming from outside—this was not a good sign.

"Back already?" Teresa's face was full of terror, looking at Merlin beside her.

"Hide first." Merlin pulled Teresa and hid under a dark cabinet.

Since the giants were already huge, the furniture they used was equally massive, making Merlin and Teresa look like rats scurrying around.

With a "crack" sound, the kitchen door opened and a giant covered in green fur walked in carrying prey.

The giant was over twenty meters tall, strongly built, with distinct abdominal muscles, sharp teeth protruding from his mouth, looking especially ferocious!

After entering the kitchen, the giant casually lit the oil lamp, the roaring flames making the pitch-black kitchen bright.

Through the gap at the bottom of the cabinet, Teresa saw the green cap on the giant's foot, immediately covering her mouth in shock, "Uh!?"

"What's wrong?" Merlin asked in confusion.

"A Chaos Giant." Teresa answered in terror.

"Chaos Giant?" Merlin frowned, unable to figure out the difference between these giants and the giants from his era?

"We are currently living on the corpse of a Chaos Giant—they are the earliest creatures in the world, with a history far more ancient than the ancient gods." Teresa paused and whispered, "When the world was still in chaos, life was scarce, only these Chaos Giants existed. A powerful giant named Ymir sacrificed himself, forming the earth and rivers, and giving birth to ancient gods and other creatures. In other words, we all have giant blood flowing in us, just in varying degrees."

Merlin looked at the huge footprints moving outside and muttered in confusion, "Impossible? That giant lying outside is probably the size of an island, how could it become land and mountains?"

"Chaos Giants come in different sizes. Legend has it that when the giant named Ymir stood up, the clouds in the sky barely reached his feet." Teresa emphasized seriously.

"? ? ?" Merlin's imagination was limited, but he could barely comprehend Ymir's enormity.

"I didn't expect a Chaos Giant is still alive? I thought they were all dead long ago. Looks like it's still a juvenile—adult Chaos Giants are much bigger than this." Teresa frowned with worry, "We're doomed, we might be trapped here. Even a juvenile Chaos Giant is stronger than ordinary ancient gods, my sister couldn't defeat one either."

"So troublesome?" Merlin's expression was grave, thinking there was no escape, he probably had to go out and kill this juvenile Chaos Giant to safely leave the dungeon.

Just as Merlin hesitated whether to act now, the Chaos Giant outside dropped its prey from its shoulders, intending to check if the water was boiled?

This action scared the two hiding under the cabinet half to death—a half-open panicked gorilla face appeared in their field of view, looking utterly hopeless.

"It wants to eat gorilla? Does gorilla taste good?" Teresa asked with a weird expression.

Merlin stared in shock, exclaiming in surprise, "...Kongou?"

"What? You know this magical beast?" Teresa completely believed Merlin, indeed living in the forest had made him lonely enough to befriend magical beasts?

Merlin wanted to speak but stopped, thinking: So this is how Kongou met the prophet? Now everything made sense.

Kongou also noticed the two "little mice" under the cabinet and couldn't help but let out low growls toward the cabinet.

This attracted the Chaos Giant's attention, so it came over and slowly climbed down, its huge eyeballs rolling around, checking the bottom of the cabinet.

Before the Chaos Giant could investigate, its two active eyeballs were slashed, and black blood surged out like a waterfall!

"Roar!!!"

The Chaos Giant covered its bleeding eyes, stumbled backward, and let out a beast-like howl of pain.

Merlin took a deep breath, decided to take care of this Chaos Giant first, and turned to tell Teresa—

"Wait for me, don't come out easily."

title: Chapter 29 — Surtr
content:
Chapter 29 — Surtr

Volume 39 · Chapter 29

“Hold on!”

Theresa hurriedly grabbed Merlin's arm, her face written with heavy worry, deeply concerned for his safety.

After all, as the first beings of the world, chaos giants' strength was actually beyond that of ordinary ancient gods.

Perhaps Merlin could easily handle himself, but that didn't mean he could oppose a chaos giant, even an unripe one.

Theresa's expression was conflicted, gripping Merlin's sleeve and refusing to let go—in her eyes, going out now was tantamount to seeking death.

“What else is there?” Merlin stopped in confusion.

“You'll die! That's a chaos giant, don't start getting arrogant just because you could handle me, I—” Theresa's expression was awkward, and she spoke in a low voice, “I’m already quite weak among ancient gods.”

“???”

Merlin's eyelids twitched uncontrollably. *You're weak? You're almost achieving everything you wish for and you call yourself weak?! Shouldn't the other ancient gods just give up living then?!*

Merlin sighed, shook Theresa's hand off, and made no attempt to accept her good intentions. Ancient god? As if he hadn't killed any before!

“Don’t worry, nothing will happen.”

Theresa wanted to say something more, but the words died on her tongue, and she could only watch helplessly as Merlin climbed out from the bottom of the cabinet, her heart pounding—

*Why am I even worrying about a guy I barely know? This is so strange…*

Outside, the chaos giant, blinded by its injured eyes, could see nothing at all. Its hands covered its blind eyes, but blood seeped through the gaps between its fingers.

The powerful giant fell into incomparable rage, clearly never expecting that one day it would have its eyes bitten by a mouse.

It began furiously smashing and overturning furniture, grabbing anything it could find and hurling it ruthlessly toward the cabinet.

When the chaos giant finally found the sharpened kitchen cleaver, its entire demeanor changed—it grew quiet, its ears twitching, listening intently to sounds in the kitchen.

“Despicable rat, daring to sneak into my kitchen. I won't let you escape—I'll throw you both into the hot oil as seasoning!”

The chaos giant roared in fury, having no intention of letting the two “rats” leave. Instead, it resolved to exterminate these bold intruders completely.

Due to its blindness, the chaos giant was at a disadvantage, able to only judge its enemies by sound. But Merlin had already seized every opportunity, creeping up behind it unnoticed!

The chaos giant's ears twitched, sensing something small approaching. Without hesitation, it snatched the cleaver from the cutting board and swung it with all its might toward the source!

Merlin was just about to draw his sword when he suddenly saw the enormous cleaver coming straight down, making his heart skip a beat. He had no choice but to dodge quickly.

Merlin performed a double jump in midair, lightly tapping the cleaver with his foot, then retreated cautiously.

The razor-sharp blade sliced into the wall with a thunderous, earth-shaking boom—the power was astonishing!

Merlin kept his eyes on the chaos giant, which had gone still again, listening intently to its surroundings. After the kitchen fell quiet, it stood motionless once more, trying to pinpoint the enemy's exact location.

“Where are you hiding again, little rat? You're the first one to dare wound my eyes.”

Merlin didn't dare make any rash moves. The opponent's state was extremely alert; rushing in blindly might result in the same fate as before—being chopped to death by that massive cleaver.

He glanced around and suddenly hatched a plan. He applied his gravity space ability to a water cup not far away, pulling it off the table.

*Crash!* The cup shattered on the ground. The chaos giant immediately reacted like a bristling lion, its entire green body tense with fury as it spun around and slashed wildly at the table behind it!

“Found you!?”

The thick solid wood table was split in two by the giant's cleaver in that single stroke, as fragile as tofu.

“Perfect timing!”

Seizing the moment the chaos giant turned, Merlin leaped into the air, landing directly behind it, and swiftly drew his sword, slashing at the giant's neck.

Terrifying killing intent erupted. The sharp blade of the demon sword Banri Garan sliced through the giant's flesh, but was caught by the hard bones at the spine!

Merlin's heart skipped a beat. He was beginning to believe Theresa's words—no wonder it was a giant that had evolved to create the earth and mountains; its bones were extraordinarily hard!

Blood sprayed everywhere. The chaos giant wailed in agony, dropping the cleaver from its hands and frantically grasping behind it.

Merlin's gaze hardened. His arm turned pitch black as he entered a partial demon god transformation. Banri Garan also shifted to black, spewing demon fire with temperatures rivaling the sun!

Surging superheated flames spewed incessantly, like a fierce rocket booster, driving Banri Garan's blade ever deeper into the giant's neck, reducing the hard bones to precarious splinters!

Merlin's right hand, still gripping the sword, exerted force once more, and with a single stroke, successfully decapitated the chaos giant!

The enormous head spun through the air, bouncing across the kitchen floor like a ball of fur. The mountain-like strong body trembled slightly, then crashed to the ground with a thunderous thud.

Merlin released the partial demon god transformation, and Banri Garan reverted to its normal appearance. He breathed a sigh of relief and looked at the giant's severed head.

“What scorching heat… similar to the sun’s temperature…”

“You fire demon, Surtur…”

“So it has finally arrived, hasn't it?”

“The prophecy of the gods has begun…”

The decapitated chaos giant murmured intermittently, seemingly having realized Merlin's identity.

*Surtur? Is that the Prophet's name?*

Confusion stirred in Merlin's heart. After all, “Prophet” didn't seem like a name—it was more of a codename, a title of respect demons used for him.

Just as Merlin was about to press further, he discovered the chaos giant had already lost its will to live.

Perhaps this unripe giant was the last remaining bloodline of the chaos giants. Unfortunately, it had now been killed by Merlin.

“Surtur… I suppose I should use the Prophet's name in this era, right?”

Merlin pondered and decided it was best not to use his real name. If he was playing the role of the Prophet in this era, then he should use the Prophet's name.

However, Merlin didn't know what the name “Surtur” truly represented. It felt like there was a deeper meaning hidden within it.

Below in the cabinet, Theresa was still worrying about Merlin. Every now and then, tremendous noises from outside made her feel increasingly uneasy.

That was a chaos giant—the oldest lifeform in the world. Even an unripe one wasn't easy to deal with.

*Is this guy who's always been cooped up in a manor really okay?*

*If he can't handle a chaos giant, then I definitely can't.*

*Could we end up being thrown into the same pot, used as seasoning?*

Theresa was panicking inside, torn about whether to go out and check. But just then, Merlin's voice reached her.

“Come out, it's safe now.”

“Hm!?”

Theresa emerged from the bottom of the cabinet with extreme trepidation, only to find Merlin stroking the massive black gorilla's fur, looking like he was meeting an old friend.

She noticed the headless corpse of the chaos giant beside them. The cut surface looked scorched by fire, completely blackened, and a faint aroma of roasted meat lingered in the air.

“You succeeded? You really defeated a chaos giant!?”

“I told you it’d be fine. This guy’s just a bit big, that’s all.”

“Just a bit big!?!”

Theresa was completely thunderstruck by Merlin’s casual remark. She wasn’t a three-year-old child—she knew very well the power of a chaos giant.

Their hard bodies made them nearly indestructible. The fact that Merlin was able to decapitate one only proved that his destructive power was overwhelmingly powerful!

Theresa suddenly frowned tightly, crossing her arms, and stared at Merlin who was communicating with the black gorilla.

*Why did I even come to this dungeon?*

*Wouldn’t it have been better to just bring this guy back?*

*There was no need to go through all this trouble searching for the sealing technique here…*

title: Chapter 30 — Wild Man
content:
Chapter 30 — Wild Man

Volume 39 · Chapter 30

Merlin stroked the gorilla's sleek black fur, suddenly understanding what it had meant back then.

The meaning of shaking its head while nodding was that it wasn't entirely a prophet—at least not back then.

Because it lacked divine grace and hadn't experienced the destruction of the Age of Gods, it was very different from that "prophet."

That's why back then Kongang would give an ambiguous answer, leaving Merlin completely baffled.

But now Merlin understood—as long as he completed the mission of destroying the gods and pushing history forward, he would become a true prophet.

"Roar."

Kongang was overjoyed, pounding its chest with its fists, grateful that Merlin had rescued it from the giant's clutches.

This era's Kongang didn't know Merlin yet, nor did it understand why this human-looking guy was calling it Kongang.

But Kongang obviously didn't dislike the title; instead, it found it majestic and mighty, so it gladly accepted the name with a smile.

"I never expected that you, who will someday dominate the Gorge Forest, would become someone else's platter food in the Age of Gods? How interesting~"

Merlin said in a teasing tone. Kongang was probably a pseudo-god-tier magical beast now, but it would be stronger in the future.

After all, having trained through multiple eras and learned to temper its body with magma, future Kongang would surely be stronger.

But even a pseudo-god-tier Kongang wouldn't be bullied easily in the forest—unless it encountered an ancient being like the Chaos Giant, in which case it might stumble.

Kongang felt Merlin was mocking it and gnashed its teeth in anger. Turning its back, it swayed its rear toward him to express its displeasure.

Merlin smiled, not caring much. After all, this era's Kongang wouldn't refuse his olive branch—

"Want to come with me?"

Kongang recalled how it had almost been stewed and eaten by the giant, still feeling lingering fear. There were other terrifying magical beasts in the forest it couldn't defeat either.

The strength Merlin had just displayed impressed Kongang deeply. Following the strong one—maybe there'd be meat to eat?

Strength-worship was the nature of many creatures, even magical beasts with some intelligence weren't exceptions.

So Kongang nodded without hesitation, wanting to follow Merlin out of this forest full of natural enemies and see the outside world.

"Good. From now on you'll be called Kongang. Remember, obey me, understood?"

Kongang scratched its head. Its current intelligence couldn't compare to the future, but it could barely understand Merlin's meaning, nodding vigorously.

Teresa couldn't help but approach, examining the giant ape magical beast, and asked curiously.

"A magical beast with intelligence—really rare. Did you tame it?"

"What do you mean, tame? It's my friend.

"Friend?" Teresa's expression turned strange, as if hearing something unbelievable. "Someone actually befriended a magical beast?

You're such a wild man."

"We'll take it with us and leave," Merlin said nonchalantly.

"Take it back?" Teresa paused, looking up at the giant ape magical beast. "Taking it back isn't impossible, but it's too bulky and inconvenient. Still, we should figure out how to leave the dungeon first."

"This isn't complicated," Merlin asked, turning around. "Kongang, how did you get in? Do you remember the way?"

Kongang nodded repeatedly, pounding its chest confidently.

Outside the forest, a large group of people had gathered—looking at their attire, they seemed to be human soldiers.

The leader wore black robes, his complexion gloomy, especially his prominent eagle-beak nose, which added to the air of a conspirator.

He was Satan, who in this era hadn't yet become the death god who created and ruled hell, but was the deputy officer beside the human leader Maria.

Satan wasn't an ancient god but an ordinary human created by someone, his strength not particularly powerful—barely reaching the semi-god tier.

He was fairly intelligent, often advising Maria and helping humanity avoid several crises, so he was given important roles.

But Teresa thought Satan was always full of schemes, and his plans were very underhanded—she didn't really like the guy.

However, Satan didn't know what he was thinking? From long ago he had pursued Teresa fiercely, trying to gain the favor of the Goddess of Luck.

Maybe Satan truly liked Teresa? Or was it to raise his status among humans by marrying an ancient god?

Although Maria knew about Satan's fierce pursuit of Teresa, she basically turned a blind eye.

As long as it didn't get too out of hand.

In Maria's eyes, Satan was ambitious and unscrupulous, but still somewhat useful.

Not long ago, Satan heard that Teresa had gone to the forest to seek a sealing technique, and was instantly terrified!

The forest was very ancient. Rumors said

title: Chapter 31 — Guard
content:
Chapter 31 — Guard

Volume 39 · Chapter 31

Jin Gang swiftly leaped through the forest, soon arriving at the outskirts where Satan and a group of soldiers had gathered.

"Hmm? What is he doing here?" Teresa frowned, noticing Satan's displeasure.

"Do you know those people?" Merlin inquired.

"I do," Teresa nodded.

Thus, Merlin had Jin Gang approach the soldiers. Even without Teresa's explanation, he could roughly guess the situation. It was likely that Teresa had entered the forest on her own, and these people had come searching for her.

Jin Gang landed with a thunderous crash, his massive body creating a deep crater in the earth. He bared his teeth at the human soldiers, his eyes filled with hostility.

Occasionally, human hunters would enter the forest to hunt, targeting the weaker magical beasts on the outskirts. Although Jin Gang lived deep in the forest, he had encountered those ruthless human hunters before.

The human soldiers gripped their weapons tightly, their faces filled with fear as they huddled together, not daring to provoke Jin Gang, the enormous monster.

Merlin set Teresa down, and Satan quickly suppressed the hostility in his eyes, adopting a composed demeanor with a smile plastered on his face.

"What are you doing here?" Teresa questioned, her brow furrowed.

"I came for you, of course. Don't you know how dangerous it is to enter this forest alone? You should be aware of the risks," Satan said seriously.

"I can go wherever I want, and it's none of your business," Teresa said discontentedly, her hands on her hips.

"You're right, you're free to go wherever you please, but have you considered the consequences? You're the Goddess of Fortune. If something were to happen to you, it would be a severe blow to humanity," Satan said with deep concern.

"I'm not a child; I know all this. Besides, the forest doesn't seem that dangerous. Look, I'm fine," Teresa said, spreading her hands.

"That's because it's you. If someone else had entered, who knows what might have happened?" Satan paused, then brought out Maria. "Lady Maria is currently telling stories to Odin. When she returns and finds you missing, you'll certainly be scolded."

Teresa's expression turned awkward as she thought of her sister Maria, and her anger dissipated.

"Moreover, I've been worried sick about your safety. Knowing you came here alone, I couldn't sleep for several nights and rushed here with my men," Satan said softly, his face filled with deep affection. "You know, aside from your sister, I'm the one who cares about you the most. My feelings—"

"Don't spout such cheesy nonsense; it's disgusting. Isn't this just part of your duty?" Teresa interrupted before Satan could finish.

"It is my duty, but with Lady Maria absent, I must manage all matters, big and small," Satan said coldly, glancing at Merlin behind her. "It's dangerous to wander off like this. Who knows what kind of trouble you might encounter?"

"I entered the forest to deal with that black dragon," Teresa emphasized stubbornly.

"Regarding Nidhogg, Lady Maria will handle it personally. Perhaps they can negotiate," Satan said lightly.

"Negotiate? Every time it's negotiate, and we end up offering our scarce resources to it. When will we ever be able to stand up for ourselves?" Teresa said angrily, having endured this stagnant situation for far too long.

"At least this way, humanity can continue to thrive, can't they?"

"I won't have to endure the black dragon's oppression anymore. In the forest, I not only found a sealing technique to counter the ancient gods but also discovered a powerful ally!" Teresa said proudly, standing beside Merlin as she introduced him to Satan.

"This guy I found in the forest is incredibly strong. He can take down a Chaos Giant with ease, so dealing with an ancient god shouldn't be a problem. Oh, and I still don't know your name?"

"I'm..." Merlin hesitated, thinking for a moment before responding, "I'm called Surtur. If it's too troublesome, you can just call me the Prophet."

"The Prophet?" Teresa looked puzzled, curiosity in her voice. "What a strange nickname. Can you really predict the future?"

Merlin smiled but didn't answer. Although he didn't possess that ability, as someone who had traveled from the future, making some predictions wasn't difficult.

"Surtur?" Satan narrowed his eyes. What kind of name was that? Where did this man come from?

"He's Satan, my sister's vice officer," Teresa introduced to Merlin.

Merlin's expression changed slightly, his gaze fixed intently on Satan as his hand instinctively moved toward the knife at his waist.

However, after observing for a while, Merlin's emotions gradually calmed, and he didn't act rashly.

In the future, Satan was an essential part of the world.

If he were to eliminate Satan now, this timeline might not have a future with hell. Who knew what other unforeseen events might occur? This wasn't a scenario Merlin wanted to see.

Satan, in this era, posed no threat to Merlin, who couldn't help but wonder how this man would become an ancient god in the future.

Sensing the hostility from Merlin, Satan spoke sarcastically, "This gentleman doesn't seem very friendly, does he?"

"Is that so?" Teresa looked at Merlin, wondering if Satan had misread the situation.

"You're right. I've never had a good impression of people full of schemes," Merlin replied bluntly, expressing his disdain.

"Alright, alright," Teresa finally sensed the tense atmosphere. "Let's discuss this back at the village."

"No," Satan said coldly.

"What now?" Teresa asked impatiently.

"This man's background is unclear. How can we bring him back without caution? What if he's harboring malicious intentions? It could put our tribe in danger!" Satan argued logically.

"That's not true! In the forest, he protected me. He's definitely not a bad person; you must have misunderstood," Teresa defended Merlin.

"Evil people don't wear their nature on their faces. His willingness to protect you might be driven by ulterior motives! Lady Teresa, you're too naive. It's easy to be deceived. This man must be trying to use you to infiltrate our tribe," Satan said, feigning sincerity.

"What ulterior motives? I think you're just being overly cautious!" Teresa's expression turned stern, her voice commanding. "He will serve as my guardian for now. When my sister returns, I'll explain everything to her. This is settled. Know your place, Satan!"

A faint, triumphant smile appeared on Merlin's face as he raised an eyebrow at Satan, everything unfolding as he had expected.

Satan's face turned red with suppressed anger, his fists clenched as he glared at Merlin furiously.

"Just you wait! Let's see how long you can prance around in front of me!

title: Chapter 32 — Trial
content:
Chapter 32 — Trial

Volume 39 · Chapter 32

At the top of the World Tree, where the most exalted ancient gods reside, lay the realm of the chief deity.

Within the exquisite garden palace, King of Gods Odin sat upon a throne forged from the stone of封神, his upper body bare.

His stature was far larger than any human, resembling a mighty giant, with bizarre law runes etched into his flesh.

An authority surpassing all living beings radiated from him, shaking every ancient god present.

This was the temperament of a prime deity—vastly superior to the other ancient gods. Wearing the Crown of Fate, he no longer counted among mortals, but had become a participant in the construction of the world.

Melodious harp music drifted through the air. The tiny human goddess knelt in the center of the hall, looked down upon by Odin and numerous higher-ranking ancient gods, possessing no dignity whatsoever.

To the gods of Asgard, the human goddess meant nothing—more like a toy to pass the time.

Maria lightly stroked the harp in her hands, singing a story she had fabricated. In a sense, she was the progenitor of future bardic poets—

"A brutal lord takes a new wife in his territory every day. By the time the next morning rises, every one of these newlywed wives has had her throat cut."

"Who knows what the lord is thinking? Perhaps boredom, or perhaps killing his wives brings him unparalleled pleasure."

"The people of the territory live in constant terror, forced to hide their daughters, yet it avails nothing. The lord's soldiers drag the girls from their cellars one by one."

"More and more victims fall. People lose hope for the future, until one person stands up."

"Her name is Daphne—a very intelligent girl with a strong sense of justice, swearing to restore peace to the people."

"She chooses to marry the brutal lord, and every night before sleep, she tells him a story. The lord becomes deeply fascinated, forcing him to delay killing her."

"Thus, the girl named Daphne successfully survives over a thousand days and nights, and the people finally taste the long-lost peaceful life."

"Yet crisis arrives silently. As inspiration wanes, the stories Daphne tells grow increasingly unable to stabilize the brutal lord."

"Then, what will become of her?"

Maria pressed down the trembling strings, interrupting the music echoing through the temple, leaving Odin and the ancient gods with endless room for imagination.

The surrounding ancient gods exchanged glances, clearly intrigued by Maria's story, though regrettably there was no continuation.

Obviously, this "Daphne" was Maria herself, and the story merely mirrored her current predicament.

In truth, Maria had reached an impasse. Odin demanded the soul of a strong human—not anyone else, but herself!

Although Maria was also an ancient god, her status was too lowly, possessing no power, and naturally became a target for Odin.

Besides Maria, humanity could find no other powerful beings; only her soul held value, qualifying her for entry into Valhalla.

To save herself, Maria tried to move Odin with her story, delaying the moment her soul would be taken, adapting her life experiences into inspiration for the tale.

But this method would eventually run dry. Maria using her current predicament as inspiration proved her story had reached its end.

"An interesting story. Congratulations, Maria. You've moved me once again. It seems I'll have to wait a while before you enter Valhalla. I'm increasingly fond of you."

The majestic voice of King of Gods Odin drifted down from the throne. Maria once again escaped the clutches of death, gaining another chance to live.

But could Maria escape next time? Her inspiration was exhausted. She could flee for the moment, but not forever.

"Thank you for your praise." Maria replied with a grim expression.

"But next time, you absolutely won't escape. I can tell—the Daphne in the story is you, isn't she? And I am that brutal lord." Odin's tone carried a hint of annoyance, feeling insulted by a lowly third-rate ancient god.

"You're joking. How could that be?" Maria denied, refusing to admit the satire in the story.

"Whether or not it is, I can feel your inspiration has dried up. That girl named Daphne will share your fate." Odin looked down at the tiny Maria, speaking slowly, "When her story ends, your life will follow to its conclusion."

Maria lowered her head, offering no response. She knew this in her heart!

"Can you tell me how Daphne in the story finally resolved this crisis?" Odin asked with double meaning, actually asking if Maria could escape next time.

"That's a story for next time." Maria answered, having made up her mind—if she couldn't escape next time, then Theresa would inherit the mantle and become humanity's leader.

"Very well, I won't force you. Go back." Odin temporarily let Maria go, saying meaningfully, "I look forward to your next visit. How will the girl named Daphne resist the brutal lord?"

Maria's expression darkened. She hugged the harp in her arms and withdrew humbly.

She finally let out a breath of relief. With her back turned to the gods, she no longer concealed—

Her eyes revealed thick "hatred," burning like flames.

"When I met the Fates, they told me the gods of Asgard would face destruction in the future—I included."

Odin spoke loudly to his loyal subordinates beside him, his single eye flashing with the light of law—

"At first I felt fear, so I built Valhalla, collecting the souls of countless powerful beings across the world."

"Planning to create the most terrifying monsters to face future dangers, ensuring our position would not waver."

"But now, I gradually realize this is mere scaremongering. How could we, the powerful, be destroyed?"

"We have ruled this world for countless eons. Have we been destroyed? Who could possibly shake us?"

"No one!"

"You are the finest gods of this world, and I am the mightiest, invincible King of Gods!"

"Even if the Twilight of the Gods is real, I will defeat that destined destruction!"

"We are supreme, and eternal!"

"Supreme and eternal, the gods?"

Merlin gazed out the carriage window, ignoring the astonished looks from Theresa and Satan, speaking slowly—

"This is arrogant nonsense. Just laugh it off as a joke."

"Things that are called eternal simply do not exist."

"Everything is temporary. The trial of the gods may already be quietly approaching."

title: Chapter 33 — Sorrow of the Era
content:
Chapter 33 — Sorrow of the Era

Volume 39 · Chapter 33

After hearing Merlin's mutterings, Satan sneered inwardly. Someone actually didn't respect those ancient gods of Asgard?

Still, Satan was very puzzled about Merlin's origins. Ever since getting on the carriage, this man had been asking questions left and right, seemingly paying special attention to the ancient gods.

This made him believe Teresa's words a little more. It seemed this person truly had never left the forest, living in complete isolation.

"You'd better not talk nonsense," Teresa said. "The ancient gods who live in Asgard are all powerful beings. They represent the highest level of strength among the ancient gods." She paused, then countered with a question, "Do you know how long Odin and his gods have ruled the world since the death of the first giant, Ymir? No one could judge them."

After boarding the carriage, Merlin took the opportunity to learn about the ancient gods, especially Asgard, gaining some insights.

The world of this era was gradually becoming clear in Merlin's mind, but the information was still insufficient, especially regarding the circumstances of other races.

Merlin really wanted to know about the demons of this era — were they also living under oppression and bullying like humans?

"That's not necessarily true. I believe fate is a balanced thing. Everyone will pay the corresponding price for what they do, even the King of Gods is no exception."

"Heh, ridiculous. What would a savage who has lived in a forest all his life possibly understand?" Satan stared at Merlin and sneered, "Do you even know how powerful the King of Gods is? He is the sole supreme deity, controlling the laws of war, invincible in every battle."

"No one in this world can defeat him. Your words fully expose your ignorance."

"I think that closed-off forest is where you belong. Why leave? Just go back."

A hint of awkwardness flashed across Teresa's eyes. She wanted to help Merlin refute him, but his words were truly impractical.

In Teresa's eyes, Merlin was like a newborn infant — completely unfamiliar with the outside world, which was why he had no fear.

"No one in this world can defeat Odin? What if someone who isn't from this world tries?"

Merlin responded half-seriously, his gaze fixed tightly on Satan's eyes. In fact, he truly wasn't from this world.

Not to mention that Merlin didn't belong to this worldline, and moreover, he was a transmigrator from another world.

This identity alone could break the wish Odin had made back then.

Perhaps no one in this world could defeat Odin, but Merlin from another world might very well be able to.

His seemingly flawless, invincible nature actually harbored an unnoticeable flaw — a weak point, a breakthrough.

Merlin sometimes wondered why he had come to this age of the gods and shouldered the mission of a prophet. Was everything arranged by fate from the moment he transmigrated?

Could it be that an extraordinary outsider like him was sent to defeat the invincible Odin, and push the stalled wheel of history forward once more?

Everything seemed perfectly logical, yet Merlin felt deeply uncomfortable. Fate — this elusive thing — was not something that could be changed by power alone.

Satan was startled by Merlin's words, his brows furrowing tightly. "What do you mean by that?"

"Nothing. Forget what I just said." Merlin smiled and didn't answer.

Satan remained suspicious, particularly intrigued by Merlin's mention of coming from another world — something he had never heard before.

Suddenly, the carriage came to a stop. Shouts and cursing from soldiers rang out from outside, drawing everyone's attention inside:

"Get lost! This is the carriage of the Goddess of Luck!"

"You common rabble, move aside quick! If the Goddess gets angry, you'll face the cruelest punishment!"

"Move or I'll draw my sword!"

Teresa quickly stepped off the carriage and saw a group of starving refugees blocking the carriage procession.

They wore tattered rags barely covering their bodies, ranging from elderly people to infants still in swaddling clothes — seemingly displaced humans scattered around?

"What's going on?" Teresa asked as she got down.

"Goddess, a group of civilians is demanding grain and has blocked our procession."

Upon hearing the soldiers' report, Teresa hurried forward and saw a frail woman kneeling on the ground, pressing her hand on her young son's head, forcing him to kneel as well.

In the woman's arms was an infant, breathing very faintly. Her own sunken eyes showed she was starved — how could she possibly have milk to feed the child?

Teresa raised her head and looked out. There were easily hundreds of people, all refugees who hadn't been accepted into any human tribe.

The boy whose head had been forced down broke free from his mother's arm, stood up, and loudly cursed:

"I won't kneel to these evil gods! They're the ones who stole our grain and caused many of us to starve to death!"

Teresa's expression changed. Her lips moved as if wanting to explain something, but she could say nothing in the end, as though there were unspeakable difficulties.

The guard beside her was shocked and raised his sword, intending to kill the insolent boy on the spot!

"Wait!" Teresa sharply commanded, stopping the guard.

Merlin also walked over and asked, "What's happening here?"

"These are people who live outside the tribes," Teresa hesitantly explained.

"Not all humans live in tribes?" Merlin asked in surprise.

"Tribe resources can't support all humans. Some are destined to survive on their own out there," Teresa said.

"I just heard you mentioned you took their grain. That doesn't quite match what you just said. Your sister isn't as perfect as you described."

Merlin spoke with a meaningful tone.

"We had no choice! Wealth and food are all prioritized for Asgard! If my sister doesn't offer these things, many people will be taken to Asgard as slaves!" Teresa lowered her head and gritted her teeth, "My sister also has no choice. The remaining food barely sustains anyone. Many in the tribe also go hungry, so... they can only take the refugees' food to replenish the tribe and ensure it continues to survive."

"So to protect their own tribe's survival, they steal from others?" Merlin nodded, thinking this was exactly the Goddess of Light he knew.

"What are you hesitating for?! Kill these refugees now! How dare they disturb the Goddess's procession!" Satan stepped out and loudly barked at the guards.

"Shut up, Satan!" Teresa's brows tightened. After a moment, she said, "Bring these people back to the tribe."

"Huh?!" Satan's eyes widened in shock, hurrying over, "Are you mad?! So many people joining the tribe — we simply can't feed them! It'll only drain our food and make things even worse!"

"What should we do? Just let them die? We stole their grain in the first place, and now they have nowhere else to go," Teresa said sternly.

"Survival of the fittest is completely normal. Your kindness shouldn't be wasted on them," Satan said with a dark expression.

"Take them back. That's my order. Everyone eats a little less, and these people might barely survive," Teresa commanded.

Satan desperately raked his hands through his hair, his mind in turmoil.

Merlin watched the woman kneeling on the ground, especially the infant in her arms — so thin she looked like a tiny skeleton.

He'd never truly understood the phrase "skin and bones" before, but this moment made it vividly clear.

No flesh could be seen on that infant, only withered yellow skin wrapping a small frame of bones.

If not for the faint breathing, Merlin might have thought the child was already dead.

Merlin's expression darkened. Without conscious thought, his fists clenched. From that infant, he saw the sorrow of this era —

Is this the age of the gods?

An era filled with oppression, hunger, and death.

Perhaps my coming here isn't just for Alice.

Those insatiable gods will surely meet their destruction.

Happy New Year, everyone!

I've been preparing for my new book recently, so updates may be slower than usual.

But at this pace, this story should wrap up next month as well.

title: Chapter 34 — Quirky Abilities
content:
Chapter 34 — Quirky Abilities

Volume 39 · Chapter 34

Merlin followed Teresa to the human tribe's settlement.

He had thought this place should be a paradise for humans, but the situation was still far from optimistic—

Merlin saw people with empty stomachs everywhere on the streets, barely clinging to life with the small amount of food distributed daily.

The houses in sight were also extremely simple, with the only stone building being the palace where Maria worked.

The atmosphere of poverty hit him in the face, a stark contrast to the living conditions of humans in the future.

In this era, it was already fortunate for the human leader to be able to rule from a stone house without being exposed to wind and rain.

Merlin glanced at the new refugees who had just joined the tribe, thinking that Satan was right—this place couldn't support too many people, only making things worse.

Satan was furious and complaining, feeling helpless against Teresa's kindness, as arranging these refugees had become a threat to the tribe's survival.

Merlin could somewhat understand Satan's feelings at this moment; from a rational perspective, driving these refugees away would be the best choice.

Unfortunately, as a goddess, Teresa wasn't a rational person, a trait she shared with Alice—she wasn't good at refusing those in distress.

As soon as Teresa stepped off the carriage, the tribe's residents rushed over excitedly, their eyes filled with adoration and respect—

"Teresa-sama, you're back!"

"Welcome back, Teresa-sama. Without you, the entire tribe has lost its color."

"Teresa-neesan! Look at the flower wreath I wove!"

Teresa took the flower wreath from the little girl, examined it, and stroked her head, "It's beautiful, made for me?"

The little girl nodded repeatedly, clearly having prepared this gift for a long time, her face full of love for Teresa.

Although Teresa was the Goddess of Fortune, she had no airs and was very close to the people.

Compared to the cold and distant Goddess of Light Maria, people seemed to love this smiling goddess more.

"Thank you, I like it very much."

Teresa put the flower wreath on her head, noticing that people were warily watching the refugees behind her.

Upon reflection, it wasn't surprising—suddenly having so many people meant their food might decrease.

Selfishness was human nature, unchanged across any era.

Teresa's expression turned serious, deciding she needed to explain to the tribe's people, or the refugees wouldn't be able to integrate.

"They are all people who have lost their way, all because we took their food."

"This tribe is humanity's hope. If we don't help these people, we should at least give them some aid."

"I know the tribe's food is scarce, but if each of us saves a little, they can survive."

"Believe me, these difficulties are temporary. The future belongs to us!"

Teresa patted her non-existent biceps, saying some encouraging words that filled people with hope for the future.

Perhaps it was the power of language itself, or the light emanating from Teresa, but it easily infected others.

The atmosphere in the tribe eased somewhat, and although many were unwilling, they could barely accept the new refugees.

Merlin stood quietly beside them, watching the girl surrounded by desperate people, and for a moment, he seemed to see Alice's figure—

No matter how much time passed, she wouldn't change, still the little guardian of justice, using her body to protect the hope that could extinguish at any time.

Whether in the past or future, people like her gave those around her endless strength, making others unconsciously want to follow her.

In the future, she would be the strongest support in his heart.

For now, she was humanity's spirit.

In the following days, Merlin lived in the tribe, spending almost every day with Teresa.

Not for romance, but to learn more about the Era of the Gods from Teresa.

Teresa didn't refuse, hoping Merlin could integrate into the tribe and answering his questions as much as possible.

However, Merlin had already made his own plans—to unite the oppressed and launch a large-scale rebellion.

Without a doubt, this was the path the demon race's prophet had taken. As long as Merlin followed it, there would be no mistakes.

But Teresa spending all day with Merlin made Satan seethe with jealousy, his mind full of ways to get rid of this savage!

Satan could sense that Teresa's gaze towards Merlin was becoming more and more improper, seemingly shifting from admiration to something else.

This wasn't a good sign. Satan eagerly awaited Maria's return, planning to add fuel to the fire and drive Merlin away.

Merlin and Teresa sat under a giant ancient tree in the tribe, looking like a couple from afar, which was why Satan was so furious.

"Are other races also living as miserably as humans?"

"Most are."

"Most? So there are exceptions?"

Merlin furrowed his brow. Besides the Asgard situation, the circumstances of other races were also important, as he might need their power later.

He had thought all races were in similar situations to humans, but there were exceptions?

"Yes, the elves." Teresa paused before continuing, "The Elf God Corellon is not only extremely powerful but also kind, taking great care of his people, so the elves live quite well, unlike us. Although my sister is also kind, she lacks strength and is easily bullied by other ancient gods."

"Is that so?"

Merlin lowered his head, thinking it was no wonder the elves' era came after the Era of the Gods. It seemed Corellon's accumulation was crucial.

It appeared that the ancient gods weren't a monolithic group, with differing ideologies within. Asgard was just the group with the most say.

In this era, for the lower classes to live a little better, two conditions had to be met: their race's ancient god had to be kind, and their ancient god had to be powerful.

Lacking either factor would leave people living in dire straits.

Teresa glanced at the Banri Garan at Merlin's waist, curiosity getting the better of her, "Is your sword very valuable? I see you don't even take it off when sleeping. Is it a divine artifact?"

Merlin came back to himself, looking down at his Banri Garan, "Yes, it's a divine artifact."

"Ah! You actually possess a divine artifact!" Teresa's eyes were full of envy.

"Is there a need to be so surprised? Aren't divine artifacts something the ancient gods have in abundance?"

"They're not! Divine artifacts are extremely precious. Each one requires massive resources to forge, and only the Asgardian gods can make one per person." Teresa looked at the sword at Merlin's waist, asking quietly, "What special abilities does it have?"

"It can release flames and kill enemies, taking their life force to replenish the user." Merlin didn't hide anything, speaking truthfully.

"Taking life force to replenish oneself?" Teresa's expression turned complex, whispering, "What a strange ability."

title: Chapter 35 — Alliance
content:
Chapter 35 — Alliance

Volume 39 · Chapter 35

Several days later, Maria finally returned to the tribe from Asgard. She looked worried, afraid she couldn't escape Odin's next coercion. Maria's inspiration had run dry; she feared she could no longer move Odin with a story, and ultimately her soul would be stripped away and locked in Valhalla. Maria hoped that by returning she could make plans for the tribe so that even if she were gone, humanity could continue. Yet she also hesitated, unsure whether the next successor should be her idealistic sister Teresa or the shrewd Satan. Both choices had problems: Teresa was overly idealistic and swayed by emotion, while Satan was corrupt and used extreme means. If she had to pick one, Maria had to consider carefully, otherwise humanity's future would be unpredictable. Holy light blazed above the tribe as Maria slowly descended, seeing many refugees among the people, her brow furrowed involuntarily. 'Lady Maria!' Satan, seeing the light in the sky, knew Maria had returned and hurried over. He had waited long for this moment and finally could seize the chance to smear Merlin's business. 'Not good, something big has happened!' 'What happened? You're panicking,' Maria said sternly. 'Not long ago, Lady Teresa brought out a mysterious wild man from the forest; I couldn't stop her.' Satan, unable to swallow this, continued to embellish, 'No one knows that guy's background; Teresa insists on bringing him back to the tribe, which could easily cause trouble—what if he's a spy for some evil force? Our tribe would...' Maria's face turned grim as she coldly said, 'Take Teresa and that person to my castle; I want to question them thoroughly.' 'Alright, I'll do it now,' Satan replied, a flash of cunning in his eyes as he thought triumphantly, 'Now I'll get that guy named Surtel kicked out of the tribe~' In the stone castle, Maria sat on the high seat with Satan, full of wicked schemes, standing beside her. Merlin finally met face‑to‑face the arch‑enemy who had dealt a heavy blow to the demon race, and was so shocked he could not speak. Because Maria's looks were almost identical to Alice's and Teresa's, if you didn't look closely they seemed completely the same! At that moment Merlin finally understood: the person Cain had painted was not Alice but Maria, who resembled her. That strange oil painting had confused him for a long time, and today he finally got the answer. Merlin glanced at Teresa, then subtly looked at Maria's chest, and muttered unconsciously, 'So big.' 'Pfft!' Teresa shot Merlin a fierce look and said lowly, 'Where are you looking? That's vulgar.' 'Cough cough!' Merlin cleared his throat to hide his embarrassment, thinking this might be the only difference between the two sisters. 'You're the one who's always lived in the forest, Surtel?' Maria asked pointedly. 'Exactly,' Merlin nodded. Seeing the atmosphere grow tense, Teresa guessed Satan must have been spreading rumors again, so she eagerly stepped forward to introduce this powerful ally to Maria. 'Sister, he's really strong—he protected me in the forest, defeated the chaos giants there, and with him we wouldn't need the blood‑pool seal to repel that hateful black dragon!' 'I didn't ask you, Teresa,' Maria said sternly. 'Well then,' Teresa replied, unable to resist, lowering her head and stepping back; she always respected her sister and would not talk back. Maria already knew Teresa had gone alone into the forest looking for the sealing technique; if she hadn't seen her sister still lively and standing here, she might have gone mad. Although Maria could sense Teresa's desire to share her burden, she could never let her sister fall into danger. 'You're lying, right? There's never been anyone living in that forest—where do you come from and what do you do?' 'I'm not lying; I really live in the forest,' Merlin glanced at Alice, 'a wild‑man~' 'What are you looking at?' Teresa complained. 'How long are you going to hide it, demon?' Maria asked bluntly. 'Uh!' Merlin was startled, glanced at the bracelet on his wrist, wondering if his aura‑concealing ability had failed. No! Even Teresa hadn't noticed—it must be Maria's keen perception spotting a flaw. 'Huh?' Teresa looked astonished, staring blankly at Merlin, 'You're actually a demon?' 'Satan has already reported everything; I've been wondering why there would be a human in a forest full of magical beasts.' Maria paused, locking eyes with Merlin, 'But after seeing you, I sensed intermittent demonic aura. Although I don't know what method you used to suppress your demonic presence so low, your identity is now obvious.' Merlin darkened his face, staying silent, though he wasn't panicking—exposing his demon identity was only a matter of time, because he needed to act as the demon race's prophet. 'Is Surtel really all true?' Teresa said, feeling uneasy, that he had deceived her for so long with no trust at all. 'Sorry, Teresa, I lied to you; your sister was right,' Merlin said, dropping the pretense, he undid the bracelet on his wrist, letting his aura show openly, 'I am a demon!' Teresa felt the strong demonic aura and was momentarily at a loss. 'Hah! So you're a demon spy!' Satan finally got his wish, stepped forward and demanded, 'Speak! Why did you come to our tribe, what evil scheme are you hatching? If you don't confess, you won't be leaving today!' Teresa's eyes wavered; if what Satan said were true and Merlin was a demon spy, then she would have committed a grave mistake, pushing the tribe to the brink of danger. In fact Merlin had planned to part ways with Teresa soon, leave the human tribe, he already knew where the demon realm lay, and wanted to quickly, as a prophet, fire the first shot in the rebellion against the ancient gods. But he hadn't expected Maria to return today, forcing him to change tactics—first win over the human side and join the resistance— 'Please believe me, I came here without malice, but for the future of the world.' 'I am Surtel, prophet of the demon race, and the demon who brought destruction to Asgard!' 'Now I am trying to persuade all peoples to gather courage and rise up against the gods of Asgard!' 'You humans are an indispensable member of the anti‑god alliance!'

title: Chapter 36 — The Black Dragon Strikes
content:
Chapter 36 — The Black Dragon Strikes

Volume 39 · Chapter 36

Merlin's speech instantly made the atmosphere suffocating.

Maria looked bewildered, while Theresa regarded him as if he were mad.

The ancient gods of Asgard had ruled the world for how many years? Could they really be overthrown just like that?

Merlin's words were like a mouse shouting that it would wipe out every cat in the world.

After all, they had never experienced an era where the gods were destroyed. Their imaginations were limited, and they could not entertain such crazy thoughts.

"What nonsense are you spouting!?" Satan roared.

"I'm serious. If you want your people to survive, the rule of the gods must be overthrown," Merlin said solemnly.

"Demon race prophet? I've never heard of such a figure among the demons," Maria probed suspiciously.

"It's normal that you don't know. The one who can lead the world to revolution and destroy the gods would hardly be someone everyone has heard of," Merlin explained.

"You unknown fellow, why should we trust you?" Satan paused and said coldly, "Resist the gods of Asgard? You say it easily. Do you have any idea how difficult that is? It's simply impossible."

"How would you know it's impossible without trying?"

Merlin came from the future and knew this path was viable — it was not impossible at all.

People of this era had been oppressed for too long, almost completely losing the courage to resist.

"How powerful are the gods of Asgard? To rebel against them means certain death!" Satan argued vehemently.

"Isn't death already our current path? The gods' rule merely lets you linger a bit longer and die a few years later, doesn't it?"

Satan was rendered speechless by Merlin's retort. In his eyes, Merlin was an unreasonable madman intent on dragging countless people to their deaths.

"Your idea is quite interesting," Maria suddenly spoke up. "But it's impractical. The gods are invincible. No one can shake their rule, and no sensible tribal leader would accept your suggestion, because the consequences of failure are unbearable."

"Isn't the outcome the same for everyone if we don't rise up and resist? We'd slowly march toward extinction. Why not be brave and fight for the sliver of hope we have? Once we succeed, the situation will completely逆转." Merlin paused and said slowly, "I know my ideas can't be accepted in the short term. Actually, the greatest enemy of each race is not the tyrannical gods, but complacency."

Maria's heart stirred. She had once harbored similar thoughts to Merlin's. The reason no one dared to resist was simply because the success rate was too low. They believed slow death was far more comfortable than a sudden one.

In a sense, Merlin's words were not far off. The pursuit of comfort was indeed the biggest obstacle in the current situation.

She felt her time might be running out. The next time she was taken to Asgard, it would likely be her death sentence. The pressure was enormous.

Maria felt a stir of restlessness. With so little time left, she was forced to make a choice. Since she was about to lose her soul anyway, why not take a gamble?

If Maria died, the unreliable Theresa and Satan who remained both had their problems. They might not be able to hold the situation together as she did, and the human race would quickly perish after her death.

"Besides us, who else can you convince? Humans are the weakest race. Relying on us alone won't work."

"Maria!" Satan was dumbfounded. Looking at Maria's attitude, she clearly shared some of these thoughts. He absolutely did not want to follow her to certain death!

"The demon race. I can definitely persuade them," Merlin answered with certainty. Having learned the Blood Pool Seal, according to the course of history, as long as he sealed Behemoth, the demons would be the first to raise their rebellion!

"The demon race?" Maria lowered her head and thought carefully. That power alone was not enough. It would be better to have the elves join as well. They were the second most powerful faction after Asgard.

"Don't worry. I'll gradually get other races to join as well," Merlin said confidently. Judging from various texts, the elven god Corellon had great influence during the age of the gods. Once he could be persuaded, the other races would pose no problem.

"Hah! Who do you think you are? You tell them to join you and they'll join? Don't be so full of yourself!" Satan couldn't help pouring cold water on him.

Merlin furrowed his brows, thinking that if he weren't afraid that killing Satan would interfere with the future, he would draw his blade and eliminate this guy right now.

"Don't forget, Odin the King of Gods is an invincible existence! Even if your plan can defeat those gods, can you defeat the King of Gods?" Satan narrowed his eyes and said sternly, "It wasn't the gods who made Odin great; it was Odin who made the gods great! As long as you cannot defeat Odin, nothing will change!"

"I can defeat Odin," Merlin answered with certainty.

"Hahaha, Lord Maria, please don't believe this babbling fool. His words are becoming increasingly ridiculous. He actually claims he can defeat Odin?"
