Satan looked down at Merlin and sneered, "I've seen many people good at bragging, but someone as delusional and unable to see reality as you is truly a first. I'd call you the pride of boasting — even cows would be terrified to see you."

"N-no, he defeated the Chaos Giant. Perhaps he really can..." Theresa wasn't confident either, her voice growing quieter.

"That was merely an immature Chaos Giant. Besides, even an adult Chaos Giant could never compare to Odin's power. These are two entirely different matters, dear Theresa."

Satan said softly, a hint of sourness rising in his heart. Could it be that Theresa was actually speaking up for a demon? This was not a good sign.

Maria, who held the deciding vote, remained silent. She was also wavering and could see no possibility of Merlin ever defeating Odin.

Suddenly the entire castle shook violently. A colossal dragon roar echoed through the air — the black dragon Nidhogg was attacking!

Above the human tribe, the black dragon Nidhogg circled overhead, its magnificent body blotting out the sky and plunging humanity once again into terrifying darkness.

Scorching dragon breath swept across, burning down countless tribal homes. Countless people hadn't even had time to scream before being turned to ash.

Nidhogg had come today to collect its due — threatening Maria into preparing young children for its feast.

"Maria! You have broken our agreement!"

"There are no young children prepared for me at all."

"As punishment, I will destroy your tribe today!"

"Let your people become fertilizer for the earth in the pitch-black flames of my dragon fire!"

title: Chapter 37 — "Killed in One Slash"
content:
Chapter 37 — "Killed in One Slash"

Volume 39 · Chapter 37

Maria and the others quickly arrived outside, discovering the black dragon in the sky spewing inky black dragon flames that were incinerating the tribe's houses.

In just a short while, many people had already perished in the scorching flames.

Watching the panicked tribe members fleeing, Maria gritted her teeth, feeling discontent. She had just returned and hadn't even had time to deal with Nidhogg's matter yet.

"Great black dragon! Please calm your anger! I didn't deceive you, I just hadn't had time to prepare!"

"I won't believe your lies anymore, Maria!"

Nidhogg's massive dragon body hovered in the sky, its scarlet eyes flashing with endless rage.

"Tch, is there no room for negotiation left?"

Under the dragon flames' burning, the temperature in the tribe suddenly soared, causing many people to sweat profusely.

If this continued, the human tribe might not survive the day!

Maria knew she was no match for the black dragon, and she was completely helpless against Nidhogg.

"We're doomed! Are we really going to die today?" Satan panicked, covering his head with a pale face, unable to help but vent his anger at Merlin, "It's all because of this guy! If he hadn't suddenly appeared, we would have already started preparing the sacrifice for Nidhogg! He's the one who brought destruction to us humans!"

Although Teresa was very tense, she managed to remain calm because she knew Merlin could kill the Chaos Giant, so he must also be able to handle the black dragon!

After bringing Merlin back to the tribe, Teresa had abandoned her plan to build a blood pool seal, placing all her hopes on him.

Teresa secretly tugged at Merlin's sleeve, revealing pleading eyes, hoping he could provide help.

"Surtur."

"A mere black-colored crawling insect, what's there to be panicked about?" Merlin looked at Maria, saying meaningfully, "Watch closely with your eyes wide open, and see if I have the ability to take down that so-called King of the Gods up high."

The black dragon Nidhogg spewed scorching dragon flames from its mouth, the extremely high temperature capable of melting the earth.

Looking at the tiny humans below struggling to escape, it felt extremely pleased with itself.

Nidhogg was the creator of the dragon race, and suppressing giant dragons was no longer enough to satisfy its desires. Now it wanted everything except Asgard to submit to itself.

So the weakest humans became Nidhogg's first target, making them its vassals before continuing to annex other races.

"Listen to the pitiful screams of humans, how wonderful and pleasant! This is the fate of those who dare to disobey!"

Just as the black dragon Nidhogg was enjoying the slaughter, it noticed a "human" below slowly approaching.

This caught its attention - in this situation, someone daring to come forward to die was probably a madman.

"Hah, did you go completely mad after seeing my magnificent body?"

"This is normal, after all, I am the great black dragon who brings despair to the world!"

"Hey! You fool! Do you really want to die?"

Merlin stopped in his tracks, looking up at Nidhogg circling in the sky, his expression unreadable, showing no signs of fear.

"Tch!" Nidhogg's mood turned unpleasant as it questioned, "Deaf? Can't you hear me speaking?"

"I can hear, but I'm not here to die. I'm here to take you down." Merlin replied straightforwardly, "You're quite unlucky to have met me. Why didn't you just stay in your nest?"

"Hahahaha!" The black dragon Nidhogg burst into loud laughter, its gaze like torches looking down at the tiny Merlin, "Did I hear that wrong? You're here to take me down?"

"That's right." Merlin nodded.

"This is the most ridiculous statement I've ever heard in my life!" Nidhogg opened its bloody maw, letting out a roar at Merlin, "A lowly human dares to spout such madness in front of me? What audacity! No matter how many times I burn you to death, it won't quench my anger!"

Merlin spread his hands, provoking, "Kill me? Go ahead and try."

The black dragon Nidhogg's eyes contracted sharply in anger, and without another word, it unleashed a blast of scorching black dragon flames at Merlin with all its might!

The flames instantly dyed the sky red, the clouds twisting and churning from the extreme heat, as if a bomb had suddenly exploded in the high sky!

Within the range of the dragon flames, the earth melted, transforming into a death zone where no living creature could survive!

Nidhogg was confident in its strength, and among the ancient gods, it was considered one of the stronger ones. Could it really not take down a tiny human?

It used its full strength to demonstrate its unmatched power to the other humans, to deter anyone else from daring to challenge it.

Merlin stood on the unmelted rock, facing the incoming dragon flames without moving, seemingly not intending to resist at all, letting the terrifying attack come.

Boom——

A massive explosion sounded as the dragon flames struck Merlin head-on, sparks flying everywhere!

A strange situation suddenly occurred - the powerful dragon flames seemed to hit an invisible wall, unable to break through this layer of defense!

Upon closer inspection, mysterious gray runes appeared floating before Merlin, clearly the power of the Law of Destruction!

This was just like when Merlin dealt with Satan, the Law's power protecting the holder of the divine position from harm.

With the Crown of Fate, Merlin now stood at the pinnacle of power, qualified to rival other main gods!

The Law's protection, like an absurd cheat, made Merlin invincible against any opponent except the main gods.

In other words, the ancient gods of this era were all lambs waiting to be slaughtered before Merlin!

They couldn't harm Merlin, but Merlin could unilaterally slaughter them!

In this era, only the King of the Gods, Odin, could barely be considered Merlin's equal.

"The power of the Law? It's even more useful than I imagined!"

The black dragon Nidhogg fell into panic and confusion, its previously arrogant attitude instantly vanishing.

It felt uneasy, with only one thought remaining - this guy was extremely dangerous, and it had to escape quickly!

"Impossible! Why is there someone else besides Odin who can control the Law?! Who are you?!"

"Now you know to be afraid? Too late!"

Merlin began to attempt using the Law of Destruction's power, forming a knife with his hand as gray runes continuously gathered in his palm.

Merlin's gaze condensed, and with a swift slash of his hand, the accumulated Law of Destruction shot out like a long knife!

In an instant, the sky shattered, a spatial rift appearing as the earth seemed to be erased like tofu, creating a magnificent giant canyon——

The seemingly powerful Nidhogg was instantly killed by Merlin's bare hands!

This was the absolute power of a main god!

title: Chapter 38 — Departure
content:
Chapter 38 — Departure

Volume 39 · Chapter 38

The black dragon, proud of its great body, seemed to disappear into thin air under the impact of the destruction law, erased in an instant. Since this was Merlin's first time trying to use the destruction law's traffic, he wasn't very skilled, and his hand knife struck a bit off. As a result, the black dragon Nidhöggr was left with only one head, accompanied by a surge of dragon blood, falling into the newly formed Grand Canyon.

Merlin knew the black dragon was still alive, and he had heard Alice talk about the Spanish kingdom, so he didn't plan to continue pursuing it. Because Nidhöggr was the creator of the dragon race, killing it now would cause all the initial dragon species to die, and there would be no giant dragons in the future. Of course, this was only one aspect of the impact of killing Nidhöggr now, and it would also trigger more chain reactions, which was what Merlin was more concerned about.

"Sister, you also saw it, right? That is... " Teresa swallowed hard, "that is the power of the law, right?" "Impossible!" Satan couldn't believe his eyes, becoming somewhat incoherent, "How can there be a second person who can use the law besides Odin?" Maria didn't speak, but the shock on her face lingered, revealing her current emotions - she must have encountered the three goddesses of fate? And obtained the highest law power like Odin! Who would have thought that in an era dominated by Odin, there would be a second ancient god?

Is it the three goddesses' deliberate arrangement? No! They are just the embodiment of the world's will and won't interfere with anything! The only explanation is that the unpredictable fate is a kind of omen. His appearance means that the era of the gods is about to be destroyed. Maria couldn't calm down, and now she deeply believed in Merlin's words. Under the rule that only the main god can kill the main god, only Merlin could end the dark era and bring death to those high-and-mighty gods.

"Why, why did a guy who suddenly appeared have the power of the law? When did the demon race produce such a powerful guy?" Satan watched Merlin from afar, feeling that his position was precarious. Maria would definitely start supporting Merlin and abandon him, this clown. And Teresa, Satan could see the complex emotions of admiration and reverence in her eyes. In front of the law controller, he had no competitiveness at all. Teresa's eyes shone, feeling that she had finally done something right, which was bringing Merlin back from the forest. In a sense, it was Teresa who rang the bell signaling the beginning of the destruction of the gods' era.

"Surtur, he must be able to lead us to overthrow Asgard!" After Merlin showed his overwhelming power, Maria changed her previous attitude and began to actively communicate with him, promising to join the resistance alliance. Merlin didn't mind the previous unpleasantness and instead talked about his plan to unite all the oppressed races to resist Asgard together. And that king of the gods, Odin, naturally only Merlin had the possibility of defeating him. The most difficult task must be undertaken by him.

However, these plans were all confidential, and it was best not to let Odin know before the united army was successfully formed, to prevent the gods from preparing. As long as everything was done in secret, the number of sacrifices could be greatly reduced, and the gods of Asgard could be caught off guard. These days, Satan was like a deflated balloon, becoming very obedient and no longer daring to say anything against Merlin, fearing that he would be eliminated with just one careless move. Now Merlin's status was extremely high, and even Maria had to be polite to him. What was Satan? Just a cowardly and arrogant little clown.

Merlin continued to live in the human tribe for a while before he had the intention of leaving. To overthrow the gods, he had to unite other races, and the most important one was the demon race. He planned to go to the demon race's Linglie first and use the blood pool seal to seal the demon god Behemoth, completely liberating those initial demons. Maybe Merlin could see his own grandfather, Mephisto, and those initial demons who died in the holy war. Originally, Merlin only told Maria about his intention to leave and didn't want Teresa to know. Because Merlin always saw Alice's shadow in this lucky goddess, he didn't know what mindset to use to face his wife's past life.

If there was someone in this era that Merlin couldn't deal with, it would definitely be Teresa. "Is the demon race's territory in the east?" The sky was still dark, and Merlin sat on Kong's head, walking out of the tribe's gate, deciding to leave quietly. "Let's go, Kong." "Roar roar~" Kong let out two snorts, and during this time, Kong had been living outside the tribe because such a large demon beast was impossible for humans to raise. Fortunately, Kong's strength was still not weak, and it could hunt and eat its fill outside the tribe. It even kindly brought back a lot of food for the humans in the tribe.

But just as Merlin walked a short distance, he heard someone calling out to him from behind. Teresa drove a light to catch up - "Surtur!" "How did you come here?" "Fine, you want to leave without telling me!" Teresa slowly landed, put her hands on her hips, and revealed a look identical to Alice's, glaring at Merlin with discontent. Merlin sighed, unsure how Teresa knew he was leaving. Was it Maria who told her? "I still have many things to do, and I won't be able to stay here forever. You should understand that resisting the gods can't rely solely on human power."

"I know, but I want..." "If you want to follow me, then forget it. I don't want to bring a burden." Merlin said all the unpleasant words first, stopping Teresa's unrealistic ideas. Teresa and Alice were ultimately different. As an outsider, he didn't want to have any emotional entanglements in this era. If they continued to interact, what if Teresa fell in love with him, or he fell in love with Teresa? Then things would become difficult to handle. Although Merlin hadn't heard the story of the prophet killing the lucky goddess, he, who came from the future, knew the final result - that this kind and gentle goddess would not exist in the future but would die, which was the fundamental reason for Alice's birth.

Merlin knew this was selfish, but to ensure that history could proceed normally, and this world line's Alice would be born, he had to do this. He had to make himself cold and unfeeling, not caring about Teresa's enthusiasm, and let her follow the normal historical trajectory to her death. Teresa's expression became sad, and she was extremely disappointed inside. Her idea of following Merlin had been strangled in her heart, and she had to swallow the words she wanted to say. Teresa, like Alice, didn't like to show her weakness. No matter how much she was hurt, she would display her strength and courage - "Don't be self-important, who wants to follow a guy like you?" "I... I just came out to see you off out of kindness!" "Be grateful to me in your heart, huh~!"

A new book has been stockpiled with 20,000 words, enough for 50,000 words, and it will be updated to the end. After that, there are many things to do, and the new book needs to be revised and optimized. The outline, plot, and pace all need to be thought through carefully, or else the original authors might not read it. It is temporarily decided that the new book is a fantasy, otherworldly, farming type, with a business model, using modern goods to dominate the otherworld. There is no system, just relying on knowledge to make things, and steadily managing the business. Of course, this is temporary, and if the brain gets too hot, the 50,000 words might be deleted, and a new book about immortal heroes might be written instead.

title: Chapter 39 — Deviating from the Historical Trajectory
content:
Chapter 39 — Deviating from the Historical Trajectory

Volume 39 · Chapter 39

"You still have time to see off a savage like me. Thanks."

"Will you come back?"

"I don't know."

Merlin didn't give a definite answer, because afterwards he'd be too busy integrating the resistance forces, with no chance to return to the human settlements.

Perhaps the next time he met Teresa, it might coincide with the Rebel Alliance launching its assault on Asgard.

"Oh? " Teresa looked disappointed, and could only mutter, "Then take care of yourself."

"That's my line. Take good care of yourself, Teresa. If possible, don't leave any regrets."

Merlin said it meaningfully, hinting that Teresa should do things without regrets while she was still alive.

"What kind of tone is that? It's just like you're saying your last words."

"Something like that."

Merlin nodded, didn't say too much, and turned to walk toward Konggang, his back to Teresa.

At this moment he was very hesitant, hoping he could tell Teresa about the future.

But he was also afraid of making the wrong choice, which could cause the future of this world line to spiral out of control.

His feelings of concealment and confession were each half and half. Merlin could only rely on his own instincts to make the right choice.

"Wait." Teresa suddenly called out to Merlin, closed her eyes, and pressed her hands together in a wishing gesture. "I hope you find happiness."

"What's this? " Merlin frowned, with a strange feeling of having received a buff from someone.

"This is a blessing from the Goddess of Luck. It might not be very effective, but it's better than nothing." Teresa had no confidence in her own power at all.

Merlin frowned. His sense of guilt grew heavier. This unreliable goddess, even when a great disaster was looming, still cared about others.

Was it because Teresa didn't die that Alice couldn't be born? So he had to watch her die helplessly?

Merlin's heart was in turmoil. He instinctively clenched his fists, as if making some kind of resolution—

"Teresa, the reason I'm called a prophet is because I can truly see some futures."

Teresa was stunned, then smiled and said, "Stop joking. What are you talking about?"

"I'm from the future of another world line. I'm not joking." Merlin paused and said in a very serious tone, "I know the fates of all the races in the future. I also know that the gods of Asgard will surely perish, and I know who will take over the world."

The smile on Teresa's face gradually faded. Seeing Merlin's serious expression, it didn't look like a joke, and she believed him a little.

"Is it all true?"

"Yes. If you don't believe it, just treat it as my nonsense. Don't worry about it."

Teresa lowered her head and fell silent. Her mind was in chaos, not knowing what to say for a time.

Merlin suddenly confessing that he was a person from the future dealt a tremendous shock to Teresa's worldview.

"Then humans in the future—"

"They're fine. They ushered in their own era. Your wish came true."

Merlin answered in a firm tone, a trace of reluctance flashing in his eyes. He wondered—wasn't Teresa curious about her own fate?

"That's great! Finally—"

Teresa's biggest wish was to hope that humanity could break free from oppression and bid farewell to the present suffering.

Hearing from Merlin's mouth that her wish would come true in the future, Teresa showed a smile from the bottom of her heart.

"Aren't you curious about your own future fate?"

"Of course I'm curious. Will I become a reliable goddess revered by everyone, just like my older sister~?"

"You'll die. Your life will fall together with Ragnarok."

The expression on Teresa's face froze on the spot. She fell into a long silence again, lowering her head and not speaking.

Merlin knew this matter was very cruel, but he believed Teresa should know some things about the future.

A goddess who was willing to sacrifice her life for humanity never saw the arrival of the human era until her death. How pathetic.

Teresa suddenly raised her head, as if she had come to terms with it. A brilliant smile appeared on her face again, and she said happily.

"If death is my fate, then I will accept it calmly."

"Why? " Merlin widened his eyes in disbelief.

"Because, as long as humanity can flourish, I'll have no regrets. My life as this unreliable goddess is nothing compared to humanity's future."

"Do you think that's enough? Can you accept it?! " Merlin's brows knitted together. He couldn't understand Teresa's thoughts.

Yeah, that's fine.

A light breeze ruffled a few strands of Teresa's silver hair. Against the morning sunlight, this smiling goddess seemed to gain a touch more dignity.

Teresa had seen too many people struggling bitterly in this era, ultimately failing to persevere, their lives withering away.

She thought things were supposed to be different. Something must have gone wrong—

After the Progenitor Titan fell, the newly evolved world was still empty and dead, with barely any life.

In order to make the new earth vibrant and no longer lonely, the ancient gods began to create many beings in their own image.

Teresa was also there, helping her older sister Maria create humanity, thinking that besides her older sister, she would also have many new companions.

The innocent Teresa thought that the newly appearing humans would feel the joy and happiness of this world.

At first everything went smoothly, just as Teresa had imagined. Different races coexisted peacefully.

Until Odin traded his eye to obtain the power of law, formed Asgard, the balance was broken, and a long period of oppressive rule began.

Humanity at the lowest level experienced oppression and torment from birth to death, without a moment's respite.

Teresa felt deeply guilty about this. This wasn't the result she wanted. Humanity wasn't created to suffer.

So Teresa wasn't afraid of death. What she feared was that her wish might not come true. After hearing the future results from Merlin, she suddenly felt less pressure on her shoulders.

Merlin sighed, turned around, and jumped onto Konggang's palm. He planned to leave the settlement and continue his plan—

To make humanity flourish. Was this the wish Teresa was willing to sacrifice her life to complete?

No wonder Maria, after putting on the Crown of Fate, didn't directly choose to resurrect Teresa.

This was all Teresa's own choice.

In a corner inside the settlement, Satan stood dumbstruck. He had heard everything just now, and his heart churned for a long time.

Originally Satan was worried that Teresa would elope with Merlin, which is why he secretly followed to check. Unexpectedly, he made an unexpected discovery—

Did I hear that right? From the future? Something like this actually exists!

If I tell Odin this news—could I then—

Merlin made the wrong choice. No previous prophet had ever confessed their origins to anyone. He was the first.

This information would trigger a butterfly effect, completely scrambling history and producing unforeseeable situations.

title: Chapter 40 — Human Who Claims to Be a Demon
content:
Chapter 40 — Human Who Claims to Be a Demon

Volume 39 · Chapter 40

In the demon race's territory, amidst a vast yellow desert, demons were hauling large stones upward. To build a magnificent and splendid palace for the great creator, Behemoth. At this time, Behemoth was not within the territory, but out on a patrol. However, the demon god's minions were still here supervising the demons, and they must quickly complete the construction of the magnificent palace.

Those present were all the first-generation demons, who had a close bloodline connection with Behemoth—the elderly had white hair, the young were still in swaddling clothes. Compared to future demons, their demonic features were more pronounced, the horns on their heads larger, and naturally they were superior in strength—

An old demon avoided the gaze of the scorpion demons, went to a corner; the fearsome-looking one actually held an infant in his arms? The demon infant's breathing was faint, its skin dark, though not yet emaciated, signs of malnutrition were visible.

“Mammon! How's the situation?” Young Mephistopheles appeared, inquiring about the infant's condition; this era's first-generation Demon Lord looked remarkably young. From the sharp horns on its head and its physique, it already possessed the qualifications to become a Demon Lord. Mephistopheles was the first demon created by Behemoth, inheriting the finest bloodline and talent. Yet he did not submit to the creator; instead, a will to rebel burned in his heart—Behemoth never regarded demons as subjects, but as expendable replacements! Mephistopheles could not tolerate Behemoth's high-handed attitude, and instead tried every means to let more demons survive. “Lucifer! Belial is almost done for; tonight we must sneak out to get some food.” The first-generation Greed Demon Lord was precisely this wretched old demon before us, and the infant in his arms was surely the future Demon Lord who would lead the demon race through its darkest period. Mephistopheles looked at the infant Belial, feeling despair; if possible, he should let the young infant continue living, but now they couldn't even afford a meal. “Impossible, Behemoth doesn't allow us to rest even for a moment; to him we are merely tools for his pleasure, and dying means he can instantly create new slaves.” “What then? Belial is still so tiny—are we to watch it starve to death? We are the very first demons created.” Mammon said sorrowfully, “If a race cannot even protect its young infants, what future is there?” The atmosphere fell into dead silence; Mephistopheles had no recourse, sweat pouring down under the blazing sun, head bowed, silent.

Behemoth's minions were whipping the demons with lashes, ordering them to work nonstop to erect a palace displaying the great demon god's majesty. Mephistopheles thought it all meaningless—was living merely to let Behemoth squeeze out all our value, then die in despair? Now the swaddled Belial was about to starve to death, proving Behemoth gave them no chance to even experience despair.

“Hey! What are you whispering about? Get back to work!” A scorpion demon spotted them, scuttling forward on its eight legs, whip already raised. “Mammon, rebel—otherwise we have no other path.” “Mephistopheles, have you gone mad? You'll be publicly executed!” “Having no chance to even feel despair, what's there to fear? Death? Don't joke.” “Perhaps we need to calm down and talk; if the palace is finished, maybe the nightmare will end.” “Don't pin your hopes on Behemoth—he is an outright tyrant; peace begged for will never last. Be brave, Mammon!” As Mephistopheles shouted loudly, he drew a dagger honed from stone at his waist and lunged at the approaching scorpion demon. One silent strike pierced the scorpion demon's heart, and he snatched away its blade as well. “Everyone! Rise up and rebel! Kill these scorpion overseers! We will be our own masters!”

Mephistopheles' cry was not met with cheers but triggered an alarm; swarms of scorpion demons came from all directions. Obviously Mephistopheles was not the first rebel—others had tried before and failed, their fate easy to imagine. Under the high-pressure state, the demons had developed a slave mentality, thinking that as long as they worked hard they could survive. Hoping Behemoth would show mercy and let them eat and stay warm? Better to wait for the sun to rise in the west. Those who dare to stand up and rebel are forever few; Mephistopheles is among them.

The scorpion demons gathering to suppress grew ever more numerous; Mephistopheles skillfully wielded his twin blades like a meat grinder, slaughtering in all directions. In a short time, his demi-god-level battle aura surged; he had already slain dozens of scorpion demons, his body soaked in demon blood. “Is that all you've got? Without Behemoth, you're nothing!” Mephistopheles roared angrily, driving back the encircling scorpion demons.

At that moment, Mephistopheles saw a road ahead—a tiny scorpion demon appeared, though small in stature, the other demons' eyes were filled with awe. “Behemoth Lord is not here; I decide—why rebel, Mephistopheles?” “I demand the rights we deserve; we were created not to be Behemoth's tools!” “Have you finished? Dare to disrupt the palace construction and stir up revolt here—you're doomed, demon chief.” The small scorpion demon flashed light from its hand; a sealing jar appeared before all demons, their faces turning to horror. Behemoth left the sealing jar precisely because he anticipated a demon uprising; as long as the jar exists, demons cannot make waves. The small scorpion demon lightly flicked the jar with a finger; Mephistopheles instantly rolled his eyes and lost consciousness, falling into a deep stupor.

<>

“This is the fate of daring to rebel! Behemoth the Great created you—ingratitude aside, you actually dare to revolt?!” “I hope Mephistopheles is the last demon executed; let no one else be as foolish as him, thinking to defy the great creator. “Only by obeying and offering everything to Behemoth will you have a future.” The small scorpion demon stood on the execution platform, delivering an impassioned speech, wishing such incidents would not happen often. Killing Mephistopheles would at least for a time serve as a warning to others. The demons bowed their heads; they never imagined that the original demon Mephistopheles would still not escape the death sentence. Mammon] lowered his head in sorrow, unable to watch Mephistopheles being hacked to white bone piece by piece. The execution demons on both sides had already sharpened their blades to razor sharpness; they would certainly not kill Mephistopheles in one stroke, but slowly torture him to death. “Indeed, there's no way to succeed.” Mephistopheles slowly closed his eyes; his whole body bound to a wooden frame, his battle aura sealed by shackles. Well, in such a miserable era, death is also a kind of release. Mephistopheles comforted himself inwardly, yet suddenly felt heat on his face—splashed with demon blood! The execution demons on either side of Mephistopheles collapsed simultaneously, their heads cleanly severed by a mysterious force, the cuts smooth. Mephistopheles stared in terror at his side; a blond man with bandaged eyes appeared, his ruby‑like eyes eerily similar— “Human?” “No, I am a demon.”

title: Chapter 41 — Shortened Lifespan
content:
Chapter 41 — Shortened Lifespan

Volume 39 · Chapter 41

The demon?"

Mefistopheles widened his eyes in shock, showing no sign that Merlin looked anything like a demon. Instead, he seemed like an ignorant human who had disrespected the demon race's territory.

Merlin glanced at Mefistopheles and thought, "Is this my grandfather? He looks so young in the age of the gods, like a simpleton."

Banri Garan was pulled out slightly, and the sharp sword energy swept through, rescuing Mefistopheles from the execution frame.

"You! Who are you?"

"Call me the Seer, the one who has come to free you."

"Ah."

Mefistopheles was confused, feeling that Merlin was just rambling, and even though the demon race was bad, it was not their place to help the weaker human race.

Merlin didn't know how to explain to Mefistopheles, and he couldn't just openly reveal that he was his descendant. He could only pretend to be mysterious and scare Mefistopheles and the other demons.

"Who are you, you reckless thing? Dare you enter our demon territory? Hand him over!"

The scorpion demon angrily commanded, and his minions quickly surrounded Merlin with weapons.

Mefistopheles became tense, as he was in a bad state and couldn't handle too many scorpion demons.

"Run, you shouldn't have come to this place."

"Why run? I'm here to free you."

"What nonsense are you talking? Saying you're going to free us, who are you?"

"I am the Seer."

Merlin suddenly pulled out Banri Garan from his waist, and the violent sword energy cut all the approaching enemies into meat pulp!

Mefistopheles widened his eyes and stopped speaking, as he realized that the mysterious golden-haired human had an incomprehensible power!

Just from the sword techniques he had just shown, he was far stronger than Mefistopheles, almost like an unknown creature from a higher plane!

"Don't! Don't come!"

The scorpion demon, holding a seal demon bottle, was surprised and lost his arrogance, only thinking about how to save himself.

Unfortunately, Merlin was difficult to detect his true demon identity while wearing the bracelet.

In the state of not knowing, the scorpion demon's seal demon bottle had no effect on Merlin, the "human," and was pierced through the head by the blade.

Merlin picked up the seal demon bottle on the ground, weighed it, and smiled with deep meaning, thinking—

Is this the tool used by Behemoth to control the demons?

Finally, I have touched the real seal demon bottle.

After dealing with all the scorpion demons responsible for supervision, Merlin gathered all the original demons.

The original demons stood in a row below, waiting for Merlin to speak from above.

Merlin's performance of power made the demons submit, and in the absence of Behemoth, they naturally followed the stronger one.

Even after several millennia, this habit did not change, and the demon race was still a group that relied on strength and words.

Merlin turned his back on the crowd and thought deeply in his heart, preparing to say something like "The kings and nobles are all alike," to inspire the demons to bravely resist.

Mefistopheles was unsure, as he didn't know who the "Seer" was? This man who suddenly appeared, claiming to free the demons, seemed unreliable!

"Cough cough!"

Merlin lightly coughed twice, holding the seal demon bottle and slowly turned around, looking a bit like the God of Justice looking down on the monkeys in the Flowery Mountain?

"I know everyone is feeling uneasy right now, but don't worry, I am your companion and your guide!"

"You can call me the Seer, or Sultear, my purpose here is simple."

"That is the precious freedom, bringing it to you all!"

The demons looked at each other, unable to trust Merlin's words, suspecting that he was Behemoth in disguise, testing their loyalty.

The original Mammon held Belial and could not help but shout in protest, "Speaking these words with a human mouth has no persuasive power!"

The demon race's racial concept was very important, and even in the future, it was still a habit, believing that those who were not of the same race had different hearts.

"Tsk!" Merlin scoffed, taking off the bracelet, and his mouth also showed sharp fangs, "Do you believe me now?"

Feeling the surging demon energy, the demons fell into silence, encountering a human without horns on their heads for the first time!

"Is... is this a demon?"

Mefistopheles muttered to himself, thinking that this energy? It's a bit similar to Behemoth, is it my illusion?

"Behemoth is tyrannical and everyone wants to kill him!" Merlin paused and continued, "You are still thinking about helping him build a magnificent palace, will he let you go? Don't be naive! You will only be exhausted and die, and then become the food for those puppies!"

Mefistopheles clenched his fists, and this idea was the same as his, and he felt a great sense of identification with Merlin.

However, other demons, due to long-term oppression, could not be as brave as Mefistopheles in a short time.

"You have no way back, if Behemoth returns and finds that the supervisors are killed, you will die without a doubt, and if you see that the palace is not built as expected, you will also die, either way you will die, why not try to fight once and for all?"

"Good!" Mefistopheles was the first to respond to Merlin, stepping forward and encouraging, "We must resist to have a chance, what do we have to hesitate about? The Seer is right, he is the one who will save us!"

"Merlin thought to himself, well, I don't have such a great sense of mission.

"Seer, although I don't know where you come from, but I dare to say, you are the savior sent by fate to save the demon race! As long as you are willing to lead us, you will definitely lead the demon race to prosperity!"

As soon as the words fell, Mefistopheles "flapped" and knelt on the ground, burying his head in the sand, which was the highest form of respect.

"Please accept my loyalty, I will do anything for you, work hard for you!"

In the future, Mefistopheles will realize that kneeling for his grandson was a shameful thing, even though he didn't know how he felt at the time, but he must have felt like a stroke.

Merlin was shocked, and finally knew why his grandfather had a bad face when he saw him, and it was not without reason!

"Don't! Get up, don't do this, I don't like it!"

"No!" Mefistopheles bit his teeth, throwing away all his dignity, determined to follow Merlin to the end and do a great thing, "If you don't agree to my request, I won't get up!"

"Ah? ?"

Merlin's face turned black, his eyebrows were so tangled that he felt his life was decreasing rapidly—

Too many generations, too many generations!

Why is my grandfather so straightforward?

title: Chapter 42 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 42 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 39 · Chapter 42

"Get up, I accept," Merlin said, unable to refuse Mephisto. He thought to himself, having his own grandfather as a subordinate, he was indeed the first person to do so.

Mephisto's face lit up with joy, thinking about how to help Merlin pull the demon race out of the mire.

The other demons, seeing Mephisto submit, were somewhat moved.

Among the first-generation demons, this "eldest son of demons" had always had considerable influence.

However, the demons were still worried. One demon raised his hand, tentatively asking, "But... can we defeat Behemoth?"

"It's not a question of whether we can or not, it's that we must defeat Behemoth." Merlin saw the infant in the arms of the first-generation Mammon, so he stretched out his hand to take the child, loudly saying, "Look at the demon race's child, how weak! Can't even raise one of their own, what future is there to speak of? Oh, what's this child's name?"

"Belial."

Pfft! Merlin's whole body trembled, almost dropping the infant in his hands. "Belial?"

"Don't underestimate him, Prophet. Including me, only seven demons have inherited a large amount of demon god blood, and this child is one of them. His future is boundless." Mephisto kindly explained.

Merlin's expression was complex, thinking that in the era of the gods, Belial was so small? Completely unable to associate this little guy with that meticulous old man.

Infant Belial squirmed a few times in Merlin's arms, making a few cute humming sounds, his eyes still unable to open fully. This was one of the seven pillars of the demon race's future.

"Useless!" The first-generation Mammon stood up, saying seriously, "We can't kill Behemoth because we were all created by it. Its death would mean our lives would be lost along with it!"

"Yes, we are connected to Behemoth by blood. If we kill it, the entire demon race will perish." Mephisto lowered his head. Without resolving this key issue, it would be difficult to resist.

Merlin smiled, thinking that as the current holder of the law's power, dealing with Behemoth was as easy as turning his hand over.

Without hesitation, he said, "We don't need to kill Behemoth, but seal it, to buy precious time for the demon race's prosperity."

"As long as the demon race prospers to the second and third generations, the connection to Behemoth in their bloodline will greatly weaken."

"At that time, Behemoth's death will have a negligible impact on the demon race."

"Really?" Mephisto was shocked, lifting his head to ask, "But sealing a powerful ancient god is very difficult."

"Not difficult at all." Merlin paused, loudly telling the demons, "I need everyone's help to build a blood pool seal!"

"Best to complete it before Behemoth returns."

A few days later, rolling dark clouds came from the west, and a god with the upper body of a man and the lower body of a deer descended, stepping on the void. It was Behemoth.

It landed on the ground, discovering that there were no people around, and the half-built palace had been abandoned.

"What's going on? Did the demons ignore my orders?"

"Who?!"

Behemoth let out a loud roar, sensing a strange aura, and discovered Merlin standing on the broken wall, looking down at it.

"Welcome back, I've been waiting for you for a long time."

"Who are you?"

"I am the Prophet, also the leader of the demons."

Behemoth sneered, saying, "What are you? Wait, I don't remember creating you, demon."

"Your era is over, Behemoth. From today on, the demons have been freed by me. They are already free, and you have no right to control them anymore." Merlin said seriously.

"This isn't for you to decide. I am the creator of demons, possessing everything about them." Behemoth paused, narrowing his eyes to ask, "Who exactly are you? If you're a demon, I should remember you."

"I am the terminator of this era, also the one who will rescue the demons from your hands."

Merlin was hinting that he would fight Behemoth again in the future, but Behemoth couldn't hear these words now, thinking the other was a madman.

"It seems my palace isn't finished, and the disappearance of the other demons are all related to you. Although I don't know who you are, the cost of provoking me is very great."

"So what? Don't know if you're ready to sleep for several eras?"

"Looking for death!"

Behemoth's eyes gleamed with ferocity, and the ancient god's power surged instantly. His arm swung quickly, and a huge black fire snake descended from the sky, striking Merlin's head!

Boom! The sound was like thunder, and a mushroom cloud slowly rose. The magnificent half-built palace was reduced to dust in an instant!

Behemoth's eyelids twitched wildly. Just as he was about to confirm if the enemy was dead, he suddenly discovered Merlin had already appeared before him!

Merlin's right hand was clenched into a fist, with threads of gray destructive law power coiling around it, striking Behemoth's abdomen like lightning.

Behemoth's body stiffened, feeling his strength being instantly drained. He trembled and lowered his head.

He saw that his abdomen had been punched open by Merlin's fist!

Thick black blood dripped to the ground like snot.

Although this punch wouldn't kill him, it dealt considerable damage, rendering him unable to resist.

"Sleep, Behemoth!"

Merlin drew his sword, splitting the earth in two. Behemoth fell into the surging blood river below with a terrified expression!

Seven crimson pillars of light shot up from different directions, connecting to form a strange sealing array!

The entire ground was shaking nonstop, and fresh red blood began to gush from the earth, continuously devouring Behemoth's body.

A blood pool seal had been laid here long ago, waiting for Behemoth to fall into the trap.

Including himself, Mephisto had chosen seven demons with great potential, using a drop of their blood as the foundation to build seven blood pools.

These seven demons were the future first-generation seven demon kings. Their descendants needed to guard these seven important seals well.

When the twilight of the gods came, and the world tree was cut down, the complete earth would split, and these seven blood pools would scatter across the world.

No!!!

Accompanied by Behemoth's desperate scream, he was quickly swallowed by the endless blood pool, sinking into the bottom where time stopped flowing.

"We succeeded! We really succeeded! Our choice wasn't wrong. The Prophet gave us precious freedom!"

Mephisto emerged from the shadows, loudly announcing the result to the demons hiding below. His eyes burned with hope for the future.

He looked at the Prophet standing in the distance, his heart full of reverence, hoping he could become as strong as the other.

The blood pool rippled slightly. Merlin lowered his head, thinking to himself—

The demon race had been freed, and everything was completely consistent with historical records. He shouldn't have done anything wrong, right?

So next should be—

The elves!

3

title: Chapter 43 — Corelon
content:
Chapter 43 — Corelon

Volume 39 · Chapter 43

The elven territory was not far, located in the southern forests of the world.

Unlike other races that suffered oppression, the elves lived well.

The reason was that they had a benevolent and powerful leader, the Elven God Corelon.

When Corelon became known across the world, Odin had not yet obtained the power of the laws from the three goddesses, nor had he assembled Asgard.

But unlike Odin, Corelon never brutally exploited any race, instead following order and balance, advocating coexistence.

However, with the rise of Asgard, the balance was broken, and the world fell under Odin's rule, continuing to the present day.

When Odin was forming Asgard, he had once invited Corelon to join, but the Elven God refused.

In Corelon's heart, he despised Odin for breaking harmony and interfering too much in other races' affairs.

The elves, having a creator like Corelon, were arguably the luckiest race of the Age of Gods; other races either had cruel creators or lacked the strength to resist.

On this day, the elves formed their usual party to gather fruits in the forest, when suddenly they heard a beast's roar from beyond the forest—

"Roar!"—

A group of elven guards held spears, surrounding King Kong, trying to prevent the magical beast from entering the forest.

The elves were clearly frightened by this powerful magical beast, shivering as they stood in a line, refusing to retreat even half a step to protect their homeland.

"Quick! Go get more reinforcements—no matter what, we can't let this magical beast breach the forest!"

Within a short time, more and more elven guards arrived, shouting for King Kong to leave, but they were also afraid the beast might lose its reason in a rage.

Frustrated and blocked, King Kong furiously hammered the ground with its fists. If Merlin hadn't been holding it back, it would have flattened all the elven guards before it in an instant.

"It's okay, it's okay, calm down. We're not here to fight," Merlin said, sitting atop King Kong, stroking it, then speaking loudly to the elves below.

"I'm not here to cause trouble. Please inform your leader that the demon race's prophet wishes to see him!"

"Who are you? Lord Corelon is not someone you can just demand to see!"

"I have very important matters to discuss with him. Don't you fools delay something crucial!"

"Stop scaring us with threats. Get your pet to leave at once, or we won't be so polite!"

"It's not my pet; it's my friend."

Neither side would yield, and the standoff continued—

Merlin had gone to great lengths to arrive here; how could he just leave?

Seeing King Kong barely restraining its anger, a dignified voice suddenly echoed from above the forest.

"Are you friends come from the demon race? No need to stop him—let him in."

The speaker was none other than Corelon. The elves exchanged glances, and though somewhat unwilling, they made way.

Merlin frowned slightly, sensing something was off, wondering—

Strange? Does this Elven God know I'm coming?

Dealing with a benevolent ancient god like Corelon, Merlin employed a different strategy, much like with Maria—winning them over whenever possible.

Only ancient gods who were cruel and couldn't be persuaded would Merlin use violent means to eliminate directly.

Guided by the elven guards, Merlin arrived at the massive ancient tree, feeling an inexplicable sense of familiarity.

This was almost identical to the ancient god tree he had seen in the elven territory when heading to the Southern United Kingdom—perhaps a sacred relic passed down by the elven race.

After entering the holy tree palace within, Merlin saw the Elven God Corelon sitting on the throne, his expression turning somewhat startled, because Corelon's appearance was rather peculiar. He looked much like an elf, except for his eyes.

Inside those two pitch-black eyes grew four eyeballs? It appeared quite eerie!

"Everyone withdraw. We will speak privately," Corelon said in a commanding tone. The elven guards departed the palace, leaving the space for the two.

Merlin looked at Corelon on the throne, the transcendent aura emanating from him—nothing the future elven king could compare to.

"It's our first meeting, Lord Corelon. I am Surtur, the prophet of the demon race."

"Lying from the start? The demon race has no prophet. Show some sincerity, Mr. Merlin."

"What?!"

Merlin's eyes widened in shock, staring fixedly at Corelon, utterly speechless, his heart churning with turmoil—

Damn it! I never revealed my true name to anyone, not even Theresa!

How could this Elven God know my name and call it out so casually?

Have I done something wrong to cause this situation?

Merlin's expression was priceless. This Elven God had given him a wake-up call right from the start, leaving him flustered.

"No, you—"

The elven king slowly rose, walking down the steps step by step, speaking with an ambiguous tone.

"I knew you would come today, so I've been preparing for a long time. There's no need for that expression—I have a slight precognitive ability and can see some future events."

"Huh!" Merlin stared into the elven king's pupils, thinking—could this be similar to the elven king's precognitive dreams?

"However, I cannot see the complete future; I only see fragments of information, and I must deduce the results myself." Corelon paused, looking at Merlin and continuing, "I saw Odin fall beneath your blade, and I also saw the elves participating in the coming war!"

"Then I'll get straight to the point." Merlin exhaled deeply and asked directly, "I intend to destroy Asgard and free the world from Odin's rule, so I'm forming an alliance. Will you and your elves join?"

"And if I refuse? What will you do?" Corelon asked curiously.

"Then I have no choice but to resort to rough measures—seal you up and forcibly make the elves join the war," Merlin said without hesitation.

"I see. That does sound like the ways of a demon." Corelon nodded, not appearing angry.

"So, what is your decision?" Merlin questioned solemnly.

"I agree." Corelon nodded, speaking softly, "Since I have seen the future of the elves participating in the war, this is something that cannot be changed. My attitude cannot be altered."

"Agreed?" Merlin was somewhat startled, thinking—this is too easy? I spent so long preparing.

"The way Odin broke the balance has always been wrong. Although affairs outside the elves don't concern me, still..." Corelon hesitated, appearing to ponder, "the flames of war will eventually reach my forest."

"I enjoy conversing with intelligent people." Merlin agreed deeply, thinking it was truly the right choice to visit the elven race; with anyone else, many complications might have arisen.

Suddenly, a flash of light shot from Corelon's eyes, and a dangerous aura suddenly attacked.

Before Merlin could react, gray laws of destruction power materialized out of nowhere, stopping Corelon's attack!

"Is this the power of the laws?"

"What do you mean..."

Merlin's eyes showed menace. Everything that just happened was too fast; he hadn't had time to prepare.

If not for the protection of the laws, Merlin might have suffered considerable harm—it was very惊险.

"Nothing. I merely wanted to see if you truly had the power to defeat Odin. Now I have no doubts whatsoever. The one who can defeat Odin can only be you."

"What's with this?" Merlin frowned deeply, completely unable to read this Elven God.

"Mr. Merlin, I will assist you to the fullest." Corelon clasped his hands behind his back, brushing past Merlin, and walked directly out of the grand hall.

"Stay at my place for a while. I will gather all the leaders of the other races."

"And we will discuss the plans ahead together."

title: Chapter 44 — Obstacle
content:
Chapter 44 — Obstacle

Volume 39 · Chapter 44

Asgard, in the castle atop the World Tree.

Today, an extraordinary guest arrived. He stood卑微ly before the gods, like an inconspicuous mouse.

Satan had secretly left the human tribe and come alone to Asgard, wanting to tell Odin about the matter of the Demon Lord's prophet.

He hadn't harbored much hope, yet Odin uncharacteristically permitted Satan to enter the palace, which left him feeling overjoyed.

Odin had no interest in Satan, who was as tiny as an ant, but he was curious about the purpose of his visit.

Normally, trash like Satan, at the very bottom of the world, would never have the courage to dare come to Asgard.

Odin wanted to see what interesting thing the little one before him would bring to him and the other gods.

Trembling under the gaze of the gods, Satan didn't even dare to raise his head, kneeling respectfully on the ground with cold sweat pouring down.

This was his first time at the gods' palace. After witnessing the greatness of the gods, he became even more convinced that Merlin's plan would surely fail.

Maria had already sided with the prophet. She might drag all of humanity into disaster, and he certainly didn't want to die alongside her.

Plus, he was jealous that Merlin had won Theresa's favor. He dreamed of Merlin's death, which is why he had come here.

"O great gods, I am Satan, deputy officer of the human tribe."

"Satan?" Odin sat on his throne, lazily eyeing him, and quipped, "I've never heard your name. Sorry, there are too many bugs; I can't remember all their names."

The gods burst into contemptuous laughter, paying the future ruler of Hell no mind at all, treating him like a clown to pass the time.

Faced with the gods' mockery, Satan was drenched in cold sweat, not daring to utter a word, cowering like a dog tucking in its tail.

He struck out hard at Merlin, who had no backing, but appeared submissive and cowardly before the gods, his servility deeply rooted in his bones.

"Well, what is it you want? I'm in a good mood today, so I'll begrudgingly listen."

"I have something very important to tell you. Someone is conspiring to unite all races and overthrow your rule!"

The moment he finished speaking, silence fell over the temple, but it was immediately followed by bursts of roaring laughter, as if Satan had told a joke.

The gods of Asgard had ruled the world for far too long and were accustomed to their current way of life. How could they possibly believe such nonsense?

There was nowhere in the entire world that could find beings more powerful than them. Trying to overthrow them was nothing short of a dreamer's fantasy!

Satan confusedly raised his head and looked at the gods mocking him. Was his words really that ridiculous? Why wasn't he the least bit nervous?

"Among the countless boring bugs, you're relatively humorous. Interesting." Odin said with a smile.

"N-no..." Satan grew anxious and continued, "I'm not joking, it's all true. Asgard is in danger!"

"Fine, I'll just ask. You say someone wants to overthrow us? Who is it? Another nameless nobody?" Odin asked patiently.

"He calls himself the Demon Lord's prophet, named Surtr!" Satan declared loudly.

This time, the gathered gods fell silent once more, but they no longer mocked Satan. Instead, they all became serious and tense, as if realizing something.

Their earlier laziness vanished instantly. Odin straightened up quickly, his expression extremely grim, putting on an air of facing a formidable enemy as he demanded—

"Surtr?"

"Yes, that's the name."

Odin fell into a long silence, his eyes shifting continuously, sometimes uneasy, sometimes angry. The dusty reverence accumulated in his mind was suddenly jolted awake!

He was extremely sensitive to the name "Surtr." In the past, merely hearing it made him restless.

This was because after Odin donned the Crown of Destiny, the Three Goddesses had told him something resembling a prophecy, which weighed heavily on his mind:

"You wished for invincibility in battle, and no one in this world could match you. But if an outsider from another world appears, your wish will fail."

"The world is always changing; no rule exists eternally."

"The order you created will one day collapse, and the one who brings destruction is named Surtr."

These words were always etched in Odin's mind. He never dared forget that someone would destroy the order he had created, nor the name of that person—"Surtr."

However, prolonged ease had given Odin the illusion that the prophecy would never come to pass, that he could enjoy the wealth and power before him forever.

But once the name "Surtr" came from Satan's lips, Odin seemed to awaken from a pleasant dream, realizing the gravity of the situation.

"So it has finally come, another world's..."

Satan did not dare speak further, but seeing Odin's nervous reaction, he couldn't help but think: Was the king of gods feeling fear?

"You say he comes from the future?" Odin looked down at the tiny Satan.

"Yes, he said it with his own mouth!" Satan nodded repeatedly.

"The future? A jumper of time. Interesting."

Odin narrowed his single eye, wondering if the Norns had secretly done something. Otherwise, how could someone capable of interfering with time appear?

Odin slowly rose to his feet, suddenly radiating an aura that looked down upon all living beings, and shouted to all the gods.

"The twilight bell has rung! We no longer have time to play!"

"We must prepare in advance. Even if we fight to the last moment, we will protect Asgard!"

"We are supreme! Eternal and everlasting!"

The gods bore grave expressions and fell into a state of full alert. They already knew what was about to happen, and this would undoubtedly bring enormous obstacles to the coalition Merlin was forming.

"Satan, you have brought us important news. What reward do you desire?"

"I don't want any reward. I only wish for the Demon Lord's prophet to die!"

Several days later, in the secret conference room within the Sacred Tree Palace, leaders of various races had gathered.

Dwarves, fairies, giants, treants, merfolk, and others —

These were all important future members of the Southern United Kingdom, having forged deep friendships back in the era of the ancient gods.

Although they were ancient gods themselves, their strength paled in comparison to Corelon's, requiring the protection of the elf race.

Therefore, Corelon's influence was tremendous, and many tribes' ancient gods were willing to follow his words.

The leaders discussed among themselves, wondering what important matter Corelon had summoned them here to announce.

At that moment, Corelon walked in with Merlin, then paused silently before everyone and loudly announced—

"Please allow me to introduce a new friend first."

"This is the Demon Lord's prophet, Surtr."

"He is also the sole leader of our coalition!"

title: Chapter 45 — Integration
content:
Chapter 45 — Integration

Volume 39 · Chapter 45

"An alliance? What alliance?"

After hearing Corelon's explanation, every chief present was utterly baffled — they had never heard of such a thing.

Corelon had long expected their reaction and explained in a calm tone.

"Because this matter requires secrecy, I did not inform you all beforehand. From now on, we will form an alliance and declare war on Asgard."

The moment he finished speaking, an eerie silence fell over the meeting room. The chiefs' minds went blank for a moment.

In their understanding, Corelon would never do something so dangerous. Suddenly declaring war on Asgard was incomprehensible.

Taken aback, the chiefs below erupted into hushed murmurs, speculating about various possibilities, for declaring war on Asgard was tantamount to suicide.

"Corelon, you're not joking, are you?"

"No, I'm serious. My purpose today is to inform you all, and then return to prepare. We must overthrow Odin's tyrannical and ruthless rule."

Corelon spoke earnestly, hoping his allies would grasp the gravity of what lay ahead. Yet many chiefs disagreed and rose to object.

"Are you mad, Corelon? Provoking Asgard without caution will bring doom upon us all — it will only lead our clans to ruin!"

"Yes, you know precisely how powerful Odin is. Even if we somehow manage to resist Asgard's other gods, Odin is invincible!"

"Corelon, I know you are strong and kind-natured, but this decision cannot be yours alone. You must consult our opinions first."

Corelon paused, then spoke softly. "This is the result of my deep deliberation. The ambitions of those gods in Asgard grow ever more rampant. We cannot simply sit idle and wait for death. We must strike first, catch them off guard, and completely overturn the wretched order that exists today."

"After banding together, we barely managed to protect our own people. What more could you possibly want? Must we truly go all the way to destroy Asgard alongside ourselves?"

The God of the Dwarves bowed his head, unwilling to provoke such a powerful enemy. He was reasonably content with the current situation.

Though they were still oppressed by Asgard, things had improved greatly compared to before — at least they could now survive with relative safety.

All of this owed its existence to Corelon, who had taken the lead in rallying disparate races to form an alliance and offer the other clans a measure of protection.

Merlin secretly sighed. Indeed, comfort was the greatest enemy — slapped in the face and then handed a sweet treat, and everyone was satisfied.

Unless Asgard was eradicated completely, the world's history would never advance, forever trapped in the Age of the Gods.

"The tranquility we see now is only temporary. The alliance you formed can barely resist Asgard's suppression, but what about the future? As Asgard's influence continues to expand, will any balance remain?"

"Why is there a demon here? The demon race did not join the alliance — this is no place for demons!"

"Calm down, don't be so impulsive. I advise you all not to provoke Lord Prophet. If he wishes to kill you, there is nothing I can do to stop him."

Corelon spoke softly to soothe the chiefs. Noticing his companions harboring hostility toward Merlin, he felt compelled to set the record straight.

If Merlin were truly angered and flipped the table right then, nobody would leave this meeting room alive.

"Uh…"

Sweat pooled on the chiefs' brows. Even Corelon was speaking words devoid of conviction — just how terrifying was this golden-haired demon before them?

"Corelon, have you been kidnapped? If so, blink twice…"

"No, I fully agree with Lord Prophet's view. He is correct — the peace we enjoy is only temporary. Unless we completely shatter Asgard, we will eventually be enslaved again!"

"I know everyone fears failure in opposing Asgard, especially when facing the undefeated Odin. But we are no longer the same as before. With Lord Prophet willing to join us, we now have a chance to kill Odin."

Those words from Corelon detonated like a bomb, shattering the atmosphere in the meeting room. The chiefs sat up and demanded —

"Is it true? Can we defeat Odin?"

"Lord Prophet, could you show us that supreme power?"

Merlin sighed and extended a finger. Gray laws of destruction danced along his fingertip. It looked weak, but the pressure it brought upon them was immense.

"This… is the power of Laws. Aside from Odin, Lord Prophet also possesses it." Corelon's gaze swept across the chiefs as he said seriously, "This is our trump card. Only he can defeat Odin!"

The chiefs fell completely silent. After witnessing the power of Laws, no one raised further objections, and their gazes toward Merlin carried a new measure of reverence.

Seeing that everyone had reached an agreement, Corelon willingly yielded the seat, allowing Merlin to take the position of honor and oversee what came next.

"Now, Lord Prophet is the commander of the anti-Asgard alliance. All of you will follow his directives."

Merlin's gaze swept over the assembled leaders, and inwardly he felt somewhat awkward. Alliance commander? He had never done anything like this before. He needed to integrate all the clans and bring out their respective strengths —

"Cough!"

"Upon returning, you must prepare as quickly as possible. We will launch a surprise attack before those gods of Asgard have time to ready themselves."

"I have already successfully recruited humanity. When the war begins, humans and demons will both join the fight."

The chiefs murmured amongst themselves below, unable to resist asking.

"Aren't humans' combat capabilities too weak?"

"I'll find a way to ensure humans play a significant role in the war as well." Merlin paused, then asked tentatively, "Additionally, what can each of you provide for the surprise attack? Equipment, tools, food — all war resources must be submitted to the alliance for distribution."

"Our elf clan can provide numerous healing potions to ensure wounded soldiers can return to battle swiftly."

"Our goblin clan can supply a great many things, such as airships and magic cannons. Recently we've been researching weapons several times more powerful than magic cannons — tentatively called the Star Annihilator Cannon."

"The dwarf clan can supply vast quantities of weapons and armor. We can also concentrate our resources to forge a legendary weapon exclusively for Lord Commander, contributing our part to defeating Odin!"

A long time later, within the territory of the dragon clan.

Flocks of dragons soared through the skies above Black Mountain.

The dragon clan's situation was similar to the demons — they also had a cruel ruler.

However, the dragons' lives were somewhat better than the demons'.

The reason was that, compared to the brutal Behemoth, Nidhogg preferred conquering outside races.

This was also the result of the white dragon Aldra's constant guidance, who often told Nidhogg —

"The dragon kin all know of your greatness, yet outsiders know nothing of you. Why not try conquering them?"

Thus, Aldra successfully directed Nidhogg's fire of desire toward humanity, bringing temporary peace to their clan.

Rather than letting the black dragon Nidhogg torment his own kin day after day, it was better to instigate him to plague other races — at minimum, the dragon clan's interior would find tranquility.

The white dragon Aldra coiled uneasily atop the mountain peak, gazing restlessly toward the distance, wearing an anxious expression.

Strange — why hasn't Nidhogg returned yet?

Although I wish he would disappear forever, it's best that he not die out there.

Should he die, it could well bring catastrophic ruin upon the dragon clan.

title: Chapter 46 — Sudden
content:
Chapter 46 — Sudden

Volume 39 · Chapter 46

Just when the white dragon Alpha doubted, a series of wild ape roars came from the sky!

A black-furred beast fell from the sky, breaking into the dragon territory on its own.

Golden eyes glared angrily at the dragons, its nose emitting provocative grunts, its fists hammering its own chest violently, making a sound similar to war drums.

The two giant dragons on patrol discovered an intruder and let out deafening dragon roars, diving down from midair.

Golden opened its mouth, revealing sharp fangs, leaping up from the ground, one hand grabbing the necks of the two giant dragons, pressing them hard to the ground, unable to move.

Merlin slid down along Golden's arm to the ground, gazing at the white dragon Alpha enthroned on the black mountain, intending to drag the dragons into the resistance alliance.

The white dragon Alpha quickly rose up, staring at the two intruders with hostility, its brilliant light wings suddenly unfolding, and it demanded——

"Who are you? How dare you intrude on our territory!"

"I am the prophet of the demon race, Sulter, and I have something to talk about."

"Is that the attitude of wanting to talk about things?"

The white dragon Alpha bared its teeth in anger, showing some wariness toward the magical beast Golden behind Merlin, clearly not easy to deal with.

"Sorry, your clansmen are too arrogant. I can't help it; I had to force my way in."

Merlin had talked for a long time with the giant dragon on guard, but the other party simply refused to let him enter the territory, so he had no choice but to choose to force his way in.

"Ridiculous words! I see you don't put our dragon race in your eyes! You will pay the price for your recklessness!"

"Tsk!" Merlin was convinced, though he knew dragons were very arrogant, he didn't expect it to be so exaggerated. It was pretty much as he thought—dragons are the hardest race to reach consensus with——

"I'm not here to fight. Please calm down and listen to me."

"Now the demon race, humans, elves, and other races have formed the Anti-Asgard Alliance."

"So I want to ask—do you dragons have any interest?"

"Anti-Asgard?" The white dragon Alpha's gaze changed, and suddenly it laughed out loud, "You must be crazy!"

"No! We are serious. Once prepared, the alliance will launch a surprise attack on Asgard, completely destroying the order established by Odin." Merlin explained concisely.

The white dragon Alpha fell silent for a while, then coldly said, "Leave our territory. Here we don't welcome lunatics. Even if what you say is true, we won't join. Who would go to die with you? Who doesn't know Odin is invincible? Going against Asgard means only a dead end!"

"I can defeat Odin. Believe me." Merlin said seriously.

"My last warning—next, quickly take your pet and disappear from my sight!" The white dragon Alpha impatiently reprimanded.

"What if I don't?"

"Seeking death!"

The white dragon Alpha revealed a fierce light, opened its maw, and sprayed brilliant light toward Merlin!

Where the blinding dragon flame passed, white flames ignited everywhere, surging toward Merlin!

Only to see Merlin not even flinch, casually dispersing the dragon flame, feeling somewhat annoyed in his heart.

"Huh?!"

The white dragon Alpha was extremely surprised, thinking that no wonder it could tame such a powerful magical beast; it really has some skills!

Before Alpha could react, a massive gravity field assaulted it, pressing it heavily to the ground, fusing with the black mountain!

Under Merlin's gravity space, Alpha couldn't move, feeling as if its dragon bones were making "crackling" sounds, ready to break at any moment.

The white dragon Alpha lifted its head, seeing Merlin standing on its nose, a cold blade's edge pointing right before its eyes.

"Refusing to join is fine, then hand over all the dragon race's inheritance crystals."

"You!?" The white dragon Alpha stared wide-eyed in horror, this was an unparalleled humiliation.

"I want one thousand inheritance crystals. No matter what method, I must gather them all. Even if I dig out your clansmen's bodies from their graves one by one, or use living giant dragons as sacrifices." You, you shameless demon, do you want to steal our power?!"

"I am originally a demon. You have seven days. If you can't gather them, then the dragon race won't have any reason to exist in the future. You should understand my meaning, right?"

Two months later, the army was busy preparing for the upcoming war against Asgard, making adequate preparations.

The experiments of the supernova cannon had reached the final stage; it would change many histories, and the first use had opened the door to Asgard.

Large amounts of weapons and armor were forged and distributed to races willing to join the alliance.

Various war materials were continuously sent to various places, everything proceeding in secret.

Everyone thought Asgard didn't know about the surprise attack, but in reality, the development was gradually deviating from the original historical war.

War materials were sent to human tribes, and people were delighted, believing that as long as the war was victorious, a beautiful life would follow.

Teresa took a piece from a pile of dragon inheritance crystals, carefully examining it, and her heart was filled with joy.

After all, human power wasn't strong enough; their role in the war was limited.

But if they could obtain the dragon race's power and cultivate a batch of dragon fighters, then humans would also have the capital to fight against gods.

Teresa turned and ran toward the castle in the tribe, wanting to tell her sister Maria this good news as soon as possible.

In the room used for Maria's office in the castle, a heavy sigh suddenly sounded.

"Maria-sama, what's the matter? Your complexion looks somewhat ugly." Satan asked knowingly beside her.

"Something happened." Maria paused, worriedly saying, "Odysseus ordered me to go to Asgard to see him immediately. Although it hasn't been long since the last time we met, I really can't guess why he called me."

"Perhaps it's to tell a story?" Satan's gaze dodged.

"I'm afraid that's the case, too, Maria." Maria paused again, honestly saying, "Actually, my inspiration has dried up. I can't tell any fresh stories this time. I might die in Asgard, and my soul will be sealed in the Hall of Heroes."

What should I do!?" Satan feigned alarm, Odysseus suddenly summoning Maria, having nothing to do with him. "We can't lose you! If you're not here, what should we do?! Anyway, we have to overthrow those dog-born ones. Don't you have to go?"

"No, the army is still in the preparation stage. Because of me, Asgard's gods might get suspicious. If they detect something? Our efforts will be in vain, and then humans will lose their future." Maria sighed, seeming to have already prepared herself. "I called you over today to settle future matters. If I'm not here, you and Teresa will jointly lead the humans. You know, Teresa is not too mature yet; she needs your assistance."

"I will do my best."

Satan said sadly, but his heart was already overjoyed, thinking that without Maria, the human tribe would fall into his hands. The simple-minded Teresa wouldn't be able to match up to him. Now he not only got the power of the human tribe but also got to keep a beautiful woman—two benefits in one!

Outside the door, Teresa had a blank expression, having already heard Maria and Satan's conversation. She was uneasy, placing her hand on her chest—

What should I do?

The future of humans can't be without sister...

title: Chapter 47 — Convergence!
content:
Chapter 47 — Convergence!

Volume 39 · Chapter 47

The next day, Maria intended to take her final farewell with her younger sister, but found that Theresa was no longer within her domain. Only a letter remained in the room—

"Sis, I've decided to go to Asgard in your place. Humanity's future needs you. My wish can only be fulfilled by you—please lead humanity out of its oppressed plight and toward prosperity!"

After finishing the letter Theresa had left behind, Maria's face went pale in an instant. Her whole body began to tremble unconsciously, and her heart sank into an ice cellar.

No one cared more about this lovely, innocent sister than she did. She would rather die herself than let Theresa go in her place!

This situation had completely exceeded Maria's expectations, leaving her at a loss, as though she had suddenly lost something precious.

Without a doubt, Theresa's choice had thrown Maria into utter disarray, her mind going blank.

Panicked, Maria pushed open her door and rushed out, hoping to chase after Theresa, but ran right into Satan.

"Lady Maria? Wh-what's wrong?"

"Quick! Send people to chase after her!"

"What's going on?"

"Theresa—she went to Asgard in my place!"

"What!?"

Satan suddenly froze, a deep terror flashing in his eyes. He still cherished Theresa greatly and had no wish for her to die—

Why?

Why did things have to turn out this way?

Weren't all my plans ruined!?

Some time had already passed since Theresa headed to Asgard alone.

The rebellion alliance's war preparations were nearing their end, and the date for launching the planned surprise attack was drawing ever closer.

The God of Dwarves himself had crafted a divine tool for Merlin—a truly Mjolnir, pure silver-white in color and radiating a piercing aura!

Although the materials used to forge divine artifacts were already quite precious during the Age of Gods, they were relatively easier to come by compared to the future environment.

Especially ancient god souls—in this era where the weak were worse than dogs, finding a weakened ancient god was not difficult.

Compared to the semi-divine tool Falsely-Named Mjolnir forged by Master Balmung, the true god-slaying sword was far more powerful and durable!

Though they differed by only one tier, the gap was indeed like heaven and earth—

The true Mjolnir completely dwarfed the counterfeit in quality, even shining with a razor-edged brilliance several times over!

Merlin gently stroked the blade of Mjolnir, a look of fondness on his face. This was a major gain for him since entering the Age of Gods.

"Excellent. As befits the masterpiece of the Dwarven God, there are no flaws in any aspect. It's practically a perfect blade."

"This was specially prepared for you by the dwarves, serving as a token of appreciation from the盟主."

Coron stood nearby with a smile. He could see that Merlin was someone who dearly loved weapons, his eyes not once leaving the Mjolnir.

Merlin felt that the real Mjolnir was too perfect—comparable in quality to the Banri Garan after its release, perhaps even slightly superior—

So this is the second legendary blade of the Prophet? As history records, it ultimately ends up in my hands.

True divine artifacts all possess certain abilities. Besides nullifying healing and resurrection powers, this Mjolnir must also hold other abilities!

Much like Banri Garan, besides being able to steal the enemy's life force, it could also unleash a demonic fire comparable to the temperature of the sun—

Merlin's heart swelled with anticipation. He planned to try it out privately when no one was around. Perhaps Mjolnir came with powerful innate skills.

"Prophet, there is a visitor outside who wishes to see you." An elf guard came in to report.

Merlin suddenly paused, silently sheathing Mjolnir into its scabbard, wondering if another tribe had brought news of good tidings.

"Who?"

"The leader of the human race, the Goddess of Light, Maria."

"???"

Merlin furrowed his brow, unable to discern Maria's purpose. At this time, he and Maria were not enemies but allies.

Could it be because of the dragon lineage inheritance I sent over earlier?

Is this goddess here specifically to thank me?

Maria stood outside, haggard and as if her soul had been lost, her mind consumed entirely by Theresa, who had left alone.

She had tried to chase after Theresa but failed.

By now, Theresa had likely already arrived at Asgard, and matters had become unpredictable.

Theresa had decided to die in her sister's place; there was no way Maria would be foolish enough to go and throw her own life away as well.

But she still wanted to rescue her kind-hearted sister as quickly as possible, so she rushed to the elven territory overnight, seeking Merlin's help.

Under the current circumstances, the only one who could save Theresa was this suddenly appeared Demon Race prophet.
