"Maria, do you need something from me? If it's to say some words of thanks, forget it. Everything I've done is solely to succeed in toppling Asgard."

Merlin walked over unhurriedly, with Coron quietly following beside him.

This God of Elves was now the second-in-command of the alliance, assisting Merlin in handling various matters.

With Coron's help, everything proceeded very smoothly.

"It's not that. The thing I most dreaded has happened, so I—I'm asking you for help!" Maria turned around, her eyes full of unease.

"Hmm?" Merlin frowned, faintly sensing something was wrong, and asked seriously, "What happened? Has the alliance's plan been leaked?"

"No, it's about Theresa. She went to Asgard alone—for me!" Maria answered truthfully.

"Huh?" Merlin was taken aback, his heart giving a thud. "Why did she go to Asgard?"

Maria lowered her head, inwardly filled with self-reproach. If not for her, things might not have turned out this way.

So Maria told Merlin everything. She had a vague suspicion that her conversation with Satan that night had been overheard by Theresa.

"That's how it stands. Theresa went to Asgard alone to die in my place—for me."

After hearing this, Merlin was speechless. This sudden development had completely caught him off guard.

Up until now, he had been acting according to historical records. He didn't know whether the former prophet had encountered the same situation.

If Theresa was destined to die in the Age of Gods, was this the very event? Losing her life to save her older sister?

Reason was telling Merlin not to interfere, for this was Theresa's fate—her death would bring forth Alice.

But Merlin couldn't help recalling that Goddess of Luck who, fully aware of her destiny, accepted it with composure, and he could not simply stand by and do nothing.

Standing dumbfounded for a long while, Merlin suddenly clenched his fist and made up his mind to forget all of history and act according to his own will—

"Coron, prepare this—

"Have the alliance assemble and mobilize immediately!"

"Begin marching toward Asgard before sunset. Launch the surprise attack right away!"

Volume 39 · Chapter 48

Korylon's gaze shifted, and he quickly interceded, "It's not the right time yet."

"It doesn't matter, just hold off the other gods, and I'll handle Odin." Merlin replied coldly.

"This reckless decision will lead to the ruin of all our slaves. I hope you can remain calm and launch the attack only when everything is certain."

Korylon spoke seriously, believing Merlin's decision was incomplete and full of problems. He didn't want the alliance to fail. If they couldn't defeat Asgard, his people would be doomed!

To support Merlin's plan, all the races had staked their futures on him. Failure was unacceptable.

Korylon thought now wasn't the right time to attack Asgard. Everything needed to be ready.

"We don't have much time to wait. Rest assured, with me here, the surprise attack won't fail."

"Some soldiers haven't received the Dwarven equipment, and the Goblins' Star Destroyers are still in the experimental stage. The timing is not ripe, and there will be heavy casualties."

"War is about dying, just a matter of how many. As long as the result is good, it's fine." Merlin hesitated, then said in a threatening tone—

"Korylon, don't forget, I am the commander of the alliance. Even you must obey me."

Korylon narrowed his eyes, though he was dissatisfied, he had no argument.

"You're not fit to be a leader."

"Interestingly, many people say that."

The meticulously prepared alliance quickly gathered and moved toward Asgard's position.

The alliance's members came from various races, with a scale exceeding a million!

Even before the alliance's shadow appeared, Asgard felt a distant vibration.

This was the largest-scale war in history, with the goal of destroying Asgard and liberating all races.

For the alliance, this was a war with no retreat, and the outcome would determine the survival or extinction of their race.

Due to insufficient preparation, some soldiers lacked weapons and armor, and even healing potions were scarce.

However, Merlin couldn't care less. He had decided not to follow history and attempt to prevent Princess Therese's death.

After half a month of travel, the alliance reached Asgard's gates, where a tree far beyond imagination stood tall.

The World Tree, which bore the entire world, seemed like a pillar, supporting the sky and the earth.

Merlin gazed at it, seeing the World Tree alive for the first time, even more magnificent than when he first entered the God's Ruins.

"Merlin!" Mephistopheles approached, concerned, "My preparations don't seem sufficient. Is everything alright?"

"With me, don't worry, victory will be ours." Merlin replied seriously.

"I also believe that." Mephistopheles was encouraged and ordered the rear troops to speed up.

Merlin sighed in relief, thinking his grandfather was straightforward. He now somewhat understood his earlier surprise, admiring someone who would become his future grandson was difficult to accept.

Except for Merlin, the leaders of other races looked unhappy, as launching a surprise attack on Asgard without sufficient preparation was too risky.

Maria looked despondent, she didn't care about the alliance's success or failure, only wanting to save her beloved sister Therese quickly.

The alliance stopped, and before them was an impenetrable wall of light.

This was Asgard's defensive barrier to seal the end, and the gods' sanctuary, unbreakable!

"Are you ready?" Merlin asked the Goblin God beside him. In his memory, the entrance to the God's Ruins had a large hole, which was the first time the Star Destroyer was used to break through.

"Leave it to me!"

The small Goblin God jumped to the ground and took out a shining magic cube from his pouch, placing it in front of the alliance and ordering everyone to step back.

The shining magic cube continuously changed shapes, and under the swirling electric currents, a massive block cannon formed, pointing at the unbreakable barrier!

"This is the Star Destroyer."

Merlin examined it carefully. This later fell into France's hands and became a precious treasure of the kingdom. He was seeing it for the first time.

The Star Destroyer quickly charged, with the cannon body gradually lighting up in a staircase of pale blue light, finally converging at the muzzle—

Energy like the sun continuously shone, almost instantly draining the elements within a few kilometers!

This scale of magical weaponry was indeed unmatched by magical cannons, and it already demonstrated its formidable power before firing!

Even Merlin's forehead beaded with sweat, thinking that without the power of the laws to protect him, he might be injured by the Star Destroyer's attack.

Everyone watched the Star Destroyer, waiting for it to break open Asgard's gates.

However, an unexpected situation occurred.

The Star Destroyer charged for half a day, and just before firing, all the energy dissipated, leaving a black, lifeless block of iron.

"What's going on?" Merlin asked.

"Sure enough, it's malfunctioning again." The Goblin God scratched his head awkwardly, "In the final stages of the experiment, sudden shutdowns often occur. You're really in a hurry, Merlin. If we could have completed the experiment properly."

"I knew there would be problems in insufficient preparation, didn't I, Merlin?" Korylon questioned, his dissatisfaction mounting.

"What do you mean? It's just a surprise attack, what's your problem!" Maria snapped.

"I think Merlin isn't liberating the world, but is doing this recklessly for your sister." Korylon replied coldly.

You!? Maria suppressed her anger.

"Prioritizing personal feelings, how can you lead the alliance?" Korylon muttered, "We've staked our lives on this gamble, yet it's not even comparable to a human goddess's sister?"

Merlin watched the silent Star Destroyer, his eyes filled with unease, because of his choices, the future had already visibly changed.

The history of the Star Destroyer destroying Asgard's gates would disappear.

Moreover, since the Star Destroyer was an experimental model and not yet completed, France would not possess this national treasure, leading to the kingdom's downfall.

This was the butterfly effect—the past's small events would cause a storm in the future—

Is this the impact of my time-jumping?

My wrong choices have made future events unpredictable!

title: Chapter 49 — Twilight Descends
content:
Chapter 49 — Twilight Descends

Volume 39 · Chapter 49

Suddenly, rumbles like thunder shook the air—the light barrier used to defend against the outside world had opened on its own!?

This had never happened in history either; obviously, because of Merlin, many things had changed.

As the barrier opened, all members of the Alliance also saw clearly what was inside—

All the gods of Asgard had long been prepared, fully armed and waiting for the enemy to arrive!

The Alliance's plan to launch a surprise attack and catch the gods off guard was completely ruined.

Not only did it fail to achieve the element of surprise, but they had fallen right into the gods of Asgard's trap!

The Alliance hadn't been fully prepared to begin with; launching a premature attack against gods who had already received word and prepared in advance, they had almost no advantage whatsoever!

Everyone fell silent, knowing their chances of victory were very low, and couldn't help but regret joining this war that was impossible to win—the war.

Merlin stared in shock, widening his eyes, thinking: Was this also because he had gone against history, making a wrong decision and bringing this result? Already—

completely different from what history had recorded!

"Someone leaked our plan!"

Chris said angrily. The plan for the surprise attack had always been top secret, yet Asgard had prepared so quickly, waiting for them to walk into a trap—clearly someone had betrayed the Alliance!

Maria's expression was panicked; the result of losing the war was simple—the rebellious races would be exterminated, with no chance of a slow death even.

"There would be none."

"Who exactly betrayed us? If we fail, what benefit would he get?" Mephisto angrily scolded, unable to understand—that anyone would betray them when their interests were so tightly bound together.

Satan lowered his head nervously, swearing he'd never admit to leaking the information. Odin had promised him he'd spare humanity and execute Maria, making him the human leader.

and execute Maria, making him the human leader.

The god of thunder Thor of Asgard descended from the sky wielding his warhammer, swinging it to summon catastrophic lightning, sweeping across the densely packed Alliance forces—

"A rabble—how dare you challenge Asgard's order? Today you'll leave, but never return!

Alliance warriors' faces changed instantly; facing the imposing aura radiating from Odin's son, many felt the urge to retreat.

Thor's gaze was sharp; he thought smugly to himself—Sure enough, these guys looked imposing but were nothing to fear. I alone could defeat them.

Just as Thor was about to order the other gods to encircle them, he suddenly felt his neck go cold—before his eyes, the world began to spin and in a daze he saw his own headless corpse.

"Huh??? I—

Merlin wiped the blood off the demon sword Banri Garan. Thor's corpse crashed to the ground, instantly waking the terrified Alliance forces.

"If you're afraid of the gods of Asgard and want to retreat, then why did you join the rebellion in the first place?

Merlin looked angrily at the several Alliance leaders around him. They were in a desperate situation with their backs to the water—no retreat, no victory meant certain death. What was there to fear? So he shouted loudly—

"What are you afraid of! Is the old habit of slaves acting up again!?

"Why did we come here? To cut the throats of the gods!

"Look closely at the corpse of the god beneath my feet. They bleed just like you—what exactly is there to fear?!

The blood of Odin's son inspired the Alliance warriors present. After long oppression, they had grown accustomed to submitting to Asgard and kneeling.

If not for Merlin chopping off Thor's head and extinguishing Asgard's arrogance, this crowd might have gladly handed over their weapons and surrendered on the spot!

Chris saw the warriors gripping their weapons again, their eyes no longer showing any fear, and couldn't help thinking—

Although this guy was impulsive and emotional, he had to admit he was quite good at inspiring people.

It seems the Demon Lord's prophet is good at overturning old rules, but not at slowly managing things.

Not a perfect manager, but indeed an excellent pioneer.

Chris evaluated Merlin in his heart, realizing for the first time that he possessed qualities Chris lacked.

"Today is the day the gods welcome their twilight. Be happy about it. Always hiding in fear behind others—you'll never witness this history.

Merlin was shrouded in flames, entering a terrifying demonic form, baring his fangs as he grinned at the gods and let out a hysterical roar!

In his hand, Banri Garan turned pitch black, burning with extremely high-temperature demonic fire. As he twisted it slightly, it released a tsunami of flames toward the pale-faced gods!

Merlin's power completely crushed the gods. Under the augmentation of law-force, no matter how much they prepared, they couldn't change their fate of destruction—their fate—

Both sides entered a white-hot battle state. The Alliance, composed of various races, charged toward the gods who had once looked down on them with a charge!

Odin's messenger Valkyrie fought alongside the human-turned Dragon Warriors; their powers were very close.

The airships developed by goblins in the sky provided fire support from above, with their magi-cannons firing at full capacity!

New forces challenged the old era's order; flowing blood gathered into rivers.

The Alliance suffered heavy losses; fighting against well-prepared gods was indeed not easy.

But through Merlin's efforts, the scale of victory was forcibly tilted toward the Alliance, and the result became increasingly clear—

Merlin the Demon Lord darting through the front lines was like an emotionless machine harvesting lives. With every slash, dozens of gods fell.

Those gods struggling in the demonic fire finally realized that before Merlin, they were nothing but lambs waiting to be slaughtered—sheep.

After achieving a phased victory, the Alliance pursued relentlessly, deciding to charge straight to the top of the World Tree and destroy Odin's lair as well.

While most of the Alliance was still dealing with remnants in the rear, Merlin had already mounted the金刚 and began constantly climbing the World Tree!

This was a gorilla living in the forest, best at climbing trees. It never expected that one day it would run across the oldest World Tree, which made it very excited!

trees, which made it very excited!

However, the gods hadn't given up completely. They kept trying to stop Merlin from reaching the top of the World Tree, but all were killed by Merlin in his demonic form—dispatched by Merlin as easily as killing chickens.

Because he had killed too many ancient gods, Merlin could no longer feel the life force stolen by Banri Garan; it seemed to be reaching saturation?

The powerful enemies killed in this battle exceeded the total of Merlin's entire life. One can imagine how mad this feast of slaughter that rewrote history was!

How mad!

Vajra unfortunately had its eye injured by an ancient god and fell from the sky, but fortunately it wouldn't die from a fall of this height.

Merlin didn't have time to care about that. One slash pierced through this god's heart. Multiple pairs of black wings burst from his back, charging straight for the World Tree—the peak—

"Odin, your era of gods is over."

title: Chapter 50 — Duel at the Apex of the World
content:
Chapter 50 — Duel at the Apex of the World

Volume 39 · Chapter 50

Merlin dropped the ancient god's corpse and saw Odin's castle perched atop the World Tree.

Unlike the future's ruined and desolate appearance, the garden now was full of life.

The Hall of the Slain was not destroyed but stood at the center of the garden. Suddenly, a massive wave of resentment struck.

Merlin frowned, sensing a dangerous aura. He had asked Korylon about the Hall of the Slain, but the God of the Elves was also unaware. It was said to be a shrine for collecting the souls of powerful beings, built by Asgard to prepare for unknown dangers.

Suddenly, the Hall of the Slain began to shake violently. A large amount of black mud erupted from within, greedily devouring the ancient god who tried to escape.

The black mud seemed to have a mind of its own, showing a strong appetite for living beings, even its own creators.

The Hall of the Slain was originally built to counter the Gods' Twilight, collecting the souls of many powerful beings in the world to create monsters capable of killing "Surtur."

However, long-term peace gave Asgard a false sense of security, and the plan was gradually abandoned.

When Odin was startled again by the name "Surtur," it was too late. He could only release the half-finished creations of the Hall of the Slain.

The result was clear. The black mud, filled with immense resentment, was out of control and only wanted to devour more life.

Once freed, the black mud expanded rapidly, spreading outward. Countless eyes blinked, making people's skin crawl.

Merlin, in his demonic form, slightly frowned, recognizing the familiar aura of the black mud. He had encountered similar auras when entering the gods' ruins, where the lifeless stone statues that devoured life were present.

After consuming many gods, the black mud finally noticed Merlin floating in the sky. It formed a giant arm covered in eyes, greedily reaching for its prey.

Merlin scoffed and unsheathed his sword, slashing with Misteltainn, the blade that sealed all undead abilities, toward the troublesome black mud monster.

The sharp, killing sword energy swept through, instantly shredding the writhing black mud into clouds of black mist that lingered in the air unwilling to disperse.

Merlin was surprised, having killed the black mud monster, but its resentment could not be eliminated, swirling above the castle.

"Ah, so these resentments are the core?" Merlin thought. "In the future, statues will form in the castle, waiting for new prey."

Merlin couldn't eliminate the monster born from the Hall of the Slain, especially this intense, massive resentment, which couldn't be cleared by brute force.

However, this resentment itself didn't cause any real harm; it was just an unfinished product that would only become a threat once it solidified.

Merlin thought that launching a preemptive strike might not be a bad idea. If Asgard's research succeeded, it would create very formidable monster weapons.

The grand hall was now empty, with the gods having gone to confront the alliance. Only Odin remained.

Odin sat on his throne, looking out into the distance, as if he could see Merlin through the walls.

He remained calm, showing no signs of panic or the tension one might expect before the Gods' Twilight.

Odin had prepared for everything. If the Gods' Twilight was inevitable, he would fight for Asgard until the very end.

"What's the ending of the story about Deiphobe? Maria?"

Theresa looked down, holding her breath, not knowing what her sister Maria had told her.

To pretend to be Maria, Theresa stuffed pillows into her dress, making her look the same size as her sister.

"Are you deliberately delaying the time to wait for the alliance to come and save you?" Odin asked coldly.

"No." Theresa explained nervously.

"I already knew you weren't Maria, but her sister." Odin revealed the truth.

"Uh!" Theresa stared wide in shock, thinking she had hidden well.

"Your actions are touching, isn't that what family is?" Odin asked without any expression.

Theresa lowered her head, not knowing how to respond. The truth had been exposed, and she didn't know what fate awaited her. Perhaps, as the prophet had said, with the end of the gods' era, her life would also come to an end.

"Actually, I knew you would come here to replace your sister." Odin paused, saying coldly, "Theresa, you are also a pawn in my hands."

"!!?" Theresa looked up in surprise, not understanding what she had done wrong.

"Do you think my goal is to repel the alliance's bunch of amateurs?" Odin asked, looking down at Theresa. "No, what I care about is one thing: killing the demonic prophet Surtur." Odin whispered, "I heard many things from someone, including your close relationship with Surtur. So, I thought, if I captured you here, would Surtur lose his mind and come to save you without hesitation?"

Theresa's expression became uneasy, wondering if all this was Odin's trap. Using her to provoke Surtur, forcing the alliance to fight unprepared, and then luring Surtur here alone!

"Now everything is under my control." Odin's smile turned sinister, whispering, "Not only is the alliance suffering heavy losses, but the prophet is also rushing here to die. I should thank you, Theresa."

Theresa's expression fluctuated, wondering if traps had been set here, and all those dead gods were bait. They would do anything to kill Surtur. Odin had made up his mind from the beginning.

"He's coming. Let's welcome him properly."

As the words left his mouth, the sturdy castle walls collapsed, and a fierce wind blew. Theresa struggled to keep her eyes open.

Merlin, in his demonic form, unfurled his black wings and floated in the air, his terrifying gaze fixed on Odin sitting on the throne.

Theresa saw the terrifying demonic form of Merlin, her face pale. If it weren't for the same aura, she wouldn't dare recognize the monstrous demon in front of her, the man who had left the forest a long time ago!

"Finally here. Welcome, demonic prophet Surtur! I've been waiting for you for a long time."

Odin's face showed no fear, but rather excitement, standing up from his throne and looking eagerly at Merlin.

Merlin glanced at Theresa, relieved to see she was safe, and then coldly replied—

"I don't need a dying man to welcome me. Have you washed your neck clean, Odin?"

title: Chapter 51 — Gungnir
content:
Chapter 51 — Gungnir

Volume 39 · Chapter 51

"Whether someone dies here today is still uncertain. Do you really think you can defeat me?"

Odin remained calm, as if victory were already assured. Even though the gods had suffered heavy casualties, not a trace of panic showed on his face.

"You have become an obstacle to the forward flow of history. Even if I hadn't appeared, you would have died."

"Did those words come from the Norns?"

Merlin shook his head and replied calmly, "No, this is the choice of history. Nothing is eternal, including the order you have established."

"Ridiculous. If a second main god hadn't appeared alongside me, I would never have suffered fate's punishment." Odin paused, then continued, "So as long as you disappear, the order I have established will remain unshaken."

"Stop trying to defy fate. Your future destiny is already clear to me." Merlin stared into Odin's eyes and emphasized, "The order you have established has become a thing of the past. The future does not belong to your Asgard. You will become dust, erased completely from history."

"Then let me teach you that so-called fate can be changed."

Seated upon his throne, Odin slowly raised his left hand. Crimson-red laws of war began to surface, surging continuously along his fingertips. With a sudden grasp of his left hand, the laws of war exploded outward in a violent force, and in the blink of an eye, it pounced toward Merlin like a famished tiger.

The confrontation between main gods was far more primal, because the protection offered by their laws had lost its effectiveness.

To kill one's opponent, close-quarters combat and exchanging bloody strikes was the simplest and most effective approach. No need for fancy techniques.

Whoever possessed the stronger law would become the victor.

Merlin raised his finger, and the grey law of destruction dispersed Odin's force, but he detected that the opponent's law power was close to his own.

However, the law of destruction was renowned as the most powerful in terms of destructive force. While the law of war was also formidable, it fell slightly short compared to the law of destruction.

"The law of destruction?" Odin narrowed his single eye and remarked with感慨, "Your luck is extraordinary. You were granted the highest destructive power. No law can compare with the law of destruction in sheer destructive capability. So that's how it is. Surtur, you who were granted the law of destruction — perhaps you are the harbinger destined to bring Ragnarök to Asgard."

Merlin did not respond. In his heart, he had only ever sought to retrieve the real Mistilteinn and the spring water蕴含ing immense life force. He had never wanted to destroy Asgard.

But along the way, he had discovered that he was playing the role of a prophet in this age of the gods. To ensure the timeline followed the correct historical path, he had to destroy Asgard and set the stalled wheels of history rolling once more.

"Nevertheless, even with the strongest destructive power at your command, you still cannot change the outcome of your death here." Odin said with confidence.

The Demon God Merlin slowly descended to the ground and gestured to Teresa, "You go hide first. Don't interfere in what happens next."

Teresa didn't hesitate. She knew she would only hold Merlin back here, so she quickly found a corner to hide in and secretly watched the only two main gods in this world battle.

Odin had no intention of using Teresa as a hostage. As long as he could lure Merlin here alone, she had already lost her value as a pawn.

Grey runes surged continuously. Merlin infused the law of destruction into his own body, and what followed was a clash of laws, where ordinary attack methods would lose all effectiveness.

Odin rose from his throne into the air, mirroring Merlin's actions exactly — he also infused the law of war into himself. His emaciated body rapidly swelled, nearly cracking the armor upon him!

Veins bulged on his forehead, as though a writhing dragon were constantly moving through his blood vessels. Crimson lightning crackled across the muscles of his arms, and dark clouds were gathering above the castle.

Before the two had even collided head-on, the two laws — mutually exclusive like fire and water — were already affecting each other. A violent storm shattered every window in the castle!

Teresa, hiding in the corner, trembled uncontrollably. She couldn't even bear to watch, curling herself into a ball. The shockwaves from the law clash could very well kill her on the spot.

"You're a rookie who just learned to use laws. Let me teach you a lesson!"

The moment those words left his mouth, the dark cloud vortex outside the castle summoned a bolt of crimson lightning, which pierced through the dome and shot straight for Merlin!

Merlin's eyes narrowed sharply, and he drew his sword in one motion!

The law of destruction merged with his iaijutsu, and the demon flame radiating from Banri Garan turned grey, imbued with the power of destruction!

The razor-sharp blade slash, wrapped in destruction fire, cleaved the war lightning in two. The fierce collision erupted in an explosion, with thunder and fire shooting skyward!

Amid the storm of clashing thunder and fire, Odin's armor shattered, his body severely injured. A divine artifact-level defense was no match for the shockwave of a law clash.

"As expected of the law of destruction. Even a beginner can wield such destructive power within a short time. I truly underestimated you. But it's over!"

Odin extended his right hand, pointing at Merlin, his expression growing intense — as though he had already seen the path to certain victory.

"Do you know what I sensed from you the first time I saw you?"

"Hmm?" Merlin looked up in confusion.

"Gungnir, the Eternal Spear!" Odin's gaze locked firmly onto Merlin's eyes. "It is my strongest divine artifact, possessing unparalleled destructive power. Once thrown, it is an absolute kill!"

Merlin's heart skipped a beat. Sharp pain flooded his chest as the golden spike embedded in his heart, which had lain perfectly still, suddenly began to stir!

Under Odin's relentless summoning, the golden spike violently churned within Merlin's heart. The immense pain made Merlin gasp sharply. The demon god's form had to fade, reverting to his true appearance.

This agony was like a sharp blade hacking wildly inside his body. Merlin dropped to one knee, coughing up bright red blood. Cold sweat poured down his face as his body trembled involuntarily, his consciousness beginning to blur.

"Come back, my companion, Gungnir!"

Odin grasped at empty air. Merlin's body was instantly thrown backward, his chest glowing with golden light — and the spear pierced straight through his heart!

Hearing Merlin's agonized cries, Teresa quickly stood up, only to find a massive hole torn open in Merlin's chest!

Blood spread across the floor like a carpet beneath Merlin's knees, his posture resembling a puppet with its strings cut.

Odin looked at the golden spike in his hand and clenched it tightly, transforming it instantly into a gleaming spear, like holding a bolt of golden lightning —

"I don't know why Gungnir fell into your hands,"

"But placing my treasure inside your own body was incredibly foolish."

title: Chapter 52 — Sacrifice
content:
Chapter 52 — Sacrifice

Volume 39 · Chapter 52

“This is the price you pay for challenging order. I am the strongest god who has never known defeat. Even if you wield the supreme rule of destruction, you will still die here.”

Odin, spear Gungnir in hand, sneered down at Merlin’s increasingly cold corpse. He had always believed, deep down, that he remained undefeatable.

Merlin’s chest was bleeding, a gaping, horrific wound torn open by the eternal spear.

That spear, hailed throughout history as the mightiest divine artifact, had always been hidden deep within Merlin’s heart, becoming the curse he sought to escape.

Though Merlin had once benefited from the eternal spear and broken free of his own limits, it had now become his Achilles’ heel.

“Surtr!”

Teresa rushed out from the corner, kneeling beside Merlin and inspecting his wound. Her face went pale at the sight.

The injuries were too severe—healing magic could do nothing. To be precise, Merlin was already in a state of death. All his vital signs had vanished.

Teresa’s eyes grew frantic. If Merlin truly died, then no one could possibly defeat Odin. The world would only grow worse.

All the clans that had joined the campaign against Asgard would face Odin’s retribution, leaving no escape for anyone bold enough to defy order.

“Teresa, do you understand now? Who truly rules this world? How absurd your thoughts of rebellion are.” Odin remained perfectly calm, his words heavy with meaning. “Although I have always been oppressing the clans outside of Asgard, I still give you a chance to barely survive. Yet you fail to cherish it. Now, you have lost even that chance. I will kill everyone who dares to challenge me.”

“How could this be?”

Teresa leaned against Merlin’s shoulder, her expression one of utter despair. Tears streamed down her face.

She had thought she would be the one to die here. Who would have expected Surtr to be the one who perished?

She was beginning to doubt whether Merlin’s claim of coming from the future had been nothing more than a joke.

Teresa pressed her forehead against Merlin’s, trying to rouse even a flicker of consciousness—anything that might bring him back.

“Wake up, Surtr. You can’t die. So many people have placed their hopes in you. If you die, it won’t just be humanity— the elves and dwarves will be—”

“Hmm? Teresa, do you particularly favor this demon? As a goddess of humanity, you weep for a demon? Is this what you call love?”

Odin’s expression turned strange. As far as he knew, in this era, humans did not harbor particular hatred or disdain for demons. They merely kept them at arm’s length, ever vigilant.

“It’s not—” Teresa answered through gritted teeth. “I am not weeping for love. I weep because I have lost all hope for this world. As long as you still live, the world will never emerge from darkness.”

“Your attitude is unpleasant, but your words are not wrong.” Odin did not regard this powerless goddess as a threat. Instead, he spoke with casual ease. “Have you ever considered that while I oppress you, I also advance the world’s evolution?”

“What do you mean?” Teresa asked, confused.

“In my view, the original world was incomplete. The interdependent relationships between the various races were flawed. This would lead to our resource-scarce world being unable to sustain so many different races.” Odin paused before continuing slowly, “Therefore, a ruthless executioner was needed—one such as I, suppressing and eliminating the weak so that the world may evolve once more. This has been my eternal mission. You can see, under my rule, everyone can live comfortably, can’t you?”

“Ugh!” Teresa was startled by Odin’s ideology and retorted, “Only the people of Asgard live comfortably, what about those outside of Asgard?”

“That is none of my concern. The law of the jungle is the most fundamental natural order. Outside of Asgard, all are weak and insignificant races, and they ought to be extinguished. You humans are no exception. Compared to other races with their various talents, humans are far too mediocre—short-lived, physically frail, and naturally should be classified among those to be eliminated.” Odin became lost in his own grandeur, seeing himself as a savior rather than a tyrant, “I have protected this world and allowed it to evolve. Anyone who dares to challenge order is nothing more than a weakling’s dying howl.”

Teresa bowed her head. Odin’s words left her seeing no future. The humans she and her sister had created would likely face extinction, leaving behind only insignificant history, swallowed by the currents of time.

“What’s wrong with living happily together? Why must you destroy the balance?”

“Your thinking is too naive, Teresa. You and your kin have no value in living. You only burden this world. Only the superior gods of Asgard deserve to continue existing.”

Odin, immersed in his own self-congratulation, stood at the pinnacle of power, arrogantly imposing his will upon the world. He believed himself to be right, and that any weak life that still wished to survive was the one in the wrong.

The primordial chaos giant Ymir, in his mercy, sacrificed himself to create the new world. Every inch of land beneath his feet was precious—born from his blood and flesh. Did those weak lives truly deserve to enjoy such gifts?

Teresa ignored Odin’s words. She had already seen the truth: this king of gods only wanted those who submitted to him to survive. Those who resisted had no right to live.

By chance, Teresa noticed the Banri Garan lying on the ground, still unsheathed. She recalled what Merlin had once told her.

The Banri Garan possessed the ability to steal life and offer it to its wielder—a divine artifact that could extend the wielder’s own life!

Teresa’s eyes widened. She suddenly understood why she had fallen during Ragnarök. Perhaps this was all part of her fate.

If she did not revive Merlin, the world could never escape Odin’s rule. Humanity and the other races would be eliminated, with no future.

Teresa’s wish had always been simple: she hoped the oppressed humans could thrive.

For that—

She was willing to offer her own life!

“You will regret this. No matter what explanation you give, you cannot hide your brutality. Even the weakest lives have the right to survive.”

“Hmm? So what?”

Teresa picked up the Banri Garan from the ground, pressed it against her neck, and took a deep breath, recalling her past memories.

Driven by curiosity and loneliness, she had desperately begged her sister to create humanity.

Maria, doting on her only sister, fulfilled Teresa’s wish.

Yet the result was this. It was not what Teresa had wanted.

If they could not live in peace, then why had she created them in the first place?

Teresa saw this as her own sin—irresponsibly creating humanity, failing to let them experience happiness, instead subjecting them to suffering and torment.

“Oh? Choosing to die for love? Very well, I won’t have to lift a finger myself.”

“In the end, I still couldn’t see the future. How tragic.”

Teresa used the Banri Garan to cut her throat. Her life force was stolen and transferred to Merlin.

Odin watched the entire scene unfold with interest, completely unaware that the Harbinger of Destruction was about to awaken. By the time he realized it, it was too late.

Merlin’s chest wound, oozing blood, began to close rapidly. He suddenly opened his eyes, his pupils spinning wildly before finally erupting in a glow like polished rubies!

title: Chapter 53 — The Ultimate in Destructive Power
content:
Chapter 53 — The Ultimate in Destructive Power

Volume 39 · Chapter 53

"What's going on!?"

The storm of the Destruction Law continued to erupt, filling Odin with deep fear. The castle's roof was torn off, revealing a pitch-black starry sky.

Odin gritted his teeth, unable to endure the close-range impact of the Destruction Law any longer. He had no choice but to wield the Eternal Spear and quickly leap into the air to create distance.

What was happening? His heart should have been crushed, his life completely extinguished by now!

Why, why was he able to stand up again? This was completely beyond his expectations!

As Odin gazed at the Banri Garan that had severed Theresa's throat, he sensed something was off. This knife could steal life's information, something he had no idea about.

"Is that it?! So that knife has the ability to counter-feed its user!"

Odin was filled with regret. If he had known the situation earlier, he would never have watched Theresa use Banri Garan to commit suicide, causing all his plans to come to nothing!

The storm gradually dissipated. The hole in Merlin's chest had already healed. In her final moment, Theresa's entire life force had been stolen by Banri Garan.

The precious life was transferred to Merlin, reviving him from death. Banri Garan truly lived up to its reputation as a bizarre divine artifact that sustained itself through battle.

Merlin looked at Theresa's body lying in the blood pool, already growing cold, still tightly gripping the unsheathed Banri Garan.

He suddenly froze, his expression becoming extremely complex. In an instant, he understood what had happened. Theresa had chosen to sacrifice her own life to save him—

In the end, had nothing changed?

No matter how he interfered with Theresa's fate, she still ended up dead.

Perhaps from the start, he had been overthinking. No matter how he disrupted this timeline, the ultimate outcome would not change.

Everyone had their own destiny. Even if he had saved Theresa here, she might still die in the future for some reason.

Merlin slowly closed his eyes, thinking deeply in his heart. He realized that the rules of time jumping were not so fragile. Even if he made mistakes, nothing would change.

Just like Theresa, who lay dead before him, this kind and lively goddess of fortune. He had done his best to save her, but in the end, nothing had changed.

Merlin's feelings towards Theresa were complicated, with a hint of guilt, especially since her death was to pull him back from the brink of death.

"Sorry, I couldn't save you."

Merlin muttered softly, slowly lifting his head, his eyes gleaming with fury as he stared at Odin in the sky.

Odin narrowed his eyes, filled with vigilance. Now, nothing could suppress Merlin. He had lost his most important trump card.

"Do you hate me? She committed suicide, it has nothing to do with me."

"You say it has nothing to do with you?" Merlin clenched his fists, the veins on his forehead pulsing wildly. "You are the source of evil that hinders the progress of history. This world will never see the future as long as you live!"

"I know you're a time jumper from the future, but so what? The future you see isn't necessarily correct. Maybe letting the world remain under my rule forever is the right choice, and you? You're just a thief who jumps through time to interfere with fate!"

Odin angrily cursed, seeing Merlin as someone who didn't belong in the Era of Gods, forcibly changing the world's course.

"Odin, fate isn't as fragile as you think. It can't be changed just because you want to. Even if I didn't appear, the order you've established would eventually collapse."

"Nonsense! I am the invincible King of Gods! Fate will also fall under my iron hooves!"

As soon as he finished speaking, he raised the Eternal Spear, which emitted a dazzling golden light like lightning.

"Watch closely, as long as I kill you, I will have successfully defeated fate. Nothing is impossible for me to defeat, including fate!"

Merlin didn't speak, but silently watched Odin, who was almost frenzied. He thought that although Odin was invincible in this world, he wasn't originally from this world. This was a huge loophole in Odin's wish.

The power of the War Law surged violently, gathering on the Eternal Spear. The dark clouds in the night sky continued to churn, as if opening a door to another world.

A deafening explosion! A crimson war lightning struck the Eternal Spear, causing it to tremble. Even Odin's powerful strength couldn't suppress the fusion of the strongest divine artifact and the War Law.

Merlin took a deep breath, slowly assuming a sword-drawing stance. The Mistilteinn at his waist was ready, his cold gaze fixed on Odin in the sky.

An inexplicable airflow swirled around Merlin's body, like countless blades hidden within the "air."

Mistilteinn emitted a clear humming sound, as if playing a soothing melody.

Next, Merlin would fuse three powers: the sword-drawing technique, the Destruction Law, and the power inherent to the Mistilteinn divine artifact.

Since Merlin had only recently obtained Mistilteinn and hadn't tried the power of the god-slaying sword, he wasn't very familiar with this artifact.

However, the moment Merlin touched the true Mistilteinn, he could feel the immense power it contained, sharp enough to sever anything.

Mistilteinn continued to quiver, as if resisting Merlin's use. But this fierce resistance was forcibly suppressed.

Excellent divine artifacts possessed their own will, actively choosing their masters. Mistilteinn was one such artifact, needing to be tamed to become truly obedient.

"Feel the power of the strongest divine artifact!"

Odin's eyes blazed with crazy flames as he threw the Eternal Spear, which had gathered a massive amount of War Law, with all his might. The impact shook the sky.

The Eternal Spear's radiance illuminated the night sky at the World Tree's peak like daylight. Under its unparalleled power, even the stars began to fall.

This divine artifact, said to be capable of delivering a fatal blow, was being used to its limits in Odin's hands, especially with the War Law's enhancement. If Odin wished, combining the War Law with the Eternal Spear could destroy an entire world.

"Hah!"

Facing the heaven-destroying attack, Merlin calmly exhaled a turbid breath. His lone eye gleamed with a fierce light as he shouted, "Slash!!!"

The sword-drawing technique, Destruction Law, and Mistilteinn—three powers fused into one, forging the most powerful destructive force in history.

As Merlin's sword descended, space itself shattered and collapsed. The sky broke like a mirror into countless fragments.

The seemingly terrifying attack vanished without a trace after Merlin's slash.

Odin and everything in the surrounding area disappeared, leaving only a spatial rift emitting dimensional storms.

At this level of destructive power, it was no longer just about killing Odin, but erasing him from existence.

If the enemy and the world were like a pencil drawing, then the fusion of the three powers was like an eraser, wiping out everything in the area with a single swipe.

Merlin watched as the sky's rift slowly healed. Suddenly, a flash of golden light appeared, and the Eternal Spear Gungnir fell. He picked it up slowly, his heart filled with emptiness.

Even a mighty main god, standing at the pinnacle of another dimension, couldn't withstand a single slash.

title: Chapter 54 — The Wheels of History Turn Again
content:
Chapter 54 — The Wheels of History Turn Again

Volume 39 · Chapter 54

Merlin placed the Eternal Spear into his bosom and then turned to raise his sister's corpse.

As he pondered how to explain the situation to Maria, she arrived, accompanied by Satan and a group of humans strengthened by the dragon race's inheritance crystals.

When Maria saw her sister's lifeless body, her face turned pale, and she trembled slightly, standing in place. This meant she had lost her only family.

Satan hurried forward, and upon seeing the scene, he was equally shocked—though he had expected it, he had not anticipated that his sister, Theresa, would die in Asgard. Seeing her corpse, he felt a pang of regret, for he had never wished for her to die.

Satan looked around at the devastation and asked, "Where is Odin?"

"Eliminated," Merlin replied simply.

"???" Satan was stunned, unable to believe the truth. "You mean you killed Odin?"

"You don't understand what I'm saying? Odin has been eliminated, and the foundation of Asgard has collapsed. A new era has begun."

Merlin looked up and explained.

Excluding Maria and Satan, the others behind them all expressed joy, as the long-standing oppression had finally ended with Odin's fall!

Those who had participated in the anti-Asgard resistance had fought with the resolve of a last stand, believing that dying alongside the gods of Asgard was the best outcome. But no one could have anticipated that the seemingly hopeless resistance would succeed in defeating Odin and freeing the world from his rule.

People couldn't help but smile with genuine joy, filled with hope for the future. It seemed unlikely that many would remember Theresa, who had sacrificed herself for the world's future.

Satan's face darkened, as these events were not part of his plan. He had assumed that Merlin could not defeat Odin and would likely die here. But the current situation left him feeling helpless, as Odin—now dead—had brought the various factions back to a more balanced level, making it uncertain what would happen next.

This demon race was even stronger than Odin? This was completely unexpected, and everything he had planned had turned to nothing!

What should we do now? Should we continue serving Maria like dogs?

No! I won't accept that.

Maria did not notice Satan's gloomy expression, her gaze fixed on her sister's corpse. For her, the future of the world was unimportant. What mattered was her sister's happiness and well-being, to be with her forever.

With Theresa's death, Maria's faith shattered completely, leaving her feeling like a hollow shell, a mere puppet.

Maria ignored the people around her, who were still in a state of joy, and stiffly walked to her sister's side, kneeling down and gently touching her cold face.

"Why did my sister die from a sword wound?"

"To save me, she willingly gave up her life."

"Why would my sister do something like that? You two didn't even know each other for long, did you?"

"Theresa did it for the future of humanity. She hoped I would stand again and defeat Odin."

Merlin answered truthfully, without hiding anything. Theresa's death was his fault, so he felt no guilt.

"I'm sorry, Maria, for your sister."

"I don't need your apologies. Give me my sister back."

Maria picked up Theresa's corpse and turned to leave, without a single pause. Her heart was filled with hatred.

Merlin's lips moved silently, as he felt unable to speak. The guilt in his heart left him without an excuse, and he could not ease Maria's hatred.

Maria suddenly stopped, turning to look at Merlin, her gaze like a winter's chill, piercing his heart.

"You shouldn't have appeared before my sister, giving her hope and making her realize that the world could change. If you hadn't, Theresa wouldn't have left me."

Merlin was stunned, unable to argue. If he had not appeared, Theresa would have believed that the gods of Asgard were invincible, and the world would never change.

It was because of Merlin that Theresa saw the possibility of changing the world, leading her to sacrifice herself to fulfill her wish!

Merlin stood there in silence for a long time, and when he finally regained his composure, Maria and the others had already left, leaving him alone.

Though Merlin felt guilty about Theresa, he knew he had to move forward. He looked at the throne made of the Seal Stone by Odin.

He picked up a piece of torn cloth and, biting his finger, wrote in simple block characters:

"Don't look for any divine artifacts here, as most of them have perished with the ancient gods. Only a few remain."

"I advise you to leave quickly, as the ruins are more dangerous than you imagine."

"Be careful of the stone statues, as they are formed from resentment and are immortal."

"Remember, stare at them and don't blink."

Now that Merlin's heart curse had been lifted, he no longer needed to rely on near-death states to activate the Draw Sword technique.

With the power of the Destroyer God's form, he could freely use the Draw Sword technique.

The torment of the curse was finally over, and Merlin had fulfilled his initial wish. He felt no threat to his life.

Merlin had long since found a secluded paradise to live alone, free from all conflicts and troubles. But now, his thoughts had changed slightly—he no longer wished to live a peaceful, solitary life. Instead, he wanted to live with Alice and his beloved daughter, enjoying a happy family life.

Merlin found the passage to the top of the World Tree and successfully reached its roots, where he saw the vast life force of the spring, nourishing the giant tree that sustained the world.

After a careful investigation, he discovered the core of the Life Spring at the bottom—a crystal the size of a fingernail! Despite its small size, it emitted a life force far greater than the spring itself!

The vast Life Spring was born from this tiny crystal, and if he took it with him, he would carry away the entire Life Spring!

Merlin carefully placed the Life Crystal Core in his bosom. Once he returned it to the original timeline, Alice would be saved.

However, this was only one of the necessary conditions for her revival. He would also need to steal Alice's soul from Maria to complete all the requirements.

Merlin looked at the World Tree's roots, intertwined and connected to various places in the world, and took a deep breath. He wielded his sword and severed all the roots—

BOOM!

A massive explosion echoed through the sky, and the grand World Tree collapsed in a blood-red twilight, withering at an astonishing speed!

The end of the gods had come, and nothing was eternal. The once-arrogant gods could not escape the grasp of fate!

Without the World Tree's support, the land formed by the primordial giant Ymir also fractured, paving the way for a new era.

The old era's history was turned, and a new epoch began!

title: Chapter 55 — 5000-Word Chapter
content:
Chapter 55 — 5000-Word Chapter

Volume 39 · Chapter 55

With the coming of the Twilight of the Gods, most of the gods of Asgard had fallen, and the world once again returned to an era without any conflict.

However, this period of tranquility was destined to be short-lived. Greed is the nature of all species, as long as people's desires do not disappear, conflict will never end.

The fall of the World Tree caused the earth to split into four and five pieces, and the seven blood pools used to seal Behemoth were also scattered to different places.

Merlin returned to the demon race for a while, then prepared to say goodbye to the several original Demon Lords.

"What!? You're leaving?!"

The several original Demon Lords surrounded Merlin, shocked by this news. They hoped Merlin would stay forever, so that the demon race would have a strong reliance.

But Merlin had his own things to do, planning to go to the nearby Despair Canyon, hiding in a cave to enter a state of false death, waiting for his own world line.

"Yes, Asgard has been destroyed, and my mission has also ended. The demon race will need to rely on you to maintain it from now on."

"Ah???" Mephistopheles frowned, unwilling to accept this, "Why leave? It's good to stay here. We are willing to do anything for you!"

"I have very important things to do, and I must leave. I believe that the demon race, under your guidance, will have its own prosperous era." Merlin said meaningfully.

"What exactly is it?" Mephistopheles asked persistently.

"I can't say too much, so please don't ask too much."

Merlin smiled, thinking that if he didn't disappear but stayed with the demon race, it would cause great pressure on Maria, and the human era might never come. Maria might not create Theresa's soul container, fearing the era of demons, and her sister would suffer too much pain.

In other words, Merlin's existence would make Alice difficult to appear in this world line.

Maria needs to relax her vigilance and successfully open the human era, and Alice, as Theresa's soul container, would appear successfully.

"That's too bad, I thought you would stay forever." Mephistopheles sighed.

"You should trust your own abilities more. Relying on me too much is not a good thing." Merlin answered indifferently.

"You're right, but what about the blood pools that seal the Demon Lord? Should we just leave them alone? Is that okay?"

"Absolutely not. Find all the blood pools, build palaces on them, and guard the seals at all costs until you breed a new generation of demons. Only then can you successfully break free from the bloodline influence of the Demon God Mephistopheles." Merlin instructed seriously.

"I'll remember, I'll do my best to guard the seals." Mephistopheles nodded seriously.

Merlin looked at the original Demon Lords present, took a deep breath, and said slowly—

"I leave you with three prophecies. These things are destined to happen in the future, so you should be prepared."

"First, the mortal world will face a serious crisis, the danger comes from all sides. If the demon race wants to continue, the seven Demon Lord Palaces should unite, choose a place that is difficult to attack and defend, and avoid any conflicts unless absolutely necessary, otherwise, you will bring about your doom."

"Second, Behemoth will eventually escape the seal and lead the demon race to destruction. Mephistopheles' daughter will give birth to a boy, and he will completely end the gloom of the ancestors."

"Third, the boy in the prophecy will eventually choose to leave the demon race and live a quiet life alone."

After the three prophecies were finished, the several Demon Lords looked at each other, confused by these things.

With Merlin's strength to say these words, the Demon Lords naturally believed him and thought he had the power to see the future.

But Behemoth will still escape the seal, which made the Demon Lords extremely anxious, and their fear was already written on their faces.

"Behemoth will still come back to wreak havoc? What should we do? We can't even beat him!"

"Stay calm, don't be afraid. The demon race will not be destroyed because Behemoth escapes the seal. The boy in the prophecy, which is your grandson, will successfully kill it."

"Is that so? My grandson is so powerful?"

"Not much worse than me?"

"Won't be? I have such a powerful grandson?"

Merlin looked at Mephistopheles, who was a bit excited, and couldn't help but show an awkward smile, thinking that it was me, how could I not be powerful?

"By the way!" Mephistopheles became excited, asking, "You said you would have a daughter, how is she? Is she cute? Does she pout?"

"Ah? This..."

Merlin's forehead slid down layers of cold sweat, and he was speechless for a while, recalling his powerful mother.

Vivian was far from being cute, she was a self-centered woman.

But seeing Mephistopheles' hopeful expression, Merlin had to say a kind lie—

"Not bad? Ha"

Is it cute? It's like that."

At sunset, Merlin stroked the black fur of the golden just, asking Mephistopheles to come alone to send him off, refusing other demons to come along.

"Mephistopheles, I'm leaving, and I have one last thing to tell you."

"Please say."

"Take this as the family heirloom of the Lucifer family, even though I will leave, my influence will always be there. It can be used to govern the demons, and if there is any internal conflict in the demon race, bring it out, and all demons will once again remember me."

Merlin took off the Banri Garan from his waist and handed it to Mephistopheles. In the future, this sword will fall into the hands of Merlin in this world line, which is also an important seed.

Mephistopheles looked at the Banri Garan in his hand and saw it release demon fire comparable to the temperature of the sun, burning the powerful gods to ashes. The value of this sword was unimaginable!

"No! I can't accept it! It's too valuable!"

"It's okay, it's not for you to use. You can't pull it out, and the one who can freely use this sword is undoubtedly the strongest demon that can match me. Remember this."

"Okay, I'll remember, I'll carefully look for its owner."

Seeing Mephistopheles respond very seriously, Merlin finally relaxed a bit and turned to leave with the golden just to the Despair Canyon.

"Wait!"

"What's the matter? Is there anything else?"

"Can you grant me a small wish?"

Merlin was puzzled in his heart and asked patiently, "What is it?"

"Can I challenge you once?"

"Challenge?"

"I know my thoughts are a bit arrogant, challenging you is like looking for death." Mephistopheles lowered his head, nervously continued, "But I also have the pride of a swordsman. Before I met you, I was very confident in my swordsmanship, but after meeting you, I saw what the strongest swordsmanship is. So I want to challenge you once, to see how big the gap is between us, and whether I have a chance to catch up with you. Isn't a swordsman supposed to constantly challenge strong enemies to make themselves go further, isn't it?"

Merlin's expression became complex, thought for a while, and asked, "Are you serious?"

"Yes! I'm serious! I hope you can help me, otherwise, it will become a regret that I can't forget in my life!" Mephistopheles' face turned red, looking very excited.

"Challenging me, you don't fear death?" Merlin asked curiously.

"Fear! As a penalty for failure, I beg you to only cut off one of my arms." Mephistopheles said shamelessly.

Merlin hesitated for a while, thinking that this matter was a bit troublesome, and then nodded and answered—

"Yes, but our challenge is not now."

"We will meet again in the future, and then there will be an opportunity."

"Believe me, you won't leave any regrets."

Despair Canyon.

The sound of a huge explosion, Merlin, according to his memory, let the golden just punch out a cave in the same place, as the next place for false death.

Merlin slid off the golden just's shoulder, looked at the cave and thought it was the right size, turned and smiled.

"It's okay, golden just, I hope you stay here to live until a boy with the Banri Garan appears. Remember to lead him to me."

"Growl?" The golden just scratched its head, remembered Merlin's words, and nodded in response, "Growl growl!"

Merlin turned and walked into the cave, put on a black cloak made of leather, found the deepest place to sit down, and then slowly closed his eyes.

Time passed by, and many things happened in this world, and the situation kept changing.

After the destruction of Asgard, the elves rose under the leadership of Corellon, and the world entered the second era, the era of elves.

Corellon promoted balance and order, and the various races did not interfere with each other, with peace as the primary goal.

The world entered a relatively peaceful era, and the various races also no longer suffered from oppression.

Unfortunately, Corellon died after being fatally injured in the fight against the gods, and the era of elves ended.

The world entered a short period of no rules and order until the demon race led by Mephistopheles rose.

The several original Demon Lords worked hard and struggled for countless years, and finally became god-level strong, and in the era of ancient gods fading, they seized the power of speech, and the world entered the third era, the era of demons.

The demon race advocated violence, liked the system of eliminating the weak, and Mephistopheles took the demons as the first principle, building a previously prosperous demon city, which flourished for a time.

To break free from the bloodline of Behemoth, the demon race began to encourage reproduction, and the number of demons reached its peak in this period.

The demons of the third era could walk freely on the continent, and the status of demons was also higher than other races, and they regarded other races as livestock and garbage.

Although other races lived in the demon era, they were not as miserable as in the era of gods, but the evil deeds done by the demons still put great pressure on the weak human race.

Until Maria and Satan, like Odin, found the natural sage stone and wore the crown of destiny that changes the rules, the human race finally had a beautiful comeback.

Maria created the holy race, launched a holy war on the demons, killing countless demons, and used extremely bloody and brutal means to end the demon era, fulfilling the wish of her sister Theresa, who was willing to sacrifice her life to achieve it.

The fourth era, the era of humans, came.

"Hey! Who are you?! You're hiding here mysteriously, and you don't look like a demon either. This should be the territory of the demon race, and outsiders are not allowed to appear here!"

The sound of a somewhat immature voice echoed in the cave, and Merlin suddenly woke up from his state of false death, seeing the young, anxious, confused, and helpless version of himself.

Several eras have passed, and Merlin has been completely outside, and many people think he has disappeared or died, but they don't know that he has been sitting in the cave, motionless, entering a state of false death.

Although he is a main god, he is almost impossible to be injured, but long-term sitting has almost made his body fuse with the rock, and his beard and hair have fallen to the ground like a carpet.

Merlin watched the past version of himself, and his heart was full of mixed emotions. He has been looking for the wicked man who gave him a curse, and it turns out to be himself. How ridiculous?

"Uh! What is it!? Don't play hide and seek, stand up and pull back your hair, let me see if you're a ghost or a person!"

Merlin paid no attention, stepped forward in front of the young man, and the young Merlin was startled, drew a knife from his back and stabbed it fiercely.

"Die!!!"

Merlin found it very easy to deal with the past version of himself, and he suffocated the young Merlin and slammed him against the wall.

"Uh! It hurts! Let me go!"

"My time is almost up, what I'm going to say to you is very important, listen carefully." Merlin stared at the young Merlin's eyes and said seriously—

"Your power is real, but the conditions for you to freely control it are extremely harsh."

"One is to obtain the god's form and become the controller of the world's rules, and the other is to put yourself in a state of near death."

"If you meet one of the two conditions, you can use the power that has been suppressed."

"This thing can help you always be in a state of near death, although it will constantly torment you, but it is indispensable for you at the moment."

"Remember, never waver in your initial thoughts. Only cowards hesitate, and some people's sacrifices are the necessary outcome of fate. You can't change it."

The eternal spear Gungnir was stabbed into the past Merlin's body by Merlin, and the young Merlin was stunned, staring wide-eyed, and the pain was so great that his soul seemed to be torn apart.

After doing these things, Merlin took a deep breath, and thus he finally completed all his missions.

Merlin drew Misty from his waist and cut off the long hair and messy beard, then whispered—

"The Three Fates, my journey has ended, let me go back."

As soon as the words fell, a time-space tunnel appeared in front of Merlin, leading to his world line and time. As he left, he looked back at the young Merlin on the ground for a moment and said warmly.

"Good luck, your story has just begun."

Drip, water droplets splashed on the damp rock.

The young Merlin woke up from unconsciousness, feeling like he had been shocked by high voltage, and was in unbearable pain.

He recalled what happened before he fell unconscious and quickly stood up, checking his body.

"What is this?!!"

The young Merlin let out a piercing scream, looking down at his chest, stunned by what he saw. He saw—

A fist-sized scar appeared in the position of the heart, the blood had just solidified into clots, and a mysterious power was constantly flowing towards the heart, and the breath was quickly condensed.

Numerous blood vessels appeared on the young Merlin's body, connecting to the scar in the heart, looking like a red spider web.

The young Merlin was greatly shocked, shivering all over, thinking he should have died, but why can he wake up with a hole in his heart?

Pang pang—

The injured heart beat, accompanied by pain that ordinary people couldn't imagine, and the soul had a feeling of being torn apart.

The young Merlin was pale, covering his heart and bending down, and cold sweat "splat" fell, and he was in great pain, twitching all over his body.

"What's going on?"

The young Merlin was in great pain, lying on the ground, and the great pain from his heart made him believe that he would die at any moment.

He didn't doubt that if his body hadn't been strengthened, he might have been painfully killed here.

The young Merlin clenched his fists, gritted his teeth, and wanted to find the golden just for help.

But just as he stood up and didn't walk a few steps, his body was pierced again by a golden spear.

The young Merlin was stunned—he was numb to pain, and he turned in terror, seeing a handsome young man, unfortunately, a one-eyed man wearing an eyepatch.

The golden spear in his hand was similar to the golden spear that had pierced his heart before, but it looked like a sharp golden lightning now.

"Die, don't jump through time again to break the order I have established. Everything should end here." The handsome young man said.

The man paused, letting out a sigh as he spoke. "I have to admit, substitutes are truly useful. I actually managed to fool the future you. Thanks to the intelligence Satan provided me, I had ample time to prepare a substitute to carry out this deception. Everyone believed I was killed by the Prophet. How amusing, hahaha."

So the handsome man was Odin—rather, this was his true form. The aged appearance was merely a deceptive illusion meant to fool the world!

As a chief god, the moment he donned the Crown of Destiny, his youthful visage had been forever frozen.

Odin knew that changing Asgard's destined destruction would be difficult, but rewriting his own fate might still be possible. Thus, he secretly created clones among the gods, seeking a way to escape with his life intact.

Like Merlin, Odin had similarly concealed his identity across several epochs, living as an ordinary person in various forms, blending into every race and faction.

Odin did not intend to let the Prophet—who had ruined his lifelong achievements—escape unpunished. He wanted that person to pay a heavy price and altered his own fate accordingly. He had planned this for a long time and ultimately found a method to defeat Merlin.

"Goodbye. If you have anyone to blame, blame yourself."

Odin drew forth the Eternal Spear Gungnir. The young Merlin's corpse collapsed to the ground, his dying expression still filled with bewilderment and terror. He probably never expected to die in an unfamiliar cave.

Immediately after, Odin beckoned, and the Gungnir from within the young Merlin's heart flew into his hand. Gazing at the two Gungnirs in his palms, he smiled with satisfaction.

"One belongs to me, and one belongs to another timeline. Perfect."

Odin turned and walked to where the Prophet had just been. Raising the Eternal Spear, he appeared to search for some trace or clue. Suddenly, his eyes lit up!

Odin thrust the long spear forcefully forward into empty air, then twisted it slightly. The temporal tunnel the Prophet had just departed through was forcibly opened once more.

"So this is it? Indeed as I suspected—jumping through time leaves behind a fissure in the spacetime continuum."

"Thinking about it, entering here should lead me straight to an old friend of mine, wouldn't you say?"

"Fates of the Norns, you three said my fate would lead to death. Then I shall rewrite fate before your very eyes!"

After Odin had entered the temporal tunnel for quite some time, the young Merlin's corpse on the ground—originally cold—should have lost all signs of life. Yet—

His right ring finger trembled ever so slightly.

To Be Continued

title: Chapter 1 — The Prophet Returns
content:
Chapter 1 — The Prophet Returns

Volume 40 · Chapter 1

Merlin slowly opened his eyes and once again found himself in the realm of fate, where he saw the aged Fate Three Goddesses.

According to the wish, Merlin's request was to return to a period in the past, though this time span seemed quite lengthy.

"Welcome back, Merlin Lucipher."

The Three Goddesses looked at the small Merlin, as if they knew everything, possibly having seen Merlin from different worldlines many times.

Merlin looked up at the Three Goddesses, thinking that now he had obtained the core of the Fountain of Life and possessed the true Mistletoe Heart. The curse on his heart had also been lifted, so next he should retrieve Alice's soul.

"Are we now to call you Lucifer the Third, or the Great Seer of the Demon Race?"

"Hmm?"

Merlin frowned, feeling that the Fate Three Goddesses were mocking him, which made him somewhat uncomfortable.

"It's all right, it's just a title."

"Congratulations on obtaining what you wanted and becoming the Destroyer of the Law, the God of Destruction."

"I'm not interested in these things. Tell me, how much time has passed outside?"

Merlin was worried that he had stayed too long in the past of other worldlines, and the outside world might have undergone earth-shattering changes, making it too late to save Alice.

"Don't worry, the rules of the realm of fate are completely different from the outside world. Time here is stationary, even though you lived for a long time in the past, it won't affect anything in your worldline. In our eyes, you only disappeared for a few seconds."

"Only a few seconds?"

Merlin was stunned, feeling somewhat incredible. He could have lived through several eras in the past, yet the realm of fate had only passed a few seconds.

According to the Three Goddesses' explanation, the realm of fate has no concept of time, it is a bizarre realm that is detached from the world's rules.

"So, when I leave the realm of fate, I will return to the correct time point?"

"That's right."

"I see."

Merlin slightly relaxed, thinking that there was nothing to fear. After leaving the realm of fate, Alice's soul in the heavens should be fine.

Because after entering the realm of fate, from Merlin's perspective, the time in his worldline had entered a paused state.

"I have a question I would like to ask."

"As long as it doesn't violate the rules, we can answer."

"Did I see myself in the past? Is there a realm of fate in every worldline, and are there many of you?"

"No, the realm of fate is unique. It exists at the center where countless worldlines intersect, as an independent region. Everyone who wears the Crown of Fate in each worldline will come to us. That is to say, Merlin Lucipher, we have actually seen you many times, even though there are countless worldlines, and the same person exists in each world, only six can reach here, and you are one of them."

"That's the case?"

Merlin looked down, feeling a bit chilled, thinking that in different worldlines, I will also come here to see the Fate Three Goddesses. Will their experiences be exactly the same as mine? Or will there be some differences in their personalities?

However, it can be certain that no matter how many worldlines there are, those who leave their names on the Crown of Fate will always be six: Odin, Maria, Satan, Lochlann, Alice, and Merlin.

Merlin left the realm of fate and returned to Leonardo da Vinci's alchemy basement, where the mist behind him slowly dissipated.

Leonardo da Vinci and Flamel, who were creating alchemy hounds beside him, were looking at the alchemy notes burning in the fire.

Merlin returned just as Leonardo da Vinci's alchemy notes had finished burning.

This proved that the Fate Goddess was correct. After Merlin left, his worldline was in a paused state and would not affect anything.

"Hmm?" Leonardo da Vinci saw Merlin return, startled. "Mr. Merlin, how did you return so quickly? You just entered the realm of fate not long ago."

Merlin looked embarrassed, not knowing how to explain the rules of the realm of fate to Leonardo da Vinci, and could only simply answer, "Time is stationary in the realm, so I actually spent a very long time inside."

Merlin did not mention the fact that he had influenced the future by going back in time, as it had nothing to do with Leonardo da Vinci, and it was also very complicated to explain.

In the human era, the influence of the Demon Race Seer had already weakened, and only those who liked to study history were interested in the Seer.

"Time is stationary in the realm?" Leonardo da Vinci looked in disbelief, as if he had discovered a domain that had never been explored. "It's a pity I couldn't go in and see it for myself. You know, your eye is..."

Merlin touched his missing eye, answering meaningfully, "This is a long story. In short, if you want to make a wish, you can't just have the Philosopher's Stone, you also need to sacrifice one of your eyes. The Philosopher's Stone can offset the cost of life."

"Originally, the rules of the Crown of Fate were like this. I have read many books about the Fate Three Goddesses, but there was no description." Leonardo da Vinci looked thoughtful, suddenly realizing that this was not important. "By the way, have you found a way to bring Alice Miss back to life?"

Merlin nodded and answered, "Although it's not possible to bring someone back from the dead directly, I have a good chance of success. However, I still need to plan carefully."

"Good luck, Mr. Merlin, please bring Alice Miss back safely."

After Merlin left, the realm of fate once again fell into a state of dead silence, with the gears turning slowly without any life. The Three Goddesses also sat silently on their stone thrones, like they had entered a state of hibernation.

Suddenly, a crack opened in the dark depths of the realm of fate, causing the entire realm to tremble violently!

The great commotion woke up the Three Goddesses, who all looked up at the sky, sensing that something was wrong. The stable realm of fate had never experienced such a huge disturbance before. This proved that the vast network of intersecting worldlines had suffered a serious malfunction!

"Someone is trying to break the shackles of fate and interfere with the fates of different worldlines. According to the rules of fate, this is almost impossible. It's extremely foolish behavior."

"We are the agents of fate, but such a situation has never occurred before. Could it be that we also have the shackles of fate?"

Odin, the young one, passed through the layers of obstacles and directly arrived in the realm of fate, landing gracefully before the Three Goddesses, with a meaningful smile on his face.

"Long time no see, my old friends."

title: Chapter 2 — Becoming a Player
content:
Chapter 2 — Becoming a Player

Volume 40 · Chapter 2

"Odin? You're not supposed to be dead? Why are you appearing here?"

The three Norn sisters looked down at Odin, seeing his state was completely unlike how he was before becoming a chief god.

This was an unimaginable situation for the three sisters, because it had never happened before—the Odin who became chief god built Asgard and was killed by Merlin, absolutely impossible to come to the Fate Secret Realm a second time!

"Because before Asgard was destroyed, I knew in advance that the prophet came from the future, and with a little thought I understood what happened." Odin paused, staring directly at the three giant goddesses, and said coldly, "A person who can freely jump between worldlines and time—surely you helped them, right?"

The three Norn sisters fell silent, not knowing how to handle this sudden situation. Since they appeared, everything had been repeated countless times.

But now the stable cycle was broken—Odin not only didn't die, but came to the Fate Secret Realm a second time. This clearly broke the rules of the realm.

"That's right, we helped the prophet jump worldlines and time—this is the will of Fate."

"What bullshit Fate!" Odin was no longer calm, screaming, "You guided me to gain the power of laws, letting me break the world's balance and establish the prosperous Asgard, but in the end you still wanted to destroy me!?"

"Odin, calm down. Everything is Fate. Before you wore the crown, we had already warned you—the gods would face Ragnarök, nothing is eternal, and your fate would ultimately go toward death."

"Would I believe your ghost stories?" Odin pointed at himself and continued, "I thought you were on my side. Unexpectedly, you built me up and also destroyed me! When I first mastered the power of laws, I was full of gratitude—reverence from the bottom of my heart! But now I see, you're not worthy at all."

"Too bad. We have no concept of any emotion. Your gratitude toward us is extremely foolish. We are the embodiment of world will; guiding fate toward the correct path is our job."

The three sisters answered calmly. Facing the sudden Odin, they didn't feel the slightest panic—perhaps they had no concept of fear either? Just three emotionless human-shaped machines.

After hearing the sisters' words, Odin laughed. Now he only wanted to escape his death fate and avenge Asgard. In his view, not dying in Ragnarök meant he had already succeeded halfway.

"Enough. Wasn't everything arranged by you? Using me as a pawn to be discarded at any time, to pamper your new toy—that demon prophet."

"It's true we arranged it, but we also acted according to Fate's instructions. We can see your fate ultimately goes toward death. You should accept it calmly—all struggles are meaningless."

"Let me accept fate calmly? That means letting me die?"

"Yes. If you're still alive, the stable world rules would develop serious cracks. That's not what we want, and Fate doesn't allow you and Asgard to exist forever."

"How laughable. Do you think I'll meekly accept my death fate? Impossible! I'll resist to the end, trample your faith underfoot, and become a transcendent god above Fate!"
