The three sisters looked at Odin in silence for a long time. In their view, the current Odin had gone mad—actually choosing to resist Fate?

But the sisters' confusion quickly disappeared, vaguely understanding why Odin, who should have died, appeared a second time in the Fate Secret Realm—

"I see. We understand. In the end, we too are beings restricted by Fate's shackles, also caught in countless cycles of reincarnation."

"Although we are the embodiment of world will, we are ultimately just pieces on the chessboard. So it is."

"We seem to have lost our reason for existence."

Odin frowned, not understanding what the sisters were mumbling to themselves. He couldn't help but speak in a mocking tone, "What are you talking about? Judging by this, you accepted your death fate before me."

"Odin, we know why you came here. This is our ending, so we accept it calmly. But finally, I'll give you advice—give up all resistance. Although you can escape Ragnarök, it still changes nothing, only deepening your pain. You'll still go toward death. Your current struggles are only delaying your death time. So-called Fate—is something that cannot be changed by any means."

The three Norn sisters seemed to have known their final fate, even breaking rules to reveal some secrets to Odin.

Yet these secrets were still useless, only deepening Odin's despair and triggering his powerful rebellious psychology.

Odin frowned, anger igniting in his heart. The sisters' meaning was: don't struggle, just lie down and wait to die.

"Nonsense! I won't be as weak as you. I won't allow anyone to control me—not even Fate!"

Odin spread his fingers, the eternal spear Gungnir appeared in his hand. With a light pinch, brilliant golden lightning erupted from both ends!

"Your game time is over. Using me as a pawn to be discarded at any time will come at a terrible price."

"Don't worry. I'll make good use of your power and become the first being to transcend Fate."

"Farewell, old friend."

As soon as the words fell, Odin poured war laws into the eternal spear and threw it!

The mighty power exploded instantly, killing the three sisters on their thrones. Flames consumed them.

The entire Fate Secret Realm shook violently. Countless gears stopped turning, and the small world began to slowly collapse.

Strangely, the broken corpses of the three sisters didn't bleed. Red, beautiful gems were exposed at the wounds—

Just as depicted in alchemy, the three sisters' bodies were composed of large amounts of philosopher's stones.

Odin's gaze was piercing. With a wave of his hand, he unleashed a terrifying war storm, dismembering and pulverizing the three sisters' corpses into dust.

The philosopher's stone dust gathered and condensed toward Odin, forming a complete set of magnificent armor on him, shimmering with brilliant philosopher's light!

The armor forged from philosopher's stone essence—probably only this one piece among countless worldlines existed on Odin. Its preciousness is imaginable.

As the precious item for opening the Fate Secret Realm and offsetting the life cost, the Philosopher's War Armor might have wondrous abilities—changing Fate might not be impossible!

Clink—

The pitch-black Fate Crown fell from the goddess throne, spinning endlessly at Odin's feet.

Odin bent down, picked up the Fate Crown, then with solemn expression placed it on his head, suddenly opening his flame-flashing single eye!

"From this moment, I too will become the player who manipulates the world."

"Fate cannot be changed?"

"No! I will change it, just you watch!"

title: Chapter 3 — Borrowing
content:
Chapter 3 — Borrowing

Volume 40 · Chapter 3

Half a month later, in the palace of France.

The old king's frail body lay weakly on the sickbed, his breathing faint.

At his advanced age, his health was deteriorating rapidly, and he could only rest in bed, unable to handle even the kingdom's affairs.

Fortunately, his daughter Margaret possessed exceptional abilities and had taken on the responsibility of managing the kingdom, allowing her father to rest and recover.

The old king felt his time was running out and began to transfer some important powers to Margaret, hoping she could grow quickly.

Although Margaret was a woman, the old king didn't mind that France would have a queen after him, ideally one as capable as Elizabeth of Great Britain.

Margaret helped her father cover himself with a blanket and said softly, "Rest early, Father. Leave everything to me."

"Having you makes things much easier. Compared to your siblings, only you are worthy of my trust." The old king paused, his voice weak, "I feel my time is near, and I fear the kingdom can only be entrusted to you. I don't trust the others."

"What are you saying? You'll live for at least another hundred years." Margaret grasped her father's hand, comforting him.

"A hundred years? Ha, I dare not hope for that. At times like these, I truly envy those of other races, with their ageless beauty and long lifespans." The old king sighed.

"Don't worry, the court physicians will do their best to care for you. This illness should be cured soon." Margaret said softly.

"My child, don't comfort me. I'm not a fool. This isn't an illness, just old age." The old king reached under his pillow, felt around, and pulled out a parchment scroll. "Take this."

"What is it?" Margaret asked in puzzlement.

"It's my will. After I die, you will inherit the throne and become the new king of France." The old king smiled in relief, saying slowly, "A talented and beautiful queen of France, it sounds quite good."

Margaret looked at the parchment scroll, her heart becoming complicated. "Father, shouldn't you reconsider? I may still have many shortcomings."

"What's there to consider? It's just you. This is my decision." The old king looked at his daughter with love, "You are my most excellent child. No one else can bear this responsibility. After this, everything will be left to you. I believe you can govern the country better than I can."

Margaret fell silent. Originally, she had wanted to obtain the throne quickly, but now that she had it, she wasn't as happy as she thought she'd be.

Because with the power came the loss of her freedom. Everything she did would be tied to the kingdom's interests.

"I have only one regret now."

"What is it? I will do my best to fulfill your wishes."

"That you haven't found someone to love. I hope you can find a trustworthy husband soon."

Margaret's expression turned awkward. "This isn't urgent at all."

"My child, you've met many talented young men, including nobles and princes from various places. Isn't there anyone you fancy?" The old king asked curiously.

"I..." Margaret hesitated, thinking that she did have someone in mind, but he already had a wife and children and wasn't interested in her.

As the father and daughter discussed this sensitive topic, Knight Blaise suddenly burst in without knocking, shouting, "Something terrible has happened!"

Margaret's face darkened, and she scolded, "What are you doing, Blaise! Can't you see I'm talking to my father? You didn't even knock!"

"Sorry, it's urgent!" Blaise was sweating profusely.

"What could be so urgent that you'd be so flustered? As the kingdom's chief knight, what kind of behavior is this?" Margaret said disapprovingly.

"Your Highness, I had no choice. I had to inform you immediately."

"What is it?"

"Someone has broken into the treasury, and it seems they're after the Star-Annihilating Cannon!"

After hearing Blaise's urgent report, Margaret's face changed dramatically. She thought for a few seconds before commanding, "Quickly! Gather all the knights in the castle!"

In response to the emergency, Margaret issued an order to assemble all knights, preparing to head to the treasury together to stop anyone with malicious intentions towards the kingdom's treasures.

The treasury stored vast wealth and treasures, but these were secondary. The crucial Star-Annihilating Cannon was also there.

The value of the Star-Annihilating Cannon was equivalent to the Lake Fairy and the King's Sword to Great Britain, the foundation of a kingdom's existence.

If the Star-Annihilating Cannon fell into outsiders' hands, it would be a disaster for France, an irreparable loss no amount of wealth could compensate for.

The castle's knights quickly gathered and followed Princess Margaret into the treasury. To their surprise, the intruder was none other than Merlin!

Merlin gazed at the floating cube before him, which he had seen once during the Era of the Gods but hadn't witnessed its power. As a weapon condensed from the essence of the earth spirit tribe, its power was likely formidable.

Merlin wanted to borrow the Star-Annihilating Cannon to blast open the Heavenly Gate above France and directly rescue Alice's soul.

"Mr. Merlin? How did you end up here?" Blaise asked, bewildered by Merlin's presence.

Merlin slowly turned around and said softly, "Long time no see, everyone."

Seeing Merlin appear, Margaret's heart skipped a beat. "Mr. Merlin, why didn't you tell me you were coming? We could have shared a drink on this lovely night~"

"Hey! Your Highness, he's intruding on the treasury, a serious crime. Please restrain yourself." Blaise reminded from the side.

"Shut up. Do I need you to manage what I do?" Margaret glared at Blaise.

"Ah..." Blaise was speechless, thinking that even if you've been pining for a married man, there's no need to be like this! He's the one who broke into the treasury!

"How about it, Mr. Merlin?" Margaret's face flushed, speaking with deep meaning, "The servants made me a new, very soft bed recently. Would you like to try it out?"

"Uh..." Merlin recalled past events and dared not be alone with Margaret, so he spoke seriously, "Sorry for the trouble. I came here on urgent business and had to force my way in."

"What business?" Margaret asked, seeing Merlin's serious attitude, and put away her flirtatious demeanor.

"I want to borrow the Star-Annihilating Cannon."

Margaret was taken aback, her expression becoming complex. This was France's greatest treasure; it couldn't be borrowed so easily.

"No way!" Blaise frowned, shouting, "The Star-Annihilating Cannon is the foundation of our kingdom. How could we lend it to you?"

"Get out!"

"Huh? What did you say, Your Highness?"

"I told you to get out!" Margaret ordered impatiently. "I need to speak with Mr. Merlin alone."

"Your Highness, this isn't right. Although you fancy him, you're the kingdom's heir. You should prioritize the greater good."

"Blaise, my patience is limited." Margaret said coldly.

Blaise swallowed the words he wanted to say and led the knights out of the treasury, glancing back at Merlin. In the princess's eyes, was the kingdom's fate less important than a man?

Pretty boy, how detestable

title: Chapter 4 — The Guns of the Decisive Battle
content:
Chapter 4 — The Guns of the Decisive Battle

Volume 40 · Chapter 4

Until everyone else left, Marguerite only then asked in detail— “What happened exactly, that you need to borrow the Annihilation Cannon? And what's wrong with your eyes?” “My eyes are a long story, don't talk about it for now, I want to borrow the Annihilation Cannon mainly to save Alice.” “Did something happen to her?” “Yes, her soul is now trapped in the heavens, I must forcefully open the gate between the heavens and the mortal world.” After hearing Merlin's explanation, Marguerite's expression froze, and an evil thought suddenly arose in her mind, if Alice couldn't be saved, wouldn't she be able to take advantage of the situation herself? “That's non-negotiable, right? Is there no other choice, besides—” “Forget it, Marguerite, I know what you're thinking, Alice means nothing to me, I must save her.” Merlin interrupted Marguerite's words, which made her feel even more disappointed, it seemed that wanting to capture the other person's heart was basically impossible. “You're really heartless, you're not even worth my consideration?” “You're a good girl, Marguerite, but I'm sorry, I've already made my choice.” “You're directly rejecting me, didn't you think about what would happen if I refused to lend you the Annihilation Cannon?” “I thought about it, but please understand one thing, what I said was just a courtesy, if I refused, France would not see the sun tomorrow.” Merlin paused for a moment, then continued, “Actually, a large number of demons have secretly gathered outside the castle, you should understand what this means.” “Demons?” Marguerite was surprised. “I am the Demon Lord, Lucifer the Third, sorry for deceiving you for so long, I'm not human.” Merlin said bluntly. “You're the king of the demon race? Really, really?” Marguerite found it hard to believe, wondering if Merlin was just joking. Merlin transformed half of his face into a demon, showing it to Marguerite, then quickly hid it, proving his identity. Marguerite covered her mouth in shock, unable to speak, her hands trembling as she pointed at Merlin. “You're really a demon?” “What else could it be?” Merlin sighed, asking, “Now, your choice has decided the fate of France, so what's your answer?” “Marguerite's expression was extremely tense, but she quickly calmed down, “As expected, I thought you were a man who wouldn't care about anyone, but I still like your kind of personality.” “???” Merlin furrowed his brow, he was indeed not used to dealing with girls like Marguerite. “You still need to ask me for an answer? I don't have any choice at all.” Marguerite took a deep breath, saying, “I never thought I would fall in love with a demon, it seems my love life is really not going well.” “So, I'll take the Annihilation Cannon for now.” “Wait, I have a request.” Merlin was surprised, looking at Marguerite, probingly asking, “What? Something that's too difficult for me to agree to.” “It's not something difficult.” Marguerite leaned in close to Merlin, staring at his eyes for a moment, then lightly kissed his face. “Ah!” Merlin subconsciously took a step back, wiping his face with his sleeve, “What are you doing?” “Nothing, I just didn't want to leave any regrets, consider it a whim of mine.” Marguerite blinked her eyes. Merlin was speechless, shaking his head, thinking— “As expected, this princess is still so difficult to handle.” The knights outside the treasure room were anxiously waiting, they had no idea what Marguerite would decide. Blaise paced back and forth, praying in his heart that Marguerite wouldn't get caught up in her emotions, after all, the interests of the kingdom should come first. The Annihilation Cannon was France's most precious treasure, if it was lent out carelessly, it would probably cause panic throughout the kingdom, even when they were attacked by Dracula, they didn't dare to use it. The stone door was opened, and only Marguerite came out from inside, Blaise's eyes widened, and he suddenly sensed that something was amiss. “Your Highness! What's the decision? Did you lend it to him?” “Of course, I lent it to him, what else could I do?” Marguerite replied irritably. “Oh no!” Blaise's expression twisted, he exclaimed, “Your Highness, how could you agree to lend it to him? That's the kingdom's most important secret weapon, it can't be lent out, it will cause extreme panic.” “If it's not lent out, the kingdom will be even less safe.” Marguerite replied helplessly. “What do you mean?” Blaise scratched his head, puzzled. “There are a large number of demons gathered outside the castle, enough to flatten our kingdom in one night.” Marguerite said seriously. “What? When did this happen? The castle patrol team didn't even react?” “It should have happened not long ago, after that, let's just pretend it didn't happen, I'm afraid many people will leave a psychological scar, if the castle is invaded by a large number of demons.” “No way! We have to do something, the experience of the saints and the British is still fresh in our minds!” “Don't worry.” Marguerite thought for a moment, then replied, “Merlin promised me that the demons won't harm us, and they'll leave immediately after the matter is settled.” “He promised? Who is he, anyway?” Blaise asked in terror, thinking that only the Demon Lord, Lucifer the Third, could command demons, and he was the one who made the Church's life a living hell. Just as Blaise finished speaking, a deafening explosion shook the heavens, and Marguerite and Blaise, along with the other knights, all fell to the ground. This sudden cannon fire shook the entire castle, and everyone was in a state of chaos. “What's going on?” “Outside, only the light of the Annihilation Cannon pierced the earth, striking the sky! A massive shockwave continued to spread, and the ground of the castle seemed to have sunk several meters! The unparalleled magical power of the Annihilation Cannon struck the heavenly gate in the sky, and the skies of France and the surrounding kingdoms were shaking! In the heavens, Alice was bound to a giant tree by thorns, sharp thorns pierced her soul and body, constantly injecting life force into her. Alice was in agony, she didn't know how many times she had fainted, feeling her soul being slowly torn apart. Such inhumane torture made even Michael and Uriel unable to bear, they had never seen such a cruel scene before. In their eyes, the once calm and peaceful Goddess of Light now looked like a ruthless female demon, torturing a helpless soul. Maria wanted to extract the remains of Theresa's soul from Alice's soul and body, completely disregarding the pain of a soul container. Suddenly, a deafening explosion shook the heavens, and countless holy spirits were thrown into chaos, a thick smoke billowed from the direction of the heavenly gate— “What's going on?”

title: Chapter 5 — Night of the Demon's Descent
content:
Chapter 5 — Night of the Demon's Descent

Volume 40 · Chapter 5

Maria gazed toward the direction of the Heavenly Gate, rolling thick smoke continuously rising—this was the first time the tranquility of Heaven had been forcibly shattered.The Heavenly Gate was blasted open with a hole, and from the crack surged a violent storm; the holy spirits felt deep unease."Master! Our gate seems to have been forcibly opened!" Michael felt a bead of cold sweat slide down his forehead."What audacity! Someone actually dares to scheme against Heaven?!" Uriel shouted angrily.Maria fell silent for a moment, then ordered, "Don't panic, Michael; take the holy spirits and go check the situation.""Yes!" Michael grabbed his weapon, leading a host of holy spirits swiftly toward the ruined Heavenly Gate."Master, just who is it?" Uriel asked hesitantly."I don't know, but anyone who dares to act with such arrogance against my Heaven must pay a heavy price."Maria's expression turned grim as she said, for now she didn't want to deal with this matter; she only wished to quickly tear Teresa's lingering soul from Alice's body.Yet Maria had a bad premonition—logically, no one in the mortal world would have the gall to challenge her, except that mysterious demon prophet who had vanished for ages.After the demon prophet disappeared without trace for several ages, Maria—had come to believe this fellow was dead; besides the prophet, she could think of no one else possessing such boldness.Because the Heavenly Gate's destruction diverted Maria's attention, the tormented Alice gained a brief respite, her consciousness slowly returning a little.Is it Merlin?Surely he would not give up.Above the skies of France, a dazzling holy light suddenly blazed, illuminating the night as if it were day.Countless holy spirits, fully armed, poured through the broken cracks and reappeared in the mortal realm.They unfurled their pure white wings behind them, exuding a warm aura that filled the sky with the Goddess of Light's radiance.Since the last time holy spirits appeared en masse in the mortal world was during the final holy war of the demon era.People lifted their heads to gaze upon these lofty messengers of the goddess, overwhelmed by their light, wishing to drop to their knees on the spot to express reverence for the goddess.The holy spirits looked down at the puny humans below and let out a series of scornful laughs; during the holy war, humans had revered them as saviors, granting them an unparalleled exalted status.Yet, as beings personally crafted by the goddess with her life force, the holy spirits held themselves in high esteem, refusing to equate themselves with frail humans, nor acknowledging that humans too were creations of the goddess.Michael, as Heaven's representative, descended to see what had happened; he slowly floated down from the holy spirits until he stopped in the low-altitude region.He flapped his many pairs of pure white wings, making himself appear more holy and majestic, and his voice thundered like rolling thunder across the entire sky over the French royal capital—"Who destroyed the Heavenly Gate?""This reckless act has already disturbed the Great Goddess's rest!" "If you refuse to step forward, then this city will cease to exist!"People's faces instantly turned pale; this harsh speech and threat clashed with the image of the holy spirits.In the mouths of those church folk, the holy spirits are all kind and benevolent, having sacrificed greatly to save humanity.But now that people have seen the holy spirits with their own eyes, they cannot help but doubt the preaching of the clergy.Disturbing the Goddess's rest would require an entire city to be buried with her—only a tyrant could do such a thing.Seeing the humans below show no reaction, Michael felt a surge of irritation; he had thought a simple threat would easily settle the matter."Tsk! You won't admit it? Then don't blame me for being blunt!""Wait, it's me.""Huh?"Michael started, his gaze sweeping over the French royal capital, when he suddenly spotted Merlin's eerie silhouette.At the highest point of the royal capital, atop the goddess statue on a church roof, Merlin stood with arms crossed, silently watching Michael hover in the air.Michael stared at Merlin for a while, feeling uncertain; amid the pressure of countless holy spirit troops behind him, it was astonishing that anyone dared to step forward."Are you?""Yes, it's me. You're looking for the culprit who destroyed the Heavenly Gate, aren't you? That was me."Merlin nodded, without hiding anything; this calm, unhurried demeanor made Michael feel uneasy, thinking Merlin either wasn't exceptionally brave or was simply a fool."Who are you?""I am the demon monarch, the third-generation Lucifer.""The third-generation Lucifer?" Michael felt a bit dazed, recalling the mighty demon lord who had slain countless holy spirits; his hair stood on end."Are you a descendant of Mephisto?!" "Exactly." Merlin, seeing Michael's reaction, thought his straight-laced grandfather must have left some psychological scar on the holy spirits?E"Do you know what you're doing? You're playing with fire and burning yourself! Why destroy the Heavenly Gate?"Michael's angry question came without fear of Merlin; he reasoned that even a third-generation demon could not compare to those early ones who possessed demon god blood."Why else? I want to bring my wife home; you have her trapped in Heaven.""Your wife? Is that woman?!"Michael stared blankly, thinking that the soul container in the mortal realm was together with the demon king—this was completely unexpected!Compared to Uriel, Michael is a calm holy spirit; he did not rush to attack but hoped to maintain stability.Michael had been somewhat influenced by the landlady Raphael, and as the goddess grew ever more cruel, he too began to doubt himself.Slaying demons is the goddess's command, not the wish of the holy spirits; those comrades who fell in the holy war undoubtedly became sacrifices for resurrecting Teresa.If possible, Michael wished to avoid another holy war, not wanting to see the remaining holy spirit companions perish.However, Michael dared not voice this thought before the goddess; the outcome might be like Raphael's—"Young demon king, don't be so angry; hear me out first.""Your actions are utterly foolish; risking everything for a mere soul container is not worth it.""Rashly breaking the Heavenly Gate could very well spark another holy war, leading to rivers of blood once more.""Your forebears guarded the last spark of the demon race with their lives; do you truly wish to extinguish it completely?""Listen to me: abandon the idea of rescuing your wife; I can find an excuse to cover this up, and we can pretend it never happened.""You want me to give up? No—hand over your wife's soul, or else after tonight Heaven will have no reason to exist." Merlin said bluntly."You foolish demon! Simply irredeemable! Aren't you afraid of triggering another holy war that would wipe out the entire demon race?!" Michael bellowed."Demons are beings that never fear war; besides, who will actually be wiped out remains uncertain." Merlin raised his palm, then clenched it into a fist, "Let us continue that holy war that has yet to end!"Seeing Merlin's signal, the demons hidden in the royal capital suddenly surged forth, flapping like a flock of crows as they soared into the sky, straight toward the lofty holy spirits above!The demons had long made ample preparations, intending to seize this opportunity to avenge past humiliations, letting the grudges of the holy war erupt fully, carrying out the principle of an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth to the bitter end!The howls and roars of countless demons intertwined, echoing across the sky over the royal capital; the inhabitants of France stared dumbfounded, becoming witnesses to the second half of the holy war."An ambush?" Michael's eyelid twitched; he swiftly retreated upward, glaring fiercely at Merlin."You're an outright lunatic!""Worsening the situation will bring you no benefit at all!"

title: Chapter 6 — Pressing Toward the Heavens
content:
Chapter 6 — Pressing Toward the Heavens

Volume 40 · Chapter 6

Demons charged toward the holy spirits in the sky, enemies meeting with clear understanding, quickly devolving into a chaotic melee. The holy spirits were utterly unprepared for the demons' ambush, caught off guard as soon as they engaged, falling into a vast encirclement. Michael had intended to descend to investigate the damage to the heavenly gate, but instead encountered an ambush. This enraged him, forcing him to order the holy spirits to assume a defensive formation and buy some time. Fortunately, the holy spirits have an innate advantage over demons; even with the demons' great numbers, they could not be wiped out in a short while. “Your Majesty.” Shu and Ophelia appeared beside Merlin, having come with the main force of the demon city. To exterminate the holy spirits, breach heaven, and avenge the grudge of the ancient holy war, Merlin had practically moved the entire demon city here. “Has Lilith not come along?” Merlin asked. “Rest assured, when we departed, Her Majesty Viviane locked her in her room, saying she would temporarily manage the demon city,” Shu replied. “That’s good,” Merlin said, feeling somewhat relieved, thinking that with Lilith’s strength she would be basically useless in this situation and would only cause trouble. “Your Majesty, long time no see, you are still as radiant as ever,” Ophelia said, her eyes blazing with fiery passion, saliva almost dripping. “Ugh!” A bead of cold sweat trickled down Merlin’s forehead. “Long time no see, Ophelia sister, please watch your manners.” “Cough cough!” Ophelia lightly coughed to hide her embarrassment, “Sorry.” “Your Majesty, you said we could take advantage of the situation to break through heaven and eradicate our demon race’s arch‑enemy—how confident are you?” Shu brought up the matter. “Completely confident,” Merlin answered firmly. “If so, the great scourge of our demon race will vanish forever—what a wonderful thing,” Shu exclaimed. “I’ll go first to open a path for you,” Merlin paused, then shouted loudly, “Avis!” A dragon’s roar rang out; the holy dragon, its body shining with light, slowly rose from behind Merlin, its massive wings stirring up a violent gale. “Do we just fly past these holy spirits and straight into heaven?” “Exactly.” “Come on, I’ll give you a lift.” Merlin leapt onto the back of the holy dragon Avis, accompanied by a resonant dragon cry, swiftly soaring upward straight toward the damaged heavenly gate. Shu and Ophelia exchanged a glance, not wasting time here but quickly joining the force exterminating the holy spirits. Because the holy spirits naturally restrain demons, the demons need several times their numbers to completely annihilate this batch of holy spirits—this qualifies as a fierce battle. Michael’s brows knelt tight; sensing that under the onslaught of so many demons he could not hold out much longer, he knew he must return to heaven to request reinforcements. But just as Michael lifted his head, he saw Merlin riding the holy dragon swiftly approaching heaven’s gate, and he flew into a rage. “Filthy demons, dare not defile the sacred heavens!” Seeing Michael draw his waist‑blade, a light comparable to the sun burst forth, raging flames swirling and gathering on the blade as it hurtled toward Merlin. Suddenly a black vortex appeared above Michael’s head, swallowing the surging divine‑sword flames whole. The vortex then rapidly expanded, a huge explosion instantly devouring the lives of dozens of holy spirits and submerging them. “You’re already on the brink of despair—do you still have time to do anything else?” Viviane appeared in her demon form; her horrifying visage made the holy spirits feel a chill, a heavy darkness continually seeping out. The smoke cleared, a massive barrier of light protected most of the holy spirits, Michael holding his divine sword unscathed. “A god‑level demon?” Michael’s eyelid twitched—it had been ages since the last holy war, yet the demon race had produced a new god‑level being, which surprised him; it seemed the previous holy war had not shaken the demon race’s foundations. Before Michael could organize the holy spirits for a counter‑attack, a strange disturbance broke out in the ranks: a group of holy spirits began slaughtering each other, as if gone mad. “What the hell? Did they fall under an illusion?” “You won’t be able to resist much longer—give up.” Asmodeus manifested in her alluring demon form, her piercing voice like a demonic melody invading their ears, continually disturbing the holy spirits’ spirits. Waves of black mist rose, the Europa demon’s wings unfurled, holding a crystal ball she ascended into the air, using divine power to bolster the demons’ strength. Suddenly a roar rang out—the terrifying King of Wrath Samael, his body ablaze with flames, slammed a fist into the light barrier shielding the holy spirits. Crack, crack—the solid barrier began to crumble, though it barely managed to hold. “There’s a god‑level?!” Michael exclaimed, becoming panicked, for the strong opponents exceeded his expectations! Viviane’s high divine power unleashed a ferocious dark shock, assisting Samael in shattering the sturdy light barrier. Deprived of their protective defense, the holy spirits thrown into chaos instantly fell under the demons’ frenzied onslaught! Michael plummeted from the sky, a trickle of blood at the corner of his mouth; just as he lifted his head, he saw the four demon lords looming above him— “What a terrible situation atop my head—I could handle one god‑level demon easily, but now there are two god‑level beings, plus a half‑god and a fake—” “Is this making me face the entire demon race alone?” “Truly doomed—I can’t even reach heaven for aid, I can only fight to the death here!” “Filthy demons! As the commander of the holy spirit legion, my glory will not allow you to trample it!” Michael raised his flaming divine sword high; the heavenly blaze instantly illuminated the night sky of France, the pressure of a god‑level being spreading, causing the weak demons to tremble in fear. The four demon lords looked down on Michael, who intended to fight to the death, and jointly unleashed their ultimate strike upon him. A violent explosion flattened everything around; as the smoke slowly drifted away, a huge crater gradually emerged. The flames of the divine sword died out, the blade plunged upside‑down into the ground, Michael, covered in wounds, collapsed, gazing at the oppressive, heavy sky as he slowly closed his eyes— “Terribly—” In heaven, Uriel noticed Michael hadn’t returned for so long and decided to go to the mortal realm to check on him. He happened to collide with Merlin riding the holy dragon, startling him greatly and shouting, “Drop dead! This is heaven! No filthy demons allowed here!” Uriel had just summoned his divine hammer when he heard a “whoosh”—Misterin flew in, piercing his heart outright and pinning him like an ornament to the heavenly gate. Uriel wore an expression of disbelief, lowered his gaze to the Misterin embedded in his chest, his lips twitching unable to speak, his eyelids fluttering before he lost consciousness. Merlin arrived at the heavenly gate, pulled Misterin out, let Uriel’s corpse slide to the ground, and turned back saying, “Avis, the rest is up to you—stay here.” “Very well, hurry—your daughter hasn’t given up; she’s draining her life force every day.” Merlin said nothing, slipped Misterin back into its sheath, fixed his gaze on the majestic heaven, his heart stirring— Alice, I’m coming.

title: Chapter 7 — Sudden
content:
Chapter 7 — Sudden

Volume 40 · Chapter 7

Maria focused on tormenting Alice, trying to quickly strip away Theresa's residual soul and restart the resurrection plan. At this stage, Alice still hadn't recalled who Maria was, undoubtedly proving the resurrection plan had failed. In Maria's eyes, Alice, the soul vessel, had lost all value and had no reason to continue existing.

Footsteps echoed from behind. Without turning, Maria asked, "What's the situation? What's happening outside?"

"Stop, Maria."

Upon hearing this familiar voice, Maria's expression drastically changed, her heart chilled to the bone. She spun around abruptly.

The demon race prophet who had mysteriously vanished for several epochs had returned at this moment?!

Maria's eyes widened in terror, doubting her own eyes. Even when the demon race faced crisis, he hadn't returned. Yet he appeared now!

"You... you're still alive?!"

"I never died; that was just your misconception." Merlin replied seriously.

"Impossible!" Maria retreated in panic, trembling. "You should be dead! Why didn't you step forward to save the demon epoch?"

"There are too many reasons; I can't explain them all in a short time." Merlin spoke vaguely, thinking that if he had stepped forward to save the demon epoch, would Alice have appeared?

"Shut up!" Maria gritted her teeth, suppressing her inner fear. "You, the culprit who brought disaster to Theresa, how dare you show your face before me!"

"I'm sorry about Theresa. I know you resent me, but I must stop your evil deeds." Merlin said firmly.

"Evil deeds?" Maria glanced at Alice behind her, seeming to realize something. "You're here for that vessel?"

"Correct, she's my wife." Merlin admitted frankly.

"Your wife?" Maria's expression was shocked, her brows furrowed. "This vessel... has she been with you?! This is an insult to my sister! I won't acknowledge this!"

"Your acknowledgment means nothing; you have no right to interfere." Merlin retorted.

"But she's the vessel for my sister's soul! In a sense, they're one!" Maria shouted, continuing, "You're relentless, leading my sister to death wasn't enough, now you're entangling her soul vessel. How much more must you torment Theresa before you'll let her go?!"

Merlin was speechless. Though his feelings for Theresa were complicated, his journey to the epoch of gods was never to entangle with Theresa, but for the future soul vessel, Alice. If comparing Theresa and Alice in Merlin's heart, Alice was undoubtedly more important, even as Theresa's vessel.

"Looks like I hit the mark, so you can't refute it?" Maria narrowed her eyes.

"You're wrong. I've never been entangled with your sister. Everything I've done is for that woman named Alice." Merlin's eyes turned cold, issuing a final warning, "Give up, Maria. Theresa is dead; your obsession is meaningless. I won't let you harm my wife. If you persist, I'll kill you."

"Are you threatening me?" Maria stood firm against the immense pressure, ready to fight to the death. "You're the powerful demon prophet who defeated the king of gods, Odin. I'm no match for you, but I can still drag you down with me! If not for wanting to see Theresa one last time, I wouldn't have survived until now!"

"Is that your final decision?" Merlin's face darkened.

"Want to take the soul vessel? You'll have to step over my corpse. That's the only way I'll see Theresa again. I won't yield."

"This is your own doing!"

Merlin instantly transformed into his ferocious demon god form, his destructive law aura overwhelming, causing the entire heavenly realm to change color!

Maria clenched her teeth, enduring the torrential destructive winds, summoning her crystal staff as life laws surged within her!

At her feet, countless plants began to revive, growing at an unbelievable speed, becoming gigantic in the blink of an eye. Under the life law's influence, these plants seemed to have their own lives, rapidly condensing into massive fists in the air, charging towards Merlin!

"Boom!" Merlin was sent flying like a fly, causing violent spatial tremors!

The demon god Merlin steadied himself, gazing at Maria surrounded by the plants below.

The life law's power wasn't in its attack but in creation. Even the smallest grass could become powerful under its influence.

Compared to destructive power, the life law was far inferior to Merlin's destructive law, even weaker than Satan's death law. However, if infused directly into an enemy, it could cause their power to expand endlessly, eventually leading to self-destruction.

Maria's claim of being able to drag Merlin down with her wasn't an empty threat.

Merlin wouldn't give her the chance to use the life law on him. He prepared for a swift battle, utilizing his advantages.

"So, your life law is indeed remarkable, but still not my match."

"You can try. When you kill me, the life law will enter your body like a toxin, amplifying your power. How much can your body endure? Tenfold? Hundredfold? Eventually, you'll be consumed by your own power."

Merlin's brows furrowed, unafraid of Maria's threat. Was this just intimidation?

Just as Merlin was about to unleash his combined destructive power, the sky suddenly lit up with a dazzling, sun-like radiance, accompanied by a piercing shriek—

A grotesquely shaped spear pierced Maria's abdomen, its two segments flashing like golden lightning. It was the strongest divine artifact, Gungnir!

Maria's body paralyzed, her eyes filled with terror as she gazed at the spear piercing her robes. This unexpected turn of events left her stunned.

"Odin... you're still alive?"

Before she could finish, Gungnir's radiance expanded, engulfing Maria's body in an explosion that painted the heavenly realm red!

The ultimate god's violent explosion shook the entire realm, destroying palace after palace, reducing the area to ruins!

The ancient tree binding Alice was uprooted in the storm, and Alice's figure vanished in the flames!

The young, handsome Odin retrieved Gungnir with a wave, his meaningful gaze fixed on the astonished Merlin.

Clad in the Sage's armor, wearing the Crown of Fate, wielding two Gungnirs, Odin's divine attire was breathtaking.

"Haha! Prophet! We meet again! Let's celebrate this reunion with a salute!"

Odin raised Gungnir, unleashing a crimson war law that surged skyward, several times stronger than before!

The Crown of Fate's ability was to enhance laws, but it could also grant the wearer multiple laws by sacrificing Sage Stones.

Odin's Sage armor, forged from the essence of the three Fates, possessed unparalleled defensive power. Combined with the Crown of Fate, it allowed him to manipulate numerous laws without restraint.

With two Gungnirs, Odin had become a terrifying existence surpassing all rules!

"Impossible! I clearly killed you. Why are you still alive?"

Even in his demon god form, Merlin couldn't hide his shock. He hadn't expected Odin to appear at this moment.

"Can't accept it? I knew it; your expression is priceless." Odin sneered, "You only killed my avatar. I've been alive all along, living in hiding like you, waiting for this moment! I'll kill you to avenge Asgard's destruction and break free from fate's shackles, becoming a god beyond all rules!"

"Avatar?" Merlin's brows furrowed, realizing he had only defeated a clone. The real Odin had been secretly observing him all along!

"Prophet, no matter how strong you are, you're no match for me now. I can use the Crown of Fate to destroy you at any time."

Odin spoke confidently, having planned this for ages, seeking to seize the power of the three Fates and control multiple laws.

With numerous laws at his disposal, defeating the demon prophet wasn't impossible. Odin's chances of victory were high.

"How laughable, thinking you can destroy me? You should reconsider your own strength!"

Merlin, in his demon god form, readied his sword, combining his sword technique, destructive law, and Mistilin. Without hesitation, he struck!

The destructive power reached its peak, capable of erasing everything. The triple fusion resembled a scythe of death, slashing towards Odin!

In an instant, the sky changed colors, and the heavenly realm's space was torn apart, revealing a narrow, dark void!

Merlin's fusion slash erased the sky, leaving only unknown dimensions as storms swept the realm!

However, to everyone's surprise, Odin floated unscathed, his Sage armor shining brightly, perfectly blocking Merlin's attack!

Under the armor's protection, Odin feared Merlin's sword technique no longer. He could literally stand still and let Merlin strike without issue.

This meant Odin could harm Merlin, but Merlin couldn't harm Odin, giving him absolute advantage from the start.

If Merlin wanted to defeat Odin, he had to find a way to break the Sage armor's protection; otherwise, he had no chance.

"Useless?"

Merlin's face darkened. His triple fusion slash was his strongest attack.

If even that couldn't harm Odin, Merlin was truly helpless.

"Haha! How pitiful~" Odin's laughter grew more manic. "Your attacks are useless against me. You're just a slightly sharper-toothed wild dog before me! Let me show you my power!"

As he spoke, the heavenly realm's temperature soared, fire laws surging, gathering in Gungnir!

The fire law represented the ultimate flames, not producing fire but causing everything to disintegrate!

The sky twisted and nearly collapsed under the fire law's scorching.

Gungnir was thrown, wrapped in terrifying fire law, piercing Merlin's shoulder in one strike!

Merlin hadn't dodged; being pierced was the result of his desperate evasion.

Now, even a slight mistake would mean instant death from Gungnir's law-imbued attack.

Gungnir's effect was to kill its target upon being thrown, making it nearly impossible to dodge.

Only someone like Merlin, without strong regenerative abilities, could survive such an attack.

Odin retrieved Gungnir, his tone surprised. "You can still dodge? Like a cornered old mouse~"

Merlin gritted his teeth, choosing to gamble everything, unleashing another fusion slash at Odin!

The result was predictable: Odin remained unharmed under the Sage armor's protection.

"Have you given up? How disappointing. I thought you had an ace up your sleeve."

Odin roared, channeling lightning law into another Gungnir, enveloping the heavenly realm in a thunderstorm.

Accompanied by deafening thunder, Gungnir pierced Merlin's left thigh, severely impairing his evasion abilities!

Odin clearly intended to toy with Merlin, slowly killing him with repeated Gungnir strikes!

Merlin endured the agony, his demon god form barely withstanding further attacks, temporarily avoiding instant death.

Again, Merlin used the fusion slash, striking Odin without hesitation, but to no effect.

"Don't you have any other tricks? I told you, your attacks—"

A crisp cracking sound echoed. Odin's triumphant expression froze as he looked down to see a hairline fracture in his Sage armor!

Merlin's three consecutive fusion slashes had targeted the same spot on Odin's chest. The relentless assault had finally breached the supposedly invincible armor!

Though the Sage armor's defense was formidable, it had limits, especially against repeated attacks on a single point.

Odin's pupils constricted, his earlier arrogance vanishing. A cold sweat broke on his forehead as he thought, "Even the Sage Stone-forged armor can't withstand this?"

Fortunately, the defense still held, but if Merlin continued, the perfect defense might crack.

"No! I must end this quickly!"

Odin's eyes gleamed with determination, ready to use desperate measures to kill Merlin swiftly.

title: Chapter 8 — Memory Fragments
content:
Chapter 8 — Memory Fragments

Volume 40 · Chapter 8

“Indeed, I still somewhat underestimated the law of destruction; as expected, it's the power said to have the strongest destructive power.

Odin narrowed his eyes, putting away his previous contemptuous attitude, becoming vigilant, even a bit worried.

The defensive capability of the Sage's battle armor is indeed formidable, but in front of Merlin it is not perfect; it's impossible to have the Hell's too many fusions of the drawing slash.

With this, as long as Merlin continues to press his attack a bit, the idle battle armor will reveal a flaw, and Odin's advantage will likewise vanish.

Although the Crown of Fate allows Odin to use various laws, laws such as life and destruction cannot be used.

Maria and Merlin, as holders of these laws, must all be eliminated before Odin can use these two laws.

Otherwise, for Odin to directly oppose the law of destruction, which is touted as having the strongest destructive power, the difficulty remains immense.

However, Merlin's injuries are severe; his shoulder and thigh have been pierced by the Eternal Spear, losing his perfect evasion ability.

This showdown undoubtedly still gives Odin an absolute advantage—

Before Merlin breaks through the defense of the Sage's battle armor, Odin can completely eliminate him.

"

Merlin gritted his teeth; due to his severe injuries, maintaining the demon god form was extremely taxing, and he could only barely hold on.

If he lost the power boost from the demon god form, he might not be able to withstand the next Eternal Spear—

Would three fusions of the drawing slash be enough to cause cracks in the Sage's battle armor?

To break through Odin's defense, he estimated he'd need at least a dozen consecutive fierce attacks.

But this was too hard.

"I know what you're plotting, but I won't give you any chance!" Odin raised the two Eternal Spears in his hand, swiftly soaring into the air; the Crown of Fate on his head suddenly burst forth with black light, rapidly devouring the heavens!

Black, the color at the dawn of world creation, under the Crown of Fate's effect, the heavens became fodder, forming a mysterious sphere?

This sphere constantly inhaled and exhaled, expanding, emitting a dense chaotic aura; it had no elemental attributes, only pure void.

Colorful runes began to appear on Odin's body, various kinds of law power swirling around him, a terrifying pressure enveloping the entire heavens!

"Let you truly witness my real power!"

"The chaos created by the Crown of Fate will devour all law power!"

"It will ultimately lead the world to fall into utter void, returning to that primordial chaotic state devoid of any life."

As Odin's words fell, he let out a skyward roar, transforming into a brilliant pillar of light, pouring all his power into the chaotic sphere above his head.

The law runes surrounding him seemed to possess self-awareness, continually merging with the chaotic sphere.

Such immense power could reset the entire world, restoring it to the initial "void" state.

Under this attack, could Merlin possibly survive?

Obviously not; the law of destruction is merely one among many laws, fundamentally unable to resist the devouring of chaos.

Chaos not only destroys any object, but can also completely devour time and space, and even the elusive fate might be reset by chaotic power.

"Did you see that, Prophet? This is the power that even makes fate tremble! It's my final gift to you!"

"You are the obstacle on my path to triumph over fate; as long as I kill you, my fate will be rewritten!"

"So-called fate will become a toy I can manipulate at will!"

After chaos devoured a vast amount of law power, it became even more terrifying; its speed of devouring the heavens increased severalfold!

Within that void sphere, it seemed to nurture a terrifying monster, an existence that could plunge the world back into primordial chaos!

The storm swept in like a blade, easily slicing the heavenly land; though its power had not yet fully shown, the gusts it kicked up were already comparable to a star‑destroyer cannon!

Merlin clenched his teeth; amidst the storm, he inexplicably gained many wounds, the ground beneath his feet rapidly crumbling, palace after palace turning to dust—

No! I must find a way to stop Odin, otherwise I and Alice will vanish along with the heavens!

Merlin had no choice; even if he perished together with Odin, he would grit his teeth and press forward, unleashing another fusion drawing slash aimed at the enemy in the sky.

"Slash!"

On the other side, Alice's soul floated up from the ruins; having been far from the earlier explosion, she suffered little impact.

Looking around at the devastation, Alice had no doubt—it must be Merlin who came.

Alice began to look around, spotting Merlin fiercely battling Odin in the sky, and she was instantly startled.

"Merlin!?"

Alice wanted to step closer, but suddenly thorny vines materialized out of nowhere, binding her and rendering her immobile; she realized the Goddess of Light was watching her!

"Where are you going? You are Teresa's soul vessel; you cannot go anywhere."

Following the voice, Alice saw Maria, her breath weak, half of her flesh lost, her surging life force slowly repairing her damaged body.

Pierced by Odin's Eternal Spear, Maria had nearly been killed, but fortunately she possessed the law of life, granting her an almost indestructible soul and body.

During this time, the law of life had already helped Maria heal many wounds; she only needed to wait a bit longer, and she would rise again.

Alice had previously been tormented by Maria to the point of unconsciousness, unaware of what had happened; looking at the dying Maria, she had even thought Merlin was responsible.

"Before I finish with Teresa's residual soul glass, you cannot go anywhere; you are the vessel I created, you belong to me."

Alice angrily gritted her teeth, lifted her head to watch Merlin and Odin's life‑and‑death struggle, a sense of worry welling up inside her.

Seeing that Merlin was clearly at a disadvantage, his several drawing slashes seemed ineffective against the enemy; if this continued, it would be dangerous!

She had already sensed the intense chaotic aura; the entire heaven crafted by Maria was being devoured.

Watching the battle between Merlin and Odin, then glancing at the dying Maria on the ground—

Alice's expression suddenly turned strange, her eyes fell into deep bewilderment, a strong sense of déjà vu surged in her heart.

She felt as if she had experienced these events before; the scene before her seemed to have happened already, while some nameless memories kept flashing through her mind.

Dotingly loving her sister, the prophet who led the allied forces to defeat Asgard, the king of gods Odin who fell with the twilight—

Suddenly, a current seemed to surge deep in Alice's soul, sharply stabbing her spirit, and fragments of memory began to emerge one after another—

What is all this?

Is Teresa me?

No, that doesn't feel right!

It feels like it'll be over in less than ten days; sorry for the late update today.

I deleted tens of thousands of words from the new book; I felt the pacing was slow, so I overturned it and am rewriting from scratch.

title: Chapter 9 — Brief
content:
Chapter 9 — Brief

Volume 40 · Chapter 9

Who do these memories belong to?

Why can't I recall going through any of this with Merlin?

That girl who looks exactly like me, who is she, really?

Could it be me? I've never lived through the distant Age of the Gods.

The flood of memory fragments constantly hammered at Alice's mind, allowing her to catch glimpses into part of Theresa's life.

Alice recalled how both Maria and Satan had called her "Theresa," and suddenly she understood something—

Her soul and Theresa's soul were one!

In a certain sense, that lucky goddess named Theresa was nothing other than her previous life's memories!

Now, stimulated by these powerful deja vu sensations, Alice and Theresa's remnant souls were further merging, revealing fragments of memory.

Though these memory fragments were fragmented and incomplete, Alice could still feel Theresa's genuine emotions from them.

This was the Goddess Maria's plan—reviving Theresa wouldn't erase Alice's consciousness. Instead, it would let Alice remember everything, granting her two lives' worth of memories!

As for who Alice considered herself to be, it seemed to have become unimportant. Besides, Theresa was only a remnant soul left, and her fragmented memories couldn't allow her to recall everything.

However, these memory fragments were enough for Alice to remember parts of the Age of the Gods, to recognize that Merlin was that demon race prophet, and that the dying Maria here was the sister who had doted on her.

Seeing Alice in pain, Maria loosened the thorns binding her slightly, then said coldly—

"What's wrong with you? Playing the victim? I won't sympathize with you."

The severe headaches gradually faded, Alice raised her head and looked at Maria with complicated eyes, her lips moving as she struggled to find words.

She had been forcefully stuffed with an entire life, and Alice couldn't accept it so quickly. Her thoughts were in utter chaos, unsure of who she truly was.

Recalling how Maria had viciously tried to rip away her soul earlier filled Alice with anger, leaving her with not an ounce of goodwill toward this Goddess of Light.

But after seeing so many memory fragments, Alice had to change her feelings—she even began developing a sense of dependence and affection toward Maria.

Alice knew all of this was caused by "Theresa's memories." No one could match Theresa's trust in her older sister Maria, and this was simultaneously affecting her as well.

Sister?

Maria's entire body shuddered. She stared at Alice in disbelief, the laws of life repairing her body coming to a halt.

She couldn't believe a miracle had truly happened—her plan hadn't failed. At the very last moment, her younger sister had returned!

"What did you just call me?"

"Sister."

"!!!"

Maria's expression froze, at a loss for words, and she silently lowered her head, sinking into a long silence.

She had hoped with all her heart for Theresa to come back, but now that she had, she didn't know how to communicate with her sister.

Maria understood that the current Theresa possessed memories from both the lucky goddess and the soul vessel.

Though she was undoubtedly the sister she had yearned for, there would still be differences.

"Have you really remembered?"

"Yes, I remembered... quite a few distant memories."

Alice showed a touch of pain, sinking into deep confusion—the one who had persecuted her was actually her older sister from her previous life?

Within a short time, Alice's role couldn't fully shift; instinctively she felt some resistance, harboring a trace of hostility toward Maria.

"How much did you remember?"

"Not much," Alice paused, speaking slowly, "only scattered memories. I saw you holding my hand and walking across countless mountains and rivers, I saw us swinging together under the sunset, and I saw your constantly busy figure."

Maria lowered her head, certain the plan had succeeded. Though Alice had only recalled partial memories, far from perfect, perhaps she would remember more in the future.

Everything Alice described was memories the two sisters had experienced together. Maria felt deeply comforted inside—her efforts had finally paid off.

Maria untied the thorns binding Alice, no longer placing any restrictions on her.

"Do you hate me?"

"A little, since you tormented me for so long." Alice looked away, her expression conflicted. "But those memory fragments make it impossible for me to hold a grudge against you. My feelings right now are very complicated—I both love and hate you. I am indeed your younger sister, though with some differences. I'd rather believe my name is Alice rather than Theresa. Those memory fragments are chaotic, but the emotions are real."

Maria's body was almost fully repaired. She slowly stood up, looking at her long-lost younger sister, her heart filled with guilt—

"Don't blame me. Everything I did was to save you."

"I helped you fulfill your greatest wish, and humanity ushered in an era of prosperity. You should be happier about this. All of this was hard-won, wasn't it?"

"That wish?" Alice frowned, recalling Theresa's wish. "It was indeed hard-won, but you shouldn't have caused so many people to sacrifice needlessly just to bring me back. That's not what I wanted, sister."

"I missed you too much. A long life is unbearably dull. I only wanted to see you again. You're my only family, so no matter the cost, I had to do it." Maria's eyes reddened. She didn't want to be blamed by her sister; she hoped for forgiveness.

"I understand you, sister, because I bear responsibility for this as well." Alice responded softly. Compared to Theresa, she was clearly stronger.

"Theresa..."

Maria slowly approached Alice, slowly extending her hand, wanting to touch her sister's face after such a long time.

But suddenly, a deafening chaotic storm struck, interrupting the sisters' reunion!

What they saw was—

The terrifying chaotic power had finally fully prepared itself. From thick fog, a colossal bloody red cross emerged, radiating brilliant crimson light!

All who saw the bloody red cross felt their hairs stand on end with fear—as though it were a key to restart the world, instilling endless despair from the bottom of their hearts!

The heavens had already shattered into pieces. As the massive bloody red cross rotated, no one except Odin could survive the catastrophe!

Odin raised his two eternal spears high, hovering before the enormous bloody red cross, like a great god who had transcended the shackles of fate!

Merlin knelt on one knee, gasping heavily, already covered in wounds. It was barely possible for him to stand up again.

He glanced at Odin's Sage Battle Armor. Though more cracks had appeared, it was still not quite broken through.

The situation had reached a decisive point. There was no doubt about it—Odin had won the final victory!

"Merlin!" Alice called out loudly, straining her mind to help, but in her soul state she could do nothing.

Maria watched Alice's reaction and a wave of bitterness surged in her heart. No matter how many times she stopped it, her younger sister would still choose to leave with the prophet.

She looked at the terrifying bloody red cross, and at the arrogant Odin.

To let her newly returned younger sister continue living, she might have to make one final choice.

Maria picked up the divine staff from the ground, gazing at the collapsing heavens—the civilization she had created still could not escape its destiny of destruction.

"I have to leave now, Theresa."

"What are you going to do?" Alice asked in confusion.

"Nothing. I'm just doing what I should do." Maria smiled, as though all burdens had been lifted, becoming light and carefree—

"Actually, I should have left long ago. It was only because of you that I survived until now."

"Perhaps this is fate, isn't it? No matter how much we change things, death will always come."

"It's time to repay everything I owe you."

"Promise me—you'll live well. Don't disappoint me."

"Finally, welcome home, Theresa. Seeing you once more is enough for me."

title: Chapter 10 — The Final Sword Draw
content:
Chapter 10 — The Final Sword Draw

Volume 40 · Chapter 10

"See this, Prophet!"

"This is the overwhelming power that can conquer fate!"

"Chaos will endlessly devour the world, until everything vanishes!"

Odin floated high in the sky, raising his twin Eternal Spears in both hands, like a god who had created the world, looking down with contempt at all the fragile living beings.

A giant blood-red cross, born from the chaos, bloomed with soul-piercing crimson radiance, sending wave after wave of world-destroying shockwaves rolling outward.

Bathed in the light of the blood-red cross, it was not only the heavens that were crumbling; all living things began to decompose, gradually dissolving into dust scattered across the chaotic skies.

Merlin saw his own blood turning into burning ash, constantly breaking apart and vanishing, while his flesh began emitting something akin to drifting dust.

He could feel his very existence starting to crumble and collapse, slowly fading away. The terrifying part was that there was no sign of this process ever stopping!

Merlin's heart burned with unwillingness. He had come to rescue Alice, yet not only had he failed to save her, he himself was now about to vanish here.

The world-ending blood-red cross was invincible. With each escalating impact, the heavens would be completely obliterated, and the civilization that Maria had created would turn to dust in the river of history, just like Asgard.

The world-ending power forged by merging countless laws was almost impossible to stop. Merlin struggled desperately to break through Odin's defense, but in the end he could not succeed. It was as if everything was already too late.

His fighting spirit was slowly extinguishing. Facing the disgusting defensive capability of the Sage Battle Armor, it was absolutely impossible for him to kill Odin before the world ended—

Was it really over here? Was there truly no way at all?

Dying alongside Alice here wouldn't be so bad, but what about Chris?

She was still so young. Would she really be okay on her own?

Merlin did not fear death. Being able to spend his final moments with Alice would already be more than enough. His only lingering worry was that daughter of his, still back in Lexham.

"Hahaha!" Odin let out an extremely smug laugh, jeering, "Prophet! Look at yourself now. You're like an old tiger stripped of its fangs. Where has your former majesty gone? Don't you want to keep resisting? Hasn't it already let you give up completely? That really isn't like you at all. You've truly disappointed me!"

Merlin remained silent. His body was disintegrating before the world-ending blood cross at a speed visible to the naked eye, his flesh and blood turning to ash and dust, scattering into the chaotic sky.

Not long from now, even Merlin's bones would be gone. He could think of no way to defeat Odin, leaving only endless regret in his heart.

"You've won, Odin. I can only congratulate you."

Odin gave a cold smile, looking down from above at the defeated Merlin, gritting his teeth as he spoke—

"This was all of your own doing. This is what comes from crossing me! When you personally destroyed the Asgard I created, you should have known this day would come!"

"You're nothing more than a time-jumping historical interferer. You can't change anything, and you can't save anyone.

"You're not the same as me. I have already defeated so-called fate, and your corpse will become the stepping stone on my path to the summit!"

Merlin lowered his head and slowly closed his eyes. He had no grounds to refute Odin's mockery. The victor becomes king, the vanquished becomes bandit—whatever the loser said was meaningless.

"I'll grudgingly offer you one compliment. As my opponent, you were competent. But merely competent. Vanish, annoying creature."

The moment those words left his mouth, the blood-red cross behind Odin's back roared, its world-destroying light surging again, nearly completely fracturing the space of the heavens!

The shadow of death笼罩ed every person. Fate seemed truly rewritten, with Odin becoming a terrifying deity beyond fate itself.

However, just then, an unexpected figure appeared behind Odin—none other than Maria, wielding her divine staff!

Maria raised her divine staff high, aiming directly at the one weakness on the Sage Battle Armor—

Precisely the spot Merlin had been relentlessly striking with his Fusion Iaijutsu. That area was already cracked through and extremely fragile. A few more heavy blows and Odin's defense would be shattered!

Because she was too close to the World-Ending Cross, Maria's entire body had already disintegrated down to bare bones. Had it not been for her desperately clinging to the Law of Life, she could never have approached Odin.

Thud!

Maria slammed her divine staff hard against the heavily cracked and vulnerable section of the Sage Battle Armor. Fragments of the Sage Stone flew up and down everywhere, but Odin's defense still didn't break—falling just short.

"What!? Maria! Are you in such a hurry to die? Your turn is next! No need to rush!"

Odin thrust both of his Eternal Spears forward at once, piercing straight through Maria's chest, twisting disgustingly as if desperate to crush this weakest of deities who dared challenge him into powder and ash!

Maria opened her mouth, coughing up dark red blood that splattered onto Odin's Sage Battle Armor. Despite being pierced through the chest, she showed no expression of pain—instead wearing a sinister smile.

"Odin, don't you love listening to stories?"

"Then let me tell you the ending of that story."

"That girl named Daphne, unable to bear her cruel lord, ultimately chose to take him down with her!"

Maria's gaze hardened. Her body erupted with blazing light, and the surging Law of Life instantly devoured her soul, an terrifying aura enveloping Odin!

A massive explosion rang out, flames spreading across the heavens along with the shockwave. Even the world-ending blood-red cross fell into a brief pause!

Maria had chosen self-detonation, sacrificing herself to crack Odin's defense, and pumping her life force—like poison—directly into her enemy's body!

A major god possessing laws choosing to self-detonate was no small threat. For the already barely-hanging Sage Battle Armor, this finally tore open a small hole!

"Maria?" Merlin's brows knitted tight. He never expected Maria to step up at a moment like this. Seeing the crack appear in the Sage Battle Armor, he glimpsed hope of victory!

"Ah..." Alice's lips trembled but no words came out. A tear track slid from the corner of her eye. Overwhelming sorrow surged in her heart. She knew it was because of those Theresa memories, yet she still felt it deeply. "Sister..."

Odin looked down at the hole in the Sage Battle Armor. Before he could feel anger, panic seized him due to the strange sensation in his body.

Odin's body was rapidly expanding. The handsome youth was becoming bloated, showing no signs of stopping, as if trying to break free from the tight confines of the Sage Battle Armor!

Among all the laws, the Law of Life was exceptionally peculiar. Like a tumor, it couldn't be combined with other laws—it caused the power of other laws to grow and swell at an accelerated rate.

On the surface, this sounded excellent, a wonderful thing that could amplify the power of laws. But every physical body had its limits.

If you could bear infinitely expanding law power, fine. If not, then there was only one outcome: explode from the inside!

Maria had originally planned to use this method against the Prophet, but never expected it to end up being used on Odin instead.

Odin dropped his Eternal Spears, his face flushing red, cold sweat pouring down, painfully scratching at his neck, desperately trying to pry open the Sage Battle Armor to ease the discomfort of his swollen body.

After seizing the Crown of Fate, Odin had already possessed multiple law powers. Now that the Law of Life had invaded him, it was undoubtedly even more fatal!

The more law powers he possessed, the stronger the amplification effect of the Law of Life—and the faster he would die!

"Damn you, Maria!!!"

Odin's body swelled like a balloon, forcefully tearing apart the Sage Battle Armor, yet the situation still didn't improve.

Finally, with a thunderous explosion, Odin's physical body burst, collapsing into writhing flesh paste on the ground.

Merlin stood dumbfounded, a chill rising in his heart. If Odin hadn't appeared, would it have been himself who died at Maria's hands?

"Is it... over? No! The world-ending hasn't stopped!"

Although Odin was dead and his consciousness had faded, his body had become the perfect nourishment for the World-Ending Cross.

Especially amplified countless times by the Law of Life—every single drop of his blood contained terrifying law power!

The world-ending blood-red cross emitted continuous rumblings, absorbing all the scattered flesh and blood of Odin—

Mud-like rivers of blood and meat flowed upward in reverse, adhering to the surface of the colossal cross!

Suddenly, at the center of the cross, a gigantic single eye opened, rolling around wildly, surveying this unfamiliar world.

This was clearly not Odin's consciousness, but a pure chaos monster that had been born—a freak creature that survived by devouring the world!

Hummm—

The giant single eye of the blood-red cross fixed its gaze tightly on Merlin, as if sensing a trace of threat. The world-destroying light surged again!

Bathed in the radiance, half of Merlin's face instantly revealed bleached white bones. He activated his Demon God Blood to its fullest, attempting to resist, but it was utterly inadequate!

The self-repair ability in his Demon God form couldn't compare to the Law of Life in the slightest. Give this monster just a little time, and Merlin would turn to dust right there on the spot!

"Danger! This place is extremely dangerous!"

Merlin gritted his teeth, staring fixedly at the world-destroying light, and resolutely assumed his iai draw stance, pouring his last reserves of strength into the Mistilteinn at his waist!

At a moment like this, he absolutely could not hesitate. He had to strike first. Being even a moment slower meant death for both Merlin and Alice. Every second counted!

The newborn monster had no Sage Battle Armor to shelter it. It presumably wouldn't be as difficult to kill as Odin had been. This was Merlin's only chance!

Merlin took a deep breath, once again rapidly fusing the three forces of his Iaijutsu, the Law of Destruction, and Mistilteinn, then drew his blade in one explosive motion!

The raised Mistilteinn erupted with dazzling radiance, in an instant piercing straight through the ravaged sky, cutting through every obstacle, becoming a heaven-splitting blade of light!

Merlin nearly bit through his own teeth. Facing the world-destroying light head-on, he brought down a devastating slash against the giant blood-red cross—

"Sever!"

The heavens collapsed. All that came into view was a blinding white world, everything becoming shrouded and indistinct!

Alice felt herself constantly falling, unable to see anything clearly. She tried to grasp onto something with her hands, but in that moment the world turned to nothingness!

Vaguely, Alice felt someone grab her hand. The朦胧 mist was peeled away layer by layer, revealing Merlin's deeply scarred face—

"Alice, let's go home."

title: Chapter 11 — Awakening
content:
Chapter 11 — Awakening

Volume 40 · Chapter 11

"My heavens, I never expected so many things to happen during my absence?"
Carl, who had just returned from cultivation, wore a look of utter shock as he listened to everyone recount the events of this period.

Having cultivated abroad for so long, Carl's strength had advanced again, seemingly catching a glimpse of the threshold of the Saint tier.
He had originally returned to visit his father, daughter, and a group of old friends, only to hear so many bizarre and convoluted tales.

Carl lowered his head, needing time to digest it all, his gaze falling on Alice still unconscious in bed, unsure of what to say.

"Hmph! Father has always been like this—leaves with a slap of the butt and dumps everything on everyone else." Lucilia said irritably.

"No, no, I also have my own reasons," Carl stammered, his face clouded with difficulty, thinking to himself that he had only left to grow stronger and protect his family; otherwise, he would never have been able to bear the separation.

"Lucilia, don't dwell on this. He left because he wanted to become someone worthy of relying on," Elder Taylor said in a soothing tone.

Lucilia refused to accept it, snorting coldly and turning her face away. Though she kept insulting her father, she was genuinely happy that Carl had returned.

"Merlin, can Alice really wake up?" Carl asked Merlin beside him.

"Yeah, it's been quite a while already, hasn't it?" Arnold waited anxiously.

"What's there to rush about? Bringing the dead back to life requires even more time; that's only normal," Rosetti emphasized.

"There's absolutely no sign of improvement," Da Vinci said, having observed Alice for a long time.

"Wait a bit longer." Faced with everyone's questions, Merlin gave a brief reply—he didn't know how to answer and his heart was pounding.

This method had been told to Merlin by the landlady; theoretically, it should be able to revive the dead.

After bringing Alice's soul back, Merlin had also fed her the core of the Life Spring, then came days of long waiting.

The husky Evis sat obediently by Merlin's feet, having been thoroughly frightened days earlier when he witnessed the Life Spring core's immense life force with his own eyes.

The life force contained in the Life Spring core—reviving an entire nation of the dead would be no problem, let alone reviving Alice!

Evis had no idea where Merlin had gotten such a thing; he could only sigh in his heart that Merlin was truly extravagant for the sake of saving his wife.

Merlin held his daughter, the little one nuzzling against her father's chest, her gaze falling on Alice in bed, filled with renewed expectation.

"Daddy, can Mommy really wake up?"

"Of course, believe Daddy. I've tried for so long already. If Daddy says it's possible, then it's possible—Daddy won't lie to you."

Merlin soothed his daughter, pressing his forehead against Chris's forehead. At such a time, he could only do his best to dispel her worries. Little Chris had wanted to ask more, but seeing her father's confident expression, she obediently shut her mouth.

Suddenly—
Alice's body on the bed began to emit dazzling light, thick with life energy that filled the entire room.

Everyone's faces changed drastically, feeling unprecedented pressure—not like facing a human, but a god!

A jade-green crystal slowly condensed above Alice's head, constantly radiating powerful life force!

Merlin recognized this aura instantly—it was the power of the law, and that jade-green crystal was nothing other than the divine core of a primary god, obtainable only by wearing the Crown of Fate!

Feeling the life law's power, Merlin's heart finally settled—this meant Alice had successfully returned from the dead. The plan had succeeded—she had gained a divine core, and the rules of the Crown of Fate had taken effect.

As long as one had worn the Crown of Fate, they would gain a divine core and become a primary god, no matter how they awakened.

But the life law's power—did it mean Alice had inherited Maria's divine core? It seemed that whether Alice was Theresa or not, she could not escape Maria's influence.

Merlin sighed inwardly. After all that had happened, he no longer hated Maria, the demon race's nemesis.

Having interacted with her, Merlin understood what kind of person she was and could offer a relatively objective evaluation.

To Maria, humanity's future did not matter; she only cared about her only relative.

Protecting humanity, hoping for humanity's prosperity? Those were actually Theresa's wishes. Maria did these things only to make her sister happy.

Theresa had sacrificed her life, and her wish for humanity's prosperity had forced Maria, when wearing the Crown of Fate, to choose not to revive her directly.

Was Maria an enemy of the demon race? Obviously yes, but Merlin felt she was not a simple brutal god, but a pitiable wretch who would resort to any means just to see her only relative again.

If Maria had chosen to perish alongside Merlin, Ophelia would have been the final victor. But in the end, she had chosen to protect her only relative and let Merlin off.

Merlin felt fortunate. Had it not been for Maria's final choice, he could never have succeeded. His impression of Maria changed somewhat, but his stance remained unshakable.

"What's this aura?! So powerful! Why is Alice's body glowing? Could it be the influence of the Fate Realm?"

Merlin's eyes widened as he watched everyone's shocked reactions, suddenly realizing something—not everyone could see divine cores. Apparently, only those who had worn the Crown of Fate or primary gods with divine cores could see that tiny divine core!

As for everyone else, they could only see the light radiating from the divine core; nothing else was visible.

The divine core of the life law slowly merged into Alice's body, the terrifying life energy settling into calm and vanishing without a trace.

Everyone's astonished expressions remained frozen on their faces as they looked at Merlin, hoping for an explanation.

Carl swallowed hard. The pressure Alice had just emitted was something he had never seen in his life and could never reach.

Alice's strength was no longer something that could be described as a sudden leap; it was a qualitative transformation. With a divine core, she had directly become a primary god who controlled the life law!

"Merlin, what just happened? This is going to be hard to explain."

Just as he finished speaking, Alice slowly opened her eyes, seeing the familiar ceiling and the familiar scent of home.

She slowly extended her arm, touching the air, trying to find a trace of the feeling of being alive.

But little Chris, seeing her mother open her eyes, could not wait any longer. She jumped onto the bed and threw herself into her mother's arms, crying out.

"Mommy! Mommy! You're finally awake! I missed you so much!"

"What? Chris, what are you doing?"

"Mommy..."

"Sweetheart, it's okay. Mommy's fine. I missed you too."

Alice showed a relieved smile, hugging Chris tightly, stroking the little girl's hair gently, and looking around at the familiar faces, she couldn't help but sigh that being alive was truly wonderful.

Merlin slowly stepped back, leaning against the wall, looking up at the chandelier, silently letting out a long breath, then slowly closing his remaining eye. All burdens were gone—finally, it was over.

Could he now go chase the peace in his dreams?

title: Chapter 12 — A Family of Three
content:
Chapter 12 — A Family of Three

Volume 40 · Chapter 12

Late at night, their familiar friends had all departed, no longer disturbing the couple's rest.

Alice's safe return was, for everyone in Lexem, a fortunate occurrence.
