On the rooftop, the couple snuggled together, looking up at the starry sky flowing like a river.

Neither spoke; they quietly watched the stars. After everything that had happened, they didn't know where to even begin.

Not knowing how much time had passed, a brilliant meteor slashed across the night sky, its long tail vanishing beyond the horizon—

"Merlin?"

"What?"

"What are you thinking about?"

Alice rested her head on Merlin's shoulder and asked curiously. His solid arm made her feel incredibly at ease. It had been a long time since she'd experienced such peace.

Only after enduring all sorts of hardships do many people realize how precious tranquility and harmony truly are—and Alice felt the same way.

"Me?" Merlin let out a long breath, a mysterious smile crossing his face. "Nothing."

"Then why are you smiling? Come on, tell me." Alice poked Merlin, feigning indignation.

"I just feel like all the burdens have lifted, and I can relax from here on out. Thinking about it, I'm still a bit unable to adapt."

Merlin gave an awkward smile. With Alice now awake and the heart curse gone, he had instantaneously lost all his goals.

It seemed he no longer needed to be busy about anything. He could properly lie low and live a quiet life?

But Merlin had long been entangled by the heart curse and other troubles, and suddenly, all his problems had vanished. The sheer contrast made it hard for him to adjust quickly.

"Yeah, everything's over. We can finally enjoy life properly." Alice paused, then continued, "But I think the busy lifestyle I had before was pretty good too. What do you think?"

"That's true, but I don't want anything like before to happen again."

"I feel the same way."

"By the way, how's your memory?"

"Whose memory are you talking about?"

"About Theresa…"

Faced with Merlin's question, Alice lowered her head and thought for a moment, unsure of how to explain it clearly.

After carefully organizing her words, Alice slowly began to speak.

"Those memories aren't complete—they're just fragmented pieces scattered here and there. But I still learned quite a lot, like the fact that some guy is the demon race prophet who jumps through time~"

Merlin scratched his head and murmured, "I figured you'd find out eventually. I was pretty shaken myself when I learned I was the prophet."

"I'm sorry, Merlin. It's all because of me—your eye will…"

"What are you talking about? 'Sorry' isn't something a married couple should be saying to each other."

Merlin cut Alice off, not wanting her to carry guilt that would make their future life heavy.

He touched his eyepatch. He had now fully adapted to living with one eye, and there wouldn't be any major issues.

"Although it's a bit regrettable, I think everything was still worth it. Trading one eye to bring you back was clearly a win on my end. So don't feel guilty about it. Weren't you the one who wore the Crown of Destiny to save me back then? Neither of us owes the other anything. We're even."

Alice's gaze flickered, and she couldn't help but mutter, "Though you're right, only having one eye still looks kind of weird."

"Huh?!" Merlin looked at Alice beside him in shock. "No way! Are you a looks-matter association member? Because I became a pirate captain, you're leaving me now? That's so real! I wanna cry~"

"No no no, that's not what I meant!" Alice looked up and firmly bonked Merlin on the head. "What kind of ridiculous thoughts are running through your head? How could I possibly do that? Good grief!"

"Is having one eye really that strange? I think it's fine," Merlin muttered, puzzled.

"It just feels like it doesn't look as good as before."

"Darn it! You're claiming you're not a looks-matter association member!? Superficial woman~"

"Why are you getting so worked up? I haven't even finished my sentence! You're the superficial stinky man!"

Sparks seemed to fly in the air as the couple faced off angrily, their glares colliding.

After all, they were the last two major deities in the world. If they actually started fighting, the mortal realm might tremble along with them.

"I mean, even someone beautiful gets tiring to look at eventually. Although you look a bit odd now, it's not bad—it has a kind of novelty feel?"

"What? Novelty? I get it. A woman who loves the new and tires of the old. Still superficial~"

"???" Alice's face darkened as she glared at Merlin, gritting her teeth. "No matter what I say, you always find a reason to call me superficial, right? I'm gonna hit you~"

"Cough cough! Let's be serious," Merlin lightly cleared his throat and explained, "I was just testing your reaction earlier, but now I'm relieved."

"Huh? What were you testing?"

"I wanted to see how much Theresa's memories had affected you. But judging from your reaction, it was minimal."

"That…" Alice fell silent for a moment before answering softly, "There will definitely be some influence, but not that significant. I still consider myself Alice. Theresa is more like dust from the past, right? I don't want to recall too many things from the Age of the Gods. Those memories aren't pleasant."

Merlin didn't respond, thinking this was fine. If she recalled too much, it would only make Alice confused about who she truly was. Everything about Theresa was already in the past.

"Hei—xiu—!"

Chris stared at her radish-like short legs as the husky Elvis carried her up to the rooftop in his mouth.

The little one had noticed her parents were gone in the middle of the night and kept fussing to find them.

Feeling helpless, and unable to bear seeing Chris so anxious, Elvis had no choice but to bring her to Merlin and Alice.

After depositing little Chris, Elvis bolted, terrified Merlin would hold it against him for interrupting their alone time.

"Daddy, Mommy~"

Little Chris squeezed between Merlin and Alice, lying in both their laps and happily kicking her legs.

"Chris, why are you climbing up here instead of sleeping properly?"

"Yeah, it's too windy up here. This isn't a place for you."

Merlin and Alice both put on stern parental faces, desperate to bundle the little one into bed and lock her away. Being disturbed was still a bit annoying.

Chris's ahoge wobbled on her head, her little pout showing she wasn't convinced, her mischievous eyes darting around continuously—

"I know, Daddy and Mommy were being sneaky up on the rooftop. You were definitely doing something naughty, right?"

"Sneaky about what?" Alice's face flushed, left speechless.

"Ohoho~, Chris is such a genius, personally stopping a depraved evil act. Truly worthy of being the acting commander of the Melon Kids Knights~"

"Depraved evil act? That's clearly a sacred ritual for adults! What would a kid like you know about it?"

Merlin, flustered, repeatedly patted Chris's small head. He had been hoping to be affectionate with Alice, but it seemed like that wasn't going to happen now—

Nope, this kid is getting harder and harder to handle.

title: Chapter 13 — The Legend Fades
content:
Chapter 13 — The Legend Fades

Volume 40 · Chapter 13

A family of three sat on the rooftop, Merlin holding Chris who wouldn't stop chattering, enjoying a rare moment of peace.

Although they couldn't say overly sweet things with the little one around, Merlin still wished this moment could last forever.

Alice couldn't help but take Chris into her arms and slowly smooth down her messy hair after waking up.

"Mmm~" Chris became much more obedient, clearly enjoying her mother stroking her hair. "Mom, will you leave again?"

"Huh?" Alice suddenly froze. "Why would you ask that?"

"Chris is very scared Mom and Dad will leave for a very long time again."

Little Chris kept her head down and hadn't dared to voice her thoughts before, afraid of becoming a child who held back her parents' work and added pressure to them.

But Chris felt the atmosphere was nice now, so she couldn't help but ask, not wanting Mom and Dad to leave her again for work.

"This..." Alice looked at her anxious daughter and couldn't bear it. She didn't know what to do next either. There was no way to predict the future.

"Of course! Mom and Dad won't leave you. We can promise you that."

"Merlin, what are you doing?"

Before Alice could figure out how to respond, Merlin had already made the promise first, and she thought this was very inappropriate.

They had already deceived Chris many times, so what if something happened in the future and they had to leave? Making promises so casually wasn't good, even if the other party was a child.

"Alice, actually, I've always had a thought."

"What thought?"

"I've always wanted to live in a peaceful paradise far away from conflicts, without worrying about anything, without any troubles, just enjoying a happy life like we are now."

"But does such a place really exist?"

Alice expressed doubt, feeling that Merlin's idea was basically impractical, purely a naive fantasy.

As a couple who had seen quite a bit of the world, the two knew that a place completely free from all conflicts basically didn't exist.

"It exists! Trust me, we will find such a pure land." Merlin said firmly.

"So you plan to leave Rexem? Leave those familiar friends?" Alice asked tentatively.

"That's right, I plan to leave, to search for a truly peaceful and tranquil pure land." Merlin shared the dream he'd always harbored in his heart.

Alice narrowed her eyes and asked suspiciously, "Weren't you planning to leave here a long time ago? To live a hermit's life on your own?"

"Well..." Merlin's gaze flickered, and he explained seriously, "I did have that thought, but now..."

"But now what?" Alice pressed.

"Now I want to take you and Chris with me when I leave. The three of us cannot be missing anyone, because we are a family."

"Is that so?" Alice's face flushed slightly, feeling somewhat relieved, and her old habit kicked in again. "Since you've sincerely invited me, I guess it's not completely unacceptable to leave with you."

"Not completely acceptable? Never mind then." Merlin looked down at his daughter. "Chris, come with Daddy. Look at Mom's troubled expression, she clearly doesn't want to go with us."

"Mom, is that true? If Chris goes with Daddy, then Mom will be all alone." Little Chris said in a panic.

"Merlin!" Alice ground her teeth, hugging Chris tightly. "You're too cunning. I, I never said I wouldn't go with you. If you and Chris aren't around, I'd feel lonely too. I'm angry, hmph~!"

"Just kidding, don't take it so seriously. No matter where you are, I will always bring you back by my side."

"That still counts as something a human would say."

"After all, you are my lovely wife. I hope we can stay together forever, just like now, quietly watching the starry night every day."

"I also hope we can be like this."

Merlin slowly leaned closer. Alice also slowly closed her eyes, waiting for a affectionate kiss.

But the ahoge on little Chris's head worked like an antenna, sensing the atmosphere had become somewhat inappropriate for children, so her short radish-like legs jumped fiercely, squeezing between Merlin and Alice, and the parents' kiss landed right on her face.

Merlin and Alice exchanged complicated looks at their mischievous daughter. Usually Chris was fine in every way, but during moments that called for just the two of them, it became embarrassingly awkward.

The two parents looked calm on the surface, but inwardly they desperately wanted to find something to distract the little one's attention. Unfortunately, that shrewd husky had long since slipped away.

Little Chris gave herself a thumbs-up, her eyes sparkling with countless little stars, proudly saying—

"Hehe! Chris totally won this round~★"

At the dojo, the old headmaster Tyler was teaching little Mini combat techniques.

After Hobbs died, old Tyler decided to raise Mini as his granddaughter and prepared to pass on to her the Thunder Strike Combat Art.

The current Mini had gradually emerged from the shadow of losing her father and had a new goal: to become an adventurer who surpassed her father.

Old Tyler hoped Mini could grow up as soon as possible, learn the Thunder Strike Combat Art, and have a skill to defend herself in the future. This was also a way to give Hobbs some kind of closure.

"Father!" Mr. Karl burst into the dojo and said loudly, "Merlin and Alice plan to leave Rexem. Let's go see them off!"

"Huh? They're leaving?" Old Tyler's eyes widened in astonishment. This news was too sudden.

The father and son hurried outside and found Merlin, Alice, and their daughter already seated in a donkey-drawn carriage named "Mengmeng," with all their luggage already packed.

"Merlin, you're planning to leave?" Headmaster Tyler asked urgently.

"Yes, it may be hard to see each other again in the future." Merlin replied softly.

"Why? Isn't living in Rexem quite nice?" Headmaster Tyler didn't understand. More importantly, without powerful figures staying in Rexem, it was obviously a huge loss no matter how you looked at it.

"Headmaster, this is the result of our careful consideration. We are going to search for a conflict-free pure land and then properly accompany Chris as she grows up." Merlin answered truthfully.

"Yes, Headmaster, we've already made up our minds." Alice nodded from the side.

Old Tyler saw that the couple had already made their decision and knew there was nothing more to say, so he could only sigh and say, "You must take good care of yourselves."

"You as well, Headmaster. Take good care of your health. You should make Mr. Karl serve you more." Merlin said with a smile.

"Stop mocking me." Mr. Karl scratched his head awkwardly.

"Lucia's eyes glistened with tears as she stepped forward and hugged Alice. "I'll miss you, Alice. If there's a chance, come back and visit."

"Yes, definitely come back and visit. Rexem is also your second home after all." Arnold said reluctantly.

"Oh... has my tragic first love ended so hastily? Is this what painful yet joyful love feels like?" Jenna also came out to see them off alongside her brother Arnold.

"That's all your fantasy, Miss Jenna. Nothing happened between us. Watch fewer love stories and step out into reality more often." Merlin responded with a dark face.

"It's so unbearable. Miss Alice is leaving, so there'll be no one to scold me anymore! How painful!"

Everyone turned to look and found that Rexem's guard captain, Price, was weeping bitterly, nostalgically reminiscing about the days when Alice used to berate him.

"Shut up, Price! You're disgusting!" Alice's forehead veins throbbed.

"So big—"

"Wait!"

Little Chris jumped down from the carriage, handed over a box containing all her toys to Mini, and gave her best playmate a hug.

"Sis Mini, I'll miss you~"

"I'll miss you too."

Everyone watched the two little ones, their hearts filled with mixed emotions for a moment. After their daughter returned, Merlin pulled the reins.

"Everyone, please take good care of yourselves. We will always be your friends."

Watching Merlin and Alice's carriage gradually disappear into the brilliant sunset glow—

Rosetti: "Sigh, even Merlin and Alice are leaving? There are fewer and fewer familiar faces in Rexem."

Da Vinci: "Out with the old, in with the new. More new faces will appear in Rexem in the future."

"That's true, but their departure will leave behind in Rexem—or rather, the whole world—a legend that is difficult to surpass, don't you think?" Mr. Karl remarked.

"What legend?"

"Need you even ask? Of course it's the legend of the strongest adventurer. Both members of the couple have extraordinary adventure stories."

title: Chapter 14 — The Legend Ends
content:
Chapter 14 — The Legend Ends

Volume 40 · Chapter 14

Ten years later.

As time passed, the experiences of that legendary adventurer couple had been embellished by countless people into stories.

Some people gradually forgot them, while others continued to remember them in their hearts.

However, without a doubt, in the adventurer profession, it was difficult for anyone to surpass this couple.

Demon Castle.

"Hey! Samiel, do you see any changes in me today?" Asmodeus asked expectantly.

"No, you're still the same, like a woman," Samiel replied truthfully.

"Ugh, Samiel, you're hopeless, your perception of subtle changes is too weak," Asmodeus couldn't help but complain.

"The color of your lipstick has changed," Ouroboros reminded from the side.

"Indeed, Ouroboros, compared to Samiel this uncouth oaf, you're much better. I have high hopes for you," Asmodeus nodded repeatedly, then began to scold, "Can't you even notice such an obvious change? You should use your brain more."

"???" Samiel became puzzled, touching his non-existent head, which remained empty above.

In the distance, Shu and Ophelia watched this scene, not knowing where to start their ridicule—

"Asmodeus-sama, are you teasing Samiel-sama again?"

"What can I do? Our Merlin-sama is the only one in the demon race who can match wavelengths with Asmodeus-sama."

Ophelia spread her hands, revealing a helpless smile, feeling that the demon lords in the Demon Castle had become so bored they were almost going crazy.

Now that the heavenly souls were extinct, demons no longer had any natural enemies, making life uninteresting.

"Yes, I wonder how His Majesty is doing? He should be living well, right?" Shu looked up, unable to help but fantasize.

"It's inevitable. Our Majesty, who destroyed the heavenly main god, is there anyone in this world who can shake him now?" Ophelia said proudly.

"However, Lilith-sama is quite miserable. Recently, she's been forced by Vivian-sama to practice magic, probably to be cultivated as a reserve demon lord.

From time to time, the palace interior echoed with Lilith's painful screams and unwilling complaints.

Lilith's magic power continued to brew in her hands, not daring to disperse it, otherwise she would face her mother's punishment.

She couldn't help but sneak a glance at Vivian beside her, immediately turning pale with fright, and muttered.

"Why do I have to do this? With my brother around, I don't need to work hard at all."

"You're talking nonsense. Your brother is your brother, and you are you. Don't shamelessly compare yourself to him."

Vivian's face turned iron-green, saying helplessly, "Are you really my daughter? You didn't inherit any of my good qualities. It must be because everyone spoiled you since you were young."

"Hmph!" Lilith puffed out her cheeks, retorting, "Why do I need to work hard? My brother will solve all my troubles."

"Shut up. If you can't learn ritual magic today, you won't have a butt left."

"Waaa, brother, come back and save me! Mom has gone crazy!"

"You're in my hands now, so give up."

Vivian's eyes flashed with red light, the whip in her hand cracking loudly.

Spanish Kingdom, Alice's younger half-brother, formerly the young Amadeo, had now come of age.

Under his governance, Spain had become prosperous, the barriers between classes were no longer unbreakable, and many decrees beneficial to common people were issued.

All of this was to prevent another Alfonso from appearing. Even though that man had been dead for over a decade, his influence on this country remained profound.

A grand royal procession marched through the new city built from the former slums. The poor people spontaneously took to the streets, cheering loudly for the king.

They had bid farewell to their impoverished lives, all thanks to Amadeo changing the distribution rules, so the people here deeply supported the young king.

Amadeo's impression on people was no longer that of the incompetent little kid from before, but had become a wise ruler in their eyes.

Looking at the cheering crowd, Amadeo, sitting in the carriage, didn't show any smile, instead letting out a quiet sigh.

"Your Majesty? Why are you sighing? Is there something you're dissatisfied with? Look at these people, they've all come for you."

Vival, the royal guard accompanying Amadeo, felt he had followed the right person, as this land had indeed become better and better.

Amadeo remained silent for a long time, never answering Vival's question, his young face showing a hint of weariness.

"I'm a bit envious of that sister of mine now."

"Why?"

"I feel like I'm trapped in a cage, losing the freedom that originally belonged to me. My sister was lucky, she successfully escaped the cage."

"Don't say that, Your Majesty. No one can replace your role. This land needs you."

"I know, but it's just meaningless complaining. I wonder how my sister is doing? She really hasn't come back."

"I heard she's retired, no one knows where she went."

"Is that so? She should be happy. Being a king is too lonely."

"Your Majesty, now that you're queen, you can't be so casual."

"Let the cabinet handle it, it's not urgent. Don't bother me, it's decided. This rigid ceremony has exhausted me, I need to reward myself properly."

Blaise immediately put on a pained expression, feeling an indescribable agony, his heart almost stopping—

I must be the most miserable knight in the world. As the queen's royal guard, I'll probably suffer for a long time.

"Maybe it's false, but I want to believe Mr. Akaron didn't lie. He was always an honest person."

"Sorry, I'm just a bit unwilling to accept it. Haha."

Inside the palace.

Elizabeth was reviewing a mountain of documents, her busy figure unchanged.

Merlin's departure was actually a good thing for Britain.

At least Elizabeth didn't have to worry every day about Merlin getting angry and destroying her kingdom.

The wounds caused by the demons had become a memory of the past, but Elizabeth didn't slacken, hoping to pave the way for the next queen.

The new selection of Thorn Knights was in full swing, with endless tasks every day.

After ten years of change, the kingdom's young generation had grown up, making it the best time to select new knights.

Knock knock knock—

"Enter."

"What's wrong with you? Your face looks terrible."

It's infuriating, I've never seen such arrogant brats!"

"Thank you, Windsor."

On an island within the kingdom, this place had become the territory of the other races.

Elizabeth had granted Sherry a title and given her this island as a fief, providing the surviving other races with land to live on.

The resilient other races hadn't been defeated, instead rising against the tide, continuing to thrive and building a new city on the island.

Sherry, as the daughter of the elf king, had become the lord of the city of other races, leading all the other races toward a brighter future.

The benevolent king Sariette, who originally held a higher position and greater strength, had voluntarily relinquished his authority to Sherry.

Perhaps it was because Sarret still hadn't emerged from the shadows, feeling guilty over the destruction of the United Kingdom.

Sarret hoped to be forgiven, so now he was using his strength, risking his life to protect the last homeland of the outcasts.

In the conference room, Shirley was planning the next steps. She was no longer the crybaby she used to be; she had become the spiritual pillar for the outcasts.

Shirley had inherited the elven king's dying wish. Rather than shirking responsibility, she had shouldered the burden of leading the outcasts to continue living.

"We need to build a school so that every outcast child can receive an education, so that outcast knowledge and culture can continue to be passed down."

"That's a great idea, I approve." Elf knight Silphen nodded repeatedly. "But each race has its own culture, so the difficulty of implementation is quite high."

"We don't need to distinguish between elves, dwarves, humans, and other races. Here we are all outcasts, so we must unify our culture. We only need to extract the essence of each race and build a new system. This is the culture of the Outcast City, and it belongs to every race living in the city."

"It sounds feasible, but there will surely be old fogies relying on their seniority to jump out and oppose it. Lord Sarret, what's your suggestion?"

Sarret, who had been silent the whole time, didn't speak but remained quiet. He didn't want to interfere with any of Shirley's decisions. He felt he had no right, nor did he deserve to.

"I have no objections. Shirley is the city lord; her word is law."

Shirley's expression grew complicated, and she said softly, "Uncle Sarret, are you still feeling guilty about what happened in the past?"

"No. For a sinner like me, just surviving until now is already a blessing from heaven," Sarret sighed.

"You don't need to blame yourself so harshly. The destruction of the United Kingdom is not your fault. If not for you, it would have been nearly impossible for the outcasts to escape that disaster. You are not a sinner; you are a hero."

"I—" Sarret lowered his head, hesitating to speak.

"The future of the Outcast City needs you. No matter what, you cannot stand aside. Immersing yourself in the past is foolish. We survived, so we must look forward. That is the lesson Mr. Merlin taught me."

Facing Shirley's earnest plea, Sarret couldn't help but lower his head, vaguely feeling that he hadn't done enough. Simply guarding the last piece of land had no future.

"Hmm? Minnie, you're back? Let big sister take a look. You didn't get hurt this time, did you?"

A mysterious world independent of the mortal realm, much like Hell and the Heavenly Realm.

Here, birds sang and flowers fragrant, with spring lasting all year round—a perfect portrayal of a utopia.

One of the Almighty God's abilities was the power to create a new world.

Merlin hadn't searched the mortal realm for a non-existent paradise. Instead, he had used his own power to create a world.

This place had been tailor-made for his wife and child, perfectly avoiding all conflicts and allowing them to fully enjoy a peaceful life.

Beneath a tree, warm sunlight filtered through layers of foliage, dappled light spots dancing across Merlin's face.

He lay on the grass, sound asleep, as if dreaming of something pleasant. The corners of his mouth curled up slightly.

Suddenly, a tickling sensation came from his nose. Merlin frowned and slowly woke from his dream, seeing his daughter's lovely smiling face.

"Daddy, Mommy says it's time to come back for dinner~ heehee~"

Chris was holding a foxtail grass, laughing nonstop. In ten years she had grown a bit, but the changes weren't obvious; she still looked like a child.

For Chris, ten years was far too short—absolutely not enough time for her to grow up. It would likely take much longer for her to truly become an adult.

"My little princess has learned bad habits. You've already learned to tease your daddy."

Merlin got up, lifted the little one from the ground and held her high, admiring his lovely daughter and feeling deeply content.

"Did Mommy send you?"

"Yes! Mommy said you definitely sneaked off here to slack off again~"

"Hah, as expected, it's always your mom who understands me best." Merlin let his daughter ride on his shoulders and said softly, "Let's go home for dinner. But your mom's cooking definitely isn't as good as mine. I'll make something delicious for you tomorrow."

"Yummy~ yummy~" Little Chris rubbed her father's hair.

"Hmm? Have you gotten heavier?" Merlin felt that his daughter seemed to have grown a bit.

"Hmph!" Little Chris puffed up her cheeks indignantly and argued, "No! Chris is a lady; she wouldn't get heavier! It's all Daddy's illusion!"

"It's not a bad thing. Gaining weight means you're growing." Merlin supported his daughter's short little legs and said like an old father, "My little princess will grow up sooner or later, and then go write her own life story."

"My own life story? Will Chris also find someone she likes, like Mommy and Daddy?" Chris asked innocently.

"Uh!" Merlin's expression grew awkward, feeling a bit like he was having a heart attack—

"Don't bring up such a mood-killing topic. I need a psychological process to accept that kind of thing."

"I definitely won't hand over my precious pearl to just any trash, and I won't let you suffer too much either."

"But you're right. In the future, you will also meet a lover worth being with, just like Mommy and Daddy."

"Will my lover be like Daddy?" Chris asked curiously.

"That might be, or it might not. In the end, it's a choice you yourself will have to make." Merlin paused and said meaningfully, "But if you do find someone you like, you must tell me. Only after passing my test will I approve of your lover."

"What kind of test?" Chris pressed.

Merlin chuckled and said in a joking tone, "That would be defeating me. I won't approve of someone who can't protect you."

"Wah! Then won't Chris have to stay by Mommy and Daddy's side forever? That actually doesn't sound bad!" The ahoge on top of Chris's head swayed happily.

Merlin smiled without speaking, thinking that Chris couldn't make her own decisions yet. She was destined to have her own life, but who could say what the future held?

“It’s too slow, the food’s going to get cold!” Alice, wearing an apron, hands on her hips, stared dissatisfied at the father and daughter before her.
“We got here quickly.” Merlin’s eyes darted away.
“Chris can vouch for Dad!” Chris’s little face grew serious.

Alice gazed at Merlin, the two of them already an old married couple, nearly becoming one person.
Merlin slowly stopped, turned back to look at the old tree, and for a moment his eyes grew wistful.
“What’s wrong? Did something happen?” Alice asked, puzzled.

Merlin chuckled, holding the cute daughter on his neck, taking Alice’s hand, they gradually walked away, returning to the home where the meal was still warm.
The old tree swayed gently in the breeze, its leaves trembling and making a rustling sound; the sunset’s afterglow dyed this secluded utopia red.
Ding ding ding—
The black iron adventurer’s token hanging from the branch trembled in the wind, as if recounting a legendary tale?
The setting sun poured down, filtering through the layers of leaves, casting that old black iron piece in a brilliant glow.
